novel_info.author: East City Order
novel_info.summary: Wang Lan's world is facing the threat of demon invasion and modern weapons are of no use. What humans can rely on are those who have awakened their Star Martial talent. Wang is one of the awakened and has a good helper. Maybe too good...“Successfully destroyed a Demon spy team, 100 thousand XP points and 5000 skill points rewarded.”“System, can you stop giving me points? I just want to focus on cultivation on my own.”“Nop, you don’t!”

chapters.title: Chapter 1: You are too weak
chapters.content:
Chapter 1: Chapter 1: You are too weak
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
"Students, summer vacation is just around the corner, and I can’t bear the thought of not seeing my dear students for almost two months. My heart is filled with reluctance, and the emotion of parting has kept me tossing and turning at night for several days..."
On the podium, a woman in her thirties with a touch of makeup, wearing a black ladies’ suit and black-framed glasses, spoke with a sorrowful expression full of reluctance.
But no matter how hard she performed, all the students below slightly bowed their heads in a serene Zen-like state, as if meditating.
"Wang Lan, what big move do you think Extinction Master is holding back today?"
"To deal with us, does she even need to hold back a big move? With Extinction Master’s BOSS level, just one glare from her is enough to empty our health bars. Logically, our class did well on the exams, so Extinction Master should show some mercy."
"Did well? That’s just you, isn’t it?"
In the back row, Wang Lan and his best friend Zhang Hao, who had been desk mates for two years, had already perfected a method of Morse code communication that allowed them to exchange messages silently or with minimal sound, sometimes telling dirty jokes.
"After much thought, I’ve decided to give each student a parting gift. The gift may be small, but it’s the thought that counts. During the summer vacation, whenever students see the gift from me, they’ll be reminded of me. After class, the boys should come to my office to carry them."
"I have a bad feeling about this..."
"Me too!"
"This final exam was a citywide mock college entrance exam in Suzhou City. Our class... did fairly well. We had three students in the top ten for the entire city, and our class ranked first in average scores, with a 77% pass rate for the top university admission tier."
"YAY—" The heavy atmosphere suddenly relaxed; they had thought Extinction Master was up to her tricks again.
"It’s right to be happy, but there’s no need to be proud of our performance. We are Class One of Suzhou No.1 Middle School. It’s only natural to get these results. But is that enough? This was just a mock exam, not the actual college entrance exam. And who will our real competitors be in the actual exam? Those small fry from Suzhou City? No! It’s all of Jiang Province.
"Tong City’s seven high schools have held Jiang Province’s top college entrance exam spots for thirteen years, and no one has been able to shake their status. Students, do you have the confidence to challenge Tong City’s dominance in a year’s time?
"WOW what? A hundred years is too long—we only fight for the day. This isn’t the neighboring Star Martial Arts Campus. Whether your future path is a broad avenue or a thorny road depends on the college entrance exam, which is less than a year away.
"Getting into a good university is how you secure a future worth speaking of. Think about your parents. Compare those who commute to work through wind and snow on e-bikes to those who drive to work and sip coffee in their offices.
"Your talents are all the same. None of you are Star Martial Warriors, yet the difference in your future lives could be night and day. Why? Because of effort. Because those who live comfortable lives once worked harder than those who commute in harsh weather.
"The college entrance exam is the battlefield that can change your life, even determine your entire future. Win, and you’ll have wealth and glory; lose, and you can only pin your hopes on the next generation. That is, if you even have a next generation."
This time, Class One did well, so the thirty-year-old single homeroom teacher didn’t explode but merely delivered a lesson filled with motivational speech.
The dose of motivational speech was enough, quite satisfying.
As the bell for the end of class rang, Wang Lan took out a box of milk from his drawer. At an age where he was still growing, Wang Lan was quite concerned about his height from his previous life. In this life, he was determined not to be short again.
"Can you still eat? Haven’t you had enough of Extinction Master’s motivational speech?"
"Rat, that might be motivational speech to you, but to me, it’s poison. I can meet Extinction Master’s demands with my eyes closed. I didn’t take in a single sip of her speech."
"Uh, Lan, I’ll excuse myself for a moment."
"Hmm?" A strong sense of killing intent suddenly loomed over Wang Lan’s head like a dark cloud.
Wang Lan looked up to find several good buddies and some top-notch students from the class gathering around him.
Cornered, Wang Lan shrank back against the wall. "My esteemed classmates... may I ask what brings you here?"
"What brings us here? Your Excellency, the Academic God, do you know how many points you scored in this citywide mock exam?"
"Four hundred... four hundred and sixty... what about it?" Wang Lan was quite pleased with such a high score, but hey, life is all about showing off, right? Without a bit of pretense, where’s the fun in life?
So the more incredible others found it, the more nonchalant he had to act.
Just ask these guys here. After every exam, didn’t every one of them exclaim how badly they’d bombed it?
But when the scores came out, each of them was somewhere between three hundred ninety-something and over four hundred. This bunch were all posers.
"What about it? You have the gall to ask that? Out of a perfect score of five hundred, you scored four hundred sixty? You tell me, what about it?"
"Last year, the admission scores for Yanda and Jingda were four hundred and seven. Tell me, why bother exerting so much effort on a mock exam? Aren’t you afraid you might hurt yourself?"
"Wolfie, look what you’ve done, you’ve inflated Extinction Master’s ego so much! She’s even planning to challenge the dominion of the seven high schools in Tong City. After discussion, the class committee has decided: for the whole of senior year, your total score must not exceed the second place by more than ten points. Otherwise, on behalf of Li Dameiren, I’ll take you down."
"Damn!" Wang Lan, faced with someone who looked even more brutish than Li Kui, immediately flipped him the bird.
"I think a verbal warning won’t be very effective. Maybe we should..."
"Makes sense..."
About a dozen of them were top students of the class, any of whom could potentially fight for the second spot. But alas, even if they beat everyone else, they could only ever hope to be second best.
Because above their heads reigned a Demon King they could never surpass—an academic god worshipped by a hundred thousand elementary school students in Suzhou City, already deified while alive.
"Esteemed masters, hold on, don’t do anything rash! Let’s talk this out, just hear me out..." Wang Lan felt a bit intimidated when he saw the situation.
"Explain? What more is there to explain? We’ve put up with you hogging first place for years, but constantly rubbing our faces in the dirt is something we simply cannot bear. Choose: either treat us to milk tea or get roughed up."
"Can I have both?" Wang Lan’s face broke into a lecherous grin. "I’ll treat you all to milk tea, and let Li Dameiren and the others do the roughing up..."
"Hey? That could work!" Wang Xuebin stroked his chin in contemplation.
"Ugh! Wang Lan, you’re picking up bad habits too," several girls blushed and retorted.
"Alright, alright, no more joking. I’m serious too. All these years, constantly crushing you all hasn’t been very sportsmanlike. Treating the whole class to milk tea as an apology is only right. I’ll order delivery; lunch today is on me.
"But as for not outperforming you in future tests... that’s a bit difficult for me. You’re all the pride of Greater Su City, high school prodigies; any one of you could unleash your potential and shoot to the top...
"But alas, I’m merely mortal. Even if I wanted to go easy on you, my abilities wouldn’t let me. Take this time, for instance. Scoring over 480 wasn’t supposed to be that hard. I intentionally got one question wrong, thinking I’d leave you all some dignity.
"But... I didn’t expect you to be so fragile. I gave you an ocean of leeway and still overestimated you all..."
Initially, the pack of academic aces could somewhat agree; everyone’s performance and ability were quite similar. Even though the ranks from second to fifteenth seemed widely spaced, the actual score margins never exceeded ten points.
But by the end of that speech, those aces were livid.
Listen to that! Was that something a human being would say? What did he mean by ’I gave you an ocean of leeway and still overestimated you all’?
The atmosphere turned deathly still for a moment, as murderous intent simmered in the eyes of the students before him.
"What are we waiting for? Get him—"
The mood in the classroom instantly livened up. The academic aces fully unleashed their playful sides, and the other students weren’t about to miss out. Boys and girls surged forward together; the chance to get their hands on the academic god was rare and too good to pass up.
BUZZ— "Congratulations to the Host for completing the Great Perseverance Trial: First place in one thousand consecutive exams, lasting six years and nine months. The Destiny System has successfully activated. Initializing system startup..."
A notification suddenly sounded in Wang Lan’s mind. In that very instant of the system’s activation, it was as if his soul detached from his body.
His physical form was being lovingly caressed by youthful hands and embraced by the soft chests of young girls. Meanwhile, his soul descended into his Spiritual Sea of Consciousness, eagerly awaiting the full activation of the Destiny System.
In reality, the Destiny System had appeared when Wang Lan was seven years old. As a transmigrator, he naturally accepted the system’s existence. After all, a golden finger is standard issue for transmigrators.
But this Destiny System was a bit capricious. Before it could be activated, one had to complete a trial. Only by passing this test could the system be enabled.
Back then, Wang Lan was so thrilled he was bouncing on his bed, thinking the apex of his life was right before his eyes. But upon seeing the trial’s test question, he was dumbfounded.
"As a person of destiny, you must embody great wisdom, great perseverance, and great fortune. To pass the Destiny Trial, you must choose one of these three aspects and complete its task.
"The Task of Great Wisdom: The chaotic openings of the Different Dimensional Space and the mystery of the Demon Clan’s origin have troubled human civilization for thousands of years. Countless Pioneers have entered the Different Dimensional Space, risking their lives. The Demon Clan has invaded our human world time and again.
"Wise youth, use your brilliant intellect to unravel all these mysteries!"
Unravel my grandma’s footbinding cloth! A problem that has stumped the entire world for millennia, one that millennia of concerted research by all of human civilization hasn’t solved, and you want a child like me to unravel it? Have some freaking shame!
"The Trial of Great Perseverance: As a person of destiny, you cannot rely solely on fate to achieve greatness. You must exert effort unimaginable to ordinary people and possess perseverance beyond their reach.
"In any examination or competition, strive for first place. Achieve first place one thousand consecutive times to pass the trial. There can be no interruptions; if the streak is broken even once, all progress resets to zero."
A thousand consecutive first-place finishes? Are you for real? Though I wasn’t a slacker in my previous life, I was certainly no prodigy either. Just thinking about a thousand consecutive firsts made me feel utterly dejected.
"The Trial of Great Fortune: As a person of destiny, you must be accompanied by great fortune. Purchase one lottery ticket and win the top-tier grand prize. If multiple tickets are purchased, only the first one bought will be considered. Young man, go forth and take on this trial. Prove that you are the one most favored by the heavens, the luckiest lad of all."The source of this content ɪs NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
Seeing this one, Wang Lan just wanted to slam the table.
One lottery ticket, seven numbers, winning a top-tier grand prize. What were the odds of that again? Is this even a task a human could accomplish?
After much deliberation, Wang Lan eventually decided that the second trial, the test of great perseverance, was the only one a mortal could possibly complete. The first and third ones? You’ve got to be freaking kidding me...

chapters.title: Chapter 2 The Awakening That Came 2 Years Late
chapters.content:
Chapter 2: Chapter 2 The Awakening That Came 2 Years Late
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
The Star Martial Arts Campus of Suzhou No.1 Middle School was just a wall apart from the main campus area of Suzhou No.1 Middle School.
As one might expect, the Star Martial Arts Campus was where students who had awakened their Star Martial Warrior talent studied. The origin of Star Martial Warriors has mystified humans for thousands of years; tracing it back, one might have to go as far as the Mythical Era.
Humans appeared around seven million years ago, while Homo sapiens emerged approximately three hundred thousand years ago. The existence of Star Martial Warriors seemed to have accompanied human evolution from the very beginning.
Some historians believe that the emergence of Star Martial Warriors is related to the opening of Different Dimensional Space, but biologists think that Star Martial Warriors are a product of human evolution. The gene of a Star Martial Warrior hides within human DNA, making it possible for any person to awaken it and become a Star Martial Warrior.
Star Martial Warriors are just a part of the complex machinery that is human civilization, special individuals evolved to ensure the continued existence of humanity.
From the legends of the Mythical Era to the histories of feudal dynasties and into more recent times, Star Martial Warriors have never been separated from the mainstream of human civilization.
In the past, awakening as a Star Martial Warrior was entirely up to destiny. But since the invention of the Soul Resonance Instrument two hundred years ago, humans have been able to use Soul Resonance Stimulation to ensure that every individual who might awaken the talent of a Star Martial Warrior would do so successfully.
The best age for undergoing Soul Resonance is between fourteen and fifteen. Therefore, every middle school student in Jade Country undergoes uniform Soul Resonance Stimulation right before graduating from junior high. Those who awaken as Star Martial Warriors are admitted into the Star Martial Arts Campus, and those without the talent continue their studies at the main campus.
Even with the aid of the Soul Resonance Instrument, the number of people who awaken as Star Martial Warriors remains scarce. Indeed, it’s rare to find even one among a hundred students.
Individuals with strong Star Martial Warrior talent generally do not wait until the Soul Resonance ritual to awaken. They usually awaken during puberty. For instance, the Ice and Snow Queen of the Star Martial Arts Campus awakened at the age of nine in her second grade.
Theoretically, Wang Lan should have awakened his Star Martial Warrior talent at the age of eight, but his talent was a bit special: he awakened a system.
Every self-aware Star Martial Warrior has a natural ability. Wang Lan’s natural ability was likely the Destiny System—and a very childish and idiotic one at that.
I’ve stuck by that assessment for years,
Wang Lan thought.
Damn it, an awakening is an awakening, so what’s with this ’assessment’? I’ve heard of others being assessed, but who assesses themselves? You’re my Star Martial Talent, like my own hands. What’s the point of slapping my own face with you?
Because of this, despite having awakened his Star Martial Warrior talent, Wang Lan had been forced to hide it for eight long years. He even failed the Soul Resonance awakening ceremony in junior high and was determined to have no Star Martial Warrior talent.
But I know my own situation,
he thought.
I simply hadn’t completed the system activation task yet.
"Lunchtime!—"
Ah, the teenage boy’s particular obsession with food. At that age, no matter how much one eats, it never seems enough to last until the next meal; the last half-hour is definitely endured in hunger.
With the ringing of the bell, all sixty-two students in the class whooshed out of the classroom. Wang Lan put down his phone, having just ordered takeout.
He had promised to treat the whole class to milk tea, and a man’s word is his bond.
"Xinyu, let’s go, time to eat," invited a sweet-looking girl, hugging Jiang Xinyu’s shoulder in the Year Two, Class One classroom at the Star Martial Arts Campus.
"No thanks, not hungry."
"Why? You scored 450, a great achievement! Second in the whole city, you’ve totally outclassed all the other second-year high school students. Why are you in a bad mood?"
"Despite thrashing all the second-year students in the city, she received a ruthless whipping from that man. Sigh, the Ice-Snow Queen has been dizzy with honor since childhood, winning awards until her hands grew weary—a well-known perfect genius. But over the past seven years, that man has whipped her over eight hundred times. He seems to have become Xinyu’s persistent shadow. After entering senior high, we in the Star Martial Class will no longer take unified exams with the ordinary classes. This was Xinyu’s last chance to challenge the academic god. But reality is cruel; there’s a ten-point gap... Once you’re above four hundred points, each additional mark is incredibly hard to achieve... Tsk tsk tsk..."
This tone was quite cheeky, sorely tempting someone to slap it right off the speaker’s face. But those who knew them understood it was just banter between close friends.
Xu Xiangwen, Gong Feiyu, and Jiang Xinyu were not only classmates but also best friends. Only amongst themselves could they jest like this. Anyone else? Come on, let’s have a spar on the battle stage.
"Xu Xiangwen, it’s fine to have a sharp tongue, but at a time like this? Aren’t you asking to be killed?" a sunny boy reminded him with a smile from behind.
"What does it matter if I’m killed? Wang Lan should be the one to die! He’s harbored thoughts of both loving and killing our Xinyu for so many years, never once giving ground. That guy’s intentions aren’t pure. He means to suppress Xinyu forever. If it were me, I couldn’t stand it. Xinyu, why don’t we go finish him off?"
"Cough, cough, cough..." The girl who had invited Jiang Xinyu to eat ran out of the classroom in a panic. Their way of talking was too frightening.
BANG! Jiang Xinyu suddenly slammed the desk forcefully, then rose and strode out of the room.
"Xinyu, where are you going?"
"To the neighboring campus!"
Xu Xiangwen turned in bewilderment. "What’s Xinyu going to the neighboring campus for?"
"Didn’t you just urge her to take care of Wang Lan? She’s headed there now. Wang Lan likes to stand on the rooftop and catch the breeze. Xinyu sneaks up behind Wang Lan, a gentle push... SPLAT! Utterly destroyed. Flawless!"
"Damn, are you mentally disturbed? You don’t think Xinyu will really go after Wang Lan, do you?"ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ
"Definitely. Who else does she know at the neighboring campus besides Wang Lan? But... I guess she might have something to say to him, like..."
Xu Xiangwen’s eyes suddenly sparkled. "The more miserable the bullying, the deeper the love; the more the trampling, the harder it is to forget. I’ve always felt that Xinyu’s feelings for Wang Lan aren’t as simple as before, heh heh heh... Shall we go together?"
"Absolutely."
"Destiny System activation complete. System starting up! Trial mission accomplished: Great Perseverance. Reward: 100 initial skill points!"
Atop the school building’s rooftop, Wang Lan looked down at the joyful and relaxed students strolling around the campus and smiled knowingly.
Normally, this relaxed atmosphere would be absolutely impossible. Jiang Province’s education system is notoriously brutal, and the pressure on high school students is a terrifying memory that those who have experienced it would not wish to revisit.
Today was the day students returned to school after the end-of-term exams. After the campus-wide cleaning in the afternoon, summer vacation would officially start. Free from the pressure of studies, with exam results already set in stone, the campus was filled with laughter and chatter during the lunch break.
Having waited eight years, Wang Lan couldn’t wait to dive into the newly activated system.
Upon opening the system, the character attribute interface came into view.
Name: Wang Lan.
Character Level: Starlight Realm Level 1.
Below were the character’s various data attributes. Most figures were between eight and nine, except for strength, which stood out at twelve.
At the very bottom was the experience bar, currently empty. In the bottom right corner was the skill point count, showing a value of one hundred. As the system had hinted, these were the initial skill points received upon system activation.
Having read countless web novels, Wang Lan immediately deduced that these skill points were likely to be a crucial item in the future, possibly fundamental to his standing and survival.
Following the character attributes page was the list of skills, which was of utmost concern to Wang Lan. For many years, never doubting that he would become a Star Martial Warrior, he had spent significant effort on grappling, physical fitness, and combat training since he was young.
Even if Wang Lan hadn’t awakened as a Star Martial Warrior, his combat ability would still likely be at the peak among ordinary people. He could easily take down a dozen unarmed opponents.
The skill page was divided into Star Martial Skills and Basic Skills, each category further split into active and passive skills. Wang Lan’s face darkened at the sight of the Star Martial Skills section.
The active skill column was empty, but the passive skill column held one passive skill: Self Healing, Black Iron LV1 (0/1).
Focusing his spiritual power on Self Healing, the skill description popped up: "Rapidly recover from physical injuries."
Is this skill any good? It seems ordinary, but it’s extremely practical. In games, it’s a Healing Skill. But this isn’t what I wanted. I’d be fine as a Mage, warrior, or assassin, but I really don’t want to be a tank! Besides, looking back through history, who ever made it big by going the heavily armored tank route? Best case, they’re called ’iron dummies’; worst case, ’iron-shelled turtles.’ And your initial skill often dictates your future path.
Why does it feel like my future is still bleak even after getting the system?
Having just awakened the system, it was normal to have no Star Martial Skill unless one came from a Star Martial family with bloodline-inherited Star Martial Skills. Most people needed to learn Star Martial Skills.
Wang Lan immediately shifted his attention to the Basic Skills page. While playing games, basic skills might be overlooked, but this wasn’t a game world; the importance of Basic Skills was no less than that of Star Martial Skills.
A saying circulated in the world of Star Martial Warriors: Star Martial Skills determine a Star Martial Warrior’s upper limit, while Basic Skills determine their lower limit. Even without Star Martial Skills, cultivating Basic Skills alone could make one a powerful Star Martial Warrior.
Extreme as this saying might be, it held some truth.
Using Star Martial Skills required consuming Star Power, which was like mana for Star Martial Warriors. Unless absolutely necessary, it was best to conserve mana. With proficient Basic Skills, one could still defeat an enemy with a single move.
Hand-to-Hand Combat, Black Iron LV8 (0/1)
Close Combat Sword Skill, Black Iron LV3 (0/1)
movement technique, Bronze LV1 (0/10)
Inch Strength Fist, Bronze LV3 (0/10)
Among the Basic Skills, two had reached Bronze level. The numbers in parentheses should be the required skill points. Seeing this, Wang Lan now confirmed the purpose of the skill points. He also understood that whether he would feast or go hungry in the future mainly depended on how he could acquire more skill points.
Advancing a Bronze level skill by one level would require ten skill points. By extension, improving a skill to Silver level would likely require a hundred points, and going from level one to ten would mean a thousand points. For a Gold level skill, it could be ten thousand...
Wow, this feels like an endless pit!
Inch Strength Fist: Active skill. A single punch unleashes triple the fist’s power.
These impressive numbers and skills were the results of Wang Lan’s seven years of cultivation. Moreover, his progress had been slow in the earlier years due to his lack of physical development; only in the last two years had his training rapidly improved.
A faint fragrance wafted to his nose, pulling Wang Lan from his contemplative state.
Unknowingly, a slender and graceful girl had appeared beside him.
"You really are here..." Her words were filled with a sense of long separation.
Since Jiang Xinyu had started attending the Star Martial Arts Campus, this was the first time in two years that Wang Lan had seen her up close. The once naive child he remembered had unknowingly grown up.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Guide to Using Skill Points
chapters.content:
Chapter 3: Chapter 3: Guide to Using Skill Points
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
Wang Lan and Jiang Xinyu had known each other from a very early age—how early? Wang Lan had seen Jiang Xinyu when she still wore split pants.
From childhood to adulthood, Jiang Xinyu’s personality had always been extremely competitive, and everyone around her complimented the naturally extraordinary and favored daughter of heaven. The only exception... was Wang Lan!
"Why are you here?" Wang Lan asked with a smile.
"You won!" Jiang Xinyu blurted out without preamble, but there was not a hint of defeat in her tone; rather, it was a declaration of victory.
"I won? What did I win?"
"You’re still so annoying, pretending not to know when you actually do. Can’t you just let me win once?" If others saw the Ice-Snow Queen Jiang Xinyu talking to a boy like this, their jaws would probably drop.
"Are you talking about the exam? You can’t seriously have been competing with me in secret all these years, can you? How boring can you get?" Wang Lan remarked sarcastically.
"You think this is boring? Boring for you?" Jiang Xinyu suddenly became a bit agitated.
"Isn’t it boring? You’re a Star Martial Warrior, and for the college entrance exam, you just need to pass the minimum threshold for the written test to be considered successful. Going to such lengths over a matter of pride? Ever heard of ’Praise be to sixty marks, any more is a waste’?"
"Heh, men."
"What do you mean?"
"Spouting that any more is a waste, and yet you? Since elementary school until now, you’ve been first place in every exam, basking in the glory of being the top student. Must feel quite vain, huh?"
"Not at all. If I weren’t forced, who would bother trying so hard? Aren’t beds cozy? Aren’t couches soft?"
"Is it because of the bet?" Jiang Xinyu asked, her cheeks slightly flushed as she lowered her head.
"No, I never make bets with people. Because of a damned trial task, I have to be first place a thousand times in a row. Is this something a human should do..." Wang Lan muttered to himself, resting his hands behind his head. "Class is about to start, gotta run!"
WHOOSH—
A gust of wind blew past, and the air suddenly got a bit colder.
Wang Lan stiffly turned his neck, only to meet a pair of cold eyes filled with murderous intent. "Have you really forgotten? Or should I say, you never cared in the first place?"
"Not good!"
Xu Xiangwen’s face changed dramatically as he shouted, quickly shutting the eye that had opened on his forehead, "Xinyu is about to make a move; she’s freaking out."
As his voice fell, two figures flashed instantaneously, rapidly heading toward the rooftop where Wang Lan was.
"Ah? Why is your temper still the same? Exploding at the slightest thing!"
HISS—
In a blur before Wang Lan’s eyes, Jiang Xinyu appeared in front of him with a trail of afterimages, grabbing his collar.
"Need me to remind you? Eight years ago, third grade..."ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
"Xinyu, don’t be rash..." A cry of alarm rose, interrupting Jiang Xinyu’s words. Xu Xiangwen and Gong Feiyu hurried onto the rooftop with panicked expressions.
"Right, Xinyu, if you’re angry, you can just break Wang Lan’s legs. Any of the three legs, just don’t actually push him off; that could kill someone."
"Damn, Gong Feiyu, are you even speaking human? Aren’t you going to save me..." Wang Lan, with half his body already over the edge of the rooftop, looked frail, helpless, and pitiable.
"What are you guys doing here?" Jiang Xinyu’s face turned cold, but she gently let go of her grip. With a slight blush on her face, she casually flicked her long hair back. "Forget it; let’s just forget it. It’s time for class."
Wang Lan patted his chest and straightened his disheveled collar.
"I’m telling you, Lan, congratulations on successfully defending your title again." Xu Xiangwen wrapped an arm around Wang Lan’s shoulder, leaning in to whisper in his ear, "Nicely done. You’ve utterly dominated her over eight hundred times; not many people can be that ruthless."
"Was it you, you bastard, fanning the flames on the side? Otherwise, why would Xinyu explode? I knew you were up to no good, trying to kill me to inherit my Q coins, right?"
"Sorry, I’m Xinyue Eight, a Purple Diamond member; your Q coins are nothing to me."
"Are we done? Shall we go? How about barbecue tonight?" Gong Feiyu suggested with a bright smile on his face.
"I’ll pass. I’ve got some things to do tonight." Wang Lan was now focused on studying the system, having awakened it along with his Star Martial Warrior talent. For the three of them, their future was likely to hold more partings than meetings, but as far as Wang Lan was concerned, there would be plenty of time.
Jiang Xinyu’s behavior had indeed been abnormal today. Wang Lan propped his chin and pondered. It had been a long time since he’d seen Jiang Xinyu in person, aside from online contacts. In reality, Wang Lan was busy studying and practicing problems, while Jiang Xinyu was busy with her cultivation.
Even their recent online chats had been just a few simple greetings, and he couldn’t remember doing anything to offend this woman, whose temper seemed to grow with her age.
Why was she so... agitated today?
Suddenly, Wang Lan shuddered.
Eight years ago, third grade?
That time, Wang Lan and Jiang Xinyu tied for first place. Even with the same scores, both being first, Jiang Xinyu insisted on being ranked above Wang Lan.
Could I agree to that? If I did, what about my trial task?
In the midst of their argument, the two seemed to have made some kind of bet...
"Wang Lan, you annoying man, I, Jiang Xinyu, swear that I will do better than you in the next exam."
"Good luck, I believe in you."
"Waaah, I’m so mad! If I can’t beat you, I’ll... I’ll... I’ll jump off from here!"
"Why such dark thoughts at such a young age? How about this—if I win, you become my wife when you grow up, how does that sound?"
"And if I win?"
"I’ll be your husband."
"Deal! It’s settled!"
Wang Lan had known Jiang Xinyu from a very young age and knew this girl could be impulsive when excited. She was also incredibly stubborn. The more you tried to talk her out of something, the more determined she became. If she said she’d jump, she might really do it.
After all, they were just kids, and Wang Lan had treated it as a joke and soon forgot about it. Besides, Wang Lan remembered the initial bet was for the *next* exam, and since then, they’d had, if not a thousand, at least over eight hundred exams.
This girl’s persistence is no longer just persistence. It’s become an obsession,
Wang Lan chuckled and shook his head.
And with Jiang Xinyu’s intelligence, couldn’t she tell it was just childish banter? Who in the world would take a ten-year-old’s bet seriously? Maybe she wasn’t talking about that time... I’ll have to think about it more.
Since it was the last day, there was only one class in the afternoon. It wasn’t really a class, just the handing out of summer homework. There were some assignments from the teachers, and also the ’gifts’ prepared for the students by Extinction Master.
As expected: five years’ worth of college entrance exam questions, three years of mock tests, and analyses of various commonly mistaken problems... Analysis, my foot!
When faced with a stack of homework even heftier than the one at the start of school, the students of Class One fell into despair. Some even stared at the foot-thick pile of assignments, muttering to themselves.
"Mad... Extinction Master is mad, Lan is mad... everyone’s mad..."
With his backpack in tow, Wang Lan hopped on the bus and went straight home.
In the business center of Suzhou City, Wang Lan owned three office buildings, each over thirty stories high. Before his mother’s disappearance, she had handed them over to professional managers to handle. No need for business operations, just renting them out for the rent income.
Wang Lan’s home was in the Xinyu Building, on the top floor in a flat of five hundred square meters. There was a private elevator that went straight up and down, operated by a fingerprint lock that only Wang Lan could use.
The parking garage was split into three levels. The first and second were public, but the third had been converted into a training area. The walls were lined with PS armor. When powered, this armor could create a strong magnetic field, rendering ordinary weapons unable to even scratch it unless its power source was exhausted.
Wang Lan lay on a chair in the training area, his thoughts sinking into his Spiritual Sea of Consciousness. First, he had a hundred skill points, and secondly, he had a Star Martial Skill called Self Healing.
Usually, when Awakening a Star Martial Skill for the first time, one’s overall attributes would be enhanced. The weaker the foundation, the more pronounced the enhancement. However, Wang Lan’s foundation was not weak. His attributes had already reached a high level even before activating the system.
As for how much enhancement, that required actual measurement.
Wang Lan approached the strength-testing machine, took a deep breath, and threw a lightning-fast punch.
BOOM—
"Two hundred kilograms."
A look of joy appeared on Wang Lan’s face. His previous maximum punch force had been only one hundred and fifty kilograms. In other words, after awakening as a Star Martial Warrior, his punch force had surged by a quarter.
Wang Lan took another deep breath and, employing the Mana-channelling technique of Inch Strength Fist, threw another punch at the target.
BOOM— A loud noise erupted.
"Seven hundred kilograms."
Wang Lan was overjoyed. Previously, his Inch Strength Fist could only produce a maximum force of four hundred kilograms. Seven hundred kilograms was beyond the lethal force of an average person. Aside from a few naturally gifted individuals capable of delivering attacks of over six hundred kilograms, for a normal person, three hundred was the limit.
That a sixteen-year-old with a slim figure like Wang Lan could produce a punch force of seven hundred kilograms demonstrated the physical quality of Star Martial Warriors.
Furthermore, the advanced combat power of Star Martial Warriors came from Star Martial Skills, and the Inch Strength Fist Wang Lan just used was merely a Basic Skill. With a Basic Skill’s power already surpassing that of most of his peers in the Star Martial Class, Wang Lan’s baseline was stronger.
But the next experiment was key. Inch Strength Fist was the skill Wang Lan focused on cultivating. It was currently at the Bronze 3 tier, and leveling it to Bronze 4 required ten points. Without hesitation, Wang Lan allocated skill points to Inch Strength Fist.
After adding ten points, the original Bronze 3 became Bronze 4. Following the skill upgrade, Wang Lan clearly felt his muscles seemed more flexible, allowing him to control his strength more smoothly than before.
"Ha!"
He punched again, making the strength-testing machine boom.
BOOM—
"Eight hundred kilograms—"
Wang Lan’s body shook, his eyes filled with astonishment. Eight hundred kilograms—a whole one hundred kilograms more than before! To a Star Martial Warrior, this increase might seem tiny, almost negligible. However, the truly astonishing part was that Wang Lan had achieved this leap from seven hundred to eight hundred kilograms in just a few seconds. If he had relied on his own cultivation, not to mention how long it would take, just reaching eight hundred kilograms, constrained by his physical development, would have taken at least a year.
"I’ve struck it rich, truly struck it rich... Ten skill points, a matter of seconds, and I’ve saved a year of hard cultivation. Skill points, indeed the cornerstone of my cheating life."
"As long as I have enough skill points, who the hell needs to race on the track? I’m going to fly!"
Wang Lan suppressed the urge to put all his skill points into Inch Strength Fist. As a studious genius, he couldn’t let go of his intelligence just because he had acquired strength.
Intelligence is a valuable asset; I can’t just toss it aside.
Skill points are precious. Figuring out how to maximize their benefit requires careful allocation.
It takes ten skill points for a Black Iron skill to advance to Bronze. Ten points are just enough for a Bronze skill to level up one tier, but they’re enough to raise a Black Iron skill by one quality level. If I relied on cultivation alone, upgrading from Black Iron to Bronze would take at least three years. This is the most cost-effective investment.
My Unarmed Combat is at Black Iron 8. I’ll add two points to upgrade it to Bronze 1.
Suddenly, there was a moment of confusion in Wang Lan’s eyes, and then he became clear-headed again.

chapters.title: Chapter 4 Ultimate Evolution of Self Healing - Undying Body?
chapters.content:
Chapter 4: Chapter 4 Ultimate Evolution of Self Healing - Undying Body?
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
That feeling was quite marvelous, akin to an epiphany as described in martial arts novels. It was as if things that were once incomprehensible suddenly became clear in an instant.
The most important aspect of unarmed combat is not the mind, but the body. No level of intellect or speed of reaction can compare to the body’s natural response. In addition to a deeper understanding and mastery of combat, Wang Lan’s mind overflowed with numerous moves he had not known before.
This is... impressive.
He then applied skill points to the Close Combat Sword Skill, elevating it to the Bronze level as well.
In the past, Wang Lan expended the least effort on his sword skill. His private coach had also advised that the true essence of Close Combat Sword Skill, which was practical in real combat, couldn’t be fully imparted to Wang Lan. If Wang Lan were to actually kill someone in combat, he himself would be executed.
Since Wang Lan couldn’t learn the essence of a combat skill, he naturally wouldn’t invest much effort in it. However, sword skill was an essential skill for Star Martial Warriors, with nearly ninety percent of them wielding swords.
Why? Because swords are simple, practical, and quick to learn.
How great is a jian? It has versatile moves and exquisite actions. Once mastered, its lethality is remarkable. But for most Star Martial Warriors, survival on the battlefield is key—what use is elegance if you can’t save your own life?
With a sword in hand, you just slash away.
So although Wang Lan knew that learning the sword was of little use before awakening as a Star Martial Warrior, he still had to learn it. But now, with a few skill points allocated, Wang Lan’s sword skill instantly surpassed the beginner stage and reached proficiency.
Even without having tested the technique with an actual sword, Wang Lan just felt it. A swordsman doesn’t need to hold a sword all day to be aware of their own strength.
Compared to Basic Skills, Star Martial Skills are the foundation of a Star Martial Warrior.
The only Star Martial Skill Wang Lan had after awakening was one passive ability—a real stark naked start. He remembered when Jiang Xinyu awoke, a sneeze had frozen the cola in her hand, straw and all.
As for myself, I would have settled for an active skill, but what the hell, I got Self Healing. Am I supposed to be some kind of punching bag?
Despite his internal disdain, Wang Lan still allocated ten points to Self Healing, which elevated the skill to Bronze LV1. But just as the skill briefly shimmered, it suddenly disappeared.
Wang Lan jumped in shock at this scene until he looked up and saw that the Self Healing skill had turned into an active skill, which finally allowed him to breathe a sigh of relief.
Wait, passive skills can become active skills? Isn’t that different from game settings?
Wang Lan concentrated his spiritual power on the new Bronze skill: "Consume Star Power to recover from injuries."
The description was still simple and straightforward.
Why would a passive skill become an active skill?
Wang Lan didn’t ponder this for long. When one first awakens as a Star Martial Warrior, they often cannot control their Innate Ability at first.
Just like when Jiang Xinyu first awoke, a sneeze had frozen Wang Lan’s cola.
Was she trying to attack me?
It was purely a lack of control.
For Jiang Xinyu at that time, wasn’t it effectively a passive ability?
With this realization, Wang Lan felt relieved.
This Self Healing is probably not as ordinary as I thought. As a man who prefers taking the initiative, the last thing I can accept is being passive.
No sooner had Wang Lan thought this than he acted upon it, grabbing a dagger from the weapon rack and lightly cutting his arm. At first, a dark red line appeared, followed by a slow seeping of blood.
He quickly channeled his Star Power to activate the Self Healing skill and stared unblinking at the wound—one second, two seconds, three seconds.
After five seconds, the wound completely healed.
Under normal circumstances, a wound heals by first scabbing over, and then the scab falls off. However, with the Self Healing skill, the wound didn’t even form a scab; it soon looked as smooth and flawless as new, without a trace remaining.
The cut was small, so it healed quickly and didn’t consume much Star Power—probably only about one-tenth or so.
And this is just Bronze LV1 Self Healing. If I upgrade the skill to Silver, or even Gold later on...
Wang Lan suddenly felt elated.
This is awesome!
The more he had disdained it before, the more he found it delectable now. Anyone else with the Self Healing skill could only hope to be a meat shield, but Wang Lan was a man with a system. As long as he had enough skill points, he could upgrade the skill indefinitely by just pouring points into it.
In due time, I’ll become Wolverine... no wait, Wolverine is trash. I must be Deadpool... also trash. I’ll be the Goddess of Death, a true Undying Body!
Self Healing equals Undying Body. This might not work for others, but for me, it’s possible! However, this process might take a long while. Before I become a true Undying Body, I need to lay low and survive.
In high spirits, Wang Lan took out his phone and dialed a number. "Master Huang, are you free right now?"
Master Huang, whose name was Huang Feilong, was Wang Lan’s personal trainer and a Star Martial Warrior of the Star Shine Stage.
There were clear divisions in the levels of Star Martial Warriors. By invoking Star Power to Open Star Palace, one could clearly and intuitively see their level. Newly awakened Star Martial Warriors were at the Starlight Stage, where a single star in the Star Palace was like a star in the sky.
The next level up was Star Shine, where the stars in the Star Palace were as bright and dazzling as the sun and moon. Above that were Star Cloud, Galaxy, and Star Sea.
As for what realm lies beyond that, I have no idea.
As far as is known, the Star Sea Stage is already the pinnacle of combat power among Star Martial Warriors. But Wang Lan, deeply influenced by web novels, was entirely certain
there must be a whole new realm above Star Sea!
A Star Shine Stage Star Martial Warrior willing to be hired by an ordinary person as a private coach? Those who don’t understand might say Huang Feilong is degrading himself for money, abandoning the honor of a Star Martial Warrior.
But for most Star Martial Warriors who are stuck in the middle tier and have no chance of ascending to higher levels in their lifetime, this is a coveted job that turns eyes green with envy.
Star Martial Warriors need to eat too. And not just eat; their food intake is several times that of an ordinary person. Just ask around in Suzhou City—which brave soul dares let a Star Martial Warrior into their all-you-can-eat buffet?
During the imperial era, the status of Star Martial Warriors fluctuated, but most were held in higher regard than ordinary people. Since Jade Country ended the imperial era two hundred years ago, the promoted tenet has been national unity and equality among citizens, with no one permitted to lord over others.
It’s an obvious truth that human civilization is like a machine, with each person within civilization being a part of that machine. The mission of Star Martial Warriors is to protect civilization from harm by external threats.
Protection is both a responsibility and a mission. If even Star Martial Warriors were to lord it over the people and act tyrannically, when humanity faces external threats, could anyone still expect them to risk their lives for protection?
Star Martial Warriors receive a state stipend and benefits, but absolutely no special privileges. The benefits and stipends are completely linked to strength. In the hierarchy of Star Martial Warrior groups, Starlight is at the bottom, and Star Shine is only slightly higher. The state stipend alone is not enough to feed them.
Then why not get a job? With the immense strength of Star Martial Warriors, they could earn money doing anything, right?
Indeed, they can make money, but not a lot of it. Star Martial Warriors are strong, but docks have cranes and forklifts. Star Martial Warriors are quick, but factories have robots on the assembly lines.
Compared to ordinary citizens, Star Martial Warriors have no advantage in the workplace. They lack the education and skills. And even if they did the same work as ordinary people, the income would not be sufficient to sustain a Star Martial Warrior’s livelihood.
An ordinary person can live on 7,000 or 8,000 yuan a month, even afford to go singing and buy clothes. But for a Star Martial Warrior, a monthly food budget under 10,000 yuan can only be described as barely staving off hunger and cold.
Therefore, for many Star Martial Warriors, there are only two prospects: the military or the Pioneering Legion.
But the existence of a Star Martial Warrior is extremely cruel; it’s survival of the fittest, where the great waves wash away the sand. It’s considered lucky for the weak to retreat in one piece, especially for someone like Huang Feilong, who is nearly forty and whose strength is stuck at the Star Shine Stage.ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
They can either become someone’s bodyguard or work as a private coach. Clearly, working as a private coach is somewhat more dignified. After all, coaches are addressed as Master or Teacher.
Huang Feilong was Wang Lan’s full-time private coach, but Wang Lan knew he coached at least five other people and also ran a small martial arts gym, charging tuition to teach students.
Juggling so many jobs still meant they had to be scheduled around Wang Lan’s commitments, as these side hustles could only be undertaken with Wang Lan’s permission. If Wang Lan didn’t allow it, Huang Feilong would either have to give up his 70,000 monthly salary and resign or dedicate himself entirely to being Wang Lan’s private coach.
A 70,000 monthly salary could afford a Star Martial Warrior a comfortable life.
That’s why to Wang Lan, Huang Feilong was always on call. Even if it meant leaving his wife at the most intimate moments, he would often just pull up his pants and leave without a second thought.
In less than half an hour, Huang Feilong’s car arrived at the third level of the underground parking lot, and he came walking over, shirtless.
Huang Feilong’s body bore many scars from blade wounds, remnants from his days in the Pioneering Legion. Scars on an ordinary man might mark him as a despicable villain, detested by women, but on a Star Martial Warrior, they were heroic badges of honor in the eyes of women.
And to have survived with so many scars yet remain physically whole, one had to be a battle-hardened veteran. Who would dare call him weak? Who would dare call him a coward? Go on, take off your shirt! If you could bear that many scars and not die, you’d earn respect as a true man too!
"Mr. Lan, why so early today?"
"Summer vacation starts tomorrow..." Wang Lan replied. He never carried the air of a rich scion, always speaking to others in a polite and approachable manner. This was also why Huang Feilong cherished this job so much.
Generous, easy to talk to, and he even lets me take on side jobs. Where else could I find such a good boss?
"So, Mr. Lan, what kind of training do you have planned for today?"
"Let’s start with free sparring," Wang Lan said, removing his outer clothes to reveal the tight-fitting, stretch short-sleeve shirt underneath.
"I’m not wearing protective gear today; it hampers movement."
"Alright!" Huang Feilong was not one to be polite, hopping onto the ring with a smile. He stood with one hand behind his back and the other in front, signaling Wang Lan to begin.
That starting pose is a bit too flashy, and I’ve been annoyed by it for ages. But alas, even if he fought me with one hand, I still couldn’t beat him. Showboating only counts if you have the strength to back it up. So, even though I’ve been irked for a long time, I can only endure it.
Wang Lan’s movement technique had reached the Bronze level, an improvement from a sudden epiphany during a previous sparring session.
What was it Master Huang said back then? ’Mr. Lan, your evasive footwork has reached a proficient level; all those punches weren’t taken for nothing!’
Just listen to that. Enough to make you cry, right?
And now, I don’t just want to dodge punches and kicks; I want to attack!
Without any probing, Wang Lan rushed straight at Huang Feilong. This change from his usual style surprised Huang Feilong for a moment. Wang Lan threw a punch aimed straight at Huang Feilong’s center, but Huang Feilong unhurriedly blocked it and then countered with a kick towards Wang Lan’s chest.

chapters.title: Chapter 5 Master Huang, I Can’t Hold on Much Longer
chapters.content:
Chapter 5: Chapter 5 Master Huang, I Can’t Hold on Much Longer
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
As Wang Lan’s dedicated coach, it was essential to have a detailed understanding of his abilities. Not only did Huang Feilong need to be intimately knowledgeable about them, but he also had to clearly recognize Wang Lan’s advantages and shortcomings to devise specialized training accordingly.
So, based on Huang Feilong’s judgment, this kick should have struck Wang Lan’s chest and sent him flying. Of course, the force had to be controlled, just like in martial arts movies where kicks look fierce but don’t land with full power.
But in the next instant, Huang Feilong suddenly felt his foot kicking into thin air. Startled, he caught a glimpse from the corner of his eye of Wang Lan inverted, supporting himself on the ground with one hand.
A thought exploded in Huang Feilong’s mind.
Damn it!
Wang Lan’s foot, coming from below, fiercely kicked upward at Huang Feilong’s chin, sending him flying into the air.
THUD—
A dull sound echoed as Huang Feilong fell backward onto the ground, thoroughly dazed.
Of course, an ordinary person would have been severely injured by such a blow, but for Huang Feilong, a Star Martial Warrior, there wasn’t much of a problem other than a bit of pain in his chin and a somewhat numb tongue from biting it.
Wang Lan approached Huang Feilong and helped him up.
"Mmh mmh mmh mmh..." Huang Feilong’s tongue was somewhat unresponsive. Although he was attempting to speak, Wang Lan couldn’t make out the words clearly.
"Master Huang, are you sure you’re a Star Shine Stage Star Martial Warrior?" Wang Lan asked with a hint of skepticism.
"Of courth I’m thure!"
"I’m only at the Starlight Stage and I took you down. You weren’t just bluffing me before, were you?"
"That’th becauth I underethtimated you... With your combat level from the day before yethterday, you definitely couldn’t have made that move... The way you dodged, counterattacked, and executed your moveth wath extremely fluid and impeccable... Have you had an epiphany in the latht two dayth? Wait, what did you jutht thay?"
"Me? I asked if you were bluffing me before."
"No, the thententh before that!"
"You, a Star Shine Stage warrior, were taken down by me, a Starlight Stage warrior?"
"You’re Starlight Stage? When did you reach Starlight Stage?"
"Just today."
"Come on, Open Star Palace for me to see..."
Wang Lan trusted Huang Feilong a great deal; the man was straightforward and had been teaching Wang Lan for five years. Besides, opening the Star Palace was the most direct proof of being a Star Martial Warrior, and it wasn’t something they typically concealed.
Opening the Star Palace came as naturally to a Star Martial Warrior as instinct; no learning was required. Wang Lan summoned the Star Power within his entire body, causing it to surge and circulate powerfully. Waves of shimmering light immediately radiated around him.
Above his head, within a flickering void ripple, a radiant star, like a gemstone, was embedded.
Watching this scene, Huang Feilong was anything but calm. "Mr. Lan? You’re sixteen years old?"
"Mm."
"Two years ago, you underwent Soul Resonance Stimulation, right? Even that couldn’t awaken your Star Martial Warrior talent, yet now you’ve managed to awaken it on your own?"
"Ah, what about it? Awakening is just awakening; there’s no need to be surprised. But you, shouldn’t you be adjusting my training plan now?"
’No need to be surprised?’ That’s too stiff an act, thumbs down!
Huang Feilong roared internally.
Soul Resonance Stimulation was scientifically certified to help 99.8% of those with Star Martial Warrior talent to successfully awaken, with the remaining 0.2% existing only to prevent arrogance from a perfect score. For those whose Star Martial Warrior talent couldn’t be awakened even by Soul Resonance, it was generally considered that they possessed no such talent at all.
Since the advent of the Soul Resonance Instrument, there was no precedent of anyone awakening later if they had undergone Soul Resonance without success. Even a hundred attempts would be futile.
Truly talented individuals don’t need Soul Resonance assistance; they usually awaken on their own before the age of thirteen. Those who awaken through Soul Resonance tend to have relatively mediocre aptitude. But what in the world is this situation? Soul Resonance couldn’t make him awaken, yet damn it, he actually bloomed like an iron tree flowering?
"To be able to awaken on your own at sixteen? Such demonic talent would certainly make the news, wouldn’t it? ’No need to be surprised?’ I might not be surprised, but the folks at the Star Martial Research Science Institute should be thrilled to invite you to join their research. Your existence proves that Soul Resonance Awakening isn’t infallible and might even lead to a second method of awakening being discovered through you, possibly even achieving mass awakening for everyone. Heh heh heh..."
Wang Lan shuddered. "Don’t scare me. Our scientists are humane, after all."
"Hmm, but sacrificing one person for the everlasting benefit of human civilization would be worth it," Huang Feilong said with a sly smile. Seeing he had genuinely frightened Wang Lan, he clapped his hands. "Alright, I won’t tease you anymore. Although your case is special, it’s not enough to shake the foundations of science; they won’t do anything to you. Since you’ve successfully awakened, it’s time for me to adjust your training. Come, let’s have a real Star Martial Warrior fight."
The two stood five meters apart and bowed with clasped fists.
"Master Huang, please guide me!"
"Mr. Lan, please guide me!"
SWISH! Both figures moved simultaneously. As soon as they engaged, fists and feet flew, their movements too fast to see clearly. If captured with a high-speed camera and slowed down three times, one could perhaps make out each move and counter in their exchange.
Huang Feilong’s combat skills were quite solid; otherwise, Wang Lan wouldn’t have chosen him as a personal coach. Being kicked into the air by Wang Lan earlier was due to his momentary lapse in concentration, coupled with Wang Lan’s free combat skills upgrading from Black Iron to Bronze.
Bronze-level skills were professional-grade. Reaching this level meant one had moved beyond the learning phase; further progress could only come through practice and enlightenment. After sparring quickly for two minutes, Huang Feilong suddenly accelerated his movements, and his power climbed another notch.
BOOM—
Wang Lan’s defense was broken open by Huang Feilong with a single Bagua Chop, leaving his chest exposed. Huang Feilong pressed forward, sending Wang Lan flying backward with a palm strike.
Wang Lan crashed into the railing of the arena, beads of sweat dripping down his forehead. He took a few deep breaths, climbed down from the railing, and said, "The gap between Master Huang and myself is still so apparent."
"Mr. Lan, I don’t know if it’s because the amplification from your awakening as a Star Martial Warrior was too great or because you experienced an epiphany, but your combat ability has indeed reached an advanced level. I dare say that even those so-called geniuses who have undergone strict training from a young age and became Star Martial Warriors many years before you might not possess a higher level of combat ability."
"Is that so?" Wang Lan’s face remained calm, not showing the joy typical of a young person receiving praise.
Seeing Wang Lan’s lack of expression, Huang Feilong thought he didn’t care and his face became serious.
"Of course. Although you were an ordinary person before, your training has always followed the standards for a Star Martial Warrior. I don’t know how high your talent is, Mr. Lan, or what Star Martial Skill you’ve awakened. But I’ve told you more than once that talent and Star Martial Skills can only determine how far a Star Martial Warrior can go in the future, whereas Basic Skills are what absolutely determine the minimum distance a Star Martial Warrior can travel. In the world of Star Martial Warriors, especially before reaching the Galaxy Stage, Basic Skills remain the primary means of combat. Fighting techniques, sword skills, movement techniques, strength, and endurance are the fundamentals for a Star Martial Warrior to survive on the battlefield. Mastering Basic Skills doesn’t guarantee becoming a powerful Star Martial Warrior, but a powerful Star Martial Warrior must have mastered Basic Skills. You must not underestimate Basic Skills just because you’ve awakened your Star Martial Warrior talent."
"I understand," Wang Lan nodded. "But Master Huang, what is the most important among the Basic Skills?"
"Naturally, it’s the martial techniques for killing enemies. Star Martial Warriors are not for show; they fight against Exotic Beasts and, when necessary, against their own kind. Hand-to-hand combat is important, but it’s too inefficient for killing. Among the martial techniques for killing, the sword is the most practical."
Indeed! What used to be the most meaningless skill for Wang Lan immediately became the most important after becoming a Star Martial Warrior. Fortunately, he had already improved his sword skill to the Bronze level; his strength in it should be no less than his free combat ability, right?
"Then let’s practice sword skills."
Wang Lan took down two training swords from the rack. Their weight and style were exactly like real swords; the only difference was that these swords hurt when they struck but couldn’t kill.
Huang Feilong secretly felt relieved. It was a good thing Mr. Lan hadn’t focused much on learning sword skills before; his skill level was still lacking in many areas. Otherwise, I would really have nothing left to teach Mr. Lan. Although it would be an honor for me if Mr. Lan distinguished himself in the future thanks to my teachings... seventy thousand a month... If I have nothing left to teach, wouldn’t I be out of a job? In a moment, I must use all my strength, determine the winner with a single decisive exchange, and show Mr. Lan that I still have true skills that will take him years to learn.
With this thought, Huang Feilong gripped his sword tightly. "Mr. Lan, come at me."
"Alright!"
Sword skills are straightforward: it’s all about chopping motions. The so-called hacking, slashing, upward strokes, and paring are just ways to utilize the blade’s edge. This differs from techniques for a double-edged straight sword, where thrusting is the primary attack. In a direct confrontation between this type of sword and a double-edged straight sword, the latter absolutely cannot meet this sword head-on. This sword generates significant force in a swing; using a double-edged straight sword to block such a swing would shatter it in minutes.
Wang Lan charged at Huang Feilong with large strides, slashing downward at a forty-five-degree angle—a most common opening move for sword users. It’s hard to judge skill from the first move; good sword use lies in the subsequent responses.
If Huang Feilong were to simply block this blow with his sword, it wouldn’t demonstrate any particular skill. Therefore, Huang Feilong instantly reversed his grip and sliced towards Wang Lan’s wrist. If Wang Lan continued his downward slash, his entire hand would have been struck.
However, since the swords were practice weapons, there was no fear of truly severing Wang Lan’s hand, though it would certainly hurt quite a bit.
But in an instant, Wang Lan changed his move. Although his sword still came slashing down, it rotated ninety degrees nimbly in his hand and thrust straight towards Huang Feilong’s wrist.
What the—
Huang Feilong’s heart skipped a beat, and he hastily changed his own move.Nᴇw novel chapters are publɪshed on Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
CLANG— The two swords collided with a crisp sound.
CLATTER CLATTER CLANG—
In a blink, sword light burst forth from Wang Lan’s hands. The hacking, slashing, upward strokes, and paring unfolded from his hands like blooming fireworks, each strike aggressive, sharp, and impeccably executed, leaving no openings.
At least in Huang Feilong’s eyes, Wang Lan’s adaptations were able to keep pace with his rhythm.
He’s a demon of talent!
Huang Feilong parried Wang Lan’s sharp onslaughts calmly, but his heart was utterly shocked.
He had taught all of Mr. Lan’s combat skills; he knew perfectly well what level Wang Lan was at. Wang Lan absolutely did not possess such proficiency in sword skills before. But then...
Suddenly, Huang Feilong felt his position was seriously challenged. Wang Lan had learned sword skills from someone else—it must be... Damn it, what scoundrel dares to poach from me? They have no sense of professional courtesy at all!
With that thought, Huang Feilong couldn’t afford to hold back any longer. He unleashed his trump card skills at once. His killing intent, complemented by sharp sword techniques, instantly suppressed Wang Lan’s attack and launched a counteroffensive.
CLANG CLANG CLANG—
CRACK—
With a crisp sound, the swords in their hands suddenly snapped.
Fake was fake, after all. Under the intensity of their genuine fight, the blades ultimately couldn’t withstand the stress and fractured.
The two men looked at each other, panting. The five minutes of intense engagement had been a spectacular display of sword skill combat. There were no tactics, no give-and-take; both were aggressively attacking in a fierce head-on clash.
Wang Lan fought with exhilarating vigor, while Huang Feilong was on tenterhooks.
The one who taught Wang Lan his sword skills is the real deal! Not just for show, but genuinely skilled.
"Master Huang is truly deserving of his reputation, formidable! If it weren’t for the swords giving out, I was about to give out..."

chapters.title: Chapter 6: I Have Nothing Left to Teach You.
chapters.content:
Chapter 6: Chapter 6: I Have Nothing Left to Teach You.
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
"I... I can’t hold on... much longer..." Wang Lan gasped, his voice trailing off, "...can’t... not holding... held on..."
These fragmented words from Wang Lan sent Huang Feilong’s mind into disarray.
I’m a Star Shine Stage Star Martial Warrior, and he, a Starlight Stage Star Martial Warrior who only awakened today, fought me face-to-face for five minutes. We even broke his sword without determining a victor, and *I’m* the one who needs comforting? Is this his idea of comforting me? Is he just trying to save my face? Me...
"Mr. Lan, have you found another master?"
"Ah? No, I haven’t!"
"No? I don’t recall giving you many lessons in sword skill, do I? I mostly just explained the techniques of using a sword and focused primarily on teaching movement technique and the power generation for Inch Strength."
Yes, I did secretly practice,
Wang Lan thought.
It only took a few good seconds to add those points, after all.
"Impossible. Combat skills aren’t some flashy performance for others to watch. You can’t learn true skills by training alone; someone must spar with you to provide practical experience. You don’t need to lie to me. If that other person is skilled, I don’t mind if you learn the real deal from them, as long as you learn it."
"Really, I haven’t!" Wang Lan said softly, wiping sweat from his brow. "Every time I practice, I visualize someone attacking me with a sword, and I counterattack that image in my mind. Over time, I just naturally developed this way."
"Meditation training?" Huang Feilong looked at Wang Lan, his face etched with shock. "You actually managed to do meditation training? No wonder... no wonder... Mr. Lan, it is my great fortune, spanning three lifetimes, to have been your enlightening teacher."
"Please don’t say that, Master Huang! Master Huang, could you give me some advice on which aspects of my sword skill I should improve?"
Huang Feilong smiled and shook his head. "Your progress in sword skill is already beyond what I can guide. I’m just a Star Shine Stage Star Martial Warrior, which is considered bottom-tier in the world of Star Martial Warriors. Mr. Lan, you’ve grown so much that I have nothing more to teach you. Your future should be even more magnificent. Today should be my last lesson with you."
"Why? I don’t intend to cancel our agreement."
"I know," Huang Feilong said. "But I take Mr. Lan’s money to teach you skills. If I can’t teach you anything new, I shouldn’t be taking your money; that’s my bottom line.
"However, before that, Mr. Lan, you still lack one crucial thing. This must be mastered before you step onto a battlefield. I have seen many individuals with exceptional talent, even young geniuses with strength no less than mine, who died at the hands of Exotic Beasts in a single round during their first battle."
"What is it?" Wang Lan asked earnestly.
"Overcoming the fear of death!"
"The battlefield of Star Martial Warriors is a true life-and-death arena. When facing fierce and terrifying Exotic Beasts, some warriors become so terrified their minds go blank. All the skills they’ve learned are utterly forgotten. They are killed by the Exotic Beasts without even managing to resist. Therefore, Mr. Lan, you must conquer the fear of death before truly going into battle. Come, let’s use real weapons."
Huang Feilong took down two real combat blades from the weapons rack—the kind that had been sharpened.
"Catch!"
Wang Lan caught the combat blade, his hand gripping the hilt, which trembled slightly. He wasn’t just nervous; there was also a thrill of excitement. He understood the need to overcome the fear of death; facing someone rushing at you with a real blade felt entirely different from a fake one.
"Are you ready?"
"Ready!"
A fierce killing intent suddenly erupted from Huang Feilong as he charged at Wang Lan like a ferocious beast. Although Wang Lan didn’t panic to the extent Huang Feilong described in his example, his mindset indeed grew much heavier.
CLANG! CLANG! CLANG—
After seven or eight exchanges, Wang Lan’s mind descended into chaos, his vision filled only with the flashing glint of the blade.
A sharp sting pricked his skin as Huang Feilong’s blade stopped just inches from Wang Lan.
"When using a fake blade, you could engage me in close combat for five minutes. But once we switched to real blades, you could only parry twelve of my strikes. Do you realize how vast the difference is?"
"I understand..." Wang Lan swallowed, silently cursing his own inadequacy.
"Your mind must be steady. Only when your mind is steady will your thoughts not be thrown into chaos."
"Again!" Wang Lan shouted.
"Not today," Huang Feilong said, pointing to Wang Lan’s arm where a small cut had appeared. "You’ve been injured. Such a wound is nothing to a Star Martial Warrior; it’ll heal in two days. We’ll train again next time. You’re young, and you have plenty of time to overcome this."
Huang Feilong couldn’t help but give himself a mental thumbs-up.
Brilliant! This way, the lessons, three times a week, can probably continue for another semester!
"No need. This wound is nothing at all."
"Of course, on the battlefield, you wouldn’t worry about such minor injuries, but there’s no need to train while injured..."
Suddenly, Huang Feilong’s words caught in his throat, his eyes bulging wide.
What did I just see?
Wang Lan’s wound was healing at a visible rate, disappearing entirely in just ten seconds! This gash was much larger than the one Wang Lan had inflicted on himself earlier, which was why it took a full ten seconds to heal.Google seaʀᴄh ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
But to Huang Feilong, that was a Medical Attribute Star Martial Skill! Could it be that Wang Lan had awakened a rare Medical Attribute talent?
What did a Medical Attribute talent signify? It meant you were a giant panda, a national treasure! Even if your combat strength was pathetic, even if you were unskilled in everything else, as long as you could heal, a legion of Star Martial Warriors would protect you. Only by protecting you well could they live longer and sustain their combat endurance.
Among ten Star Martial Warriors, you might not find even one with an Auxiliary Department talent. And among ten of those with Auxiliary Department talents, you might not find even one with a Medical Attribute. A Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior, even with mediocre aptitude, could still be specially recruited into major prestigious academies for the finest training.
At that moment, Huang Feilong felt a sharp pang of envy.
"You’re... you’re actually a Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior?"
"No, my Talented Skill is Self Healing. It only allows me to recover from my own injuries."
"Bullshit!" Huang Feilong’s mouth twitched. "A Medical Attribute is a Medical Attribute. If you can heal yourself, you’ll eventually be able to heal others. You’ve only just awakened. It’s not strange for many Medical Attribute Star Martial Warriors to only be able to heal themselves in the initial stages. But as you become more proficient with your Talented Skills and learn Star Martial Skills that can treat others, you’ll be a Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior."
"Alright, Master Huang, let’s go again."
"You’re a Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior, so why are you still trying to train like this? Do you still want to lead the charge into battle? Forget it! From now on, just stay safely in the rear. When wounded warriors are brought back from the front, you’ll be responsible for treating them. Don’t worry, you’ll be a precious treasure that every Pioneer Team will be desperate to recruit."
"Even if I really am just a healer, I also have the heart of a warrior. If I don’t conquer my fear of death, I can’t take the first step as a Star Martial Warrior. You told me that."
I really don’t understand the world of the rich,
Huang Feilong sighed, shaking his head.
He could clearly rely on talent, yet he insists on relying on hard work.
"Fine, let’s continue!"From three in the afternoon until six, Wang Lan was repeatedly injured and then healed himself through their combat.
Knowing that Wang Lan could heal himself, Huang Feilong abandoned his initial cautious approach. His sword techniques became increasingly sharp, his angles of attack more cunning and unpredictable.
His only goal was to force Wang Lan to face the specter of death again and again, until he could calmly confront and overcome its terror.
For an average person, three hours of such training might only yield initial results. Unfortunately for Huang Feilong, he was dealing with someone far from average. Perhaps it was his Self Healing ability that gave Wang Lan courage, or perhaps Wang Lan genuinely possessed an innate talent for psychological resilience.
After Huang Feilong finished the session, he formally announced Wang Lan’s graduation. This time, there was truly nothing more he could teach him. The fear of death still had some influence, but it was no longer significant. He would have plenty of time to get used to it on the battlefield in the future.
"Mr. Lan," Huang Feilong began, "I find it somewhat hard to part with you so suddenly. However, my abilities are limited; I can only provide you with introductory guidance. As for how you’ll walk your path in the future, as someone who has been there, I have only one piece of advice for you.
"Seize every chance and opportunity to grow stronger. Forget what I said about Medical Attribute Star Martial Warriors being able to relax in others’ protective circles—that was nonsense. When real danger comes, the only one who can protect you is yourself.
"The life of a Star Martial Warrior is spectacular, but also perilous. Guard against arrogance and rashness. Run with all your might; as long as you run fast enough, death itself won’t be able to catch up to you."
"I understand," Wang Lan said, picking up his cellphone and waving to Huang Feilong, who was sitting in the car.
With a press of the accelerator, the car sped out of the garage and disappeared. Driving away from Wang Lan’s home, Huang Feilong’s heart was not calm. He hadn’t expected Wang Lan to become a Star Martial Warrior, but even if Wang Lan hadn’t, he would still have been the most outstanding student Huang Feilong had ever taught. And the only one to whom he had imparted even his most treasured, "bottom-of-the-chest" skills.
BEEP—
A text message alert popped up on the car’s display, notifying him that 200,000 yuan had been deposited into his account.
He muttered, "This darn kid... Couldn’t he think of a more thoughtful teacher’s gift than this? So tacky!" Even as he said it, a smile bloomed across Huang Feilong’s face.
But I like it,
he thought.
Having sweated profusely several times today, Wang Lan took the elevator straight to the top floor for a good hot bath.
Having started with one hundred skill points from his activated funds, Wang Lan now had fewer than thirty remaining. During the training to overcome his fear of death, he had spent thirty points to upgrade his Self Healing Talented Skill to Bronze Level Four. At Bronze Level Four, Wang Lan’s Self Healing speed had greatly increased, more than twice as fast as it was at Bronze Level One.
However, this was still just Self Healing. It wasn’t at the level of someone like ’Uncle Wolf,’ who could regenerate even if his vital organs were hit. It could only ensure that he could recover quickly enough from injuries to continue fighting.
With the remaining thirty skill points, Wang Lan felt torn. Should he allocate them to Inch Strength Fist or add more to Self Healing? Inch Strength enhanced his offensive output, while Self Healing boosted his resilience.
Sigh, I want both. What should I do?
Wang Lan mused.
Suddenly, Wang Lan stared at his sword skill entry in shock.
His sword skill had reached Bronze Level Two! He clearly remembered it was at Bronze Level One before. This meant there was only one explanation: skill enhancement wasn’t only achieved through point allocation but could also be improved through practice.
Spending the afternoon overcoming the fear of death made my sword skill sharper and my presence more imposing, which effectively translated to an increase in my sword skill’s proficiency!
Wang Lan realized. That made perfect sense.
Turning off the water, Wang Lan returned to his room wrapped in a bath towel. He had just sat down when his phone began to ring.

chapters.content:
Chapter 7: Chapter 7 Your Password Entry is Incorrect
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
"Auntie, are you back in the country yet?"
"Lan, there’s a very important emergency meeting here in Han City, so I won’t be able to make it back tonight..."
"Oh, take care of your health, Auntie."
"I know. Lan, can you go and keep Jiajia company tonight...?"
"What’s wrong?"
"I promised I’d return tonight and accompany her to summer camp tomorrow, but something came up here... I just called her, and she slammed her phone down. Can you go and coax her for me?"
"No problem, Auntie. Focus on your meeting; leave it to me!" Wang Lan agreed readily.
When Auntie was pregnant with Song Jia, her husband had an accident during a scientific research experiment. Later, Auntie started a biotechnology company on her own and raised Song Jia by herself.
When Wang Lan’s mother went missing, Wang Lan was eight years old and lived at his aunt’s house for three years before moving out to live independently. In Wang Lan’s eyes, both his mother and aunt were incredible women, each reaching heights in their respective fields that many men could hardly achieve.
Some precocious children understand the pressures and hardships adults face, but others can’t. Instead, they might think that in adults’ eyes, careers are more important than they are. Wang Lan could understand his aunt, and he could also understand Song Jia’s feelings.
He got dressed, took the elevator, then hopped on his mini electric scooter and headed out.
Auntie’s house was in Fragrant Courtyard Bay, a rather high-end villa community in Suzhou City. Since it was summer, even though it was past six in the evening, the sun still hadn’t set; it wouldn’t get completely dark until around seven.
