Fragrant Courtyard Bay was a fully enclosed community, inaccessible to outsiders. Even deliveries and couriers had to be handed over to property management, which had designated personnel responsible for delivering goods to residents’ doors.
First-rate service, first-rate efficiency, and first-rate quality were the calling cards of Fragrant Courtyard Bay.
"Sorry, electric scooters are not allowed in this community," a security guard politely told a girl trying to enter on her scooter at the gate.
"Do you think I’m blind? I just saw an electric scooter go in."
"That scooter belongs to one of our community’s residents."
"I’m a resident of this community too! Let me in!"
"I’m sorry, but you’re not. If you’re looking for someone, please tell me their name, and I’ll contact them for you. Please don’t block the entrance."
The girl, having failed to negotiate, had to step aside. She then suddenly pulled out her phone.
"Dear friends at the Jing Fish livestreaming platform, I originally wanted to take you all inside to experience the environment and atmosphere of Fragrant Courtyard’s high-end community. Sadly, Qiuqiu can’t even get through their gate.
"No wonder it’s known as the community in Suzhou City with the strictest management and highest security. Qiuqiu did some research before coming. Almost all the residents here are company bosses or regional presidents of listed companies, so such stringent management is understandable. You have to carry an access card to go out, and even using the elevator requires a fingerprint scan..."
Wang Lan’s electric scooter ambled towards Fragrant Courtyard. Seeing the guard also move to stop him, the girl’s face lit up with a schadenfreude-filled smile. Misery loves company, after all, and it often improves one’s mood.
"Look everyone, a pitiful kid facing the same ordeal as Qiuqiu is here! Brave young man, let’s see what trick you use to get past!"
"Excuse me, sir, our community doesn’t allow electric scooters..."
"Scram!" Wang Lan suddenly lifted his foot.
"Mr. Lan, please go right ahead!"
"PFFT... HAHAHA... Is this supposed to make me die laughing?"
"666! Qiuqiu, it looks like it’s not that you can’t get in, but that you used the wrong password."
"That’s right, the unlock code is voice-activated. It’s just one word: Scram!"
"Qiuqiu, you’ve got the password now, hurry up and try to get through!"
"No wonder it’s the most strictly managed and highest-security community. A voice-activated unlock code like that—most people would never think of it!"
The security guard chuckled as he walked back, looking a bit awkward under Qiuqiu’s gaze. "He’s a resident of our community."
"You clearly don’t know him, okay?"
"I’ve been a security guard in this community for three years. I know every resident. Mr. Lan comes several times a month."
"Then why did you try to stop him just now?"
"Isn’t it a conditioned reflex? I stop dozens of outsiders like you every day. When I saw an electric scooter approaching, I just went up. I only realized it was Mr. Lan when I got closer."
Wang Lan rode straight into the community. It wasn’t that he was genuinely that arrogant; he was just very familiar with Liu, the security guard at the gate. That "Scram!" was a playful greeting, similar to how Wang Lan often kicked Zhang Hao’s butt and told him to "get lost."
He rode the electric scooter to the underground parking garage and directly took a car parking space.
When he entered his aunt’s house, Mrs. Feng, the housekeeper, was busy in the kitchen. "Mr. Lan, you’re here?"
"Yes! Hello, Mrs. Feng." Wang Lan went to the sofa and sat beside Song Jia. Song Jia was currently staring blankly at the television, clutching a teddy bear. Her left cheek read ’unhappy,’ her right cheek read ’displeased,’ and her forehead was practically engraved with ’angry.’
Basically, Song Jia’s entire face was a canvas of anger, frustration, and the urge to erupt.
"Jiajia, want to turn off the TV?"
"None of your business!" Song Jia retorted coldly, pouting.
"Since you’re not in the mood to watch TV anyway, isn’t leaving it on a waste of electricity? What’s the situation with the summer camp tomorrow?"
As soon as Wang Lan mentioned this, Song Jia’s eyes reddened, and tears began to stream down her face.
"The top ten students from each grade in the final exams, along with one parent, are supposed to gather at school tomorrow morning at seven to go to the Sky Curtain Lake Resort Area for summer camp.
"How could Mom do this? She promised she’d be back tonight, she promised... She’s always telling me to be trustworthy, to have a sense of commitment, but what about her? She bailed on me, bailed on me!"
"Stop squeezing it; you’ll break it if you squeeze any harder."
"Can’t I go by myself?" Wang Lan asked curiously.
"No. Sky Curtain Lake is an ecological resort area; you have to bring a parent. Do you know how hard it was for me to get fifth in the grade... SOB SOB SOB... Mom doesn’t care about me at all!"
"Alright, it’s not that big a deal. The requirement for a parent is just to prevent any accidents with you precious little things. How about I go with you?"
"You?" Song Jia turned her head, looking Wang Lan up and down. "You look too young. Maybe you should put on a fake beard and glasses..."
"You watch too many TV dramas. I’ve already got my ID card; I’m an adult. I’m perfectly capable of being your guardian. To be honest, Bro had something on tomorrow, but nothing is as important as Jiajia’s business. Bro will go with you."
Song Jia blinked her tear-stained eyelashes. "Since you’re requesting so sincerely, then I’ll mercifully agree. I’ll take you."
"Not upset anymore?"
"I’m going to pack my backpack! I want to bring lots of yummy food..." Song Jia skipped away.
Wang Lan hadn’t lied to Song Jia about having something to do the next day. Awakened Star Martial Warriors needed to go to the Star Martial Hall to complete their registration. Only registered Star Martial Warriors could swagger around carrying weapons, and only by becoming a Star Martial Warrior could one enjoy their benefits.
The benefits and such, Wang Lan didn’t really care about them. But the Star Martial Warrior identity could be used for showing off.
Previously, when Wang Lan saw those Star Martial Warriors on the street carrying Wolf Fang Clubs or shouldering greatswords, leaning against rugged off-road vehicles and hitting on girls, he would get so angry he felt like rushing up and castrating them.
「The next morning.」
Song Jia kicked open Wang Lan’s door.
"Lazy pig, get up!"
Startled by the heavy blow, Wang Lan instinctively sat bolt upright. Seeing Song Jia’s small, flushed, excited face, Wang Lan glanced wordlessly at the alarm clock beside him.
"Young miss, it’s only five o’clock!"
"The sun is already so high, and you’re still not getting up for me!"
"Getting up is fine, but can you leave my room?" Wang Lan scratched his tousled hair. He had awakened as a Star Martial Warrior yesterday and had been too excited to sleep well that night. He felt like he had just drifted off when this little ancestor came to make trouble.
"I’m afraid if I go out, you’ll just fall back asleep. Get up! Big lazy worm."
"I’ll get up, but I can’t change clothes with you in my room. You don’t expect me to go to summer camp with you in my pajamas, do you?"
"Oh. You have five minutes."
They were supposed to gather at school at seven o’clock, but they arrived by six-thirty. Wang Lan had thought he was already very early, but he hadn’t expected some people to be even earlier.
"Jiajia, over here—" a girl waved to Song Jia.
Wang Lan followed Song Jia, sizing up this famous prestigious academy in Suzhou City. Multi-Wheel Bilingual Academy, located in the Suzhou Park Trading District, had the most top-tier hardware facilities, the most top-tier teaching staff, and of course, required the most top-tier, expensive tuition fees.
The families who could afford to send their children to Multi-Wheel Bilingual Academy were definitely either rich or noble. When these rich and noble families entrusted their children to the academy, the academy had to deliver the highest quality education.
Rich kids are hard to manage, but things like causing trouble in school were absolutely impossible here. The school’s management was famously strict. Causing trouble? Campus bullying? Any child here was made of gold; any bump or scrape was a big deal. So, if you didn’t obey the school’s discipline, sorry, please take your child back.
"Wow, Your Excellency, the Academic God?" When Song Jia brought Wang Lan to the third-grade assembly point, several of Song Jia’s classmates already waiting there suddenly cried out in alarm upon seeing Wang Lan.
"That’s not me; you’ve mistaken me for someone else," Wang Lan denied decisively.
The title ’Academic God’ was given to Wang Lan by the hundred thousand elementary and middle school students in Suzhou City. The first time he heard such a chuunibyou name was when he had just started high school. His alma mater, Chongshan School, had published a report card of Wang Lan’s scores from first grade to junior high graduation, along with his ranking in every exam.
The original intention was to motivate students to emulate student Wang Lan and be hardworking, good students. But once this report card was published, it deified Wang Lan in one fell swoop. Not only did it fail to start a trend of learning from student Wang Lan, but it instead stirred up a wave of feudal superstitious thinking.
From the first exam to the final high school entrance exam, this beast Wang Lan had actually been number one every single time. For class-level unified exams, he was first in class. For grade-level unified exams, he was first in the grade. For city-wide unified exams, he was first in the city.
For students in the same cohort as Wang Lan, first place was an impossible dream. Even if they vied for it, they could only fight for second.
Such an outrageously dazzling report card—was that the work of a human? Student Wang Lan had cultivated for nine years, achieving first place every time, his merit perfected, firmly establishing his godhood. The mortal realm could no longer permit such a Demon to exist.
For a while, praying to the Academic God before exams guaranteed you wouldn’t fail. Tossing a coin to pray to the Academic God was effective every time.
Academic God above, three sticks of incense morning and night.
When Wang Lan found out, he was so angry he nearly had a Soul Out of Body experience.
So, hearing this title again, a killing intent gradually rose in Wang Lan’s eyes. These people before him were no longer cute elementary schoolers, but a group of soon-to-be chief culprits...
"The Academic God? WOW! I’m so touched to see a living one!"ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
"Little Fatty, don’t be too moved. I’ll bless you to fail every time," Wang Lan said, his smile as bright as sunshine, but his inner curse was extremely vicious.
"Academic God, can you sign an autograph for me?"
"Sorry, I didn’t bring a pen."
"This is a tablet; you can write directly on it." The tablet handed to him actually displayed his ID photo.
"Where did you get this photo?"
"I downloaded it online. Your photo is hung high like a shining mirror in the Academic God Tieba."
Wang Lan wouldn’t really bother arguing with elementary schoolers, so he smoothly signed his name. As he handed it back to the other party, he suddenly paused. "How many inches is this tablet of yours?"
"Seven inches." The boy replied, very pleased with himself as he flicked his bangs.
"Oh dear. Sorry, I accidentally pressed delete..."
"..."

chapters.title: Chapter 8 Accidents
chapters.content:
Chapter 8: Chapter 8 Accidents
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
"Why hasn’t it come yet? I’ve waited so long I could have wilted!"
"Yeah, we were supposed to leave at seven, and now it’s already eight."
Complaints began to emerge from the fifty students, from first to fifth grade. Children have limited patience; they started grumbling after just a ten-minute delay.
"Please don’t worry, everyone. It’s rush hour, and as you know, traffic in Suzhou City can be terrible. It won’t clear up for a while, so please be patient," the teacher in charge continuously tried to soothe the students.
Sure enough, before long, a bus arrived, and the elementary school students cheered as it came to a halt.
"It’s bus number one, but where is bus number two?"
"Yeah, where’s bus number two?"
"Don’t worry, students. I left half an hour before bus number two and only just arrived, so it will probably be a bit longer for them. Children and parents for bus number one, please follow me and line up in an orderly fashion."
"Forget it, I’m not going anymore. After waiting so long, it’s better to stay at home and play video games."
"Yeah, yeah... This is so dull!"
After bus number one left, the remaining elementary school students became even more vocal with their complaints. Song Jia kicked the ground continuously, a look of unhappiness on her face. However, Song Jia was relatively quiet by nature, so she refrained from complaining for a long time.
Joy always comes unexpectedly. Not long after bus number one had departed, bus number two also arrived. The sight of the second bus elicited another round of enthusiastic cheers from the students.Nᴇw novel chapters are publɪshed on ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
Especially those who had been clamoring to give up and go home were now jumping around more than anyone else. Ah, their mouths protested, but their actions revealed the truth.
There were fifty-two seats on the bus, with adults and children sitting in pairs. The parents from this prestigious school indeed had good manners. They lined up in order and took their seats systematically. Aside from the noisy chatter of the students, the adults conversed softly and gently.
"Hey, Mr. Huang, we’re boarding the bus too. How’s traffic on your end?"
"Ugh, don’t even get me started. We’re stuck and not moving an inch. We probably won’t reach Sky Curtain Lake until noon. I don’t know what’s going on today; there’s fog everywhere, the overpass is closed, and the whole city is gridlocked."
"Nothing we can do about it then. See you at Sky Curtain Lake."
"Alright!"
After Mr. Qiu hung up the phone, the driver suddenly spoke up, "Mr. Qiu, the city traffic is so bad, why don’t we take the Ring City National Highway? There should be fewer cars there. It might mean an extra thirty kilometers, but we could arrive in about an hour."
"Really? Then please, take the Ring City National Highway."
"Alrighty, kiddos and parents, please fasten your seat belts; we’re setting off!"
The bus slowly began to move. Sure enough, a massive traffic jam awaited right outside the school gate. After crawling through a slow stretch of road, the bus finally picked up speed. Traffic in the city was almost at a standstill; it was actually faster to circle the outskirts of Suzhou City to reach their destination.
The bus filled with chatter and laughter; the teachers were occupied with playing games with the children, ensuring a cheerful and lively atmosphere throughout the journey.
Wang Lan rested his head to the side, looking out the window.
Perhaps this summer offers my final moments of peace. Having awakened as a Star Martial Warrior, I’ll have to seize every opportunity to become stronger. In the world of Star Martial Warriors, you either grow stronger or perish.
For average people, this world was safe. They lived in a country that was constantly growing stronger. There was stability and a booming economy; everyone was well-fed and clothed.
However, this safe environment couldn’t exist without the Star Martial Warriors’ constant battles and efforts. Since the Demon Clan was repelled seventy years ago, human civilization had enjoyed this long period of peace. But throughout history, the Demon Clan never gave humanity much time to recuperate.
Each invasion by the Demon Clan brought painful memories to humanity. Between two hundred and seventy years ago, over a period of one hundred and thirty years, the human population plummeted from seven billion to two billion. Generation after generation, if one were to count the dead, it would be an astronomical number too harrowing for humanity to contemplate.
Although there was no war at present, Different Dimensional Spaces opened frequently. Each one required the dispatch of Pioneer Teams and armies for exploration. Spaces that could be controlled served as training grounds; those that could not were sealed off.
If left unchecked, Exotic Beasts from the Different Dimensional Spaces would break out and hunt humans. One only needed to look at the cities destroyed by Exotic Beasts in the Middle East, or witness the people displaced by their weakened nations, to realize how fortunate it was to be born in such a strong and safe country.
The country’s strength came not only from its booming economy but also from the formidable power of the Star Martial Warriors. An economy without Star Martial Warriors is but a castle in the air, while Star Martial Warriors without an economy leads to destructive militarism. Jade Country, however, balanced both, demonstrating agility and strength combined.
Suddenly, the bus began to slow down, and Wang Lan’s thoughts were interrupted.
Outside the window, a blanket of dense fog had appeared. It was so thick that one couldn’t see their own hands in front of their face. Visibility wasn’t just less than five meters; it was probably less than two.
"What’s going on? How could there be such heavy fog..."
"The weather is really abnormal today. Driver, can you still drive? Should we stop?"
"We can’t stop here; we’re on a mountain road. If we stop, cars behind us might hit us, and we could tumble down the cliff. Low visibility isn’t a problem; we’ll use the horn to get our bearings."
The bus inched forward at a snail’s pace, rocking gently. After around half an hour, they hadn’t encountered any other vehicles on the road.
Wang Lan frowned. Although the Ring City National Highway often had fewer vehicles, it should still have had a steady stream of traffic.
"Driver, did we take the wrong turn?" Wang Lan suddenly realized something was wrong and asked aloud.
"No, I know Ring City National Highway like the back of my hand; I could drive it blindfolded."
But the problem is, driving now is no different from driving blindfolded. Visibility of only two to three meters is virtually like being blind.
"Driver, something’s not right. We’ve been going uphill for half an hour. What place has such a long incline?"
"Incline? Are we going uphill?" The driver suddenly yelled anxiously, "Why do I feel like we’re on flat ground? Ah! Not good—"
A scream startled everyone on the bus, and in an instant, the bus began to lean steeply. Wang Lan quickly wrapped his arms around Song Jia beside him as piercing screams filled the air, and suddenly, the bus seemed to lose its weight.
The world spun wildly, and the bus tumbled repeatedly down the slope.
BOOM—
With a violent jolt, the rolling bus came to a halt.
Once the bus stopped, Wang Lan quickly released Song Jia from his embrace. "Jiajia, how are you? Are you hurt?"
"Brother... it hurts so much..."
"SOB SOB SOB... It hurts, Mommy..."
"Uncle, my head hurts so much, and I’m bleeding..."
In an instant, cries filled the interior of the bus. Wang Lan unbuckled his seatbelt. As the bus lay on its side, Wang Lan punched through the glass and nimbly climbed out.
Just moments ago, the fog had been dense and disorienting, but now the sun shone brightly. Moreover, their surroundings resembled a canyon. If there was a canyon in Suzhou City, it would be West Mountain Canyon, but this didn’t look like it. Perhaps it was the different angle.
"Brother!" Song Jia struggled to look up at Wang Lan.
"Come, give me your hand, and I’ll pull you up."
After pulling Song Jia out of the bus, a fashionable woman handed over her child.
"Everyone, come one by one, don’t push..."
Wang Lan took the children one by one and then helped the people inside climb out of the bus.
"We fell from such a height, and all of us are still alive?" Once outside, several parents looked incredulously at the cliff hidden in the clouds above.
"Not everyone is alive. The driver died."
"Let’s not feel relieved yet. Hurry and make a phone call for help."
"Damn, I don’t have a signal on my phone. What about your phones?"
"Same, no signal."
"Didn’t they say 4G covers the entire city?"
"Maybe the mountains are an exception."
"I’m afraid it’s not that simple..." one of the middle-aged men, who looked to be in his forties, said as he gazed solemnly at the bus.
"Look, the bus has been reinforced. It’s because of these reinforcements that we didn’t die when we rolled down from the top of the mountain. But with the driver dead, I can’t be sure if the bus was reinforced long ago for passenger safety or if it was a temporary measure."
"Regardless of that, we first need to find a way to call for help. Everyone spread out and see where there is a mobile signal."
There were twenty-five children on the bus, and twenty-five adults too. Aside from a few who were injured, most adults were fine. In this situation, the children were disoriented and could only cry, but the adults had already started to look for solutions.
RUMBLE—
Suddenly, the sky darkened, not giving people a chance to breathe, and it started to drizzle.
It was June, and normally a little drizzle wouldn’t be a problem. But strangely, this rain felt unusually cold, chilling them to the bone.
The dozen or so parents searching for a signal had to run back. Adults might endure the rain, but the children could not, especially those who were frightened and injured.
"Listen up, return to the bus! First, let’s right the bus. Quick!" The middle-aged man suddenly began to command. His tone naturally carried a leader’s aura, and everyone subconsciously followed his orders.
Wang Lan found a fallen dead tree not far off, and it took twenty people to right the bus.
Once again, they took shelter inside the bus, as the rain pitter-pattered outside. Gradually, beads of ice formed on the windows. Hail began to fall, in June!
"Mommy... I want to go home..."
"SOB SOB SOB... I will never go to summer camp again..."
One set off another, and cries quickly filled the bus again. Meanwhile, Wang Lan frowned, feeling an uneasy premonition.
The weird fog, the eerie fall into the canyon, and now the bizarre hail.
"Just waiting here won’t do us any good. How about this: who can offer a phone? I’ll make a simple signal-sending device. There probably isn’t a signal repeater here, which is why our phones have no reception," a bespectacled man from the central-south region calmly suggested.
"It’s no use!" The middle-aged man who first gave orders spoke in a deep voice, "My phone is equipped with Sky Blue Star’s top signal-sending device. It connects to satellite communications and is military-grade. Self-checks indicate everything is normal, but now, it has no signal either."
The middle-aged man went to the driver’s seat and moved the driver’s corpse aside. "Let me see if the bus can still be driven."
He skillfully started the engine, engaged the gears, and checked everything. After a short while, he turned the bus off again.
"The bus can start, but the brakes are broken. It seems the brake pads have shattered. Without spare parts, we can’t fix them."
"What shall we do then?"
"The most optimistic scenario is to wait until people outside notice we’re missing and come to rescue us."

chapters.title: Chapter 9 First Kill Demon Clan
chapters.content:
Chapter 9: Chapter 9 First Kill Demon Clan
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
The weather in the valley was truly bizarre. Just moments before, small hailstones had been falling, but soon after, it turned into a sunny day, and the temperature rose as well.
Wang Lan looked at the cliff over which the bus had tumbled. It wasn’t very high, about a hundred meters.
"Jiajia, you stay in the bus and wait for me. I’ll climb back up the way we came to see if I can flag down a vehicle."
"Brother... the cliff is so high..." Song Jia was actually scared of Wang Lan leaving. In such a perilous situation, children need adults nearby to provide a sense of security.
"It’s okay, I can handle this height. Mr. Qin, could you please look after Jiajia for me?"
"Young man, are you a Star Martial Warrior?" the composed middle-aged man asked with a slight smile.
"Yes, but my strength is quite poor."
"Really? I never expected you to be a Star Martial Warrior. That’s great..."
To ordinary people, Star Martial Warriors were like superhumans, their physical conditioning and abilities beyond imagination. Having a Star Martial Warrior nearby could provide them with security.
After leaving Song Jia in the care of these parents, Wang Lan dashed toward the cliff and began to climb it with his bare hands.
Luckily, this side of the cliff was not very smooth; the uneven rock face made climbing easier for Wang Lan. Using his hands and feet, he climbed rapidly, his physical prowess far surpassing that of an ordinary person.
Just as he reached halfway, a breeze blew past, and an even thicker fog suddenly rose above him. Wang Lan felt for handholds on the rocks, climbing up the cliff bit by bit.
Looking up at the sky from the bottom of the valley, the sun shone brightly. But after climbing the cliff, it was still so foggy he couldn’t see his hand in front of his face. The climate here was too strange. Wang Lan had previously noticed that the hail falling from the sky didn’t seem like ordinary hail but more like dry ice.
When the hail had landed on the bus windows, it had released a dense mist, but because it was raining, the mist had vanished instantly. Now, however, the fog in front of him reminded Wang Lan of dry ice.
Normal fog couldn’t be as ethereal as this. In typical foggy weather, fog is perceived as still. But the fog before him was rolling violently, and he could even disperse parts of it by waving his hand.
Wang Lan found the uphill path the bus had taken, but the fog obscured his vision so much that he couldn’t discern the direction and had nearly stumbled off the cliff again.
CRACK—
A crisp sound rang out as Wang Lan stepped on a broken wooden sign. He picked it up. An English place name was written on it in red paint, though Wang Lan could only recognize the word "town."
An English name? Dammit, did we travel through time?
Wang Lan was shocked.
Had the bus accidentally entered a wormhole?
In this world where Different Dimensional Spaces frequently opened, Time and Space Tunnels were not rare. At least every year, someone would inadvertently enter one and inexplicably appear hundreds or even thousands of kilometers away.
If we inadvertently entered a Time and Space Tunnel, then the lack of signal on everyone’s cell phones would be normal. However, even Mr. Qin’s military phone has no signal, and it’s equipped with global satellite communication capabilities. That doesn’t make sense. Also, it’s still daytime, and the sun’s angle matches the time on our watches. Logically, the distance deviation shouldn’t be too great.
Wang Lan found where the wooden sign had been planted; below it was an arrow.
This means there should be a town nearby. Finding it might allow us to contact the outside world.
Wang Lan followed the direction indicated by the sign, almost feeling his way along the edge of the path to avoid veering off course. Suddenly, he stopped. Before him was the very cliff he had just climbed.
If this sign is genuine, does it mean the town is the cliff? Is this a prank, or has something else happened? Or... was the sign destroyed because the town moved away?
Venturing into such heavy fog to explore would be extremely unwise. Not to mention the dangers, if I get lost, who knows when I’d find my way out?
After hesitating at the cliff’s edge for a long time, Wang Lan finally decided to go back down and rejoin Mr. Qin and the others to discuss what to do.
Descending the cliff was much faster than climbing up. As he neared the bottom, Wang Lan glanced up. The cliff edge was enveloped in rolling fog, yet the sky above it was bright with sunshine.
Truly bizarre weather,
he thought.
When he found the bus, the children inside were still sobbing. Only a few injured adults remained, along with Mr. Qin, the only one who could drive.
"Brother..." Song Jia called out, pleasantly surprised, tears still welling in her eyes.
"Young man, did you find anything?"
"No, but I did find a wooden sign." Wang Lan handed the sign to Mr. Qin.
"Cricket Town? Is this overseas?" Mr. Qin was also shocked.
Well, now... instead of reaching the Sky Curtain Lake Resort Area, did we just teleport out of the country?
"Mr. Qin, do you know this town?"
"There must be thousands, if not tens of thousands, of towns called Cricket Town around the world. Who knows which one this is? Since it’s supposedly overseas, having no signal is normal. Moreover, I suspect this valley has a disruptive magnetic field, interfering with the satellite receivers in our phones. Did you find the town?"
"No. Visibility is still too low. I was worried about the fog, so I came back to discuss things with everyone. Where are the others?"
"They said they were going ahead to see if they could walk out of the valley, hoping to run into someone. But they’ve been gone for quite a while now..." As he said this, Mr. Qin looked worried.
"Mr. Qiu is leading them?"
"Yes."
"The entire valley is enveloped in dense fog. I’m worried they might risk venturing into it. If they get in and can’t get out, it’ll be dangerous. How about this: I’ll go look for them."
"Alright. We’ll have to trouble you then, young man."
"Brother... take me with you?" Song Jia quickly grabbed Wang Lan’s clothes.
"If I take you, what if I lose you?"
"I’m the one who made you bring me! I’m more worried I’ll lose *you*! I promise I’ll hold your hand the whole time."ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
"Alright!"
Wang Lan couldn’t stand Song Jia’s pleading eyes. That look was an instant-kill tactic effective on everyone in his family. How could he refuse his adorable little cousin?
Leading Song Jia, Wang Lan set off along the path the parents had explored. He had thought the valley wouldn’t be too large, but after half an hour of walking, dense forest still flanked them on both sides, and a seemingly endless gravel beach stretched out before them.
The scorching sun beat down on the earth. Song Jia’s face was flushed red, and sweat dripped continuously from her cheeks. She kept sticking out her tongue to lick the corners of her mouth.
"Thirsty?"
"Yes, I forgot to bring my backpack."
"I don’t have any water either. Should we look for a source?
It’s strange. Considering how far they’ve walked, the parents probably wouldn’t want to go any further. They’d rather have Mr. Qin drive the bus over. Even with the broken brakes, he could still drive on this spacious beach.
"
"Brother, there’s a bottle of mineral water!" Song Jia excitedly ran over and picked it up. "It’s unopened, and the expiration date is good! We can drink it."
"Wait. Why is there a bottle of mineral water here?"
"Maybe one of the parents accidentally dropped it?"
"In this heat, no parent would willingly discard an unopened bottle of mineral water." He looked around but still saw no one.
"Brother, look! That looks like Li Xiuxiu’s mom."
Song Jia’s eyesight really was... incredibly sharp. Following her pointing finger, Wang Lan did indeed see a woman in red. He remembered her as one of the parents.
"Hey—"
Wang Lan took Song Jia’s hand and, waving, walked towards the woman. The woman turned, saw them, and waved back.
"Over here..." the woman said.
"Why did you all go into the woods? You shouldn’t enter forests in unfamiliar places," Wang Lan asked quizzically as he reached the woman.
"We were tired from walking, so we rested at the edge of the forest. I went in to relieve myself, and when I came out, I couldn’t find the others. Little brother, have you seen them?"
Shaking his head, Wang Lan replied, "I came from the bus and didn’t see anyone. How long have you been separated from them?"
"Only about ten minutes..."
AH—
Song Jia suddenly leaped up. A bloody ear lay next to her foot. It was fresh, the blood still wet.
Could they have had an accident...?
Just as the thought arose, a sense of crisis struck him from behind. Wang Lan had no time to think; his body reacted instinctively. He shifted to the side and lashed out with a kick.
Li Xiuxiu’s mother suddenly pulled out a fruit knife and attacked Wang Lan. Her speed was far beyond that of an ordinary person. If Wang Lan’s movement technique skill hadn’t reached Bronze Tier 1, he would have been hit.
"What are you doing?" Song Jia screamed. The next moment, intense fear filled her face.
The skin on the woman’s face suddenly turned a vivid green, and her eyes bulged from their sockets like a lobster’s.
AH—
Instantly, Song Jia turned deathly pale, gripping Wang Lan’s arm tightly. "Ghost! Ghost!"
"Not a ghost, it’s a Demon!" Wang Lan shook off Song Jia’s hand, warily eying the Demon before him. The most critical issue now was that he was unarmed.
Strike first and gain the upper hand!
With that thought, Wang Lan surged forward. Although he had only awakened as a Star Martial Warrior the day before, the system had provided "startup funds," ensuring his Basic Skills were not inferior to other Star Martial Warriors his age.
And Wang Lan had an advantage his peers lacked: Inch Strength Fist.
Inch Strength Fist was an ordinary martial art, one most Star Martial Warriors disdained to learn. In their view, having Star Martial Skills was sufficient; at most, they might also learn Basic Combat or Basic Swordsmanship.
But Star Martial Skills consumed Star Power. In contrast, an ordinary martial art like Inch Strength Fist, which could produce effects comparable to Star Martial Skills without consuming Star Power, could be a Star Martial Warrior’s hidden trump card.
Wang Lan punched at the Demon’s head, while the fruit knife in its hand stabbed viciously at his throat.
If he hadn’t undergone the training to overcome his fear of death just yesterday, that knife strike would have been fatal. So, Wang Lan was fortunate. After conquering his fear, a life-and-death battle felt almost no different from training.
Wang Lan had also diligently trained in unarmed combat against armed opponents.
The key to unarmed combat against an armed opponent was to be quick, precise, and ruthless—to disarm them by surprise. Wang Lan instantly changed his move. A knife-hand strike chopped down on the Demon’s knife-wielding wrist. Power surged from the edge of his hand, and the knife flew from the Demon’s grasp.
Without the slightest hesitation, Wang Lan pressed forward again.
"Inch Strength—"
BOOM!
His fist struck the Demon’s chest with a dull thud!
"Triple Force—"
Fingertips, knuckles, fist—the three stages of Inch Strength Fist exploded instantly. The Demon’s red dress burst into shreds, scattering like butterflies.
Only then did the fruit knife, sent flying earlier, fall from the sky.
Wang Lan snatched up the fruit knife with lightning speed. Before the Demon could recover from his assault, he stabbed the knife into its throat and slashed sideways, opening a gruesome wound.

chapters.title: Chapter 10 The War is Coming
chapters.content:
Chapter 10: Chapter 10 The War is Coming
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
Green blood gushed out. The Demon clutched its throat, its lobster-like eyes wide, and sank to its knees unwillingly.
"First kill achieved. Reward: thirty skill points and fifty experience points." In his mind, the Destiny System suddenly broadcast a system notification.
First kill?
Wang Lan murmured, immediately grabbing Song Jia and running outside.
Along the way, Song Jia remained silent, perhaps terrified by the Demon’s monstrous and frightful appearance. Suddenly, Song Jia lifted her head and looked at Wang Lan. "Brother..."
"Jiajia, don’t be afraid. I’ll protect you."
"Was that a member of the Demon Clan from our textbooks just now?"
"Yes, a Demon! It must be a low-ranking Demon. There are many types of Demon Clan members. The blood of low-ranking Demons is mostly green and has a foul, fishy smell."
"Demons really do look terrifying. Such invaders should all be killed."
"Yes, I’ll do my best."
「At the entrance of the Multi-wheel Bilingual Academy, a school bus wobbled to a stop at the school gate. The security guard walked out of his booth with a puzzled expression.」
"The traffic was terrible. I’ve never encountered such congestion before," the driver said with a smile, rolling down the window.
"What are you doing at the school?" asked the security guard curiously.
"Huh? Weren’t you the ones who booked a ride to Sky Curtain Lake?"
"The bus left nearly an hour ago, and you’re just getting here? That’s not right. The school only booked two buses. Are you sure our school booked you?"
"Look, here’s the order information, my license plate number..."
"You’re Route Two? Then who was driving the Route Two bus that left earlier? Wait, let me make a call to confirm."
「At the Sky Curtain Lake Resort Area, Mr. Huang was also frantically making phone calls.」
"What’s going on? We all left together, but I’m here and there’s no sign of them. Their phones have been out of service too... Could something have happened?"
The students of the Multi-wheel Bilingual Academy were all from wealthy or influential families. The school always took great care to ensure the children’s safety, even if it was a hassle. When the school leaders learned of the situation, they immediately checked but found no information on this particular bus at all.
At this point, the school leaders were sweating profusely. They promptly reported to the traffic management department to check the whereabouts of the bus.
The safety of more than twenty children, and by extension, their wealthy and influential parents, was at stake, so the traffic management department naturally cooperated fully. But strangely, once the bus cleared the congested area, it headed straight for the Ring City National Highway and then vanished.
"Send police cars to search. A bus can’t just disappear without a trace."
"Call the mayor," said the head of the traffic bureau with a grave expression.
"Ah? Isn’t that unnecessary? We don’t need to inform the mayor, do we?"
"Qin Weimin, a military advisor from the Southeast Military Region headquarters, was also on that bus. Furthermore, the bus itself is suspicious; our vehicle registration system has no record of it. I’m afraid it was deliberately targeted."
"This is bad... Director, you make the call."
「At the headquarters of the Tianjian Bureau in Suzhou City.」
The phone on Wang Qianfeng’s desk suddenly rang. "Hello?"
Suddenly, Wang Qianfeng stood up. "Director."
"Yes, dispatch a team to search immediately." After hanging up, Wang Qianfeng picked up another phone. "Have Xu Shiyun come to my office."
「Running frantically with Song Jia, Wang Lan soon spotted the bus ahead. It seemed to be on the verge of departing.」
"Hey, wait a moment—"
Wang Lan hurriedly called out. Though the bus’s brakes were broken, it had just started moving, so it quickly came to a stop.
"Young man, didn’t Mr. Qiu say you were by the canyon entrance?" Mr. Qinqin asked as he opened the door to let Wang Lan in.
Hm?
Upon hearing this, Wang Lan furrowed his brows and quietly covered Song Jia’s mouth. "Mr. Qin, where are you driving?"
"Song Jia, come here, come to your teacher. Hello, Wang Lan. Mr. Qin told me you went looking for us. After we passed through the woods, we found the canyon exit, but it was blocked by rubble. There’s a road just outside the exit.
"So, we had Mr. Qin drive the bus over here first. Once we clear the rocks, we can leave this cursed place," Mr. Qiu said with a smile, then gestured for Song Jia to come closer. "Jiajia, come here..."
"Brother... the teacher is missing an ear..." Song Jia said softly, her face buried in Wang Lan’s chest.
Damn, how sharp is this girl’s eyesight? Spotting a missing ear hidden under hair?
But Song Jia’s words made Wang Lan even more certain that something was wrong with this Mr. Qiu. Or rather,
all the parents who had gone exploring are probably done for.
"Kids, settle down. Your uncle is about to drive," Mr. Qin said with a smile.
Wang Lan strode into the bus, appearing to look for a seat. But as he passed Mr. Qiu, the fruit knife hidden behind his back flashed out, plunging deeply into Mr. Qiu’s eye socket.
Green blood spurted out. Wang Lan swiftly pulled out the fruit knife and, before Mr. Qiu could react, plunged it into her other eye socket.
Wang Lan’s movements were too fast, his strikes too ruthless. The two stabs took less than two seconds. This scene left the elementary students completely stunned, their minds blank.
The driver, Mr. Qin, was also startled by Wang Lan’s sudden attack, but his mind didn’t go blank. Instead, he instantly analyzed the situation. When he saw green blood gushing from Mr. Qiu’s wound, his tense nerves relaxed slightly.
"Ah— You bastard..." A rough male voice suddenly erupted from Mr. Qiu’s mouth. Wang Lan didn’t dare hesitate. He threw Mr. Qiu to the ground and stabbed fiercely at his forehead with the fruit knife.
CRACK! With a crisp sound, the fruit knife broke, but the blade remained lodged in the Demon’s brain. The Demon convulsed on the ground, its body rapidly deforming.
"Open the door!" The bus door opened, and Wang Lan threw the Demon’s corpse out.
"Why did you just throw the corpse out?" Mr. Qin asked in surprise.
"Shouldn’t I have?"
"Aren’t you going to extract the Soul Bead?"The source of thɪs content is NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
I completely forgot in my nervousness!
Wang Lan slapped his forehead. Soul Beads are pure, round orbs found in the brains of Demons and Exotic Beasts, containing pure Star Power. Star Martial Warriors can absorb Soul Beads to supplement their Star Power or use them to raise their Star Martial level.
In layman’s terms, Soul Beads are like elixirs for Star Martial Warriors. However, these elixirs cannot be crafted; they can only be obtained by hunting.
"It looks like my guess wasn’t wrong..." Mr. Qin lit a cigarette, taking a heavy drag with a solemn gaze. "You don’t mind, do you?"
"I don’t mind." Wang Lan was somewhat discomposed. Although he had acted decisively moments before, it was an adrenaline-fueled response to danger. Now that the immediate crisis had passed, his mind was in turmoil.
History books were filled with tales of the bitter feud between humans and the Demon Clan, chronicling endless blood debts. But when truly faced with it, how many people could confront war with the Demon Clan so calmly?
How many of those who constantly clamored to exterminate the Demon Clan and avenge past atrocities would actually act on their words when they encountered Demons, charging to the front lines with blades and guns?
Wang Lan was just a visitor from another world. To him, the existence of the Demon Clan defied logic even more than his own transmigration.
"My name is Qin Weimin."
"I’m Wang Lan!"
"I’m a military advisor in the Southeast Military Region and also a weapons researcher. When I discovered our cell phone signals were blocked, I suspected we might have entered a Different Dimensional Space.
"To avoid causing panic, I didn’t disclose the full situation. My phone’s GPS is active twenty-four hours a day. The Southeast Military Region would have been alerted within an hour of the signal being lost.
"By now, people on the outside have likely started searching for us, so don’t worry too much. We’re not isolated and without help."
"I’ve heard that Different Dimensional Spaces are usually full of fierce Exotic Beasts, and when these spaces open, Exotic Beasts invade the human world. But... why are there members of the Demon Clan here? And I haven’t seen any Exotic Beasts."
"That indicates only one thing: this isn’t an Exotic Beast’s Different Dimensional Space. It was created by the Demon Clan, and our entry was orchestrated by them.
"I mentioned before that this vehicle was reinforced; that’s why we didn’t suffer mass casualties when we fell from the cliff. This was all part of the Demon Clan’s plan. From what happened with Mr. Qiu, I can roughly guess their objective.
"They intend to replace everyone on this bus."
Wang Lan’s heart grew heavier.
The Demon Clan is planning to invade again, just seventy years after their defeat?
War was an unbearable burden, especially for Star Martial Warriors, who carried the legacy of all human civilization.
The grievous wounds from the last brutal war had not yet healed into scars. The astronomical number of casualties weighed on Wang Lan like a massive stone, almost suffocating him.
"You’re a Star Martial Warrior, and falling into this predicament together... it must be fate. I can tell you responsibly that history textbooks have glorified the war that began two hundred years ago.
"Perhaps humanity has defeated the Demon Clan at some point in history, but certainly not the last time. In reality, we lost. We lost our final capacity to resist."
Lost? If we lost, why weren’t we subjugated by the Demon Clan? Why are we still...
Wang Lan found it hard to believe. Although he possessed the memories of two lifetimes and knew that many truths could be distorted, he still couldn’t accept that seventy years of rapid development and peace were built upon a foundation of defeat.
Qin Weimin took a long drag, finishing half his cigarette in one go. "Because, at the final moment, the Demon Clan retreated on their own accord."
"You should know how brutal the Third Demon Calamity was. Jade Country was the first nation to announce it would forsake all prejudices and abandon all interests, solely to protect human civilization.
"Subsequently, 273 nations worldwide declared their full commitment to the war. It lasted for 132 years—more than a century, a struggle spanning five generations.
"Can you imagine families where the father died in battle, so the son went to the front lines; the son died, so the grandson went; the grandson died, and then the great-grandson went? In those war-torn years, such things were commonplace.
"During the Third Calamity, Jade Country’s military death toll was 120 million. That’s the number of soldiers who died in battle. But if you ask for Jade Country’s total death toll, you can add a zero to that number.
"One billion! One hundred and thirty years, five generations! Such heartbreaking figures. Can you comprehend the despair behind them?
"Think of the Dongdao Kingdom. The King of Dongdao, in a hoarse voice, declared to the world that they would ’rather be shattered jade than an intact tile.’ He then ordered the detonation of twelve nuclear warheads buried in seven of their own cities, resulting in seventeen million people perishing alongside the Demon Clan legions.
"King Kathe committed suicide by smashing his head against a wall after the nuclear detonations.
"You’ve read about this in your history textbooks, haven’t you? While we lavish praise on the Dongdao Kingdom’s integrity, have we ever considered what desperate circumstances could have forced them into such a decision?
"It was because the Demon Clan had successfully conquered all of Dongdao’s territory and amassed a vast army there, their forces aimed directly at Jade Country. By then, Jade Country had already fought to the point of utter depletion, with no ammunition or supplies left, completely unable to withstand the Demon Clan’s grand army."

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Crazy Leveling Up
chapters.content:
Chapter 11: Chapter 11: Crazy Leveling Up
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
Speaking of this, their hearts both became heavy. Although what Qin Weimin said deviated greatly from what was written in the history textbooks, rationally, Qin Weimin’s words could very well be true.
Wang Lan wasn’t the kind of adolescent who couldn’t face reality. He wouldn’t deny objective facts just to stick to his own ideas. Humanity had fought for one hundred and thirty years, reaching a point of utter exhaustion, while the Demon Clan’s army still kept coming in endless streams. Under such circumstances, they had launched only a desperate counterattack.
And then to determine the fate of the universe with a single battle? The textbooks merely used idioms like "stake everything on one throw," "unity is strength," and "pooling efforts for a common cause." But could the disparity in strength really be overcome by these things?
Wang Lan shook his head.
"Then why did the Demon Clan retreat?"
"I don’t know; their retreat was very sudden."
"Don’t we have guns? We have missiles and even nuclear bombs, so why did we suffer such a terrible defeat?"
"Firearms are almost ineffective against the Demon Clan’s army, except for low-level Demon Clan members. High-level Demon Clan members are simply not threatened by firearms, and they also have countless Exotic Beast armies.
As for missiles and nuclear bombs, they truly can cause effective damage. However, missile technology and nuclear bomb technology only emerged eighty years ago. By then, humanity had already been at war for a hundred years, resources were exhausted, and the population was on the brink of extinction."
At this, Wang Lan’s eyes suddenly brightened. "What about now then? Our technology has leaped forward, weapons with long-range killing power are everywhere. Can we easily defeat the Demon Clan now?"
Qin Weimin gave a faint smile. "I am a weapons expert, as well as a military consultant, and this is one of the topics I’ve researched. Soldiers in Jade Country commonly think as you do, but the result of my research is... it won’t work!"
"Why not?"Thᴇ link to the origɪn of this information rᴇsts ɪn NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
"Weapons aren’t the key to decisive victory, at least not the only factor. Comparing the Demon Clan’s capabilities to ours, their individual combat abilities and mobility are still not something we can match.
If the Demon Clan’s tactics were similar to ours or were like ancient human warfare, we would certainly win. But the Demon Clan is different; they won’t fight us in a straightforward battle.
The Demon Clan has not only its own members but also Exotic Beasts. There are deep-sea creatures in the water, flying creatures in the sky, and on the ground, there are burrowers, tanks, and mobile types. No matter how strong a weapon is, you must hit the target. Something like using missiles to swat mosquitoes—that level of precision is currently hard for us to achieve.
Moreover, the Demon Clan can open Different Dimensional Spaces to airdrop directly. If the Demon Clan invades, landing directly in our large cities, what do we do then? There are tens of millions of people in big cities; do we use missiles for a blanket strike? Use nuclear bombs to wipe out the Demon Clan?"
Wang Lan’s chest instantly grew heavy. The military power of his previous life was similar to the present, and Wang Lan believed that no one could defeat Huaxia if it possessed long-range missiles and nuclear weapons. But now, the very rules of war had changed. What if an enemy could disregard distance and teleport directly into Huaxia’s heartland, even into its major cities?
What could Huaxia do then? Would long-range missiles and nuclear weapons still be a deterrent? Making this comparison, Wang Lan realized their advantages couldn’t be leveraged, while their disadvantages were unavoidable.
"So what shall we do?"
"Fight! What else can we do? Even if it comes down to the last person, we must resist. Human civilization began its rise five thousand years ago and has stubbornly persisted until today under the threat of the Demon Clan.
Our ancestors passed down civilization even in times of technological inferiority; we can do it too. To inherit civilization and protect humanity. This is the mission of us soldiers and also that of you Star Martial Warriors."
"Human civilization is a colossal machine, and we Star Martial Warriors are the armor on this machine. Every person is a part of the machine, and the existence of Star Martial Warriors is to protect this machine from harm..." Wang Lan muttered the Star Martial Warrior’s declaration in a low voice, reflecting the faith of a Star Martial Warrior.
"Demons, demons—" Suddenly, a child in the car started to scream frantically. Following their gaze, a soul-shaking scene appeared before Wang Lan’s eyes.
Out from the depths of the dense forest, there emerged a humanoid creature with a green head resembling an otherworldly being. Its occiput and back merged into one entity. It was over two meters tall, its legs folded and bent backward, which made it clear that this monster possessed powerful jumping capabilities.
On its ferocious face was a lamprey-like maw bristling with sharp teeth. Sharp spikes protruded from the tips of its fingers, and from its appearance alone, one could tell it was a warrior born for combat.
"Demon Clan warrior... Drive fast!" Wang Lan’s face instantly changed, and the moment his words landed, the bus roared and sped forward abruptly.
Breaking free from the slope, the bus entered the gravel plain, and the Demon Clan warriors behind it swiftly gave chase.
They chased the bus by running and leaping, their speed comparable to a cheetah’s. The bus had no brakes, so all Qin Weimin could do was use his exquisite driving skills to keep the bus balanced.
On the shimmering gravel, the bus couldn’t go fast. The strong vibrations from traveling at eighty miles per hour on the rocky terrain nearly made Wang Lan vomit last night’s dinner.
Several children in the bus weren’t faring so well, with quite a few of them vomiting all over. Instantly, the acrid stench of vomit filled the bus, triggering a chain reaction of sickness.
The current situation made Wang Lan’s nerves tighten. Casting aside all other considerations, he knew he was the only one who could protect the children on this bus.
Accessing the system, he saw he had seventy skill points left and frenziedly added them to the Inch Strength Fist skill.
Bronze LV5.
Bronze LV6.
Bronze LV8.
Bronze LV9.
With only ten points left, he aimed to upgrade the skill to the silver level. However, after adding nine points, the last skill point just wouldn’t apply, no matter how he tried.
Damn it, why was it one point short?
Perhaps this was related to his own cultivation level; that was his only guess. If skill level upgrades weren’t limited by character level, could a Starlight 1 individual possess silver, gold, or even platinum-ranked skills? He could only surmise that his Inch Strength Fist couldn’t be upgraded to silver because of the limitations imposed by his Starlight cultivation boundary. From another perspective, reaching Bronze LV9 was the peak for skill upgrades within the Starlight boundary. This meant his Inch Strength Fist was now at the highest level achievable for someone at his cultivation. He couldn’t quite estimate just how strong it had become.
"Wang Lan, have we lost them?" Qin Weimin suddenly cried out anxiously.
"Not yet, but if we maintain this speed, they won’t catch up to us."
"That’s no good!"
"What’s wrong? Are we out of gas?"
"Ahead is Dead Gorge; there’s no way out."
"What?" Wang Lan turned his head abruptly. He saw the gravel flat becoming narrower, hemmed in by cliff walls on both sides. In the direction the bus was heading, a sheer cliff face loomed. The bus had driven into a dead-end pocket.
"Brake, brake hard, stop—"
"The brakes are broken; we can’t stop—"
BOOM—
A fierce collision sounded as the bus smashed directly into the cliff. Instantly, there was another round of children’s wailing and howling. These children, pampered by their parents, had never experienced such dangers.
"Mr. Qin, are you okay?"
"My arm is a bit hurt, might be dislocated. I’m alright..."
"Open the door!"
"What are you going to do?"
"I’ll hold the entrance to the gorge, try to buy as much time as possible. Whether we can survive depends on when the rescue team outside arrives."
Qin Weimin looked deeply at Wang Lan. "Brother, take care!"
Wang Lan immediately jumped off the bus and went to the rear. The environs of the gorge were like the back entrance of a stadium—Wang Lan had to guard the entrance from the outside. Not a single Demon Clan warrior could be allowed in, not even one.
"Big brother... come back, what are you doing... You came with me, you said you’d listen to me..." Song Jia’s cries came from the bus.
"Jia Jia, I have good news for you. Big brother has awakened the Star Martial Warrior talent, so from now on, please call me a Star Martial Warrior! Don’t worry, I’ll protect you."
ROAR—
ROAR—
The roars, one after another, came from afar. The pursuing Demon Clan warriors weren’t as numerous as at the start, but there were still nine of them. Nine Demon Clan warriors, facing someone who had just awakened their Star Martial talent the day before, was indeed a tough challenge.
As the Demon Clan warriors approached Wang Lan, they slowed their pace, their blood-red eyes staring at him. Although they were slowing down, the aura of slaughter emanating from their bodies grew even denser.
Fear spread through Wang Lan’s heart, his pulse pounding violently. Suddenly, as if he had reached a critical threshold, the tension in his muscles eased. Wang Lan seemed to enter a state of serene clarity.
Some people stiffen up completely in the face of dire terror.
Others unleash incredible potential in the face of dire terror.
Wang Lan was the latter; after breaking through the critical threshold of fear, his body entered a state of extreme calm and heightened agility.
And in that instant, a Demon leaped high into the air, its sharp chitinous spike aiming a stab at Wang Lan’s face.
Wang Lan appeared stunned, motionless as if petrified, while a look of disdain and cruelty spread across the Demon’s face.
But in a flash, Wang Lan lightly swerved, avoiding the spike and simultaneously delivering a fierce punch to the Demon’s chest. The evasion was also an attack, the timing and speed achieving a perfect balance.
The Bronze LV9 Inch Strength Fist erupted. The terrifying punch power, combined with the force of the Demon’s descent, almost instantly caved in the Demon’s chest armor. Then, with a sickening crack, a huge hole burst open in the Demon’s back, and its internal organs sprayed out like the contents of a squeezed boil.
The green blood exuded a pungent, foul stench. The few Demons who were gearing up to pounce halted in their steps, their blood-red eyes fixed on Wang Lan.
Killing a low-level Demon Clan soldier, skill points +1, experience points +10.
WHIRR—
A warm current flowed through Wang Lan’s body as the experience points filled up, and Wang Lan leveled up to Starlight 2 in an instant.
A character leveling up is most directly reflected by the enhancement of physical fitness. Although this enhancement was minuscule compared to the transformation from a normal person to a Star Martial Warrior, even a slight increase in strength was an additional glimmer of hope for survival.
Wang Lan bent down slightly, grabbed the chitinous spike from the Demon’s arm, and with a forceful twist, broke it off, holding it in his hand as a makeshift weapon.
"ROAR—" Accompanied by a roar from one behind him, two more Demon Warriors once again stepped forward slowly, closing in.

chapters.title: Chapter 12 The Man Who Created Miracles
chapters.content:
Chapter 12: Chapter 12 The Man Who Created Miracles
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
Two Demon Warriors, one to the left and the other to the right, charged at him, their intention clear: a pincer attack from front and rear. If he employed conventional combat strategies, Wang Lan, a Star Martial Warrior at the Starlight Stage, would stand no chance of surviving such an assault.
Even at that moment, Wang Lan had already prepared himself for certain death.
A newly awakened Star Martial Warrior, fallen into a Demon Clan trap, facing a group of their warriors while protecting a bus of twenty-five children.
It would be extremely difficult for anyone in Wang Lan’s situation to survive.
I’m a transmigrator, my legendary life hasn’t even started yet, how can I die just as the story begins?
Such thoughts had no place in this dire situation.
Since it’s death either way, I might as well take one down with me.
As this thought crossed his mind, the two Demons attacked from front and rear.
Wang Lan’s advantage was that, although a newly awakened Star Martial Warrior, he had been diligently practicing for years; his combat skills had not fallen behind his peers. In fact, his close-combat skills were even superior to those of some at the Star Shine Stage.
Even without relying on Star Martial Skills, Wang Lan was formidable. And since the lower-level Demons lacked the talent for Star Martial Skills, this narrowed the gap between them.
The Demon in front aimed to pin Wang Lan down while the one behind prepared a killing blow. Such combat coordination was ingrained in their very marrow. Thus, as the Demon Armor in front thrust towards Wang Lan, the Demon in the rear suddenly accelerated its own thrust.
Wang Lan’s body moved instantaneously. He executed his Bronze-level movement technique and, moving faster than the Demon, dodged the incoming armor spine. He then closed in on the Demon’s chest and hurled a punch.
BOOM—
The terrifying internal energy of the Inch Strength Fist exploded within the Demon’s body. At that moment, Wang Lan dared not hesitate, as the armor spine of the Demon beside him had already pierced his shoulder. Instantly, he spun around. With his left hand, he tore off the armor spine that had pierced him, transforming it into a streak of cold light. This light stabbed into the eye socket of the sneak-attacking Demon, piercing through the eye and exiting from the back of its skull.
This exchange lasted only five seconds. Wang Lan’s arm was drenched in blood, having traded an arm for the lives of two Demons.
In just a short amount of time, three Demon Warriors had been dispatched.
The remaining six Demons began to re-evaluate Wang Lan. Based on an assessment of his strength, Wang Lan should be at the lowest tier among Star Martial Warriors.
But could a bottom-tier Star Martial Warrior really kill three Demon Warriors in such a short time?
Have we Demons regressed over the years, or have humans progressed this rapidly?
Inside the bus, Song Jia’s eyes were swollen from crying. When she saw the blood flowing down Wang Lan’s arm like a stream, she closed her eyes, unable to watch.
Inside the bus, Qin Weimin watched Wang Lan with bloodshot eyes, his jaw clenched tightly and veins bulging on his forehead.
Those two exchanges—Wang Lan had performed beautifully. Truly beautifully!
In terms of raw strength, Wang Lan could barely hold his own against a single Demon Warrior. But in those fleeting seconds, Wang Lan had killed three with lightning speed.
This was an achievement far beyond what Wang Lan should have been capable of.
If it weren’t for this desperate situation, if Wang Lan didn’t have to face so many Demons alone, I would be seeing the sapling of a future towering tree,
Qin Weimin thought.
Moreover, the sight of Wang Lan’s slender yet upright figure continuously brought to Qin Weimin’s mind faces deeply buried in his memory.
"Commissioner Qin, rest assured, I’ll definitely bring you back."
"Commissioner Qin, go that way, keep going, don’t stop. After twenty kilometers, someone will meet you... I’m sorry, I misspoke... My brothers have all honored their duty, and now it’s my turn... This medal, please give it to my parents for me, tell them I didn’t bring disgrace to the Lao Niu family..."
That time, Qin Weimin had been ambushed by international mercenaries, forced to land outside the borders of Jade Country. An escort team, outnumbered and with insufficient ammunition, had safely escorted him back to the country while pursued by the mercenaries.
But that escort team... not even their bodies had made it back to the land they cherished.
Weren’t those men back then so very similar to the young man before me now?
Wang Lan’s arm was injured; he could no longer execute the splendid desperate counterattacks he had managed earlier. Perhaps in the next second, he would vanish like an exploding firework.
"Wang Lan..."
Another two Demon Warriors suddenly charged at Wang Lan. This time, they didn’t split up for a pincer attack. With one arm incapacitated, the Demons believed Wang Lan no longer possessed the strength to kill them.
A mere Starlight Stage Star Martial Warrior has actually killed three of our Demon Warriors!
We’ll savor eating this detestable human bit by bit later, just like eating spicy strips,
the Demons had already decided.
Two armor spines stabbed at Wang Lan’s vital points. In the next second, he would be skewered like a string of candied hawthorns. But in an instant, Wang Lan’s body vanished.
Just as confusion flickered in the Demons’ minds, a surge of intense pain shot through their lower abdomens. Wang Lan had somehow crouched down, unnoticed. Still agile enough to dodge their attacks from this position, he then launched an upward assault, both fists striking the abdomens of the two Demon Warriors.
BOOM—Follow current novels on NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
"Impossible..." The Demon Warrior’s blood-red eyes bulged, its face a mask of disbelief.
His arm was clearly disabled! That armor spine definitely pierced his shoulder! With a pierced shoulder, his fist shouldn’t be able to generate any force! But how could he still deliver such a punch? And with both hands simultaneously?
Sitting inside the vehicle, Qin Weimin also widened his eyes, his face full of disbelief. He was a weapons expert and also an expert on human anatomy. Only with a clear understanding of the human body could one design powerful personal weapons suitable for human operation.
This was especially true for the exoskeleton armor he was currently researching, which demanded a complete understanding of human muscle kinematics.
With Wang Lan’s shoulder pierced, Qin Weimin believed it impossible for his arm to even be raised, let alone throw a punch. Yet, the scene unfolding before him clearly showed Wang Lan not only punching but also, in an unexpected instant, killing two Demons.
In the next moment, Qin Weimin’s eyes lit up again. He saw that although Wang Lan’s arm was still dripping, the blood flow had stopped. The originally gruesome wound had vanished, leaving not even a scar.
A Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior?
In an instant, this thought flashed through Qin Weimin’s mind like lightning.
He isn’t just a perceptive, genius Star Martial Warrior, but also an extremely rare Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior? Damn it, why did such a treasure have to fall into these dire straits? If Wang Lan can survive, his value is far greater than my own...
At that moment, Qin Weimin wished he could have taken Wang Lan’s place.
ROAR—
Angry roars erupted as the remaining four Demons became furious.
A low-level human had actually killed five of them—five!
And not by stealthy ambushes, but killed in direct combat! If their opponent had been a powerful warrior, they might have accepted it. But this was just a despicable, low-level warrior!
The Demons were enraged. Shamelessly, all four charged at Wang Lan simultaneously.
Face? Demons had no need for such a thing.
With all four Demons charging at once, the previous hit-and-run tactics were no longer effective. But regardless, even if he died, he could still take one down with him.
A murderous gleam shone in Wang Lan’s eyes; each Demon was a target to drag down with him.
You! The one charging at the very front!
Instantly, Wang Lan moved. A knife-hand strike parried one Demon’s armor spine, and he landed a fierce punch on that Demon’s chest.
BOOM—
PFFT—
Simultaneously, another Demon’s armor spine pierced Wang Lan’s back.
The stabbing pain, far from inciting despair, instead triggered something wild within Wang Lan. He twisted his body, muscles clenching around the embedded armor spine, and snapped it. Then, he threw a punch that exploded the head of the Demon who had ambushed him.
PFFT—
PFFT—
Two more armor spines plunged into Wang Lan’s chest, embedding themselves over an inch deep.
Blood gushed from his chest, drenching his torso in a warmth like the sun.
"KILL—!" Wang Lan’s eyes instantly became bloodshot as a thunderous roar erupted from him.
His roar momentarily stunned two Demon Warriors. Seizing this fleeting opportunity, Wang Lan, fueled by lingering fury and summoned potential, threw two punches, killing both Demons on the spot.
Nine Demon Warriors, all killed by an early Starlight Stage Star Martial Warrior. If word got out, no one would believe it.
Yet, this incredible feat had truly unfolded right before Qin Weimin’s eyes.
At that moment, Qin Weimin could no longer care about the danger. He leaped from the bus and rushed to Wang Lan’s side.
"Brother, how are you?"
Wang Lan’s legs gave out, and he collapsed against Qin Weimin. The wounds to his chest and back would have been fatal for any other Star Martial Warrior, but not for Wang Lan. He possessed Healing Star Martial Arts.
Unfortunately, he had too little ’blue’ left. He had just managed to stabilize the fatal wounds when his energy reserves bottomed out.
"Soul Bead... Soul..."
Qin Weimin understood that for a Star Martial Warrior, a Soul Bead was a life-saving Dan. But without a blade, he couldn’t crack open the skulls of Exotic Beasts to retrieve Soul Beads. To make matters worse, three more Demon Warriors had arrived. Though initially cowed by Wang Lan’s killing spree, they now began to slowly advance as Wang Lan fell.
Qin Weimin snatched up a nearby stone and stood protectively before Wang Lan, exuding the gallant spirit of ’a single brick in hand, and the world is mine.’
"Brother, this time, I’ll buy you time! You have Medical Attribute Star Martial Arts, right? Heal up quickly! I might not be able to hold them off for long."
At this moment, Wang Lan just wanted to say,
Cut the melodrama! Just give me a few Soul Beads, that’s what’s real!
No sooner had this thought settled than three Soul Beads suddenly landed in front of Wang Lan, rolling into his hand.
Huh... did I make a wish to the Dragon God?
Wang Lan looked up in confusion. Floating silently above him was a mysterious woman in a tactical vest and white mask.
"Wind Blade Net!" Her voice, like a judgment from heaven and earth, accompanied a gale that erupted from her, forming a tornado. Crescent-shaped wind blades swirled within the tornado, instantly rushing towards the three Demon Warriors.
When the tornado passed, the gravel on the ground had turned to sand. Where the three Demons had stood, only three Soul Beads now remained.
"What are you still dazed for? Do you want to die?" the woman in the sky chided in a low voice, seeing Wang Lan still stupefied.
"Um... how do I absorb a Soul Bead?" Wang Lan asked, a question so basic it nearly made the woman plummet from the sky.

chapters.title: Chapter 13: I Want to Eat 10 Portions
chapters.content:
Chapter 13: Chapter 13: I Want to Eat 10 Portions
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
"You’re the first person I’ve come across who doesn’t know how to absorb a Soul Bead. Are you really a Star Martial Warrior?" The speaker was a woman with long, flowing hair; judging by her voice, she was quite young.
Although she was wearing a mask and her face couldn’t be seen, Wang Lan imagined she must be a valiant and handsome female warrior.
"I only awakened yesterday, so it’s only natural I don’t understand."
"But you don’t look like you’re thirteen or fourteen. Hold the Soul Bead in your palm, sense the Star Power within, and try to move it."
Following her instructions, Wang Lan tried it. He found it incredibly easy; like sucking jelly, he SLURPED the Star Power from the Soul Bead into his body. Moreover, the pure Star Power was instantly assimilated by Wang Lan’s own Star Power.
Skill point +1.
Wang Lan hadn’t expected that Soul Beads, besides replenishing Star Power, could actually grant skill points.
Does the system expect me to slay Demons or Exotic Beasts in the future?
With the new Star Power, the Self Healing skill activated once again.
"Zeng Xiaomo, Captain of the Starlight Team, 3rd Squad, 1st Task Force of the Suzhou City Tianjian Bureau’s Action Department, reporting to Director Qin. Is Director Qin unharmed?"
"Thanks to this young man, I’m okay. However, there must be many Demon Warriors still in the secret realm, so you should be extra careful."
"Don’t worry, not a single Demon in the secret realm will survive," Zeng Xiaomo’s tone was light, but the overbearing aura in her words was unmistakable.
A woman showing off is truly more pleasing to the eye than a man doing the same.
WHIRR—
There was a sudden tremor in his mind. "Mission: Guard complete. Rewards: 1,000 experience points, 100 skill points."
The moment the notification sounded, Wang Lan instantly felt a warm current flow through his body, keenly aware of the increase in strength. He quickly dived into the system for a swift look and saw he had risen by two levels, reaching Starlight Level 4.
Wang Lan had no idea how long it normally took for a first-time awakener to reach Starlight Level 4, as this ten-level distinction only existed for him.
However, Wang Lan knew that most senior students from the Star Martial Arts Campus were still at the Starlight Stage. Only the top third managed to reach the power of the Star Shine Stage before graduation.
In just one day, he had reached Starlight Level 4.
If he had a few more experiences like this, could he catch up with his peers by the start of the school year?
At this thought, Wang Lan suddenly felt a chill.
Yes, to possess such talent was terrifying, even to himself.
A phrase even surfaced in his mind:
"This boy is too demonic; he absolutely cannot be allowed to live!"
He shivered.
However, he suddenly felt a pair of eyes on him and looked up to find Zeng Xiaomo curiously observing him.
"Miss Zeng... is... is there a problem?"
"Did you just have a breakthrough?" Zeng Xiaomo’s eyes, like pearls, fixed on Wang Lan’s. "You’ve only absorbed three Soul Beads and advanced from the early to the mid-Starlight Stage?"
"No... not yet to the mid-stage," Wang Lan hastened to deny, though he wasn’t lying.
Mid-stage is level five, right? Being one level short still means there’s a gap. I didn’t lie.
"What are you afraid of?" Zeng Xiaomo snorted coldly. "You weren’t afraid when fighting nine Demon Clan warriors alone, and now you’re scared?"
"I didn’t have time to be scared then, did I?" Wang Lan pointed to the Demon corpses on the ground. "These are the warriors of the Demon Clan? The ones invading us? They’re indeed very strong."
"They are the lowest-ranking bioengineered soldiers, not true Demon Clan warriors. They can be mass-produced, like cannon fodder, just as we manufacture firearms. A true Demon Clan warrior... anyone below the Star Shine Stage facing them means certain death. So, you’re quite lucky."
"That’s true. Surviving really is a miracle." Wang Lan didn’t want to dwell on the subject and quickly ran back to the bus.
The children’s crying had stopped. Song Jia was tightly clutching her own arm, searching for injuries, only to be puzzled by the absence of any wound where one should have been.
"Jiajia, your brother’s awakened Star Martial Skill talent is an Undying Body. Cool, huh?"
"Really?" Song Jia was young and gullible. Though normally cunning, she tended to believe what people told her when it came to serious matters.
"Absolutely!" Wang Lan patted Song Jia’s head. "I didn’t expect you liked me so much. You cried so terribly when I was nearly killed."
"Not at all! I brought you out, so I had to bring you back. If you were gone, Mom would’ve killed me. You’re annoying! Don’t tease me about that in the future, or else... I’ll bite you."
"Okay, okay. Jiajia..."
"Hmm?"
"Why are you pinching me?"
"To see if the Undying Body is real!"
"..."
"Stop pinching, it still hurts!"
Wang Lan kept looking out the back of the bus, where Qin Weimin was recounting the incident to Zeng Xiaomo.
Suddenly, shadowy figures flickered in the distance, moving rapidly. Though there seemed to be only about twenty people, their sprinting conveyed the momentum of an army of thousands charging forward.
Each one wore a mask, their bodies stained with green blood.
"Are they all dealt with?"
"Dealt with. We also found seven or eight survivors in a canyon on the other side of the dense forest. They were lucky; they hid in some burrows and escaped disaster," a man reported to Zeng Xiaomo.
Soon enough, seven or eight parents were brought over by some members of the Tianjian Bureau.
"Mom—"
"Uncle—"
Excited cries came from the children on the bus, but Wang Lan’s expression abruptly darkened. He swiftly stood up and jumped off the bus.
"Brother..."
"Don’t worry, I’ll be right back."
After jumping off the bus, Wang Lan strode over to Qin Weimin’s side.
"Wang Lan, what’s wrong?" Seeing Wang Lan’s solemn expression, Qin Weimin asked with a tinge of nervousness.
"There might be something wrong with those people. Do you remember Mr. Qiu?"
Qin Weimin’s face changed. He quietly approached Zeng Xiaomo and the man, whispering something. The two nodded and swiftly moved towards the eight approaching parents.
"Pull the window curtains on the bus so the children can’t see. It would be too traumatic for them; I’m afraid it might cause psychological damage," Qin Weimin hastily instructed.
Wang Lan saw Zeng Xiaomo and the others take the seven or eight parents to a more secluded spot. After only a few seconds, the sound of intense combat erupted. However, it wasn’t long before the two returned, their expressions grave.
"The Demon Clan’s goal is likely to infiltrate spies among the human race."
That one sentence was heavy. Anyone could infer that the Demon Clan had already begun to take action and that a new war might have already begun. Yet, no one dared to utter the word ’war’.
"Are all the children alright?"
"All twenty-five children are fine. Of the fifty people on the bus, eighteen parents were killed. Five injured parents haven’t left the bus. Among the adults, only Wang Lan and I are okay," Qin Weimin said solemnly.
"This debt of blood will, sooner or later, be reclaimed from the Demon Clan. Director Qin, let’s go. Can the bus still be driven?"
"No, it can’t."
"Everyone take a child! Let’s evacuate!"
Song Jia, of course, was carried on Wang Lan’s back. He ran madly along with the Tianjian Bureau warriors. The space around them had begun to warp, threatening to collapse at any moment, and they had to escape before that happened.
The children were crying out for their moms and dads. The young ones were not even considering, or perhaps dared not contemplate, that their parents might never return.
Wang Lan felt immensely sorry for these children but was powerless to help them.
This was the chaos of war—the saying that one would rather be a dog in times of peace than a human in times of turmoil was no empty talk.
With the assistance of the Tianjian Bureau, Wang Lan and the others successfully escaped the collapsing space. They returned to the Ring City National Highway, where seven or eight military vehicles were parked by the roadside. The group boarded the vehicles, which started up and quickly departed.
It was only at this moment that Wang Lan’s heart truly began to calm down.
He had awakened his Star Martial Warrior talent only yesterday, and today he had already encountered such a thrilling event. Though the world of Star Martial Warriors was never short of danger and death, this had all come too quickly.
In the vehicle, Jiajia fell asleep in Wang Lan’s arms. As he looked out the window at the rapidly receding scenery, he slowly closed his eyes to rest.
