The sound of braking woke Wang Lan from his drowsiness. "Where are we?"
"The military hospital. Everyone needs to undergo examinations and treatment. The Demon Clan’s methods aren’t limited to killing—they have many plots and schemes beyond our imagination," Zeng Xiaomo said flatly.
A series of blood tests, ultrasounds, CT scans, and X-rays took more than an hour. Afterward, Wang Lan was placed in a separate ward to be questioned by the Tianjian Bureau. Although Qin Weimin had already given a brief account of the events, Wang Lan had to recount them again. It wasn’t until 4:30 in the afternoon that he was told he could leave.
"I’m hungry!" On the way back, Song Jia suddenly clutched her stomach.
"We haven’t eaten anything since breakfast. I’m hungry too. What do you want to eat?"
Song Jia pointed at a barbecue restaurant in front of them.
"Okay!"
"I want two steaks."
"No, let’s get ten!"
The meal cost a thousand yuan. Besides the ten portions of steak, they ordered a variety of other dishes as if they were free. However, these frenzied orders didn’t faze the well-trained waitstaff.
The appetite of a Star Martial Warrior could allow one to consume an entire cow in a single meal. Therefore, the staff were accustomed to clients like Wang Lan. The existence of Star Martial Warriors also meant the food and beverage industry was always one of the most profitable in this world.
Even running a noodle shop would be a sure profit, as long as the owner didn’t make a strategic blunder.
After dropping Song Jia off at home, Wang Lan intended to leave, but Song Jia was scared, so he agreed to stay and keep her company. After showering and changing into pajamas, the two played video games in front of the TV, unaware that the sky had already turned dark.
"Why hasn’t Mrs. Feng come back to cook?"
"You forgot you were supposed to be at Sky Curtain Lake for two days. There’s no one at home, so Mrs. Feng must have gone back to her own place. She won’t be back until tomorrow afternoon. Are you hungry again?"
"Today’s steak was really delicious. It’s the first time I’ve realized how good steak can be."
"You, you should be starved a bit; otherwise, your picky eating habits will never be cured. People who have never truly been hungry don’t understand how blissful it is just to fill one’s stomach."
"You speak as if you’ve been hungry before..." Song Jia, now fully revived, not only talked back but also rolled her eyes at him.
"I really have been hungry!" Wang Lan replied with a slight smile. He recalled a time from his previous life when he had gone out to find work. His money was stolen, leaving him with only two hundred yuan. He had to survive on that for a whole month until he received his first paycheck.Follow current ɴᴏᴠᴇʟs on ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
Suddenly, his phone vibrated. Wang Lan stood up and answered, "Hello, Auntie, you’re back in the country?"
"Where are you? I’ve been looking all over the hospital for you!"
"I’m not at the hospital; I’ve gone home."
"Stay at home and don’t wander off," Auntie commanded, then hung up.

chapters.title: Chapter 14 You Are the Son of the Flame Emperor
chapters.content:
Chapter 14: Chapter 14 You Are the Son of the Flame Emperor
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
It was less than half an hour before the entrance door to his aunt’s house opened. Windblown and dusty, his aunt, Wang Qi, walked in, her eyes frantically searching the living room. Her face relaxed only after she saw that both children were there.
"Mom—" Song Jia hurriedly dropped the remote control and opened her arms to hug Wang Qi.
"Mom, I missed you so much! Mom, let me tell you, today you almost lost your precious baby! If it weren’t for Wang Lan, everyone on our bus would have died. Wang Lan was the Knight who saved this princess, so I didn’t argue with him today."
Wang Lan, sitting on the sofa, felt the corners of his mouth twitch slightly.
During the bus ride, being called ’brother’ felt so satisfying, yet not even two hours after getting home, she’s back to calling me Wang Lan directly. This girl... I really shouldn’t have been nice to her.
"Let Mom have a look, are you hurt anywhere? I was scared out of my wits when I got the call in Han City. I got off the plane, called to find out you were at the military hospital, and rushed over, only to learn that both of you had already gone home... It’s good that you’re fine. It’s good that you’re fine."
Wang Qi, who always appeared so strong, was indeed thoroughly frightened. These two children were her only relatives in the world. If something had truly happened to them, she wouldn’t have known what to do.
"You watch TV for a bit; I want to talk to your brother." Wang Qi hugged Song Jia tightly and kissed her twice before standing up and waving towards Wang Lan. "Lan, come here for a second."
Wang Lan obediently walked over, following Wang Qi to the balcony. "Auntie!"
"When did you awaken?" Wang Qi stared intently into Wang Lan’s eyes. "Awakening is such a big deal, how could you not tell me?"
"I just awakened yesterday."
"Yesterday? How did it happen? Tell me the details." Wang Qi’s eyes suddenly brightened. Apart from being Song Jia’s mother and Wang Lan’s aunt, she was also the CEO of Jiayi Biotechnology Company and a top genetic biologist in Jade Country.
"It was yesterday when the final exam results were handed out. I scored four hundred sixty points, again the top scorer in the city. I got so happy, so excited, that I awakened."
If word of this got out, countless parents might whip their children to death. Listen to this—do well on an exam, get excited, and awaken a Star Martial Warrior’s talent? Sleep? Play games? Dream on! Get up and study all night, you hear me!
Then, countless hardworking students would crowdfund to sacrifice the ’Study God’ to the heavens. A creature like that shouldn’t be allowed to live!
"TSK TSK TSK..." His aunt gave Wang Lan an appraising look from head to toe. "The Soul Resonance couldn’t trigger your Star Martial Warrior talent, but a single exam gets you excited enough to awaken? Now I’m wondering if there’s a flaw in the Soul Resonance Technology, or if there’s something special about you."
His aunt’s gaze was frightening.
Especially when she licked the corner of her mouth with her tongue... it makes me want to turn and run. She’s a total Orochimaru!
"Auntie... I think I should be normal..."
"It’s not about what you think; it’s about what I think. My research into biological gene coding just encountered some problems..."
"Auntie, I suddenly remembered I have something to do at home. I’ll take my leave now, goodbye!"
"Stop right there! You’re staying here tonight!" his aunt commanded in an undeniable tone.
"Oh."
"Then I’ll go play with Jiajia," Wang Lan smiled and turned to leave.
Wang Qi folded her arms, muttering to herself regardless of whether Wang Lan heard, "
Do well on an exam, get excited, and awaken? Who’s he trying to fool? From the first grade, when has he not done well? Every time it’s either a perfect score or top of the class. Is he still excited by that? He’d probably only get excited if he flunked!
"
Mrs. Feng had gone back to her hometown, and Wang Qi couldn’t cook. Fortunately, there was something in this world called takeout. Wang Qi ordered more than a dozen dishes from a local restaurant to be delivered, knowing the appetite of a newly awakened Star Martial Warrior.
When she was a child, her sister Wang Ling had performed a feat in front of Wang Qi: devouring a pig in three bites. Wang Qi had been so frightened that she didn’t dare sleep in the same bed as Wang Ling for half a month, fearing she would wake up in the middle of the night to see a pair of glowing green eyes, and then be eaten in three bites herself.
Thinking of her sister Wang Ling, Wang Qi’s eyes darkened slightly. What had seemed like ordinary life back then could now only be relived in memories.
After dinner and a bath, Wang Lan returned to his room to look up the process for applying for a Star Martial Badge online. Each Star Martial Warrior had to independently apply for a Star Martial Warrior ID, and their previous ID would be canceled and voided.
"Lan, come here a moment," Wang Qi, dressed in a cool silk nightgown, knocked on Wang Lan’s door.
"Okay."
Wang Lan stood up, opened the door, and followed Wang Qi. His aunt had also just showered; her hair was still damp. Nearing forty, Wang Qi bore no traces of age.
She was beautiful, mature, and charming. With memories and a soul from two lifetimes, Wang Lan naturally knew how to appreciate her beauty. But appreciation was just that. His only curiosity was why his aunt hadn’t found another boyfriend over the years.
The two of them went out to the balcony, leaning on the railing and looking at the distant city lights, both silent. Wang Qi in this pose was particularly alluring, and Wang Lan had to avert his gaze to the distance.
"How long has Sister been gone?" Wang Qi suddenly asked softly.
"Seven years and eight months," Wang Lan replied without a second’s hesitation.
"Nearly eight years, huh... Back then, you were only this tall..." His aunt gestured to a height and smiled. "You children are more thoughtful than adults sometimes. Such a big thing happened, and you didn’t even make a fuss. If I hadn’t heard you crying those nights, I would have thought you were heartless."
"I wanted to cry too, but Mom said crying is a sign of weakness, and she didn’t want to raise a good-for-nothing."
"Sister might still be alive," Wang Qi suddenly said, turning to look at Wang Lan.
What surprised her, however, was the lack of any change in Wang Lan’s expression. There was only a faint smile at the corner of his lips, from which Wang Qi read a clear meaning—
Just as I thought!
"You knew all along?" Wang Qi asked in a low voice.
"Auntie, I am, after all, the guy known as the ’Study God’ by a hundred thousand elementary school students. Please, don’t doubt my intelligence, okay? If Mom really died on a mission, why did you insist on telling me about her fate only after I graduated from junior high?
"Before junior high graduation, there’s a Soul Resonance ceremony. Therefore, the answer you’d give me had two possibilities. Which one you told me depended on whether I could awaken the Star Martial Warrior talent.
"Since you told me Mom died on a mission, then the other answer must be that she’s still alive, right?"
"What a smart child," Wang Qi sighed softly. "However, I’m also not sure if your mother is still alive. She’s just missing—has been for nearly eight years. Everything about your mother is highly classified. Even I can’t inquire or ask about it. So... her whereabouts are up to you to investigate.
"Once you become a Star Martial Warrior, you’ll have the chance to access these secrets. All I know is that your mother had an incredibly important mission back then, and then she never returned."
"Okay, I will," Wang Lan nodded.
"Do you understand your mother well?" Wang Qi suddenly smiled and asked.
"What do you mean? She’s my mom. How could I not understand her?"
"You know she’s a Star Martial Warrior, but do you know what level of Star Martial Warrior she was?"
"That..." Wang Lan shook his head; he honestly didn’t know. His mother was very strict with her belongings and never allowed Wang Lan to go through them. Moreover, she never brought anything work-related home, including her Star Martial Badge, work identification, or even her uniform and combat suit.
Every time Wang Ling came home, she was dressed like a professional woman from the city. She spent at least two hundred days a year away on missions. The only thing he knew was that his mom was very stern and had a very dominant personality.
"Among the Star Martial Warriors of Jade Country, the most elite ones all have titles. And among these titled Star Martial Warriors, the Five Elders and Five Emperors are the most famous, and they are the pillars of Jade Country’s international standing.
"You should know about the Five Elders. They are five Elders who hold immense prestige among Star Martial Warriors, and their influence can change the entire Star Martial Art landscape of Jade Country.
"The Five Emperors are the five individuals with the highest combat capabilities in Jade Country: the Eastern Azure Emperor, the Southern Flame Emperor, the Western White Emperor, the Northern Nether Emperor, and the Central Mysterious Emperor. Your mother, my sister Wang Ling, held the title of Southern Flame Emperor."
Wang Lan’s eyes contracted violently. On his usually calm face, an expression of utter astonishment finally appeared.
The person with the absolute top fighting power in Jade Country... the very, very top... person...
This was something Wang Lan couldn’t bring himself to believe, no matter what. Wang Ling had only been thirty when she disappeared. Although the peak age for Star Martial Warriors was indeed between thirty and forty, Wang Lan still found it incredible that his mother was among the strongest Star Martial Warriors in Jade Country.
A woman, an ordinary woman.
Without family backing, resources, connections, or an Inborn Talent of the Bloodline, how did she achieve such heights at that age?
It’s simply impossible!
Wang Lan thought.
Two lifetimes of experience told him this wasn’t an era just after a war, where many empty spaces allowed people to rise arbitrarily. The social structure was now tightly knit, wealth and resources highly concentrated.
High-ranking families don’t have impoverished scholars among them, and low-ranking families don’t produce nobles.
A commoner genius could rise, could climb high—Wang Lan believed that. But for a commoner genius to climb to the very pinnacle in a short time through sheer effort alone was nearly impossible.
You’re a genius, but aren’t others? You work hard, but don’t those from Star Martial Warrior families also work hard? The difference in talent among top geniuses is limited, and so is the difference in effort. What truly widens the gap is resources—wealth. Unless you’re such a genius that you can disregard resources and wealth entirely... Was Mom truly a genius to that extent?
"Hard to believe, isn’t it?" Wang Qi asked with a smile.
"Not exactly, just a bit unexpected. If Mom was the Southern Flame Emperor, then her disappearance must have been a huge deal for Jade Country, right? Why wasn’t there any news about it back then?"
"How could the country possibly report such a thing? I can even tell you that in the eyes of foreign countries, the Flame Emperor is merely on a certain mission, or perhaps she’s a high-ranking official in our country, maybe even working at the Ministry of Defense. In the entire world, probably no more than a hundred people know about your mother’s disappearance."
"’True,’ Wang Lan mused. ’But still, Mom was so incredible, yet she left me practically nothing... Not a single Star Martial Skill at home, not even a Soul Bead. Didn’t she know how to save for the family?’"
"Didn’t she leave you three office buildings in the CBD? Plus a commercial plaza in Modu City, and two in the Imperial Capital."
"’Money is an external possession. What’s the use of having more? I mean Star Martial Skills, secret techniques...’"
"Hmph! If your mother had really left you such things, do you think you’d still be alive? You’d have been sliced into eighteen pieces long ago!"
So that’s how it is...
Wang Lan instantly understood, but still felt it was a pity.
With such an incredible mom, it’s a shame she didn’t leave any real inheritance for her son.
Wang Lan sighed softly.
"However, your mother did leave you something," Wang Qi said, turning to point at a box on the balcony coffee table. "Your mom entrusted this to me before she left. She said she didn’t know when she’d be back, and if she hadn’t returned after a few years, and you had awakened your Star Martial Warrior talent, then I was to give it to you."

chapters.title: Chapter 15 Platinum Grade Star Martial Skill
chapters.content:
Chapter 15: Chapter 15 Platinum Grade Star Martial Skill
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
"What’s inside?"
"I don’t know; it’s unlocked with your fingerprint. Now it’s yours. Just take it back to your room and open it."
Wang Lan picked up the box; it was heavy. The box was made of metal, but he didn’t know what kind. As he was about to take the box back to his room, his aunt suddenly turned around and called out to him.Nᴇw novel chapters are publɪshed on NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
"There’s something I’ve always wondered about... have you ever cared to know who your father is?"
"My dad? Have I met him?"
"I don’t think so..."
"Then there’s no need to worry about it." Wang Lan smiled and went into his room.
Of course, Wang Lan knew who his father was, and he knew who his biological mother was. He also knew that Wang Ling had never been married nor had a romantic relationship.
No one would have thought that Wang Lan was born with an adult’s soul, although as a small child his brain wasn’t fully developed, and he spent much of his time in a daze. He first met Wang Ling when he was about a week old.
He vaguely heard shouts of killing, and then Wang Ling appeared and carried him out of the blood and fire. From then on, he was Wang Lan, Wang Ling’s biological son.
In his childhood memories, Wang Ling was always busy, but she would set aside one day every week to spend with him, teaching him to call her "Mom." These memories were ordinary, something every child experiences, but to Wang Lan, they were precious.
Remembering Wang Ling’s appearance, Wang Lan nervously placed his finger on the surface of the metal box.
"BEEP BEEP BEEP—" The indicator light suddenly lit up, and after flashing for a few seconds, a voice announced, "Password verification correct!"
The intricate metal box slowly opened. No wonder it was so heavy—its walls were at least five millimeters thick. Inside the metal box lay a video player and a crystal-clear Soul Bead.
A Soul Bead? Mom, aren’t you being a bit stingy? Do you think your son hasn’t seen a Soul Bead before? The only heirloom for your son is a Soul Bead?
Wang Lan gave a wry smile as he picked up the Soul Bead and examined it.
Maybe this Soul Bead contains a lot of Star Power?
Wang Lan knew that Star Martial Warriors from wealthy families improved their cultivation level by absorbing Soul Beads, and even a low-level Soul Bead cost at least 50,000 to start.The so-called "wealth changing destiny" was nothing more than this, something that most affluent families couldn’t afford. Children from average families, even if they awakened as Star Martial Warriors, couldn’t possibly receive Soul Beads for cultivation, so they had to rely on eating.
What Star Power truly is hasn’t been answered by the scientific community to this day. The subjective consensus is that it’s a mix of the energy from bodily cells and spiritual power. Hence, only by consuming a massive amount of food can one extract enough energy.
But this assertion still had many contradictions, though the general direction might be correct. At least, no Star Martial Warrior had ever been seen to be overweight despite their frightening food intake.
Moreover, many Star Martial Warriors, in order to refine more Star Power, didn’t hesitate to damage their bodies through excessive depletion of cells, leading to a gaunt appearance.
"Force-loadable Star Martial Skill detected. Do you wish to force load?"
Star Martial Skill? Force-loadable?
This prompt made Wang Lan somewhat puzzled. He had never heard of a Soul Bead containing Star Martial Skills. Star Martial Skills were developed by powerful Star Martial Warriors through years of research. Soul Beads merely contained Star Power; the two were entirely different things.
He’d heard of Star Martial Skills being passed on through spiritual power, but never of one being engraved within a Soul Bead.
Load!
Wang Lan silently commanded in his heart.
Since it’s a Star Martial Skill, and one left by Mom, of course, I have to learn it.
"Please add skill points."
On the system interface, a skill slot appeared with a plus sign: (0/100).
Wang Lan glanced at his remaining skill points, then at the skill points required for loading the skill.
"Heh... what a smooth transition," he muttered, though he quickly started allocating points.
A hundred skill points, earned through near-death experiences where I almost died for good, weren’t even warm in my pocket yet, and in the blink of an eye, they were all gone.
WHIRR—
As the hundred skill points were added, the dark icon instantly lit up. And as it did, it seemed as though the entire system interface brightened along with it.
Enlightenment instantly burst forth from his Spiritual Sea of Consciousness.
Learning a skill through the system was different from in games. The system was just a way of truly representing what was learned. It wasn’t that one had to click the skill to use it; rather, because it was truly mastered, it was reflected on the system interface.
At least, if Wang Lan needed to use a Star Martial Skill, he could do so instantly.
But this force-loaded Star Martial Skill was special. Even though the skill icon lit up, Wang Lan’s understanding of the skill was merely superficial. He quickly looked at the skill icon and almost lost his temper on the spot.
The skill icon was gray. That meant, even though the skill was loaded, Wang Lan hadn’t learned it and couldn’t use it. Damn it, did I spend a hundred skill points just for show?
He focused his spiritual power on the gray icon.
"Phoenix Form, platinum-level skill. Learning requirements not met. Skill locked."
Why don’t you just go die?
Wang Lan’s scalp tingled upon seeing this.
Learning requirements not met, skill locked? Then what was the point of force-loading it for me? Spit them out! Cough up the hundred skill points you took from me!
"Hm?" Suddenly, Wang Lan discovered a plus sign at the bottom right of the grayed-out skill icon.
What does this mean? It wants me to add more skill points? I only have nine skill points left, and those were the spoils given to me by the Tianjian Bureau after I killed nine Demon Warriors and they extracted the Soul Beads.
Left with no choice, Wang Lan tentatively clicked the plus sign.
"Add one skill point: Phoenix Form can be executed for 0.1 seconds."
How long is 0.1 seconds? A snap of the fingers is about 0.3 seconds, right? So, by that logic, even if I add ten skill points, I can only use it for one second? One second, what’s the use of that?
Fortunately, after adding one point, the skill icon was no longer gray. With the skill unfrozen, its description became visible.
"Phoenix Form, platinum-level skill (upgradable). Once activated, unlocks the first form of the Phoenix, unleashing Galaxy Stage combat power."
Upon reading this description, Wang Lan was shocked. The Galaxy Stage was very far out of reach for him; he wouldn’t even dare think about it before he turned twenty.
The Galaxy Stage represented top-tier combat strength among Star Martial Warriors, the main character in any scenario. According to the 5018 Star Martial Warrior strength census, Starlight Stage warriors constituted 30 percent, Star Shine Stage warriors 36 percent, Star Cloud Stage warriors 18 percent, and Galaxy Stage warriors made up 12 percent. The remainder were of the Star Sea Stage and beyond.
This data was enough to show that Galaxy Stage Star Martial Warriors stood at the pinnacle of the pyramid. And Wang Lan, a rookie who had just awakened his Star Martial Warrior talent, a Starlight Stage weakling, could actually unleash Galaxy Stage combat power with a single Star Martial Skill?
This has to be a cheat, right?
While the power of the skill was undeniable, its consumption cost made Wang Lan equally despair.
Ten skill points per second. Do the math. Is this burning money? This is burning life! I barely survived near-death experiences to earn a hundred skill points, and it’s only enough to activate this for ten seconds. What can I do in ten seconds? It’s probably only enough for one move, right?
"Ah—this is killing me... Where the heck am I supposed to earn more skill points..."
With a sigh, Wang Lan picked up the video player. Pressing the power button, his fingernails whitened slightly from the pressure.
There was only one video file on the player. Wang Lan’s fingers trembled as he clicked to open it. The video played, and the image of his mother, Wang Ling, appeared on the screen.
"Lan Lan, congratulations on becoming a Star Martial Warrior. Mom always believed you could do it. Mom is going on a very important mission. If you’re watching this video, it means Mom might have already died, or perhaps gone missing.
"Do you see the Soul Bead placed there? It contains a part of your soul that Mom cut using a secret technique and then compressed the Phoenix Form Star Martial Skill inside.
"This is Mom’s most powerful Star Martial Skill, with infinite evolutionary potential. It’s a skill that can transcend the Star Sea and break through into the boundless realms of the Immortal Spirit Domain.
"However, Mom set a restriction on the Soul Bead: you must reach the Galaxy Stage before you can learn it. There’s no way around it; the learning requirement for the Phoenix Form is the Galaxy Stage."
Wang Lan chuckled wryly, "Heh, Mom, you’re still as overconfident as ever. What about that restriction you mentioned? I’ve already learned it."
The video continued, Wang Ling’s voice clear, "Mom’s going to carry out her mission now. No need for extra words; I’ve already explained everything to your aunt. Hang in there. Mom is looking forward to fighting alongside you someday."
The video ended there. When the screen faded to black, Wang Lan was already in tears.
"Mom, it’s been eight years..."
Lying in bed, he quietly stared at the ceiling. His mind was filled with speculation.
Is Mom still alive, or is she already dead? What kind of mission could make one of Jade Country’s top-tier experts have no certainty of returning alive?
The more he thought, the more frustrated he became. Wang Lan calmed himself and began to explore the system in his mind.
The character attribute panel had changed. He had advanced from Starlight Stage One to Starlight Stage Four, and every attribute had increased by two points—a significant enhancement in strength.
An attribute classification now appeared on the character panel. Wang Lan’s attribute was shown as Fire, indicating that he was suited to learn Fire-type Star Martial Skills; otherwise, he could only study attributeless and form-changing type skills.
A single attribute... My talent isn’t as ideal as I’d hoped. But why wasn’t this displayed before? Has the system been secretly updating without me knowing?
It had been a day of dramatic ups and downs. Even someone with Wang Lan’s exceptional constitution was thoroughly exhausted. Closing his eyes, he quickly fell into a deep sleep.
After returning from his aunt’s home, he changed his clothes, choosing the most stylish and cool-looking short-sleeved windbreaker from his wardrobe.
Wang Lan had never been particular about his clothing. He usually wore T-shirts in the summer, tracksuits in the fall, and down jackets in the winter, all ordinary items purchased online. Despite an annual income of seventy to eighty million, he never spent recklessly. If it weren’t for having the experiences of two lifetimes, few could probably achieve this.
His aunt occasionally bought him clothes, but he hardly ever unwrapped them. It wasn’t that Wang Lan was intentionally trying to be low-profile; there simply was no need to show off.
This windbreaker was Wang Lan’s only relatively flashy article of clothing, bought on impulse for two thousand yuan because its style reminded him of the Fourth Hokage’s robe. After buying it, he had never worn it.
After all, a man soon to become a Star Martial Warrior should be in high spirits.
He left the house, took the subway, and half an hour later, arrived at the entrance of the Star Martial Hall.
The Star Martial Hall was an institution specifically dealing with Star Martial Warrior affairs, such as strength assessments, level evaluations, processing Star Martial Badges, and even purchasing Soul Beads and Star Martial Skills.

chapters.title: Chapter 16: A New Species is Born
chapters.content:
Chapter 16: Chapter 16: A New Species is Born
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
Before arriving at the Star Martial Hall, Wang Lan thought the outfit he was wearing would make him the most striking guy there, but after he arrived, the prouder he had felt before, the more foolish he felt now.
Who were the people getting their Star Martial Badges? Ninety percent were junior high school graduates. And Wang Lan, standing at 1.76 meters, truly stood out. Especially with that Fiery Cloud Cloak—every wannabe teenager was staring.
Don’t think Wang Lan was only two years older than those eighth graders; during puberty, two years could make a huge difference. Wang Lan was just 1.6 meters tall when he graduated from ninth grade, and now he was 1.76 meters.
And with the average height of the middle school students there being around 1.5 to 1.6 meters, Wang Lan felt completely out of place in that crowd.
He had forgotten that the first few days of summer vacation were the peak time for junior high graduates to get their Star Martial Badges.
"Scholar God?" A chubby kid suddenly smacked Wang Lan’s shoulder excitedly and called out.
"No, you’ve got the wrong person."
"No way! I worship your portrait every day. There’s no chance I’m mistaken."
"A portrait?"
"No, I mean, there’s a poster of you at the supermarket opposite our school, and my room’s walls are covered with them! I haven’t flunked a single subject in ninth grade, all thanks to my devout faith. You are indeed His Eminence, the Scholar God."
"Actually... I’m his younger brother. His name is Wang Lan, and my name is Wang Feng. As you know, he’s already in eleventh grade this year, and he’s just an ordinary person. I’m in the same year as you; I just had the luck to awaken," Wang Lan replied in a low voice.
"Really? What is the Scholar God like at home? Does he get up before dawn every day and study for twenty hours?"
"How could that be possible? You’d drop dead from working that hard."
"Right. If hard work alone could turn you into the Scholar God, then many would have claimed that title by now. The Scholar God must be someone who doesn’t need to study anything to know it—someone who can play games and sleep in yet still come first in exams."
"It’s not like that either. Talent is certainly key, but hard work is indispensable. A perfect score is 100 points on a test. Hard work can earn you 95, and talent is that last five points."
"Is that so? That makes sense. From a rational perspective, exam results are pretty mystical. Like me, last year, whenever I felt like I did well, I’d end up unsatisfied with my grades. In my final year, I just gave up. For exams, I’d rely on guessing, and on copying for what couldn’t be guessed, and yet I still managed to score above 60."
Rational, my foot! Using rational analysis to explain mysticism?
"Next!" While speaking in hushed tones to the chubby kid, it was Wang Lan’s turn to reach the registration desk.
Wang Lan respectfully took out his ID card. "Wang Lan? Sixteen years old. You’ll be a senior next semester, right?"
After confirming Wang Lan’s identification, the staff member asked with surprise, "Weren’t you a failure in soul stimulation? This is the registration desk for Star Martial Warriors."
"I know. I’ve just awakened."
"Awakened? How is that possible? Come on, Open your Star Palace and let me see."
Wang Lan had previously opened his Star Palace in front of Huang Feilong, but that was in private. Doing it in front of so many people felt a bit embarrassing, especially since the chubby kid he’d conned in the queue was giving him mournful looks like a widow cursed with seven lifetimes of ill-fated love.
Wang Lan couldn’t help it. If he admitted it then, the middle school students behind him would probably start exclaiming. To date, the Scholar God forum was still among the top five busiest sections on Suzhou City’s bulletin board service.ɪꜰ ʏᴏᴜ ᴡᴀɴᴛ ᴛᴏ ʀᴇᴀᴅ ᴍᴏʀᴇ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs, ᴘʟᴇᴀsᴇ ᴠɪsɪᴛ novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
Wang Lan took a deep breath and exerted himself. The Star Palace above his head opened, a Starlight shining within.
"Huh, you really awakened? Weird, Soul Resonance didn’t trigger your Star Martial Warrior talent. How did you awaken?"
"Maybe... I was in a good mood, I guess."
The lady at the registration desk clicked away on her keyboard, and soon, a printed form was handed to Wang Lan.
"Follow the procedure on the form and take the tests one by one. After completion, go to the badge distribution area to receive your Star Martial Badge. The Star Martial Badge is integrated with a bank card; the staff who provides you with the badge will explain it to you clearly."
After thanking her, Wang Lan turned to leave. Just as he took a step, he felt someone blocking his path. Wang Lan was still looking at the procedure on the form and slightly sidestepped.
But the person seemed to do it on purpose and once again moved to block Wang Lan’s way. Only then did Wang Lan look up and find Jiang Xinyu scrutinizing him. The situation was somewhat awkward.
"Jiang Xinyu, what a coincidence..."
"I’m accompanying my sister to get her Star Martial Badge. What are you doing here? Wait, is that a Star Martial registration form you’re holding? You’ve awakened a Star Martial talent? You..."
"You seem more excited than I am," Wang Lan said with a wry smile, then turned towards Jiang Xinchen beside her. "Yo, Chenchen, long time no see. You’ve grown so much, almost catching up to your sister now."
"Nice to see you, Lan!" Jiang Xinchen and Jiang Xinyu, though sisters, had completely different personalities. Jiang Xinyu was the classic Ice-Snow Queen: strong, domineering, with a ferocious temperament—a veritable guardian deity for the home.
But Jiang Xinchen was quite introverted, like a well-mannered young lady from a respectable family. The only downside was that she didn’t talk much, and trying to have a conversation with her could be quite awkward.
Jiang Xinchen was two years younger than Jiang Xinyu and had not awakened any Star Martial Warrior talents. While her sister had automatically awakened at the age of nine, Xincheng had only done so after this Soul Resonance.
"Xincheng has already finished the test; you haven’t yet, have you? I’ll take you!"
With someone guiding him, Wang Lan naturally wouldn’t refuse. "Actually, all that health check data is useless. There’s no need to test it. What really needs to be tested are strength, speed, reaction ability, and combat ability."
Jiang Xinyu, familiar with the process, led Wang Lan to the testing area. The Star Martial Hall had opened less than half an hour ago, and the main group was still queuing for basic item tests. Consequently, there were very few people in the comprehensive testing area, meaning almost no queue at all.
The rules of the test were simple. There would be a circle with a diameter of one and a half meters on the testing ground, and Wang Lan needed to stand inside it. Surrounding him, thirty-six tennis ball launchers were set up.
Of course, the number of launchers, their speed, and even their angles would be adjusted according to the difficulty level. The levels ranged from one to nine, with freshly awakened Star Martial Warriors naturally starting at level one.
Level one difficulty involved launching tennis balls directly at the participant. The balls were coated with white powder, and Wang Lan had to block with his arms or evade, ensuring no balls hit his body. This level of test posed no difficulty for Wang Lan.
Wang Lan didn’t even need to move his feet, casually blocking all the tennis balls with ease.
"Switch to level two difficulty," Jiang Xinyu whispered to the operator.
At level two difficulty, another tennis ball launcher was added, creating a crossfire with the first. Not only did the number of balls double, but the speed also increased significantly.
Still, this level was no issue for Wang Lan. The tennis balls were launched roughly every three seconds. This speed was several magnitudes slower than Huang Feilong’s full-speed punches and kicks.
"Increase it to level five difficulty," Jiang Xinyu instructed indifferently.
"Miss, level five is the difficulty for professional Star Martial Warriors, and he has just awakened as a Star Martial Warrior..." the staff member asked, somewhat surprised.
"From what I know of him, his strength has definitely reached a professional level. I want to know where his limit lies now. I’ve always thought that he’s been training so hard because he couldn’t accept his fate, but I never imagined he would miraculously awaken as a Star Martial Warrior. Just set it to level five."
Jiang Xinchen looked at her sister in surprise, then at Wang Lan, who was effortlessly handling the test. Level five was a height she looked up to. After being forced by her sister to train every day for years, she had barely reached level three.
Was Lan that strong?
Level five added eight more launchers, firing from all directions at increased speeds of one ball per second. With eight launchers, this was essentially the same as launching eight balls every second.
If translated to an opponent’s punch speed, it was like facing eight punches per second. Even worse, the launchers were not static, meaning the balls could come from any direction or angle at any time.
Even among Star Shine Stage Star Martial Warriors, those who could last five minutes under level five difficulty were rare.
The sudden spike in difficulty startled Wang Lan. He had assumed this was a routine test for Star Martial Warriors. He had done his homework. Failing the Star Martial Warrior test would mean no Star Martial Badge.
But... is the Star Martial Warrior test really this hard? Isn’t it a 99% pass rate? Am I just that bad? Are other freshly awakened Star Martial Warrior kids this strong?
Wang Lan didn’t realize that this comprehensive testing platform was managed by the Xinyu family. Normally, passing level one difficulty would suffice. Level five was professional level, meaning that passing it would qualify someone as a professional warrior.
What’s professional, you might ask? Singers who can participate in ’I Am a Singer’ are professionals, athletes who can compete in the Olympics are professionals, and those who can play in the World Cup are... well, let’s just say I didn’t say that.
The sudden increase in difficulty caught Wang Lan off guard. In that moment, he felt as though he was facing a group attack by five Star Martial Warriors of Huang Feilong’s caliber.
Blocking, dodging, rolling, leaping, blocking while dodging, and rolling while blocking—the tennis balls showered down like a storm, Wang Lan’s agile body moving through the maelstrom like a phantom.
The newly arrived Star Martial Warriors suddenly stopped in their tracks, staring dumbfounded at the scene unfolding before them.
"Holy shit—"
"Did we come to the wrong place? Is this the professional-level evaluation area? No, it’s for newly awakened Star Martial Warriors, right? Wasn’t it supposed to be easy? Just dodging twenty incoming tennis balls counted as passing, didn’t it?"
"Maybe... we were misinformed. It’s not a total of twenty balls, but twenty per second?"
"At this difficulty, I can confidently say I’d easily last half a second."
"Who on earth designed such an inhuman test? I’m not taking it."
"I heard if you don’t pass the comprehensive assessment, they won’t issue a Star Martial Badge..."
"What kind of international joke is this? Is this difficulty humanly passable? Is that even human in there?"
"If it’s not something a human can pass, then what the hell is that thing inside?"
"That person is certainly not human. I strongly suggest that once he’s done, we capture him and send him to the zoo as a top-priority protected species for research—a new species has been born!"
Most of those gathered were middle school graduates, each more capable of running their mouth than the last. Inside, however, Wang Lan was a bundle of nerves, his brain highly tense. This level of test difficulty was obviously not intended for newly awakened Star Martial Warriors. Even Huang Feilong would struggle to pass it.
Could it be... Huang Feilong has been misleading me all these years? What about his claims that my fighting ability is no less than that of someone at the early Star Shine Stage? And that if Star Martial Warriors aren’t allowed to use Star Martial Skills or amplify their physical qualities with Star Power, there are few below the Star Shine Stage who could match me?
I don’t believe you, you mischievous old codger! You’re terrible!

chapters.title: Chapter 17 The Ineffable Serendipity
chapters.content:
Chapter 17: Chapter 17 The Ineffable Serendipity
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
"Stop!"
The tennis ball launcher immediately ceased, and Wang Lan stood up, panting. Less than ten minutes had passed, and Wang Lan was already drenched in sweat. It was an incredibly high-intensity exercise; Wang Lan had estimated that he needed to make three to five large movements per second to dodge.
"Comprehensive evaluation passed." Jiang Xinyu, with an odd expression on her face, came over to Wang Lan and handed him the evaluation sheet. "Come on, we’ll do the individual tests next."
The process was like a medical check-up at a hospital, with each test needing to be completed one by one. Strength, reaction speed, and endurance evaluations all scored an A. Although Wang Lan was not quite sure what an A rating meant, judging by the evaluators’ expressions, it seemed to be quite high.
Finally, Wang Lan arrived at the Attribute Analysis Detection Department.
"Attribute analysis is about checking your star power attribute, and even hidden attributes can be detected. Once you know your precise attributes, you will know the direction for future progress and what type of Star Martial Skill to choose. Before the invention of the attribute analysis machine, Star Martial Warriors could only determine their attributes on their own. It was fine for those with obvious attribute characteristics, but for others with less distinct attributes, their innate talents might be buried. Once you get there, channel your Star Power into the crystal sphere. The machine will automatically analyze your star power attribute."
"Alright!" Hearing this, Wang Lan immediately channeled his Star Power into the crystal sphere, and soon, the entire device began to vibrate, with indicator lights flashing rapidly.
"CLICK, CLICK, CLICK—"
A report was quickly printed out. Just as Wang Lan was about to take the report, Jiang Xinyu snatched it away. Looking at Jiang Xinyu, who seemed even more anxious than himself, this behavior did not seem characteristic of her.
"Seventy percent Fire Attribute, thirty percent Yang Attribute? Not bad at all."
"Does this count as dual attributes?" Wang Lan asked excitedly.
"No, everyone has Yin and Yang attributes, even ordinary people. You should know that the most fundamental force that constitutes everything in the world is electromagnetic force, and electromagnetic force itself has yin and yang poles. So as long as you exist, you have Yin and Yang attributes. I know what you’re thinking—why is there only Yang and no Yin? The machine makes the selection automatically. If the Yang Attribute is more prominent than the Yin Attribute, the machine defaults to Yang. If the Yin Attribute is stronger, it’d be Yin. This thirty percent represents the proportion of Yin and Yang attributes."
"Then, is my attribute considered good or bad?"
This was something Wang Lan really didn’t understand. Some books were only available for borrowing and purchasing by those holding a Star Martial Badge.
"The higher the single attribute percentage, the better. Your ratio is seven to one, which is pretty good," Jiang Xinyu said with a smile.
"What about you?" Wang Lan asked subconsciously.
"My Ice Attribute naturally carries both Wind and Water Attributes, so Ice accounts for 45 percent, Wind for 15 percent, Water for 30 percent, and Yin for 10 percent."
I shouldn’t have asked; I really have a big mouth!
Wang Lan silently chastised himself.
After completing all the tests, one could go to the Star Martial Badge administration to handle the badge. As each test was finished, data was synchronized to the central server. So by the time Wang Lan completed the last item, the Star Martial Badge had already been processed, and it was ready for pickup at the window.
Running through a dozen or so tests had taken over two hours, and it was nearly noon by the time he got his Star Martial Badge.ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ꜰʀᴏᴍ NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
"Thank you for today. Without you, I might have had to wait until the afternoon. How about I treat you to lunch?"
"Of course, but I choose the restaurant."
"Certainly."
In the end, the three of them chose an Eagle-Style Restaurant. White Eagle Country’s tastes are rather heavy, with steaks made in the shape of rectangular loaves, large and filling. Even the well-off Star Martial Warriors had to consider value for money.
At the dining table, Jiang Xinchen was silent throughout, either bowing her head to eat or her big eyes darting back and forth between her sister and Wang Lan. Meanwhile, Jiang Xinyu was watching Wang Lan the whole time, seemingly with intent.
"Why are you looking at me? Is the way I eat that unsightly?" Wang Lan said, somewhat speechlessly. Jiang Xinyu seemed a bit strange today.
"Isn’t there something you want to say to me?"
"COUGH, COUGH—" Jiang Xinchen suddenly choked on a beverage, hastily reaching for a tissue as she coughed.
"Xincheng, you’re not being good."
"Sis, I’m sorry..."
"Don’t be so hard on Xincheng. I haven’t seen anyone more well-behaved than her. How can she not be well-behaved when she’s that quiet?"
"You don’t understand; this girl definitely thought about something she shouldn’t have just now. Right, I was asking you a question."
"Something to say to you? Oh, thank you. I really appreciate it, deeply grateful..." Wang Lan quickly stood up, his face serious and sincere.
"You’re doing this on purpose, right? When did you become a Star Martial Warrior? How did you awaken? Shouldn’t you give me an honest explanation?"
"Just a few days ago, on the day school let out for break."
"Soul Resonance didn’t awaken you... yet you awakened on your own at this time? Something feels off... That day on the rooftop, you had already awakened, right?"
"Yes, it was at that time."
"Do you remember what I said to you on the rooftop?"
"What?"
"You won!"
"I remember, I do."
"Forget it! It doesn’t count."
"What?" Wang Lan looked confused.
Women really do change their minds as suddenly as legends say!
"You’re now a Star Martial Warrior as well. Next term you should transfer to the Star Martial Arts Campus, straight into your senior year. Class One should be fine."
"Is that my decision to make? Also, how about this, I admit defeat, okay? I really didn’t intend to compete with you; I had my own reasons for insisting on being first..."
"The reasons aren’t important, nor does it matter who admits defeat. What’s important is that I want to beat you.
"You’ve become a Star Martial Warrior, and we have a long road ahead to walk together. It’s not yet time for us to part ways, so the bet must continue.
"You know, either let me win splendidly, or let me accept defeat wholeheartedly. If you dare to go easy on me, I might actually kill you. And about you joining Class One, I’ll arrange that."
"You’re arranging it? How will you arrange that?"
"Donating a teaching building, how tough can it be?"
"You’re ludicrously rich!"
"Do you have any plans for the summer vacation?" Jiang Xinyu suddenly asked.
"No plans for now. If nothing else comes up, I will probably be focusing on my cultivation. After falling behind for two years, I need to catch up quickly if I want to go straight into senior year. I’m not too stressed about the academic subjects, but I do need to spend a lot of time catching up on the Star Martial Art courses."
"Your overall strength has already surpassed more than half of the seniors. Except for your Star Martial Art level, which is a bit low, your other qualities are even better than Xu Xiangwen and Gong Feiyu."
"Really?" Wang Lan was surprised.
"Really. You can’t rush the Star Martial Art level; after all, you’ve only awakened a few days ago. However, I plan to go to the trial ground during the summer vacation. Do you want to join?"
"The beginner trial ground? Isn’t that a place for professional Star Martial Warriors to gain experience?"
"Don’t make such a fuss; I’ve been there several times. The trial ground is teeming with Exotic Beasts, and naturally, lots of Soul Beads. Your foundation is very solid, so there won’t be instability from quickly enhancing your Star Power. The trial ground is a good option. Of course, if you’re willing to spend one or two hundred million to buy Soul Beads, that’s possible too."
"One or two hundred million? Do you think money just flies into my wallet? I’m from a poor family; I can’t afford that."
"You just collect rent. How is that any different from money blowing in with the wind?"
"Fine, I’ll go. When?"
"In three days, I’ll come to pick you up. It’s quite a distance."
"Okay!"
As Jiang Xinchen listened to their conversation, her eyes suddenly sparkled, and she looked up at Jiang Xinyu.
"Don’t even think about it. When you can pass the Level 5 test, I’ll consider taking you. Otherwise, it’d be a death sentence for you to go."
"Oh!" Jiang Xinchen was unhappy and lowered her head to eat her steak.
The red limited-edition sports car roared out of the underground parking lot and zoomed into the street, disappearing from the envious eyes of onlookers.
"BEEP—BEEP—"
"Xu Xiangwen, three days from now, go to the beginner trial ground."
"Understood!"
After hanging up the phone, Jiang Xinchen turned her head to look at her sister, whose face was flushed with excitement. She knew that her sister was always very composed, and it was rare for her to be this thrilled. Right now, she was incredibly excited; if someone handed her a glass of wine at that moment, she would probably down it in one gulp.
"Sis, do you like Lan?"
"Don’t talk nonsense, that’s not true," Jiang Xinyu replied, her tone as cold as ever and filled with a stern warning.
"Then why were you so excited today? From the moment you saw Lan... your heartbeat has consistently been around 180."
"You wouldn’t understand!" Jiang Xinyu suddenly spoke with profound emphasis. "It’s been eight years. You can’t comprehend it. Eight years, every single exam, he’s been first. When I got a hundred percent, so did he. When I got ninety-nine, he still did.
"Everything the teachers knew, he knew; what they didn’t, he also knew. I’ve excelled in everything since I was young—violin, piano, painting, calligraphy—I’ve won so many awards I couldn’t carry them all. Math Olympiads, physics, chemistry... always first in every competition.
"But! Only in exams, I never got first place. With my temperament, how could I stand it? By the end of my junior year, that was my last chance to beat him, yet I still lost by ten points. I thought I’d never get another chance to beat him in my life.
"Heaven must have eyes, for he awakened the Star Martial Warrior’s talent. My competition with him can continue!"
"Sis, do you really think I would believe all that?"
"Believe it or not, I don’t care!"
"Hm... knowing my sister’s personality, if it really weren’t true, she wouldn’t bother explaining a word. But you explained so much, which only proves one fact."
At that moment, Jiang Xinyu’s grip on the steering wheel tightened.
"Explaining means hiding, and hiding implies..."
"The steering wheel’s in my hands, and I have control of the brakes and gas pedal. Think carefully before you speak," Jiang Xinyu coldly interrupted.
"You’re already thinking of murder to silence someone, and yet you say it’s not true? How boring!"
Music suddenly filled the car.
"Tomorrow I will marry you la..."
Next song!
"Love is just a word, I only..."
Next song!
"I beg Heaven..."
Turn off the playback!
"That’s fate, ah..." Jiang Xinchen laughed happily. "Actually, Lan is really amazing, even the most remarkable person of our generation that I’ve ever seen.
"I’ve seen people who are good at studying, geniuses like my sister. But someone who’s dominated every test with a godlike performance from first grade until now, evoking my urge to bow in respect, is something else.
"Even my genius sister, despite all her efforts, couldn’t achieve this. I think only he could in this world. A person like that, could he be ordinary?"
"Some people are born extraordinary," Jiang Xinyu agreed with a nod.
"Having this person as a brother-in-law would be quite something... Ah—Sis, I was wrong... Slow down..."

chapters.title: Chapter 18 Are you a freak? No, You’re Completely Abnormal
chapters.content:
Chapter 18: Chapter 18 Are you a freak? No, You’re Completely Abnormal
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
Three days later, Jiang Xinyu drove to Wang Lan’s doorstep.
Wang Lan changed into combat gear, carrying a steel knife as he walked out, only to search for the car door handle for ages and not find it.
At this moment, the car door slowly opened like spreading wings, revealing Jiang Xinyu behind sunglasses.
"Sometimes I really wonder if you’re actually rich. Logically speaking, you earn over a hundred million a year. How can you be as clueless as a bumpkin?"
"So being rich means I should be into cars, yachts, and tender models at clubs?"
"Get in the car," Jiang Xinyu said, too lazy to argue with Wang Lan.
"Let me make this clear: we’re entering the Tinglin Elementary Trial Grounds. Even though it’s just a beginner level, it’s still very dangerous. Any of the Exotic Beasts inside could kill a grown adult in a few seconds.
You’re bound to be nervous on your first entry, so stick close to us, and do not move more than three meters away from the team. With your skills, killing Exotic Beasts on your own shouldn’t be difficult, but real combat and training are two different things. You’re going to encounter real dangers and need to adapt quickly.
Also, entering the Trial Grounds isn’t just about getting hurt; you could also die. Especially for first-timers, the fatality rate is twenty percent. If you’re scared, it’s still not too late to back out."
The car had already entered the highway. Jiang Xinyu chattered non-stop, offering advice, while Wang Lan stared at her hands, slightly nervous.
"What are you looking at? I’m a woman too; it’s perfectly normal and reasonable for me to paint my nails."
"I know. When did you get your driver’s license?"
"Last year. Why?"
"How many times have you driven?"
"Spit it out!" Jiang Xinyu frowned. "What? Doubt my skills? You think I’m like those female drivers on the internet?"
"Hard to say... How about I get out and take a cab myself?"
"Sit tight and don’t test my patience. Besides Xincheng, you’re the first one to ride in my car."
"You mean the first one brave enough to ride! Seeing you this nervous, how could I not be scared?"
"Nervous? Which eye of yours sees me as nervous?"
"Your hands are clenched on the steering wheel. Only a novice grips the steering wheel like it’s a life-saving straw, while experienced drivers just casually rest their hands on it; some don’t even bother holding it..."
"Really?" Jiang Xinyu suddenly went quiet and then deftly switched gears.
"Although I’m not quite sure why your car has twelve gears, this road has a speed limit of eighty..."
"Shut up!"
VROOM—
From the campus to the southern district, it was forty-three kilometers along the ring road. Half an hour later, the car slowly drove into the parking lot of the Trial Grounds.
"Get out!" Her tone was icy and carried a strong hint of murderous intent.
"It’s no big deal. No need to be angry. It was just a fine of two thousand, right? That’s just peanuts for you. The traffic cop was right. It’s a highway with a speed limit of eighty, and you pushed it to two hundred sixty. He only fined you two thousand, which is already very lenient.
Being pretty has its perks, huh? If it had been me, it definitely wouldn’t have been less than twenty thousand, and they would’ve impounded the car and revoked my license..."
"Believe me, if you keep gloating, I’ll punch you! Would I have been speeding if it weren’t for you?"
"How’s that my fault? The steering wheel, accelerator, gears, brakes – they’re all under your control."
"Would I have been speeding if you hadn’t doubted my driving skills?"
"Is there a necessary logical connection between me doubting your skills and your speeding?" Wang Lan retorted, not to be outdone.
"Xinyu, over here..." At that moment, a voice called out. Outside the Trial Grounds, where a line of shops stood, Xu Xiangwen waved and shouted from the entrance of a fast-food restaurant.
Wang Lan followed Jiang Xinyu over. Xu Xiangwen was slightly stunned to see Wang Lan, then a knowing smile spread across his face. "You lad, not bad at all!"
"You knew?" Wang Lan smiled faintly, thinking Xu Xiangwen was talking about him becoming a Star Martial Warrior.
"Hehehe, I didn’t know at first, but seeing you here made it obvious. Let’s go inside."
Next to Gong Feiyu sat a young man whom Wang Lan didn’t recognize, probably someone from the Star Martial Arts Campus. Jiang Xinyu approached, pausing slightly with a somewhat displeased expression that quickly vanished.
"Wang Lan? Hey, what a surprise, and such an unexpected one at that! Let me introduce you. This is our classmate, Wang Youle. And this is Wang Lan, my childhood friend turned best buddy."
"Ah, the legendary Study God! I’ll go order the food," Wang Youle said with a smile, getting up to leave.
"Why did you bring him along?" Jiang Xinyu asked Xu Xiangwen.
"Hasn’t he always teamed up with us? I notified him right after you called me. Were you thinking it would just be us?"
"Forget it, one more doesn’t make a difference. I’m going to use the restroom." Jiang Xinyu stood up and left, leaving Wang Lan sitting with Xu Xiangwen and Gong Feiyu.
In a flash, two pairs of eyes fixed on Wang Lan.
"When did it happen?"
"The day the vacation started," Wang Lan smiled.
"Who made the first move?" Gong Feiyu promptly asked.
"First move?" Wang Lan was bewildered.
"It must have been Xinyu! The day we had dinner together, she drank three glasses by herself. She never used to drink before. Feiyu and I thought she was drowning her sorrows, but it turns out she was gathering her courage."
"Gathering courage? I feel like what you’re talking about isn’t the same thing I’m talking about."
"Humph, humph, humph, still playing dumb? You’re with Xinyu now, aren’t you? Did you come here today to flaunt your relationship? No worries, Feiyu and I can handle this public display of affection.
Don’t worry too much. We’ve been to the Trial Grounds three times and know them inside out. In ten days, I guarantee I’ll return Xinyu safely to you. I can at least assure you of that, right?"
"Which shameless person has the nerve to say that? It’s more likely Xinyu would be protecting you than the other way around."
"Wait, you’ve got it all wrong."
"Wrong my foot! You just admitted it."
"I admitted I awakened my Star Martial Talent, but I didn’t admit to anything else."
"Listen to him, he admits to awakening... Wait a second, what did you say? I didn’t catch that?" Xu Xiangwen’s shout was so loud the entire restaurant suddenly fell quiet.
Wang Lan looked at Xu Xiangwen, exasperated.
How has he not changed at all after all these years?
"Can you not be so loud?" he said. "Sit down and talk, will you?"
"No, Lan, Uncle Lan, you can’t be serious! You’ve really awakened?"
"Awakened."
"When?"
"The day the holiday started."
"That makes no sense... There was no Soul Resonance, how did you just suddenly awaken? So is this... a spontaneous awakening or a stimulated awakening?"
"It should be a spontaneous one, I guess, since the Soul Resonance failed, right? Even with a delay, it wouldn’t be two years late."
"Cough, cough..." It was only then that Gong Feiyu recovered from his shock. Looking at Wang Lan with disbelief, he said, "I always suspected you were some kind of mutated species, and now I can confirm you belong to the completely mutated type.
So Jiang Xinyu is taking you to the Trial Grounds? Isn’t that messing around? The Trial Grounds are a battlefield, and she’s letting someone who just awakened as a Star Martial Warrior go straight into battle? That’s practically murder."
"Who’s being murdered?" Wang Youle walked back with a smile and sat down. "The order’s placed. Wang Lan, I only ordered half a portion for you; I was afraid you couldn’t finish it."
"Thanks."
"Hold on, Wang Lan, show me your Star Martial Badge," Xu Xiangwen said, still skeptical, reaching out his hand.
"Oh." Wang Lan took out his Star Martial Badge and handed it to Xu Xiangwen. Xu Xiangwen took the badge and scanned it with an app on his phone.
"Searching for information... Search complete. Wang Lan, Star Martial ID: ZZ501807080115."
"Holy shit, it’s real! You just got it the day before yesterday! You’ve really awakened? That’s great, we can hang out together again!"
"It really is good news. Let’s see the ratings," Gong Feiyu said, also smiling, while Wang Youle looked at Wang Lan in surprise, an inexplicable hostility in his eyes.
"Wang Lan, born on January 3, 5002; awakened Star Martial Talent on June 30, 5018; Star Power attribute: Fire. Strength rating A, Speed rating A, Endurance rating A, Potential rating B. Overall combat power rating: Professional Grade, B+."
"Wait, did you read that wrong?" Gong Feiyu quickly asked. "Shouldn’t the overall combat power rating be Entry Level? Professional Grade? We’re only at Professional Grade ourselves!"
"I wish I read it wrong, but... my vision is 2.0."
"At least you’re still Professional Grade B+, same as Wang Lan. I’m just Professional Grade B, one level below Wang Lan. Don’t believe me? Look for yourself. My dear Lan, I think Feiyu’s earlier assessment of you is wrong, ridiculously wrong.
You’re not just a completely mutated species; your DNA must have a hundred percent match with insects."
"Xu Xiangwen, you’ve made progress. Learned how to insult without using dirty words?" Wang Lan folded his arms and sneered.
"Xiangwen... why say it matches insect DNA?" Wang Youle asked curiously.
"Because insects are the only species in nature that undergo complete metamorphosis."
"I get it now why Xinyu would bring a greenhorn like you, who just awakened, to the Trial Grounds. Just awakened and already possessing professional-grade combat power! If your Star Power level increases, who knows how formidable you’ll become," Gong Feiyu said.
"The Study God is truly the Study God. Even as a Star Martial Warrior, he’s a genius among geniuses," Wang Youle complimented from the side.
"There’s no such thing as geniuses in this world." Jiang Xinyu came over to the group, gesturing to Wang Youle, who quickly moved to sit beside Gong Feiyu.
"You all just see that Wang Lan has professional-grade strength right after awakening as a Star Martial Warrior. But you didn’t see the kind of arduous training Wang Lan went through all these years."
"We don’t know, but Xinyu, how would you know?"
"I guessed." Jiang Xinyu’s eyes darted about; she quickly changed the subject. "I called you all here because I need your help. I reached the peak of the Star Shine Stage this April, and I’m hoping to break through to the Star Cloud Stage with your assistance during this opportunity.
Mu Shaoyun of Class Three has also reached the peak of the Star Shine Stage, and so has Duan Ziqi from Class Five. Out of the nine sophomore classes, there are twelve at the Star Shine peak. And I am going to be the first to break through to the Star Cloud Stage."
"Of course! Her Majesty the Queen always comes first!" Xu Xiangwen raised his hand.Follow current ɴᴏᴠᴇʟs on ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
"Shut up!" Jiang Xinyu shot Xu Xiangwen a sideways glance. "So, I’m covering the cost for everyone to enter the Trial Grounds this time. The Soul Beads we obtain, apart from those needed to replenish your Star Power, will all be given to me.
This will continue until I break through to the Star Cloud Stage. In exchange, during the winter holiday, I will take you to the Intermediate Trial Grounds and ensure that you all reach the Star Cloud Stage before the start of the provincial martial arts competition... Hmm... Wang Youle is an exception. You’re only at the early Star Shine Stage now; it would be a bit difficult to get you to the Star Cloud Stage."
"I understand," Wang Youle nodded obediently.
"So, who agrees with my proposal, and who opposes?"
"Agree!"
"Agree!"
"Agree!"
"I..." Wang Lan was about to say he agreed when Jiang Xinyu suddenly interrupted.
"Since everyone agrees, that settles it. As for Wang Lan, he’s an auxiliary member of the team, so he won’t be part of the distribution. The Soul Beads he collects belong to him alone."

chapters.title: Chapter 19: The First Slaying of Exotic Beasts
chapters.content:
Chapter 19: Chapter 19: The First Slaying of Exotic Beasts
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
"This..." Wang Youle seemed to have something to say.
"Do you have any objections?" Jiang Xinyu’s piercing gaze shot towards Wang Youle, scrutinizing him from a position of superiority.
"No... none!" Wang Youle shook his head repeatedly.
"Good. Hurry up and eat, then we’ll enter the grounds!"
During the short meal, Wang Lan managed to clarify the relationships within this small team. He wasn’t familiar with Wang Youle, having only met him today. The other three, however, Wang Lan had known since childhood. Jiang Xinyu was his childhood friend, while Xu Xiangwen and Gong Feiyu were his classmates from elementary to middle school. The four of them were quite close.
Jiang Xinyu seemed to despise Wang Youle. However, Xu Xiangwen was a bit closer to Wang Youle, while Gong Feiyu simply didn’t dislike him.
Looking at it this way, although the four were a team, their relationship wasn’t very solid. Wang Lan finally understood the fleeting hostility he had seen from Wang Youle upon learning of Wang Lan’s awakening as a Star Martial Warrior.
Wang Lan already had a tight bond with the other three, and now that he had awakened as a Star Martial Warrior, it was evident he posed a threat to Wang Youle’s position.
However, Wang Lan felt no guilt about muscling in or taking someone’s place; after all, he had at least eight years of friendship with the other three. Furthermore, even without Wang Lan, Wang Youle’s position in the team was precarious. Wang Lan felt he had already shown utmost benevolence by not actively trying to oust Wang Youle; the rest didn’t matter.
Star Martial Warriors had to pay to enter the Junior Trial Grounds. Despite being a Different Dimensional Space, the trial grounds were safe, or at least relatively so. Moreover, troops were stationed within the trial grounds to maintain order and protect the Trialists, all of which cost money.
The cost for a Star Martial Warrior below the Star Cloud Stage was 5,000 a day. For ten days, that amounted to 50,000. This time, the main goal was to help Jiang Xinyu break through to the Star Cloud Stage, totaling 250,000 for five people.
This figure might take an ordinary person five years of scrimping and saving to accumulate, but for Jiang Xinyu, it was a trifle. She swiftly swiped her card for entry.
"Since I won’t be participating in the distribution, I should pay my own 50,000," Wang Lan murmured.
"Fine. For next quarter’s rent, you can help me by waiving the odd amount," Jiang Xinyu replied.
What a ripoff! That odd amount clearly starts with a nine.
Upon entering the trial grounds, they first had to go to the changing room to switch into combat gear. The climate within the trial grounds was bizarre and ever-changing, so they needed clothing that could maintain a constant temperature and facilitate combat.
Wang Lan glanced at the combat gear, and his mouth twitched. It resembled the tight-fitting leather suits worn by superheroes in American comics. Breathability aside, Wang Lan couldn’t accept the design alone.
"What are you dawdling for? Aren’t you going to get dressed? Don’t make Xinyu wait until she’s changed before you even start," someone urged.
"Who designed such an awkward outfit?"
"It was developed by the Xinyu family’s company, didn’t you know? Isn’t their logo on the clothes?"
"Isn’t wearing this embarrassing?"
"What are you thinking? This is just an internal thermoregulating shirt. You still need to wear the Graphite Thin Armor on the outside. All the embarrassing parts will be covered. Did you think you’d just go out wearing this? My ’big weapon’ wouldn’t stay hidden like that," Xu Xiangwen remarked.
"Xu, I’ve realized something... you’ve become increasingly flamboyant," Wang Lan commented.
"You’ve only just noticed? I’ve found him unbearable for the past year," Gong Feiyu interjected as he donned the leather suit. He pressed a blue button on his belt, and the outfit suddenly tightened, clinging perfectly to his body.
Following suit, Wang Lan put on the form-fitting leather suit and searched his locker. "Where’s the armor?"
"Follow me," Gong Feiyu said, patting Wang Lan’s shoulder and leading him out of the changing room to another. Only then did Wang Lan realize the armor was fitted by robots on a specialized platform.
No explanation from Gong Feiyu was necessary. There were footprints on the ground indicating where to stand; one simply had to stretch out their hands and grasp the handles on either side.
"Scanning model... Pairing model... Loading model. Please remain still. Robot initiating automated equipping sequence."
Then, the chest plate, backplate, and skirt armor were swiftly equipped.
"Equipping complete. Please step off the platform."
Wang Lan looked at himself in the mirror. "This is more like it."
The tight-fitting colorful leather suit served as an inner layer, and with the armor on, he looked exceptionally valiant and dashing.
"The backpack contains water, energy bars, and other essentials. The war blade can be worn at your waist or carried in your hand. Let’s go, Xinyu is probably waiting for us."
Following Gong Feiyu out, Wang Lan saw Jiang Xinyu emerge from the opposite side. Seeing Jiang Xinyu in female armor, Wang Lan’s eyes lit up. Although he knew she was beautiful, this was the first time he had seen such a valiant side to her, prompting him to take a longer look.
"Is everyone ready? The next ten days will be tough. Our target is the Snow Spider. The Snow Spider’s attributes match mine, and its Soul Bead can help me advance faster. Let’s head out!"The source of this content ɪs NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
Their watches contained a map of the Exotic Beasts’ distribution within the trial grounds and could also project holograms in the Different Dimensional Space. This technology, unrealized in the outside world, was surprisingly implemented here.
"Xinyu, I heard that any technological weapons fail in the Different Dimensional Space. Is that true? What’s the principle behind it?"
"That is indeed the case, but I don’t know the principle."
"If firearms worked in the otherworld, the Pioneering Legions wouldn’t face so much danger. Against the Exotic Beasts in the junior trial grounds, give me a Type-95 automatic rifle, and I could take down an entire clan by myself. Sadly, while I can bring a Type-95 in here, it’s only good as a fire poker."
"It must be because the physical laws are different," Wang Lan sighed.
"While we haven’t reached our destination, let me introduce the abilities of our team members," Jiang Xinyu began. "There’s no need to introduce myself; you already know my capabilities. Xu Xiangwen has awakened the Heavenly Eye, allowing for long-range scouting that ignores obstacles. His Star Martial Skill is Physical Clone. Every time we manage to retreat safely, it’s all thanks to Xu Xiangwen.
"Gong Feiyu possesses Earth Attribute Star Power, and his Star Martial Skill is also Earth Attribute. Wang Youle is Fire Attribute.
"You currently don’t have a Star Martial Skill, but your close-combat abilities are impressive. You can act as the team’s melee fighter. With that setup, I’ll be the ranged damage dealer, Gong Feiyu will handle crowd control and support, Xu Xiangwen will remain on constant reconnaissance, and Wang Youle will provide backup as needed."
"Okay!"
Soon, the team of five arrived at the Snow Spider territory. It was a stretch of continuous snowy mountains. It was hard to imagine that just a kilometer away lay the scorching desert of Chibi, yet here it was a world of ice and snow. Such a close distance with such vastly different climates could only exist in a Different Dimensional Space that defied common sense.
Looking from a distance, the slopes were covered with an array of white spiders. Their bodies were the size of millstones, and they had eight furry, long legs. Unlike what Wang Lan had imagined, the Snow Spider’s legs weren’t the slender, knife-like killing implements he’d envisioned.
"The Snow Spider is an imperial-style gregarious Exotic Beast, with living habits similar to ants and bees," Jiang Xinyu explained. "There is one Spider Queen and one Spider King in each Snow Spider tribe. The Spider Queen is the matriarch, responsible for laying eggs. The Spider King commands all other Snow Spiders and closely protects the Queen.
"Snow Spiders move very fast, with strength equivalent to an adult human. Their skills are Rapid Freezing Cold Air and Ice Needle Rain Dew. The Rapid Freezing Cold Air is spewed from their mouths—a blast of frigid air exceeding negative one hundred degrees Celsius. Ice Needle Rain Dew is sprayed from orifices on their bodies, covering a one-hundred-eighty-degree angle.
"The back of the Snow Spider is covered in hard armor. Below the Star Shine Stage, it’s almost impossible to breach their defenses. However, their abdomen is very soft, and that’s their weak point.
"Actually, the best person to deal with Snow Spiders would have Earth Attribute abilities, as the Earth Spike skill could kill them in large numbers. However, Snow Spiders live on glacial and snowy terrain. An Earth Attribute Star Martial Warrior’s Earth Spikes can’t break through the ice layer, and the ice itself interferes with the deployment of Earth Attribute skills. It’s a pity..."
In fact, Jiang Xinyu’s team already knew this information; she was merely reiterating it for Wang Lan’s benefit.
"Is everyone ready? Once we’re set, we’ll start ’fencing off’ the area."
"Fencing off" meant luring a few Snow Spiders into their designated combat zone to be killed. With Snow Spiders covering the entire mountainside, rushing in head-on would be suicidal. They would be surrounded and devoured, bones and all, in minutes.
Jiang Xinyu dashed forward instantly, shooting ice arrows to enrage a few Snow Spiders. The Snow Spiders had been comfortably perched on the snowy ground, enjoying the caress of the glacial cold, napping cozily. The sudden attack startled them awake.
With the Snow Spider’s explosive temper, and with so many brethren around, would they tolerate such a provocation?
Instantly, the enraged Snow Spiders stood up, their long legs carrying them rapidly towards Jiang Xinyu.
The Snow Spider’s Ice Needle Rain Dew and Rapid Freezing Cold Air attacks had limited range; they mostly fought in close combat.
"Get ready!" Jiang Xinyu called out, and the team instantly shifted positions, dividing their tasks.
Wang Lan stood shoulder-to-shoulder with Jiang Xinyu. On her signal, he dashed towards the Snow Spiders like lightning.
The greatest threat from the Snow Spiders was their Rapid Freezing Cold Air, which could instantly freeze a person solid with temperatures colder than negative one hundred degrees Celsius. Moreover, the amount of cold air each Snow Spider could store varied, affecting the severity of their icy breath.
Therefore, Wang Lan couldn’t charge directly at the Snow Spiders. He had to constantly change directions, approaching indirectly. As he maneuvered to a Snow Spider’s flank, a whistling sound suddenly cut through the air.
An ice spike shot from a Snow Spider towards Wang Lan. Truth be told, Wang Lan hadn’t clearly seen where it was fired from, but the Snow Spider’s aim was somewhat off. In any case, that particular ice spike definitely wouldn’t graze his clothes.
When one ice spike failed, the Snow Spider suddenly unleashed a barrage, launching at least twenty more within a second. This instinctively reminded Wang Lan of the comprehensive test he had taken at the Star Martial Hall.
So the test device was actually designed based on the Snow Spiders.
Wang Lan’s blade flashed, deflecting the ice spikes that posed a threat. Those that wouldn’t hit him, he naturally ignored.
「Three minutes later」
Wang Lan successfully closed in on a Snow Spider.
In close combat, the Snow Spider’s legs swept at him like long clubs. A Snow Spider has eight legs, but only needs four to maintain balance; the other four served as its weapons.
CLANG!
A crisp sound echoed as Wang Lan’s body was instantly flung away.
Who said Snow Spiders only have the strength of an adult human? Does an adult human possess this kind of power?!
Wang Lan grumbled internally.
The Snow Spider’s armor was incredibly hard, capable of clashing head-on with his war blade.
Quickly, the Snow Spider pressed its attack again, four legs stabbing fiercely towards Wang Lan’s chest.
"Wang Lan—" Jiang Xinyu cried out in alarm.
SWOOSH! A flash of his blade, and Wang Lan had swept it upwards, cutting through the joints of two of the Snow Spider’s legs. While the outside of the joints was armored, the inside was not. With one slice, the two legs were left dangling, connected only by their outer armor.

chapters.title: Chapter 20: Acting Cool All the Way
chapters.content:
Chapter 20: Chapter 20: Acting Cool All the Way
Editor:
EndlessFantasy Translation
Severe pain shot through his legs, and the Snow Spider instantly lost its balance. Wang Lan sprang up with a leap, kicking towards the Spider’s lower jaw and sending it reeling onto its back.
SHLICK—
A knife stabbed into the Snow Spider’s underbelly, and with an upward slice, it spurted a stream of green blood. Wang Lan swiftly retreated as the spider struggled in its death throes for a few seconds before collapsing with a THUD.
"First Exotic Beast kill completed, reward: 500 experience points, 30 skill points!" The prompt sounded in his mind.
"Nice—" A voice of praise rang out. Wang Lan finally had the chance to look around and saw that in addition to the Snow Spider he had slain, the other four lured by Jiang Xinyu’s team had also been killed.
"Ten minutes to kill a Snow Spider on your own... Lan bro, you’re awesome," Xu Xiangwen excitedly cheered, brandishing his large sword.
"What’s awesome about that? You guys killed four."
"Lanzi, don’t puff yourself up like that. We’re a four-person team, fighting together, whereas you took down one all by yourself. How can that be the same?"
"Stop flattering me. Do you really think I don’t know? Could I have fought alone? Without you guys covering me and preventing a second Snow Spider from joining the fight, I would have been killed in three minutes. To call it a solo fight is a stretch; it’s still teamwork with you guys. It’s also cooperation; Xu Xiangwen killed three by himself, while I only took down one. The difference is obvious."
"Humblebragging, keep humblebragging, I’m all ears! Don’t parade your serious-faced act in front of me; you’re just fishing for compliments!"
