"I don’t believe you one bit!"
"You..."
"I forgive you!" Wang Lan hurriedly responded, fearful that Jiang Xinyu might repeat her stunt. "I didn’t blame you after I found out Ice Snow was you. Back then, you were only twelve or thirteen, a child who didn’t understand... Besides, without Ice Snow, Xiao Ai wouldn’t have come into existence. It’s okay, no worries."
"But... Xiao Ai has been after Ice Snow for years. Just last month, Ice Snow took a trip abroad and had barely appeared for ten minutes before Xiao Ai was hot on its tail. If Ice Snow hadn’t set up an early warning bomb in advance, it would have been caught."
"UH... that was an instruction I gave Xiao Ai three years ago. I’ll cancel it when I get back."
"Actually... artificial intelligences grow faster by interacting with each other. The main reason Xiao Ai and Ice Snow have developed so quickly is their years of pursuit. They clash over a hundred times a year, and each year their intelligence significantly increases. Ice Snow is a copy program of my family’s company’s intelligent computer, but in just three years, Ice Snow’s intelligence level has far surpassed its original. It seems our playful rivalry unintentionally created two rather remarkable things, huh?"
"Really? Anyway, my Xiao Ai is my butler, and you’re not allowed to have any designs on it. I won’t hand it over to anyone."
"Ice Snow is my child, too, and I won’t give it up either."
The car stopped, arriving at the entrance of the Star Martial Hall.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ
"What are you doing here?"
"Buying Star Martial Skills. I’ve successfully advanced to the Star Cloud Stage, so my Star Martial Skills also need to keep up. There are a few new A-grade Star Martial Skills available today, and I’m here to improve myself."
"Keep your skills updated? Are you saying that only by learning new Star Martial Skills can you improve once you reach a certain stage? What about the older Star Martial Skills?"
"Of course. Why else would Star Martial Skills be graded into five levels? Isn’t it because the power of the skills varies? A C-grade Star Martial Skill has C-grade power, while an A-grade Star Martial Skill has A-grade power. I only have one A-grade wind-attribute Star Martial Skill; the rest are all B-grade. This time I’ll buy a few A-grade skills and try to master them before the school term starts."
"Is that so? What if you were to elevate a B-grade Star Martial Skill to A-grade?"
"How could that be possible!" Jiang Xinyu unbuckled her seatbelt and got out of the car, her face full of confusion as she looked at Wang Lan. "Do you know what level of comprehension of Star Martial Skills is needed to exhibit the power of a higher-level skill with a lower-level one? Using terms from martial arts novels, it’s like turning the rotten into the miraculous. This is a feat that only those at the ’Fairy Spirit Stage’ can master. We are just ordinary people."
Wang Lan followed her out of the car, his eyes flickering.
He seemed different from others. For others, there might be limits to a Star Martial Skill, but it appeared there were none for him. As long as he had enough skill points, he could elevate close combat all the way to Gold or even Platinum.
Wang Lan wondered, what would it be like if close combat skills reached the Platinum level? Shattering the sky with a punch, splitting the earth with a kick? And if one dared to dream even higher, to Diamond level? To the King level? Could one throw a punch at the true speed of light? That would truly be a One-Punch Man.
It seemed his future truly held limitless possibilities. His only concern was whether he would live long enough to see them.
Following Jiang Xinyu into the Star Martial Hall, the sales area featured a Soul Bead marketplace and a Star Martial Skill marketplace. Each client was given a tablet to select what they needed.
"Basic Soul Beads... Eighty-thousand each? They dare to sell them for eighty-thousand when their buyback price is only one thousand? That’s just extortion!" Wang Lan casually clicked on the Soul Bead section and was immediately stunned.
"The state needs to provide benefits for Star Martial Warriors. With more than two million of them nationwide, that’s a huge financial expenditure. If they weren’t this expensive, most lower-ranking Star Martial Warriors would be left with nothing. You haven’t even seen the middle-grade Soul Beads priced at three hundred thousand, and the High Precision Soul Beads at a million."
"So expensive, which Star Martial Warrior can afford that..."
"Therefore, those who can afford it are usually from well-established Star Martial families with histories of several hundred to a thousand years. For people like us, money can only be an aid; advancement still relies on ourselves."
Jiang Xinyu focused on choosing Star Martial Skills, while Wang Lan also started looking through them. The Star Martial Union mostly had D and C-grade skills. There were very few B-grade and above, just over ten, and only three A-grade new arrivals.
Among the dozen or so B-grade skills, two were fire-attribute, one wind, one thunder, and the rest were attribute-less Star Martial Skills.
Star Martial Skills are divided into those with attributes and those without. Attributed skills can only be learned by Star Martial Warriors of the corresponding attribute, while attribute-less Star Martial Skills can theoretically be practiced by anyone. But don’t assume that attribute-less skills are less powerful. The strength of attributed and attribute-less Star Martial Skills is relatively equal. However, in terms of learning difficulty, skills matching one’s own attribute are the simplest to learn. Attribute-less skills, often involving high-level manipulation of Star Power forms, place high demands on the Star Martial Warrior. You either need enough talent, or you need to work hard enough.
And the A-grade Star Martial Skills were like the two types Wang Lan had just learned; the cheapest of them cost five million. Clearly not something the average person could afford.
Jiang Xinyu’s decisive personality shone through. The four A-grade Star Martial Skills seemed tailor-made for her, as she bought them all in a package, spending a total of twenty million.
Truly extravagant.
"Aren’t you buying any?" Jiang Xinyu asked in a low voice. "I saw many C-grade Star Martial Skills that would suit you."
"Forget it."
"Why?"
"Once you’ve seen the ocean, other waters will pale in comparison; once you’ve witnessed the grand mountains, other hills will seem trifling."
Jiang Xinyu’s pretty face blushed, and she gave Wang Lan a coquettish, sidelong glance.
Xinyu, you’ve got it wrong! I mean it in the literal sense. Having just learned two A-grade Star Martial Skills, do you think I’d be interested in these C-grades? And there’s nothing I want in the current selection of A-grade skills.
After leaving the Star Martial Hall, Jiang Xinyu drove Wang Lan home. Before parting, Jiang Xinyu called out to him, "Focus on improving yourself this term. The theoretical lessons for the second year have already ended. Our priority in the third year is to prepare for the provincial martial arts competition and the college entrance exam. Your ability is noteworthy, but you should master a few Star Martial Skills. Those at the Star Shine Stage can already demonstrate the power of their Star Martial Skills. I’m also going into a month of intensive training. Since you’re two years behind, you’ll really need to catch up."
"I know. Take care on the road."
Jiang Xinyu closed the car door, her face showing a hint of annoyance. "Jerk!"
Wang Lan returned to the Xinyu Building. Of the many skill points he had previously been rewarded with, upgrading Star Cloud Sword Dance to Silver V consumed half. From the remainder, he spent two hundred points to upgrade Inch Strength Fist to Silver II, one hundred points to learn Flame Sword, and another two hundred points on Basic Combat and movement technique.
All of his skills were at the initial Silver rank, and his skill points had now been expended. Having just joined the Tianjian Bureau, he probably wouldn’t have any tasks so soon. Earning skill points and upgrading could be put on hold for now; the pressing issue was to catch up on his lessons. The two years’ worth of Star Martial Class curriculum he had missed would take a month to cover.
This was an enormous undertaking. The textbooks he purchased with his Star Martial Badge had already been delivered, piled in his study and occupying a full square meter of space.
If he couldn’t keep up with the average third-year level, Wang Lan would have no choice but to start over from the first year, a prospect he categorically could not accept.
I thought that awakening the system would spell the end of my years drowning in a sea of practice exams. The revolution is not yet a success; the struggle continues!

chapters.title: Chapter 53: You Still Count for Nothing
chapters.content:
Chapter 53: Chapter 53: You Still Count for Nothing
Fortunately, Wang Lan was long accustomed to a dull academic life and enduring solitude, having mastered his own study methods. For an entire month, he rose at six every morning and went to bed at ten every night, with all three meals being takeout.
After a whole month of fruitful dedication, he finally managed to go through all three years of textbooks. But did that mean mastery? Wang Lan could only say he had a basic grasp.
To keep up with Jiang Xinyu and Xu Xiangwen, he would need to spend another half a year practicing and repeatedly comprehending. Learning is never an overnight affair.
But... the first day of school had arrived.
Two days earlier, Wang Lan had received an enrollment notice from Suzhou No.1 Middle School’s Star Martial Arts Campus. The class he was assigned to was Senior Three, Class One.
It was uncertain whether Jiang Xinyu had pulled some strings or if the school had arranged it that way.
Wang Lan’s home wasn’t far from Suzhou No.1 Middle School. He usually walked, or, if he managed to squeeze onto a crowded bus, he’d take that.
Today, being the first day of school, every bus was packed to the brim, so Wang Lan leisurely walked to school. Although he had been at the same school for two years, this was his first time entering the Star Martial Arts Campus.
Upon arriving at the entrance, he saw Jiang Xinyu, dressed in a white dress, leaning against the gate and looking at him. Beside her, Xu Xiangwen and Gong Feiyu were chatting, their arms over each other’s shoulders.
Wang Lan strode forward. "You guys are here so early?"
"Lanzi’s here? Early? Everyone gets up very early on the first day of school."
"It’s only you, Lanzi, who’s like an old cadre, as steady as a rock all year round."
Following the three into Class One, Wang Lan saw that about half of the students had already arrived. He clearly felt many eyes on him; after two years with the same classmates, a new face would naturally draw attention.
Only junior high and elementary school students held exceptional reverence for Wang Lan, the ’Scholastic Deity.’ His high school peers might have heard his name, but eight or nine out of ten wouldn’t know what he looked like.
"Where should I sit?"
Jiang Xinyu pointed to a seat not far away. "There. It used to be Wang Youle’s seat."
As soon as Wang Lan set down his bag and took his seat, a buzz arose in the classroom.
Wang Lan discreetly surveyed the class. He realized that the Star Martial Arts Campus was indeed full of eccentricities. Some students had hair dyed in various colors, others sported a distinctly non-mainstream look, and he could even spot a few extreme fashion aficionados in a corner of the classroom.
The ratio of boys to girls was quite balanced, but their hairstyles all boldly expressed their individuality. Wang Lan, whose appearance would normally blend into any crowd, actually stood out as an oddity in this classroom.
Wang Lan picked up a book and began to read quietly. After some time, the bell signaling the start of class rang. A stylish female teacher in high heels walked into the classroom.
"Students, it’s been a summer vacation since we last met. Did you miss your teacher?"
"We did—"
"Especially in the dead of night—"
"We were going stir-crazy at home!"
"Alright, I have some grave news to announce. Our classmate, Wang Youle, was in the Tinglin Trial Ground during the summer break for training when he inadvertently discovered a Demon Clan spy’s plot to destroy the facility. Wang Youle didn’t turn a blind eye. Instead, he took a stand for the greater good of our nation and tracked the spy. Unfortunately, he was discovered and subsequently pursued and killed by a high-level demon. Though he sacrificed his life, he successfully relayed the intelligence to the garrison at the trial ground. Thanks to his efforts, the Demon Clan’s plot was foiled, and their forces within the trial ground were completely annihilated by our troops. As we celebrate our victory, let us also give a round of applause to our martyr, Wang Youle."
Crisp applause filled the room.
Wang Lan had previously forgotten to ask if Wang Youle’s death would cause any complications, but now it seemed... there would be no trouble. To the public, a noble death was its own reward.
"Alright, I have another announcement. Starting today, we have a new student joining our class: Wang Lan. Please stand up and greet your classmates."
Wang Lan stood up. "Hello everyone, my name is Wang Lan. Some of you may have heard of me; I’m the Wang Lan from the neighboring campus. I look forward to getting along with all of you!"
"Huh? The Scholastic Deity? What brings you here?"
"No way! Did the other campus run out of room for you?"
"Scholastic Deity, tell us, is your awakened Star Martial talent related to studying?"
"Your Eminence, Scholastic Deity, the great task of raising our class’s liberal arts average score now rests on you!"
Even though this was a Star Martial Class, they were just like the senior students at the other campus—a bunch of goofy teenagers.
"Please take your seat, Wang Lan. Wang Lan awakened his Star Martial Warrior talent during this past summer vacation. Ordinarily, he would have to start from the first year. However, after discussion and deliberation, the school considered his excellent past academic record and decided to let him join Senior Three directly. I believe with Wang Lan’s abilities, he should be able to catch up on his academic subjects, right?"
"I don’t think it will be a problem," Wang Lan nodded, smiling confidently.
As the Scholastic Deity, I am unbeatable in the domain of learning.
"Good. The school also has an additional arrangement for you. If, by the end of the next semester, your academic performance hasn’t reached the expected standard, the school will make an exception and have you repeat the year. I hope you won’t mind, Wang Lan. After all, the school leadership considers you a seed student for the Four Great Academies. In fact, the principal of the neighboring campus nearly came to blows with our principal over your transfer."
The classroom erupted in laughter.
"Alright, let’s begin with the roll call—"
The atmosphere in the Star Martial Arts Campus classroom was very relaxed, something unimaginable at the neighboring campus. In an ordinary high school, students were on edge not only during class but even during breaks, not daring to slack off for a moment. Every student and every teacher was racing against time.
The bell signaling the end of class rang. Students either left the classroom or gathered in small groups to chat.
"How is it? Settling in okay?" Jiang Xinyu’s voice asked.
"Surprisingly relaxed!"
Just then, Wang Lan noticed a girl with long, orange-red hair from two rows behind him hesitantly approaching. She had a sweet face and a tall figure. However, she seemed a bit shy, stopping beside Jiang Xinyu and hesitating to speak.
Jiang Xinyu seemed not to see her, but Wang Lan turned to look at the girl with some curiosity.
"Xie Sisi?" Jiang Xinyu turned her head slightly, asking indifferently.
"Um... Xinyu, since Wang Youle sacrificed himself... does that mean your team has an open spot? I wanted to ask..."
A flicker of pity crossed Jiang Xinyu’s eyes, but she slowly shook her head. "Your strength is too lacking."
"Xinyu, I really do train very hard... and I successfully broke through to the late Starlight phase during the summer break... Plus, I have a talent for Star Power control... I won’t hold the team back..."
"Your strength isn’t the main issue. Our team is already full," Jiang Xinyu said, shaking her head with a hint of helplessness.
"Is that so? Then... I’m sorry to have bothered you." Xie Sisi’s voice was dejected as she quietly turned and walked away.
"Xinyu..." Wang Lan waited until Xie Sisi had left before speaking to Jiang Xinyu in a low voice.
"Lanzi, now you see where Xinyu gets her ’Ice-Snow Queen’ title, right? Cold as ice, frosty as snow, utterly ruthless, Her Majesty the Queen!" Xu Xiangwen teased with a light laugh.
"Entering the trial ground at the Starlight phase is tantamount to suicide, and I can’t always be there to protect her," Jiang Xinyu explained. "It’s better to be firm now and extinguish her hopes than to be soft-hearted and lead her into a fatal situation."
Wang Lan nodded silently.
Sometimes, being kind isn’t truly beneficial for others; decisiveness, even if it seems harsh, can also be a form of care.
"I say, Monitor, you really are reaching, aren’t you? Pushing yourself forward like that. To them, we commoners are nothing. It’s a good thing she rejected you. If she hadn’t, you might not even know how you died."
At this, one student from a group of four in the class suddenly called out, his tone laced with sarcasm.
"Song Bo, what are you implying?" Xie Sisi, who hadn’t gone far, turned back.
"Implying? I wouldn’t dare. Wang Youle definitely went into the trial ground with you three. All of you came out fine, but his death is so mysterious, tsk tsk tsk... Who knows how he really died?"
"Song Bo, are you looking for a beating? How about we settle this on the sports field at noon?" Xu Xiangwen slammed his hand on a desk and retorted angrily.
"Does Young Master Xu only know how to reason with his two greatswords? Monitor Xie, I advise you to stop trying to curry favor with those who are indifferent. They’re rich young masters, and we’re commoners; you need to recognize your own standing."
"Who’s eating lemons?" Wang Lan suddenly shouted, fanning the air vigorously with his hand.
"Eating lemons? Who?" someone asked.
"If no one’s eating lemons, then why is the air thick with such a sour smell?" Wang Lan retorted.
"It seems the Scholastic Deity takes issue with what I said?" Song Bo sneered. "Well, that figures. The Scholastic Deity walked in with them; you must be from a wealthy family too, right?"
"Don’t spread false rumors! I’m quite poor. It’s just that you’ve been spouting nonsense from the start, trying to confuse things, and I can’t stand it."
"How have I been spouting nonsense? You tell me! Why did Wang Youle die while the three of them lived? How can you be sure Wang Youle wasn’t set up to die by them?"
"There are official news reports and announcements stating Wang Youle died at the hands of a Demon Clan spy. That shouldn’t be false, right? As for why Jiang Xinyu, Xu Xiangwen, and Gong Feiyu made it out unscathed, isn’t that obvious? They’re strong, so they survived. Wang Youle was less skilled, so naturally, he didn’t make it. What, is your logic that the strong should have weaker survival skills? That’s illogical!
Furthermore, you claim that you ’commoners’ are nothing in the eyes of the ’elite.’ Does Jade Country even have such a clear divide between ’elite’ and ’commoner’? Can any student here say who has proclaimed themselves ’elite’ and looked down on ’commoners’? Is being from a well-off family a sin? I haven’t heard any well-off students calling themselves ’elite’ or despising ’commoners.’ On the contrary, all this talk of ’elite’ and ’commoner’ comes from you. Jiang Xinyu and her friends haven’t called themselves ’elite,’ yet you’re quick to label yourselves ’commoners.’ It seems the one who truly looks down on ’commoners’ is you.
As for your claim that in Jiang Xinyu’s eyes, Xie Sisi is less than nothing, that’s even more wrong.
I think, in Jiang Xinyu’s mind, you could at least count as a fart. Otherwise, she would have completely ignored the fart you just let out."
"PFFT—"
"Hahaha..."
"Brilliant, absolutely brilliant!"
"My good sir, you’re mistaken! How could you be less than nothing... you can definitely count as a fart! Hahaha... I’m dying of laughter..."
"When the Scholastic Deity lays down a burn, it’s truly on another level!"
The classroom erupted into laughter, while Song Bo and his three companions trembled with rage.
"You... you’re asking for death!"
Just as Song Bo was about to lunge forward, the temperature in the classroom suddenly plummeted!The source of this content ɪs
RIIING—
At that precise moment, the bell for the next class rang.

chapters.title: Chapter 54 Yin Damage Move
chapters.content:
Chapter 54: Chapter 54 Yin Damage Move
The bell for class rang on time, and all the students who had been watching the commotion returned to their seats.
In the Star Martial Class, there were three cultural lessons in the morning, while the afternoon was devoted to martial skills training, taught by hired Star Martial Warrior teachers who imparted Basic Combat abilities.
「After lunch.」
Wang Lan still habitually went up to the rooftop, as he had grown accustomed to this way of relaxation. After a period of study, standing on a high floor and gazing into the distance, with the breeze blowing through his hair, he felt incredibly refreshed.
But when Wang Lan arrived at the rooftop, he found to his astonishment that there were four lounge chairs set up, each accompanied by a sun umbrella. Xu Xiangwen and Gong Feiyu, the two scamps, were already lounging in chairs, flipping through magazines.
A cola straw was at Xu Xiangwen’s lips. SLURP...
The serene atmosphere of the rooftop was instantly shattered, leaving only the ostentatious air of a gold-sand beach.
"Wang Lan, you’re late..." Xu Xiangwen slightly lifted his pitch-black sunglasses. "What do you think? Satisfied?"
Wang Lan took a deep breath and approached the edge of the rooftop. The old campus area was right before his eyes.
"My carefully selected feng shui spot... ruined completely by you two clowns. A perfectly good rooftop, and you set up lounge chairs? And sun umbrellas? Why don’t you just set up a barbecue grill while you’re at it?"
"Good idea! I’m also sick of eating takeout every day. Feiyu, why don’t you bring some food tomorrow, and we’ll grill it ourselves?"
"Are you serious?"
Wang Lan had never realized before how ridiculous these two could be.
"Do you think this rooftop belongs to your family?"
"It’s not owned by my family... but! This building was constructed by the Xinyu family, so only we have the right to use the rooftop. Otherwise, why do you think such a good feng shui spot would allow us to set up lounge chairs and sun umbrellas?"
"Heh..."
Wang Lan felt he had no common ground with them.
He sat down on the lounge chair beside Xu Xiangwen. "Xiangwen, what’s the situation with our class?"
Xu Xiangwen slowly moved aside his magazine. "Are you asking about Song Bo, Wu Xiaowei, and the others?"
"Not just them, but also the so-called divide between commoners and the wealthy... I feel that our class, with just fifty people, is split into seven or eight groups. To put it nicely, people are sticking to their own circles, but to be blunt, it’s full of cliques. It’s supposed to be one class, right?"
"That... You’re not used to it because it’s your first class. It’s not as complicated as you think. In fact, it can be divided into five categories."
"’Just’ five categories? That’s a good one! What ordinary class gets divided into five categories? Your elite circle is truly complex."
"What elite circle? You’re now one of us, part of the elite quartet. You’re one of our own!"
Xu Xiangwen took a gulp of cola and chuckled. "Although we’re still students, we’re also Star Martial Warriors. As Star Martial Warriors, it’s inevitable to be categorized.
Do you know about the disdain chain in the Star Martial Warrior world?"
"There’s a disdain chain?"
"It’s just a term. It’s like stage actors looking down on movie actors, and movie actors looking down on TV actors. Do they truly disdain each other? Certainly not. It’s just an implicit status issue, and it’s also related to strength.
In the Star Martial Warrior world, at the top of the disdain chain are the Star Martial noble families. These are families with inherited talents and Star Martial Skills. Our class has three of them. They don’t associate with us, and we don’t associate with them.
Below them are Star Martial Warrior families and what they call the ’noble’ families. Star Martial Warrior families refer to classmates whose parents are Star Martial Warriors. Besides what they learn at school, they can also receive private tutoring from their parents and practice with Soul Beads provided by them.
And then there are people like us, the so-called ’nobles.’ But ’noble’ isn’t a term we came up with. It was those idiots from the Commoner Genius Association who coined it.
We prefer to call ourselves the ’cash-spending clan.’ If luck won’t save the unlucky, then spend cash to change your fate.
Our type of people usually come from families that run companies or businesses, but our parents are ordinary people. We made our families proud by awakening our Star Martial Warrior talents. Our families, of course, are willing to spend a lot of money to support us.
Star Martial Skills, buy! Soul Beads, buy! Weapons, buy, buy, buy!
Because of this, some idiots become envious and intentionally exacerbate the conflict. The majority of our class comes from commoner families; commoners make up more than thirty out of the fifty students.
Their parents are ordinary workers. Even if they work their hardest, it’s already difficult enough to support a household, let alone afford Soul Beads and skills for their children. Some can’t even afford to eat their fill."
Wang Lan: "..."
"That’s an exaggeration! Can’t even eat their fill? Isn’t the goal this year to eradicate poverty? How many people would have to be executed for that to be true?"
"You’ve only recently awakened and haven’t attended any practical classes, so it’s normal that you don’t know." Gong Feiyu said with a smile from the side. "Did you notice this morning that most students in our class are rather thin?"
"I did notice that. After all, Star Martial Warriors need to train."
"That’s not actually the main reason. In our first year, the Star Martial Art teacher taught us a method to extract Star Power from our cells—something not found in textbooks. Star Martial Warriors can extract energy from their cells to increase their Star Power.
But this method has a drawback. After extracting cellular energy, you’ll lack nutrients and feel very hungry. A Star Martial Warrior’s appetite is generally twice that of a normal person. If they extract cellular energy, their appetite will skyrocket tenfold.
Their parents are mostly ordinary workers. Even if both parents work themselves to the bone, it’s already a struggle to cover family expenses, let alone satisfy such a ravenous appetite.
Most children from ordinary families aren’t well-fed. But it’s an unavoidable situation. If they don’t want to go hungry, they shouldn’t extract cellular energy. But if they don’t, they can’t keep up with the others. So..."
"Sometimes we do feel sympathy for these students. In the first year, we often treated our classmates to meals. But ever since the Commoner Genius Association appeared, we stopped putting ourselves in an awkward position.
The president of the Commoner Genius Association is Duan Ziqi. He’s said to be a genius who came out of an orphanage. He awakened his Star Martial Warrior talent at age eight and is very strong. He founded the Commoner Genius Association, specifically inviting talented commoner students to join.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
Initially, their creed was that even children from commoner families could surpass us ’cash-spending elites’ if they worked hard enough. But their message gradually twisted, and they began inciting commoner students to resent us.
When we treated classmates to meals out of kindness, they portrayed it as us giving handouts or charity, implying that anyone who ate with us was a beggar or something similar. In the end, our good intentions backfired, making us look bad from every angle. So, yeah... we stopped treating people to meals after that.
But although there’s a rotten apple in the Commoner Genius Association making things nasty, most of the other classmates are pretty decent. Everyone has just tacitly accepted their respective circles, leading to the situation you’re seeing."
"It’s true what they say: wherever you have people, you’ll have complex social dynamics!" Wang Lan sighed. "So, which circle do I belong to?"
"Do I even need to say it? You’re obviously in our circle."
"But my family doesn’t own any businesses, and my mom is a Star Martial Warrior. By that logic, I should be part of a Star Martial family."
"Nonsense! Your mom is the Flame Emperor, one of the Five Emperors. The Star Martial family circle wouldn’t dare accept you. If anything, you’d belong to the Star Martial noble family circle. But their standard requires a four-generation Star Martial Art lineage, and you’re only the second generation.
Besides, even though your family doesn’t own a company, you earn way more money than my old man, okay? In Suzhou City, you own three office buildings in the business center.
You rake in eighty million just in rent each year, there’s a shopping mall in Modu City worth three billion, and two more in the Imperial Capital. You’re the real deal, a tycoon. Let’s become sworn brothers, shall we?"
"Who did this?" Suddenly, a cool voice rang out. Jiang Xinyu had appeared on the rooftop, seemingly out of nowhere.
"I did it. You like it?" Xu Xiangwen said smugly, nudging his sunglasses up.
"It’s too showy. There’s a baseline test this afternoon!"
"So what if there’s a test? We haven’t slacked off during the summer vacation."
"Hu He told me that Song Bo and his gang are planning to give Wang Lan a hard time this afternoon. Their Star Martial Skills aren’t great, but their Basic Combat abilities are solid. Plus, they fight dirty—no holds barred, truly underhanded moves. Be careful!"
"Underhanded moves? Like what?"
Gong Feiyu slowly stood up. "For example, Monkey Steals Peach, Black Tiger Heart Pluck, Thousand Year Kill."
COUGH! COUGH! COUGH! Wang Lan shivered with revulsion, goosebumps prickling his skin. "That’s just sleazy."
"What’s sleazier is they don’t differentiate between guys and girls!"
「In the afternoon, the class bell rang.」
In the martial arts gym, students from their class sat in a fan shape on the wooden floor.
"This assessment will primarily test your combat strength, comparing it to your performance in last semester’s final assessment to see if you’ve improved or regressed," the middle-aged coach said indifferently, holding a name list. "The assessment will consist of paired fights. Students whose names are called will come forward to participate. Once your assessment is complete, please take a seat on the opposite side.
A summer vacation, two months. I’m sure you all had a very comfortable time, didn’t you? However... you are Star Martial Warriors, born with a mission to fight, to get stronger.
For a Star Martial Warrior, there are no holidays, no rest, no comfort. When there’s a battle, you fight. When there isn’t, you train.
On a grand scale, you shoulder the heavy burden of protecting human civilization. As long as the threat remains, your nerves must always be taut. On a smaller scale, in less than a year, you’ll be taking the college entrance exam. Whether you become a dragon soaring in the vast ocean or one confined to shallow waters will depend on your consistent efforts.
This assessment focuses on testing your combat strength, to see whether you’ve improved or regressed since last semester’s final assessment. The assessment consists of paired fights. Those whose names are called, please come forward to participate. Once your assessment is complete, sit on the opposite side.
Jiang Xinyu, Song Qi."
As the assessment began, Jiang Xinyu, touted as one of the top three powerhouses in Suzhou No.1 Middle School, could easily overpower other students even without using Star Power or Star Martial Skills. The student paired against her was virtually defenseless.
Yet, in several instances where Jiang Xinyu could have finished the fight with a single hit, Wang Lan could see she was holding back. She also gave Song Qi ample opportunity to display his skills. However, after five minutes, Song Qi was knocked to the ground and conceded defeat.
"Mm, you both have made significant progress in your combat skills over the summer. Keep up the good work."
"Thank you, teacher!"
"Next two, Ma Chengcheng, Xu Jiayu!"
The combat level at Suzhou No.1 Middle School... seemed quite average to him. So far, he felt that out of the people who had competed, only Jiang Xinyu might be a match for him. After all, his silver-level Basic Combat skill was something even a typical Star Shine Stage student might not possess. Unless it was a Star Shine Stage practitioner specializing in combat, anyone else would likely get a good thrashing from him.
"Next pair, Xie Sisi and Song Bo!"
"Ah?" On hearing this matchup, Xie Sisi’s complexion immediately turned pale.
Song Bo stood up with a smug look, swaggering forward as if he were the most impressive person in the arena.
"Song Bo, Xie Sisi is not very strong in combat. Don’t hit too hard."
"Got it, got it. How could I ever hit our class leader!"
"Song Bo, please instruct me!"
"Please!"
They quickly engaged. Xie Sisi’s combat ability... well, her movements were textbook but rigid, lacking any real drive or adaptability. There could only be one reason for this: she trained alone, with no one to spar against. No matter how much one practices alone, it ultimately amounts to mere posturing without actual combat experience.
Suddenly, a sly smile touched Song Bo’s lips, and his entire demeanor shifted dramatically. With a swift movement, he closed the distance, landing three sharp knife-hand strikes on the joints of Xie Sisi’s arms, followed by a sudden punch.
Wang Lan shot to his feet, but it was too late. Xie Sisi was struck squarely in the chest by a palm and sent flying backwards.
SPURT—
Blood sprayed through the air, the sight shocking all the classmates pale.

chapters.title: Chapter 55 Returning the Original Number
chapters.content:
Chapter 55: Chapter 55 Returning the Original Number
The sight of Xie Sisi spewing blood caught everyone off guard. Disbelief was etched on every face; even Song Bo, standing in the ring, was bewildered and unsure of what to do.
Among all the students, only Wang Lan understood what had transpired.
Dark Strength Fist!
Inch Strength Fist is a type of Dark Strength Fist, but Dark Strength Fist encompasses more than just Inch Strength Fist.
Dark Strength Fist is a general term for a category of fist techniques, with Inch Strength Fist being merely one variety. Through a special method of exerting force, a seemingly ordinary punch could unleash power several times greater.
Within the Dark Strength Fist techniques, there existed an even more insidious type. Its fist energy would penetrate the target’s interior, causing internal damage. Mastering the force exertion technique of Dark Strength Fist required repeated practice and intuitive understanding; it was something that could be comprehended but not verbally conveyed.
"Song Bo, what are you doing?" the combat instructor roared furiously.
"I don’t know... I just meant to push her away with an ordinary palm strike. I don’t know what happened to Xie Sisi. I... I didn’t do it on purpose."
"You... Two students, quickly take Xie Sisi to the infirmary."
Wang Lan rushed to Xie Sisi’s side, Jiang Xinyu’s figure flashing as she followed.
Wang Lan touched Xie Sisi’s neck to check her pulse.
Such a vicious punch,
he thought.
Dark Strength penetrated right through, directly perforating her stomach. An injury like this is incurable; she can only be carefully nursed.
Furthermore, the quantity and types of food she could ingest would be severely restricted. In other words, if treated with conventional methods, Xie Sisi’s stomach would essentially be as useless as a newborn’s.
As for Song Bo’s claim that he threw the punch unintentionally, that was simply impossible.
One might not be able to execute a Dark Strength Fist even if they tried intentionally, let alone by accident. It required the coordination of dozens of muscles and the fluid transfer of that muscular power to the hand.
It was a complex, precise operation, completed in an instant. Unintentional? The difficulty was akin to acing the entrance exams for Tsinghua or Peking University with your eyes closed.
"Don’t move!" Wang Lan whispered to Jiang Xinyu. "Severe internal injuries, gastric perforation! Cover for me."
Jiang Xinyu understood immediately. Wang Lan discreetly slipped his hand under Xie Sisi’s collar, pressing down on her stomach. Star Power surged from him, rapidly healing Xie Sisi’s injuries.
"What are you all doing? Why haven’t you taken her to the infirmary yet?"
"Wang Lan is a Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior! He’s treating her, and I’m assisting him!"
"Oh?" The instructor’s eyes lit up, a pleasantly surprised smile spreading across his face.
Wang Lan’s name was renowned among the faculty of Suzhou No.1 Middle School.
For Wang Lan to awaken his Star Martial Warrior talent on the eve of his second-year graduation was considered nothing short of a miracle. He had been a promising student, on track for Jade Country’s top university, but then he had unexpectedly transferred to the Star Martial Arts Campus. The authorities at Suzhou No.1 Middle School were not pleased.Nᴇw novel chapters are publɪshed on ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
But what could they do? All students with Star Martial Warrior talent had to attend the Star Martial Class.
The principal of the Star Martial Arts Campus had even allowed Wang Lan to enroll directly as a third-year student. Many saw this as a move that would ruin Wang Lan’s future. Even for a genius like Wang Lan, falling behind two years meant that just catching up to the average academic level in a single year would be an extreme challenge.
Getting into a good university? Don’t be ridiculous!
However, the principal had issued a strict directive at a teachers’ meeting: Wang Lan was to be given special attention and cultivated.
What was to be done?
Liu Jie felt immense pressure.
But now... Liu Jie suddenly realized,
Our principal truly is our principal—shrewd and far-sighted!
Wang Lan being a Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior meant he could practically walk into a prestigious university.
Shielded by Jiang Xinyu, no one saw Wang Lan’s hand slip under Xie Sisi’s collar. The unconscious Xie Sisi was also unaware. A few seconds later, Wang Lan swiftly withdrew his hand and stood up.
"She’s out of danger now."
"That’s excellent! Wang Lan, I had no idea you were a Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior. What kinds of injuries can you treat?"
"Basically, I can treat most physical injuries. It just consumes a fair bit of Star Power, but it’s manageable."
"Alright, let’s move on to the next pair."
Soon, all twenty-four pairs in the class had completed their sparring matches. However, with fifty students in the class, there should logically have been twenty-five pairs.
"Since Qin Qiaoqiao is on leave, and today is Wang Lan’s first day, we’ll conclude the assessments here..."
"Ah, some people have all the luck, getting to skip the test... Teacher, what rank would Wang Lan have gotten in this assessment?" a male voice called out from the students.
"Since Wang Lan did not participate, he won’t be included in the rankings."
"Is that so? Then is Wang Lan even part of our class? Teacher, have you considered his feelings? His esteemed self, the God of Studying, has deigned to grace our class, and you’re treating him like an outsider..."
"Exactly! This is a placement test. Teacher, you should at least gauge the new student’s abilities, right?"
Wang Lan glanced towards the speakers; they were the members of the so-called Commoner Genius Association. Song Bo was being the loudest.
"Mr. Liu, I’d like to participate in the assessment. I studied combat before becoming a Star Martial Warrior, so I have some foundation."
"Is that so? Alright, I’ll pick a classmate to spar with you. Remember, keep it to a light touch!"
"Teacher, I’ll do it!" Qin Jian, a tall and burly student, shot up from the crowd.
"I should be the one," Song Bo also stood up, a smile on his face.
"You sit down! I haven’t even dealt with you for injuring Xie Sisi like that. What are you trying to pull now?"
"Mr. Liu, now, now... I’ll turn myself in after class, how about that? Who knew Xie Sisi was unwell? She didn’t say anything. My palm strike was gentle, practically no force behind it. Everyone saw that."
Jiang Xinyu sneered inwardly, then looked down at Xie Sisi in her arms, who seemed to be stirring.
"Are you alright?"
"It... doesn’t hurt anymore? I’m fine!" As Xie Sisi spoke, her ears turned crimson.
"Teacher, let it be Song Bo then," Wang Lan said. "I also saw what happened; Song Bo didn’t do it on purpose. Xie Sisi probably has a stomach ulcer from an irregular diet, and Song Bo’s punch triggered it. Just let Song Bo spar with me; we’ll stop at a touch, right?"
"A stomach ulcer?" Liu Jie looked at Wang Lan with a strange expression. "Are you implying I’ve never seen a stomach ailment, or that I can’t tell what kind of injury this is?"
"Mr. Liu, Wang Lan is a Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior. How could he misdiagnose it?" Xu Xiangwen chimed in with a smile.
"Exactly! Since Song Bo is so enthusiastic, Teacher, you shouldn’t stop Wang Lan from interacting with his classmates..." Gong Feiyu added his support.
"Well... alright then!" Liu Jie agreed, though a little worried. "Just a light touch, understand? Song Bo, you are not to attack any of Wang Lan’s vital areas, got it?"
"Understood, understood. Limbs are fair game, right?" Song Bo stepped into the center of the practice area, his face beaming with excitement.
Hitting Xie Sisi was just because I was furious that bitch made the four of us lose face this morning. Hitting her with a Dark Strength Fist was just to vent some anger.
But as for Wang Lan? Hehehehe...
How could I vent this anger if I don’t cripple you? And you, what the hell do you think you are? If you’d cursed us some other way, it would have been over. But you, you son of a bitch, had to make your insult so ’classic’?
Now, it’s not just the third-years; even the first and second-years are talking about it. In a single morning, I got the nickname Pi! Damn it! It’s a monumental disgrace, and my infamy has spread far and wide. If I don’t make you a cripple for life, I, Song Bo, will take your surname!
As for why Jiang Xinyu and the others weren’t stopping this, and even seemed happy for Wang Lan to spar with me?
This made Song Bo hesitate for a moment.
But the hesitation was instantly dismissed. All things considered, you, Wang Lan, only awakened two months ago. How strong could your combat skills possibly be? An ordinary person’s fighting ability is child’s play in the eyes of a Star Martial Warrior. Only when one truly becomes a Star Martial Warrior does their training truly begin.
This fist of mine carries five years of training. You, a newbie who awakened just two months ago, think you can block it? Dream on.
"Song Bo, I look forward to your guidance!" Wang Lan said respectfully, bowing to Song Bo.
"I look forward to your guidance too, Wang Lan. You may attack first," Song Bo replied, placing one hand behind his back and the other before his chest.
Wang Lan raised his fists and charged towards Song Bo with large strides.
Song Bo’s eyes narrowed, a cold smirk playing on his lips.
Unsteady footing, an unstable lower body, his attacking intent is too obvious. No attempt at a feint? Such a novice. Trash!
Just as this thought crossed his mind, Wang Lan’s gaze suddenly sharpened. With a swift shuffle of his feet, Wang Lan instantly closed the distance.
Song Bo’s expression changed drastically. He hurriedly crossed his arms before his chest to block, but Wang Lan’s hands, like Mantis Blades, instantly pried open Song Bo’s defense.
A fist shot out, then instantly transformed into a palm.
BOOM—
With that push, Song Bo’s body was sent flying backward.
As Song Bo sailed through the air, blood sprayed from his mouth. A searing pain, as if his internal organs were being scorched by fire, instantly engulfed his entire body.
This series of actions happened so quickly that even Mr. Liu didn’t have time to react.
A deathly silence fell over the area. Every student stared, eyes wide with disbelief, at Wang Lan’s back. Xie Sisi, in particular, was stunned. Two words echoed, dominating her mind.
So cool—
The same scene, the same situation... Could it be that Wang Lan did this for me?
A young girl’s thoughts are wonderfully complex. In that instant, her heart felt as sweet as honey.
THUD—
Only then did Song Bo crash to the ground.
"Challenge successful. Reward: ten experience points, one skill point!"
COUGH COUGH COUGH— Violent coughs wracked Song Bo’s body, accompanied by spatters of blood.
"Huh? How could this happen? You... Song Bo, do you have a stomach ulcer too?" Wang Lan exclaimed in feigned disbelief.
"Song Bo!" The other three members of his group rushed to his side. As they tried to help him up, a sharp, crisp sound came from Song Bo’s chest.
CRACK—
Song Bo let out a bloodcurdling scream, "Ahh—"
Wang Lan’s earlier punch had broken three of Song Bo’s ribs, but the force had been so well controlled that the bones were merely fractured, not displaced. However, with his three classmates now trying to lift him forcefully, the ribs had shifted out of place.
"Broken... They’re broken..."
"You!" Qin Jian whirled around furiously. "Teacher, it was agreed no attacking vital areas! Aren’t you going to do anything?"
"Wang Lan, explain yourself!" Mr. Liu’s face darkened. This was becoming blatant.
"Teacher, your instruction about not attacking vital areas was directed at Song Bo, not me. Besides, the area I struck wasn’t a vital point. As for Song Bo coughing up blood, everyone saw I just pushed him. It shouldn’t have been that serious, right?"
"You bastard, you broke Song Bo’s ribs!" Qin Jian roared.
"It was very quiet here just now. I believe many students heard it. That cracking sound seemed to occur when you three were trying to help him up, didn’t it? There are surveillance cameras here. If necessary, we can review the footage. I’m starting to wonder, did you three break Song Bo’s bones just now to frame me?"
Wang Lan looked utterly innocent, baffling the watching students.
Indeed, it had seemed like Wang Lan had only given Song Bo a light push, and he had gone flying. If bones could break that easily, how brittle must they be? Amidst the confusion, Jiang Xinyu’s lips curved into a faint smile.
"Wang Lan, please treat Song Bo," Mr. Liu said.
"Teacher, treating Xie Sisi earlier exhausted my Star Power. To treat him now would require... about three hours for my Star Power to recover. Don’t worry, I’ll make sure he’s healed before school ends."

chapters.title: Chapter 56 The Instructor Goes Mad
chapters.content:
Chapter 56: Chapter 56 The Instructor Goes Mad
The test completed, Liu Jie began to offer specialized guidance to each student.
Song Bo, injured, sat in a corner, occasionally letting out a cough or two. Qin Jian and the other two quietly gathered around Song Bo with questions.
"Song Bo, what exactly is your condition? How could you be pushed so easily by him..."
"Pushed so easily my ass! He’s a master! An ancient martial arts master! What do you think his palm strike was?"
"You mean... his palm strike was just like the one you threw before..."
"The same strength, he did it on purpose. Now I understand why Jiang Xinyu and the others were so keen on egging me on to fight Wang Lan. This academic god is a monster. Even before becoming a Star Martial Warrior, his strength was in no way inferior to ours. He has mastered incredibly profound ancient martial arts."
"I see. I was wondering how strong a newly awakened Star Martial Warrior could be, especially one with the Medical Attribute. So that’s the reason! Song Bo, what do we do? Ambush him after school?"
"Ambush? Jiang Xinyu and the others won’t just turn a blind eye. To get even, we’re probably going to need the boss and the Twelve Vajra Brothers to step in."
Wang Lan sat quietly aside, head down, still pondering the ’experience value ten, skill point one’ thing from earlier. He had always thought that to gain experience points, he must kill, and not just any kill like chickens, fish, or rats—it had to be something substantial, even something that could threaten his life. Wang Lan gained experience points either from completing tasks or killing Demons, Demon Soldiers, and Demon Generals. But who knew defeating a classmate could also net him experience points and skill points? By that logic, pummeling Song Bo would reward ten experience points and one skill point—do that five times and it’d be equivalent to killing an Exotic Beast. But what if he did it a hundred times in one day? That’s a thousand experience points and a hundred skill points.
At that thought, Wang Lan suddenly looked up at the Song Bo quartet, who no longer seemed so annoying in his eyes.
What were they? Walking experience points, walking skill points! Maybe... beat them up again?
Wang Lan looked up at Song Bo and his group with ill intent, his blatant gaze causing them to shudder instantly.
"Wang Lan!"
"Yes?" Wang Lan quickly stood up.
With his head down looking at the evaluation form, Liu Jie paused with his pen, then looked up at Wang Lan. "Your move earlier was too fast, the duration too short for me to clearly see your strength. How about this, I’ll be your opponent this time to get a sense of your ability."
"This... might not be a good idea, right?" Wang Lan hesitated.
All his system skills were silver grade, and although Liu Jie was a Star Shine Stage Star Martial Warrior specializing in combat, Wang Lan didn’t think Liu Jie’s strength could comprehensively reach the silver level. If he really had that kind of strength, what was he doing teaching? He’d have joined the Pioneering Legion to hunt for treasures long ago. Or wouldn’t he prefer to be an army officer?
"Don’t worry, I’ll hold back, and you don’t need to feel pressured. Just attack freely, I just want to see your weaknesses."
"Well... okay then!"
Wang Lan stood up and moved to the center of the area, while the other students immediately looked on with anticipation, especially Xie Sisi, whose heart suddenly began to race, her beautiful eyes shimmering with starlight.
Liu Jie put down his record chart and began unbuttoning his neatly arranged Zhongshan suit, revealing the snow-white shirt underneath.
When Liu Jie performed these actions, Wang Lan’s gaze sharply grew serious.
Meticulously executed movements might appear ordinary when done by an average person, but there was a suffocating pressure and an intense aura of a master when Liu Jie did them.
Wang Lan’s eyes narrowed slightly, focusing on Liu Jie’s head. His hair, dark and shiny, was combed without a strand out of place.
A suit fanatic? No, this is a master!
As soon as Liu Jie flung his jacket aside, Wang Lan could hardly suppress his urge to move; his body immediately surged forward.
"Good, your momentum is solid. Seems like you have had your fair share of real combat drills."
Wang Lan leaped up, swinging down a punch from above.
Liu Jie quickly raised his hand to block in front of him. Wang Lan’s punch landed on his arm, and he pressed down hard with another blow.
Liu Jie’s expression shifted slightly to one of astonishment as a force beyond his expectation transmitted through his arm, and then, another fist grew larger in his field of vision.
BOOM—
The entire class stared with wide eyes as Wang Lan’s punch connected, and their combat instructor was hit square in the face, his head hitting the ground.
THUD—
"Huh?"
"Challenge completed, reward: ten experience points, one skill point!"
Wang Lan’s complexion turned panic-stricken as he quickly lifted Liu Jie. "Mr. Liu, you..."
His palm placed on Liu Jie’s swollen cheek, warm Star Power flowed in, and soon, the pain on Liu Jie’s face and the dizzy sensation in his head disappeared.
As the two stood up, a buzzing of discussion arose from the surrounding students.ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
Liu Jie’s face was a bit flushed. "I was careless... I didn’t expect Wang Lan to possess such Massive Strength... Is this your talent?"
"Yes, teacher!" Given an out by Liu Jie, Wang Lan smoothly handed him the proverbial step down. "This talent of mine is called Massive Strength Fist—I can punch a huge hole in the concrete walls at home. The teacher didn’t know and suffered a big loss..."
"So that’s how it is..." The murmuring students suddenly understood.
"So it’s like that. I knew Mr. Liu couldn’t be that weak, to be KO’d by a single punch..."
Liu Jie smiled faintly, satisfied with Wang Lan’s response.
"Mr. Liu, please be careful. I’m very strong, so please do not take me lightly."
"Don’t worry, I won’t let my guard down this time."
As his words fell, Wang Lan instantly charged at Liu Jie again. Liu Jie had indeed learned his lesson and no longer dared to take Wang Lan’s attacks head-on, nimbly dodging Wang Lan’s fists with his agile movement technique.
But as soon as his stance stabilized, Liu Jie’s face drastically changed. He had just executed an actual combat movement technique, which should have allowed him to widen the gap with Wang Lan before countering.
But... he had never expected...
Before he could steady himself, Wang Lan’s figure was already shadowing him closely.
Such a fast movement technique!
Liu Jie hurriedly shifted his stance again, his feet moving quickly, even utilizing feints to confuse his opponent. By combining Ghost Step and Space Step dodging techniques, he changed positions twice in one second.
Yet Wang Lan’s movement technique could still easily keep up!
Is it just your punches that are strong? Why didn’t you tell me your speed was also this fast?
Just as shock began to rise, a dark shadow suddenly appeared before him. Wang Lan’s leg swept across with a devious angle, appearing strangely out of nowhere.
Liu Jie could only manage to cross his arms in time as the leg kicked him fiercely.
WHOOSH—
Liu Jie’s figure was sent flying once more.
WHAM! He landed flat on his back!
The world suddenly seemed so quiet...
"Challenge complete, reward ten experience points, one skill point!"
Indeed, challenges could be repeatedly farmed.
"Teacher... are you alright?"
Liu Jie slowly sat up and suddenly burst into laughter.
"Teacher, are you alright?"
"You little rat, who is Huang Feilong to you?"
"Mr. Liu, you know Master Huang? He’s my coach."
"How many years have you learned from him?"
"About five years..." Wang Lan grew even more puzzled.
"How often did you have classes?"
"Around four or five classes a week..."
"The student surpasses the master!" Liu Jie stood up, turned to the stunned students and said, "Classmates, did you clearly see how Wang Lan just attacked?"
"We saw it clearly..."
"But did you understand it?"
At this question, no one knew how to respond.
"Wang Lan was taught by Huang Feilong. Back when we were pioneering together, I was on the same team as him. We were both melee combat fanatics, especially fond of close-quarters fighting. I used to spar with him whenever we could, so I recognized the style of Wang Lan’s strikes at first glance.
"In your eyes, Wang Lan is the neighboring school district’s scholarly prodigy, a novice Star Martial Warrior who has just awakened, and just now, he has shown his Medical Attribute Star Martial talent. But he has been learning from Huang Feilong for five years, four or five lessons a week. And what about you? You have been learning from me for only two years. For those students from families with deep martial backgrounds, it may be fine, but have most of you really been diligent over these two years? Have you truly applied yourselves?
"Even before Wang Lan became a Star Martial Warrior, he had already trained his fighting skills to a professional level, while you are already Star Martial Warriors. What excuse do you have not to work hard? Do not believe in so-called geniuses in this world, nor in peerless talents. Before you say someone stronger than you is a genius with better talent, use your head. Even the smartest infant is still an infant; don’t casually use ’genius’ to deny effort.
"Seeing Wang Lan today, I suddenly realize that I have been too lenient with you all, letting you have it too easy. Now, everyone get ready, except for Song Bo! Everyone will frog jump around the Cultivation Hall ten times, followed by five hundred high kicks, five hundred side kicks, five hundred snapping kicks, five hundred whip kicks, then a thousand push-ups, and finally run twenty laps around the field."
"Ah—"
Mr. Liu had gone mad; such a full schedule left no chance for the students to catch their breath. It was one thing for the boys, but such training was brutal for the girls.
The September weather was so blisteringly hot.
Even for Star Martial Warriors with their extraordinary constitution, such a continuous three-hour session was extremely draining.
Yet, half of the class still completed these devilish training tasks, which to ordinary students would seem unimaginable, with calm and composure.
As the school day neared its end, all the students of Class One weakly collapsed inside the Cultivation Hall, while Mr. Liu walked back and forth in front of them with a roster in hand.
"Do you see? Do you all see?" Mr. Liu pointed at the half of the class that maintained their composure. "Do you see the difference? They were once considered by some of you to be wealthy heirs who can only increase their Cultivation Level by purchasing Soul Beads and would be nothing without their powerful parents. What about now? Are you ashamed? This level of training intensity is the most basic and low-level training in the world of Star Martial Warriors. And what about you? You’re so exhausted you can’t even stand.
"Strength does not come from having great parents or great resources, but from oneself! Physical fitness is the best way to measure how hard a person has worked day-to-day. Do you think their physical fitness was also boosted by Star Power? Not reflecting on yourselves is nothing but self-deception. I hereby declare that your senior year will be very miserable, extremely miserable, so much so that you will not want to look back after graduating high school. Take my word for it! If you can’t handle it, I suggest you transfer out. Do you understand?"
"We... understand..."
"Class dismissed!"

chapters.title: Chapter 57 We Are Different
chapters.content:
Chapter 57: Chapter 57 We Are Different
After changing clothes, the classmates helped each other and walked toward the classroom.
"Wang Lan, who would have thought you were a Star Martial Warrior of the Medical Attribute! Please take good care of us in the future!"
"Wang Lan, I got injured during training. Can you treat this?"
"Wang Lan, let’s hang out together later."
Star Martial Warriors of the Medical Attribute were truly the most popular in the world of Star Martial Warriors. Even the circles of Star Martial Warrior families that had previously shown indifference to Wang Lan were now extending friendly overtures.
Although one couldn’t become friends just through a few words, friendships also start from initial contact.
"Wang Lan!" Suddenly, Song Bo, whom Wang Lan had healed, appeared in front of him.
"Our club president wants you to come over after school. If you’ve got the guts, don’t run away when school’s over."
"Oh! Okay."
"Huh? Duan Ziqi thinks he’s so badass? Sending a dog to do his inviting?" Jiang Xinyu and the others hadn’t even spoken when Mingyue Wucheng suddenly came to Wang Lan’s side and smiled faintly at Song Bo.
"Even if you are Duan Ziqi’s dog, you’d better remember your kennel is in Class One. If you don’t have that awareness, I guarantee you won’t last in our class."
"Mingyue Wucheng, you..." Song Bo’s face instantly turned pitch black, but he dared not make any arrogant remarks. Mingyue Wucheng, from the Mingyue Family—a Star Martial Warrior family renowned throughout Jade Country for their unique Illusion Secret Arts.
The Commoner Genius Association, to put it bluntly, only dared to provoke people like Jiang Xinyu, who, despite her family’s wealth, had ordinary parents. They wouldn’t dare offend children from Star Martial Warrior families, let alone the scions of Star Martial Warrior noble families.
"That’s right... Although you were an eyesore in the past, you’d just buzz around a bit, like an occasional fly. But you know exactly what you were doing with that punch you threw at Monitor Xie today. Do you think we’re naive chicks? That we can be deceived? If Wang Lan hadn’t dealt with you, do you think you’d be having an easy time after school?" another representative from the Star Martial Warrior family circles said, crossing his arms with a cold laugh.
"Right, isn’t it time you apologized to Monitor Xie?"
"Apologize? What apology? I just..."
SLAP!
A slap directly stunned Song Bo.
Mingyue Wucheng lightly shook his hand. "Dark Strength Fist, is it that hard to master? Next time we’re paired in a spar, I’d also like to experience your esteemed Dark Strength Fist. Don’t be afraid to use it. Even if you don’t, I will. Just make sure you don’t get killed by a light punch from me, alright?"
At these words, the faces of Song Bo and his three companions turned deathly pale, large beads of cold sweat continually dripping down.
"Monitor Xie, come here for a second."
Xie Sisi was called over and looked puzzled at Jiang Xinyu beside her. Accompanied by Jiang Xinyu, she approached.
"Now that Monitor Xie is here, Song Bo, if you don’t kneel and apologize today, this won’t be over. Let me tell you, there are at least seven people in our class who can use Dark Strength Fist. It all just depends on your luck now. Go ahead, calculate the odds of being matched against one of us seven."
Song Bo’s face turned even paler, and he couldn’t stop trembling.
It wasn’t anger, but fear.
Sparring was a mandatory part of every practical combat class. The teacher always drew pairs at random; it was a probability of slightly more than one in three. He might avoid it once, but could he be lucky every time?
Moreover, the tricks I thought were perfectly concealed were actually noticed by so many classmates! I knew you all liked to play weak only to strike hard later, but I had no idea how much you were really hiding! If I can’t properly account for what happened today, forget staying in Class One, I probably won’t even be able to stay in Suzhou No.1 Middle School!
Under the pressure from all his classmates, Song Bo eventually caved.
He slowly knelt before Xie Sisi. "Monitor, I’m sorry. I learned Dark Strength Fist over the summer break... but I truly didn’t know it was so powerful. I just wanted to show off a bit; I didn’t mean to hurt you intentionally. That punch used Dark Strength Fist, and at most, it unleashed twice the normal fist power, making you spit blood, Monitor. It wasn’t on purpose. Please forgive me..."
"This... this..." Xie Sisi, a gentle girl, was immediately flustered by such a scene.
"I... I’m fine now... We’re all classmates... Don’t do this again. Get up..."
"Humph! Song Bo, since the Monitor has forgiven you, and you’ve suffered enough for today, we’ll let this slide. But remember, this is the only time. If you dare use dirty tricks on your classmates again, you’ll find out what real dirty tricks are."
Wang Lan was a mere spectator throughout, saying nothing, not fanning the flames, just watching quietly.
Song Bo had intended to stir up trouble, but the united classmates thoroughly humbled him within minutes.
Although, this unity likely formed only because I’m a Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior,
Wang Lan mused.
「The school dismissal bell rang.」
Students from the Star Martial Arts Campus either headed to the cafeteria or packed their bags to leave.
Wang Lan, slinging his shoulder bag, slowly walked down the stairs. Jiang Xinyu, Xu Xiangwen, and Gong Feiyu silently followed by his side.
"What’s up with you three? Why the solemn expressions?"
"Duan Ziqi’s strength has always been a mystery. In any case, his overall strength has always been in the top three at our school, on par with Xinyu. Even though Xinyu has broken through to the Star Cloud Stage, she still wouldn’t dare underestimate him," Xu Xiangwen explained.
"Uh-huh, and then?"
"Of course, we’re going with you! Didn’t you agree to go to the Commoner Genius Association after school to settle things?"
"I agreed?" Wang Lan asked, his eyes wide with astonishment.
"You said ’Okay!’" Xu Xiangwen insisted.
"’Okay!’ means I agreed?"
Xu Xiangwen stopped in his tracks, his expression priceless.
"Shit, I almost forgot Lanzi’s usual style is to lay low! He even flakes on Xinyu so casually. Who the hell does Duan Ziqi think he is, expecting Lanzi to keep his word?"
"You’ve got a point... So, what were we doing again?" Gong Feiyu asked Xu Xiangwen with a wry smile.
"Forget it, forget it! Let’s go home!" Xu Xiangwen waved his hand dismissively and turned to leave.
"Lanzi, see you tomorrow then."
"Wang Lan, do you want me to give you a ride?" Jiang Xinyu asked coolly.
"Better not. If classmates see us, who knows what rumors will spread tomorrow? I’ll take the bus myself."
"Hmm, be careful."
Though it was only my first day of school, today’s gains were quite good. I had been fretting over how to earn experience points and skill points. Since I can earn them through battles... should I consider changing my style? I’ve grown accustomed to keeping a low profile over the past dozen years. After all, I’m nearly forty in my mind, and it’s really awkward to be ostentatious among a group of kids. But if it can earn me points, it seems the ostentatious path is the only one to take, right?
In my mind, an image of myself setting up a challenge arena appeared. "I am Wang Lan, who has roamed the Jianghu for decades, seeking defeat in vain, my life as lonely as snow. Having heard that Suzhou No.1 Middle School’s Star Martial Arts Campus is teeming with experts as numerous as clouds and strong warriors as plentiful as rain, I hereby set up this challenge arena, seeking not fame nor fortune, but only defeat! Whoever defeats me shall receive one million silver Jade Coins..."
Isn’t that a bit too arrogant?
Before he knew it, he had arrived at the bus stop.
Suddenly, he felt a gaze fall upon his face.
He looked up to find a student in a Suzhou No.1 Middle School uniform smiling at him.
"Wang Lan, I’ve heard a lot about you. Let me introduce myself. My name is Duan Ziqi, from Class Five of the senior third grade."
Wang Lan’s brow furrowed. He hadn’t expected Duan Ziqi to corner him here.
"Shall we find a more secluded place?"
"Wang Lan, you’ve misunderstood. I’m not here to cause you trouble."
"Oh? Then what is it...?"
"Wang Lan, you possess extraordinary talent. Although I believe there are no true geniuses in the world—or if there are, they are hardworking geniuses—with the same effort, a genius indeed makes more progress than an ordinary person. I don’t deny your diligence, Wang Lan, but I must also admit that you are a true genius. If the revered title of Study God could be obtained through effort alone, then Suzhou City would have produced many Study Gods by now. If your ability to defeat Teacher Liu Jie truly came purely from hard work, then those classmates who have trained just as diligently for ten years should also be able to do it."
Wang Lan felt somewhat embarrassed by the praise.
I have worked quite hard, adding quite a few points...
The other party slowly took a piece of paper from his bag and presented it to Wang Lan. "I hereby sincerely invite you to join our Commoner Genius Association. Once you join, you will immediately become the thirteenth core member, and I will find ways to provide you with all the resources you need."
"Wait!" Wang Lan suddenly interjected. "Duan Ziqi, are you perhaps mistaken about something? I remember your Commoner Genius Association only recruits students from impoverished families, right?"
"Wang Lan, although it seems you are on good terms with Jiang Xinyu, that rich second-generation, to my knowledge, your family circumstances are not good. You and I are both orphans. Your mother passed away when you were very young. And you, from elementary school until now, have always walked or taken the bus to school. You never compete with others, never wear brand-name clothes, and don’t even own an electric scooter. During the summer after your junior high graduation, for two whole months, you delivered milk in the mornings and worked food delivery for the rest of the time. And you did all that delivering on foot, rain or shine! Am I wrong?"
"You managed to investigate all this?"
"It’s not difficult to find this information!"
I was speechless. If you were going to investigate, couldn’t you have been more thorough? You’re right, I am an orphan, and my mother did indeed... well, actually, I’m not so sure about that anymore. But is my aunt’s Jiayi Biotech Company just for show? Also, that summer I did indeed deliver milk in the mornings and food at other times, all on foot, rain or shine. But that was planned training to push my physical limits. You definitely don’t know I was wearing fifty-five pounds of weights while delivering milk and food. Information about me living in the Xinyu Building shouldn’t be hard to find either, right? Do you only see what you want to see?
"Wang Lan, I sincerely hope you will join my Commoner Genius Association. I have always believed that poverty is not the shackle that limits our growth. It makes us more resilient, harder working, and also brings us closer together."
"In principle, I agree with your view. But may I ask you a question, Duan? Do you know what the three major economic zones of Suzhou City are?"
"The Jin Lake Economic Zone, the Eastern Heaven Gate Economic Zone, and the Sea-view Avenue Economic Zone? Wang Lan, why do you suddenly ask about this?"
"In the Jin Lake Economic Zone, there’s a Yuanxing Building. Do you know it?"ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ
"I know of it..."
"What about the Xinyu Building in the Eastern Heaven Gate Economic Zone?"
"I’ve seen it from a distance." Duan Ziqi’s expression grew more puzzled, not understanding why Wang Lan was bringing these up.
"And the landmark building of the Sea-view Avenue Economic Zone, the Sea-view Tower, must also be quite famous, right?"
Duan Ziqi nodded silently.
"The owner of these three buildings... is me!"
"Suzhou No.1 Middle School stop is next. Passengers alighting, please exit through the rear door..."
"My bus is here. See you, Duan!"
Ignoring Duan Ziqi, who was sinking into an existential crisis, Wang Lan grabbed his shoulder bag and hurriedly boarded the bus from the front door.
BEEP—Student Card.

chapters.title: Chapter 58 How have you survived all these years?
chapters.content:
Chapter 58: Chapter 58 How have you survived all these years?
Ever since then, Wang Lan’s life seemed to have returned to its former routine. Although Wang Lan was not a talkative person, he was very approachable and easy to get along with.
In his previous class on the neighboring campus, which was full of academic powerhouses, there was fierce but veiled competition. Yet, Wang Lan managed to get along very well with every student. He could shoot the breeze with the top students and the strugglers alike.
Now that he was in Class One of the third year of the Star Martial Class, Wang Lan quickly navigated various social circles like a fish in water. They were happy to engage with Wang Lan, and he was just as happy to be on good terms with them—all except for Song Bo’s group of four.
On the tenth day of school, Wang Lan found himself in an academic crisis.
The revered "Academic God" unexpectedly failed to secure first place in the initial exam, bested by the Ice and Snow Queen.
That day, the sky was exceptionally clear; that day, Jiang Xinyu was particularly haughty.
That day, the way Jiang Xinyu looked at Wang Lan, as if he were her personal property, sent a shiver down his spine.
It was just one win; was it necessary to be so smug?
After class, Wang Lan stared blankly at the question before him: "Please provide a detailed analysis of the rules of change and the operational formula for the transformation of Star Power forms, and specify the seven key points.
Please provide a detailed analysis of the operational formula for the changes in the properties of Star Power, the three major protective measures to ensure property attributes do not backlash, and the three key points..."
Such specialized Star Martial Art knowledge questions could be easily answered by those who knew them. Even those with a half-baked understanding could try to bluff their way through. But for someone like Wang Lan, who was clueless, all he could write was "Solution:".
"Wang Lan, don’t worry, relax and don’t overthink things. Even if you didn’t come first, you still ranked fifth, right? It’s fine; Jiang Xinyu’s past performance wasn’t beneath yours, and she was only a few points behind you in each test. This time, it was a Star Martial Art category exam. You didn’t have the home-field advantage, so it’s natural that you lost..." Mingyue Wucheng said consolingly, wrapping an arm around Wang Lan’s shoulder.
After all, being revered as an "Academic God," losing the first test after transferring schools must have been tough, so Mingyue Wucheng came to offer comfort.
However, why did seeing Wang Lan fall from his pedestal feel so incredibly satisfying? No, I must hold back the laughter. But what if I can’t help it?
"The question wasn’t beyond the syllabus, was it?" Wang Lan was still bothered.
Logically, he had skimmed through the Star Martial Class’s high school textbooks in a month. Even if he hadn’t mastered everything using his self-devised learning method, he shouldn’t be completely clueless. Even if he didn’t know the answer, he should at least have some impression. But when it came to the transformation of Star Power forms and properties, Wang Lan was at a complete loss.
"It wasn’t beyond the syllabus; this is a practical Star Martial Art course!" Jiang Xinyu said proudly, lifting her head. "It’s not in the textbooks, but the Star Martial Art teacher covers it. Plus, they said it would definitely be on the college entrance exam."ᴛhis ᴜpdated by NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
"Wang Lan, if you don’t know, I’ll demonstrate for you. Don’t underestimate these two knowledge points; they are prerequisites for learning Star Martial Skills. If you can’t master the transformation of Star Power forms and properties, you won’t be able to learn ninety percent of Star Martial Skills. For form transformation, the most important thing is control over Star Power. To put it simply, Star Power in your hands should be as malleable as playdough," Mingyue Wucheng explained.
As he spoke, Mingyue Wucheng spread out his hand, and a mass of Star Power slowly took shape in his palm.
"The key is to extend from the theoretical knowledge of Star Power. The source of Star Power is cellular energy, and we can control Star Power because we have spiritual power. By mixing spiritual power with Star Power, allowing them to completely fuse, one gains control over the Star Power. The more thorough the fusion, the stronger the control. For beginners, the ratio of spiritual power to Star Power is generally one-to-five; a better one is one-to-three. This requires training. The optimal fusion ratio is one-to-one. Of course, a true master can achieve a ratio where the spiritual power component is even less than one. Once fusion is achieved, look..."
The ball of Star Power in Mingyue Wucheng’s hand suddenly began to change shape. In a moment, it became a sphere, then it squared off. One second it flowed like water, the next it spun like a vortex.
"Impressive... Mingyue Wucheng, have you achieved perfect control over your Star Power?"
"How could it be so fast? I’m only at a one to one-point-five ratio now. To achieve perfection would take seven or eight years of dedicated practice..."
Suddenly, Mingyue Wucheng’s eyes bulged, and the other students watching his demonstration were all dumbfounded.
Actually, as soon as Mingyue Wucheng completed the demonstration of form transformation, Wang Lan suddenly realized he seemed capable of it. The Silver-rank Star Martial Skill, Star Cloud Sword Dance, was an application of Star Power form transformation—and an advanced one at that. The prerequisite for learning this Star Martial Skill was perfect control over Star Power form transformation.
Don’t underestimate this theory and control method. It might look simple, but actually doing it is very difficult. It’s a skill honed through meticulous effort, like performing surgery. Theoretically, it’s just a few steps: make an incision, separate or suture, and then stitch up. But try doing it yourself. It involves countless subtle operations, requiring understanding, experience, and muscle memory, all working in concert. For Mingyue Wucheng to achieve a one to one-point-five control ratio at his age truly earned him the title of a genius of a Star Martial Art family.
Wang Lan, on the other hand, had mastered Star Power form transformation solely by allocating points. Those initial one hundred skill points certainly hadn’t been wasted. He was the type who could do things but couldn’t explain the theory behind them. Now, after listening to Mingyue Wucheng, he instantly understood.
He spread his palm, and one mass of Star Power split into two.
The two masses of Star Power turned into two stick figures, which then, dammit, performed a blockbuster-level martial arts sequence right in Wang Lan’s palm.
The entire classroom... fell into dead silence.
SNAP!
The mass of Star Power in Mingyue Wucheng’s palm... burst.
Is this even the same concept? Is this a whole different realm? Mingyue Wucheng is just managing to roll Star Power into a ball, and you—dammit—are already using it to shoot blockbuster movies? It’s like I just invented the bicycle and was proudly announcing my genius, then you roll up in a Ferrari you invented!
"FUCK!" Someone, no one knew who, suddenly let out a deep-throated roar.
All the students snapped back to reality in an instant...
Jiang Xinyu glared at Wang Lan resentfully. "You did that on purpose, didn’t you?"
Did she even need to ask? Wasn’t it blatantly obvious? He could control Star Power form transformation to a level that made others despair, and he was claiming he couldn’t solve that problem?
Mingyue Wucheng currently wished he could just take off his shoe and smack Wang Lan with it.
I was sincerely teaching you, and you were there acting like a complete newbie, all humble and eager for guidance. Then you suddenly pulled a stunt that nearly threw out my back!
