He didn’t live stream but only made videos. His videos were all about explaining the secrets of the Star Martial Warrior world to ordinary people, as well as introducing powerful Star Martial Warriors and some powerful Star Martial Skills. Mr. Qin had only published thirty educational short videos on a certain platform, but his fan base had reached an astonishing 30,000,000.
Some speculated that Mr. Qin might be a scion of a Star Martial family, and it was because of his powerful background that he could so boldly display the world of Star Martial Warriors in front of ordinary people.
"Mr. Qin, what is an A-Level Star Martial Skill? Mr. Qin, can you talk about the outcome of this match?"
"Yeah, Mr. Qin, since you’re here, can’t you drop some insider info?"
"Mr. Qin, leave some insider info, and I’ll invite you to be the gatekeeper."
"Qiuqiu, give me the mic," Mr. Qin replied curtly. With such a revered figure dropping in, Qiuqiu dared not hesitate and promptly handed the mic over to Mr. Qin.
"Hello everyone in Qiuqiu’s live stream room, I am Mr. Qin. I don’t like to be interrupted when I speak, nor do I like it when you spam the chat with lewd jokes. Otherwise, I’ll mute you all.Googlᴇ search
"Now, to the point: what *is* an A-level Star Martial Skill? To answer that, we need to start with the classification of Star Martial Skills based on power. Star Martial Skills are divided into five levels based on their power and the difficulty of learning them: D, C, B, A, and S.
"I won’t talk much about the difference in power between these levels, as you wouldn’t be able to comprehend it even if I did. Instead, let me talk about who typically uses A-level Star Martial Skills. A-level Star Martial Skills, known as Star Cloud Skills, are Star Martial Skills commonly possessed by Star Cloud Stage Star Martial Warriors.
"They are the most frequently used category of skills by Star Cloud Stage warriors. Owning three A-level Star Martial Skills means you could be considered among the top experts even among Star Cloud Stage warriors. Moreover, Star Cloud Stage warriors hold at least a captain’s rank in the army, and peak Star Cloud Stage experts may be granted the rank of senior captain or major.
"In the Pioneer Legion, Star Cloud Stage Star Martial Warriors can serve as commanders leading a hundred-man Star Martial Warrior legion to fulfill pioneering tasks. In other words, a Star Martial Warrior who possesses A-level Star Martial Skills has at least the achievement of being a commander in the Pioneering Legion and a core force in the military.
"If Star Martial Warriors of the same level face an opponent with higher-level Star Martial Skills, the best course of action is to concede defeat straight away."

chapters.title: Chapter 65: The Competition That Stirred Up the Whole Network
chapters.content:
Chapter 65: Chapter 65: The Competition That Stirred Up the Whole Network
"Mr. Qin, are you suggesting that this masked man is at the Star Cloud Stage?"
"No! Those at the Star Cloud Stage would not participate in the Star Martial Arts contest. This platform is too small, and Star Martial Warriors at the Star Cloud Stage simply disdain to join. This masked man is still a Star Shine Stage Star Martial Warrior. However, he has mastered an A-level Star Martial Skill."
"But from the previous match footage, the masked man didn’t seem to have an advantage over the cheongsam lady, did he?"
"Of course he didn’t have an advantage! Because that cheongsam lady is no unknown; if I’m not mistaken, she should be the one hailed as Lan Die, the Thousand Hands Guanyin. Lan Die, a peak Star Shine expert, possesses two A-level Star Martial Skills. Thousand Hand Phantom is her technique for throwing hidden weapons; with both hands, she can launch thirty projectiles in a single second, each with a different trajectory and target. Her other skill was unknown to me before, as Lan Die’s records lacked detailed information. But now it seems to be her ability to control objects with her mind. Lan Die is quite famous in Kunming for pioneering new fields and is said to have a good chance of breaking through to the Galaxy Stage before the age of thirty-five. It’s just unexpected that she would participate in the Star Martial Arts contest. Logically, she should be pioneering new fields in Kunming right now. Both of them are not your regular Star Shine Stage warriors. So, we are quite lucky to witness a match of finals-level quality in the preliminaries. The masked man appeared very passive, yet his movement technique was not at all chaotic, and his evasions were effortless. Initially, I thought that while Lan Die’s attacks were sharp, they couldn’t be sustained. Her hidden weapons are finite. Lan Die either had to win before running out of hidden weapons, or once the Star Cloud Sword was launched, the outcome would be hard to predict. But now, seeing that Lan Die can control her hidden weapons, it’s a completely different situation. For Lan Die, her hidden weapons are endless. The masked man is unlucky. With his strength, he was a safe bet for the top twenty. Unfortunately, he encountered such a formidable opponent in the preliminaries and might not even make it to the official competition."
With Mr. Qin’s commentary through the live streaming platform, the audience watching the spectacle finally began to comprehend the nuances of the contest. The moment Mr. Qin appeared, the number of viewers in Qiuqiu’s live broadcasting room suddenly exploded. Rockets flew by, attracting viewers from other broadcasters’ rooms. For a while, the traffic of other broadcasters at the venue plummeted, while Qiuqiu’s live broadcasting room was particularly outstanding; its success could be described with a single phrase: ’in a league of its own’!
"It’s exploding! Qiuqiu, your stream is lagging! Aren’t you on a 5G network?!"
"I... Is 4G not enough?" Qiuqiu felt like crying. She was just a second-rate broadcaster from Suzhou City, never imagining that one day her streaming room would break the three million viewer mark, when her previous best was only one hundred thousand viewers.
"I’ll top up for you, just stabilize the network for me."
"The final showdown! Shit, it’s ’All Swords Return to the Origin’!"
In the image, the battle between Wang Lan and the cheongsam lady had indeed reached its final stage. The cheongsam lady’s Talented Skill seemed inherently designed for hidden weapons. Wang Lan even felt that her earlier throws were a waste of time. If she had controlled the objects directly, Wang Lan might not have been able to withstand the first onslaught.
If analyzed by a data system, the cheongsam lady’s prowess with hidden weapons would likely be rated at the Silver level. She didn’t just throw her hidden weapons out all at once; the rhythm, direction, coordination between the hidden weapons, and the angle of attack were all perfect.
Perhaps the hidden weapon technique was meant to lull the opponent into a false sense of security!
Thinking about this, Wang Lan broke into a cold sweat.
If the lady hadn’t reminded him that her Star Martial Skill was magnetism-based, Wang Lan would have charged at her, only to be attacked from behind by hidden weapons rising from the ground. He might already be dead by now, wouldn’t he?
I’ve learned my lesson.
A contest isn’t a real battle, after all. The restriction against killing is a significant limitation for experts who truly fight on battlefields.
The sky filled with hidden weapons that danced like dragons, swirling darkly like a passing swarm of locusts. The spectacle was indeed just as the audience in the live broadcasting room shouted, reminiscent of ’All Swords Return to the Origin’.
At this moment, Wang Lan had successfully closed in to within five meters of the cheongsam beauty. This range, merely five or six steps, was an extremely dangerous distance.
A torrential rain of swords suddenly fell, attempting to stop Wang Lan from pressing closer. The concrete floor, unable to withstand the bombardment of the hidden weapon rain, shattered.
The combined damage to Arena Number 7 from dozens of previous fights wasn’t as horrific as the destruction from this single match.
Wang Lan’s heart tightened. He faced a very skilled cheongsam lady.
If he couldn’t even make it past the preliminaries, wouldn’t this trip have been in vain?
Open the system! Add points for me!
In an instant, his Star Cloud Sword Dance, which was at Silver Rank 5, was pushed to Silver Rank 6, then Silver Rank 7.
The moment Star Cloud Sword Dance reached Silver Rank 7, Wang Lan’s eyes suddenly sparkled. He had comprehended another assault-and-kill type Star Martial Skill hidden within the Star Cloud Sword Dance.
"Butterfly Passing Through Flowers!"
Wang Lan’s figure suddenly turned into afterimages. Amidst the torrential rain of hidden weapons, the space at the center of the battle seemed to twist, and faintly, a butterfly spread its wings.
BOOM—
All the hidden weapons filling the sky were suddenly blown away by terrifying Star Power. Wang Lan’s figure transformed into a streak of light, charging towards the cheongsam lady before him.
The cheongsam lady’s expression changed dramatically. She instantly controlled the sky full of hidden weapons, attempting to weave a shield in front of her.
But just as the shield was forming...
BOOM—
A loud crash echoed as Wang Lan’s figure, like a drifting cloud, collided with the coalescing shield of hidden weapons. The terrifying force instantly exploded, and the shield, like a dam obliterated by a tidal wave, burst apart.
The cheongsam beauty was briefly stunned. Through her distorted vision, she saw a butterfly flicker and vanish. When her sight finally focused, a figure stood before her.
The Ghost Wail in his hand was pressed against the cheongsam beauty’s throat.
CLICK—
With a crisp sound, Wang Lan’s mask instantly cracked, unable to withstand the horrifying explosion of Spiritual Power.
"I lost."
The woman’s voice sounded—low, soft, and young—like an arrow piercing Wang Lan’s heart.
"Actually, I lost! If you hadn’t told me earlier that you are a magnetism-controlling Star Martial Warrior, I would already be a corpse. Thank you for showing mercy."
"There’s nothing to thank me for. This is a competition, and I can’t kill anyone. Since I can’t kill, the least I could do was give you a warning. If you were about to unleash a hidden killing move on me, you’d warn me too, wouldn’t you? It’s only fair."
"Arena Number Seven, contestant forty-four, wins!"
Wang Lan silently turned away.
"Wait! What’s your name?" the lady in the cheongsam suddenly asked.
"Nice Person!"
"Nice Person? You’re strong. I hope you can return to the battlefield someday; this place isn’t for you."
"Uh! I will." Wang Lan didn’t explain, responding indifferently.
As Wang Lan left the arena, the live streaming chat exploded.
This was the most stunning match they had seen to date. It was so breathtaking that they even forgot to breathe. Neither Wang Lan nor the lady in the cheongsam held back in the slightest. Every move they made, every attack they launched, had only one purpose: to defeat the other. The high-frequency exchanges, rapid evasive maneuvers, and every feint and shift electrified the spectators’ nerves. This was a feast for the eyes, a fiery eruption of combat.
Ordinary people rarely had the chance to witness Star Martial Warriors in battle. Whenever Star Martial Warriors were needed, the first order of business was to clear and isolate the area.
While films and television featured many Star Martial Warrior battles, the techniques and fight scenes were choreographed for visual appeal. They were impressive to watch but lacked realism.
As netizens often said, protagonists never die, no matter how fiercely they fight; they always manage to turn the tide even in the direst situations. But what about reality? No one is the protagonist; the whole world is a furnace where anyone can die, where death could come for anyone.
A real battle is relentless, with no moment for breath or letup. There’s only one moment you can let your guard down: when the fight is utterly over.
In a battle lasting less than ten minutes, they danced with death countless times. Who could truly enjoy the thrill of dancing on a stage where hidden weapons fell like rain, or endure the gentle graze of Sword Qi across their cheek?
Each intense frame of the battle left a profound impression on the viewers.
The live streaming room fell into a brief silence, lasting perhaps ten seconds.
"Who would have thought that a match worthy of the finals would take place in a preliminary round. It’s fortunate this is only a preliminary round and isn’t broadcast; otherwise, even the official matches would pale in comparison."
In the end, it was Mr. Qin’s words that broke the silence in the streaming room.
"Holy shit!"Googlᴇ search NovᴇlFirenᴇt
"A big freaking holy shit!"
"A graveyard-sized holy shit!"
"You’re telling me this is a prelim? I feel like I’ve just watched the finals of this season’s Star Martial Arts contest."
"Who is this guy with the mask? And who’s that cheongsam beauty?"
"Even a noob like me saw more than a dozen brushes with death... Can someone tell me if this is real? Are you sure it’s not a planned stunt? They could really die, right?"
"Come here, the brother who says it’s a stunt. Let’s test this ’design.’ Forget everything else; just stand there while I throw a few hundred frying pans at you from the twentieth floor, and you dodge every single one without a scratch."
"If you get hit, of course, you’d die, but they didn’t get hit, did they? We’re all Star Martial Warriors; we know how to measure our blows... Sorry, gotta go. I’m visiting the grave of a brother who attempted a similarly dangerous move last time. To support his wife and daughter, I haven’t had time to weed his grave, and it’s overgrown waist-high."
"Hey, commenter above, you didn’t kill your brother just because you coveted his wife and daughter, did you?"
"Open up, community care coming through."
"Look, I spent thirty seconds to capture this frame at one-tenth speed for everyone’s enjoyment."
In the frame, six hidden weapons attacked Wang Lan from various angles, but his body twisted and turned, evading all six with impossible agility. The image was but a fleeting moment on screen. Yet on the battlefield, it could be the fraction of a second that mattered. Who knows how many such moments there were throughout the battle?
I daren’t even think about it. Just imagining it makes my scalp tingle.
"Fuck, is this guy even human?"
"In a mere fraction of a second, to calculate the trajectory and timing of incoming weapons and execute movements with machine-like precision... what kind of terrifying control over one’s body would that take?"
"Is the commenter above in mechanical engineering? But I have to say, control over one’s body is, in a way, control over Star Power. Clearly, the Star Martial Skills utilized by the masked man belong to the Form Changing Star Martial Skills. Mastering such skills requires gaining subtle control over Star Power, let alone succeeding in their cultivation. To perform Form Changing Star Martial Skills, one must have that level of control over their body."
"The commenter above is right. Sit down, everyone; this is basic stuff!"
"Basic stuff, my ass! Do you think I’m not a Star Martial Warrior? That level of control, even if it hasn’t reached the theoretical perfect 1:1 fusion ratio, is damn close. Achieving anything below 1.5 is impressive, and below 1.3 is god-tier."
"Seeing such masterful prowess, I wanted to compose a poem in his honor, but alas, I’m uncultured. All I can say is, ’Damn, he’s on another level!’"
By the time Wang Lan got back to the stands, the announcement for Hu Qing’s match was sounding.
Hu Qing could only hurriedly congratulate Wang Lan before rushing off.
"Qiuqiu, Qiuqiu, the god-tier player is sitting right in front of you, what do you think?"
"About your thoughts, I have a suggestion."
"About your suggestion, I have a plan."
"About your plan, I would like to make a point."
"Regarding the point you made, I have a... fuck, I can’t keep this up."

chapters.title: Chapter 66: Straight-Man Cancer is Also a Disease
chapters.content:
Chapter 66: Chapter 66: Straight-Man Cancer is Also a Disease
"In short, anyway, Qiuqiu, go ahead and have a romantic encounter with the bigshot."
"And try to get his name, age, identity, and sexual orientation for me."
"Hold on a second, commenter above, what do you mean by having Qiuqiu get his sexual orientation? Could it be you’re..."
Even Qiuqiu’s face turned red from what the ridiculous netizens were saying, her heart pounding furiously.
The strong man before her, according to Mr. Qin’s words, was definitely a genius even among Star Martial Warriors. Although he participated in the Star Martial Art competition, his future was definitely different from everyone else present at the competition.
Maybe that was why he chose to compete anonymously; he really was just there to improve himself. For a girl like Qiuqiu, who was destined to be an ordinary person for life, such a Star Martial Warrior was an irresistible temptation.
Not to mention what might become of it later, even becoming friends would be great. Having a Star Martial Warrior as a friend—how prestigious would that be?Nᴇw novel chapters are publɪshed on NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
And with such a perfect opportunity, if she didn’t strike up a conversation, would Qiuqiu still have the face to hang around in her live stream room?
May the ridiculous netizens give me courage!
She silently cheered herself on, stood up, and slowly walked toward Wang Lan.
Wang Lan was looking down, still contemplating the woman he had just sparred with. According to Hu Qing, a woman of such strength wouldn’t be interested in participating in a flashy show like the Star Martial Art competition unless there was a special reason.
Hu Qing wanted to raise money for his sister’s medical bills, but what about her?
Although she threw her weapons with such style, Wang Lan noticed that in the end, she collected all of them, even stealthily taking some of the metal materials from Suzhou City’s sports venue.
"Um... young man... may I sit here?" Qiuqiu timidly approached and asked Wang Lan in a low voice.
"Ah? Sure. Huh? I recognize you," Wang Lan said, his expression lighting up as he saw Qiuqiu’s face clearly.
"Ah? You know me?" Qiuqiu’s face beamed with surprise as if bathed in Holy Light.
"Yes, you’re the streamer from Startling Fish, right? Called... called..."
"Qiuqiu, my name is Qiuqiu!"
"Wow, Qiuqiu is about to be conquered... Quick, someone give Qiuqiu a sedative."
"Qiuqiu, you’re already a mature streamer; this is a common flirting tactic. You have to hold steady, really hold steady!"
"I guess Qiuqiu is going off-air tonight... Oh no... my Qiuqiu..."
After this exchange, the live stream room immediately exploded.
And all these warnings, reminders, and such, not a single word could enter Qiuqiu’s mind.
Embarrassed, Qiuqiu looked down and fidgeted with the hem of her skirt.
"Have you watched my live stream before?"
"No, I remember seeing you not long ago. You seemed to want to do a live stream at Fragrant Courtyard Bay, but then the security guard stopped you, and you couldn’t even get through the gate..."
Couldn’t even get through the gate... get through the gate... get through...
Qiuqiu’s expression froze instantly.
Dead silence in the live stream room...
"HAHAHA..."
Immediately, the bullet comments exploded.
"Is this guy serious?"
"That comment wounded Qiuqiu deeply!"
"Qiuqiu, my condolences!"
"HAHAHA... This guy must have no friends, right?"
"I don’t know about friends, but definitely no girlfriend. No girl can tolerate such a blunt man."
Don’t get angry, don’t get angry! Qiuqiu, you’re a mature streamer; you can’t get angry.
"Young man, thank you for the wonderful match today. Could you say hello to the viewers in my live stream?"
"Um... I guess so?"
"Hello everyone in Qiuqiu’s live stream room, I’m contestant number forty-four, Nice Person! Wait a minute..." Suddenly Wang Lan stopped mid-sentence. "Didn’t they say no live broadcasts or transmissions during the preliminaries?"
"That... only the official live streams and broadcasts are not happening. Us small-time streamers can still come in to stream."
"But I thought non-competitors aren’t allowed in here. How did you sneak in?"
The conversation came to a dead end—again. Qiuqiu silently gave a close-up to Wang Lan’s mask and then, saying she was sorry for disturbing him, turned and left. If she stayed any longer, Qiuqiu might have burst a blood vessel from frustration.
Forget it, forget it. I should just focus on my live streaming. As expected, not many Star Martial Warriors are sane.
At noon, the second round was announced to have ended.
Hu Qing and Wang Lan successfully entered the third round, the final preliminaries reducing two hundred contestants to one hundred.
"Successfully entering the third-round preliminaries: Reward 800 experience points, 80 skill points."
Having allocated all skill points to Star Cloud Sword Dance previously, my skill points had been depleted. These 80 skill points eased my anxiety about the insufficiency of skill points.
"Director Min, the high-definition footage of Wolf’s and Lan Die’s matches has been cut and edited. When should we release it?"
As soon as the morning’s matches ended, emergency video editing was immediately conducted backstage to ensure that the most authentic, clearest, and most exciting moments were captured from the best angles.
The computer screen on Min Jian’s desk was currently playing the footage of Wang Lan’s encounter with Lan Die.
Every single frame was a breathtaking scene. Even Min Jian was thoroughly engrossed in it.
"Director Min, you’ve got it already?"
"Yes! Look how exciting and beautiful the fight is. Imagine the impact if this match were in the main tournament! I regret putting this battle in the preliminaries now."
"Director Min, the contenders in the official competition are also very strong. In the second round, we discovered more than a dozen powerful contestants. Their strength is no less than Wolf’s, and once the official competition starts, there will surely be more high-quality showdowns like this one."
"I hope so. God knows how much pressure I’ve been under since taking over this program with its reputation in ruins. This video will be our weapon to turn public opinion around. But don’t rush to release it; let’s wait for the buzz to build online and keep them on tenterhooks."
"You’ve been working hard, Director Min. Should we also arrange an opponent for Wolf in the third round? We can focus on building up Wolf, make him famous before the competition starts, and then drive interest in the official competition."
"No need... one battle is enough. If the preliminaries are all this splendid, it will outshine the official competition."
"Understood!"
Peak confrontations like the one between Wang Lan and Lan Die are rare finds. Even if it were the same two players fighting another match, it’s not guaranteed to reach such a high level of competition again.
After watching that match, all other matches seemed like plain broth without any flavor, even during the round reducing two hundred contestants to one hundred, even if Wang Lan entered the arena again.
The audience hoped for an intensely thrilling battle, yet Wang Lan staged a ten-second KO.
The onsite commentators were alright; they were merely the eyes of the broad audience watching the live stream. But online, the viewers who saw that match were already itching for more.
"Unleash the keyboards!"
"Welcome to the second episode of the Masked Man Star Martial Art Competition! The contestants have entered the arena, so don’t even blink because the match is about to... end! Don’t ask me why I’m saying it’s over; I swear, I didn’t even blink."
"Lackluster and feeble. Could it be because the opponent wasn’t a beautiful young lady? The last match, you fought for ten minutes, but this one, you only fought for ten seconds, half of which was spent on pleasantries."
Anyway, although everyone was criticizing Wang Lan for ending the fight so quickly, the real fire was concentrated on the Star Martial Warrior he faced. "If you’re so weak, why bother showing up? Are you just wasting everyone’s time?" they exclaimed.
"Passed through the preliminaries: Reward 1,500 experience points, 150 skill points..."
When the official list of contestants for the main competition was announced, Wang Lan’s system reward also arrived.
In the system, I was a little less than halfway to reaching Star Shine four. If my progression went smoothly, I should be able to advance to Star Shine four after completing this competition.
"Welcome home, Wang Lan."
"Xiao Ai, make me a cup of coffee."
"Alright!"
"Xiao Ai, look up the girl I fought today. Who is she?" Wang Lan sat on the sofa, recalling the scenes from today’s combat.
I never expected that the first time I fully overcame the fear of death would be at a competition. Even saying it now, I find it hard to believe.
Previously, although I could face death, I hadn’t truly conquered it; I’d merely managed not to let the fear of death paralyze me. Truly overcoming the fear of death meant entering complete calmness in the face of danger, undisturbed by any external factors.
Initially, when facing that rain of hidden weapons, I was neither afraid nor did I enter a state of calm. But when I saw the woman’s eyes, as indifferent as an autumn pond, I was suddenly shaken. Her gaze held no emotion; she was like a cold machine.
In the past, she definitely wasn’t like this.
I tried to purge emotions but not thoughts and discovered the result was surprisingly effective. My cognitive abilities, body coordination, and even reaction speed all improved greatly.
And I named this state of wartime calmness "Sage Time."
"Wang Lan, I’ve found her. Her name is Lan Die, twenty-eight years old. Last year, she was the leader of a Pioneering Legion, commanding twelve people. Last year, they suffered severe losses while exploring a Different Secret Territory. Of the thirteen in the team, only she survived.
What’s more peculiar is that she developed a phobia of blood; even the sight of red paint would send her into a mental breakdown. That’s why she chose to leave the Pioneering Legion. Alone, she decided to take care of the families of the twelve fallen comrades. This past year, she worked four jobs: two full-time and two part-time."
"Why did she take on the burden for twelve families? Didn’t the families of her fallen comrades receive government compensation?"
"They did. It seems Lan Die feels responsible for the deaths of her team members. Rather than say she took on the burden for twelve families, it’s more appropriate to say it was a form of self-punishment."
"Understood."
After a bath, I went to bed.
The official competition would commence in three days, with one hundred official contestants going through fifty advancement matches. With each episode lasting one and a half hours, there would be ten matches, meaning just the first round would require five days of broadcasting. Wang Lan’s match was scheduled for the third day of the official competition, the third match; all of this was known well in advance.

chapters.title: Chapter 67: The Amazement of Classmates
chapters.content:
Chapter 67: Chapter 67: The Amazement of Classmates
The next day, Wang Lan got up early to go to school. To his surprise, the bus wasn’t very crowded. It wasn’t long after he squeezed on that he heard his former classmates animatedly discussing the Star Martial Competition.
The popularity of this show had reached a point where it had become a national conversation. The official broadcast wouldn’t start until next Monday, but for competitors like Wang Lan, it would begin in three days. The three-day delay was for post-production editing and camera work.
Upon entering the classroom and just managing to set down his backpack, he suddenly heard a classmate next to him exclaim.
"Holy shit, the official high-definition video is out? Awesome, awesome! The power of the masses is indeed strong."
"What high-definition video?"
"Could it be *that* one?"
"Yes, that one! The high-definition video of the fight against Lan Die. Holy shit! A match of less than ten minutes, and it’s over a gigabyte? Isn’t that a bit too high definition?"
"Can you download it?"
"There’s a download link!"
"What the hell are you dawdling for? Give me the torrent link!"
"Send it to the class group, blast it out."
Watching the excited classmates, Wang Lan turned his head in confusion. "What’s going on with them?"
Xu Xiangwen, who had just clicked download, looked up at Wang Lan with a faint smile. "For someone like you, a caveman who never goes online to stay updated, it makes complete sense that you wouldn’t know."
With that, he came over and sat next to Wang Lan. "Wasn’t yesterday the Star Martial Competition preliminaries? A match blew up the internet through live streaming. Two Star Martial Warriors staged a peak showdown within ten minutes.
"These two had similar levels to us, but if it were a real battle... I watched it, and I wouldn’t last two minutes against either of them. If it were a life-and-death duel, I’d probably be killed the moment the match started."
Wang Lan looked at Xu Xiangwen in shock.
This guy has never been so humble in my memory. Plus, isn’t his evaluation of me a bit high? If I really wanted to kill him, I’d need at least five seconds, right?
"Didn’t you say that the Star Martial Competition is all orchestrated with no real educational value?"
"But you can’t ignore it when a phoenix hatches in a chicken coop."
"It seems this season of the Star Martial Competition has truly changed. From the live streaming, the preliminary matchups were indeed real. That’s the right way to go! The Star Martial Competition should be about real combat. Who cares about Star Martial guidance and choreographed moves? If it’s all staged, what’s the point of vying for supremacy?"
"After hearing you guys, I’m suddenly looking forward to this season’s Star Martial Competition."
"Me too. I’ll deign to watch one round of the official matches. Real or fake, I’ll know at a glance."
The bell for class rang, interrupting the classmates’ lively discussion. But even though their chatter was disrupted, everyone seemed distracted during the morning’s cultural lessons.
The afternoon practical lesson was switched to the multimedia classroom.
When the class entered the room, everyone was excited. The screen in the multimedia room was playing the high-definition video downloaded earlier; it turned out that today’s lesson with Teacher Liu was an analysis of that battle.
Children who are Star Martial Warriors are much like most other kids; they have little regard for dry theory. You could talk to them about the cruelty of the battlefield and the laws of survival, and they would forget as soon as you finished. But tell them war stories of Star Martial Warriors or the legendary feats of certain individuals, and they’d remember every word.
The combatants’ Star Martial levels were similar to about half of the students in the class, not far from their own. But the match they staged won everyone’s genuine respect. Even Xu Xiangwen, who was always hard to impress, acknowledged it, let alone the others who were tired of platitudes.
The bell rang for class, and Liu Jie walked into the multimedia classroom with a stack of materials. Seeing the gleaming eyes of anticipation from everyone, he felt as if he were back in their first year, the first time he led them in a practical lesson.
Back then, most students had no foundation. And those who did, what had they learned? So-called martial arts that had impressive names but were just for show.
"Students, today’s practical lesson will be held right here in the classroom. No one has any objections, right?"
"None—" came the uniform reply.
"How many of you have seen this video?"
"We’ve all seen it..."
"I saw it last night, but it was through the live streaming interface, and from a distance, it wasn’t clear."
"I just finished downloading it and watched it twice..."
"Alright, whether you’ve seen it or not isn’t important. Today’s practical lesson is to take you through a detailed analysis of this rare real combat footage.
"Do you know why it’s rare? Because real Star Martial Warrior combat rarely gets captured on camera. It’s either done in a Different Dimensional Space, where cameras can’t be used, or the two Star Martial Warriors are fighting for real and end up behind bars eating government meals. Almost all of the so-called Star Martial Warrior duel videos circulating on the internet are choreographed fakes.
"This video released by the organizers of the Star Martial Competition is truly a genuine piece. You may find the fight thrilling, but we need to look at their on-the-spot reactions and the significance of their improvised maneuvers, so you understand where the real difference lies between students and warriors.
"This class is important. If you understand it, it will help with your mental growth.
"I always tell you that among you, there are some who are called geniuses, and even some whose Cultivation Level is stronger than the teacher’s. For example, Jiang Xinyu reached the Star Cloud Stage before starting her senior year.
"In a head-on duel, I admit I couldn’t beat you. But if we were to be placed in certain terrain in a Different Dimensional Space, and our task was to kill each-other, the odds are I would survive and you would die.
"Why? It’s because of experience—rich experience."
"I’m not bragging about myself," the teacher continued. "I’ve experienced desolation, I’ve traveled abroad, and I’ve seen too much of the dark side of this world. Half the enemies of Star Martial Warriors are Exotic Beasts and the Demon Clan, and the other half are our own human Star Martial Warriors.
"Don’t ask me why—why members of the same race would become enemies. When you all grow up, you won’t even bother to ask this question.
"Now, back to the point. Let’s start analyzing this video from the very beginning."
Saying this, Liu Jie dragged the video progress bar to the very beginning.
"The match begins. Remember, at that time the referee’s whistle had already sounded. From a rules perspective, the fight could have commenced at that point. I’ve seen many online comments expressing resistance to Lan Die’s surprise attack at the start of the match.
"But classmates, on the real battlefield, there are no rules, no courtesies, only life and death. His returning Lan Die’s courtesy shows a lack of experience right from the start. Because of that gesture, he lost the entire initiative.Follow current novels on NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
"I have emphasized the importance of initiative before—it’s not about striking first, but striking when the opponent is completely unprepared. That’s what initiative really is. If his reaction had been just a little slower, the match would have ended right there and then.
"Analyzed rationally, he made a major error in this battle. This set the stage for his passive position for the next five minutes.
"I don’t know this Lan Die, but she is definitely a warrior who has experienced life-and-death situations and extreme difficulties. Her hidden weapons seem like a simple, indiscriminate barrage, but look: every angle and attack point she launches from is calculated."
As he spoke, Liu Jie paused the video and drew Lan Die’s attack patterns and objectives on the blackboard.
Through detailed analysis, the students of Class One began to understand the complexity behind Lan Die’s hidden weapons. She had not only anticipated the opponent’s next evasive move but had calculated even five or ten steps ahead.
In the rapidly changing fray, to be capable of calculating so much in an instant was eye-opening. When Liu Jie laid bare these underlying strategies before all the students, they all felt a chill go down their spines.
Impossible to dodge! Certain death!
This was the judgment that surfaced in most of the students’ minds.
Not on the same level of planning at all. If any of us had been in the match, we probably would have been turned into a beehive at the start, right?
"Shocked, aren’t you? But the real shock is his way of dealing with it. This set of Star Martial Skills looks beautiful, doesn’t it? Sword light afterimages, forming an absolute defense, blocking the barrage of hidden weapons for a full five minutes without a single gap?
"Now, I’ll slow down the playback speed by thirty times, and you all take another look!"
The scene slowed down, and the illusion of impregnability was lifted. A barrage of hidden weapons found their gaps, with a small percentage successfully breaching the Star Cloud Sword Dance’s defense and targeting Wang Lan’s vital points.
But these attacks were all evaded by Wang Lan with agile and skillful movements—in one second, he changed position three or more times, each change requiring him to dodge over five hidden weapons.
"Holy crap!"
"Holy crap!"
Cries of "Holy crap!" rang out; even the descendants of several Star Martial noble families from Mingyue Wucheng exclaimed in unison.
"His Star Martial Skill doesn’t include the movement technique he’s using. Movement technique is a Basic Skill that you naturally grasp and master through our regular combat training.
"In such a short, dangerous time, to be honest, even I couldn’t do it, and none of you here could either.
"This movement technique, by the Star Martial world’s evaluation, should be at a specialized level. If we only consider this set of evasive actions, we could classify him as an assault-type Star Martial Warrior with specialized evasion.
"However, look at the sword in his hand. The Star Martial Skill only allows his sword to resonate with Star Power to create physical sword afterimages, but the sword skill he uses to slash at hidden weapons is one of his Basic Skills, honed through relentless practice.
"Jiang Xinyu, you are also specialized in sword skill. What do you think of his sword skill?"
Jiang Xinyu stood up solemnly, her eyes inadvertently sweeping over Wang Lan. "Without using Star Martial Skills, just in terms of sword skill, I am no match for him."
"Classmates, Lan Die is a warrior at the pinnacle of the Star Shine Stage. His (Wang Lan’s) official strength is listed as mid-Star Shine Stage, not much different from many students here.
"But your Basic Skills’ proficiency is worlds apart from theirs.
"Have you become complacent? Those of you in your third year of high school who have reached the Star Shine Stage can indeed be called prodigies. But compared to them, where do you fall short?
"Your movement technique is a bit off, your sword skill is a bit off, your ability to respond in battle is a bit off. But when you add it all up, the difference is that if they were to get a bit serious, you wouldn’t even know how you died.
"Every time you proudly judge your achievements based on your Star Martial level, please take a moment to watch this video and then look at yourselves in the mirror."
For the first time, not one or two students talked back after being lectured like this by Liu Jie.
How could they talk back? The difference between the two people in the video wasn’t large in terms of Star Power level, but the differences in other areas were clear. Previously, everyone could only express their shock with a "Holy crap." Don’t forget, everyone here is a Star Martial Warrior. At the same Star Shine Stage, why can they achieve such feats while those present can only say "Holy crap!"?
Still, after being lectured like this by Liu Jie, some students became enlightened, but Wang Lan was just embarrassed.
Every time Liu Jie describes me as a prodigy, I feel as if a pair of eyes are sharpening knives behind my back.
Taking advantage of Liu Jie drinking water and catching his breath, Wang Lan quietly raised his hand.
"Teacher, may I go to the restroom?"

chapters.title: Chapter 68 The Official Competition Begins
chapters.content:
Chapter 68: Chapter 68 The Official Competition Begins
Wang Lan was extremely grateful he had opted for anonymous competition; during a bathroom break, he mentally gave his cleverness a thumbs-up.
Just as he exited the bathroom, he saw Jiang Xinyu leaning against the wall outside, hugging her arms while gazing up at the sky.
At this sight, Wang Lan felt an impulsive urge to make a dashing turn and walk away.
"Stop right there!"
Halting in his tracks, Wang Lan smiled slightly. "I’m just going to dry my hands."
"Xinyu, you came out to use the bathroom too...?"
"Awkward small talk!" Jiang Xinyu rolled her eyes at Wang Lan.
"Are you looking for me?"
"When did you start practicing swordsmanship?"
"Huh?" Wang Lan’s face was a canvas of confusion.
"Don’t play dumb with me. I know it’s you!"
"No, I’m not!" Wang Lan denied with utmost seriousness.
"You..." Suddenly, Jiang Xinyu smiled sweetly, the metaphorical ice around her thawing. "Have you ever looked into who produces the Star Martial Competition?"
"No... It hasn’t been publicly announced, has it?"
"Although the Star Martial Competition production team hasn’t publicized it, it can still be found with a little effort. Jiangcheng Entertainment is a subsidiary of Jiang Technology. My family is one of the producers of the Star Martial Competition. So..."
"If you know, just keep it to yourself..." Wang Lan said, a hint of embarrassment in his voice.
"You still haven’t answered me: when did you learn swordsmanship?"
"I learned it while practicing martial arts..."
"You only had Master Huang as a teacher, but Huang Feilong doesn’t know the first thing about swordsmanship. I started training in swordsmanship at the age of six and, over ten years, have studied under five sword masters, all of whom have passed on their true teachings. Yet, after watching your battle video against Lan Die, I believe your level of swordsmanship is above mine."
"You flatter me!"
"You know I don’t flatter. Your swordsmanship is stronger than mine, and that’s a fact. I just want to know who you trained with and how."
"Are you looking to become an apprentice?"
"If there is a worthy master, I should indeed seek their tutelage."
"Actually, I just downloaded some videos online and practiced by following along... You know, I learn things very quickly. Studying the sword is actually quite simple—just understand its attack methods, how to apply techniques, and then gain insight into counters through actual combat..."
I’m running out of lies, what do I do?
Wang Lan’s voice grew quieter, his gaze becoming more evasive.
Jiang Xinyu sighed softly. "Never mind. If you don’t want to tell me, I won’t push. What are your thoughts?"
"About what?"
"About joining the Star Martial Competition. What made you do it?"
"To test what I’ve learned, and to spar with fellow martial artists!" Wang Lan said earnestly, as if reciting a line from a martial arts TV drama.
"Such a poser!" Stepping right in front of Wang Lan, Jiang Xinyu challenged, "Isn’t sparring with us good enough?"
"No!"New ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄhapters are published on NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet
"Why not? Do you think I’m too weak to be a worthy opponent?" Jiang Xinyu’s stubborn streak flared up. A wrong answer here could be perilous.
"It’s not that!" Wang Lan quickly denied, lowering his head slightly and gazing deeply into Jiang Xinyu’s eyes. "With you, I can’t bring myself to be harsh, nor can I bring myself to strike!"
Survival instinct +100
That single sentence struck Jiang Xinyu’s heart like a heavy hammer, making it pound forcefully like a drum.
Jiang Xinyu, somewhat flustered, looked down. "I see. How do you usually train? Why are you so outstanding? Whether it’s studying or practicing, you’re... so outstanding it’s almost demoralizing."
"You’ve been watching me for over two years; how could you not know how I study? As for training... have you ever heard of mediation?"
"Mediation? The Idea Sword Flow?"
"Mhm! Master Huang asked me that too. I told him that when I train, I visualize an opponent in my mind. He’s there in my head and right before my eyes. We continuously spar, and my abilities naturally improve."
"I’ve heard of the Idea Sword Flow mediation technique, but my master forbade me from practicing it. This method is indeed effective, but it has a drawback: there’s a chance it can create a second persona. If that second persona is merely sword intent, it’s manageable. But if it’s an evil persona that tries to consume the dominant one, then it’s disastrous. You’re forbidden from using it from now on."
"Alright, alright..."
"Be serious. Promise me you won’t use it anymore. Also, go to the hospital this Sunday."
"What for?"
"To check if you’ve developed a second persona."
"I feel fine; I know my own condition," Wang Lan quickly shook his head.
Are you kidding? My swordsmanship comes from allocating skill points, not some profound mediation. Without any actual mediation, there’s no way I’d develop a split personality!
"Everyone dragged to a psychiatric hospital insists they’re not sick. Don’t worry, you’ll go to my family’s medical center. I guarantee no one will find out, and it’s just a quick test. It won’t take much of your time."
Wang Lan wanted to argue, but under Jiang Xinyu’s unyielding gaze, he could only raise his hands in surrender. "Your humble servant obeys the decree!"
Logically, Wang Lan’s popularity should have started to wane after three days. However, there seemed to be an unseen force at play, causing the video of the pinnacle duel to gain even more traction online.
Even though Wang Lan had chosen to compete anonymously, if someone were truly determined to dig, they could still uncover his real identity. In fact, some bored, wealthy individuals online were offering a reward of a million to definitively identify Wang Lan.
However, thanks to further encryption personally overseen by Jiang Xinyu, Wang Lan’s registration information was now deeply buried. Unless Wang Lan revealed himself, not even the organizers’ database would contain his true details.
「Friday, eight o’clock at night.」
Wang Lan, wearing a mask, walked through the doors of the Suzhou City Satellite TV studio.
Here, the official recording of the Star Martial Competition would take place. How it was recorded and how the entertainment value was enhanced were the organizers’ concerns. For Wang Lan, it was simply about winning his matches and advancing to the next round.
By the time Wang Lan arrived, Hu Qing was already there. Wang Lan noticed that the other contestants were looking at him strangely today, their eyes holding a subtle, almost imperceptible hostility.
"What’s going on? Am I being targeted?" Wang Lan quietly asked Hu Qing.
"Have you any idea how popular your fight video has become? You’re a big star now..."
"It’s a bit popular, so what? Even if most of them are here for fame, they can’t just turn hostile out of jealousy, can they? Do Star Martial Warriors have so little magnanimity?"
"Of course, if it were just jealousy, it wouldn’t be this bad. But right now, in their eyes, you’re a golden stepping stone, a chance to soar to fame in a single bound. If anyone manages to defeat you in a match, they’ll use you to achieve instant success. So be careful. The opponents you face will likely come at you with everything they’ve got from the start. Even though many are here for fame, quite a few of them actually have some decent skills."
"They want to use me as a stepping stone? Perfect!" Wang Lan’s voice instantly dropped, becoming much deeper.
The competition soon began.
Wang Lan was third in the lineup, and Hu Qing was seventh.
While the two of them chatted quietly, the first match had already started. The two contestants on stage had very distinct characteristics: both were tank-type Star Martial Warriors. One was 1.98 meters tall, the other 2 meters tall.
Both of their Star Martial Skills were of the Body Mutation Type, a common category for Star Martial Warriors who typically served as a team’s initiator, tank, or assaulter.
Once their Star Martial Skills were activated, their bodies swelled, and their strength, speed, and defense increased significantly. It was similar to Wu Changfeng’s Steel Body, which was also a Body Mutation Type Star Martial Skill, though Wu Changfeng’s was far more advanced than what these two possessed.
The visceral thrill of flesh meeting flesh sent adrenaline surging through the audience. The two on stage resembled ancient behemoths locked in a life-or-death struggle.
Their moves weren’t flashy, and their Star Martial Skills lacked dazzling light and shadow effects. What mattered was the explosive sense of reality. A punch to the ground left a huge crater in the stage; a heavy blow made the ground shake violently.
When the two had nearly demolished the entire stage, one of them suddenly underwent a secondary transformation, growing another two sizes larger, and then proceeded to crush his opponent with absolute strength.
Finally, he grabbed his opponent’s ankle and slammed him repeatedly from side to side, splattering blood and sending dust billowing into the air.
The scene incited the live audience to scream incessantly; even the judges on the stage lost their composure, shouting wildly.
"Stop! Stop! Contestant Number One wins! Number One wins!"
The first match lasted a full twenty minutes. By that calculation, ten matches would take over two hundred minutes. An episode was at most an hour and a half long...
I wonder how much will be cut.
"For the third match, contestants Number Five and Number Six, please take your places—"
When the announcement sounded, Wang Lan, who was backstage, stood up. His opponent was a lean young man with a very non-mainstream look: his hair was spiked, his face bore camouflage paint, and he wore a nose ring.
"Contestant Number Five, Gan Lie, hails from Liaoning Province. He is in the late Star Shine Stage and previously served in the Northwest War Zone. After his discharge, he joined the largest Pioneer Legion in the northwest. Gan Lie is known as the ’Wind Chaser’ for his wind-like speed and punches that can break the sound barrier. His Wolf Tooth Steel Fist, capable of delivering seven punches per second, often defeats opponents before they even have time to react. According to those familiar with Gan Lie, his strongest Star Martial Skill isn’t his fists. What could it be? Let’s wait and see!
"As for Contestant Number Six, Wolf—let me correct something. Many online videos claim that Contestant Number Six’s name is XX. We cannot ascertain his real name. As he is competing anonymously, the organizers are obligated to protect Contestant Wolf’s privacy. He registered for our Star Martial Competition under the name Wolf. While the organizers cannot reveal Wolf’s past, his strength is evident to all. In the preliminaries, the ’Butterfly Dance’ Star Martial Skill that Wolf used at the end undoubtedly left a deep impression on everyone.
"Now, let’s welcome both contestants to the stage!"
Explosive music erupted, accompanied by cheers from the audience.
Heh... I feel like I’m at a boxing match,
Wang Lan mused.
"Mr. Xiaobao, what are your thoughts on this match?" the host asked, turning to the judges’ table.
The three Star Martial Art judges at the table looked serious. Bao Longqing, who had been addressed, leaned forward slightly. "Both contestants are very strong. Honestly, without seeing them fight, I can’t make a judgment. Wolf’s strength is plain to see, and Gan Lie’s record is also very impressive. Looking at their Star Martial Stages, Wolf seems to be at a slight disadvantage, but his Star Martial Skill is very powerful."
"I don’t quite agree with Mr. Xiaobao’s view," another middle-aged judge with a mustache, sitting next to Mr. Xiaobao, suddenly interjected.
A disagreement between two judges—this was a highlight for the show. Of course, it might have been deliberately arranged.
"Mr. Qin, what are your insights?"
"We need to analyze this objectively. Wolf’s strength is indeed formidable, as we saw in his preliminary match. But what was the real reason that match became so explosive? Was it purely his strength? If so, could he be stronger than a Star Cloud Stage Star Martial Warrior? There are many videos online of Star Cloud and Galaxy Stage Star Martial Warriors fighting. Why haven’t they gone viral, while the fight between two Star Shine Stage Star Martial Warriors did?"

chapters.title: Chapter 69 Vertical Flame Sword
chapters.content:
Chapter 69: Chapter 69 Vertical Flame Sword
"Mr. Qin means..." Bao Longqing furrowed his brows.
"Because it’s real, because it’s clear! Because this is some of the clearest and most genuine Star Martial Warrior battle footage in recent years. Because the two Star Martial Warriors engaged in the battle were both fighting with the intent to kill the other. I’m not saying they had the intention to murder; I’m describing the authenticity of that battle. So, contestant Wolf became famous overnight, but does this mean that contestant Wolf has the strength to back up his fame? Contestant Wolf is only at the mid-Star Shine stage. Although the Star Shine rank isn’t the absolute standard for measuring strength, it is the most important one."
"Does Mr. Qin mean that contestant Wolf might be at a disadvantage?"
"Correct," Mr. Qin said indifferently as he took a sip of water.
"Then let us wait and see."
"The thirty-third match of the official Star Martial Competition now begins!"
"Please guide me!" Gan Lie said solemnly, slightly cupping his fists.
Wang Lan had learned his lesson. Even though he bowed in return, his eyes remained fixed on Gan Lie’s every move. However, Gan Lie showed no intention of launching a sneak attack. Instead, he slowly tightened the bandages wrapped around his hands.
"Even though I don’t know who you are, your strength is indeed decent. I’m not one of those half-baked braggarts. I’ve been to the battlefield to fight Star Martial Warriors from other countries, and I’ve hunted in barbaric Different Dimensional Spaces. Your practical combat skills are very solid. You became famous in one battle during the preliminary competition, but don’t think you can live up to all that hype. You won because you haven’t met me! In this match, I’ll shatter your myth!"
"Stepping over me to ascend?"
"HUMPH!" As soon as he finished speaking, Gan Lie suddenly leaned forward and rushed at Wang Lan. In an instant, Gan Lie’s figure turned cyan, wind whirling around him, his body seemingly becoming lighter and more agile.
Wind-attribute?
Wang Lan took half a step back as an afterimage nearly grazed his face.
The speed was like that of a high-speed train whisking past one’s cheek.
The Wind attribute has two characteristics: one is terrifying cutting force, and the other is speed. Although not as fast as Thunder Attribute Star Martial Warriors, it still ranks second. Wind-attribute Star Martial Skills involve the dual application of form and attribute; using the Wind attribute to accelerate is an application of form variation.
"In the world of martial arts, nothing is truly indestructible; only speed is unbreakable! Before the velocity of wind, your Sword Qi will be meaningless!"
At that moment, Gan Lie’s body seemed to transform into a whirlwind. His face was the only human aspect visible at the front of the wind mass; the rest of his body appeared to merge into the wind. Suddenly, images of Gan Lie appeared everywhere on the stage.
On the three hundred-square-meter stage, Wang Lan danced in the center, leaving afterimages. Meanwhile, Gan Lie, like a ghostly shadow, appeared in every corner, and only the howling wind could be heard.
If the first match was a collision of muscles, then this third match was a showcase of speed. Wang Lan’s speed was already very fast; his movement technique had reached a level that made uninformed audience members exclaim in disbelief.
However, Wang Lan’s speed, while agile, was still far from true quickness.
So-called quickness completely overrides agility. Even if you see it, know it, and understand it, you are helpless and can only watch in despair as you are crushed by speed. That is true quickness—so quick you’d be left in the dust.
In the arena venue, more than a dozen cameras captured the action, creating highly engaging visuals.
Min Jian stood in the main control room, rapidly issuing commands for camera switches.
"Camera Seven, zoom in for a close-up."
"Camera Eight, tenfold slow-motion replay... no, twelvefold..."
"Camera Nine, bird’s-eye view! Beautiful!"
"The judges, what are the judges doing? Get a shot of the judges! Damn it! Judges, what are you doing? You’re not the audience; you’re seasoned teachers! How can you look so dumbfounded? Start commenting already!"
"COUGH, COUGH... Mr. Xiaobao, did you see that?"
"It’s truly unexpected. I thought contestant Wolf was already one of the strongest contestants in this year’s competition, but who would have thought that contestant Gan Lie’s strength would also be so astonishing."
"A contestant’s strength is relative to their opponent. For example, if a Galaxy Stage Star Martial Warrior is defeated in a single move by a Star Sea warrior, does that mean the Galaxy Stage Star Martial Warrior is weak? Not at all. Contestant Wolf became instantly famous due to his stunning performance in the preliminary competition, but if we look at it rationally, our Star Martial Competition is filled with hidden talents. I’ve always been optimistic about contestant Gan Lie, not only because his Star Martial rank is higher, but also because he has experienced so many brutal battlefields. This shows that contestant Gan Lie is also a battle-hardened warrior. With his rich experience and solid Basic Skills, plus the suppression from his Star Power level—even if contestant Wolf also possesses extensive experience and solid Basic Skills—he will find it difficult to bridge the gap in Star Power. Based on the current state of the battle, my judgment should be sound."
"But Mr. Qin, contestant Wolf’s performance is also very steady. Look, he’s dealing with contestant Gan Lie’s highly aggressive attacks in a calm and collected manner."
"Constant defense without any counterattacks will inevitably lead to defeat."
Wang Lan used Star Cloud Sword Dance to create a flurry of afterimages, effortlessly dodging each of Gan Lie’s Speedy Wind assaults. Although Wang Lan could not match Gan Lie’s speed, the afterimages he created misled Gan Lie into attacking false targets.
It might have seemed like Wang Lan was constantly dodging while Gan Lie increased the pace of his attacks, but so far, Gan Lie had not even touched the hem of Wang Lan’s clothing.
Wang Lan’s brow furrowed. This Gan Lie’s Basic Skills were indeed solid, but he relied too heavily on this one Star Martial Skill.
In Wang Lan’s mind, surely the same Star Martial Skill couldn’t be sustained for long? To Wang Lan, Gan Lie’s use of Speedy Wind seemed just like the Flaming Leopard King’s flame acceleration technique. However, the Flaming Leopard King’s version was several times more potent. Even so, when the Flaming Leopard King used such a move, Wang Lan had figured out how to counter it in less than a minute. Where did you get the confidence to think that with one move, you could remain unbeaten?
Wang Lan made up his mind, just as the commentary from the judges’ panel ceased.
"Kid, is dodging all you can do? Come on, use that Butterfly Passing Through Flowers Star Martial Skill from yesterday! Bring it on—" Gan Lie began to verbally taunt Wang Lan. As he spoke, his figure was enveloped by a whirlwind, his body rapidly spinning into a horrifying wind-drill as he charged straight at Wang Lan.
This time, however, Wang Lan stood rooted to his spot, unmoving.
"What’s contestant Wolf trying to do?"
"Get the first aid ready—"
Even Min Jian, watching from backstage and tapping his fingers, suddenly froze mid-tap. He worked in show business; dramatic scenes were fine for the program, but on-screen deaths were an absolute taboo.
Simultaneously, Wang Lan suddenly crossed his hands, and two Flame Swords burst from his palms. The Flame Swords crossed like scissors. Instantly, a vertical blade of fire appeared with Wang Lan, and between his palms, the flames morphed into a massive chainsaw.
This scene made everyone gasp.
Fire counters wind; even a primary school student knows about the restraining relationships between Star Martial Attributes.
So when Wang Lan suddenly utilized a Fire-attribute Star Martial Skill, the stands erupted.
"Damn, how did I not realize Wolf was a Fire-attribute Star Martial Warrior?"
"Don’t say you didn’t realize it; the three judges on stage didn’t realize it either."
"Listen to all the long-winded theories Mr. Qin has been spouting—from Star Martial ranks to Basic Skills to Gan Lie’s combat experience and so on. He analyzed and compared everything, yet damn it, he didn’t consider that Wolf might be a Fire-attribute Star Martial Warrior."
Compared to the audience’s reaction, Gan Lie’s was even more spectacular.
With a ferocious expression and a cruel, sinister smile, accompanied by the shrill howl of the wind, he savagely hurtled towards Wang Lan.
But the moment the Flame Sword ignited, Gan Lie’s expression froze, a look of dumbstruck bewilderment laced with disbelief.
And when the howling drill was effortlessly bisected by the Flame Sword, his face showed deep despair and intense fear.
But he couldn’t stop himself now.
The moment Wang Lan had paused, Gan Lie had already committed to a last-ditch effort.
After nearly three minutes of using Speedy Wind, his Star Power was almost depleted. If he missed this chance to settle the fight, he was destined to lose. Therefore, Gan Lie had resolutely taken action.
But why, just why, was Wang Lan so coincidentally a Fire-attribute Star Martial Warrior? You’re Fire-attribute, so why the hell didn’t you show it earlier? You fought three rounds in the preliminaries and faced Wind-attribute Star Martial Warriors too, right? Why didn’t you use this move back then? If I hadn’t seen that match where you split the wind blade with your Sword Qi and knocked out your opponent with a punch, how could I have ever thought your Star Martial Skill was the Star Cloud Sword Dance? You...
If Wang Lan knew Gan Lie’s thoughts at that moment, he might only be able to spread his hands and think,
Blame me, it’s all my fault!
But there were no ’what-ifs.’ Gan Lie, having made his gamble, could not turn back. He couldn’t even stop his momentum, let alone turn back.
With such high-speed inertia, imagine colliding head-on with Wang Lan’s Flame Sword.
It would be like a live pork-cutting demonstration at the Meat Union Factory—a single, clean slice!
So when this scene flashed by, everyone in the audience instinctively closed their eyes.
And in that split second, Wang Lan suddenly withdrew his blade.
The Flame Sword vanished, replaced by Wang Lan’s tightly clenched fist.
BANG!
Gan Lie’s entire face slammed squarely into Wang Lan’s fist. Wang Lan even felt the crisp snap of a nasal bone shattering.
THUD!
Gan Lie crashed heavily to the ground, his body convulsing violently as if electrocuted.
Deathly silence. The arena was utterly silent.
"Damn it, I closed my eyes just now..."
"Me too, I didn’t see it. What happened?"
"Replay! We strongly demand a replay!"
"I... I saw it..." a young man wearing glasses said hoarsely, his face filled with a mixture of shock and regret.
"What did you see?"
"Quick, tell us! How exactly did Gan Lie lose?"
"Wolf put away his Flame Sword, then just extended his fist. Gan Lie ran head-first into Wolf’s fist and then collapsed."
PFFT!
HAHAHA...
"The thirty-third match victor is contestant Wolf! Contestant Wolf has successfully advanced to the top fifty!" The referee’s announcement suddenly rang out.
"First round of the official competition completed. Advancing to the next round. Reward: 2,000 experience points, 100 skill points."
Wang Lan turned and walked away, his footsteps slightly hesitant.
He hesitated for a moment, wondering if he should heal Gan Lie. But he instantly dismissed the impulse. The Medical Star Martial Technique was one of his trump cards, and there was no need to expose it unless absolutely necessary.

chapters.title: Chapter 70: The Crowd Goes Wild
chapters.content:
Chapter 70: Chapter 70: The Crowd Goes Wild
Advancing to the second round, the remaining matches were of little concern to Wang Lan. With two more days left in the first round, he remained indifferent, attending school regularly and punctually.
「Before he knew it, the weekend had arrived.」
Although he had crammed for two rounds of Star Martial Art classes and not only caught up with his classmates but also ranked among the top, human nature is such that there’s always that slight dissatisfaction; one isn’t content unless they are vastly superior. This left Wang Lan feeling that life wasn’t quite perfect.Nᴇw ɴovel chaptᴇrs are published on NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
That’s why, despite having complained countless times before,
Who the heck would study so hard if not to unlock the system?
, even without the system’s impetus, Wang Lan still led a fulfilling life.
He read books and solved problems; when the school didn’t provide enough, he bought more practice sets. Although the theoretical knowledge of Star Martial Warriors wasn’t as vast as scientific subjects, its volume was still considerable. One topic in particular—the theoretical application and development of Star Power—had Wang Lan utterly engrossed, unable to extricate himself.
As Wang Lan immersed himself in the ocean of knowledge, the prime-time Star Martial Overlord Competition was being broadcast at 8 p.m.
The announcer’s voice boomed from the television, "The third season of the Star Martial Overlord Competition, third episode, officially begins!"
"This program is sponsored by Jiangcheng Entertainment! This program is sponsored by Roland Home Textiles..."
A comment flashed across the screen: "He’s about to appear... Let the bullet comments fly!"
At this moment, a pre-match segment played, showcasing the conflicting opinions of Mr. Xiaobao and Mr. Qin through clever editing.
Mr. Xiaobao scoffed, "This Qin Xian doesn’t know a thing about Star Martial Warriors! He’s not even a Star Martial Warrior himself, just some amateur pundit."
Mr. Qin countered, "I don’t think so. Wolf has gone viral, exploding in popularity online, but an internet celebrity is still just an internet celebrity. Is his strength really as formidable as it’s hyped up to be?"
More comments scrolled by:
"Rational netizen here. Mr. Qin’s analysis makes sense!"
"Wolf has strength, sure, but he’s definitely not top-tier. That Gan Lie, on the other hand, is the Wolf of the Northwest! His experience is vast; he’s practically a special forces operative among Star Martial Warriors."
"Neither has a realm advantage, and their combat skills and experience aren’t drastically different. It’s likely going to be a fierce battle."
Amidst the heated debate in the bullet comments, the match began. Right from the start, Gan Lie unleashed a killing move. As his Wind-attribute Star Martial Skills flared, the screen filled with multiple images of him.
Watching it live would undoubtedly cause motion sickness, but the program benefited from post-production. Amateurs saw an exciting spectacle; experts appreciated the technical skill. In terms of production, Min Jian’s grasp of pacing and visual composition was undeniably at the industry’s peak.
The dazzling combat visuals, combined with shifting camera angles and slow-motion analysis, allowed viewers to effortlessly follow the fighters’ conditions and understand their movements.
From this standpoint alone, the third episode was undoubtedly the best of the Star Martial Overlord Competition so far.
In the slow-motion replays, Gan Lie attacked relentlessly. Wang Lan could only use his Star Martial Skills to dodge and parry Gan Lie’s onslaught within the arena. Gan Lie’s punches and kicks, though unflashy, possessed a thrilling, fast-paced rhythm.
For a moment, the stream of bullet comments dwindled.
"Awesome! Exciting!"
"Wolf’s finally showing his true colors! His strength was overhyped. Against a truly strong opponent, he’s clearly outmatched."
"I bet Wolf goes down within a minute! If not, I’ll livestream myself eating..."
"Eating what?"
"Durian!"
"Wolf’s done for..."
"Tsk, all that hype for nothing. Unsubscribing. Fan to hater."
"Did the commenter above forget Wolf used this exact same tactic in his famous debut battle?"
"Yeah! I got a sense of déjà vu right from the start. How can so many clueless netizens not see it? It’s Wolf’s classic ’I’ll let you go first for five minutes’ routine!"
"
Let him be strong; the gentle breeze skims the mountaintop!
Wolf just waits for his opponent to tire out, then launches a decisive counterattack. I can practically see the ending already."
"Exactly! It’s like that legendary boast: ’Let your opponent run thirty meters first; my forty-meter saber can afford to wait!’"
That was the beauty of online streaming platforms. Even if you were watching alone in your room, you were never truly alone.
Millions of netizens were there, watching and commenting right alongside you.
Fingers flew across keyboards, and the bullet comments blotted out the screen. In the comment section, discussion threads surged like the unceasing flow of the Yangtze River.
「Five minutes later」
Gan Lie’s Star Power was reaching its limit. Having attacked relentlessly without success, he lost his composure and, in a desperate gamble, launched the Wolf Teeth Tornado Drill.
Suddenly, the flood of bullet comments vanished as the scrolling text froze.
Whether watching on computers, phones, or televisions, all viewers collectively held their breath, their eyes wide and unblinking, fixed on the screen.
In that instant, eighty percent of viewers had toggled off the bullet comment display.
On screen, Wang Lan’s back was to the camera. Then, in an instant, the perspective shifted to a close-up on him.
Wang Lan stood firmly in a wide horse stance, his hands crossed before him. Red flames suddenly erupted from his palms, intertwining and then parting like a pair of scissors. A vertical Flame Sword instantly materialized in front of him.
At this sight, everyone’s scalp tingled.
Fuck! After all the speculation, who the hell would have guessed Wang Lan was a Fire-type Star Martial Warrior? Even among Fire-types, people usually saw fireballs, flame jets, or spreading ground fire. Nobody had ever seen a vertical Flame Sword like this!
The scene replayed in thirty-times slow motion. Gan Lie’s desperate attack, the Wolf Teeth Tornado Drill, slammed directly into the vertical Flame Sword—which perfectly countered his technique. The drill was effortlessly sliced open by the Flame Sword, exposing Gan Lie within, his expression rapidly transforming.
From ferocious and cold, to startled, then in an instant to disbelief, followed by fear, and finally, despair. Only a master actor could convey such a rapid cascade of emotions in so short a time.
The camera cut to the live audience. Many turned their faces away, unwilling to watch, while others covered their eyes, gasping in shock.
Min Jian’s ability to stir the audience’s emotions had reached its zenith. This particular cut caused the viewers’ excitement to skyrocket, as if hitting a second stage booster, their heartbeats accelerating wildly.
After three seconds, the view switched back. Just as Gan Lie was about to crash into the razor-sharp Flame Sword, Wang Lan suddenly retracted it. Then, with a leisurely and relaxed air, he simply extended his fist.
THWACK—
All the viewers exhaled in unison, as if a massive weight had been lifted from their shoulders.
Gan Lie hadn’t been sliced in two.
Then, the slow-motion replay showed Gan Lie’s entire face smashing violently into Wang Lan’s fist. The sight made everyone who saw it burst out laughing, or nearly spit out their drinks.
"Damn it! My brand new Weilong phone!"
"You only dropped a phone? I just spilled half a bottle of water on my Great Wall computer! That’s a 12,000-yuan Great Wall Ninth Generation!"
"Hahaha..."
"I know it’s mean to laugh right now, but why can’t I stop myself?"
"Student Gan Lie, I’d like to conduct a special interview: what did it feel like to take that punch to the face? Don’t worry, we’re professionally trained. We usually don’t laugh... unless we absolutely can’t help it. Hahaha!"
"Last semester, I was chasing a bus on my e-bike. The bus slammed on its brakes, and my face smacked right into its side. It was flattened like a pancake! It hurt so much I couldn’t talk for a week. Seriously, don’t laugh, it was agonizing!"
"Hey, commenter above, let me interview you instead!"
"Yeah, ’student from upstairs,’ please share your story!"
After the climax of Wang Lan’s match, the subsequent fights seemed dull by comparison. Although viewership numbers didn’t drop, the intensity of online discussion fell by fifty percent.
By the end of the show, the first batch of reaction memes, fresh off the digital press, began to flood the comment section.
A meme of Gan Lie: "All you do is dodge? If you’re a man, let’s fight for real!"
A meme of Wang Lan: "Behold my Vertical Flame Sword."
A meme of Gan Lie recoiling: "Nope, can’t mess with that. I’m outta here!"
The night was quiet, her room illuminated as if by daylight. Jiang Xinyu silently finished watching the latest episode of the Star Martial Overlord Competition, then replayed Wang Lan’s match from beginning to end one more time.
After hesitating for a long while, Jiang Xinyu opened QQ.
A notification popped up on Wang Lan’s computer: "Wang Lan, you have a new message from Jiang Xinyu."
"Hm?" Wang Lan looked up from his book and clicked on the flashing QQ icon.
Jiang Xinyu: "Where did you learn that Star Martial Skill?"
Wang Lan: "Which one?"
Jiang Xinyu: "The Flame Sword!"
Wang Lan: "That... I learned it from an uncle. It’s not convenient for me to disclose his identity. I also didn’t expect so many ’uncles’ and ’elders’ to suddenly appear after I awakened as a Star Martial Warrior."
Jiang Xinyu’s fine brows furrowed slightly. After thinking for a long moment, she quickly typed, "Let’s have a sparring match another day."
Wang Lan: "No way!"
Seeing the decisive rejection pop up, Jiang Xinyu’s eyelid twitched. "Why not?"
Wang Lan: "You’re a Star Cloud Stage practitioner bullying me, a mere Star Shine Stage. Have some dignity!"
Jiang Xinyu: "I’ve learned a new Star Martial Skill and need real combat practice to master it."
Wang Lan: "A pre-packaged Grade A Star Martial Skill?"
Jiang Xinyu: "Yes!"
Wang Lan: "Then that’s even more of a reason to say no!" he refused without hesitation. "I’m afraid I’ll be dead and gone before you even get the hang of it. Don’t mess around. Wait until we go to the training field next time to practice."
Jiang Xinyu: "Fine..."
Closing the chat window, Jiang Xinyu gritted her teeth.
That blockhead!
"Sis..." Jiang Xincheng had appeared behind Jiang Xinyu at some point. "Knowing Lan, he’d never guess at your complicated feelings."
"What complicated feelings?" Jiang Xinyu asked, her expression blank.
"You saw Lan showing more and more strength, and deep down, you were thrilled. Your internal monologue was probably something like,
That’s the man I’ve set my sights on!
So you couldn’t wait to share that sense of pride with him.
"Unfortunately, Lan is a hopelessly dense guy. He wouldn’t realize that a small thing like asking for a sparring partner could easily wait until school tomorrow. A girl contacting a boy this late at night... even a complete idiot would think of other possibilities.
"So, Sis, your strategy was flawed. If you don’t spell it out for him, Lan will probably die alone, still clueless."
"Die alone?" Jiang Xinyu’s eyebrow twitched.
"Yeah. Lan earned his single status through his own sheer ’talent’ for cluelessness, and by that same ’talent,’ he’ll likely die alone."
"Xincheng, you’re only fourteen," Jiang Xinyu said.
"But girls mature faster than boys, don’t they? In ancient times, fourteen-year-old girls were already mothers."
"What I mean is, you seem to have a lot of free time lately to be thinking about such things. Wang Lan awakened his Star Martial Art talent at the same time as you. He’s already at the mid-Star Shine Stage, while you’re still at the Starlight Stage. It took him just over a month to catch up to most geniuses. Don’t you think you should be working harder?"
"I know, I promise I’ll work hard tomorrow."
"Tomorrow is too far away. Seize the present," Jiang Xinyu said, shutting down her computer and standing up. "Come with me."
"Sis, are you trying to kill me? It’s ten o’clock already! I have school tomorrow!"
"For the past two years, I haven’t gone to bed before midnight."
"But I’ve already showered..."
"You can shower again; we can afford the water. No more excuses. Follow me to the Training Room!"
Xincheng grumbled under his breath, "Hmph! Just because you’re upset, you take it out on me. If you’ve got the guts, go bother Lan!"
"What did you say?" Jiang Xinyu’s voice was dangerously soft.
"Nothing! I’m coming right now!" Xincheng shivered, shook his head quickly, and reluctantly got up to change his clothes.

chapters.title: Chapter 71: The Poisonous Scorpion Beauty
chapters.content:
Chapter 71: Chapter 71: The Poisonous Scorpion Beauty
Wang Lan was famous, yet he wasn’t.
At least, for the past few days, on his way to and from school, the name Lu Sheng heard most often was Wolf.
Since Wolf was competing anonymously, everything about him was a mystery. This obscurity only further ignited the public’s desire to gossip about Wang Lan.
What was Wolf’s real identity? What did Wolf look like? Did he have buck teeth? A face full of pimples? Or perhaps large lips?
Regardless, wherever Wang Lan went, he could hear people discussing him.
This had... absolutely no impact on Wang Lan’s life.
Wolf is blowing up online? What does that have to do with me, Wang Lan?
That was his stance.
He ate when he should, drank when he should, bragged and jested with Xu Xiangwen and the others as usual. If a female classmate needed her hormonal balance adjusted, he adjusted it. In short, he was as composed as ever, steady as a rock.
Unknowingly, another week passed.
Friday night at nine, Wang Lan arrived at Suzhou City TV station, almost perfectly on time.
The second round was to narrow fifty contestants down to twenty-five, with a total of twenty-five matches spread over three days. Wang Lan was assigned to the third day, and specifically the seventh match, so arriving at the TV station by nine gave him plenty of time.
Just as he walked into the TV station, he found the entrance blocked by a large crowd; some girls even held glowing signs with "Wolf" written on them.
Is this... fans showing their support?
Wang Lan hesitated for a moment, a sudden flicker of fear appearing.
"Wolf—Wolf—"
"Wolf hasn’t arrived yet! Please maintain order, everyone. You’re blocking the entrance and disrupting our work. Please disperse. This isn’t an open-air concert..."
"Young man, we don’t mean any harm. We just want to see the real Wolf."
"Yeah, we just want to see if Wolf is real or not. If possible, I want to take him home!"
When girls got suggestive, even the old hands were impressed.
Wang Lan sighed, quietly tucked himself into a dark corner, and scanned the area but found no side doors.
Taking a mask from his backpack, he steeled himself and put it on.
"Wow—Wolf is here!"
"Sisters, let’s go—"
"No matter what, I have to snatch off his mask and see! I’m dying of curiosity!"
"Big sis, that’s what you really think, isn’t it?"
