Facing the surging crowd of hundreds, Wang Lan’s figure suddenly twisted, becoming almost fluid, like a gentle breeze passing silently through the center of the throng.
In the blink of an eye, Wang Lan reached the entrance of the TV station. The rushing, fanatical fans only saw a blur before Wolf disappeared. Turning around abruptly, they then spotted Wang Lan standing under the bright lights of the TV station’s main door.
"This is my competition pass."
"Okay, Mr. Wolf, please come in."
Wang Lan turned back to wave at the distant fans, then spun around and vanished without a trace.
"That fleeting glance... it’s captivated me for so long..."
"So dashing, so gentle... Brother Wolf must be a kind and handsome man..."
"Fangirl!"
"Fangirl +1!"
Different worlds came with different cultural values. In this world, so similar to his previous one, middle and high schools were never short of these young fans.
Their fandom wasn’t always genuine affection; sometimes, they just joined the hype because everyone else did.
In this world’s setting, Star Martial Warriors held an extremely high status. If Star Martial Warriors chose to debut en masse, internet celebrities would have long been obsolete.
But many powerful Star Martial Warriors kept their identities secret. Thus, Star Martial Warriors and celebrities were like parallel lines that rarely intersected. So, when a popular and strong Star Martial Warrior like Wolf appeared, the young fans’ excitement was instantly ignited.
Behaviors that mature adults might deem foolish, these young fans performed without a second thought, justifying it with the romantic notion of youthful recklessness. The act of gathering at the TV station to mob someone received an overwhelming response.
The secrecy around Wang Lan’s identity was precisely the kind of mystique these young fans adored. Countless imagined backgrounds were meticulously crafted in their minds.
Noble scions, heirs to financial conglomerates, descendants of royalty, and so on...
Couldn’t see his face behind the mask? Couldn’t they just imagine it? A pretty boy, a stylish man, a shy older brother type? They could picture him however they pleased.
Ah, I can’t take it anymore, I can barely hold it in!
The excited young fans gathered, engaging in a kind of mass self-hypnosis, creating a veritable army that swept through major forums and live-streaming platforms.
When Wang Lan reached the backstage preparation room, the matches had already begun.
Inside the preparation room, the fourteen contestants who had advanced to the second round looked at Wang Lan with even sharper gazes. Compared to the previous round, however, there was far less scorn.
Previously, Wang Lan had risen to fame suddenly, achieving the goal most of them had for entering the competition—recognition—before even participating in an official match. Most were indignant, righteously thinking,
It’s because you didn’t meet me in the preliminaries.
But now, all the contestants had set aside their disdain. Anyone who could make it into the top fifty out of eight hundred registered participants was no weakling.
"Wolf, you’re here," Hu Qing greeted enthusiastically.
"You haven’t gone on stage yet, have you?"
"Not that fast!"
"Brother Wolf, could you give me an autograph?" a cloyingly sweet voice cooed from behind. A chill ran down Wang Lan’s spine, and he turned around warily.
The woman’s face was caked with thick makeup, obscuring her true features, though she didn’t look very old. She wore a form-fitting, one-piece leather suit.
What made Wang Lan cautious was that this woman had managed to sneak up behind him without him noticing at all.
The beauty held a colored photo, a snapshot of herself from the preliminaries.
"Brother Wolf, I really like you. Please go easy on me later," she said.
"Are you my opponent?" Wang Lan still didn’t know who he was up against in this match, as he hadn’t been there for the draw. Signing quickly, he returned the photo to her, calm and composed.
The woman sashayed away. Wang Lan vaguely heard Hu Qing gulp beside him.
"Brother Hu, captivated?"
"Forget it. Is a woman like that someone a guy like me can even dream of? Looking is enough," Hu Qing said, not trying to hide his feelings, instead laughing openly.
"You’d best not even look. The more you look, the more dangerous she becomes," Wang Lan said with a light chuckle.
"What’s wrong?"
"That woman is devious. She put poison on the pen she gave me."
The moment Wang Lan grasped the pen, his Healing Star Martial Arts involuntarily activated. This reaction only occurred when Wang Lan was injured. Therefore, there was only one explanation: something was wrong with the pen.
A woman who would resort to such tactics would stop at nothing to achieve her goals.
"So you... you were poisoned?" Hu Qing asked, his voice low and nervous.
"She *thinks* I was."
"Heh... looks like things are about to get interesting."
There were only eight matches for each session of the second round, so time wasn’t as tight. It was unclear whether the contestants’ abilities had genuinely improved or if the program had deliberately designed it for entertainment. Regardless, the battles so far had been much more exciting than those in the first round.
At least to Wang Lan’s eyes, there were fewer unnecessary movements, and the thrilling sensation of dancing on a knife’s edge was more pronounced.
"Contestant number six, Hu Qing, and contestant number thirteen, Ye Hua, please prepare."
After the preliminaries and the initial official matches, only fifty contestants remained. These fifty contestants were all in the mid to late Star Shine Stage. Based on the strength displayed, the only one truly worth Wang Lan’s attention was Hu Qing.
Frankly, Hu Qing had yet to use any actual Star Martial Skills.
But deep down, Wang Lan didn’t believe for a second that Hu Qing lacked them.
To have fought his way into the top fifty using only Basic Skills and Star Power manipulation, Hu Qing’s strength was formidable. His Moonstep was especially notable; a single step could instantly cover a distance of ten paces. Once he closed in, his opponents faced a relentless barrage of palm-edge strikes.
Against Hu Qing’s sharp attacks, I don’t have an effective defense.
Other Star Martial Warriors relied on explosive Star Martial Skills to win, whereas Hu Qing had so far overcome every obstacle relying solely on Basic Skills.
While Wang Lan was lost in thought, Hu Qing indeed demonstrated his prowess. He seized a fleeting opportunity with his solid fundamentals, nimble movement technique, and battlefield control, dispatching his opponent in a single, decisive wave of attacks.ɪꜰ ʏᴏᴜ ᴡᴀɴᴛ ᴛᴏ ʀᴇᴀᴅ ᴍᴏʀᴇ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs, ᴘʟᴇᴀsᴇ ᴠɪsɪᴛ NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
"Truly deserving of the name ’One Wave Hu Qing’! Always the same strategy: seize the opportunity for a decisive counterattack, giving his opponent no chance to breathe. Once Hu Qing finds a flaw, victory is sealed."
Next was the judges’ commentary segment, followed by the host’s Q&A session.
"Next match, contestant number seven versus contestant number fourteen!"
「After three more matches, it was finally Wang Lan’s turn to take the stage.」
The treatment for popular contestants and ordinary ones was indeed different. Even Wang Lan’s entrance music was distinct. As he walked out, screams erupted from the audience.
But this was immediately followed by an even more intense wave of shrieks. The sexy woman opposite him, An Wei, sauntered forward with seductive, cat-like steps. Her tight leather suit, with a zipper that couldn’t quite reach her neck, made many in the audience howl like hungry wolves.
In the eyes of the spectators, An Wei was all curves. In the brief ten seconds it took her to walk to the ring, several minor "tragedies" had already occurred in the stands. The men who had brought their girlfriends to the live event felt a sharp pang in their hearts.
"Brother Wolf... you have to go easy on me, okay?" An Wei said, winking at Wang Lan. It felt like a tangible jolt of electricity shot straight into his mind.
The moment the referee announced the start of the match, An Wei’s figure instantly split into more than a dozen clones, surrounding Wang Lan.
"A clone talent? That’s a rather rare Star Martial Talent! It’s used to confuse and bait opponents, suitable for battlefield reconnaissance and close-quarters combat. It remains to be seen whether contestant An Wei’s clones are Physical Clones or Ethereal Clones."
The clone Star Martial Talent was a strong Yang Attribute talent. However, within clone talents, there was a distinction: Physical Clones had limitless potential, while Ethereal Clones had limited room for growth.
The dozen An Weis quickly circled Wang Lan, searching for an opening. Although they moved swiftly, their steps were utterly silent. Not only was there no sound, but there was also no sense of vibration.
But at this moment, Wang Lan smiled.
As the woman ran, the powder she had applied to her body fluttered off. This powder, when mixed with the poison she had previously used on Wang Lan, would create a paralyzing toxin. If Wang Lan weren’t a Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior, he would have fallen for her trick. Using poison was one of the Star Martial Warrior skills officially permitted; the sole exception was using poison before a match.
However, An Wei’s method of using poison was undetectable beforehand. Who knew how many people she had tricked this way?
You made it into the top fifty with just Ethereal Clones and such weak combat ability? So, you won by relying on your... generous assets, huh?
An Wei, thinking
The poison is taking effect!
, licked her lips seductively. Suddenly, more than a dozen figures lunged at Wang Lan from all directions.
A flash of triumph crossed An Wei’s eyes.
Thank you for being so popular. The higher your popularity, the higher my starting point when I use you as a stepping stone. Wolf? Hah!
That "Hah!" however, never fully formed.
Suddenly, An Wei felt her vision blur, and then she lost sight of Wang Lan. By the time she perceived him again, Wang Lan had already closed in, maneuvering beneath her attack to get extremely close—
BOOM—BOOM BOOM BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 72: Breaking Through in Excitement
chapters.content:
Chapter 72: Chapter 72: Breaking Through in Excitement
Eight punches a second was an outstanding punch speed among Star Martial Warriors. Hu Qing, with his rapid hand-chop speed of ten times a second, was unbeatable on the Star Martial Competition’s field.
At least until now, among the many participants in the Star Martial Competition, Hu Qing had the fastest hand speed, with others at best managing about eight punches a second.
Wang Lan’s display of such rapid punch speed did not surprise the audience much. Perhaps their expectations of Wang Lan were too high, as they wouldn’t be amazed no matter how much more ability he demonstrated.
However, when Wang Lan instantly knocked An Wei off the stage and sent her flying towards the stands with such a ruthless move against a lady, it indeed plunged the venue into a deathly silence.
But soon, An Wei quickly got up from where she landed. She looked up at Wang Lan, who was facing her on the stage, a flash of embarrassment and annoyance in her eyes, snorted coldly, and turned to leave.
"It seems... though Wolf appeared to strike very hard, he was actually using controlled force. His goal was just to knock An Wei off the stage," the host quickly said, lightening the atmosphere and breaking the silence.
"Good—"
"So manly—"
In the stands, the audience, understanding everything, cheered enthusiastically. Although this battle was not as intense and exciting as the previous one, could they blame Wang Lan?
He didn’t want the opponent to be too weak, after all.
"Successfully advanced to the third round. Reward: 2,000 experience points and 150 skill points."
Backstage, Hu Qing came up to him. "Congratulations!"
"You’ve finished your matches, haven’t you? Why haven’t you left?"
"The next round is from twenty-five down to thirteen, so we have to draw lots in advance. There will also be one bye slot."
"So, I can’t leave before tonight ends?"
"Just wait. There’s only one match left."
The match ended half an hour later. Following the host’s emotive speech, the entire audience sent off the contestants eliminated in the round of fifty to twenty-five with warm applause.
"Next up is the drawing for the third round, which will narrow the field from twenty-five contestants down to thirteen. The organizers have stipulated that every contestant who successfully enters the fourth round—the top thirteen—will be awarded a cash prize of 100,000 yuan each. This is the organizers’ recognition of the contestants’ strength and an encouragement for their exciting performances. However, before the drawing for the matches to go from twenty-five to thirteen, a lucky contestant who will receive a bye will be drawn. This contestant will advance to the top thirteen competition without a fight and will also easily receive the 100,000 yuan cash prize from the organizers. Who will this lucky contestant be? Please look at the big screen!"
The photos of the contestants flashed quickly across the big screen.
"Stop!"
The big screen froze. The image of Wang Lan, wearing a mask, appeared in the center.
"Wow—"
"Wolf! Wolf—"
"It’s contestant Wolf! Congratulations to contestant Wolf for directly advancing to the top thirteen with a bye!"
Wang Lan himself was stunned. During the draw, he really hadn’t expected the bye to be his. But it just confirmed the saying: "Good things come when you least expect them." Some people buy lottery tickets every day without winning, while others buy a ticket just to get change and end up winning a big prize.
This world, isn’t it annoying?
"Successfully advanced to the fourth round of the Star Martial Competition. Reward: 3,000 experience points and 200 skill points."
After the contestant with the bye was decided, the system suddenly displayed another prompt. The moment the prompt appeared, a warm current flowed through Wang Lan’s entire body. It was as if he were basking in an ocean of Star Power; Star Power surged through his limbs and every fiber of his being.
At this moment, the big screen was giving Wang Lan a close-up. At the same time, his body suddenly radiated intense Star Energy Fluctuations.
If it weren’t for Wang Lan’s restraint, he would have inadvertently opened his Star Palace.
But! Is that the point?
Backstage, all twenty-five contestants—including those participating today and the victors from previous rounds—were gathered.
Could the surge of Star Power around Wang Lan escape their eyes? Such a familiar scene of Star Energy Fluctuation—a live breakthrough!
At that moment, everyone realized Wang Lan’s true Star Power level.
It wasn’t the late stage as speculated, nor was it the mid-stage as officially announced. Damn it, he was actually in the early stage? The early Star Shine Stage? Only now has he broken through to the mid-Star Shine Stage.
Wang Lan quickly immersed himself in his Spiritual Sea of Consciousness to check the system. "Character: Wang Lan! Level: Star Shine 4. Experience: 300/50,000."
In my mind, Star Shine 4 should still be considered an early stage, right? After all, I’m not even at the midpoint yet. But do regular Star Martial Warriors have such clear and detailed distinctions? Early, mid, and late stages are just vague judgments based on how far one is from the next breakthrough.
Exiting his Spiritual Sea of Consciousness, Wang Lan looked up.
The world was so quiet. Everyone around him was staring, their eyes wide as if they were wooden carvings.
"Uh? Did it freeze?" Wang Lan asked, a hint of mischief in his voice.
"Hahaha..." In the spectator stands, upon hearing Wang Lan’s disarmingly innocent remark, the audience burst into laughter.
"Uh, Wolf, did you... make a breakthrough?" Hu Qing asked, stuttering slightly.
"Ah? No, not really. A breakthrough isn’t that easy. It was just a minor gain."
"Brother Wolf, you can’t just lie like that to our faces!" a burly man pointed at Wang Lan, his face a mask of aggrieved indignation. "You clearly just broke through from the early Star Shine Stage to the mid-Star Shine Stage!"
"Yeah, that Star Energy Fluctuation doesn’t lie. We always thought Brother Wolf’s Star Power level was in the late Star Shine Stage, and that the official announcement of mid-stage was a deliberate attempt to hide your true strength."
"But... we were still wrong. The officials did indeed hide your strength, but we never expected you to actually be at the early Star Shine Stage."
"You only broke through to the mid-Star Shine Stage now, yet you’ve already defeated three opponents at the late Star Shine Stage. Brother Wolf, you don’t need to be so modest! A breakthrough is a breakthrough; what’s there to deny?"
"Cough, cough, cough..." Wang Lan recoiled slightly. "Everyone, I’m really not being modest. An improvement within the Star Shine Stage... does that even count as a breakthrough?
I always thought a ’breakthrough’ meant advancing an entire Star Power rank.
"
Backstage, silence fell once again.
Everyone looked at Wang Lan with a mixture of disbelief and astonishment.
Suddenly, a large hand clapped down on Wang Lan’s shoulder. It belonged to a two-meter-tall, powerfully built man who looked as if he were forged from steel.
Wang Lan tensed up instantly. "Zhu, what... what can I do for you?"
"Brother Wolf, do you have any idea how many Star Martial Warriors in the Star Martial Warrior world get beaten to death each year for showing off? At least five hundred! They were just too full of themselves, completely disregarding whether others could take it or not. Now... I really want to hit you. But if you tell me how you managed to break through under these circumstances, I’ll let you off. How about that?"
"Yeah! Otherwise, I’ll get the organizers to change the rules, and in the next match, we’ll all gang up on you!"
"Exactly! Exactly!"
Everything happening backstage was being broadcast live, without omission, to the audience out front. The five hundred spectators in their seats immediately showed knowing smiles, watching with great interest.
To ordinary people, Star Martial Warriors were mysterious, mighty, and serious figures. Most of their exposure to Star Martial Warriors came from movies and the internet. Even if there were Star Martial Warriors around them in real life, ordinary people couldn’t understand their lives or how they interacted with each other.
Now, seeing Star Martial Warriors interact just like ordinary people—joking around, playing pranks, teasing each other, and making sarcastic remarks—the warriors backstage underwent a true transformation in the audience’s eyes.
They are also human, ordinary folks just like us,
the audience thought.
Not solemn ascetics who are meticulous to a fault. Not brutal savages who resort to violence at the slightest provocation.
They also crack jokes, brag and show off, and engage in heated meme battles. Maybe that keyboard warrior you argued with online for three thousand rounds is actually a famous Star Martial Warrior you know of.
"Should I... really tell them?" Wang Lan hesitated. But at his words, everyone’s eyes brightened.
Could there actually be a way?
they wondered.
They were only joking, trying to lighten the atmosphere and get closer to Wolf.
Wolf was different from them.
They had reached their limits. Unless they used Soul Beads, further improvement was practically hopeless. Most of them were nearing thirty or even forty years old; any further extraction of cellular energy would be slow suicide.
But Wang Lan was different.
The fact that he could still break through meant he was still in his growth phase. Maybe, just as the rumors said, he was someone with a significant background. Perhaps his participation in the Star Martial Competition was genuinely just for fun.
Hearing the hint in Wang Lan’s tone, the twenty-odd Star Martial Warriors backstage all pricked up their ears.
"Actually, it’s just... I was lucky enough to get a bye just now, and I even pocketed a cool hundred thousand yuan. A hundred thousand! Man, I don’t even make that much in a year. I was so excited! Finally, I can afford to eat meat! The moment I thought about it, my blood surged, and I instantly broke through the governor and conception vessels..."
"Fuck! I can’t listen to this anymore! Where’s my greatsword? Damn it, where’s my greatsword?!"
Wang Lan’s figure flashed, and with a WHOOSH, he vanished.Thɪs updatᴇd by ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
"I’ll be off then! See you at the official match—" His voice still lingered backstage, but Wang Lan himself was long gone.
After Wang Lan left, the show’s recording also drew to a close.
While Wang Lan was enjoying a nice shower and then a good night’s sleep, news about him quietly started trending online.
"Shocking Reveal: Wolf’s True Strength Exposed! Turns Out, He’s Merely at the Early Star Shine Stage!"
"Got a Bye, Snagged 100,000 in Prize Money! Wolf So Excited, He Broke Through on the Spot!"
"What Made Wolf the Public Enemy of the Star Martial Competition? Too Good at Showing Off, Nearly Caused a Riot!"
One intriguing headline after another, along with spoiler-filled articles, hooked the audience members who were anxiously awaiting the Star Martial Competition broadcast, sending them into an excited frenzy.
With bloodshot eyes, they clicked on each spoiler post like ravenous wolves, devouring the content.
"Wolf is only at the early Star Shine Stage? Hahaha... I told you he was all show and no substance! He deserves to be eliminated."
"The commenter above is obviously a professional keyboard warrior who just spouts nonsense. Didn’t you read the content? Wolf thrashed his opponent and advanced to the next round!"
"It’s long been said in the world of Star Martial Warriors that true powerhouses can disregard differences in Star Power ranks. Wolf, with his early Star Shine Stage in Star Martial Art, overwhelmed many enemies in the late Star Shine Stage. He undoubtedly proved this principle."
"So, even Star Martial Warriors like to show off, huh? Now I’m wondering... that troll I had a 300-round flame war with online last night, could he be a Star Martial Warrior?"
"A moment of silence for the commenter above..."
"Prayers for the commenter above..."
"Lighting incense for the commenter above..."
"What do you all mean by that? Are you jealous that I went head-to-head with a Star Martial Warrior online?"
"Poor kid. If you had a 300-round argument online and the other party was really a Star Martial Warrior, and they decided to track you down via your internet connection to ’pay you a visit’ in real life... how many rounds do you think you’d last then?"
"Not much time left for the commenter above..."
"Yeah, really not much time left for them..."

chapters.title: Chapter 73: 13 into 7
chapters.content:
Chapter 73: Chapter 73: 13 into 7
「Three days later, the second round and the third episode began to air.」
At Suzhou City TV station, in the backstage area for the Star Martial Warrior competition organizers, Min Jian stood on the balcony with a cup of coffee, quietly watching the distant lights.
By the second round, the ratings for yesterday and the day before had increased significantly compared to the first round. As the rounds progressed, the events became more exciting, naturally boosting viewership. However, this particular episode left Min Jian feeling uneasy.
The final episode of the second round had just finished recording when it suffered a ruthless spoiler leak. Through posts by live audience members after they returned home, channels like Weibo, and with the aid of internet armies reposting, the details of this episode’s matches were almost completely revealed.
Having spoilers reposted was proof of the show’s popularity. Min Jian should have been happy that his program was blazing hot. His achievements since the official start of the third season were clear for all to see, solidifying his position as a top variety show director.
But there is a limit to everything.
A small number of spoilers can pique the audience’s desire to watch, a promotional tactic Min Jian was deeply familiar with. However, excessive spoilers can drain that anticipation, leading the audience to not watch it immediately, or even at all.
As netizens said, browsing the forums felt like having already watched the latest episode.
"Director Min, the ratings for the first ten minutes are out," the assistant said hurriedly, approaching Min Jian with a spreadsheet in hand.
"How much did they drop?"
"Zero point eight percent."
Although he had mentally prepared himself, the coffee in his hand still trembled slightly.
"What about the online viewership rate?"
"It also fell by thirteen percent."
"SIGH—" Min Jian slowly turned around and returned to his seat.Follow current novels on NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
"Director Min, what do we do? The show’s hype has already been stirred up, and spoilers are unavoidable. After all, it’s a competition, and the ultimate highlight is the outcome. Once the results are known, the audience’s desire to watch decreases. What if we hold closed competitions? Without an audience?"
"The live audience’s reaction is also an essential effect for the show. Without a live audience, the viewers at home won’t have an immersive experience. We can’t do without a live audience..."
"Then... what should we do?"
"I plan to initiate a semi-live broadcast, with a half-hour delay in the live stream."
"Ah? But how will we manage the post-production in time?"
"We’ll hire the most professional team for simultaneous post-production. As long as no unexpected incidents occur at the venue, managing the program’s rhythm shouldn’t be a major issue. The Star Martial Warrior Competition is this popular; there’s no reason for it to start with a bang and end with a whimper."
"Should we consult the producers and get their opinion?"
"It’s my show; I make the decisions. Don’t worry, get the word out."
Gradually, the show neared its end.
Suddenly, a strange shout erupted in the data monitoring office, "Damn!"
Min Jian lifted his head and looked coldly at the technician who had yelled.
Doesn’t he realize that such a sudden outburst in the quiet office could startle people?
Min Jian calmly pulled out a tissue and wiped the coffee that had splattered onto his pants.
"Damn!" Another shout followed.
"What’s happened?"
"Director Min, the ratings are up..."
"Director Min, the online view count has also suddenly bounced back."
"What’s going on?"
"It must be related to Wolf’s appearance on stage..."
"Right, it’s currently broadcasting Wolf’s match. Most of the highlights of this episode are actually from the backstage segment where Wolf is showing off. His actual fight wasn’t that impressive."
"Yes, the comments on the online video are starting to get lively too."
On the online player, what was once a quiet comment stream suddenly exploded with messages.
"He’s here, he’s here, walking with a stride that disowns all kin!"
"He’s here, he’s here, swaggering in with the audacity of a rogue..."
"PFFT! HAHAHA—"
"Wow, so white, so round, so pretty!"
"Wow, so long, so straight, so sexy!"
"So many talented trolls online! Can a real wit come up with a fitting caption?"
"Busy licking the screen, no time!"
"Is Wolf fighting this missy today? Why do I feel a bit sorry for her?"
"I heard Wolf KO’d this missy in the match. She’s so pretty, how could Wolf bear to strike... I feel so sorry for the missy."
"Get lost, you sissy above! A real man kills girls to prove his Dao!"
"Exactly! The land of tenderness is a hero’s tomb. In the world of Star Martial Warriors, there are no girls, only brothers! Does nobody want this girl? I’ll take her."
"The one above is despicable!"
"SLURP—"
As the barrage of comments increased, keyboard warriors got all fired up, unleashing their lightning-fast fingers, filling the screen with so many comments that not a single gap remained.
The match itself held no real suspense; Director Min and the production team were well aware of this. It was a completely mismatched battle. While a one-hit knockout might be dazzling, what the audience really wanted to see was a fiercely competitive fight between equals.
So, after Wang Lan quickly knocked An Wei out of the ring with a flurry of punches, the screen was flooded with celebratory bullet comments. The occasional simp who chastised Wolf for not knowing how to treat a lady gently, questioning how he could strike such a beauty, was quickly drowned in the deluge of comments.
Then, An Wei stood up, completely unharmed. The commentators explained that Wang Lan’s rapid punches hadn’t actually injured An Wei but had merely pushed her out of the ring. After this, those simpering comments naturally vanished.
Then, the real climax arrived.
Originally, Wang Lan receiving a bye had made the keyboard warriors in front of their computers so frustrated they felt like smashing their keyboards.
This season of the Star Martial Warrior competition really only has Wolf as its main attraction. If not for watching Wolf, who would care about this show?
But unexpectedly, after being drawn for a bye, Wolf actually broke through on the spot, in public.
The production team made a special edit of this unforeseen event. They dimmed the lights, cut the sound effects, and zoomed in on the surging Star Power around Wang Lan. Then, they cut to a close-up of the bewildered faces of the audience in the stands. This editing pushed the atmosphere to its peak, making the viewers at home feel a tension so palpable it was almost suffocating.
Suddenly, Wang Lan’s Star Power erupted, then just as quickly, it returned to calm.
"Holy shit, so a Star Martial Warrior’s breakthrough really is like what they show in TV dramas?"
"This is a genuine breakthrough, damn it, with zero special effects!"
"Although it’s not as visually spectacular without special effects, why do I feel so moved... I never thought I, a mere muggle, would witness a Star Martial Warrior’s true breakthrough in my lifetime... It’s too emotional."
"To the commenter above, don’t cry. Give me your address, and I’ll come over to give you some warmth."
"To the two commenters above, may you have a hundred years of happy marriage and an early case of AIDS!"
Next up, of course, was Wang Lan’s show-off segment. When the audience heard his theory on breakthroughs, the bullet comments exploded.
"The way he’s showing off... forget these Star Martial Warriors, even I want to take a knife to him."
"I originally thought Wolf, with the mask, was a serious Star Martial Warrior. Now I know this guy is anything but serious."
"Can some big shot tell me why these Star Martial Warriors are reacting so strongly to Brother Wolf’s breakthrough?"
"Kid, you don’t understand, do you? A Star Martial Warrior’s breakthrough requires a lot of preparation. The most basic is a massive source of Star Power—either Soul Beads or a body filled with abundant Star Power."
"Then, you absorb or extract it all at once, striking the Star Shine within the Star palace. When the Star Shine breaks through the Star Power limit, that’s a breakthrough."
"Exactly. But Wolf clearly didn’t do any prep work. He just broke through, openly, without any regard for others’ feelings. This is completely shattering the worldview of the other Star Martial Warriors."
"Oh, Brother Wolf really is the best!"
The last episode of the second round came to a successful close. Although its average viewership wasn’t great, it did have a peak in ratings, giving the production team a respectable way to save face.
Deep into the night, as all grew quiet, the online jesters were still bursting with energy.
On a certain popular platform, talents converged, and one parody video of Wang Lan after another was shared like crazy. But all of this had nothing to do with Wang Lan anymore.
After reaching the Star Shine Stage, the speed of breakthroughs slowed considerably.
Well, that’s to be expected. The total experience required is a hundred times that of the Starlight Stage. It started at ten thousand, and now, having successfully upgraded to Star Shine Four, advancing to Star Shine Five actually requires forty thousand experience points.
Possibly, probably, maybe... Even if I win the Star Martial Warrior competition, it would at most fill half the experience bar, right?
Thinking of this leveling difficulty, Wang Lan couldn’t help but feel a wave of despair.
「Unknowingly, another weekend arrived.」
The third round wrapped up perfectly, with the top thirteen successfully decided. Besides Wang Lan’s effortless selection, Hu Qing also won a brutal victory against his opponent to secure his place.
However, it was said that although Hu Qing had a tough victory, he had also sustained considerable injuries. That one hundred thousand yuan prize money was hard-earned. If Hu Qing faced another tough battle next, he might be eliminated. But luck always seems to open doors when you least expect it.
In the draw for advancing from thirteen to seven, Hu Qing fortunately received a bye.
This meant not only did Hu Qing effortlessly gain two hundred thousand yuan in prize money, but he also got two days of rest.
Two days of rest were more than enough for Hu Qing’s injuries to heal. For Star Martial Warriors, as long as they had time to rest and sufficient food, their Self Healing abilities were remarkably strong.
The greatest value of a medical Star Martial Warrior was on the battlefield, enhancing a team’s endurance when there was absolutely no time for rest.
Upon learning of the situation, Wang Lan called Hu Qing. Over the phone, Hu Qing sounded energized, saying he had only broken two ribs and that two days of rest would be enough for him to recover completely. "It’s nothing!" he said, telling Wang Lan to focus on his own matches and also make it into the top seven.
To this request from Hu Qing, Wang Lan replied that it was a given.
What am I here for, after all? I came for the championship.
With each advancing round, the experience and skill point rewards would skyrocket. Winning the championship would probably be worth the effort of several previous battles combined.
Since it’s the same effort to beat someone up, of course, I have to brawl my way to the championship throne.
「Arriving backstage, today six elimination duels were scheduled to determine the top seven. After these, there would be a day of rest, and then on Monday, the competition for the top seven rankings would take place.」
By now, those who remained were basically all experts; there were definitely no slackers left trying to get by. As for who would secure a definite win or who would be eliminated, none of the contestants backstage dared to make any guarantees.

chapters.title: Chapter 74: This is a Provocation
chapters.content:
Chapter 74: Chapter 74: This is a Provocation
Starting from this round, the competition adopted a semi-live broadcast format. It was recorded half an hour in advance, and then the production team would immediately edit the footage, broadcasting it before any spoilers could leak.
The first step was to draw lots for the matchups. Wang Lan’s opponent this time was a Star Martial Warrior with a Gold Attribute.
Seeing the draw results, Wang Lan looked up, only to find his opponent also looking his way, giving him a thumbs up. Just as Wang Lan was about to respond, the opponent suddenly wore a sly smirk and turned his thumb upside down.
Hah... childish!
The Gold Attribute wasn’t particularly rare among Star Martial Warriors, but neither was it common. Its characteristics involved controlling metal and using Star Power to create metal.
Wu Changfeng was a Galaxy Stage expert with the Gold Attribute. Wang Lan had discussed with Wu Changfeng before and learned that the practical applications of the Gold Attribute weren’t as extensive as he had initially thought.
Gold Attribute Star Martial Warriors are not Magneto; that ability belongs to the Magnetic Attribute. The most common application for Gold Attribute Star Martial Warriors is to cover their bodies in metal, increasing their defense. This is different from Wu Changfeng’s Iron Body, which metallizes the entire body—an advanced state rarely achieved. For a typical Gold Attribute Star Martial Warrior, simply being able to cover their body in metal is already commendable. Encased in metal, they become like tanks, bulldozing their opponents.
Perhaps, in the opponent’s eyes, Wang Lan’s Star Cloud Sword Dance and Flame Sword weren’t enough to penetrate his metal armor. Coupled with Wang Lan’s publicly revealed mid-Star Shine Stage, the opponent most likely looked down on Wang Lan and mocked him childishly.
What he didn’t know was that his covert antics backstage were captured by the cameras. Min Jian, stroking his chin, stared at the frozen frame on the screen.
"Director Min, should we cut this out?"
"Movies, TV shows, novels, and so forth all have protagonists. Who is the protagonist of our Star Martial Battle?" Min Jian suddenly turned and asked.
"Obviously, it’s the Star Martial Warriors themselves, with each one being the protagonist in the eyes of their fans."
"No! Not everyone is a protagonist; there is only one. Maybe at the start, anyone could become the protagonist. Throwing them together to compete is to let the real protagonist emerge victorious.
"People’s attention is limited, as is their affection—it can’t be divided so thinly. It’s like a group of people walking down the street; whoever stands out the most, that’s the protagonist.
"Since the third season of the Star Martial Battle began broadcasting, the contestant Wolf has stood out from all the others and become the protagonist. The discussions about him and his popularity tower over all the other contestants."
"Director Min, do you mean..."
"Since we have a protagonist, the others are supporting characters. So, our job is to create controversial topics and let the audience feel the conflict. Since that Jin Cheng contestant provoked the protagonist, instead of cutting it, we might as well give him a close-up. Let the viewers see the protagonist being challenged, thereby heightening their anticipation for the battle."
But... isn’t this bad for Jin Cheng?
"If he cared about his reputation, he wouldn’t have made such a disgraceful gesture backstage."
"Got it, I understand."
「The competition officially began.」
Wang Lan’s match was second to last. He sat quietly backstage, watching the fights on the big screen.
By the fourth round, the battles had become particularly fierce. To outsiders, they appeared incredibly intense. But in Wang Lan’s eyes, they were particularly... superficial, all show and no substance. It was hard to describe. The contestants appeared ferocious, as if nursing deep grudges, and their fights were earth-shattering with dazzling effects, yet many moves were merely flamboyant and unnecessary. Several times, Wang Lan saw a contestant could have easily dodged using a simpler method but chose to block with a Star Martial Skill instead. Often, they could have won by engaging in close combat, yet they insisted on using Star Martial Skills.
Star Martial Skills also have drawbacks. At the very least, they cause Star Energy Fluctuations and are predictable. Punches and kicks are silent and swift. While less powerful, they are more covert and faster. For Star Martial Warriors, close-quarters combat is the most common method of dispatching enemies in actual battles. However, in the previous two matches, hand-to-hand combat was merely an appetizer, with the later stages dominated by exchanges of Star Martial Skills.
The audience was thrilled, watching wide-eyed and slack-jawed in amazement. But to Wang Lan, such theatrics were too fake to bear.
Halfway through the competition, the TV station’s live broadcast began.
While the host fluently rattled off sponsors’ names, several contestants appeared on the TV screen, one after the other.
"Finally, we see Wolf!"
"I’ve been waiting two days. The previous two episodes were exciting, but without Wolf’s matches, something felt missing."
"I feel the same. It’s like switching channels to a different show."
"Is Wolf going to fight this time?"
"He’s here now, might as well finish the matches before leaving."
"They’ve drawn lots. Oh my, he’s up against that tank!"
"I’d say Wolf is more of an agile warrior type, right? I paid close attention to Jin Cheng’s ’tank’ build in the previous episodes. He’s completely encased in a steel frame, possessing seemingly invincible defense—practically unbeatable."
"I watched too. His armor looks as thick as a real tank’s. Unless you hit him with armor-piercing rounds, he could probably stand there all day and you wouldn’t break his defense."
"Is Jin Cheng really that strong?"
"Very strong. If you’re asking that, you definitely haven’t been watching the other matches closely and just focused on Wolf. No one has managed to counter Jin Cheng’s ’tank’ style so far."
"Doesn’t that mean Wolf is in danger?"
"Go Wolf, you can do it!"
"Wolf is invincible!"
"Wait a minute, let me take a screenshot!"
Soon, a screenshot appeared in the comment section below the video player, and new posts with the screenshot also surfaced on forums.
"Just captured this moment, although the camera quickly moved on. But did we see what I think we saw?"
"Jin Cheng actually provoked Wolf?"
"How old is he to be doing such childish things? So arrogant!"
The internet is a magnifying glass. Sometimes it turns a trivial matter, even one that Wang Lan hadn’t taken seriously, into a major event sweeping across the entire net in an instant.
A hot search topic suddenly shot up to tenth place and quickly entered the top six.
"Director Min, the comments online have exploded. Many people are trashing contestant Jin Cheng. Is this... really okay?"
"If he cared about his reputation, he wouldn’t have made such a disgraceful gesture backstage. Besides, we didn’t orchestrate this or deliberately give him a close-up; it just so happened that those two seconds of footage got edited in.
"But in terms of the show’s impact, we’ve succeeded. The groundwork for conflict has been laid, the audience’s emotions are stirred, and now we just wait for Wolf to deliver the satisfying climax of a ’face-slapping’ victory to the audience."
"But what if Wolf loses?" the assistant asked hesitantly.
"Wolf won’t lose."
"Director Min, you’re so certain?"
"I’ve asked the judges, haven’t I?"
"What?" The assistant looked incredulously at Director Min. "Don’t you know that Mr. Xiaobao, Mr. Qin, and the others are known as the ’Strategic Bluffing Trio’? Are their predictions even trustworthy?"
"I didn’t ask them. I asked a real professional Star Martial Warrior master. In his own words, so far, he has not found any weaknesses in Wolf. Even his perceived weaknesses may just be things he hasn’t shown yet.
That Star Martial Warrior master is at the Star Cloud Stage."
"Let’s thank Chang Shuangyue and Long Needle for bringing us a thrilling match! Although Long Needle fought his hardest, he ultimately fell short against the consistently stable Chang Shuangyue.
Now, we’ll ask the Earth Attribute staff to repair the arena. While they’re doing that, let’s go to a commercial break. After the break, it will be our fifth match: Wolf versus Jin Cheng! Audience members, please don’t go anywhere; we’ll be right back after these messages!"
Having said that, the host seemed to deflate, pulling out a handkerchief to wipe the cold sweat from his forehead.
Only God knew what an ordinary person like him, standing on the host’s platform outside the arena, experienced when watching two powerful Star Martial Warriors clashing with their Star Martial Skills at such close range. His accidental injury insurance was already at ten million, and now it seemed that wasn’t enough; he needed to increase it. Too damn risky!
The arena was quickly repaired, and Wang Lan entered the stage amidst fierce BGM.
Wang Lan arrived at the center of the arena, but Jin Cheng was nowhere to be seen on the opposing walkway.
Just as the audience began to wonder, a slight trembling sound, followed by heavy footsteps, began to resound.
Jin Cheng was bare-chested, his brick-like muscles rippling with each step. On his back, he carried a massive, gleaming black iron pillar, nearly twice his own size.
That thing must weigh several tons, right? Yet Jin Cheng walked onto the platform carrying it on his back without any change in expression.
"Isn’t that way too exaggerated? He’s leaving footprints on concrete!"
"Was the concrete not dry?"Thɪs ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
"Dry my ass, those were made by his stomping! Damn, how heavy is that? A dozen tons?"
"Jin Cheng has never carried such a huge thing before. Could it be his weapon? Can he even wield something that heavy?"
"Whether he can wield it or not isn’t my concern; what worries me is whether the protective barriers on the arena can hold. If they break, all of us in the studio could be smashed to death, right?"
"Damn it, I want to sit in the back row."
"Get to the front!"
The commotion in the stands was also precisely captured by the camera, a development that pleased Min Jian immensely. If it were just a stellar performance by Wolf alone, this matchup would fall far short of audience expectations.
A formidable opponent creates more suspense and heightens the audience’s anticipation and tension.
Jin Cheng’s appearance today was a complete departure from his usual light and unburdened style. Carrying such a behemoth, he seemed like an entirely different person from the lightly equipped Jin Cheng of the past—the difference between a man and a monster.
Wang Lan watched Jin Cheng solemnly. There were only two explanations for someone to carry such a weight with ease: either Jin Cheng’s strength had surpassed the limits of a Star Martial Warrior, or he possessed a Star Martial Skill that made lifting heavy objects seem light. If it was just surpassing strength limits, that would be one thing. But if he had a Star Martial Skill to lift weight as if it were light or to alter gravity, then this would be Wang Lan’s second truly challenging battle since the competition began.
WHIRRING—
Tiny drones buzzed, their wings whirring as they circled above the venue. They then found a perfect vantage point and settled, their camera lenses fixed on the two individuals on stage.
「In Suzhou City’s Tianjian Bureau」
Wang Qianfeng hadn’t gone home after work. Instead, he sat in his office, having brewed a cup of fragrant tea, and watched the live feed captured by the drones, sipping contentedly.
TAP TAP TAP! A knock at the door interrupted him.
"Who is it?"
"Me!" He MingXue’s voice rang out from the other side.
"What do you want?"
"You’re not going home after work, so I came to see what mischief you’re up to in your office," He MingXue said as he pushed open the door, his gaze immediately drawn to Wang Qianfeng’s computer screen.
"What are you holding there?" Wang Qianfeng asked with a frown.
"An HD projector. Your computer screen is too small."

chapters.title: Chapter 75 This is playing out of the ordinary
chapters.content:
Chapter 75: Chapter 75 This is playing out of the ordinary
Both of them smiled knowingly. Although Wang Lan participated in the competition anonymously, could this truly be hidden from Wang Qianfeng and He MingXue? Even though they did not approve of Wang Lan joining such an insignificant competition, since he had already joined, they would let him do as he pleased.
The current Star Martial Art Competition was well-organized and had some substantial content. Moreover, Wang Lan’s gradual display of his strength during the Star Martial Art Competition also allowed Wang Qianfeng and He MingXue to see how well he had mastered the two A-rank Star Martial Skills.
The Vertical Flame Sword in the first match thoroughly impressed He MingXue; even he hadn’t expected the Flame Sword to be used in such a manner.
As the saying goes, a mentor can lead you through the door, but the practice is up to the individual. Star Martial Skills are just like that; it all depends on who uses them and how they are used.
"Did you see that provocation from Jin Cheng just now?" He MingXue suddenly asked.
"Just a piece of trash, no need to pay him any mind."
"I checked out that Jin Cheng. He’s very strong!" While speaking, the projector was already set up, and on the background wall of Wang Qianfeng’s office, Jin Cheng appeared, walking with that huge steel rod on his back.
"Indeed, he has brought ’Victory Heaven’!"
"’Victory Heaven’? That name sounds familiar."
"Thirty years ago, in the northwest region, there was a small Star Martial family known for forging Star Martial weapons. Their weapons had excellent Star Power conduction, and their craftsmanship was no less than that of renowned weapon forging families like Dragon Spring.
Thirty years ago, this Star Martial family obtained a special piece of Tungsten Iron material that was naturally formed. They forged a batch of divine Star Martial weapons and then sought out a Gold Attribute Star Martial Warrior to test the quality of these divine weapons.
Unexpectedly, all the weapons were deemed substandard. Not only could they not pierce the body of a Gold Attribute Star Martial Warrior, but they would also soften like noodles upon mere contact. It was later discovered that this special material could be easily controlled by Gold Attribute Star Martial Warriors, with a Star Power conduction speed a hundred times that of ordinary metals.
In the hands of a Gold Attribute Star Martial Warrior, this material was like their own Star Power.
Later, the Star Martial family presented this special material to that Gold Attribute Star Martial Warrior. This gave birth to a legendary Star Martial Warrior from the northwest, known as the ’Northwest War Dragon.’
Ten years ago, a spatial rift appeared in the northwest. The Northwest War Dragon went into battle with the army and never returned. The powerful weapon the Northwest War Dragon relied on was this strange piece of Tungsten Iron known as ’Victory Heaven’."
"What’s the relationship between Jin Cheng and the Northwest War Dragon?"
"He’s the son of the Northwest War Dragon. He was stripped of his Star Martial Warrior benefits for refusing to enlist in the army. As the descendant of a military martyr, he would have received additional care and compensation from the country had he enlisted. Yet, he still held a grudge over his father’s death."
"After his father died, the country actually took care of him. Otherwise, where would he have gotten the Soul Beads to elevate his Star Power, and how could he have entered the training ground for free?
The country cared for him for ten years, yet this is how he repaid them. It’s quite disheartening to talk about... Although I don’t like him, I have to admit that he’s very strong. He is at the peak Star Shine rank in Star Power, trained in combat by army experts, and has participated in real battles in the training ground. Combined with the same Gold Attribute talent as his father and the aid of ’Victory Heaven,’ Wang Lan facing him doesn’t look good."
"He only cares about his personal grudges, lacking any of the awareness expected of a Star Martial Warrior. Moreover, he’s a fool who can’t tell right from wrong. His father died in battle, not at the hands of the northwest army. He should feel honored for his father.
In my eyes, such a person is trash. If Wang Lan can’t beat him... Hmph!"
"So what if he can’t?"
"Then he’s even less than trash!"
"Wang Lan is definitely talented, but unfortunately, Jin Cheng is practically cheating," He MingXue sighed, arms folded.
"You think that kid doesn’t have his own tricks?"
"Are you talking about the Phoenix Form? Old Wang, I can guarantee that even if Wang Lan were beaten to death, he wouldn’t use the Phoenix Form on such an occasion. He may seem humble, but he’s actually very proud inside. Unless it’s a matter of great importance, he wouldn’t resort to cheating."
The host delivered an impassioned speech, and with the sound of a whistle, the match began.
Suddenly, Jin Cheng placed the Tungsten Iron he had been carrying on his back down in front of him, and it bizarrely began to squirm like water.
"Huh? Jin Cheng’s Star Martial Skill is unlike anything we’ve seen before. We all know that Jin Cheng is a Gold Attribute Star Martial Warrior who can control metal. But metal itself is an extremely hard substance and, typically, can’t be manipulated as flexibly as substances like water or earth.
Yet in Jin Cheng’s hands, the Tungsten Iron can move as fluidly as if he were controlling water. Has Jin Cheng’s control over Gold Attribute Star Power reached such a bewildering level? It’s truly astonishing."
WHOOSH—
Suddenly, the Tungsten Iron wall before him instantly shot out several steel spikes. Thin chains were connected to the back of the spikes, leading to the Tungsten Iron wall in front of Jin Cheng, where his hand rested.
Witnessing this scene, Wang Lan instantly deduced Jin Cheng’s method for controlling the Tungsten Iron. Gold Attribute Star Martial Warriors can’t manipulate metal from a distance, similar to how most Earth Attribute Star Martial Skills require contact with earth-based substances.
Earth-based substances are everywhere, but Gold Attribute materials are hard to find in the wilderness. So, Gold Attribute Star Martial Warriors who can’t achieve Elementalization of their bodies always carry a block of metal with them, a fact Wang Lan was aware of.
However, he didn’t expect Jin Cheng to control metal to such an extent; with a mere gesture, sharp attacks were already flying at him.
Wang Lan instantly drew Ghost Wail. Contrary to everyone’s expectation, he didn’t choose to dodge. Instead, with a flicker of his body, he slashed through several tentacle-like chains with a single stroke.
As long as Jin Cheng’s hand remained on the Tungsten Iron wall, the chains he shot out would pursue their target like living creatures.
If he started dodging, he would be caught in the chains’ relentless assault.
CLANG, CLANG—
Two crisp sounds rang out as the incoming chains were blocked by Wang Lan, but contrary to expectation, the chains did not break. The chains, which appeared to be only thumb-thick, were extraordinarily tough.
After ascertaining the toughness of the Tungsten Iron, Wang Lan changed his strategy.
Chains rained down from above towards Wang Lan, who easily evaded them with a flicker of his body.
BOOM! The chains pierced deeply into the cement floor, kicking up a cloud of dust.
Wang Lan’s figure became a series of afterimages as he rapidly closed in on Jin Cheng. Under Jin Cheng’s control, the chains pursued as fast as streaks of light. Even with Wang Lan’s phantom-like movement technique and a powerful Star Martial Skill like Star Cloud Dance, he couldn’t shake off the pursuing chains.
Jin Cheng, clearly a Gold Attribute close-combat warrior, had somehow developed a ranged attack capability similar to a Mage. This was definitely an anomaly among Gold Attribute Star Martial Warriors, an outlier among outliers.
Every second was a dance with death; every fleeting image, a heart-stopping crisis.
The audience members all clenched their fists tightly, staring unblinkingly at the thrilling chase unfolding in the arena.
Compared to his duel with Lan Die, although this lacked that same overwhelming sense of pressure, the speed and danger were no less intense.
Even the Star Martial Warriors watching backstage all wore solemn expressions.
They were all pondering one question: if they were in Wang Lan’s shoes, could they dodge Jin Cheng’s razor-sharp attacks?
In the end, everyone silently shook their heads.
"Too fast, too strong, and just too indefensible," an agile warrior murmured, shaking his head.
"The weakness of Gold Attribute Star Martial Warriors lies in their speed. Once you break through their defenses, victory is basically assured. But if you’re facing someone like Jin Cheng, how can you break his defenses if you can’t even get close?"
"Unless... your attack range is longer than Jin Cheng’s."
"Not necessarily. There’s also the assassin class of Star Martial Warriors, who have invisibility and stealth skills. But Wolf, at least, doesn’t have invisibility or stealth skills, nor does he possess any long-range attacks. In this battle, Wolf is being completely countered."
"Not necessarily!"
"Brother Qi Ming, do you have any insights?"
"Have you all forgotten that Wang Lan is a Fire Attribute Star Martial Warrior? Fire Overcomes Metal."
"That depends on what kind of metal it is. The Tungsten Iron that Jin Cheng is controlling requires flames of at least five thousand degrees to be affected. That damn monster! How does he control metal so quickly and flexibly? It’s unreal!"
"Indeed, unreal. With such strength and ability, he would have been identified as a talent for special training long ago. Why is he participating in the Star Martial Art Competition? What are he and Wolf thinking?"
"Perhaps what we pursue means nothing in their eyes?"
The contestants’ analysis backstage was fully recorded by the organizers. Soon, these analyses would become material for the broadcast, designed to hook the audience and leave them desperate for more.
While the contestants backstage analyzed the battle, Wang Lan, using his Star Cloud Dance movement technique, had painstakingly managed to close in on Jin Cheng.
Wang Lan’s intentions had been clear from the start, obvious even to the audience.
When Wang Lan closed to about four or five meters from Jin Cheng, Jin Cheng’s mouth suddenly curled into a cold smirk. He gave a thumbs-down, a clear echo of his gesture after the initial draw.
"WOW—"
"He’s that arrogant?" A wave of surprised exclamations erupted from the stands.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
In that instant, a dozen more chains shot out from the Tungsten Iron wall, swift as arrows, instantly arriving before Wang Lan’s face.
"Not good!"
"AH—" Many audience members instinctively covered their eyes.
In Wang Qianfeng’s office, Wang Qianfeng and He MingXue both held their breath for a moment. This attack was too fast. Evidently, judging by Wang Lan’s previous actions, he hadn’t realized the Tungsten Iron wall could launch more than just a few chains.
If he was caught unprepared, the probability of being hit and losing the match was as high as ninety percent.
Suddenly, Wang Lan’s body spun a full one hundred and eighty degrees vertically in mid-air, like the hand of a clock, the iron chains barely grazing past him.
Suddenly, Wang Lan extended his palm, and a cyan flame shot up from it.
FSSSHH—
The Flame Sword flashed, and five chains were instantly severed.
The severed ends glowed bright red.
"WOW—"
"Just as expected, Wolf used the Flame Sword after all," someone backstage said nonchalantly, folding their arms.
"That can’t be right. Those are Tungsten Iron chains. Even cyan flames shouldn’t be able to sever them instantly, should they?"
"Perhaps Wolf’s cyan flames are many times hotter than we imagine."
"Old Wang, quick, playback, playback!" He MingXue exclaimed excitedly.
"What for? It’s the decisive moment..."
"Never mind that, playback!"
The footage rewound to the moment Wang Lan executed the Flame Sword slash.
"Zoom in, zoom in, zoom in more! Play it at thirty times slower speed."
Soon, the footage revealed the form of the Flame Sword.
It turned out that although the Flame Sword was made of cyan flames, its form had transformed into a saw. This saw had rapidly moving serrations, which were still too fast to discern clearly even when the playback speed was slowed by a factor of thirty.
"Damn! How did this Demon manage to control the Flame Sword with such precision? Is this a Star Martial Skill of attribute manipulation or shape manipulation?"

chapters.title: Chapter 76 Does Your Face Hurt?
chapters.content:
Chapter 76: Chapter 76 Does Your Face Hurt?
"You asking me?" Wang Qianfeng, digging at his ear, glanced at He Mingxue with contempt written all over his face.
"Wasn’t the Flame Sword something you taught him? You have the gall to ask me?"
"..."
He Mingxue was choked for words and couldn’t come up with a retort.
The moment Wang Lan’s blade severed the chains, Jin Cheng’s expression finally changed. He hurriedly manipulated the Tungsten Iron wall, raising it to shield himself.
To Wang Lan, this move seemed like a classic blunder. The best defense is offense. Facing my advance, Jin Cheng chose to retreat instead of launching another attack to push me back? The moment Jin Cheng made that choice, he was doomed to lose. How could I miss such a golden opportunity?
With a flicker of his movement technique, Wang Lan instantly closed the distance to Jin Cheng’s Tungsten Iron wall, fiercely thrusting his Flame Sword into it.
"Damn it!" Wang Qianfeng shot up in alarm.
How could Wang Lan be so stupid? Jin Cheng isn’t encased in Tungsten Iron; that thrust won’t reach him! Instead, Jin Cheng can counter-attack in an instant. Jin Cheng made a mistake letting Wang Lan get close, but Wang Lan just made an even dumber mistake! Utterly, incredibly stupid!
Jin Cheng was thinking the exact same thing. Seeing the Flame Sword pierce the Tungsten Iron, yet still remain a considerable distance from his body, Jin Cheng smirked.
He’d seen people court death before, but never quite like this...
"AH—!"
But just as Jin Cheng placed his hand on the Tungsten Iron, a piercing scream erupted.
The Tungsten Iron was still the same pitch-black, but its temperature had already soared above 200 degrees Celsius.
This scene left everyone utterly perplexed, from the judges on the platform and the host of Star Martial Warriors backstage, to the competition host by the ringside.
"What’s going on here?"
"I get it now."
"The thermal conductivity of Tungsten Iron is over five times that of steel. Although it has a high melting point and isn’t easily melted, it can be heated to such a high temperature that Jin Cheng wouldn’t even be able to touch it. Now I understand what ’Fire Overcomes Metal’ truly means. It’s not just about one method; metal’s inherent thermal conductivity is high. If you heat the metal, even a Gold Attribute Star Martial Warrior hiding inside a metal shell would just be popped like popcorn by a Fire Attribute Star Martial Warrior."
After the bespectacled student finished his explanation, the surrounding spectators showed signs of enlightenment. The young man gently pushed his glasses up the bridge of his nose.
That’s the brilliance of a science student for you.
BOOM—
Wang Lan kicked the Tungsten Iron away and strode toward Jin Cheng.
His Flame Sword, now gripped in both hands, emitted an intimidating cyan fire. As Wang Lan closed in, fear flickered in Jin Cheng’s eyes.
He knew Wang Lan’s close-combat prowess. Jin Cheng had repeatedly watched Wang Lan’s videos and knew that in terms of practical combat skills, he was no match. And Wang Lan was a Fire Attribute Star Martial Warrior who specialized in the Flame Sword. Once Wang Lan got close, defeat was certain. He’d considered activating his Gold Attribute armor, but after what happened with the heated Tungsten Iron, he instantly realized that even if he encased himself in an iron ball, he’d still be roasted by the flames. To withstand such fiery temperatures, he’d need to achieve Elementalization of his body. But... if Jin Cheng possessed that kind of power, why would he even be in this Star Martial Art competition?
"I... I... concede!"
Before Wang Lan even made a move, Jin Cheng suddenly conceded. Not only was Wang Lan baffled by this, but the host was also somewhat at a loss.
"Um... Contestant Jin Cheng, what did you just say? You... concede?"
"Yes, I concede. My attribute is countered by his. I can’t win anyway, so I concede!"
"Cut it out!"
"Acting all high and mighty one second, then chickening out the next. Could you be any more predictable?"
"Damn, I also thought you had no chance against Wolf, but I expected you’d at least struggle a bit! Did you have to fold so completely?"
The audience in the stands immediately began to jeer. They collectively made the same trash gesture Jin Cheng had used earlier, effectively returning the favor.
In Wang Qianfeng’s office, the atmosphere was deathly silent.
After a long while, He Mingxue let out a lengthy sigh. "Old Wang, does your face sting?"
"What do you mean, does my face sting?" Wang Qianfeng, panting heavily, glared murderously at He Mingxue.
"What else could it be? Who was it just now saying Wang Lan’s move was ’unfathomably stupid’? But to me, that move was ingenious. Countering a Gold Attribute Star Martial Warrior with the temperature of the flames—it’s amazing he thought of that. No wonder he’s a good student, applying his knowledge so flexibly."
"What the hell are you so smug about? You didn’t think of it either, did you?"
"I’ve used the principle before, just not in that specific situation. As for why I’m smug... Heh heh heh! The Flame Sword, I taught him that. It feels like Wang Lan’s Flame Sword is much better than his Star Cloud Sword Dance. Is it just my imagination? Strange..."
The match was over, and naturally, it was time for He Mingxue to leave. He stood up leisurely, stretched, and muttered smugly to himself.
Suddenly, he froze mid-step.
He Mingxue sensed an enraged beast behind him, emanating intense murderous intent.
"He Lao’er, you dare show off in front of me? Get your ass to the training grounds! Let me see what you’re really made of!"
"Are you being unreasonable now? Wang Lan’s skill with the Flame Sword proves it suits him. You think I’m like you, hoarding good Star Martial Skills and fobbing him off with that trash Star Cloud Sword Dance?"
"Trash Star Martial Skill? Are you kidding me? That’s a Star Martial Skill passed down in my family! I gave him my ultimate technique, and you call it trash? He Lao’er, don’t you dare run! I’ll chop you to pieces!"
Two figures burst through the window and raced wildly through the Tianjian Bureau headquarters.
"Contestant Jin Cheng has voluntarily conceded! Contestant Wolf successfully advances to the fifth round, securing a spot in the top seven! Let’s give a warm round of applause to Contestant Wolf! And let’s also applaud Contestant Jin Cheng for the exciting match he brought us!"
SHH—
"Successfully advanced to the fifth round. Reward: 3,000 experience points, 250 skill points."
As the host’s voice faded, the system’s notification echoed in Wang Lan’s mind.
*You’re* the 250.
"Next, we will proceed to the final match of the fourth round."
The last match of the fourth round concluded quickly. In less than ten minutes, one contestant was defeated by their opponent’s overwhelming strength.
Once all the matches of the fourth round were concluded, it was time for the fifth-round draw. The prize money for the fifth round was 400,000. Whoever drew the bye to advance directly to the semi-finals would be incredibly lucky.
Soon, the results of the fourth-round draw were announced. A Star Martial Warrior named Xing Feng, a favorite for the championship, received the bye. Backstage, at least two Star Martial Warriors secretly breathed a sigh of relief.
Next were the pairings for the upcoming three matches. Wang Lan was matched against an Earth Attribute Star Martial Warrior, while Hu Qing drew Chang Shuangyue.
Even now, Wang Lan couldn’t gauge Chang Shuangyue’s true strength. So far, Chang Shuangyue had crushed nearly all his opponents. Hu Qing is going to have a tough fight ahead.
「Shortly after Wang Lan left, the TV and internet livestreams began broadcasting the start of his match against Jin Cheng.」ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ NovᴇlFirenᴇt
"Go, Wolf!"
"Take him down!"
"Exactly! Did you see the gesture he made at you backstage? If it were me, I wouldn’t have been able to stand it!"
"Whoa, what the heck is that thing he’s carrying?"
"Such a massive slab of iron? Is he planning to forge weapons right here on stage?"
"Who cares what he’s planning? An agile warrior against a heavily armored tank—it’s a surefire win no matter how you look at it."
"Go, Brother Wolf!"
"Girl upstairs, don’t run away!"
When the match officially began, Jin Cheng’s fierce attacks instantly flooded the screen. In that moment, the entire stream of bullet comments vanished. For a full thirty seconds, there was dead silence. Then, suddenly, a torrent of comments erupted.
"Holy crap, that’s a tank? You’re telling me that’s a tank?"
"Yeah, it’s a tank, alright—a tank from the planet Cybertron!"
"Those ranged attacks are insane! Even a Mage would be crying."
"No wonder he dared to provoke Wolf, even knowing how strong Wolf is. Turns out he actually had some tricks up his sleeve."
"To prevent friendly fire, person above, please declare your allegiance! My thirty-meter blade is already halfway out of its sheath!"
"Tricks up his sleeve, my ass! If it weren’t for that coffin lid he’s carrying, Wolf could’ve toyed with him however he wanted!"
"You fanboys up there are exaggerating. Jin Cheng’s control over metal has to be world-class. I’ve never seen a Gold Attribute Star Martial Warrior manipulate metal with such flexibility."
"Jin Cheng is strong, and so is Wolf. Everyone, please exercise some restraint and send fewer comments; it’s disrupting our ability to watch the match."
"Then just turn off the damn comments if they bother you! And hey, you stop commenting too!"
Amidst the uproar, Wang Lan successfully closed in on Jin Cheng. A swift slash of his Flame Sword severed the chains. His fluid and graceful movement technique immediately drew howls from his female admirers.
"So handsome! How can anyone be *that* handsome? This old auntie can’t take it anymore!"
"Auntie, please maintain your dignity! If you really can’t, you can always send me a private message."
The more intense the battle, the more explosive the internet traffic became. Many keyboard warriors had already lost focus on the match itself; their primary source of excitement was engaging in sprawling online flame wars.
When Wang Lan brilliantly used the high temperature of his flames to counter Jin Cheng’s metal control, the comment section exploded with "666."
"This guy is definitely a top student."
"Definitely a science major."
"You idiot! Didn’t you learn about the thermal conductivity of Tungsten Iron in high school? Anyone who isn’t an elementary school kid should know this, right?"
"Oh, please! Like *you* could? In a situation like this, would *you* even remember your high school physics? Put you in that spot, and you probably couldn’t even do basic addition and subtraction!"
"Exactly! During such a high-intensity battle, the brain is entirely focused on movement and evasion. To even think of using thermal conductivity to win, Wolf must have been incredibly calm. My god, did Jin Cheng’s threat not faze him in the slightest?"
"Plus, Jin Cheng publicly gave him a thumbs-down! Wasn’t Wolf even a little bit angry? How could he stay so calm and pull off that incredible counter-play?"
"You’re all amateurs, so you wouldn’t understand. Maintaining absolute composure during combat is a fundamental requirement for any Star Martial Warrior on the battlefield. Those who can’t remain calm end up dead."
"What? Star Martial Warriors can die?!"
"What? Star Martial Warriors go to war?!"
"What? The world of Star Martial Warriors is that brutal?!"
This barrage of comments left some of the Star Martial Warrior keyboard warriors speechless with frustration.
Have we been protecting the world *too* well, or something? Do these people really think human civilization is all sunshine and rainbows?
"There’s no such thing as a perfectly peaceful world or a completely tranquil era. You live in peace and prosperity because you were born in a powerful and stable nation. Try living in some smaller, weaker country and see if you’d even know if you’ll survive to see tomorrow!"
"Damn it! He folded instantly!"
"Damn! What happened to all that bravado when you gave him the thumbs-down? You’re just going to fold like that?"
"Jin Cheng, for this fight, I respected you as a true man. But after seeing that, I take it all back."
When the video broadcast reached the part where Jin Cheng didn’t even attempt a final struggle and just raised his hands in surrender, the online comment section absolutely erupted...

chapters.title: Chapter 77: There Is Always a Hurdle in Life That One Cannot Overcome
chapters.content:
Chapter 77: Chapter 77: There Is Always a Hurdle in Life That One Cannot Overcome
"Director Min, the ratings broke four this cycle!"
In an era where the internet is advanced and most people haven’t watched TV in years, a rating breaking four is already a very impressive achievement.
At least, none of Min Jian’s favored programs from recent years had broken four.
"What about online on-demand views?"
"Sixty million views immediately upon release, and barring any surprises, it will break a hundred million by tomorrow morning."
"Not bad! There are only two episodes left: Friday’s competition for the top seven warriors, and Sunday’s final battle to decide the champion. Although we’ve already achieved a significant milestone, we can’t let our guard down. After the Star Martial Warrior competition concludes perfectly, I’ll give each of you a big bonus, out of my own pocket."
"Director Min is mighty—"
"Director Min is powerful—"
As Wolf’s popularity continued to soar, he gradually showed signs of becoming a national idol.
The Star Martial Warrior competition boosted Wolf’s popularity, and Wolf’s consistently stable performance, in turn, sustained the competition’s buzz. The two were mutually reinforcing.
And Wang Lan felt more and more as if his identity were splitting. Sometimes he would feel confused: was he Wang Lan, or Wolf? It seemed that once he put on the mask, he, Wang Lan, transformed into someone else.
The usual Wang Lan continued his school routine, as unflappable as ever. Sometimes, he would pretentiously discuss the Star Martial Warrior competition with his classmates, arguing heatedly until their faces were red about who would win the championship.
Every time Jiang Xinyu saw this, she couldn’t help but cover her face, unable to watch. She really hadn’t realized before that Wang Lan was such a good actor.
During the break, a cellphone rang.
Jiang Xinyu quietly stood up and walked outside the classroom.
"What’s up?"
"Miss, the sponsor just called me. There’s a talent agency that wants to unlock Wolf’s information. They’re offering ten million..."
"Are we short on money?"
"Not really, Miss. But even if we aren’t short on money, every little bit helps, right? Ten million just for Wolf’s real information—this deal is too good to pass up."
"Hmm! If Wolf’s real information gets leaked, you’d better disappear. Preferably to another country."
"Ah?"
"That’s settled then. Go to the central data computer, delete Wolf’s registration file, and shred it completely. Wolf’s information must never be leaked. Understood?"
"Understood."
"I have to get back to class. Hanging up."
「Friday evening, as the city lights began to shine.」
Wang Lan took the subway with the crowd to the vicinity of Suzhou City’s TV station and quietly put on his mask in a secluded corner. Just as he was about to head to the TV station, he heard a familiar voice.
"Brother Lang, you’ve placed all the bets, right? I’m confident in my strength."
"Are you sure? Perhaps you’re the only one in the whole world who’s confident. But whatever, since you believe in yourself, go ahead. But remember, the deal is final once you buy."
"I understand! But you can’t scam me."
"Huh? You think I, Brother Lang, built my reputation by bragging? I, Brother Lang, navigate this world by upholding principles and loyalty, and I have many brothers. If you didn’t trust me on that, you wouldn’t have come to me. Besides, I wouldn’t dare scam a Star Martial Warrior, right?"
"Good!"
Hu Qing turned and waved goodbye, only to spot Wang Lan standing not far away, wearing a moon-white mask. Hu Qing strode over. "You’re here?"
"What kind of deal were you making with him?" Wang Lan frowned.
Although he hadn’t heard everything, he had a general idea.
"Nothing much... Let’s go, the competition is about to start."
Wang Lan hadn’t known Hu Qing for long; it wasn’t enough time to forge a deep friendship.
But at least to Wang Lan, Hu Qing seemed like a decent person.
This was particularly evident given that someone had offered three million for Wang Lan’s real identity. This fact would have been well-known among the Star Martial Warrior competition participants. Especially in the last two days, many Star Martial Warriors had secretly tailed Wang Lan after he left the TV station. But Wang Lan, using Xiao Ai to control the cameras and his own nimble movement technique, had shaken them all off.
Hu Qing had no reason not to know about this. As the only one aware of Wang Lan’s true identity, taking the three million would have been easy for him. Yet, Wang Lan’s identity remained unexposed.
Initially, Wang Lan hadn’t expected to suddenly become so famous, which was why he had exchanged real identities with Hu Qing. Hu Qing desperately needed money, yet he had protected Wang Lan’s identity, proving he was a man of principle with a clear moral compass.
Therefore, Wang Lan didn’t want to see Hu Qing go down the wrong path.
"Since I was young, I’ve known that gambling has only one end: utter ruin. Actually, many people know this, but it’s like an addiction they can’t quit. Once trapped, they see no hope and just live day by day. But smoking only harms oneself; gambling harms oneself and one’s family."
Hu Qing’s steps halted. "I know, but my sister’s illness..."
"Your sister’s illness isn’t an excuse for your downfall. Many people dream of getting rich overnight, but they all know gambling won’t make them rich; that tempting money is just bait on a trap."
"This might be my last stand." Hu Qing pulled out a crushed pack of cigarettes from his pocket. "Do you know how heavily I used to smoke? Three packs a day. I had to have one before bed just to be able to sleep.
"My comrades gave me this pack of cigarettes when I was discharged from the army. I’ve been smoking them sparingly ever since, and I still have half a pack left. All to save that cigarette money.
"For her, I even quit smoking.
"I originally thought I could win the Star Martial Warrior Competition and earn those three million. But having come this far, I’ve realized I can’t go any further. You asked me the other day why I hadn’t slept well? That night, the hospital issued another critical condition notice for my sister.
"She’s so well-behaved, and only ten years old.
"I don’t know how long I can hold on; my parents are on the verge of giving up. I can’t take it, I really can’t take it anymore. It’s a bottomless pit, a true bottomless pit. But I swear, even if she ultimately has to leave us, I’ll spend every last bit of my strength to keep her here until the very last second.
"I’ve bet on myself to win. This battle, I must win."
"And if you lose?"
"I won’t lose!" Hu Qing glared, his eyes bloodshot, killing intent erupting from him.
"After the competition, take me to see your sister," Wang Lan said calmly.
"Alright!" Hu Qing managed a faint smile. "Let’s go. Lately, fans looking for you have been all over the place outside the TV station. I just don’t get it. They don’t even know what you look like, so why do they like you so much?"
"Perhaps it’s precisely because of this sense of mystery."
"Dear live audience and viewers at home! Responding to your overwhelming demand, the third season of Suzhou City’s Star Martial Warrior Competition, the battle for the top seven, is officially kicking off!
This battle for the top seven will be broadcast live—no delays, no editing. What our viewers at home are seeing is exactly what’s happening here, right now.
