It wasn’t just Xing Feng who had this thought, but also the millions of viewers watching the livestream.
From the beginning of the match, Cheng Qingzhu attacked fiercely.
He was well aware of Chang Shuangyue’s terrifying power; even Hu Qing, despite his great strength, had been beaten to a bloody pulp by him. Cheng Qingzhu had no confidence in winning. The only sliver of hope lay in Hu Qing’s Gravity Fist being a blunt attack, whereas his own wind-attribute Star Martial Skill possessed unrivaled cutting force.
Unfortunately, two high-cost Star Martial Skills had failed to break Chang Shuangyue’s defense. On the contrary, it was Cheng Qingzhu, famed for his speed due to his wind attribute, who was pushed to a corner of the ring.
The battle had only lasted three minutes, but there had already been more than three final-bout-level clashes.
At this moment, Cheng Qingzhu’s face was covered in sweat, his chest heaving dramatically.
The entire venue was silent. The audience, the judges, and the host were all clenching their fists, unwilling to make a sound.Thᴇ link to the origɪn of this information rᴇsts ɪn novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
Even backstage, Director Min, who had absolute control over the program, was staring at the screen without blinking. This match was too tense. Chang Shuangyue was like a monster, closing in on Cheng Qingzhu step by step.
And Cheng Qingzhu, like a small creature evading a predator, tried every trick to counter the hunter, but to no avail each time. His pitiable and helpless appearance evoked sympathy, making one want to help him.
At this moment, the number of people watching the livestream continued to rise, but the comment section was unusually quiet.
There were no rampant comments, and even the bullet screen messages had thinned out.
Countless people were utterly transfixed, staring intently at the video on the screen, holding their breath.
"PHEW—" Cheng Qingzhu exhaled a long breath; his Star Power was nearly exhausted. If this continued, admitting defeat would be his only option.
Therefore, he had to make one last desperate gamble.
That move was an A-rank Star Martial Skill, and a very powerful one at that, which he had practiced for three years without being able to fully master. But now was his last chance.
Cheng Qingzhu’s eyes suddenly hardened. He gently lifted one foot, spreading his hands in a starting position, like a golden rooster standing on one leg.
Chang Shuangyue’s eyes were blood red, his face twisted as if he were enduring some kind of intense pain. Wang Lan saw all of this.
What on earth is Chang Shuangyue enduring?
Wang Lan wondered.
Are there side effects to activating this invincible mode? Like my own Phoenix form, does it have some hidden risk? It must be. Would such a powerful Star Martial Skill really have no drawbacks? Would being such an aberration be appropriate?
An azure wind instantly howled around Cheng Qingzhu.
Chang Shuangyue, who had been closing in step by step, suddenly stopped.
Suddenly, Cheng Qingzhu, using one foot as a pivot, began to spin rapidly. The swift rotation stirred up the Speedy Wind, and in an instant, he created a massive tornado that reached up to the arena’s barrier.
The tornado shot up into the sky, transforming in the void into a colossal, four-edged wind blade, tapering to a sharp point like an awl.
"Sky Punishment Wind Erosion!" On the judges’ panel, Bao Longqing stood up excitedly.
"Sky Punishment Wind Erosion? Mr. Xiaobao, you know this move?"
"This is the signature ultimate technique of the Titled Strongman, Zeng Xiao, the Dragon King of the Wind, from fifty years ago. Sky Punishment Wind Erosion is a Star Martial Skill that pushes the Wind Cutting attribute to its absolute limit. It’s said that Zeng Xiao used this technique back then to defeat the Diamond King of Gran Country. Sky Punishment Wind Erosion can even slice through a diamond wall one meter thick! To think it would appear on the stage of the Star Martial Arts Tournament."
Hearing Mr. Xiaobao’s explanation, many in the audience showed expressions of awe.
Those who didn’t understand simply felt it was impressively mysterious, while those in the know nearly choked on their laughter.
This included the two middle-aged men watching the livestream on a projector in Wang Qianfeng’s office.
"PFFT—" He MingXue spat out a mouthful of new tea, almost ruining the high-definition projector he had acquired for ten thousand yuan.
"Was that necessary?" Wang Qianfeng glanced at He MingXue with disdain.
"This judge, where did the Star Martial Arts Tournament organizers dig him up? Does he get all his information from online search engines?"
"Sky Punishment Wind Erosion is indeed a decent A-rank Star Martial Skill, but is it as incredible as he claims? If it were truly that incredible, would it still be an A-rank Star Martial Skill? It’s true that Zeng Xiao defeated the Diamond King with Sky Punishment Wind Erosion. But that was because he was Zeng Xiao. If anyone else performed it, they couldn’t even break through a ’Glass King,’ let alone the Diamond King. Zeng Xiao had an extraordinary natural affinity for the wind attribute; any wind-attribute Star Martial Skill in his hands was effectively three times more powerful. Wielded by Zeng Xiao, Sky Punishment Wind Erosion reached power nearing S-rank. Besides, it’s obvious that Cheng Qingzhu hasn’t mastered this move yet..."
"Why are you rambling on to me about this?" Wang Qianfeng sipped his tea calmly. "You think I don’t know?"
"But isn’t this misleading the audience?"
"So what if it misleads them? Does the audience need to know the truth?"
"They don’t?"
"They won’t become Star Martial Warriors, and which of those who can become Star Martial Warriors doesn’t already know this? However... I’ve actually become interested in this Chang Shuangyue kid."
"Oh? Has his talent piqued your curiosity?"
"No, I just have a feeling that Chang Shuangyue is a bit odd. His Star Martial Skill is somewhat different from those I remember. It’s neither a berserker form nor like the blood-stopping secret technique. It feels... like it might be an innate talent Star Martial Skill."
"Who cares... Let’s just keep watching."
As those words fell, the Wind Blade in the sky fiercely charged toward Chang Shuangyue’s chest. Chang Shuangyue’s skin turned an even deeper red. Instead of dodging, he tilted his head back and threw a heavy punch straight up at the Wind Blade.
"My God—has Chang Shuangyue gone mad? To recklessly throw a punch like that?"
"Damn, that’s hot-blooded! That’s domineering! This is what a real man looks like! A real man throws a punch head-on! Go for it!"
Cries of shock and roars of encouragement burst from the mouths of the audience watching the live broadcast.
Cheng Qingzhu clenched his teeth tightly, his form merging with the Wind Blade. He kicked Chang Shuangyue’s fist aside and slammed fiercely into Chang Shuangyue’s chest.
"Something’s wrong!" Cheng Qingzhu’s expression changed dramatically.
Chang Shuangyue’s chest didn’t feel like flesh; it was as if he had kicked solid fine iron.
Chang Shuangyue’s body kept retreating. The terrible impact forced him back relentlessly.
His legs, like two iron stakes, were firmly planted on the ground, carving long furrows into the solid cement floor.
Suddenly, Chang Shuangyue, who had kept his head bowed, slowly lifted it. A sinister smile appeared on his twisted face.
With one large hand, he grabbed Cheng Qingzhu’s airborne leg. The howling wind dissipated, and the world fell silent. Cheng Qingzhu, dangling in his grasp, looked utterly helpless, weak, and pitiable, like a small chick.
"CRACK—" A crisp, clear sound.
Chang Shuangyue had actually, with raw force, broken Cheng Qingzhu’s leg.
"AAAAH—"
Before Cheng Qingzhu could even let out a scream, the audience at the scene erupted in an outcry.
Since it was a real combat competition, injuries were bound to happen; breaking a leg was considered within the realm of normal injuries. There are many ways to get injured, and many ways to break a leg.
But to snap a leg off as if it were a corncob—that was excessively bloody and cruel.
"Damn, hasn’t Chang Shuangyue broken the rules?"
"According to the rules, it’s not a foul, but no one does something like this in public during a match. Is he determined to go down a dark path?"
Chang Shuangyue’s actions didn’t stop there. Suddenly, he grabbed Cheng Qingzhu’s arms.
"CRACK—"
As if wringing a towel, he twisted Cheng Qingzhu’s arms a full 180 degrees.
"That’s too much!"
"So cruel... Is he some kind of psycho?"
"Damn, he really did it?"
"Stop! Stop! The match is over! Chang Shuangyue wins! Chang Shuangyue, you are forbidden from continuing to harm contestant Cheng Qingzhu! Release him now!" The announcer, having lost his composure, hurriedly shouted in panic.
Cheng Qingzhu was discarded onto the ring like trash by Chang Shuangyue. Chang Shuangyue silently turned and, step by step, walked away from the ring. Wherever he went, the audience scattered as if avoiding a plague god.
Such a peerless fiend, exuding a terrifying aura of savagery.
Backstage, Xing Feng’s Adam’s apple bobbed.
It took him a long time to regain his composure.
"If I encounter him, it might be better to just forfeit."
"I’m going to step out for a bit. Can you wait for me for five minutes?" Wang Lan said calmly as he stood up.
"Sure, but if you treat him now, your Star Power..."
"It’s no problem."
Wang Lan’s figure flashed as he dashed out of the backstage area. This moment was, of course, broadcast by the live cameras.
"Is the Wolf King going... to the bathroom? Did he get scared into peeing himself?"
"You’re the one who got scared into peeing! Did you forget the Wolf King revealed he was a Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior in the last match?"
"He’s going to treat Cheng Qingzhu? He’s about to compete. Isn’t that a waste of Star Power?"
"Little Wolf is so kind, so heartwarming... You two upstairs have no compassion; you deserve to be single for life!"
"Hey, don’t assume just because you’re a girl I won’t call you out. Do we seem like we lack compassion? We’re just rationally analyzing the pros and cons, okay?"
"Bro above, you’re arguing about rationality with a woman? From that alone, you’re not rational enough."
"I... I’m wrong! You’re right. What the girl says is right."
Cheng Qingzhu was carried away on a stretcher, heading straight for the medical room.
In the medical room, Medical Star Martial Warriors were already on standby. Seeing Cheng Qingzhu’s injuries, they shook their heads somberly.
"I can’t treat these injuries. The bones are twisted like rope. Unless a senior Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior treats him, he’s definitely crippled. Moreover, we can’t delay. We must find a senior Star Martial Warrior within six hours. Otherwise, even with a senior Medical Star Martial Technique, it will be too late to save him."
"Miss Ji, even you can’t do anything?"
"There are many types of Medical Attribute skills. I can ensure wounds heal, but his issue isn’t about wounds—it’s that his bones have been crushed into powder."
"Let me try," a voice, gentle as a breeze, reached the ears of everyone present. Wang Lan, wearing a moon-white mask, slowly approached the unconscious Cheng Qingzhu.

chapters.title: Chapter 85 I Admit Defeat
chapters.content:
Chapter 85: Chapter 85 I Admit Defeat
Wang Lan’s brows furrowed slightly as he looked at Cheng Qingzhu’s injuries. It wasn’t the complexity of the injuries that bothered him, but the cruelty and ruthlessness of Chang Shuangyue. Everyone was here for the competition, not embroiled in deep-seated hatred; was there really a need for such a heavy hand?
Fortunately, Cheng Qingzhu had passed out. Had he been conscious, how much suffering would he have endured?
ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
"Player Wolf, these injuries are difficult to treat. I know your medical skills are extraordinary, but his injuries are different from Hu Qing’s," Miss Ji said, pausing slightly as she looked at Wang Lan, as if she thought he was at a loss for what to do.
"It’s manageable," he said, reaching out to touch Cheng Qingzhu’s leg.
A surge of Star Power flowed, and a hazy light radiated from the palm of Wang Lan’s hand. Underneath the light, the severely twisted and swollen leg slowly reverted to its original state, as if time itself was being rewound.
To the other staff members, this scene didn’t seem extraordinary; they assumed all Medical Star Martial Techniques were this miraculous. But Miss Ji saw it differently.
Pure Medical Star Martial Technique? No, that’s not right. It’s not a Star Martial Skill. This is... Is this an Inborn Talent of the Bloodline?
Miss Ji’s eyes widened in disbelief.
Medical Star Martial Techniques utilized Yang Attribute Star Power, altering it in a way that stimulated the target’s cells to heal. But even powerful Medical Star Martial Techniques had their limitations.
For instance, if the bones had been crushed to dust, they would need to be reassembled before any healing could start. And completely shattered bones simply couldn’t be restored by Star Power. So in Miss Ji’s eyes, even if they managed to save his leg and hand, his future as a martial artist was finished.
What use is a warrior whose bones are made of flour?
However, pure medical healing, or rather, pure medical Inborn Talent of the Bloodline was different. They often possessed the miraculous ability to turn decay into something magical, reminiscent of the Shen Family, which had been wiped out by a mysterious force seventeen years ago.
Known as the Jade Silkworm family of Jade Country, they were like the meat of Monk Tang to the Star Martial Warrior community, containing a miraculous Life Force within them. As long as they awakened their Inborn Talent of the Bloodline, their medical abilities could revive a person to full health, restoring them to peak condition, provided they weren’t already dead.
Pity that this family, seen as a treasure of Jade Country, was mysteriously slaughtered, and to this day, Jade Country has not found the culprit.
Collecting his thoughts, Wang Lan had already finished treating Cheng Qingzhu’s leg. The leg, which had been completely deformed and twisted, was miraculously restored to its original form in such a short period.
Miss Ji gasped, quickly moving to Cheng Qingzhu’s side, gently probing his leg. She closed her beautiful eyes, sensing the condition of the injuries on Cheng Qingzhu’s leg.
The crushed bones have been perfectly realigned... Not just realigned... It’s as if they were never injured, without the slightest damage or crack?
Miss Ji opened her eyes, looking at Wang Lan in utter disbelief.
By now, Wang Lan had withdrawn his hand, and Cheng Qingzhu’s arms, too, had been restored to their original state after mere seconds of healing.
"Next up, please welcome player Wolf and player Xing Feng to the stage!" the announcer’s excited voice blared from the public speakers.
Wang Lan took a towel and wiped his forehead. "He should be fine now. I have to go to the stage."
"Wait!" Miss Ji suddenly called out. "What’s your name?"
"I’ve entered the competition anonymously and don’t intend to reveal my identity."
"Such a powerful Medical Star Martial Artist can’t be without fame. But your medical method is something I’ve never heard of, so... you haven’t debuted yet, have you?"
"Uh... My participation in the competition isn’t for the sake of debuting."
"You’re still a student?"
As Miss Ji finished her speculation, Wang Lan couldn’t help but shiver and hurriedly started to leave, lest he reveal too much.
With a flash, he disappeared.
Watching Wang Lan flee, the medical room staff couldn’t help but cover their mouths and chuckle.
"What are you laughing at? Do I look like I eat people?" Miss Ji coldly glanced at the staff.
"It seems that player Wolf is really quite innocent... An old hand would have relished the chance to spend more time with Miss Ji."
"Is that your excuse for not leaving?"
"Sorry, I’ll leave right now. As for player Cheng Qingzhu..."
"Take him away, take him away! Once he wakes up he’ll be jumping around. What’s the use of keeping him here?"
Wang Lan dashed toward the arena while Jiang Xinyu slowly approached from the opposite side, casually tossing a mid-level Soul Bead into Wang Lan’s hand. Instantly, Wang Lan absorbed the Soul Bead, and his Star Power, which had been depleted by nearly half, was instantly replenished.
「Atop the stage, Xing Feng stood in a corner of the ring, his arms crossed, eyes closed, and still as a mountain amid the cheers of the audience.」
The cameras spun 360 degrees without a blind spot, broadcasting Xing Feng’s poise to every viewer in front of their television sets.
"So cool! Xing Feng really does have the demeanor of a great master."
"Just standing there, he has the air of a master."
"His image and temperament are impeccable, but... I still like Wolf King more."
"Me too, Wolf King seems more genuine. He can show off, he can act cute, he’s kind-hearted, his martial arts are strong, and even though he wears a mask, he’s more sincere than all the other contestants."
"Those without masks seem to wear an invisible one, whereas the one with a mask seems to be unmasked. Perhaps that’s what makes the Wolf King truly unique."
"Wolf King knew there were two matches ahead, yet he still expended his Star Power to heal Cheng Qingzhu without a second thought. It’s clear that in Wolf King’s heart, a single contest is far less important than a fellow Star Martial Warrior."
Amid the anxious wait of the audience, Wang Lan’s figure appeared in the walkway on the opposite side, his appearance instantaneously setting the audience abuzz, with many even standing up to applaud him.
"Good, contestant Wolf has entered the stage. Before the match begins, I, on behalf of the organizers, announce a new rule: Contestants are not allowed to harm their opponents in non-essential circumstances. Anyone who is judged by our referees to have intentionally caused injury will be disqualified. Do either of you contestants have any objections?"
"No objections!"
"No objections!"
"Alright, then, I hereby declare the second semi-final match of the Star Martial Championship, Wolf versus Xing Feng, officially begins!"
The moment the host’s words dropped, suddenly, the audience members on the platform excitedly stood up and let out a collective gasp.
This situation also caused the two contestants who were just about to move to stop in their tracks. Because on the big screen, they saw Cheng Qingzhu, unscathed, walking from backstage to the audience area.
Cheng Qingzhu’s injuries had been severe, something all present had witnessed; it was no exaggeration to say his entire body had been twisted into a knot. And it had only been about five minutes, yet there he was, appearing completely unharmed.
Cheng Qingzhu arrived backstage and gave Wang Lan a deep bow, holding it for several seconds before straightening up and then turning to leave.
"You could heal such injuries so quickly; you’re the strongest medical Star Martial Warrior I’ve heard of. Why do you come to compete?" Xing Feng suddenly asked.
"To compete against all of you."
"To refine your combat skills?"
"Yes!"
"That’s such a naive idea... Most people come to the Star Martial Championship to make a name for themselves, a few for the prize money. I’m afraid no one, except you, would want to refine their combat skills against us, a group who has already given up on themselves..."
"What about you? What for?"
"Fame! Money, to comfortably live as a big star, to comfortably spend my life," Xing Feng said with a self-deprecating wry smile. "Once, when I was as young as you, I too dreamed of making a name for myself. But later, I gradually realized my place.
"It’s important to know yourself. I am not some child of destiny; I’m just an ordinary person among the masses. You may not believe it, but I once had grand delusions of becoming like the Five Emperors.
"In my youth, it was the time when the Flame Emperor from the South came into prominence.
"Do you have any idea? Back then, the Southern Flame Emperor was the idol of our generation, the epitome of striving for success. The Flame Emperor, a noble child from a humble background, became the brightest star of the era.
"But, failing college entrance exams, drifting through the military, joining the Pioneering Legion for nearly a decade with a narrow escape from death, I remained at the Star Shine Stage. My talent is not higher than those around me. My opportunities aren’t better either, and I haven’t worked any harder than them.
"I seem to be a rivet, fixed in that position.
"If my life is already destined, then why can’t I live a little more comfortably? Be a star, make films, live my remaining years in comfort?
"Why go through life and death, or perhaps one day die in a Different Dimensional Space, becoming food for the Exotic Beasts?
"In the world of Star Martial Warriors, one more or one less of me makes no difference.
"Is this too much blathering? These words aren’t just my thoughts, but also those of the Star Martial Warriors who have given up their identity and prefer to live as ordinary people.
"Whether they’re the big stars idolized by everyone or Star Martial Warriors who guard houses and serve as enforcers. They’re all deserters from the Star Martial world.
"It’s shameful, but hey, it’s not illegal! We’re afraid, yes, we’re afraid of living those days when death could come at any moment.
"Without goals, without dreams, what’s the point of a salted fish dreaming of leaping through the dragon’s gate?"
"You shouldn’t have said that," Wang Lan said with a bitter smile.
"Right, I shouldn’t have. Voicing it is like ripping off their fig leaf. They would turn from national idols into objects of public scorn, and I would gain nothing while earning nationwide condemnation.
"But still, I said it, because I feel inferior. Seeing you, I feel inferior. You’re a medical Star Martial Warrior. A medical Star Martial Warrior coming onto this stage to refine your combat skills, and I, a lightning Star Martial Warrior, am... scrambling for fame, for a comfortable life.
"Think about it. With your strong healing abilities, you could lie back and have endless Soul Beads. You only need to express a need, and many Star Martial Warriors would willingly work tirelessly for you. Any team would consider you a key protected member.
"You don’t have to face death or fight in battles; you only need to heal those who retreat injured from the battlefield. You could even refuse to go to the front line and wait to heal after the fighting is over.
"And yet, you possess a fighting strength that astonishes and impresses even me. You’re only at the mid-stage of Star Shine. Are you even a healer? Huh? Don’t you have any awareness of what it means to be a healer?" Xing Feng suddenly shouted, as though he was venting his inner sense of shame.
He, a lightning Star Martial Warrior, had given up on his dreams, while this medical Star Martial Warrior in front of him had picked them up.
Forget competing with Wang Lan; just standing next to Wang Lan, Xing Feng felt utterly powerless.
"Um, Contestant Xing Feng, don’t get too worked up. In fact, you’ve overthought it a bit. The match started three minutes ago; we should really start now," Wang Lan said casually, breaking the awkward tension. He then clasped his hands in respect and bowed slightly. "Contestant Xing Feng, I look forward to your guidance."
"I admit defeat!"

chapters.title: Chapter 86: There are always choices in the journey of life
chapters.content:
Chapter 86: Chapter 86: There are always choices in the journey of life
"What?" Wang Lan looked at Xing Feng in astonishment.
"I surrender!"
WHOOSH—
But Xing Feng lifted his head, looked seriously at Wang Lan, and spoke those three words.
The entire audience let out a collective gasp of surprise; some even unconsciously stood up.
"Surrender? How can you surrender? I paid for a ticket, you know? You’re not even going to fight before you give up?"
"Yeah, I voted for you! I wanted to see your Thunder Step, and now you’re just giving up?"
"Damn, I bet on you to win, and now you’re making me lose money!"
"If you can’t beat him, fine, but to just give up without even fighting?"
The uproar from the audience wasn’t deafening, but it wasn’t quiet either.
Yet, like needles, it pierced the protective barriers and reached Xing Feng’s ears. In that moment, his heart was truly wounded.
If one has no heart, one cannot be heartbroken; if a heart is numb, it cannot feel pain.
But Xing Feng had a sudden epiphany.
His past self-abandonment, his renunciation of the dreams he held when he first became a Star Martial Warrior, his willing degradation to a commoner far detached from the martial world... What he called ’seeing through life and death,’ ’seeing through the mortal world for a peaceful life,’ was, in truth, nothing but a cowardly escape.
The audience’s words were like knives stabbing into his heart.
Star Martial Warriors aren’t actors! Their battles aren’t for your entertainment, nor for your betting!
But what reason did he have to refute them? What right did he have to argue?
Before this moment, when Wang Lan had turned away to rescue Cheng Qingzhu, whose limbs had been brutally twisted, wasn’t this what he himself had thought? What he himself had done?
You came to act a part, so how can you blame them for treating you as an actor?
Is there anything wrong with giving up being a Star Martial Warrior? No! Is it wrong to want to become famous, to make easy money? No! Tired of fighting, wanting a peaceful life—is that wrong? Also no.
What’s wrong is the state of your own convictions.
The good hate themselves for their evil, and the evil loathe themselves for their good.
Xing Feng’s thinking had changed. That was why he now detested his former, self-degenerating self and the heart that had lost its conviction through numbness.
Never forget your original intention, and you will reach your destination. Is it too late for me to return to the battlefield now?
Xing Feng asked himself this, then slowly turned and left.
"Wait, contestant Xing Feng! Are you certain you want to surrender?" the host asked, trying to persuade him. "This is the semi-final of the Star Martial Competition. If you win this battle, you’ll not only earn a million in prize money but also have the chance to vie for the title of Champion of the Star Martial Competition. Are you really going to give up these honors, now that they’re within your grasp?"
"To you, these may be honors, but not to me, not anymore," Xing Feng said, then silently turned to look at Wang Lan. "I’ve taken the wrong path, and I want to go back. I forfeit the match!"
"Little Wolf, I know you must be very young. As someone who’s been there, let me give you a piece of advice: Never lose yourself in the years to come. If you ever become numb, remember this experience in the Star Martial Competition—why you came here, and what your original intention was. Brave the wind and rain, and forge ahead."
Xing Feng disappeared from the end of the stage. The production team instantly scrambled to adjust the competition’s schedule.
"Successful entry into the finals. Reward: 4,000 experience points, 400 skill points," a voice announced in his mind.
At that moment, the internet exploded.
"What’s going on with Xing Feng? Why the sudden change? He was so full of fighting spirit before! In the last match, when asked about his confidence in winning the championship, he said that while he had no absolute assurance, he would fight with all his strength."
"Yeah, Xing Feng’s strength isn’t actually inferior to Wolf King’s. The Thunder Attribute isn’t really countered by the Fire Attribute. Plus, his Star Martial Art level is higher than Wolf King’s, and his combat experience and fundamentals are certainly not lacking in comparison."
"If they had really fought, it’s hard to say who would have won."
"Yeah! Why did he suddenly surrender?"
"He must have chickened out. Xing Feng is trash."
"It probably isn’t that he chickened out, but that his perspective has changed."
"Is there a psychological analyst who can figure out what’s going on with Xing Feng? What made him suddenly forfeit?"
"Same question!"
Meanwhile, at the Star Martial Competition finals, the TV station had a contingency plan to ensure broadcast times were met, prepared for any unexpected and uncontrollable events. After all, such things had happened multiple times before.
They had invited celebrity guests for performances, with heavyweight stars for the opening act. Naturally, they had also made preparations for intervals in the broadcast.
But did the millions of viewers care about celebrity performances now? No. They cared about how this highly anticipated match had ended so anticlimactically.
The semi-finals! Just half an hour or an hour away from the championship match! Even if you had something urgent, couldn’t it have waited for this short while?
While the entire internet was ablaze with debate, a post analyzing contestant Xing Feng’s psychological journey caused a massive stir, being wildly reposted by countless people.
"His name is Xing Feng, a Star Martial Awakener from the Class of 5002. That year, he was young and full of vigor, gazing up at the stars. That same year, the Flame Emperor from the South proved his path to power, dominated Sky Blue Star, and became the youngest of the Five Emperors, his posture one of invincibility.
In 5005, Xing Feng failed to gain admission to any of the four major Star Martial Academies—the dream of all Star Martial Warriors. He didn’t even make it into a top-tier academy. Instead, he completed his studies at a little-known Star Martial Academy in the northwest.
By 5010, Xing Feng had retired from the Northeast Military District. Five years of military life had washed away all his youthful airs. He was no longer that spirited young man, but merely one among the two million rank-and-file Star Martial Warriors.
That year, his idol still shone like the sun, but he was no longer that young dreamer. Afterward, Xing Feng joined the Pioneer Legion.
Over eight years, former comrades fell one after another. Many brothers who were talking and laughing together just yesterday would be dead on the battlefield the next. Many who had fought courageously on the front lines just the day before would pack their belongings today, saying they were going home to marry and start families.
Fighting. Disappointment. Disappearance. Farewell.
Xing Feng had grown tired of this life, never knowing if today would be his last.
More and more tired.
Finally, in 5018, he made a decision. He would leave the Pioneering Legion, return to the great cities, abandon the glory of being a Star Martial Warrior, and become an ordinary person again.
To become an ordinary person again, debuting and achieving fame seemed the most comfortable path. He chose to participate in the Star Martial Competition—a very fast track to that life.
But was he really content with that?
He thought he was, but in fact, he wasn’t!
When he saw Wolf, participating anonymously, and asked why he’d come to the Star Martial Competition, Wolf’s simple answer was, ’To hone my combat skills.’ Such a pure answer, yet it touched Xing Feng’s heart.
Such a pure reason! Just like when Xing Feng himself had first become a Star Martial Warrior. Back then, he too had been as pure as Wolf.
Many people see Wolf this way: although he wears a mask, they see his purity. Meanwhile, Xing Feng and others like him, though their faces are bare, are constantly wearing a metaphorical mask of numbness.
Seeing Cheng Qingzhu’s limbs brutally broken by Chang Shuangyue reminded Xing Feng of comrades who had fallen beside him on the battlefield.
In that moment, Wolf stood up. He was a Star Martial Warrior of the Medical Attribute; healing comrades was his duty. But what had Xing Feng said at the time? ’If you go now, what about the upcoming match?’
Wolf replied, ’It doesn’t matter,’ and turned away without hesitation.
At that moment, faced with Wolf’s pure character, Xing Feng felt ashamed—ashamed not only in comparison to Wolf’s integrity but also in comparison to his own past self.
He too had once been like Wolf. But somewhere along the way, he had lost that former self, becoming the very kind of person he once despised.
Wolf was clearly a powerful Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior; he was only gone for a few minutes, yet Cheng Qingzhu returned completely unharmed.
Such a powerful Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior could clearly live a life that even Xing Feng would envy.
But what about Wolf? He possessed great strength. Whether in fighting techniques, Star Martial Skills, or actual combat experience, he was no less capable than any battle-hardened professional Star Martial Warrior who had faced life and death.
Wolf was ’just’ a Medical Attribute, yet he had the heart of a warrior. Xing Feng, on the other hand, was a warrior, yet he had long possessed the heart of a retired old man.
To Xing Feng, Wolf was like a mirror. Talking to Wolf was like talking to his own former self.
He once had dreams. He longed to be like the Flame Emperor of the South. Even if he couldn’t reach such heights, he hoped to make a name for himself through hard work.
But reality had submerged him in the vast sea of mediocrity.
He had thought it was because he was born ordinary, destined never to fulfill his dreams. But seeing Wolf, he realized it wasn’t unjust fate; it was because he hadn’t tried hard enough—at least, not compared to Wolf.
The flame in his extinguished heart reignited.
He didn’t want to waste another second of his life on this stage.
So, he chose to concede, leaving the stage to Wolf. As for himself... perhaps he was going home to pack his bags, ready to return to the true battlefield.
Xing Feng, blessings to you. May you ride the favorable wind and soar high into the sky!"
The post was long, yet it seemed to perfectly capture Xing Feng’s innermost thoughts and feelings.
But everyone understood that Xing Feng couldn’t have written this post; he probably hadn’t even returned home yet.
So who was it?
Everyone was curious about the identity of the poster. In the end, however, all they could find was an ID: ’Starlight Tear,’ with no other substantial information.
In an old residential complex in Suzhou City, a young girl gently stood up, drew back the curtains, and walked onto the balcony.
She looked up at the sky.
The weather was clear, yet there were no stars.
A tear slid down her cheek. She wept silently, then suddenly smiled, laughing even as she wiped her tears away.
DING-DONG—
The doorbell rang. The girl hurriedly wiped her tears and peered through the peephole.
Then, with a gentle smile, she opened the door. "Feng, you’re back?"
Xing Feng stood at the door, somewhat hesitant to meet the girl’s eyes. He lowered his head. "Tear, I’m leaving."
Another tear escaped the girl’s eyes, falling with a soft PAT to the ground. "Going back to the frontier? When will you return?"
"Probably by the end of next year. I just called my old captain; he said they’re short-handed. If I go, I can lead a team of twenty."
"Mm, pioneering is dangerous. You have to be careful. Don’t be careless or push yourself too hard. If the Exotic Beasts are fierce, wait for the main force to assemble before going with everyone. If you encounter danger, find a place to hide..."
"Tear, there’s something... I want to ask you..."
"What?"
"Could we... get our marriage certificate tomorrow? I’ve held you back for so many years; you’re nearly thirty... I heard Granny has even started introducing you to potential partners. I know... this is terribly rushed, and I’m sorry, but they’re desperate for people over there. They want me to leave tomorrow night. By the time I come back, another year and a half will have passed. I’m afraid that by then... you’ll have married someone else..."
"Okay," the girl said softly.
"Really?"
"Really!"
Xing Feng scratched the back of his head and grinned, the same foolish grin he’d had eighteen years ago.Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
"What are you still standing at the door for? Come in."

chapters.title: Chapter 87: Do you want it steamed or braised in brown sauce?
chapters.content:
Chapter 87: Chapter 87: Do you want it steamed or braised in brown sauce?
"Dear friends at the venue and viewers in front of your TVs. Due to Xing Feng’s concession and withdrawal, our Wolf has effortlessly advanced to the finals.
"After adjustments by the organizers, the championship battle, originally scheduled for nine o’clock tonight, will now begin ten minutes earlier due to unforeseen circumstances.
"It’s now 8:49:30. I hereby announce that the long-awaited final battle of the third season’s Suzhou City Star Martial Competition officially begins!
"Let’s welcome both contestants to the stage with a round of warm applause!
"The warrior known as the Blood God of Suzhou City, Chang Shuangyue! And the legendary Wolf King, our Wolf! Welcome them with your applause!"
Amid the thrilling music, Wang Lan walked steadily onto the stage.
Chang Shuangyue was a powerful and dangerous opponent. His ruthlessness and cruelty had been deeply etched into everyone’s hearts through the two previous battles. It could be said that from now on, any Star Martial Warrior facing him would feel a measure of trepidation even before blows were exchanged, just knowing his identity.
But Wang Lan was definitely not among them.
It wasn’t because Wang Lan was strong enough to disregard Chang Shuangyue’s ruthlessness, but because... Wang Lan could take a beating! His Healing Star Martial Skills prioritized healing himself before others, and the self-healing effect was several times more potent than healing someone else.
Your defense is impregnable? My Undying Body won’t break under your assault. In the end, it’s still debatable who will wear down whom first.
Chang Shuangyue stood quietly in the distance. His features were so twisted that even his smile was a grotesque sneer, sending shivers down one’s spine.
Wang Lan’s eyebrows furrowed slightly. Chang Shuangyue seemed even stranger than before. His features were now exaggeratedly contorted, as if he were enduring some indescribable pain.
"Contestant Chang Shuangyue, you seem to be in pain. Are you feeling unwell?" the host suddenly asked, perhaps on instruction from backstage.
"No! I’m fine!" His voice was deep, like a muffled drum.
"Are you sure you’re all right? Although the final battle is important, the contestants’ physical condition is paramount. If there’s any discomfort, we can delay the match and let you seek medical attention immediately."
"Stop talking nonsense; there’s nothing wrong!"
"Alright! Since contestant Chang Shuangyue has no health issues, I will now announce the rules of the match. Especially for you, contestant Chang Shuangyue, the referees have added a new rule.
"You are not to inflict harm on the other Star Martial Warrior under non-essential circumstances. If the referee panel deems an act as intentional harm, the offender will be immediately disqualified. Have both contestants understood?"
"Understood."
"Got it!"
"Then, I officially declare the match—begins!"
As the host’s voice fell, Wang Lan’s figure instantly vanished, charging toward Chang Shuangyue.
At the same moment, Chang Shuangyue’s skin turned as red as a cooked crab.
Wielding Ghost Wail, Wang Lan appeared before Chang Shuangyue like an afterimage flickering in countless mirrors, his sword dancing to form a fan of shimmering silver. Concealed within was a deadly move aimed straight for Chang Shuangyue’s eyes.
"Damn—a killer move right off the bat?"
"Classic Wolf, as sharp as ever."
In Wang Lan’s previous battles, except for the last one where he seized the initiative, he had never managed to gain the upper hand. This was partly due to inexperience, and partly due to other reasons.
This time, Chang Shuangyue doesn’t seem particularly agile. If I can’t even take the initiative against him, I really should slap myself a few times.
CLANG—
Although Chang Shuangyue’s movement technique wasn’t as fast as Wang Lan’s, his reflexes were certainly not slow. In the instant Ghost Wail stabbed toward his eyes, Chang Shuangyue swiftly raised his palm to block. Ghost Wail struck his palm, yet it felt as if it had struck the PS Armor from Wang Lan’s home, its sharp edge deflected.
The moment he blocked Wang Lan’s Sword Qi attack, Chang Shuangyue’s hands became blades, chopping down at Wang Lan’s forehead. The speed of the chop was faster than the eye could follow.
To the audience, it looked as if Chang Shuangyue’s hands were still raised, yet the chop had already reached the top of Wang Lan’s head. Wang Lan’s form split in two, provoking screams from many in the audience.
"Damn! Was he one-shotted?"
"Are you blind? That’s an afterimage!"
The split image of Wang Lan disappeared. In the next instant, he reappeared above and behind Chang Shuangyue. Both hands wielded Flame Swords, radiating a golden light.
"Golden flames?" Many of the girls in the audience watched with fascination, their eyes sparkling.
Girls inherently have a special affection for beautiful things. Didn’t that brilliant golden flame resemble the fabled gold of the Vermilion Bird? Wang Lan swung his golden Flame Sword, slashing down from Chang Shuangyue’s shoulder.
HISS—
A wisp of green smoke rose, leaving a shallow gash on Chang Shuangyue’s shoulder. Instantly, the gash writhed and vanished.
Completely unaffected, Chang Shuangyue counterattacked with a slash that cut Wang Lan in half at the waist. Wang Lan’s form dissolved into flowing light and, in the blink of an eye, reappeared at Chang Shuangyue’s chest, his Flame Sword dancing and erupting in brilliant sparks against Chang Shuangyue’s body.
"Such beautiful flames! Is this the legendary True Sunfire?"
"Have you watched too many cartoons or what? Never taken physics? Flames are just infrared radiation; different colors represent different temperatures. Ordinary flames are red or orange. Golden flames are hotter than red ones."
"Exactly! Don’t spout nonsense if you don’t know. Even if you haven’t seen a jet’s afterburner, haven’t you seen the blue flame on your gas stove at home?"
"Can’t mess with the science guys, no way."
"Those guys upstairs are so earnest. I really want to tease them, what should I do?"
"Someone has infiltrated our ranks of science guys! Find them! While it’s true that a blue flame is hotter than a red flame, it also depends on what substance is burning. The blue flame of natural gas is determined by the substance, not the temperature.
"Gas combustion and plasma combustion colors aren’t reliable indicators alone. Drag that spy out and shoot them!"
The comment section was buzzing with talent, everyone excited to see Wang Lan unleash his golden flames. Ultimately, however, the temperature of the golden flames was still insufficient to harm Chang Shuangyue in his red-skinned form; all attacks proved futile.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
Moreover, Chang Shuangyue was extraordinarily fast, retaliating almost within 0.2 seconds of Wang Lan’s attacks. If not for Wang Lan’s ability to perfectly switch between the Star Moon Sword Dance and the Flame Sword, he would have been defeated long ago.
"This kid Wang Lan... his talent is terrifying. Just from his ability to ignore the transition time between Star Martial Skills, he has limitless potential if he uses it well," Wang Qianfeng couldn’t help but sigh.
In the world of Star Martial Warriors, effort is indispensable, but talent is crucial. Talent cannot replace effort, but when efforts are equal, talent is the deciding factor for victory.
And this particular talent Wang Lan possessed had already, by its nature, surpassed 99.9 percent of his peers.
At least, there was no record of anyone ever being able to ignore the transition time between Star Martial Skills.
"But this can only make him difficult to defeat; winning is still a challenge. With such formidable strength at the Star Shine Stage, that Chang Shuangyue shouldn’t be a nobody. How did he end up competing in the Star Martial Competition?"
"I looked this up yesterday. Chang Shuangyue used to be a pioneer in the northwest. Two years ago, his squad was ambushed by Exotic Beasts and suffered heavy casualties; only three survived.
"After that, he left the Pioneer Team and returned to Suzhou City, where he opened a martial arts school teaching practical combat. His strength... according to the data, wasn’t actually that high, and the Star Martial Skills he was now displaying had no prior record.
"Moreover, his records indicated he was a very gentle person. It’s unfathomable why he’s acting so brutally now. The information on record and our current observations make him seem like two different people. But it’s definitely him. We’ll need to keep a close eye on this individual.
"This kind of temperament is bound to lead to trouble."
"Look, Wang Lan has changed his tactics!" He MingXue pointed out. Wang Qianfeng looked up at the match screen again.
Wang Lan had created distance between himself and Chang Shuangyue, retreating to the edge of the ring. His face was somewhat pale; he had expended a large portion of his Star Power.
Chang Shuangyue, meanwhile, advanced with heavy strides. His massive body seemed to make the ground tremble as he ran, leaving a trail of deep footprints in the concrete floor.
Those who chose the path of stacking armor rarely ended well, as they couldn’t keep up with the battlefield’s rapid changes. But if one could stack armor to such an overwhelming degree that even specialized armor-piercing assassins were left in the dust, then they had successfully become an ironclad.
It had to be admitted: Chang Shuangyue’s Star Martial Skill was a success.
Wang Lan had attacked countless times, only to seemingly tickle him. Conversely, if Wang Lan took even one of his blows, it could be game over.
Just now, I went all out with Three Strengths in a Fist. Despite suffering a comminuted fracture in my hand, I did no damage to him. It’s clear that a more piercing attack is required to penetrate his defense.
I still have eight hundred skill points left; that’s my greatest asset.
Flame Sword, power up!
In the brief moments Chang Shuangyue took to charge toward him, Wang Lan swiftly upgraded his Flame Sword to Silver 9.
As his Flame Sword was enhanced to the highest level possible for his current realm, an epiphany flowed through his mind.
A confident smile touched Wang Lan’s lips.
"What on earth is Wang Lan doing? He’s been pushed back so far, why isn’t he moving?" Wang Qianfeng asked, frowning.
"Who knows? Actually, there is one way to break through Chang Shuangyue’s defense: use the Purple Flame Sword!" He MingXue said in a low voice.
"Are you kidding me? You practiced the Flame Sword for seven years before mastering the Purple Flame Sword. Wang Lan has been training for two months at most. If he can master the Purple Flame Sword in such a short time, I’ll eat this coffee table!" Wang Qianfeng roared impatiently.
Wang Qianfeng was the type who detested unrealistic assumptions. Any suggestion or plan had to be within the realm of possibility. This applied to everyone.
You’re saying Wang Lan can master the Purple Flame Sword in two months? Why not just say he can master the Vermilion Bird Form in three years?
But on the screen, Wang Lan suddenly moved.
His hands transformed, and in an instant, two purple Flame Swords erupted from his palms—enchanting and dazzling.
Wang Qianfeng’s expression turned to stone. He stared with vacant eyes at the screen, at Wang Lan wielding the Purple Flame Sword, soaring high to confront Chang Shuangyue...
"So... how do you plan to eat that coffee table? Steamed? Braised? Or stir-fried?"

chapters.title: Chapter 88 Chang Shuangyue’s Demonization
chapters.content:
Chapter 88: Chapter 88 Chang Shuangyue’s Demonization
"Do you still have the face to mock me? Have you lived like a dog these past seven years? It took you seven years to master the Purple Flame Sword, and he did it in two months. If I were you, I would have already crashed into a wall and died," Wang Qianfeng quickly retorted.
"Me? I accepted my fate when Wang Lan learned the Flame Sword on the spot. Isn’t it nice to live happily? Why compare yourself to a prodigy? Remember Mr. Haoyue? He insisted on competing with the Flame Emperor, and what happened in the end? His belief was shattered, and he’s still in a state of seclusion."
At the martial arts competition arena, Wang Lan leaped forward, viciously plunging the twin Purple Flame Swords into Chang Shuangyue’s shoulders. Chang Shuangyue seemed to have unparalleled confidence in his defense, a faint, cold smile curling his lips as he aimed a claw toward Wang Lan’s shoulder.
PSCHT— Warm blood spurted, and both Wang Lan and Chang Shuangyue’s movements halted.
In an instant, dozens of cameras swiftly changed angles, broadcasting this frozen moment to the thousands of households watching their TVs.
Chang Shuangyue’s hand was only an inch from Wang Lan’s shoulder, but Wang Lan’s twin Flame Swords had already penetrated Chang Shuangyue’s defenses, stabbing into his shoulders—entering from the front and protruding from the back.
"AH—"
"Fuck, that strike was sharp."
"I fuckin’ didn’t even see what happened! Who can explain this to me?"ɪꜰ ʏᴏᴜ ᴡᴀɴᴛ ᴛᴏ ʀᴇᴀᴅ ᴍᴏʀᴇ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs, ᴘʟᴇᴀsᴇ ᴠɪsɪᴛ ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
"Explain my ass! Just watch the replay later. The Wolf King lives up to his name, still holding back a trump card. That purple flame... the legendary highest flame..."
"Upstairs, the legendary highest flame is the colorless flame, okay? Invisible and intangible, it kills in an instant."
"Can it still be called a flame if it’s colorless and formless? Idiot!"
"You fuckin’ moron? Flames are a manifestation of infrared radiation. Just because you can’t see the color doesn’t mean infrared radiation doesn’t exist! How did you even pass middle school? Trying to argue with me?"
"I have a primary school diploma, and you’re asking me about middle school? Is your brain damaged?"
"Big shot, I can’t afford to offend you. I’m out!"
In an instant, Wang Lan retracted his Flame Sword and once again delivered a powerful Three Strengths in a Fist punch to Chang Shuangyue’s chest.
BOOM—
With a loud bang, Chang Shuangyue’s body was flung high, falling backward. Wang Lan, however, also grimaced in pain at that moment.
Damn it, every time I use Three Strengths in a Fist with all my might, my hand bones feel like they’re shattering! What kind of freak was the ancient martial arts master who created this technique? Were their bones made of adamantium like Wolverine’s?
BOOM— Chang Shuangyue’s body crashed thunderously to the ground. Wang Lan immediately closed in, stepping on Chang Shuangyue’s chest with one foot and pressing the Purple Flame Sword to his throat.
AN UPROAR—
"He won!"
"Wolf’s might—"
"Wolf King’s dominance—"
The audience members slowly rose to their feet, clapping and cheering.
This battle was a feast for their eyes, utterly thrilling. They had witnessed Chang Shuangyue’s seemingly invincible posture firsthand, and Wang Lan’s dazzling display of Star Martial Skills had gotten their blood boiling. Moreover, every moment of these thrilling fights was a brush with death. It wasn’t like the last round, where a combatant who obviously could have finished with a final strike didn’t, and there was so much pointless posturing before releasing Star Martial Skills that it just seemed fake.
But in the end, Wang Lan’s demonstration of the Purple Flame Sword broke through Chang Shuangyue’s invincible defense—truly a turnaround from the brink.
At this moment, with Chang Shuangyue’s arms injured and the Wolf King’s Purple Flame Sword pressed against Chang Shuangyue’s throat, there was no further suspense as to who the champion of the Star Martial competition would be.
In the judges’ box, after a few referees nodded to each other, one stood up.
"After deliberation by our panel of judges, the champion of the third season Star Martial championship finale is..."
BOOM—
A loud explosion suddenly erupted in the center of the ring. Chang Shuangyue unleashed a terrifying Star Energy Fluctuation that shattered the cement floor beneath him.
In that instant, a sense of crisis flooded Wang Lan.
Wang Lan retreated in the blink of an eye, narrowly dodging the lethal strike of Chang Shuangyue’s approaching claw.
"I haven’t lost... How could I possibly lose... I haven’t lost yet—" Chang Shuangyue’s expression twisted into something even more ferocious, the skin on his body gradually turning from crimson to an inky black, as if stained.
"You deserve to die... I am going to kill you—"
"Contestant Chang Shuangyue, our panel of judges has already made a decision regarding the outcome. Please abide by our decision."
"Abide by it, my ass! What do you know about fighting? What do you understand about Star Martial Warriors? Are Star Martial Skills mere combat techniques? There’s only one standard for determining victory! The one who lives is the victor. The one who dies is the loser. This not only decides victory and defeat but also life and death!"
ROAR—
Suddenly, Chang Shuangyue tilted his head back and let out an earth-shattering roar. As he roared, sections of pitch-black carapace emerged all over his body. In almost an instant, Chang Shuangyue transformed from a man into an upright, insectoid monster.
"Come on with your Purple Flame Sword again... Try and see if it can break through my defense this time," Chang Shuangyue taunted with a cruel smile, raising his fist, now covered in sharp spikes.
"Magical Martial Artist!" Wang Lan shouted sternly. "Quickly evacuate the crowd! Everyone, evacuate!"
When Chang Shuangyue heard Wang Lan utter the term "Magical Martial Artist," he faltered for a moment, his expression drastically changing.
BOOM—
Wings sprouted from his back. He soared into the sky, breaking through the glass ceiling above and flying high into the air.
Meanwhile, the two people in Wang Qianfeng’s office watching the live broadcast sprang up the moment they saw Chang Shuangyue’s Demonization and rushed out the window, heading towards the Suzhou City TV station.
Wang Lan was stunned for half a second before his figure flashed, rushing towards the hole in the ceiling. He then turned into a fading afterimage, vanishing from everyone’s sight.
All of this happened so quickly that everyone was left dumbfounded.
「On the internet, there was dead silence for about ten seconds.」
"Fuck, what just happened?"
"Why did they all run away? Chang Shuangyue, what was that? Did an armored warrior just transform?"
"Why don’t you say it’s a Beetlemon digivolving?"
"This might not be simple. Chang Shuangyue fled in panic after transforming, and the Wolf King didn’t hesitate to chase after him. Maybe... there’s big news coming."
"Damn, this is explosive, really explosive!"
"So, who is the champion then?"
"Duh, who else could it be? Definitely the Wolf King—"
After his Demonization, Chang Shuangyue had grown wings, which caused considerable trouble for Wang Lan’s pursuit. Fortunately, perhaps due to his overly large size, Chang Shuangyue’s flying speed wasn’t too fast, and Wang Lan could faintly keep up from a distance.
Chang Shuangyue flew rapidly away from the scene of the disturbance towards the dense industrial zone. Between the city and the industrial area lay vast stretches of urban farmland.
Wang Lan had little Star Power left. Continuously using the Star Cloud Dance to travel, he could sustain it for at most another ten minutes. He didn’t know when the Tianjian Bureau’s reinforcements would arrive, and his cell phone was the only way to give his comrades his location. Therefore, Wang Lan had to cling tightly to Chang Shuangyue. If he lost him, finding him again would be incredibly difficult.
Do I have to use the Phoenix Form? I really don’t want to.
Suddenly, a wave of energy emerged, indistinct in the pitch-black night, yet Wang Lan instinctively sensed danger.
The energy vanished as quickly as it had appeared. Chang Shuangyue, high in the sky, suddenly split in two and fell. Wang Lan abruptly halted. In the open field, a high-speed train sped by in the distance.
A gentle breeze brushed Wang Lan’s cheeks. Far across the open fields, a humanoid Demon waited, its blood-red eyes fixed on him.
At its feet lay the neatly bisected corpse of Chang Shuangyue.
"Demon Clan!"
Wang Lan’s heart clenched.
A successfully demonized Chang Shuangyue had strength at least at the mid-Star Cloud Stage, possibly even late-stage. Yet this being instantly split him in two. So, the Magical Martial Artists appearing in Suzhou City must be connected to this Demon!
Phoenix Form, activate!
The space between Wang Lan’s eyebrows lit up instantly. The moment the red emblem appeared, he had already transformed into a streak of light, charging towards the Demon.
With a punch, his fist’s energy scorched the blistering air, creating a bright red pillar of flame. But the opponent easily dodged it, leaped into the sky, and with a flicker, vanished in an instant.
Even in Phoenix Form, I couldn’t stop him?
"Where do you think you’re going!" A streak of light cut across the sky where the Demon had vanished, but ultimately, nothing was left behind. At that moment, two figures appeared before Wang Lan.
Wang Lan deactivated the Phoenix Form. Its activation this time had been brief. Coupled with his vastly improved physical constitution, he avoided embarrassing himself, though his limbs still felt a little weak.
"He Lao’er, that must have been a real member of the Demon Clan, right?" Wang Qianfeng asked lightly, looking towards the direction where the Demon had disappeared.
"It must have been. Even Wang Lan in his Phoenix Form couldn’t capture that person..."
"Director Wang, Director He!" After recovering for a short while, Wang Lan approached the two and saluted.
"You did well to think of chasing after him immediately," Wang Qianfeng said, his expression as flat as ever, even when complimenting. To receive such praise from him was no small feat.
"Seeing the Magical Martial Artist transform, it was my duty as your subordinate to follow. However, the Magical Martial Artist was killed by a member of the Demon Clan, and I failed to prevent it in time. I am filled with guilt."
"Guilty, my ass! You’ve only been with the Tianjian Bureau for a few days?" He MingXue, who lacked Wang Qianfeng’s stoicism, laughed and cursed. "We owe you one this time. If it had been his precious Xu Shiyun, that youngster might have been done for here."
"I caught a glimpse of that Demon from afar. He originally intended to kill you. But you decisively activated the Phoenix Form and counter-attacked. Realizing he couldn’t dispose of you quickly, he fled. If anyone’s to blame, it should be us for not rushing here faster, for being just a second too late. Sigh..."
"Director Wang, Director He, I suspect there’s an organization leading these Magical Martial Artists. Their Demonization is likely related to the Demon Clan. There’s a Demon Clan spy lurking in Suzhou City."
"You encountered Magical Martial Artists in the trial zone?"
"Yes! But I didn’t realize it at the time, so I just thought he was an ordinary mutated Star Martial Warrior. It was only after discovering the Demon Clan base that the incident in the trial grounds was triggered."
"It seems the Demon Clan is plotting something big in the shadows!" Wang Qianfeng murmured to himself before looking up at Wang Lan. "The credit for discovering the Magical Martial Artist will go to you. But considering you have to go to school, involving you might not be appropriate..."
Wang Lan stepped forward, eagerly grasping Wang Qianfeng’s arm. "Please let me be involved, even if it’s just as an assistant!"
Now that I’ve stumbled upon the Demon Clan’s activities, how could I possibly miss out?
Winning a Star Martial Championship battle only yields a few skill points and a handful of experience points. How can that compare to the rewards from thwarting a Demon Clan conspiracy and securing a victory for humanity?
If I really miss this because of school, I’ll probably cry myself to sleep with regret!
"You’re still young. Your education should be your priority."
"Director Wang, I could actually take a leave of absence from school."
"Nonsense! In the Tianjian Bureau, who isn’t a graduate of a prestigious school? If you take a leave of absence, give me back your uniform! Also, I’m giving you a mission right now: you must get into one of the top four Star Martial Academies. If you don’t, I’ll personally thrash you!"
A notification suddenly chimed in his mind: *"Successfully completed the Star Martial Championship and earned your first championship title. Reward: 5,000 Experience Points, 500 Skill Points."*

chapters.title: Chapter 89: Subsequent Reactions
chapters.content:
Chapter 89: Chapter 89: Subsequent Reactions
"Director Wang, when you lured me into joining the Tianjian Bureau, you didn’t pitch it to me like this, did you?" Wang Lan felt it was necessary to make one more effort, his face full of grievance.
"You said I was a student, but first and foremost, a warrior..."
"Didn’t you just say I lured you?" Wang Qianfeng looked at Wang Lan with surprise, his eyes expressing disbelief at Wang Lan’s naiveté. "Now that you’re in my clutches, of course, the story changes."
"So you’ve completely dropped all pretense?" Wang Lan stared at Wang Qianfeng, his face like stone.
"What are you still doing here? Tomorrow is Monday, don’t you have school? The competition is over, and so is the mischief! Go back, sleep. Do what a student should do."
Wang Qianfeng chased him back from the suburbs, and by this time, the internet had already exploded.
The audience who watched the entire Star Martial Art Supremacy Competition final was ecstatic. The unexpected twists and turns in the finals far outshone the excitement of the competition itself.
Everyone had thought Xing Feng’s forfeit would be the climax, only to discover it was merely a prelude. In the end, Chang Shuangyue transformed into a giant beetle and soared into the sky, completely shattering the audience’s understanding of the world.
"Star Martial Warriors can transform like that?"
"Then, what about the other Star Martial Warriors? What are their transformed forms? Are there any roaring evil dragons? Any Angel forms?"
"The user above is way too into anime! Transformation, my ass! It’s obvious Chang Shuangyue has issues. If there was nothing wrong with his transformation, why the hell would he run? Why would the Wolf King chase him?"
"Could that Chang Shuangyue... be a member of the legendary Demon Clan?"
"The Wolf King seemed to say something at the end, but it was too noisy to hear clearly. But it’s certain that the Wolf King said something that made Chang Shuangyue choose to flee. Damn it, why did the Wolf King wear a mask? Even if we wanted to lip-read, we couldn’t."
"Wait for the official announcement! Leave messages for the officials!"
"Official announcements are crap! Look, they just declared Wolf the champion of the Star Martial Art Supremacy Competition and didn’t say a single word about Chang Shuangyue. They must have been issued a gag order."Googlᴇ search NovᴇlFirenᴇt
"We want to know the truth!"
"Citizens of Jade Country have the right to know the truth—"
In contrast to the netizens howling online, major media outlets in Suzhou City took direct action, scrambling with cameras and rushing to the Suzhou City TV Station in their news vans.
What? Suzhou City TV is the big boss of Suzhou media? So what? Careful about being blacklisted? Blacklist my ass! Fortune favors the bold; the timid starve. Whoever snags the first news scoop, even if they get blacklisted, it’s worth it!
Outside the Suzhou City TV Station, dozens of media outlets had gathered. These included reporters chasing headlines for various platforms, news websites, and even live streamers from different broadcasting sites.
"Ladies and gentlemen, please, quiet down! Regarding the incident during tonight’s Star Martial Art Supremacy Competition, we are also unaware of the full details and are currently investigating. Please remain calm and exercise restraint. We will make a public announcement to the entire city once the investigation is clear..."
"I call bullshit! You think we’re greenhorns? We used to pull the same stunts on the public!"
"Exactly! Did you know about this beforehand? Was Chang Shuangyue using banned substances?"
"With such a major incident happening in plain sight, you have to give us some explanation, right?"
Amid the noisy commotion, a black sedan pulled up outside the TV station.
Wang Qianfeng stepped out of the car. He frowned slightly, looking at the besieged TV station. "Call their superiors. Within ten minutes, I don’t want to see anyone still asking about this."
"Yes, sir!"
The Tianjian Bureau was an enigmatic department in the eyes of the public, yet it wielded absolute power within its jurisdiction. Directly subordinate to the Ministry of Defense, it didn’t fall under local government control. Sometimes, local governments even had to cooperate unconditionally with the Bureau’s operations.
This night was lively; for many, it was a sleepless one. Work tomorrow? Screw work! With the fires of gossip burning so fiercely, who could think about work now?
"Fuck, my post was deleted!"
"Fuck, the authorities have stepped in."
"Damn it, I’ve been warned! One more post, and they’ll ’check my water meter’... Wait, the ’water meter reader’ is here. I’m going to open the door. Brothers-in-arms, remember to send me food in prison!"
"Farewell, brother upstairs! Huh? Who’s knocking so late?"
"A moment of silence for our two fallen comrades upstairs."
"..."
Wang Lan had a good night’s sleep. He woke up refreshed, brushed his teeth, washed his face, and got ready for school.
The Star Martial Art Supremacy Competition had concluded. This competition, which lasted nearly half a month, had allowed Wang Lan to gain a character level and earn just over a thousand skill points. He spent four hundred skill points to improve his Flame Sword and used the remaining six hundred to enhance his Basic Combat, Basic Body Skill, Basic Swordsmanship, and the Star Cloud Sword Dance.
His strength had greatly increased, but skill points were still incredibly scarce.
Now, Wang Lan’s desire for skill points far outweighed his desire for character levels. Back then, it had only taken him half a month to advance from an awakened Star Martial Warrior to the Star Shine Stage. Yet now, two months had passed, and he still hadn’t broken through from the Star Shine Stage to the Star Cloud Stage.
Am I becoming too complacent?
Wang Lan reflected, staring at himself in the mirror while brushing his teeth.
"Do you think I can break through to the Star Cloud Stage before the end of this semester?"
CRACK—
With a crisp sound, the perfectly fine mirror suddenly fractured. Wang Lan stared at it in astonishment.
It must be the sudden cold snap—the mirror couldn’t withstand the thermal expansion and contraction...
「Monday」
The bus was packed again.
Wang Lan walked to school, carrying his shoulder bag. When he returned to his classroom, it was in an uproar, with students clustered in groups, engaged in heated discussions.
"Lanzi, Lanzi, did you watch yesterday’s Star Martial Art Supremacy Competition?" Xu Xiangwen asked excitedly, throwing an arm around Wang Lan’s shoulder.
"Watched... watched a bit."
"Don’t you think Chang Shuangyue’s transformation at the end felt kind of familiar?"
Wang Lan certainly understood Xu Xiangwen’s meaning and nodded immediately.
"It’s like that person we encountered in the trial grounds during summer vacation. They’re probably the same type of Star Martial Warrior."
"See? I wasn’t talking nonsense! This Chang Shuangyue is definitely a Body Mutation Type Star Martial Warrior. If Body Mutation Types can transform into a Beastman Form, why can’t they transform into an insectoid form? Chang Shuangyue isn’t the first, nor is he the only one."
"Impossible! Beastification has occurred many times among Star Martial Warriors throughout history, but they’ve always turned into wolves, leopards, and the like—never insects. There must be something wrong with Chang Shuangyue’s mutation; otherwise, why would he run? And why would the Wolf King give chase?"
Only then did Wang Lan understand what his classmates were arguing about.
"Wang Lan, why don’t you explain it?" Jiang Xinyu suddenly asked, looking up. Her tone implied Wang Lan knew the real story.
"Well... I’m not entirely sure about the specifics, so it’s hard to say definitively, but we can analyze it.
"What’s the principle behind human Star Martial Warrior mutations? Essentially, it’s the presence of animal genes in their genetic code. Take humans and mice, for example. Despite their vastly different appearances, their genes are about ninety percent similar. This is a prerequisite.
"Insects already existed when human ancestors were still fish. By that calculation, humans and insects are genetically separated by the evolutionary distance equivalent to that of fish. In other words, humans and insects have been distinct species since the Cambrian explosion.
"We’re people of a new age; we must believe in science. It would be easier for us to mutate into a fish than an insect. If a human possesses insect genetic codes, I’d say that person isn’t entirely human."
"Is that so?" Xu Xiangwen looked unconvinced. "But isn’t it said that all life originates from a single point?"
"Correct. All life originates from a single point—organic matter. That’s why all living things decompose into organic matter after death. But humans and insects diverged very early on.
"If you trace our lineage back, all Gnathostomata Mammals belong to one family, all amniotes share a common ancestor, and all terrestrial vertebrates evolved from a fish that first ventured onto land.
"Insects, however, are arthropods... For a human to mutate into an insect would mean crossing the boundaries of dozens of biological classes. Based on the principle of mutating towards the closest genetic match, human Star Martial Warrior mutations generally don’t extend beyond Gnathostomata Mammals.
"Exceeding that is an aberration! Jumping dozens of classes? That’s pure fantasy."
"But back at the trial grounds, that’s not what you said, was it?" Xu Xiangwen looked confused. Though reluctant to agree, Wang Lan’s reputation as an academic prodigy, coupled with his logical arguments, made him hard to refute.
"Hmm, after we got back, I thought it was suspicious, so I looked into it. Anyway, theoretically, humans can’t exhibit arthropod mutation traits. There’s definitely something wrong with this Chang Shuangyue."
As the class bell rang, the discussion came to an end.
「At noon」
The four of them gathered on the rooftop.
Wang Lan took out his Tianjian Bureau phone to check the latest on the investigation into Magical Martial Artists. As a registered member of the Tianjian Bureau, Wang Lan had access to information within his clearance level.
The file on Chang Shuangyue stated that he had once been involved in pioneering efforts in the Northwest. He returned to Suzhou City two years ago and subsequently opened a martial arts school to teach students. He wasn’t particularly prominent, and the general impression among his students and their parents was that he had a mild temperament.
Mild-tempered? Do these students and parents have a different definition of ’mild’? Casually crushing legs and twisting people into pretzels—is that their idea of a loving touch?
Chang Shuangyue had a sister, Chang Yu, an ordinary person working as a nurse at Ren’ai Hospital. Last night, his sister was on the night shift. The Tianjian Bureau’s investigation determined that Chang Yu was unaware of the changes in Chang Shuangyue. She also revealed that her brother’s personality had begun to turn strange and irritable about six months ago.
Furthermore, they had been in less frequent contact. The Tianjian Bureau concluded that Chang Shuangyue’s Demonization began about six months ago. His social circle was relatively simple, consisting of a few friends, his students, and their parents.
In short, all leads for tracing Chang Shuangyue... had dried up!
Dried up?
Wang Lan found it hard to believe the conclusion posted on the Tianjian Bureau’s information bulletin.
This is the Tianjian Bureau, for crying out loud! Even if you can’t divine heavenly secrets with a snap of your fingers, you’re giving up after just one night? Can’t you even try to investigate further?
"So... what’s really going on with Chang Shuangyue? It was too crowded and noisy in the classroom, so I didn’t ask then," Jiang Xinyu finally asked.
"It’s nothing much," Wang Lan replied.
"Then why did you chase after him?" Jiang Xinyu pressed.
"Hmm... It’s better if you don’t know," Wang Lan said, looking up at Jiang Xinyu’s profile.
"Alright, I understand," Jiang Xinyu replied.
"Feiyu, what do you think Lanzi and Jiang Xinyu are whispering about?" Xu Xiangwen asked.
"If I were you, I wouldn’t look, and I certainly wouldn’t ask," Gong Feiyu replied.
"But I’m curious! Aren’t you? Do you think those two... Ouch, why is my butt so cold?" Xu Xiangwen exclaimed.
"It’s frozen," Gong Feiyu said nonchalantly, glancing over.

chapters.title: Chapter 90 I Love Learning
chapters.content:
Chapter 90: Chapter 90 I Love Learning
Amidst the total network lockdown, the fervor surrounding the Star Martial Competition gradually cooled. The enthusiasm for gossip among the citizens of Suzhou City rarely lasted long.
For the students of Class One, Grade Three at the Star Martial Arts Campus, the current topic of discussion was where to go for the National Day holiday.
That’s right, National Day! November 1st.
Two hundred years ago, the last emperor of Jade Country issued his final sacred decree: to rally the entire world against the Demon Clan’s invasion. Following this declaration, he announced his abdication and personally handed the Jade Seal, a symbol of supreme imperial power, to the six Cabinet Ministers of that time.
From that moment, Jade Country completed its transition from an absolute monarchy to a democratic republic. Representatives elected from across the nation supervised the government and appointed capable individuals to key positions. The people truly became the masters of their country.
Therefore, every year on November 1st, Jade Country celebrated its National Day with a seven-day mega holiday, comparable to the New Year’s Spring Festival.
Students, in particular, had a unique obsession with holidays. It might be more accurate to call it a students’ holiday rather than a public one. For a large segment of the working class, holidays without income were even more exhausting than workdays—so what was the point?
"Lanzi!" Before school ended, Xu Xiangwen approached Wang Lan. "How do you plan to spend the seven days of National Day?"
Me?
Wang Lan was pondering just that.
Wang Lan was born in the Year of the Dragon, but sometimes he felt he should have been born in the Year of the Rat—specifically, a hamster. A strong sense of crisis was embedded in his character, a kind of phobia about food shortages and empty granaries.
In his previous life, only when he saw at least a five-figure balance in his bank account could he sleep peacefully. Otherwise, he would be anxious, always worrying about what to do if a day came when he needed money but had none.
When it came to work plans, he liked to have everything for the next three months arranged clearly and well in advance.
In this life, he didn’t lack money. His study plan had always been fully booked. If not for that damned system, Wang Lan might have taken advantage of the long holiday for a spontaneous trip.
But... with this system, my skill points are insufficient, my level is insufficient, and this fear of insufficient strength is erupting all over again. It hasn’t even been ten days since I reaped rewards from the Star Martial Competition, and I feel like I’m wasting my life like a salted fish. This holiday, why not find something to do? I should check if the Tianjian Bureau has any short-term tasks. The rewards might be small, but it’s still something. In terms of strength, I consider myself a master at the Star Shine Stage. If all else fails, there’s still the Phoenix form, right? Strength isn’t an issue.
"Hey? Aren’t you going to say something?" Xu Xiangwen urged impatiently, having waited for a while without an answer from Wang Lan.
"For now... I don’t have any solid plans. What’s up?"
"Xinyu said a new Universal Amusement Park has opened in Modu City, right? It’s reportedly the largest amusement park in the country right now. A few of us are thinking of going. Wanna come have some fun?"
"During National Day? And at the newly opened Universal Amusement Park? Are you guys going to have fun or to be turned into dumpling filling? Won’t you get crushed to death?"
"Nonsense! In this day and age, money paves the way; without money, you hit red lights everywhere. If it’s crowded, can’t we just use the VIP entrance?"
"People who go to the Universal Amusement Park at that time are usually wealthy. I’m afraid even the VIP line will be congested."
"Then we’ll go VVIP!" Jiang Xinyu’s voice rang out coldly. "You’re a grown man, why the dilly-dallying? Are you going or not? Just say it."
"Not going!" Wang Lan simply shook his head.
This answer almost made Xu Xiangwen stumble.
Lanzi, you’re a true man! Jiang Xinyu herself invited you, and you rejected her so bluntly?
"Why not?"
"Compared to going out... I prefer studying." A naive and gentle smile appeared on Wang Lan’s face.
This made Xu Xiangwen stare in amazement, and he couldn’t help but give a thumbs-up. "Bro, you’re solid!"
"If you’re not going, forget it. I’ll take Xincheng instead."
"Right! I have an apartment in Modu City. I’ll send you the address and the passcode later; you can stay there. Don’t waste money on some ridiculously expensive hotel," Wang Lan said with a sincere look on his face.
"Why should you care?" Jiang Xinyu rolled her eyes and stopped paying attention to Wang Lan.
"What’s with her?" Wang Lan, completely clueless the whole time, turned and asked Xu Xiangwen.
"Nothing... nothing... Lanzi, as long as you’re happy."
When school let out, perhaps due to the upcoming holiday, the students leaving the campus were in exceptionally high spirits. All their discussions revolved around where to go and what to do for fun.
Kids these days, they just don’t understand the importance of prioritizing their studies. Playing? That’s just a waste of youth.
Wang Lan looked down on such an attitude.
After returning home and ordering takeout, Wang Lan sat on his bed, scrolling through his phone. He logged into the Tianjian Bureau’s internal network page, searching for tasks he could accept.
In fact, there was an ongoing task in Wang Lan’s system. That task had appeared after Wang Qianfeng ordered him to get into one of the top four Star Martial Academies. Clearly, it was a long-term task.
The Tianjian Bureau’s records showed quite a few tasks, but they were all marked as completed. Scrolling through the task list from top to bottom, he saw that every task was either already taken or completed.
Is the Tianjian Bureau’s efficiency really this high?
Wang Lan clicked on one of these completed tasks. Hmm, Lige.
The next one, Lige.
The one after that, still freaking Lige.
After flipping through seven or eight tasks, he finally found one that wasn’t Lige, but the very next one was Lige again.
Flaunting task completion like this... wouldn’t he get beaten up by his colleagues?
