"If you hadn’t beaten me so comprehensively that I couldn’t fight back, how could I be so sure? But no worries, this can’t be rushed. At least, you’ve now overcome your psychological block, and your combat strength should be enough to rank in the top ten in the class."
"Thank you," Xie Sisi said earnestly.
"No need to thank me. I’ve also gained from fighting you."
Wang Lan wasn’t being insincere; he genuinely felt this way. Although Xie Sisi initially wasn’t a match for him at all and couldn’t exert any pressure, Wang Lan used the opportunity to refine his own combat techniques, eliminating unnecessary moves and pointless actions.
This kind of reflection wasn’t possible when sparring with an equally skilled opponent.
Over these ten days, Wang Lan’s movements became swifter and his techniques more ruthless. The most direct manifestation of this was Mingyue Wucheng getting beaten by Wang Lan so badly that he wailed, calling Wang Lan a monster and claiming his strength had doubled.
"Then..." Xie Sisi sat up and leaned slightly towards Wang Lan. "Can I come to practice with you again tomorrow?"
"Eh? Why would you ask that? Even though your combat skills have improved greatly, you are still far from competent."
"Really?" Joy sparked in Xie Sisi’s eyes.
"Have you practiced sword skill?"
"Mr. Liu taught me, and I also practice it often."
"Rest for a while, and then we’ll move on to sword skill training."
"Yes, tomorrow is the end-of-month test... For the first time, I’m actually looking forward to the end-of-month combat test," Xie Sisi said, looking up, her eyes watery.
In the past, merely hearing about the end-of-month combat test always cast a shadow over her. Xie Sisi’s academic performance was outstanding, and her Star Martial Art level wasn’t low, but her combat grades were severely lacking. She was basically at the bottom of the class.
No matter how hard she tried, she just couldn’t perform well during tests.
But now, Xie Sisi had finally shed the gloom and could truly hold her head high for once.
"Rest well! Now, take a practice sword."
"Okay!"
Xie Sisi overcame her psychological hurdles, improving not only her bare-handed combat strength but also unleashing her Close Combat Sword Skill. However, it seemed her training in sword skill was insufficient; her level couldn’t compare to her hand-to-hand combat.
She still had to practice!
Today, the weather was clear and sunny, without a cloud in sight.
In this rare good weather, Liu Jie decided to hold the end-of-month practical assessment on the field.
"Students, another month is about to pass. There’s less than a month until winter break. Five months until the senior high provincial martial arts competition, and six months until your college entrance exam."
"Time flies quickly. It seems as if last month’s assessment was just yesterday. I don’t know if you all feel the same. Time is always merciless. All a teacher can do is try their hardest to help you improve as quickly as possible."
"But how much you can improve is up to you."
"This time, for the group practice, I will let you choose your own partners. I will draw names at random, and then you can choose your opponents for the practical combat assessment."
"Now, I’ll start calling names. Jiang Xinyu!"Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
Jiang Xinyu stood up and went into the arena. "Wang Lan, please teach me."
Jiang Xinyu called out Wang Lan’s name directly, which was something he had expected.
Defeating Wang Lan had seemingly become Jiang Xinyu’s obsession. Ever since Wang Lan had joined Star Martial Art Senior Year Class One, he experienced an initial period of discomfort. This gave Jiang Xinyu a chance to turn the tables. However, by the second half of the first semester, Wang Lan had once again come to dominate the entire class with absolute superiority.
In academic tests, Wang Lan was always the top scorer. As for combat assessments, Wang Lan could handle Jiang Xinyu and Mingyue Wucheng’s tag-team onslaught all by himself.
Yet, to the rest of the class, Wang Lan’s true combat strength might not even qualify for the top five. However, Jiang Xinyu knew that even if she used her Star Martial Skills, she might not be able to defeat him.
This was because Wang Lan was, in fact, the Wolf King—the champion of the Star Martial Warrior Tournament’s third season, whose popularity hadn’t diminished even after more than a month.
Over the past month, the outside world had persistently tried to discover the Wolf King’s true identity. Several renowned detective agencies in the city were even hired for the task. Unfortunately, the Wolf King’s identity remained unconfirmed.
A few imposters were also exposed after briefly deceiving the public.
"Jiang Xinyu, please teach me."
"Wang Lan, please teach me."
There was no doubt about Jiang Xinyu’s strength in hand-to-hand fighting. She had good conditions and talent. The only thing she lacked was a ’cheat’ like Wang Lan’s.
Xie Sisi watched Wang Lan and Jiang Xinyu’s spar without blinking. She used to understand their moves, but her current understanding was different.
She compared herself with Jiang Xinyu and, to her dismay, found that her supposedly transformed hand-to-hand combat strength still fell far short of Jiang Xinyu’s.
If Wang Lan knew what Xie Sisi was thinking, he would probably want to give her another serious beating. How inflated had her ego become? She even dared to compare herself with Jiang Xinyu! Wang Lan himself had to be extremely cautious when sparring with Jiang Xinyu. The slightest carelessness could lead to his defeat.
For Xie Sisi to defeat Jiang Xinyu, she would either need to awaken her untriggered Star Power synchronization ability or let her other self emerge.
In a high-level contest, it wasn’t just about skill. It was also about who made the first mistake.
Jiang Xinyu grew impatient, allowing Wang Lan to catch a fleeting gap in her defense. He seized her wrist, broke through her guard, and stopped a knife-hand strike right in front of her face.
The match was over.
"Next up, Mingyue Wucheng."
"Forget it. I was going to pick Wang Lan, but Jiang Xinyu beat me to it. So then, Gong Feiyu, shall we have a go?"
"Sure!"
Within less than half an hour, six groups of students had completed the assessment. Although Liu Jie maintained a stern expression throughout, he was quite satisfied deep down.
In the latter half of the semester, Liu Jie had really pushed the students hard. His training regimen for Class One was much more intense than for other senior classes.
While harsh, the results were indeed significant. Since the midpoint of the semester, the students’ practical combat scores had soared. If Class One’s bare-handed combat performance had been about the same as other classes in the first half of the semester, Liu Jie now estimated they were at least a full level higher.
Reduce their load? You must be joking. They are warriors destined for the battlefield. If we don’t apply pressure, who will be responsible if they die later in battle?
"Next, Xie Sisi!"
When Xie Sisi’s name was called, Liu Jie couldn’t help but frown.
Teachers naturally favor students with good grades and dislike underperformers. But Liu Jie just couldn’t bring himself to dislike Xie Sisi.
In Liu Jie’s eyes, Xie Sisi was almost the perfect student: obedient, clever, studious, attractive, and gentle. But why, then, were her practical combat grades so poor?
Such a temperament, in Liu Jie’s eyes, was simply not suited to becoming a Star Martial Warrior. He even considered having a talk with Xie Sisi, suggesting she give up on becoming one.
But such words would have been too cruel for a student, so Liu Jie never brought himself to say them.
Xie Sisi stood up, smiling as she looked around. "Song Bo, please teach me."

chapters.title: Chapter 117: The enemy won’t die, the attack continues
chapters.content:
Chapter 117: Chapter 117: The enemy won’t die, the attack continues
The words had barely left her lips when the training field fell silent in an instant.
Liu Jie’s expression was one of astonishment, and he rubbed his ears as if he had misheard. "Xie Sisi, what did you just say?"
"Mr. Liu, I would like to challenge Song Bo," she said.
Song Bo, sitting among the crowd, had been keeping a somewhat low profile recently. Ever since Mingyue Wucheng had warned him last time, he had even gone to Duan Ziqi to complain, hoping Duan Ziqi would back him up.
But the response Song Bo received had chilled him to the bone.
Mingyue Wucheng hadn’t been exaggerating. In Class One, there were at least five people whose strength was not inferior to Song Bo’s.
At first, Song Bo didn’t understand what that meant, but he grasped it after Duan Ziqi’s explanation.
In Suzhou No.1 Middle School’s Star Martial Arts Campus, Duan Ziqi ranked in the top three of the senior year.
This was a fact.
But did this ranking represent the true strength hierarchy? Obviously not. Some students were very low-key, like those from Star Martial Art families. They had their families as backing and possessed resources unimaginable to ordinary students.
Even which university they would attend and where they would work after graduation had been meticulously arranged since their birth.
Understanding this, Song Bo kept a low profile. Aside from whispering with his group of four, he dared not speak loudly all day.
But does being low-key mean anyone can just step on you? Xie Sisi, don’t you have any idea about your own combat level? Is it just because you’ve gotten close to Jiang Xinyu and her three companions recently? Because your relationship has improved? Now even you dare to step on my face?
Song Bo was furious, absolutely enraged.
So, three seconds after Xie Sisi finished speaking, Song Bo shot to his feet with a WHOOSH.
"Since the class president has called me out, I will naturally oblige."
"Wait... Xie Sisi, wouldn’t it be better to choose another female student? After all, it’s somewhat inconvenient for male and female students to fight," Mr. Liu interjected.
This was pure nonsense. Liu Jie had been teaching Class One for nearly two and a half years; when had he ever cared about this? It was only after Xie Sisi was accidentally injured by Song Bo that Liu Jie had started assigning opponents more carefully, right?
Besides, was there really a distinction between men and women in the world of Star Martial Warriors? No, they were all comrades, brothers and sisters in arms.
There was even a story, almost a meme, that had circulated online from the Pioneering Legion. After a bitter battle, only two Star Martial Warriors remained. One of them was critically injured and might not survive to return to base.
The only one unscathed was a female warrior. She asked her injured comrade if he had any unfulfilled wishes. He replied that he was the only son in his family and couldn’t bear the thought of his lineage ending with his death.
Without hesitation, the female warrior took him then and there. Upon returning, she used IVF, and eight months later, bore a child for her comrade. This news shook Jade Country. When asked about it later, the female warrior pointed to the C-section scar on her abdomen and declared calmly, "For a brother, I’d go through fire and water."
On the battlefield, who cared about propriety between men and women? Survival came first.
So, Liu Jie’s words were clearly just an excuse.
"Let’s stick with Song Bo. Since that incident, he has been carrying a deep sense of guilt and was so troubled he couldn’t speak to me for a long time. As class president, I have a duty to guide my classmates. Another fight will resolve Song Bo’s psychological barriers."
Hearing this, Liu Jie immediately rolled his eyes.
You’re the one holding a grudge, aren’t you? And you know perfectly well why Song Bo has been avoiding you, right?
But since Xie Sisi was insistent, Liu Jie couldn’t say much. He could only stand as close as possible to the combat circle, ready to intervene at the slightest sign of trouble.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
"Monthly assessment, Xie Sisi versus Song Bo. Begin!"
The words were barely out of his mouth when Xie Sisi moved. She moved with incredible speed, like a car zooming past.
Everyone had witnessed Xie Sisi’s strength. Yet, for the past half month, she had merely sat aside every afternoon, watching Wang Lan dominate Mingyue Wucheng and Jiang Xinyu in spars.
Everyone thought Xie Sisi had given up on herself.
But Xie Sisi knew such sparring was useless for her. Only Wang Lan’s style of attack, a relentless barrage measured in moments, could help her overcome her psychological barriers.
Now that her psychological barriers were overcome, her strength instantly returned to its normal level.
While Wang Lan felt this was far from Xie Sisi’s true limit, for her, it was enough. All those years of grueling, almost self-destructive training shouldn’t have resulted in such pitiful strength.
In that moment, Xie Sisi’s eyes were incredibly sharp as she instantly charged in front of Song Bo.
One punch, aimed squarely at his face.
This was what Wang Lan had taught her: always aim for vital points with the first strike. And a person’s head was the most obvious and easiest vital point to target.
Xie Sisi’s speed caught Song Bo completely off guard; he was still in a daze.
By the time he realized he needed to block, her fist had already viciously struck his nose.
Instantly, an indescribable, searing pain shot through him, like biting into a mouthful of wasabi that went straight to his brain.
At that moment, Song Bo forgot everything around him; his consciousness was filled with nothing but pain.
But Xie Sisi’s attack was far from over; she steadfastly implemented Wang Lan’s combat philosophy: never stop attacking until the enemy is down. Even if they fall, the assault must continue.
Xie Sisi’s strength was honed by years of carrying weights and her painstaking daily practice of striking concrete blocks. As a result, she possessed a speed and power with her fists that none of her classmates could have imagined.
In an instant, Xie Sisi’s hands became a blur to Liu Jie. Her countless punches, like a torrent of Starlight, rained down on Song Bo. Song Bo stood rooted to the spot, trembling for a full thirty seconds as if being riddled by machine-gun fire.
"Stop— stop—" Liu Jie finally reacted and hastily called for a halt.
Xie Sisi instantly stopped her attack and rapidly retreated three meters from Song Bo, her arms raised in a defensive stance.
What kind of defense is that?!
At that moment, a wild beast seemed to roar within Liu Jie’s heart.
Song Bo has been beaten by you into a state of Soul Out of Body; in his current condition, how could he possibly counterattack?
Sure enough, Song Bo struggled to move his face, swollen like a pig’s head, staggered a step forward, and then pitched straight down. He fell face-first, a fall that had all the tragic grandeur of a hero meeting his end.
If his body hadn’t been twitching, the scene might have even been picturesque.
"What happened? What’s going on?" Liu Jie hollered twice in succession.
The surrounding students stared with wide, terrified eyes.
They wanted to know what was going on too.
Has the world turned upside down? Has she become some kind of spirit? A magical girl transformation! Is this the same class president they remembered, the one who couldn’t take a single hit? Is this still the class president who was always defeated in one move? This is too intense! But... Xie Sisi wasn’t like this half a month ago, was she? Hadn’t she given up on herself for the past half month? Hadn’t she skipped all combat practice during that time? What in the world is going on?
"Xie Sisi, what happened to you?" Liu Jie asked with a furrowed brow.
"Report, Teacher, I..." Xie Sisi faltered, her usual nervousness kicking in. "I didn’t mean to... Teacher, you taught me that the best defense is a good offense. So, I was merely attacking."
Attacking? Is this what she calls attacking?
Liu Jie wondered if Xie Sisi truly understood the difference between attacking and simply mauling someone.
Then again, after careful consideration, brawling and attacking... there isn’t much of a difference, is there?
"Why didn’t you stop after your attack landed? You continued attacking for thirty seconds! Continuing to attack after Song Bo had lost the ability to fight back constitutes intentional injury."
"I’m sorry... I... I didn’t know if Song Bo had lost the ability to fight back, so... as long as Song Bo hadn’t fallen, I couldn’t stop my attacks."
Her explanation... doesn’t seem to have any loopholes... But... your angles of attack were just too good, weren’t they? You didn’t hit anywhere else, just kept aiming for the head. From a physics standpoint, with such rapid, fragmented attacks to the head, you could beat someone to death, and they might not even fall over. The vectors of force weren’t aimed at knocking him down.
"Wang Lan—"
"Present!"
"Treat Song Bo." Wang Lan wouldn’t refuse such a request. If Song Bo were truly seriously injured, Xie Sisi would be in trouble too.
However, I hadn’t expected the seemingly innocent and harmless Xie Sisi to harbor such cunning thoughts. The thing was, it was clearly intentional, yet she could stare at Mr. Liu with such innocent eyes that he was left speechless. I’ll never believe in truly innocent girls again. Innocent? What a load of crap!
"Next pair—"
Wang Lan’s healing abilities were tailor-made for the battlefield; Song Bo’s injuries were a trivial matter for him.
Once the bruises on his face vanished, Song Bo was once again a handsome man with sharp, striking eyebrows.
Wang Lan lightly tapped Song Bo’s cheeks. "Song Bo, wake up."
"Ah? What just happened? Where am I... What’s today’s date?"
"Hahaha..." A burst of laughter erupted from the students.
"Wang Lan, what’s wrong with Song Bo? He hasn’t... developed a problem up here, has he?" Liu Jie asked, pointing to his own head.
"Don’t worry, Teacher. It’s temporary amnesia from the heavy blows to his head. He’ll remember everything shortly."
The subsequent sparring matches passed without any heart-stopping moments, but Xie Sisi’s sudden, dramatic improvement continued to weigh on Liu Jie’s mind.
"Xie Sisi." After the exam, Class One began their routine physical training. Liu Jie called Xie Sisi over to ask about her situation. Initially, Xie Sisi kept her head down and said nothing. It wasn’t until Wang Lan noticed her state that he approached Liu Jie to explain.
"I see..." Liu Jie had a sudden realization. "Indeed, finding the right method for each individual is crucial. The sparring method you described suits Xie Sisi, which explains her rapid improvement in such a short period."
"Mr. Liu, I believe my method is suitable for all students. I was trained this way myself. You and Master Huang were comrades-in-arms; you should know what he’s like."
"Huang Feilong’s old nickname was ’The Madman.’ Whether he was killing Exotic Beasts or training team members, his attacks were always frenzied."
"Teacher, I think we can promote this method to the entire class. I may not be the most talented, but I’m willing to step up and assist you in training these students. For future combat practice, we can go by student numbers, and I’ll spar with every classmate in turn..."
Wang Lan’s intentions were once again laid bare before Liu Jie.
"Get lost! If I were to use such a brutal method on my students, I’d be forced to pack my bags and leave by tomorrow. This kind of sparring demands immense mental fortitude and a very close bond between partners. The slightest misstep could turn these training sessions into bitter personal vendettas. You think I don’t know that? Only that madman Huang Feilong would dare to train you that way."

chapters.title: Chapter 118: Have the governor and conception vessels been opened?
chapters.content:
Chapter 118: Chapter 118: Have the governor and conception vessels been opened?
The exam was over, and the next day was the weekend.
Wang Lan and Xie Sisi left home one after another, pretending not to know each other. Wang Lan would return home first, while Xie Sisi would later take a bus to Wang Lan’s house for their practice session.
Neither of them noticed, however, that not far behind them, a pair of eyes narrowed slightly.
"Miss, Miss, what are you looking at?"
"There’s something fishy going on!"
"What?"
"Nothing. Go on back by yourself; I’ll return home later tonight."
"This... is that alright?"
"I’ll call my dad. It’s fine."
"Well... Miss, please be careful. Call me when you need me to pick you up."
"Mhm!"
Xie Sisi’s talent wasn’t bad. Although she had just begun learning the sword skill, there were actually few moves. A blade is essentially an extension of the arm; it’s even possible to wield a blade using general combat techniques.
So, after three days of practicing the sword skill, Wang Lan felt that Xie Sisi was ready for the final step of her training.
Overcoming the fear of death!
This step was crucial for a Star Martial Warrior. Everyone understood its importance, yet few managed to overcome this fear before their first true battle. The reason was simple: it was too dangerous.
Wielding a real sword and slashing away! Who could guarantee they could hold back? And if one truly held back, the genuine sensation of death would be lost.
But this wasn’t a difficult problem for Wang Lan. With his healing ability, he seemed naturally suited to helping others overcome this. As long as someone wasn’t killed instantly, Wang Lan could restore them to full health with his healing skills.
He was a Silver-rank, level 9 healer—a Battlefield Resurrection Master.
However, the first step to overcoming the fear of death was to conquer one’s own heart. If one’s heart resisted the training, it would be ineffective.
Xie Sisi held a real sword, her fingers white from gripping the hilt so tightly. The tip of the blade hung by her side, trembling incessantly.
"Xie Sisi, at this point, you need to overcome this yourself," Wang Lan said. "A real sword is like a practice sword. You can fight me evenly with a practice sword, so you can do the same with a real one."
"But a real sword is still a real sword—it can kill."
"With a practice sword in your hands, you feel no fear, so you can exert your normal strength. Using a real sword, however, puts you in a completely different state of mind."
"Many people don’t understand this difference even when they step onto a real battlefield. They always think that with their abilities, they won’t die at the hands of Starlight-level Exotic Beasts. But when they actually see the Exotic Beasts charging, they get so scared they freeze up like a log."
"Therefore, this is a psychological barrier that every warrior must overcome. You’ve already successfully overcome one psychological barrier. Having conquered that, the fear of death shouldn’t be too difficult for you, should it?"
"I..." Xie Sisi clenched her jaw, her hand still trembling.
This was because, at that moment, Wang Lan was truly emitting a murderous intent.
The Wang Lan before her now was not the same rookie from the Ring City Viaduct Secret Realm; he was a veteran who had experienced many battles. The killing intent he exuded could instantly make an opponent feel a tangible murderous aura.
"I... I know. Wang Lan, attack me," Xie Sisi finally said.
No sooner had her words fallen than Wang Lan’s figure became a streak of light, appearing before Xie Sisi in an instant, his sword slashing viciously toward her head.
At that moment, Xie Sisi thought she was truly dead.
The blade stopped before Xie Sisi’s forehead, less than three centimeters away.
Xie Sisi didn’t move an inch.
Her eyes were fixed on Wang Lan.
CLANG—
The sword in her hand fell to the ground.
Wang Lan frowned. Xie Sisi’s face was pale, and large beads of cold sweat trickled down her forehead.
"Xie Sisi, are you okay? Shall we take a break?"
"No!" Xie Sisi’s voice was a bit hoarse but exceptionally firm.
"Wang Lan, come at me again. I feel... much better."
"Okay!"
Wang Lan distanced himself from Xie Sisi again, and then, a strong murderous intent locked onto her.
Indeed, just as Xie Sisi herself had said, her reaction this time was much better. At least her body wasn’t as tense, and the hand gripping her sword didn’t tremble violently.
Wang Lan took a deep breath and charged towards Xie Sisi once more.
His sword flashed like lightning, slashing towards Xie Sisi’s forehead.
At that moment, a gloomy-faced Jiang Xinyu entered the second level of the underground parking garage. The access code to Wang Lan’s training room... well, that was no secret to Jiang Xinyu.
Not just Jiang Xinyu, but Xu Xiangwen and Gong Feiyu knew it as well.
Jiang Xinyu had followed them to the vicinity of the Xinyu Building. Settling into a coffee shop opposite, she then watched Xie Sisi furtively enter the Xinyu Building and head for the underground garage entrance.
Instantly, the temperature in the coffee shop seemed to drop by three degrees.
After stirring her coffee for half an hour, she finally couldn’t restrain her curiosity and also followed them into the Xinyu Building’s underground garage.
What if I see Wang Lan and Xie Sisi doing something... what should I do? Should I give them my blessing, confront Wang Lan, or...?
Jiang Xinyu’s mind was a maelstrom of conflicting thoughts.
But in the next moment, all the scenarios Jiang Xinyu had mentally prepared vanished like smoke.
All that remained in Jiang Xinyu’s mind was the image of Wang Lan raising his sword to strike Xie Sisi.
Jiang Xinyu was not like Xie Sisi; she had already completed the warrior’s transformation. She could clearly sense that Wang Lan’s strike wasn’t practice; he was genuinely trying to kill an enemy.
Moreover, Wang Lan’s sword has a metallic glint. That’s not a practice sword; it’s a real weapon!
What is Wang Lan doing? Is he using a living person for sword practice?
Fear surged through Jiang Xinyu’s heart, then shot down to the base of her spine like an electric current.
CLANG—
Xie Sisi swiftly raised her sword, parrying Wang Lan’s slash.
Jiang Xinyu secretly breathed a sigh of relief.
However, she had barely exhaled when Wang Lan’s sword flashed again, streaking towards Xie Sisi’s throat. The speed and angle were utterly without feint—a true killing blow.
Xie Sisi leaned back slightly, her footwork instantly adjusting, the blade barely grazing her throat as it passed.
Wang Lan closed in again, the light of his sword blossomed before Xie Sisi.
A series of crisp CLANGS erupted instantly.
The two combatants hadn’t even reacted, but Jiang Xinyu, watching in secret, broke out in a cold sweat. But then, she understood.
She understood why Xie Sisi had seemed to transform in such a short period. And in that moment, Jiang Xinyu grasped the significance of this kind of live-blade, true-stakes combat.
Sparring, in the end, is just practice.
Practice can never replace true combat!
Only real battle truly hones combat skills. How you fight in training is how you’ll kill on the battlefield! But... people could die. What if there’s an accident?
Soon, Wang Lan had Xie Sisi completely on the defensive.
SNAP—
Accidents always happen so unexpectedly.
Wang Lan’s sword slashed down. Xie Sisi frantically raised her own to block. Theoretically, the block should have held. However, there might have been a flaw in the quality of Xie Sisi’s sword.
The instant Wang Lan’s sword connected, Xie Sisi’s blade snapped.
Wang Lan’s blade continued its descent. Although he tried to redirect it, it still sliced deeply into Xie Sisi’s shoulder.
Blood spurted out.
Wang Lan quickly withdrew his sword, pressing his hand on Xie Sisi’s shoulder.
His Star Power surged, and his healing skill activated instantly.
Xie Sisi, seemingly stunned by this turn of events, stared at Wang Lan with wide, horrified eyes for a long moment.
"I’m sorry... I didn’t expect... Does it hurt?"
Wang Lan’s gentle voice reached Xie Sisi’s ears, and only then did she return to her senses. By then, the wound on her shoulder had vanished. In fact, she hadn’t even felt any pain before it healed completely.
However, that slash had felt like a trip to the Ghost Gate and back.
The feeling of death had been so real.
But once the fear dissipated, Xie Sisi suddenly felt an immense sense of release, as if a great weight had been lifted.
It was like bungee jumping for the first time. At first, the fear is overwhelming—screaming, crying, clinging to the railing for dear life, refusing to jump.
But once you’re pushed, an incredible thrill floods your senses. After the extreme fear vanishes, it’s replaced by an indescribable exhilaration.
Afterward, those who were terrified remain terrified, but those who are captivated become utterly addicted to the thrill.
Xie Sisi belonged to the latter group.
Suddenly, Xie Sisi’s face flushed crimson, her capillaries seemingly on the verge of bursting. An immense pleasure, as if a Heart Demon within her had been unleashed, surged through her, making her long for another round.
"Are you... okay?" Wang Lan asked, a little nervous.
This time, I really overdid it. Thankfully, I have my healing skill.
"I’m... I’m fine... I feel... I feel like I’ve completely overcome my fear! Shall we... go again?"
"Eh?" Wang Lan’s eyes widened as he looked at Xie Sisi in disbelief.
That wasn’t my reaction when Huang Feilong trained me. Even though I overcame the fear of death, I definitely wasn’t excited. Girl, isn’t your way of processing this a bit off?
"Come on~"
Her voice was so seductive it made Wang Lan almost drop his weapon and surrender.
Damn it... this feels really wrong.
"This time, I won’t use a sword. Just attack me directly. Quick, I feel like I’m on the verge of a breakthrough!"
Looking at Xie Sisi’s eager expression, Wang Lan backed away a few steps, half-believing, half-doubting.
"Are you sure?"
"I’m sure! Hurry, attack me!"
Why does that request sound so familiar?
The thought flashed through his mind and was just as quickly dismissed. Wang Lan raised his sword and lunged at Xie Sisi again.
But Xie Sisi didn’t dodge; instead, she advanced. As Wang Lan’s sword slashed down, her hand shot out like a striking snake, aiming straight for his throat.
Damn!
Wang Lan’s heart clenched.
What a sharp counterattack!
Wang Lan sidestepped slightly, swiping his sword horizontally, but Xie Sisi dodged with ease, launching another attack as she moved.
Something’s not right.
At that moment, Wang Lan was certain—Xie Sisi’s condition was abnormal.
Her unarmed combat prowess had seemingly doubled in an instant. This was the kind of power Wang Lan had sensed from the ’other’ Xie Sisi.
Quickly, Wang Lan looked into Xie Sisi’s eyes.
But what he saw startled him. The look in her eyes didn’t belong to the ’other’ Xie Sisi. This meant the Xie Sisi before him was genuinely capable of such lethal unarmed combat now.
What in the world? Did my slash somehow open her governor and conception vessels or something?

chapters.title: Chapter 119: I Will Not Disappoint Your Intentions
chapters.content:
Chapter 119: Chapter 119: I Will Not Disappoint Your Intentions
Though it happened in a flash, Xie Sisi’s arms invaded Wang Lan’s chest like a pair of agile snakes, moving rhythmically as Star Power flowed around them. Suddenly, Wang Lan’s saber began moving uncontrollably, as if caught in a strong undercurrent underwater.
"CRACK—"
With a crisp sound, Wang Lan’s saber was instantly snapped by Xie Sisi.
"CLANG—"
The broken saber blade hit the ground, and Wang Lan looked at Xie Sisi in astonishment.
She had done it. She had not only overcome her fear of death but also... managed to perfectly utilize Star Power in her basic physical movements?
Moreover, Xie Sisi’s demeanor just now was strange. When his saber was about to strike, Wang Lan clearly felt that Xie Sisi’s expression wasn’t fear, calmness, or restraint, but...
Freaking excitement?
She could get excited about this?
Surprise crossed Xie Sisi’s face, followed instantly by ecstatic joy. A radiant smile bloomed on her face. "Wang Lan... I succeeded... I really did it! I’m not afraid anymore... I..."
Suddenly, Xie Sisi pounced on Wang Lan, crushing him beneath her like Mount Tai toppling down, and then leaned down to kiss his face frantically.
"COUGH, COUGH—"
A soft cough sounded, startling Wang Lan and Xie Sisi apart instantly.
Jiang Xinyu walked over with an indifferent expression.
"Xinyu... I... It’s not what you think... Wang Lan and I..."
"I’ve seen it all!" Jiang Xinyu’s tone was somewhat strained, although she had indeed seen everything.
Xie Sisi had pounced on Wang Lan in her excitement, and the kiss was merely an outlet for her ecstatic joy. However, if Jiang Xinyu hadn’t appeared, things might have escalated into Heavenly Thunder and Earthly Fire.
"I was wondering why your combat skills had improved so abnormally. It turns out you’ve got a private coach." Jiang Xinyu walked over to the edge of the sparring platform, resting her chin in her hand while looking at Wang Lan. "You two are crazy. One really dares to chop, and the other actually lets him? What if there had been an accident?"
"It’s okay, Wang Lan can heal..." Xie Sisi quickly tried to make excuses for Wang Lan.
"Healing isn’t omnipotent. If you had dodged even a fraction of a second later and your head was chopped off, what good would healing do? Can a severed head be reattached?"
"That... was just an accident..." Wang Lan also felt that the earlier situation had indeed been a bit dangerous, but his method had worked.
It was the right call.
"Sisi, take a rest," Jiang Xinyu said to Xie Sisi as she slowly unzipped her jacket and climbed onto the platform.
The implication was clear. Wang Lan, however, felt somewhat apprehensive.
During school practice sessions, it was just sparring, and Wang Lan had been able to easily suppress Jiang Xinyu. But now, Jiang Xinyu’s stance clearly indicated she wasn’t just aiming for practice.
Wang Lan had witnessed before just how terrifying a serious Jiang Xinyu could be. Moreover, his impression of her had always been of a formidable character, one who attacked fiercely—the kind of person whose presence in a home would make ghosts and gods flee.
Jiang Xinyu went to the weapons rack and selected an Octagonal Han Sword for herself. She gave it a light flick, indicating it felt suitable.
"What are you still standing there for?"
"Uh... Xinyu, shouldn’t I also take a break for a bit?"
"You don’t look like you need a break. Stop wasting time. Use Ghost Wail."
"Are you serious?"
"Dead serious! If you don’t fight with the intent to kill me, I’ll kill you!"
In an instant, a chill shot up Wang Lan’s spine. In his eyes, Jiang Xinyu’s Octagonal Han Sword was no longer just a sword but a gleaming, ice-cold cleaver.
"You can fight like that with Sisi? Why the hesitation with me? Do you think I can’t even dodge your attacks properly? That you could kill me with a single strike?"
"That’s not what I meant... Alright, fine!" Wang Lan resigned himself, took out Ghost Wail, and slowly drew it.
If I don’t go all out with her today, she probably won’t let this drop.
WHOOSH—
Suddenly, Jiang Xinyu’s figure flashed. She appeared in front of Wang Lan and thrust her sword toward his heart.
Wang Lan reacted instantly. Ghost Wail emitted a ghostly howl as it deflected Jiang Xinyu’s sword.
Swordsmanship and sword skill differ fundamentally. Swordsmanship is not as aggressive as sword skill; it stresses technique over power. Swordsmanship is more elegant and dazzling, and mastering it is several times more difficult than mastering sword skill.
In many aspects, learning swordsmanship is much more challenging than learning sword skill.
Sword skill is easy to practice, with simple moves. Learning swordsmanship, however, requires insight and talent.
Although practicing swordsmanship is difficult, once mastery is achieved, its potential for growth is incomparable to that of sword skill. To put it simply, sword skill is easy to learn but hard to master.
When using a saber to kill an enemy, if you strike a vital area, all’s well. But if not, you might have to strike ten times before they’re subdued. However, being pierced by a sword once can cause instant death.
If you have the aptitude and talent to learn swordsmanship, and can wield a sword well, then swordsmanship is definitely superior to sword skill. In the simplest terms, the harder something is to learn, the more useful it becomes once mastered.
The sword, from its very inception, abandons defense. The sword, from its very inception, is designed to kill with a single blow.
Therefore, the fight between Wang Lan and Jiang Xinyu wasn’t as overtly fierce as the one with Sisi, but the degree of danger was several times greater.
Xie Sisi, watching from the sidelines, finally understood the feeling Jiang Xinyu must have had when she spied on them from the shadows.
Fear, trembling. I wish I could just close my eyes and not watch. But I’m so worried!
She could only stare wide-eyed, unblinking, as she watched the two narrowly escape death time and again in their exchanges.
Before Wang Lan, it felt as if he were facing a true enemy intent on killing him. In Jiang Xinyu’s eyes, Wang Lan’s saber also showed no mercy. But only such a merciless opponent could expose the flaws in her swordsmanship.
Wang Lan thrust out his saber in an instant, his body also closing the distance immediately.
This moment was precisely when Jiang Xinyu was transitioning between moves, leaving Wang Lan a roughly 0.2-second opening.
When Jiang Xinyu intended to withdraw her sword for defense, Wang Lan’s saber was a fraction faster.
Blood blossomed. Ghost Wail pierced Jiang Xinyu’s shoulder, half an inch deep. This was only because Wang Lan had promptly pulled back his strike.
Wang Lan quickly withdrew his saber and placed a palm on Jiang Xinyu’s shoulder. Meanwhile, Jiang Xinyu frowned deeply, continuously replaying the scene of Wang Lan’s thrust in her mind.
This move has a flaw, an unavoidable one!
She had never noticed it before, but today it was revealed in actual combat. Only by discovering flaws can one mend them. At this moment, Jiang Xinyu felt incredibly grateful that her previous combat experiences hadn’t involved a true swordsmanship master.
Otherwise, the flaws in her swordsmanship could have led to her utter downfall.
By the time these thoughts had passed through her mind, Wang Lan had already healed her wound.
"Are you alright? You’re not angry, are you?" Wang Lan asked cautiously.
Jiang Xinyu came back to her senses and shook her head. "It seems this kind of sparring is indeed necessary. I’ve practiced this move for so many years and used it countless times, never realizing that particular motion was actually backward or had been altered. If you hadn’t discovered that flaw, I would have eventually died because of it."
"Ancient martial arts have been passed down through generations. Some are refined, while others are corrupted or altered. The swordsmanship techniques you’ve learned may not all be correct. However, remember that while techniques are created by others, you are the one who wields them. I still believe the highest realm of swordsmanship is ’No Technique.’
Pure instinct, instantly subduing the opponent. I’ve never formally trained in swordsmanship. All I know are basic sword forms, but these basics didn’t put me at a disadvantage against you. Can you predict whether my next move will be a thrust or a parry? My sword moves are simply the methods I use to defeat an opponent.
Certain sword techniques can sometimes be very crafty and indeed achieve the unexpected, catching people off guard, but this can only be considered treading a heterodox path. I prefer the grand and righteous way."
"’No Technique?’" Jiang Xinyu savored these two words, her eyes flickering with thought. The more she contemplated them, the more profound their meaning seemed, yet she couldn’t fully grasp their essence.
"Explain it to me in detail. What is ’No Technique’?"
Wang Lan had forgotten that in this world, due to the existence of Star Martial Warriors, wuxia novels didn’t exist. Instead, novels about Star Martial Warriors were popular, narrating the rise of legendary Star Martial Warriors from obscurity.
This was a difference in cultural context. In his previous life, almost anyone could recite the three great realms of the Sword Dao, but to the people of this world, such concepts were unheard of, let alone considered.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
Thinking this, Wang Lan slowly turned his back and gazed into the distance.
"Swordsmanship has three great realms. The first is the Realm of Sword Moves. One diligently practices sword moves, striving for perfection, training arduously alone, enduring heat and cold, achieving mastery after ten years. With mastery, one can challenge the world.
But people’s fortunes are not constant, and water has no fixed form. No matter how skillfully, ingeniously, or fluidly you execute them, sword moves will always have flaws. There are no perfect sword moves in the world; any techniques can be deciphered and countered.
Thus, the second realm of swordsmanship emerged: No Technique! First, one masters all existing techniques and comprehends the Sword Dao. Then, one forgets all the techniques learned. Forgetting doesn’t mean truly forgetting, but rather disassembling the techniques entirely until they become instinct.
One faces different situations and encounters different enemies, adapting spontaneously. There are no fixed moves, no predetermined routines. When even you don’t know your next move, how can the enemy?
This realm is like unarmed combat. Doesn’t unarmed combat also emphasize having no set moves, only methods to defeat the enemy? As long as it can defeat the enemy, anything can be a technique.
And the third realm is the Realm of No Sword.
With no sword in hand, everything in heaven and earth can be a sword. To walk the path of the Sword Dao for a lifetime, the emphasis is on sword intent. Intent precedes the sword. Upon reaching this realm, you yourself become an unsheathed sword.
Whether you hold a saber, a spear, a sword, a halberd, or even a brick, all can be used as a sword to slay the enemy. However, this realm is very profound, and even I cannot fully comprehend it. You are likely also very far from this realm.
But your swordsmanship has already reached a certain level. You can start considering the realm of No Technique. Once you thoroughly grasp the core of No Technique, all techniques in the world will appear full of openings to you."
Jiang Xinyu stared at Wang Lan in utter shock. If she hadn’t understood, she would merely have been confused. But precisely because she understood, she was profoundly shocked.
No master had ever spoken of such theories. As a seasoned Swordsman with eight years dedicated to the Sword Dao, if there were a foundational theory, a veritable general principle of swordsmanship, she would have no reason not to know it.
There was only one explanation for Jiang Xinyu’s ignorance: this theory had never been revealed to the world before.
"These three realms... did you comprehend them yourself?"
"How could that be possible!" Wang Lan immediately shook his head. "I haven’t even reached the Realm of Sword Moves. How could I possibly comprehend these things?"
Jiang Xinyu’s eyes shimmered; she thought she understood.
This theory... it might be a comprehension of the Lord Flame Emperor! Although I’ve never heard that the Flame Emperor used a sword, she *is* the Flame Emperor! Shouldn’t the Flame Emperor be versed in everything, a master of all arts?
Instantly, Jiang Xinyu’s gaze towards Wang Lan filled with gratitude.
Wang Lan actually shared such a precious, unreservedly passed-down family secret with me! This invaluable theory... He truly doesn’t see me as an outsider...
"Don’t worry," she declared, "I won’t betray your kind intentions."
"My kind intentions? Wait, Xinyu, have you misunderstood something?"
"I say it is, so it is! No arguments accepted."
Her Majesty is mighty!
What else could Wang Lan do?
With that temper, she’s destined for a life of solitude with a blue lamp and an ancient Buddha.

chapters.title: Chapter 120
chapters.content:
Chapter 120: 120
Deep into the night, Jiang Xinyu finally had her driver pick her up, taking Xie Sisi home as well.
The next day, Saturday, not only did Xie Sisi arrive, but Jiang Xinyu and even Xu Xiangwen and Gong Feiyu showed up.
"Lanzi, you’re not being fair," Gong Feiyu slung an arm around Wang Lan’s shoulder. "With such a great training method, how could you secretly help only Monitor Xie? Don’t you consider us brothers?"
"That’s a classic case of forgetting your bros when a girl’s around! When Lanzi first awakened, how did we support you? Three Kings and one Silver leading you, a Bronze. Now look at you! You’ve got this amazing training method, but you only care for the girls, without a single thought for us."
"Are you sure it was three Kings leading a Bronze?" Wang Lan glanced at Xu Xiangwen with disdain. "Besides, do you think this training method is all benefits and no drawbacks?"
"What drawbacks? That we’d hate you if you hit us too hard? You’re overthinking it. Given our bond as brothers, even if you broke my third leg, I would... just need you to fix it."
"What are you thinking? Do you imagine I have unlimited healing power? Healing one person is easy; two is pushing it. But now there are four of you, mind you. I just don’t have enough healing energy."
This was indeed a very real problem. Wang Lan’s healing abilities consumed three times more Star Power when healing others compared to himself. As for Star Power recovery, replenishing the energy for a single healing session took at least an hour.
Caring for Xie Sisi these past few days had been manageable. Yesterday, however, attending to both Xie Sisi and Jiang Xinyu had already proven strenuous. This time, with four people, Wang Lan felt he might be drained completely dry.
Soul Beads could be purchased to replenish Star Power, but outside, a single bead cost 80,000—not something many could afford. Within the trial grounds, Soul Beads could be used freely, but in the outside world, only the wealthiest tycoons could manage such an expense.
"It’s not a big deal!" Jiang Xinyu walked over casually, tossing a cloth bag in front of Wang Lan. "There are ten Soul Beads inside. That should be enough, right?"
"Damn, Xinyu, you’re still the most lavish one here. I only brought three," Xu Xiangwen immediately exclaimed, giving a thumbs-up.
"I brought three as well," Gong Feiyu rubbed his wrists. "Who am I fighting?"
"Of course it’s Xu. Could it be me?" Wang Lan stated as if it were obvious.
"I’ll spar with Sisi today," Jiang Xinyu informed Wang Lan, her tone leaving no room for discussion, her decision firm.
"Hold on, Xinyu, are you talking about actual combat sparring? With Monitor Xie?" Xu Xiangwen suddenly cried out.
"Yeah, what about it? Do you still think Sisi is weak? Want to try? I guarantee you’ll be beaten so badly you won’t know what’s real."
"Is it really that exaggerated?" Although Xu Xiangwen voiced doubt, his expression suggested he believed her. Jiang Xinyu rarely joked; her words were usually serious.
"You guys should start with bare hands to warm up."
Xu Xiangwen and Gong Feiyu sat down below the platform, ready to watch. The two women on stage, dressed in tight short-sleeved shirts and hot pants, were a dazzling sight simply standing there.
Wang Lan, acting as referee, idly tossed a coin between his fingers.
With a light flick, he sent it spinning into the air.
DING—
The moment the coin hit the ground, the two figures on stage instantly blurred and clashed.
Jiang Xinyu’s fighting style was agile and versatile, a blend of technique and aesthetic grace. Xie Sisi’s combat skills, in contrast, were simple and direct. If Jiang Xinyu was a practitioner of a graceful, soft fist, then Xie Sisi wielded an explosive, steel fist.
But regardless of their stylistic differences, both moved with lightning speed.
From the first exchange, it was an all-out, ferocious battle.
Watching from the sidelines, Xu Xiangwen’s face froze, his eyes wide in a stare that petrified him for a good half-minute.
Wang Lan walked over to Xu Xiangwen and patted his shoulder. "So, what do you think?"
"I... I really might not be able to beat her," Xu Xiangwen said with a wry smile, returning to his senses.
"Never mind you; even Xinyu and I couldn’t beat her."
"No way?" Gong Feiyu was shocked. "Your and Xinyu’s unarmed combat skills are among the best in the entire Star Martial Arts Campus."
"Don’t believe me? Just keep watching."
Jiang Xinyu was only holding her own against Xie Sisi because Sisi hadn’t yet used her unique secret technique. Incorporating Star Power into combat required extremely high control over it. It also demanded the ability to run two CPUs in sync without them interfering with each other.
It was like one person singing a duet.
An ordinary person definitely couldn’t achieve it.
From this perspective, Xie Sisi had already transcended the ordinary.
Sure enough, as Xie Sisi grew more excited and her fighting style became wilder, Star Power surged around her, her body seemingly enveloped in a cloak of it.
Sisi’s speed increased continuously, and her punches grew heavier. Soon, Jiang Xinyu was completely overpowered, just as Wang Lan had been during their last full-powered spar.
Five minutes later, Jiang Xinyu’s defenses suddenly crumbled. Sisi instantly seized the opening, unleashing a flurry of sharp attacks.
"Holy shit—" Xu Xiangwen leaped to his feet. "Stop, stop!"
Xie Sisi halted her movements. Jiang Xinyu hastily retreated three steps, her face visibly swelling.
But Jiang Xinyu shot Xu Xiangwen a glare. "Who told you to call a halt?"
"Not call a halt? And just watch you get pummeled?"
"Great enlightenment and major breakthroughs can only be achieved in moments of great crisis. With Wang Lan here, it’s impossible for me to be beaten to death. Don’t you dare call a halt next time," Jiang Xinyu emphasized earnestly. "This is the true meaning of combat training. Otherwise, how is it different from regular sparring?"
Xu Xiangwen understood the logic, but this was just too brutal.
After Wang Lan treated Jiang Xinyu’s injuries, he jumped off the platform. "Gentlemen, this way, please. Bare hands or weapons, your choice. My weapons rack here has everything, and I assure you, they’re all the real deal."
Xu Xiangwen looked at the two frenzied women battling on the platform again and swallowed hard. "Feiyu, are we really doing this?"
"Scared? Come on! Either I beat you to death, or you beat me to death!"
Undergoing this kind of life-or-death combat training was an enormous challenge to one’s mental fortitude. When it became almost too much to bear, they would take a rest, then continue.
And so, by the end of each day, everyone felt as if they were dancing on Yama’s head.
Fists and feet were merely the warm-up; fighting with real swords and spears was the main course.
Xu Xiangwen had counted; that day, Gong Feiyu had cut him nearly twenty-five times. Gong Feiyu had it even worse, getting cut by Xu thirty times. After all, Xu Xiangwen was a close-combat fighter, while Gong Feiyu was an Earth Attribute Mage.
As for Jiang Xinyu and Xie Sisi, Xie Sisi almost perfectly suppressed Jiang Xinyu. The injuries Jiang Xinyu sustained in that single day surpassed all she had received since becoming a Star Martial Warrior.
Without Wang Lan there to ensure her safety, Jiang Xinyu would have been bedridden in a hospital for at least a month.
But the results of the day’s training were undeniably obvious. Though outsiders might not sense it, they themselves could feel the distinct improvement.
The group of five met almost daily at Wang Lan’s house to train. Either Wang Lan would fight Xu Xiangwen and Gong Feiyu, or Jiang Xinyu would fight the two of them. After those two were tormented to the point of doubting their existence, Wang Lan and Jiang Xinyu would then, in turn, be tormented by Xie Sisi.
Ever since Xie Sisi had her governor and conception vessels opened, her combat strength became potentially unmatched throughout the entire Star Martial Arts Campus, a level that could even include instructors and teachers.
「Time flies silently. When you realize it, it has already passed you by.」
The final exams for the first semester of senior year arrived quietly, marking the halfway point of their last year in high school.
For Wang Lan, exams had never been an issue. His only regret was that he hadn’t secured first place in both academics and martial arts.
As for Xie Sisi—this girl who had been seriously overlooked by everyone due to her uneven abilities—she completed her transformation after two and a half years of accumulation, truly metamorphosing.
Seventh in the school for academics and eighth in the martial arts exam. If Xie Sisi’s Star Martial level hadn’t been merely at the peak of the Starlight Realm, breaking into the top five wouldn’t have been a challenge.
This achievement nearly caused an uproar throughout the school.
Having one Wang Lan was one thing. Although Wang Lan was only at the mid-stage of Star Shine, he still made it into the top five of his grade. But then again, Wang Lan had dominated for nine years under the title of a prodigy. The students of the Star Martial Arts Campus had developed some immunity to such a Demon.
But for an unknown student, an ordinary girl at the late Starlight Realm, to soar from 150th place to a combined seventh in the entire grade? Was that scientific? Was it reasonable?
The school’s response was that this was completely logical; there wasn’t the slightest hint of discrepancy in the exam results.
The commotion died down after two days because vacation had begun.
「Xinyu Building, underground training room.」
The five of them, completely soaked in sweat, lay sprawled in the four corners of the ring, gasping for air with no regard for their image.
"Sisi, weren’t you a little too excited today... taking on all four of us... I, Xu Xiangwen, hereby declare you the wildest woman!"
"It’s my first time... my first time getting such a high rank... Shouldn’t I be excited?" Having grown familiar with the group of four, Xie Sisi seemed to have blended in with them. She spoke more casually and joked around without inhibition.
A sexy smile touched the corners of Xie Sisi’s lips. Ever since Wang Lan had helped her overcome her psychological barriers, Xie Sisi seemed to have become increasingly... unrestrained.
Her wildness carried a hint of bloodlust—mesmerizing, yet also daunting.
To use Gong Feiyu’s words, one glance at her made you want to get closer. But once near, you couldn’t help but maintain a safe distance. Get too close, and you risked being torn to shreds at any moment.
"Sisi, don’t get carried away," Wang Lan couldn’t help reminding her. "School exams only test academics and unarmed combat. Those are your strong points. But in terms of real strength, you might not even secure a spot in the class’s top ten, let alone the entire grade’s."ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
"I know," Xie Sisi was a very self-disciplined and mature woman, so she understood what Wang Lan meant.
Her Star Power was only at the Starlight Realm, and apart from her innate water-control Star Martial Skill, she possessed no others. Star Martial Skills were the true measure of a Star Martial Warrior’s combat prowess.
Take Mingyue Wucheng, for example.
If he were to truly display his strength, no one in their class could guarantee they would last three minutes against him. Mingyue Wucheng’s family Illusion Technique was so potent that one look from him could mean death.
Descendants from other Star Martial families had mastered at least three A-grade Star Martial Skills or more. How could Sisi fight against them? A single Star Martial Skill attack would be enough to take Sisi down.
Don’t be fooled by her ability to dominate Xu Xiangwen and Gong Feiyu in the ring. If they were to use their Star Martial Skills, Sisi wouldn’t last long either. That was the true gap.

chapters.title: Chapter 121: Heading to the Intermediate Trial Grounds
chapters.content:
Chapter 121: Chapter 121: Heading to the Intermediate Trial Grounds
"Winter vacation has already started..." After resting for a while, Jiang Xinyu suddenly said.
Everyone was momentarily stunned, but it only took a second for them to understand. This was a plan that had been made long ago, and had been promised by Jiang Xinyu during the summer vacation.Nᴇw novel chapters are publɪshed on NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet
"There are fourteen days left until the New Year. We’ll take a day off tomorrow to make preparations, and head to the Taoyuan District’s intermediate trial field the day after tomorrow morning."
"Understood!"
"OK."
Wang Lan smiled without saying anything. Xie Sisi, who was leaning close to Jiang Xinyu, lowered her head slightly, a hint of disappointment crossing her face. Even if she wanted to go in, she didn’t have the money.
She currently had only 500,000, and the intermediate trial field cost 100,000 a day, so ten days would be 1,000,000. She couldn’t afford it.
"Sisi, why don’t you come with us?" Jiang Xinyu’s next words made Xie Sisi abruptly lift her head, her face showing astonishment. She seemed somewhat unable to believe it, touched with surprise.
"Sisi, I refused you last time because with your strength at that time, it would have been too dangerous to enter the trial field. But now, you’ve reached the professional level. As long as you stick with our team, we can still look after your safety."
"I understand, Wang Lan has explained it to me... it’s just... how many days are you going in for?"
"Ten days."
"If it’s ten days... my money won’t be enough."
"PSSSH—" Xu Xiangwen made a disdainful sound. "You don’t need to worry about money. Which one of us here lacks that? No worries, we’ll cover it."
"That won’t do..." Xie Sisi quickly shook her head. "That’s a million, not a small sum. Even if you consider me a friend, it’s not possible. I... can’t accept it."
"No problem, Sisi. You told me you have five hundred thousand, right? You can put in your 500,000, and I’ll front you the other half. Once we get Soul Beads inside, you can pay me back with those."
"This... alright then." Xie Sisi, though feeling like she was still taking advantage of Wang Lan, reluctantly agreed.
Now that it was settled they were going to the trial field, Xu Xiangwen and Gong Feiyu quickly left to go home and prepare. Wang Lan, however, felt there was nothing much to prepare; he just needed to bring Ghost Wail with him.
Just when he was planning to continue practicing with Jiang Xinyu and Xie Sisi to accumulate some skill points, Jiang Xinyu gave Wang Lan a look that said ’figure it out yourself’ and, pulling Xie Sisi along, said they were going shopping.
Shopping? Is that helpful for improving strength?
The answer was obviously no.
Since it wasn’t helpful, why bother? You guys go ahead; studying is what I love the most.
This time, not only was Jiang Xinyu at a loss for words with Wang Lan, but even Xie Sisi looked at him as if she had seen a ghost. How could such a creature still exist in this world after nearly twenty years?
「Two days later,」
Wang Lan drove himself to the entrance of the Taoyuan District’s intermediate trial field. When Wang Lan arrived, Xu Xiangwen and Gong Feiyu had already booked a table at the barbecue restaurant by the entrance.
"Yo? Has our antique finally wised up today and decided to show off the family luxury car? Don’t you prefer electric scooters and buses?"
Xu Xiangwen had long been drooling over the four luxury cars in Wang Lan’s garage. However, Wang Lan guarded them closely and never even let Xu Xiangwen touch them, let alone lend one for a drive. These four cars were all custom models, with no identical ones on the entire Sky Blue Star. Moreover, even with Xu Xiangwen’s shrewd eye, he couldn’t discern which company produced these cars.
"Such big talk! Why don’t you build me a subway or start a bus route here? If I don’t drive, am I supposed to walk?" Wang Lan retorted.
"Has Xinyu not arrived yet?"
"She said she’d be here in twenty minutes, but..." Xu Xiangwen suddenly looked somewhat displeased.
"What’s wrong?"
"When I called her, I heard Xincheng’s voice, which means she hasn’t set off yet. Twenty minutes... TSS!"
A distance of 42 kilometers could be covered in twenty minutes if one drove at 100 km/h. But considering the time to go downstairs, start the car, and then deal with traffic lights... that would be terrifying. No wonder Xu Xiangwen gasped; Jiang Xinyu was planning to race over here at 200 km/h!
While Wang Lan was chatting and teasing the two, a red sports car charged from a distance like a runaway stallion. An elegant drift parked the vehicle perfectly in a parking spot. The gull-wing doors opened, and Jiang Xinyu and Xie Sisi got out. It was evident from Sisi’s slightly unsteady steps that she was a bit off-kilter. Wang Lan completely understood; it had been the same for him the last time.
"Good morning!" Jiang Xinyu greeted the three with a smile as she approached.
"Morning, my foot," Wang Lan immediately retorted. "You were speeding again, weren’t you?"
"There are hardly any cars on this road; a speed limit is a completely superfluous design."
"I think giving you a driver’s license was a completely superfluous design." Glancing at Xie Sisi, who was still blushing, he asked, "Didn’t scare you, did she?"
"No... no."
"HEH..." Jiang Xinyu let out a cold laugh. "Are you mistaken about Sisi? Not only was she not frightened, but she also urged me to go faster. Her flushed face isn’t from fear, but from excitement."
I believe that!
Wang Lan thought.
I’m even afraid of how excited Xie Sisi can get.
"The trial field opens at nine, and we have twenty minutes until then. Have you ordered?"
"Ordered long ago." Xu Xiangwen stretched out his hand and snapped his fingers.
The waiter promptly brought out the dishes: a plate of barbecued meat for each person, each piece as large as a slice of toast, charred on the outside and tender inside, the aroma tantalizing.
"It’s settled. Feiyu and I will cover the fees for this trip. I’m being a fool, and so is he."
"You’re the fool!" Gong Feiyu was so annoyed he almost wanted to spear the guy on the spot.
"I..." Xie Sisi lifted her head. "I brought money with me. Wasn’t that what we agreed on last time?"
"That’s so much trouble. Let’s just pay directly. As for what was agreed upon last time, we’ll settle that after we get out."
"But, I’ve brought the money." Saying this, Xie Sisi even held up the slightly cute canvas bag in her hand. It was quite large, perhaps a trendy style.
But the next instant, Wang Lan and the others all stopped what they were doing. "You didn’t... bring five hundred thousand in cash, did you?"
"Ah! I don’t have a bank card... and all the money I’ve earned is in cash."
"Lanzi, you’ve found your kin," Xu Xiangwen teased. "You’re both like primitive people who’ve time-traveled to the present."
"What era is this, still carrying cash around? Anyway, the trial field has storage lockers. We’ll put it in one then; it’s not safe to leave it in the car."
"Oh!" Xie Sisi nodded obediently, so adorable that Jiang Xinyu, standing beside her, almost couldn’t resist pinching her cheeks.
Twenty minutes slipped by quietly, and Wang Lan’s group of five stood up and headed towards the intermediate trial field.
"Five people, ten days."
"Five million." A lean young man spoke indifferently. "Swipe your card or scan for payment?"
"Swipe the card."
"Huh? Brother Wang Lan!" Suddenly, the attendant noticed Wang Lan standing behind Gong Feiyu and called out.
Wang Lan looked up. The face was somewhat familiar, but he couldn’t recall the name.
He recognized me, so it would be impolite not to respond, right?
"Oh— you’re that... uh... that person..."
"’That person’ my foot! If you don’t know who I am, why pretend you do? I’m the unlucky guy who got an arm chopped off and went missing. You’re the one who reattached it for me."
With those words, the lean man stood up and saluted Wang Lan. "Martial Arts Corps, Third Battalion, Second Lieutenant Gu Jia!"
Wang Lan hastily returned the salute. "Second Lieutenant Gu, I’ll definitely remember you from now on. Given the circumstances back then, how could I have remembered everyone?"
"Understood. Are you with them?"
"Mm!"
"BEEP. BEEP. BEEP. Deduction successful: two million!"
"..."
The five of them looked at Gu Jia, their faces full of question marks.
"Brother Wang Lan’s entry to the intermediate trial field is free, and his friends get a fifty percent discount."
"This isn’t against the rules, is it?" Wang Lan asked.
"Of course not. These are instructions from Corps headquarters. Brother Wang Lan, with your strength, I won’t waste words. Be careful, and I wish you a bountiful harvest."
"Thank you!"
After changing into their combat suits, the squad of five regrouped.
"We haven’t been to the intermediate trial field before, so we’re unfamiliar with the terrain and the Exotic Beasts. Which Exotic Beast should we choose?" Gong Feiyu asked first.
"A few key points: they must be plentiful to ensure a good haul, adapted to close combat, and their habitat should have earth and water. Do we have any targets fitting that?" Wang Lan asked.
The need for abundance was self-explanatory; hunting a tribe with few Exotic Beasts would be a waste of time. Suitability for close combat was also crucial, as among the five of them, only Jiang Xinyu had long-range attack capabilities. Gong Feiyu’s Earth Attribute abilities were mostly for control.
This wasn’t the beginner trial field; Exotic Beasts here could appear at the Star Cloud Stage at any time. Jiang Xinyu’s strength couldn’t guarantee absolute suppression. Ordinary Exotic Beasts might mostly be insignificant creatures at the peak of the Starlight Stage, but there were also quite a few at the Star Shine Stage.
In short, the difficulty was more than double that of the beginner trial field.
"Got it! The Golden Mantis!" Xu Xiangwen exclaimed.
"The Golden Mantis, a Gold Attribute Exotic Beast, is located in the mining area and mainly feeds on ores. Because they consume ores year-round, their bodies undergo metallization. However, this fortification is not self-generated; instead, it’s caused by Gold Attribute deposits leading to armor formation. Their joints and the gaps in the armor plating on their bellies are their weak points. The Golden Mantis’s main forms of attack are its forelimbs, the Mantis Blades, and its terrifyingly powerful mandibles. Additionally, the Golden Mantis is incredibly fast and capable of short-range, low-altitude flight. Most Golden Mantises lack attribute-based attacks, but mutated ones can launch attacks of other attributes—any attribute is possible. Golden Mantises have high attack, high defense, and high agility. Most Star Martial Warriors are reluctant to provoke them."
"Seriously? I asked you to filter, and this is what you came up with?" Wang Lan said, looking at Xu Xiangwen with exasperation.
"Although the Golden Mantis seems strong, its flaws are also obvious," Gong Feiyu analyzed. "The very fact that it rarely has attribute attacks aligns well with our hunting criteria. Our squad has three specializing in physical combat arts, one with strong offensive power, one scout, and one for group control. I don’t think we’ll have any problems hunting Golden Mantises."
"Let’s go with that then." Jiang Xinyu snapped her fingers, finalizing the target as soon as Gong Feiyu finished speaking.
The squad hurriedly made their way toward the Golden Mantis habitat, 18 kilometers from the trial field entrance. Even at full speed, it would take at least forty minutes to reach.
"Nervous?" Wang Lan asked Xie Sisi softly.
"No... not nervous. I feel like my condition has never been better."
"Stick close to me later. Absolutely do not stray more than three meters from the squad. This is the intermediate trial field, and it’s our first time here," Jiang Xinyu added.

chapters.title: Chapter 122: That hurts, bro
chapters.content:
Chapter 122: Chapter 122: That hurts, bro
Soon, the five of them arrived at the habitat of the Golden mantis.
Normally, mantises should be jungle insects that stay on trees hunting prey. But Exotic Beasts are not true insects; even if they look very similar to mantises, their habits are entirely different.
The Golden mantis is a burrowing animal. They dig into the ground to mine and eat ore. Strangely, though, they greatly dislike staying underground and prefer basking in the sun.
Since the Golden mantis is a communal animal, when Wang Lan and the other two chose a place to rest and retreat, they arrived at the territory of the Golden mantis. Just upon arrival, a Golden mantis stood erect, staring intently at Wang Lan and the four other newcomers.
The routine was still the same.
Jiang Xinyu used ranged attacks to disturb the Golden mantis, drawing the creatures before sending them off in one fell swoop.
Indeed, under Jiang Xinyu’s ice arrows, twelve Golden mantises were attracted. When they ran, they would open their wings to flap and assist, making their charge very fast.
"The attributes of the Golden mantis are a great counter to mine; I can only manage to restrict their movements," Jiang Xinyu said, her strength having surged since learning new Star Martial Skills.
To say she couldn’t deal with the Golden mantis was certainly impossible. But powerful Star Martial Skills meant a great expenditure of Star Power. If the targets were too insignificant, using potent Star Martial Skills was pure waste.
And hindering the movements of the Golden mantises was tantamount to cutting off all their effective methods of attack. It was like laying the Golden mantises on a chopping board for easy cutting.
No sooner had her words fallen than Jiang Xinyu’s Star Martial Skill activated. The Golden mantises were fiercely charging, but suddenly a layer of frost rose from under their feet, freezing them in place like flies stuck to flypaper, utterly immobilized.
With the twelve mantises frozen, Wang Lan and the other three charged at them instantly.
This time, Xu Xiangwen did not swing his Two-handed Great Sword; instead, he split into three clones in an instant, along with his real body rushing towards four Golden mantises.
"Damn, you managed to master three clones in just one term?"
"Are you kidding? Last term I could already split into two, did you forget?" Xu Xiangwen retorted while leaping onto the back of a struggling Golden mantis.
As he raised his right hand, it was only then that Wang Lan noticed Xu Xiangwen’s arm was equipped with a metal gauntlet. With the swing of Xu Xiangwen’s fist, a surge of Star Energy Fluctuation spread out.
One punch, hammering down toward the Golden mantis’s head.
BOOM—
A loud blast erupted, making Wang Lan glance towards Xu Xiangwen in surprise.
Wang Lan had initially assumed the gauntlet was just to enhance Xu Xiangwen’s punching power. He had wondered,
Why would you punch an Exotic Beast with a head full of metallic armor instead of using a sword?
Now it was clear: Xu Xiangwen’s gauntlet was merely for protecting his fists. This term, it wasn’t just Wang Lan making rapid progress; Xu Xiangwen and Gong Feiyu had also learned new Star Martial Skills.
The sheer force of Xu Xiangwen’s punch was no less powerful than a hand grenade.
A typical Golden mantis’s strength was only at the peak of Starlight or the early stages of Star Shine, and they were also in a state of restricted movement. With one punch from Xu Xiangwen, the Golden mantis’s entire head was obliterated.
The issue was, Xu Xiangwen had three clones, and almost simultaneously, they each executed the same set of Star Martial Skills. With a BOOM, all four Golden mantises were decapitated nearly at the same time.
"Damn, going all out with such intense Star Martial Skills right off the bat? Aren’t you worried about depleting your Star Power?" Gong Feiyu exclaimed.
"The Star Power consumed can be replenished with just one Soul Bead. I took out four in one blow and still gained three, isn’t that worth it?"
The realization struck Gong Feiyu, who was prying at a Golden mantis with his blade.
He has a point. Then why the hell am I still hacking away?
He tossed aside his battle blade, and a surge of Star Power stirred. In an instant, the earth around him churned, swallowing up the four Golden mantises before him. Gong Feiyu clapped his hands together forcefully, and the four Golden mantises let out a piercing scream as they merged with the earth.
The ground undulated slightly, and four Soul Beads, like moles burrowing out, emerged from the depths.
Indeed swift!
Witnessing this, Wang Lan felt his composure crack.
These two are showing off, aren’t they? They must be. Did they even ask for my permission to show off in front of me?
Wang Lan instantly changed his strategy as well. His Flame Sword flared into existence with a WHOOSH—the Purple Flame Sword, with fire blazing at nearly ten thousand degrees.
Like a gust of wind, Wang Lan swept past the Golden mantises in front of him, and with each passing, their heads fell like plucked fruit.
In the blink of an eye, four Golden mantises were decapitated.
The three were showing off their moves without considering whether Xie Sisi, next to them, could handle it.
And at that moment, Xie Sisi clearly realized just how vast the gap was between herself and Wang Lan and the others.
Don’t think that being surpassed in close-quarters combat is the only measure of strength. Under the might of Star Martial Skills, a mere flick of their fingers could cost me my life.
My heart aches, but I can’t cry.
I know the cause of all this is my lack of resources. Being brought into the intermediate-level training ground is already a blessing for me.
Fortunately, Xie Sisi’s blade was fast and steady.
Additionally, Xie Sisi had a skill.
Her brother was a chef, and back home, he often taught Xie Sisi cooking. Xie Sisi had a keen understanding of where to cut any ingredient quickly and precisely.
So, Xie Sisi’s knife accurately stabbed into the seam in the back of the Golden mantis’s armored plate, and with a forceful slice, the head fell along the seam of the plate.
It happened so quickly, the Golden mantis didn’t even realize what was going on before it was...
on the dinner table...
no, dead.
Even if you put the Golden mantis’s head back in its place, you couldn’t see any sign of a cut. It took three or four seconds to deal with one; besides dodging the Mantis Blade and positioning oneself to strike, the speed of drawing her blade was very fast. In just three minutes, the heads of four Golden mantises were all chopped off.
"Collect the Soul Beads," Wang Lan reminded.
Xie Sisi made the same mistake he did the first time, not knowing to collect the Soul Beads.
"Oh, oh—"
Xie Sisi hurriedly set about the task, precisely slicing open the mantis’s head. The Golden mantis’s head was about the size of a bowl, yet the Soul Bead inside was not small at all.
It really makes one wonder if this creature’s brain is just the Soul Bead.
"You’re doing much better than I did initially. It took me seven to eight minutes to slay a single Exotic Beast, and you finished off four in three minutes."
"Thank you, but this time it was Xinyu who limited their movements. If it were a real fight, I might not be able to defeat even one..."
"Don’t be so modest. You’re only at the Starlight Realm. At the Starlight Realm, facing even the most common Exotic Beast means certain death, let alone Golden mantises, which are not common Exotic Beasts at all. Right, you two?"
What’s up with these two? Knowing them, they should be chiming in by now. Why are they so quiet?
ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
Wang Lan looked back only to see Jiang Xinyu’s lips twitching ever so slightly, holding back a laugh with great effort.
"Wolf King." A voice, brimming with aggrievement, sounded in his ear. Wang Lan turned his head to see Xu Xiangwen’s intense, affectionate, and startling gaze that momentarily set his heart racing.
"Whoa, I’m not into that—" Wang Lan quickly stepped back. "And yeah, I can understand if your preferences are different, but I just can’t quite grasp why you’re talking backward. Can’t you speak normally?"
"Wolf King!"
Wang Lan, seeing the expression on Xu Xiangwen’s face, realized he was not jesting and looked at him worriedly. "Do you really have a problem? Try calling me by my correct name."
"Wolf King!"
This is serious.
"You’re the one who’s sick! I’m asking you, are you or aren’t you Wolf King?"
"My name is Wang Lan, not Lan Wang!"
"Hello, Wolf, it’s nice to meet you," Gong Feiyu’s voice came from behind. It was then that Wang Lan suddenly realized that Xu Xiangwen wasn’t getting his name wrong—he was calling him the Wolf King.
The Wolf King was a nickname fans on the internet had for Wang Lan. And Wang Lan himself didn’t pay much attention to it. After the Star Martial Art Championship, he didn’t even go online to look at related forum posts or news articles.
Plus, he soon encountered the matter with the Demon Clan spy, and if Gong Feiyu hadn’t addressed him as Wolf, he would have nearly forgotten about the Star Martial Art Championship. Since he didn’t know about his internet nickname, the Wolf King, he naturally failed to catch on immediately.
"Uh... I think there’s something off about your gazes," Wang Lan said, looking at the two who were steadily closing in, his voice revealing a hint of vulnerability.
"Lanzi, you were really good at keeping us in the dark... Your acting is impressive, truly worthy of an Oscar. Still remember how you argued with me about who the Wolf was, acting like a die-hard Wolf fan..."
"Lanzi, did you know your head has a bounty of eight million out there?"
"I... Is it really that serious? I just didn’t want people to know my identity, so I entered the competition anonymously. What’s wrong with them, have they got nothing better to do?"
"Anyone who uncovers your real identity wins a reward of eight million. I really didn’t expect the poster I hung on my wall, the one I’d look at every night before sleep, to be my own bro whom I see every day."
"You can’t blame me for that," Wang Lan shrugged.
"Now that I think about it... Wolf King’s fancy footwork and his sharp close-combat fighting skills, they looked so familiar. If it hadn’t been for the Wolf King showing off two advanced Star Martial Skills, I would have confirmed it was you."
"I refuse to believe this... When did you learn two A-grade Star Martial Skills? And I’ve checked online; they say you’ve already advanced to a high level with those two A-grade skills."
"Damn! That’s unscientific!" Xu Xiangwen suddenly yelled.
"A-grade Star Martial Skills take at least five years to master fully. Unless one is a high-tier warrior learning downward, mastery is not possible in under five years. You only awakened your Star Martial Warrior talent half a year ago, and you participated in the Star Martial Art Championship just two months after your awakening. When did you learn them?"
"I learned them right after coming out of the beginner’s trial ground. What’s so strange about that? Isn’t learning things quickly just a basic operation for me?" Wang Lan said, looking at the nearly collapsing Xu Xiangwen with an expression that suggested it was perfectly natural.
"Silly boy, have you forgotten? I even learned an S-grade Star Martial Skill."
That sentence was like drawing the last bit of soul from Xu Xiangwen, leaving his expression frozen like a sculpture.
You forgot? Have you forgotten...
I really almost forgot!
This guy is a complete monster; how could I have forgotten...
But why do I suddenly feel like strangling him?
