The Eastern Heaven Gate was a place they frequented for dining, and they knew exactly where to find good food and service. After a hearty meal and singing karaoke, the five of them partied until late before going their separate ways.
With the gathering over, it was a perfect end to the ordeal at the trial ground.
Lying in bed, Wang Lan suddenly felt a sense of emptiness, as if he had been busy for a long time and suddenly found himself at a loose end, not knowing what to do.
He had plenty of skill points in the system, but due to level restrictions, there was nowhere to use them.
Wang Lan wasn’t the type to wait around. The surplus skill points needed to be converted into strength as soon as possible. Thus, the only option was to purchase Star Martial Skills.
Star Martial Skills were only sold at the Star Martial Hall, and one had to go there to purchase them, but browsing what was available could be done from home.
Thinking of it, he promptly sat up and switched on his computer.
After quickly completing identity verification, he entered the main page of the Star Martial Hall. He clicked to enter the Star Martial Skill sales center...
Damn it, what is this trash?
Last time Jiang Xinyu was at the Star Martial Hall, she had packed up three A-grade Star Martial Skills. This time, however, when Wang Lan scanned through, there wasn’t a single A-grade Star Martial Skill to be found. There were only five or six B-grade ones at most. Almost all the Star Martial Skills were either C or D-grade.
"The Star Martial Hall is getting worse and worse. I’m not even expecting any S-grade Star Martial Skills anymore, but at least give me some A-grade options," Wang Lan muttered to himself while searching.
He didn’t know the cost of living until he took charge; he started with a platinum-grade Phoenix form and got two A-grade Star Martial Skills right at the beginning. But for an ordinary Star Martial Warrior, what even was an A-grade Star Martial Skill?
Heard of it, never seen it,
they’d say.
B-grade Star Martial Skills were peerless secret tomes; C-grade were treasures. If there was a C-grade Star Martial Skill that fit, you bit the bullet and bought it. Don’t underestimate these lower-level Star Martial Skills—they can save your life at critical moments.
After refreshing several times and still not finding anything satisfactory, Wang Lan felt utterly disappointed.
Even if these skill points rot, I won’t waste them on these C-grade or B-grade ones.
Just as he was about to close the page, a pop-up window appeared.
"Haven’t found a Star Martial Skill to your liking? Then try the Wishlist Registration. Register your desired Star Martial Skill according to the prompts. When a suitable Star Martial Skill is available in the library, a notification will be sent. The Star Martial Hall wishes every Star Martial Warrior can possess a satisfactory Star Martial Skill."
A fine promise, that every Star Martial Warrior can possess a satisfactory Star Martial Skill,
Wang Lan thought.
But in reality, most powerful Star Martial Skills are controlled by the Star Martial families. Or you must enroll in a Star Martial Academy of the corresponding grade to have access to them.
Moreover, good Star Martial Skills are so expensive that ordinary people can only kneel before the price and sigh with longing.
But Wang Lan still chose to register.
Wang Lan had already done a data analysis on his shortcomings. His position was that of a close-combat support. Although he was thriving on this path, it wasn’t enough for Wang Lan. As a support, he was already tired of watching cooldowns.
What type of Star Martial Skill do you hope for?
He, of course, chose offense.
As a support who’s better at healing myself than others, why would I need defense? I’ll take the hits when I can, and if I can’t, I’ll just heal myself and keep going.
What type of attack do you hope for?Follow current novᴇls on novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
It must be long-range,
he decided.
For close-quarters combat, I have Star Cloud Sword Dance for evasion and Flame Sword for damage output. Star Cloud Sword Dance also offers confusion, positioning, control, and other functions. I’m not lacking in close-combat options.
Do you hope your Star Martial Skill is an attribute change or a form change?
Either is fine,
he thought.
If it’s an attribute change, then naturally, it would be fire-type.
What grade do you wish your Star Martial Skill to be?
Wang Lan really wanted to select S-grade, but there was no S-grade option.
Could it be that the Star Martial Hall itself believes S-grade Star Martial Skills are too unlikely to appear in their offerings, so they simply removed the choice?
So the S-grade section in the Star Martial Skill library is a redundant design? Then why put it there in the first place?
Registration complete, submitted to the database. He closed the computer and continued to lie in bed, browsing Tianjian Bureau intel, keeping an eye on the condition of his brothers.
"Report!"
"Come in!"
Wang Qianfeng pushed open the door to Lu Zhao’s office.
"Director! The investigation results are out, and they are far from Ruyi."
"What’s the matter? A few Star Martial Warriors’ identities shouldn’t pose a challenge to you, the intelligence chief, right?"
"They’re not ordinary Star Martial Warriors. No, they are Star Martial Warriors without identities. The ones who entered the trial ground had forged identities. When we followed the leads from their Star Martial Badges, we found the original owners were still pioneering in a Different Dimensional Space. Not to mention the ones Wang Lan killed, even if they hadn’t been killed, they couldn’t possibly appear in two places at the same time."
"Hmm? The Star Martial Badge contains verification information. The central system would raise an alarm if two people with the same identity appeared in different places."
"Indeed, but... the Star Martial Warrior monitoring database has been tampered with. The person who tampered with it died in a car accident two years ago, and it’s too long gone to trace back now."
"So you’re saying that these people were selected and this plan was set in motion two years ago?"
"It appears so."
"What about face recognition?"
"Here’s where it gets even trickier. The people in the intermediate trial grounds, their appearances matched those on the Star Martial Badges exactly. It’s as if they are... clones of those Star Martial Warriors. But I’ve confirmed they’re absolutely not clones. Their Star Martial Skills, behavioral habits, and even the DNA we’ve retrieved are all different. The DNA database has only begun to be properly established in the past decade, and there’s still a large number of Star Martial Warriors not yet registered. These sixteen individuals are like people who simply don’t exist; not a trace of them can be found."
Lu Zhao’s brow furrowed. He leaned back in his chair and pondered for a moment.
This is more complicated than I imagined.
"But no matter how complicated, we will investigate thoroughly. It will just... take time."
"Currently, the Demon Clan has not made any substantial moves. Especially after we learned about their Ant Hill Plan, they should lie low for a while. Take your time with the search, but make sure to be thorough!"
"Understood!"

chapters.title: Chapter 130 Siblings, Equally Savage
chapters.content:
Chapter 130: Chapter 130 Siblings, Equally Savage
Twenty-fourth, Little New Year’s Eve.
Wang Lan wore a down jacket for the first time, bundled up like a panda as he stepped out the door.
In truth, fire-attribute Star Martial Warriors weren’t afraid of the cold; if they felt the temperature drop, a slight surge of Star Power circulating through their bodies felt even better than being covered in heat packs.
Because he was riding an electric scooter to his aunt’s house, Wang Lan was dressed so warmly. His aunt had called that morning, inviting Wang Lan over for dinner.
He skillfully entered the apartment complex and parked his scooter in the underground garage of his aunt’s building. Upstairs, he punched in the code. As the door opened, two pairs of wide eyes stared at him simultaneously.
Wang Lan was slightly taken aback, surprised to see Hu Feifei at his aunt’s place.
"Wang Lan, you’re here? Change into your own slippers; don’t get the floor dirty," Song Jia said, her tone casual but carrying the air of the mistress of the house.
"Jiajia, with the floor like this... is there even any space left to get dirty?" Wang Lan said speechlessly, scanning the floor littered with potato chip bags, nutshells, and paper airplanes.
"It’s a bit messy, but I’ll clean it up in a bit," Song Jia’s face turned red as she quickly assembled the interlocking toy in front of her.
Hu Feifei, however, had already put down what she was holding and hurriedly stood up, timidly approaching Wang Lan.
"Feifei, how do you know Jiajia? Don’t you recognize your Big Brother anymore?" Wang Lan asked with a smile as he gently ruffled her hair.
Unexpectedly, Hu Feifei suddenly hugged Wang Lan’s waist. "Big Brother, after I was discharged from the hospital, you never came to see me... A few days ago, I missed you and tried calling, but I couldn’t get through."
"Those few days, Big Brother was training in the practice area, and my phone was switched off."
However, such a warm scene caused a pang of jealousy in Song Jia’s heart.
The affection between Song Jia and Wang Lan was definitely not something ordinary cousins could compare to. Wang Lan had been brought home by Wang Ling, and aside from his aunt, he had no other relatives. Thus, Song Jia became Wang Lan’s only sister.
It was much the same for Song Jia. After her father had an accident during an experiment, Wang Qi hadn’t even let Song Zifeng’s family know of her own existence, let alone Song Jia’s. To Song Jia, the only family she had in the world was her mother and Wang Lan.
Although the two occasionally bickered, their affection for each other was incredibly strong. The last dangerous incident had made it evident that Song Jia trusted Wang Lan enormously when she was scared, wishing she could always hide in his embrace.
Sometimes Wang Lan would compare Song Jia to Jiang Xinchen. Though both were like sisters to him, Jiang Xinchen was well-behaved and sensible, while Song Jia was rather haughty.
But now, seeing her good friend hugging Wang Lan so intimately and even calling him "Big Brother"? My position is clearly threatened!
You, Wang Lan! You already have this princess, yet you dare to flirt with someone else’s sister? Is this princess not cute anymore?
Angry, Song Jia stopped playing with her toy; CLATTER! It fell apart instantly. She hopped off the sofa, walked over in her slippers, pulled Hu Feifei away, and hid her behind herself.
Raising her head, she gave Wang Lan a look that was both sharp and adorably blank, leaving him utterly baffled.
"Wang Lan, Feifei’s so young, how could you even think of laying a hand on her? Are you even human?"
Wang Lan’s expression froze for a moment. Though initially perplexed, his face quickly darkened.
What am I going to do with this sister? At such a young age... to think that... Have elementary school students really reached this point?
"Jiajia, Big Brother didn’t bully me," Feifei timidly tugged at Song Jia’s clothes as she spoke.
"You don’t understand. Bullying doesn’t have to be direct; there are many ways to bully someone. Direct bullying is beating you up. Indirect bullying is getting someone else to beat you up. And the most despicable kind is to deceive you.
The teacher just taught us last month that we girls must learn to be vigilant and always be careful to protect ourselves. Some people show a caring face, yet who knows what they’re plotting deep down..."
This is getting more and more outrageous... Listening to her, what does she take me for? I can’t stand this!
"Jiajia, Big Brother’s face is turning dark; he’s unhappy."
"It’s fine, I’m used to it. How did you and Jiajia get to know each other, Feifei? I remember you two aren’t classmates, right?" Wang Lan asked, changing the subject.
"Well, let me tell you! Feifei is now my classmate and my deskmate," Song Jia declared. "I’m warning you, Hu Feifei is under my protection. You’re not allowed to have any ideas about her. Otherwise, Humph!"
"Feifei, you’re at Duo Lun School too?" Wang Lan asked in astonishment. Duo Lun School’s annual tuition fees were quite expensive. Even with Hu Qing working for the police, considering the previous impoverished state of Hu Qing’s family, it seemed unlikely they could afford such fees.
"Nope, I’m at Tang Town Elementary School," Hu Feifei said, confused.
"Duo Lun School? That place is history, okay?" Song Jia said scornfully. "Have you forgotten what happened last time? So many people died; no one could let Duo Lun School off the hook. Anyway, the headmaster and the school board were exposed for many crimes and got arrested by the guards.
My mom transferred me to Tang Town Elementary School before the start of last semester, so I’ve been in fourth grade there since school began. Honestly, whether it’s a prestigious school or a regular one, they’re all pretty much the same.
At first, a few clueless fools bullied us transfer students, but they quieted down after a few beatings. Feifei transferred after National Day, and I really don’t get why those idiots love picking on new students so much.
They dared to call Feifei a ’little nun’ and made her cry. As someone so filled with a sense of justice, how could I possibly tolerate that?"
"Then you gave them another good beating?" Wang Lan asked nervously.
"No!" Song Jia shook her head resolutely. "One beating wouldn’t be enough. I beat them for three days!"ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
"Seriously!" Wang Lan was momentarily at a loss for words to praise Song Jia and could only raise a thumb in a gesture of slight respect. "You behave like this at school? Does Aunt know?"
"How could I let her know? I gave each of those dummies a hundred yuan to buy snacks. They scurried off laughing like they’d gotten a great deal. But I heard they got another beating from their parents when they went home."
"And why was that?"
"Simple. They didn’t spend the hundred yuan on snacks or hide it. Instead, they bought a toy and swaggered home with it. Then, the next day, their parents came to school asking if the hundred yuan came from me.
You know what I did then? Could I admit to it? Of course not! I denied any knowledge. So, those dummies got beaten by their parents, who accused them of stealing money from home. Sigh..."
After listening to Song Jia, Wang Lan shivered. "This was all part of your plan, wasn’t it?"
"As if!"
"When you beat them up, you made sure it happened where no one would see. But everyone knows you had a fight with them. I guess there’s a missing piece to the story," Wang Lan said teasingly, stroking his chin while looking at Song Jia, who was holding a plushie on the sofa.
"You even know that? After I beat them up, I reported them to the teacher. I’m still a good little student in the teacher’s eyes... But I didn’t make it sound too serious. I just said they were trying to bully me and pushed me, but didn’t actually hit me."
"Naturally. If you’d made it sound serious, the teacher might have called their parents. Then, word could’ve reached Aunt. You wouldn’t want that. You just needed the teacher to know there was bad blood between you and them."
"All I did was ensure they wouldn’t dare trouble me again. It was legitimate self-defense!"
"Then you secretly gave them money to set them up."
"I’m just a girl, and there were three or four of them. What if they sought revenge later? Giving them money was like an apology. I couldn’t do it openly, so of course, it had to be done privately."
"You had it all planned out from the start! Don’t try to wriggle out of it!" Wang Lan tapped Song Jia’s forehead lightly and said, "This strategy is one I taught you. You might fool others with these tricks, but can you fool me?
"For ordinary kids to suddenly have an extra hundred yuan for toys, their parents would definitely get suspicious. They’d naturally say it was from you, and all three or four of them would stick to the same story.
"You even had another backup plan, but thankfully you didn’t take things too far. If you had admitted to giving them the money when their parents asked, they would have been accused of extortion. They might even have been expelled from school, right?
"Your classmates all knew about your conflict with them, and so did your teacher. With that setup, any explanation they gave would be worthless. How can you be so adept with such schemes at such a young age?"
Song Jia pouted and turned her face away. "If their parents hadn’t had a fairly decent attitude and tone, I would’ve boldly admitted it right in front of the teacher. And I would’ve added that they cornered me and snatched the money from me. Humph!"
Wang Lan and Song Jia both knew exactly what was going on, but Hu Feifei, who was standing to the side, was completely confused. Her curious eyes darted back and forth between Wang Lan and Song Jia.
CLICK—
The lock turned, and the front door opened.
Aunt Wang Qi appeared at the doorway dressed in a black suit.
"Mom! You’re back! You must be tired. Let me get your slippers..." Song Jia instantly ran over, eagerly trying to curry favor.
"And next, my little Jiajia is trying to subtly find out when Mom got home and how long I was standing at the door, right?" Wang Qi’s smile was as radiant as spring sunshine, but the smile on Song Jia’s face gradually faded.
Suddenly, Song Jia turned to Wang Lan and glared. "Wang Lan, did you set me up?"
"I didn’t say a word. You confessed everything yourself."
"Mom has been so busy with company matters lately, I didn’t realize my good daughter had unknowingly accomplished such a big thing... We’ll have a good chat tonight," Wang Qi said.
"Auntie, hello... Auntie, Jiajia only argued with those people to help me. Could you please not scold her? If anyone needs to be scolded, please scold me..." Hu Feifei pleaded.
"Ah, what a sweet little girl. Are you Jiajia’s deskmate? What’s your name?"
"I’m Hu Feifei! Big Brother Wang Lan knows me too."
Wang Qi looked up at Wang Lan.
"Her brother and I are friends. His name is Hu Qing, and he works for the police now. Feifei was unwell for a long time and spent a lot of time in the hospital, but she’s fully recovered now," Wang Lan explained.
"By the way, Feifei, how’s your Star Power control coming along? Do you practice regularly at home?"
"I practice every day. My brother says I’m pretty good at it, but I still need to work hard. Right now, I can only achieve 3.0 mixed control." As she said this, a sweet smile spread across Hu Feifei’s face.
"Wait a second!" Suddenly, Song Jia looked at Hu Feifei, baffled. "Feifei, you’re a Star Martial Warrior?"
"Yep. I awakened at the end of September this year. I only went back to school after I gained full control."
"You... you’re a Star Martial Warrior, and you still let them bully you? Why didn’t you fight back when they pushed you?"
"My brother said... Star Martial Warriors aren’t supposed to attack ordinary people," Hu Feifei stated matter-of-factly.

chapters.title: Chapter 131: Has the Crow’s Mouth Come True?
chapters.content:
Chapter 131: Chapter 131: Has the Crow’s Mouth Come True?
"Are you stupid?" Song Jia’s eyes were filled with a resentful gaze, looking at Hu Feifei with disappointment.
"But if anyone bullies Jiajia, I’ll definitely help you beat them up," Hu Feifei quickly added.
"Feifei, fighting... is wrong," Wang Lan said. "You should get along well with your classmates. If someone wants to argue, I’m not saying you should let them win, but you can ignore them. Your brother is a guard, so that’s why he tells you these things. Actually... a Star Martial Warrior shouldn’t use offensive Star Martial Skills against ordinary people, but purely defensive ones are fine. Moreover, as long as a Star Martial Warrior doesn’t attack ordinary people with Star Martial Skills, throwing a couple of punches or kicks isn’t really a problem. I’m not inciting you to fight; I’m just telling you not to be bullied easily. Although the schools in Jade Country have the best management in the world, school bullying objectively exists. We don’t bully others, but we can’t let others bully us."
"Mhm, I understand," Hu Feifei obediently nodded.
"Tonight’s Little New Year’s Eve, Feifei. Why don’t you stay and have dinner with us? I’ve already ordered the meal; it should be delivered in about half an hour," Wang Lan’s aunt said.
"Thank you, Auntie, but I don’t need to. My brother just sent me a message. He’s off work now and will come to pick me up soon."
"Since he’s coming, he can join us too," Wang Lan said. "Here, let me give your brother a call."
As she spoke, she took out her phone and dialed.
Hu Qing was driving, but his car phone didn’t interfere. He knew Feifei was visiting a classmate’s home today but didn’t expect this classmate to be Wang Lan’s cousin.
Fate is such a curious thing,
Hu Qing thought.
I never imagined the world could be this small.
When Wang Lan saw Hu Qing, her expression tensed. Hu Qing looked gloomy, with deeply sunken cheeks and bloodshot eyes. A mustache under his nose added an air of maturity and fierceness to his appearance.
It’s only been a month since I last saw him,
Wang Lan thought.
How could he have changed so much?
"Brother Hu, what happened to you?"
"Oh?" Hu Qing was initially taken aback but quickly understood. As if changing masks, he flashed a smile. The moment the smile appeared, the gloom and chill on his face melted away as if scorched by intense fire.
The same face transformed in an instant, making him seem like two different people. This sudden change of expression left Wang Lan stunned.
"How was that? Isn’t my acting top-notch? I practiced camouflage and infiltration in the army. The tip you gave us last time led us to uncover something much deeper. It turns out all those visible gangs we saw were just small-time operations; the situation is far more complex than it appears. I’m now on a mission to infiltrate the enemy, and for my identity... well, I’m conveniently borrowing Lang’s. My sister’s illness was cured, but not by you. It was because I agreed to sell myself to a gang leader in exchange for some black-market advanced technology treatment. I now have the lives of several guards and over a dozen other people on my hands; there’s no turning back. Just now, did my expression look like that of an extremist who’s gone completely off the deep end, someone antisocial and anti-humanity?"
"Damn... I was wrong. You really should have become an actor in the first place."
"Hahaha... I thought so too. Enough talk for now. We can wrap things up after the New Year, and I’ll treat you to a meal then."Follow current novᴇls on NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
Wang Lan quickly covered Hu Qing’s mouth with her hand. "Don’t you know you shouldn’t jinx it like that?"
"Lanzi, you actually believe in that stuff?"
"It’s something countless predecessors have proven with tragic consequences; it’s better to be careful. I’ve heard going undercover is very dangerous."
"Don’t worry, everything is under control."
Since Hu Qing currently had a different identity, it wasn’t appropriate for Wang Lan to invite him in for dinner. She casually said goodbye and watched his car drive away.
Back home, Song Jia was dutifully cleaning the living room she had turned into a mess throughout the day. Her pitiful, aggrieved expression was enough to make anyone’s heart ache. Wang Lan immediately grabbed a broom, about to help, when her aunt called her over.
"Let her clean it by herself. You come and talk to me."
"Auntie, please don’t punish her. Honestly, I think she did a good job. To handle things so well at such a young age, she’s guaranteed not to be at a disadvantage in the future."
"I’m not punishing her. Doing household chores is an essential life skill she needs to master. When you were her age, you were already living alone in Xinyu Building." Her aunt had changed out of her uniform and into casual home clothes—a very light and breezy outfit.
Although there’s no central heating in the south, for wealthy families, things like heating and air conditioning weren’t an issue as long as they had money. The temperature outside was approaching zero degrees Celsius, but indoors it was a comfortable twenty-seven or twenty-eight degrees; one wouldn’t even feel cold in short sleeves.
Her aunt sat in an armchair on the balcony and sighed deeply.
"What’s wrong? Are you tired?" Wang Lan asked with concern.
"Very tired, but also very excited! The company’s Gene Potion has achieved a breakthrough, and it’s now in the clinical trial phase. We expect good news in the next few days. Once the clinical trial results are out, people will be able to use genetic coding to treat most diseases originating from the body itself. By then, hereditary diseases and most types of cancer could be completely cured."
"Really? That’s incredible!"
"Of course, it’s incredible..." As her aunt spoke, her eyes showed not only pride but also a faint trace of sorrow.
"The research your uncle left behind ten years ago... it took me eleven years just to begin to truly understand it. Compared to him, I feel like a complete idiot. If he were alive, human biotechnology would have advanced by at least fifty years..."
"Uncle... was a true genius," Wang Lan sighed regretfully.
Actually, Wang Lan didn’t know much about her uncle. When she was very young, she had only met Song Zifeng a few times. He was a somewhat scholarly young man who didn’t talk much.
However, she had heard her mother, Wang Ling, say that Song Zifeng was one of the rarest, most exceptional talents she had ever encountered. His genius was comparable to any of the greatest scientists in human history.
Unfortunately, heaven is often jealous of exceptional talent. At the young age of twenty-six, Song Zifeng died prematurely due to a malfunction in an experimental apparatus.
Previously, Wang Lan hadn’t understood the full weight of her mother’s praise for him. But now, knowing Wang Ling’s true identity, she felt an even deeper regret for Song Zifeng’s death.
Her aunt was already one of the country’s top scientists in biotechnology, yet it had taken her ten years just to begin to grasp the research Song Zifeng had produced a decade prior.
By the time Song Jia had nearly finished cleaning, the takeout her aunt had ordered arrived.
The three of them were at home, toasting to celebrate Little New Year’s Eve. As dinner progressed, fireworks suddenly filled the night sky over Suzhou City.
DING-DONG—
Xie Sisi sent a celebratory text message: "Wang Lan, Happy Little New Year’s Eve! The fireworks outside are so beautiful."
DING-DONG—
Jiang Xinyu sent a text, but it was just two words: "Cheers."
Then, that guy Xu Xiangwen also sent a long string of messages, with the classic ending: "Whoever doesn’t forward this will be single forever..."
Definitely his style,
Wang Lan thought.
His aunt had wanted Wang Lan to stay over, but he still chose to take his leave.
After Little New Year’s Eve, the festive atmosphere in Suzhou City grew even stronger. Supermarkets played New Year’s songs, and every place he went was a sea of vibrant red and joyous celebration.
Even though Wang Lan was alone, he believed celebrating the New Year, even by himself, had to be filled with a sense of ceremony.
Sweeping away the dust, bidding farewell to the old year, and decorating his home—Wang Lan had to do all of this himself. It was only at this time of year that he truly felt what an extravagance it was to live alone in a four to five-hundred-square-meter house.
Cleaning up is so exhausting,
he thought.
It took Wang Lan an entire day to clean the house. That was even with him using the Star Cloud Dance; otherwise, with conventional cleaning methods, it would have easily taken three or four days.
Wang Lan then made another trip to the supermarket, buying spring couplets, "Fu" character posters, fireworks, peace knots, and other festive decorations, filling an entire shopping cart.
Driving home, he found the roads of Suzhou City very empty as it was the end of the year; hardly anyone was around. He leisurely drove to the entrance of his underground parking garage.
The barrier lifted. Just as Wang Lan was about to drive down, he suddenly slammed on the brakes.
Through the rearview mirror, out of the corner of his eye, he caught sight of something lying in the flowerbed near the entrance.
Wang Lan got out of the car and cautiously approached the flowerbed. A person was lying prone there, their condition unknown—dead or alive.
Carefully, he reached out and checked the person’s neck for a pulse. It was there—faint, but present. The person was alive. Wang Lan gently turned them over. Their face was covered in blood, and their body was soaked in it too.
When Wang Lan clearly saw the person’s face, his expression changed drastically.
"Hu Qing!"
He quickly carried Hu Qing to the car. While driving into the underground garage, he pressed one hand against Hu Qing’s chest, healing him.
By the time Wang Lan parked the car, Hu Qing’s life-threatening injuries had mostly stabilized.
Wang Lan hurriedly carried Hu Qing out of the car and took the elevator back to his apartment.
"It’s only been two days since I last saw you, and you’ve already gotten into an accident! I told you back then that you shouldn’t have tempted fate, but you didn’t listen! You’re lucky you ran into me. Otherwise, the next time we ’chatted,’ I’d be lighting incense for you."
Stripping off Hu Qing’s clothes revealed a shocking sight. Besides knife wounds, Hu Qing’s body had over a dozen gunshot wounds. He was riddled with so many holes he almost looked like a beehive.
If it weren’t for the nearly abnormal physical defense of a Star Martial Warrior, coupled with Hu Qing’s Earth Attribute Star Martial Skills for protection, so many gunshot wounds would have certainly killed him long ago.
There were more than ten bullet entry wounds, but none had penetrated deep enough to damage his internal organs. Even so, due to excessive blood loss, Hu Qing was in a critical condition.
Without hesitation, Wang Lan immediately began to heal him. He worked for a full three minutes, consuming half of his Star Power, to repair Hu Qing’s injuries. However, there was nothing Wang Lan could do about the massive amount of blood Hu Qing had already lost.
Was Hu Qing’s undercover mission exposed? Or did something else unexpected happen?
Wang Lan wondered. To know the exact situation, he would have to wait for Hu Qing to regain consciousness.
"Wang Lan, the situation is a bit problematic," Xiao Ai’s voice suddenly sounded.
"What is it?"
"Unauthorized individuals have entered the building."
"How many?"
"Thirty!"
"They must be the ones chasing Hu Qing. Connect to the security cameras and track all of them."
The television screen in front of him lit up, displaying more than a dozen feeds. Some intruders were taking the stairs, some were in the elevators, and others had reached the underground parking garage, attempting to breach the security door of the second basement level.
"There’s no one else in the building, right?"
"Everyone has already gone home from work."
Wang Lan’s Xinyu Building primarily rented office space to high-end, high-paying companies. These companies strictly adhered to national labor laws regarding working hours and rarely had employees work overtime. Even if they occasionally did, everyone would definitely be gone after six o’clock.
Although each company might only have a few dozen employees, any one of these thirty-odd companies boasted an annual profit exceeding one hundred million. This often made Wang Lan quite envious, to the point where he had even considered raising the rent.
"Cut the power to all floors below the top floor."
"Understood!" Xiao Ai replied.
CLICK!
Instantly, the entire Xinyu Building, except for the top floor, plunged into darkness.
Seven or eight people were trapped in the elevators.

chapters.title: Chapter 132: You Also Died Because of Underestimating the Enemy
chapters.content:
Chapter 132: Chapter 132: You Also Died Because of Underestimating the Enemy
"What’s going on?"Thᴇ link to the origɪn of this information rᴇsts ɪn
"Did some idiot accidentally bump into the circuit breaker?"
"Could it be Hu Lang?"
"Impossible. He’s been shot so many times, he’s probably dead by now. But no matter what, we must find that item."
With a Bluetooth earpiece, Wang Lan listened to Xiao Ai’s report on enemy distribution. By the time he reached this floor, Wang Lan no longer needed Xiao Ai’s reports.
The sudden blackout was a blatantly abnormal situation. Truly elite warriors would have immediately sought cover. Not only did these men fail to do so, but they even felt like chatting?
To call them a ragtag bunch would be a compliment; they were a group of idiots who didn’t even know how to spell ’death’.
In an instant, Wang Lan’s figure transformed into a streak of light at the stairwell entrance.
"What was that?" A cry of surprise erupted instantly from the corridor opposite.
Star Martial Skills were all well and good, but there was one problem—their damn light effects couldn’t be turned off. Wang Lan didn’t understand the deal with these light effects. Unless one inherently possessed stealth, other Star Martial Skills, or talents for hiding, activating a Star Martial Skill would not only cause Spirit Power Fluctuations around the user but also generate light effects as distinct and dazzling as fireflies in the night.
When Wang Lan burst out of the stairwell, the others weren’t blind; they all saw him. But seeing him was one thing; reacting in time was another.
Almost at the exact moment they managed to draw their guns, Wang Lan weaved through the four men before him as nimbly as a butterfly flitting through flowers.
One punch each, and the four of them didn’t even manage to utter a complete sentence before Wang Lan knocked them out cold.
Wang Lan immediately deactivated the Star Martial Skill. His figure vanished like a Ghost, disappearing with several swift flashes.
These four intruders lacked experience, but I feel like I’ve also made a basic mistake. Was there a need to use the Star Moon Sword Dance Star Martial Skill against these ordinary people? Wouldn’t it have been better to just knock them out under the cover of darkness?
Thinking this, Wang Lan rapidly adjusted his tactics. The voice in his earpiece reported more people making their way up the stairs, two floors below him.
Each of them carried a tactical flashlight.
Wang Lan tiptoed silently and swiftly down the stairs, then hid in a corner. In contrast, the three people below made noise intermittently as they climbed.
"Hiss—damn it, I kicked the handrail!"
"Can you shut the hell up? You scared the crap out of me."
"Damn it, don’t shine that flashlight in my eyes! I can’t see a thing in this pitch-black darkness! Where’s the damn circuit breaker? How are we supposed to find anyone if we can’t even find an exit in this mess?"
THUD! THUD! THUD!
Three dull thumps, and the world went silent.
From the seventh floor down to the underground parking garage, Wang Lan moved like a Ghost dancing in the night. Xiao Ai had reported thirty hostiles, and Wang Lan silently neutralized every one of them in the darkness. His descent was as swift as lightning and flowed seamlessly, taking less than half an hour.
Wang Lan commanded, "Lights on!"
CLICK!
All the lights in the underground parking garage flickered on.
Before Wang Lan lay five or six men, scattered about. Each had been knocked into a deep unconsciousness by a single punch. Their flashlights lay strewn across the ground.
DING!
The elevator doors suddenly slid open on the second basement level of the parking garage. Seven or eight men, cursing loudly, rushed out.
"Damn, that scared me to death! Why did the power suddenly go out? We almost got trapped in there..."
THUMP! THUMP! THUMP!
One by one, as they emerged, Wang Lan struck them down. In under three seconds, all seven or eight men were unconscious at the elevator entrance.
CLAP. CLAP. CLAP.
Just as Wang Lan was deciding his next move, crisp applause echoed through the garage.
Wang Lan’s expression changed drastically. He swiftly turned around, warily staring at a middle-aged man who, despite the cold winter, wore only a short, traditional-style jacket over his bare upper body, his muscular arms exposed.
The man’s face bore a cross-shaped scar, and his hair, the color of fire, spiked upwards. His brawny arms were covered in blue tattoos.
The man looked at Wang Lan mockingly, stepping closer bit by bit. With each step, the intensely powerful aura of a Star Cloud Stage expert emanated from him.
This man is a master, definitely a superior opponent for me right now. Without activating my Phoenix Form, I might not be able to beat him. But I’m reluctant to use the Phoenix Form... Besides, I can’t be sure if there’s anyone else lurking in the building.
Xiao Ai hadn’t warned Wang Lan about this man at all. While Wang Lan was still trying to figure out how to deal with this newcomer, the man spoke first.
"I never expected to accidentally bump into a Star Martial Warrior. You’re quite young. Still a student, I presume? If you’re a student, you should be focusing on your studies, ’studying hard and improving every day,’ as they say. What are you doing playing hero so late at night? Think you’re in some White Eagle Country action flick?"
A glint flashed in Wang Lan’s eyes.
This guy clearly didn’t expect me. He probably had no idea I was here before entering the Xinyu Building. That explains why those thugs I took down seemed so fearless and brazen when they entered the building.
"Your words don’t make sense. A bunch of unidentified people broke into my home. What, you expect me to pretend I didn’t see?"
"Your home?" The man looked at Wang Lan with doubt.
"The Xinyu Building is mine. You barge into my property and act like you’re in the right?"
"My apologies for this. We were chasing an enemy, and he fled in here. We pursued without much thought. Little brother, perhaps you could help us? If you hand him over, we’ll pretend tonight never happened. How about it?"
"Pretend it never happened? I can’t just pretend it never happened. What happened today is clearly your fault. Even if I slaughtered all these Muggles, it would be considered self-defense, wouldn’t it?"
Wang Lan instantly shifted his demeanor, adopting the persona of someone who didn’t want trouble but had been innocently dragged into a messy situation.
"How do you want to settle this?"
"You trespassed on my property and caused considerable damage to the Xinyu Building. Demanding a few million in compensation isn’t unreasonable, is it?"
"Never mind a few million; I’d give you ten million. But you have to hand over the person we’re looking for."
"I have no idea who entered my home. I was just doing my homework when your intrusion triggered the alarm system. What does the person you’re looking for look like? I don’t want to get involved in your business. You pay the money, take the person, and it’ll be like you were never here."
"His appearance? I have a photo right here." Saying this, the man reached into his pocket.
But in that instant, Wang Lan’s figure became a streak of light, charging at him. He activated Butterfly Passing Through Flowers, instantly lunging forward. The ten-meter distance was covered in less than half a second.
The man was still in the process of pulling out the photo, completely unprepared for Wang Lan’s sudden assault. By the time he realized what was happening, Wang Lan was already striking at his face.
The man proved himself to be a battle-hardened expert, immediately countering even in such a dire situation.
A concrete wall erupted before him, enclosing him like two halves of a ’Kinder Egg’. Normally, such a response to a surprise attack would be flawless and unassailable.
Unfortunately for him, he was facing Wang Lan—someone who defied all common sense.
Almost instantly, Wang Lan switched Star Martial Skills. A Flame Sword materialized from his hands. He crossed his palms, and a vertical Flame Sword formed before him.
Like a streak of light, Wang Lan’s figure skimmed past the ’Kinder Egg’ shell, his Flame Sword etching a perfectly straight, narrow gash upon the ground.
As the Flame Sword extinguished, a sharp CRACK echoed from the ’Kinder Egg’ construct behind Wang Lan. It then began to crumble, like a shattered eggshell.
Inside the remains of the earthen shell, the man’s lower body was already sinking into the ground. Unfortunately for him, his attempt to escape underground was too slow. He had never anticipated Wang Lan would unleash a vertical Flame Sword so instantaneously.
Thus, as the Flame Sword swept past, it cleanly bisected his upper body.
Wang Lan’s shift from feigned negotiation to sudden attack was utterly without warning. The man had utterly failed to anticipate Wang Lan’s combat tactics. The swift kill was a result of Wang Lan’s decisiveness, a touch of luck, and, crucially, the man’s underestimation of his opponent.
He would never have dreamed that a seemingly ordinary high school student possessed not only the strength of the Star Shine Stage but had also mastered two incredibly lethal A-rank Star Martial Skills.
What’s more, he couldn’t have imagined that both Star Martial Skills had been cultivated to such a profound level.
Thus, this early-stage Star Cloud Stage Earth Attribute Star Martial Warrior lost pitifully and died a miserable death.
Even as he was bisected, an expression of utter disbelief and shock was etched on the man’s face.
Why the hell use a vertical Flame Sword? Wouldn’t a horizontal one have worked?
System Notification: Cross-level kill completed. Reward: 1,000 Experience Points, 20 Skill Points.
BANG!
The notification in his mind chimed almost simultaneously with the sharp crack of a nearby gunshot.
Wang Lan’s body jerked violently. He looked down in shock as a bullet hole blossomed on his chest, right over his heart. Blood gushed out.
Clutching his chest, Wang Lan collapsed, a bewildered expression on his face.
Blood flowed through his fingers in torrents.
Firearms could still inflict fatal harm upon Star Martial Warriors. At least before one reached the Galaxy Stage, a rifle’s lethality was comparable to a B-rank pure-attack Star Martial Skill.
Wang Lan hadn’t anticipated another hidden assassin. This one had successfully evaded Xiao Ai’s camera surveillance and fired a deadly shot when Wang Lan was completely defenseless.
From behind a load-bearing pillar in the garage, a young man dressed in black slowly emerged. He seemed to defy gravity, walking on the ceiling as if it were solid ground.
The distinct sound of footsteps echoed from the ceiling. Reaching a point directly above Wang Lan, the young man dropped down, landing before the corpse of the middle-aged Star Martial Warrior Wang Lan had killed—the one whose lower body was still embedded in the earth.
The young man slowly removed his hat, his low voice drifting out.
"I always knew your arrogance would be your undoing; I just didn’t expect it to be this soon. But don’t worry, I’ve avenged you. We were supposed to leave together after this last job... Looks like we’re both leaving, just not together anymore."
Suddenly, the young man in black felt the ground beneath him give way, his body lurching downwards as if he’d stepped off an unseen ledge.
Astonishment flickered across the young man’s face.
There wasn’t a pit here before, was there? How did I suddenly fall into one?
Then, in an instant, he realized it wasn’t a pit. His legs had been cleanly severed at the thighs.
While astonishment still painted his features, another streak of flame flashed before his eyes. His arms flew off, like discarded toys, landing some distance away.
Only then did the searing pain from his severed limbs register in the young man’s brain. His face twisted into a grotesque, terrifying grimace.
"AAAAARGH—!"
A Shadow fell over the young man’s face. Wang Lan, who he’d thought dead, now stood before him, completely unscathed. The young man’s gaze instinctively darted to where the gunshot wound on Wang Lan’s chest should have been.
What the actual f*ck... Not even a scratch? Then what was all that blood gushing like a fountain just moments ago?
At that moment, a single, eloquent thought dominated the young man’s mind:
FML.
"Looks like you’ll be dying from underestimation too," Wang Lan’s low voice rumbled, laced with thick killing intent. "And it seems you will be ’leaving together’ after all."

chapters.title: Chapter 133: The Whereabouts of the Demonic Transformation Potion
chapters.content:
Chapter 133: Chapter 133: The Whereabouts of the Demonic Transformation Potion
I was nearly killed, really. Good thing the Healing Star Martial Arts had upgraded from a passive skill. Wang Lan always worried about one thing: if he was seriously injured in an instant, or fell into a coma from a major injury, could healing still save his life?
Now he finally had his confirmation. Healing had evolved from a passive to an active skill, yet it still retained the characteristics of a passive skill. When faced with a life-threatening injury, healing didn’t require Wang Lan to activate it consciously.
Moreover, falling into a coma is the body’s self-protection mechanism, as is the activation of the Healing Star Martial Arts. Both self-protection mechanisms wouldn’t operate simultaneously.
That is to say, in the face of severe injuries where healing was needed for repair, no matter how serious the wound, Wang Lan would not fall into a coma. No matter the pain, he would just have to bear with it.
Since becoming a Star Martial Warrior, Wang Lan had only fallen into a coma twice. Both times were induced by severe side effects of using the Phoenix form, resulting in forced dormancy. Since the healing determined that these side effects wouldn’t endanger Wang Lan’s life and weren’t bodily injuries needing repair, it didn’t activate, allowing Wang Lan the ’luxury’ of passing out.
Wang Lan’s true strength was at the Star Shine Stage. His body couldn’t withstand the impact of bullets.
And this gunshot came silently. Wang Lan was completely unprepared.
A bullet pierced Wang Lan’s heart. Anyone else would have been dead beyond doubt.
Unfortunately for the attacker, they had encountered an oddity like Wang Lan.
Even if the vital heart was shattered, after all, the heart is just another organ to the human body. A fist-sized heart was repaired in just ten seconds under the full activation of healing.
So Wang Lan stayed conscious the whole time, waiting for the other party to get close.
He had thought this sneaky viper would be careful enough to check if he was really dead. But to his surprise, the cautious-looking assailant didn’t even bother to check and went to grieve for their fallen comrade instead.
At such a moment, if you’re not the one to die, who is?
Therefore, Wang Lan instantly launched an attack, first severing the assailant’s legs and then their arms. The young man in black, now a human stump, still wore an expression of bewilderment and disbelief.
"Who sent you here?"
"You... you’re not dead... how could you not be dead... AH—DIE, JUST DIE—"
The youth in black howled ferociously, Star Energy Fluctuations suddenly flashing over his body. The moment these fluctuations rose, Wang Lan slashed down with his sword, and the young man’s head was severed.
Ah, still so uncooperative. Forget it.
He stood up and flashed back to the corner.
Picking up the phone, he dialed a number.
"Hello? Wang Lan? Wishing me a Happy New Year this early? You big spender, you’re so insincere! A New Year’s greeting should at least involve bringing a gift in person, and you think you can just make a phone call?"
As soon as the call connected, Xu Shiyun’s teasing voice came through.
"Xu, I was ambushed by two Star Cloud Stage Star Martial Warriors and about thirty normal people, but all armed with guns."
"What?"
Dressed in casual home attire, Xu Shiyun, busily tidying up the fruit peels his wife kept spitting out, exploded upon hearing this news.
"Where are you?"
"At home! They came straight to my place. I killed the two Star Martial Warriors, but I knocked out the thirty normal people," Wang Lan replied.
"Good! I’m on my way."
After ending the call, Xu Shiyun’s expression shifted uncertainly.
He was thinking much more than Wang Lan had mentioned. Who was Wang Lan? The Tianjian Bureau’s lucky charm, their intelligence division’s mascot. A name that reached up to the heavens. Wang Qianfeng had kept it from Wang Lan, fearing it would make him conceited, but Xu Shiyun knew that Tianjian Bureau Director Zhang from Jin City had gone personally to the Imperial Capital Tianjian Bureau headquarters to commend Wang Lan. Not only the top brass in the Ministry of Defense, but even the leaders remembered Wang Lan’s name. Someone dared to assassinate such a person? Someone dared to attempt assassination in Wang Lan’s home on New Year’s Eve? What did this imply? What kind of white terror did it represent behind the scenes? This was definitely the Demon Clan’s retaliation. The Demon Clan was declaring war on the Tianjian Bureau: The person I want dead won’t survive this year! Xu Shiyun’s imagination ran wild. If the Demon Clan spy leaders knew, they’d probably be in tears, thinking, "Buddy, you’re seriously overthinking this. We didn’t..."
"Xu, what’s wrong? Something big happened?"
"Big, something very big!" Xu Shiyun snapped out of his trance and immediately made a phone call. "Notify all the brothers, cancel all leaves, head to the Xinyu Building immediately, IMMEDIATELY!"
SWOOSH. Xu Shiyun returned to his room, yanked open the wardrobe to grab his combat uniform, and left home.
Wang Lan, wary of the group of normal people waking up halfway, bundled them all up and stuffed them into the underground storage room. The Xinyu Building was originally constructed to anti-air raid standards; its underground structure could withstand missile strikes. He shoved them into the storage, ensuring they couldn’t get out.
After all this, Wang Lan finally returned to the top floor and home. He had just entered when he saw Hu Qing, wrapped in a bedsheet, anxiously standing at the elevator entrance.
There was no helping it. Hu Qing’s clothes were all torn apart by Wang Lan, so she was left stark naked and washed in the bathtub before being placed in the guest room. Upon waking, her first realization was that this was Wang Lan’s home. After searching for a long time without finding any clothes to wear, she had no choice but to grab a bedsheet and drape it over herself.
"You’re awake? Are you planning to streak out like this?"
"Wang Lan, what’s up with your elevator? It won’t open no matter how much I press. And what’s with your smart house assistant, Xiao Ai? I told it I’m your friend and to open the elevator, it just kept saying without Wang Lan’s permission, it won’t open the door."
Although Wang Lan wasn’t in the mood for laughter, hearing Hu Qing burst out with that, he couldn’t help but laugh.
"Don’t rush off just yet. How big of a hornet’s nest did you actually stir up? Two Star Cloud Stage experts with dozens of underlings, each armed with a gun, chasing after you?"
"They’re here?" Hu Qing’s face turned pale, and she asked anxiously.
"Yeah, I took care of them," Wang Lan said casually, returning to the sofa. "Want something to drink?"
"Wait a minute!" Hu Qing suddenly interjected. "What you just said... if I understood you correctly, you’re saying you dealt with those two Star Cloud Stage experts and dozens of gunmen?"
"Yeah."
"When did you break through?" Hu Qing looked at Wang Lan in astonishment. The last time she had checked, Wang Lan was only in the middle stage of the Star Shine Stage, so how had he broken through?
"I haven’t broken through," Wang Lan said, looking back at Hu Qing puzzled, not quite understanding what she meant.
"You’re still at the Star Shine Stage?"
"Right!"
"Middle stage?"
"Middle stage."
"And you, a Star Shine Stage middle-stager, managed to take out two Star Cloud Stage masters without a scratch? And also took care of dozens of gunmen? All by yourself?"
"Who says without a scratch? I almost died, okay!"
"Forgive my poor eyesight, but I really can’t tell. Listen Wang Lan, you, a middle Star Shine Stager, took down two from the Star Cloud Stage, can you not talk about it as if it’s just a matter of course?" Hu Qing said excitedly, nearly letting her blanket fall to the floor.
"This is my home court; I had the home-ground advantage. Isn’t it quite reasonable to counter-kill them? Besides, I really almost died."
Wang Lan pointed at his chest. "The gunshot wounds on your body were left by that Star Martial Warrior who likes guns, right?"
"You fought with him?" Hu Qing’s expression darkened as she nodded solemnly.
"They were Crow’s left-hand and right-hand men, and yet Crow has no record in police files. But he’s been secretly controlling the underground forces for ten years.
"The mission I mentioned to you last time was to go undercover by Crow’s side. After a month, I gained Crow’s trust. He has two Star Cloud Stage experts.
"One is called Earth Wolf and the other Viper. Earth Wolf is a dual-series Star Martial Warrior of earth and fire, while Viper controls gravity. Viper’s strength is actually much greater than Earth Wolf’s. Though he uses guns, he’s stronger when he doesn’t.
"No one can find him when he hides in the shadows, and by the time you do, you’re already dead. He’s a true assassination master; most of the people Crow wants dead are killed by Viper.
"Viper comes and goes without a trace, and he says he’s even escaped from the hands of Galaxy Stage experts.
"I used up all my tricks and barely escaped with my life to your apartment building’s entrance. That you managed to counter-kill them... It’s unbelievable. Wait, I almost forgot the most important thing! Hurry downstairs. In the trash can by your building’s entrance, there’s crucial evidence."
"I can’t guarantee there aren’t other experts lurking outside. I’ve already called my colleagues. It’s risky for us to go out like this. What crucial evidence? Why are you so nervous?"
"I’m not sure what it is, but I know it’s a blue vial, looks like some kind of potion."
Hearing this, Wang Lan sprang up, quickly pulled out his phone, and asked, "Is it this kind?"
"Yes! That’s the one. Exactly the same."
"You stay here, I’ll go find it," Wang Lan said, instantly heading towards the elevator.
"Let’s go together. In case there’s danger, we can look out for each other."
Wang Lan looked at Hu Qing and considered for a moment. "Okay then. Xiao Ai, link to the surrounding cameras; monitor everything within a three-kilometer radius and check for anyone suspicious watching this place."
"Got it!"
Stepping into the elevator, Hu Qing looked at Wang Lan with uncertainty.
"This smart home system of yours... it’s not your average household system, is it?"
"I remember you calling it stupid just a moment ago."
"But it can control more than just the appliances in your home; you even had it monitor..."
"Good that you know. Just don’t spread it around, okay?"
"Understood!" Hu Qing instantly got it and nodded her promise.
"Wang Lan, the situation is currently safe. Twelve suspicious individuals have been spotted, but none of them can pose a threat to you. You can leave the house with peace of mind."
"Okay!"
Despite being told it was safe to leave the house, after what had just happened, who could really be sure? The two of them covered each other and dashed lightning-fast to the trash can at the entrance, where Hu Qing quickly rummaged through it. Soon, two blue Demonic Transformation Potions were in her hands.
"Got them! Let’s get out of here!"
The two swiftly made their way back to Xinyu Building and took the elevator up to Wang Lan’s top-floor home.
"Wang Lan, do you recognize this stuff?"
"This is called Demonic Transformation Potion. Our Tianjian Bureau is investigating its origin. You got this from that Crow guy?"
"Right! But this stuff didn’t come from Crow himself; a woman gave it to Crow. Although Crow controls the underground forces, he’s also being controlled by someone else."

chapters.title: Chapter 134: The Roundup of the Crow
chapters.content:
Chapter 134: Chapter 134: The Roundup of the Crow
"You said a woman? What kind of woman?"
"I don’t know her identity. She always comes alone, wearing heavy makeup and sunglasses. You know, after a woman puts on makeup, even her own mother might not recognize her, let alone an outsider like me."
"So Crow even has you around when he meets that woman? It seems you’re quite trusted."
"That’s not it." Hu Qing tightened the blanket around himself. "This woman comes to see Crow whenever she pleases, anytime at all. Sometimes, Crow will be in a meeting, and she’ll just push the door open and walk right in. And every time she does, Crow doesn’t get angry. Instead, he immediately drops whatever he’s doing to speak with her privately."
"Today, the woman brought a box when she came to see Crow. And tonight, we had laid bait, waiting for Crow to bite. I had a feeling Crow and that woman were up to something suspicious, so when Crow was distracted by our bait, I snuck into his office. I found the box, and inside were these two blue bottles. But unexpectedly, two Star Cloud Stage Star Martial Warriors discovered me, and they chased me all the way here."
"You said Crow took the bait tonight. Are the police planning to conduct their raid tonight?"
"Yes. The original plan was for after the New Year, but the boss said, ’Why keep trash like this around for the New Year? Deal with it before the holiday.’"
Wang Lan had Xiao Ai order a set of clothes to be delivered to the Xinyu Building. They arrived about half an hour later.
"Wang Lan, Xu Shiyun is here."
"Have them wait in the underground garage. I’ll be right down."
Wang Lan and Hu Qing, who had changed into his new clothes, took the elevator to the second basement level.
"Xu, have you called in the entire Intelligence Division’s Action Team?"
"Anyone who dares to mess with our Intelligence Division’s mascot is declaring war on our entire Action Team! The brothers have all come. The Demon Clan wants to stop you from seeing the New Year? Then the brothers will spend it with you! I’d like to see which member of the Demon Clan is blind enough to try anything!" Xu Shiyun declared domineeringly.
Mascot?
Wang Lan heard this nickname again and felt...
it might just stick with him forever.
Wait a minute. The Demon Clan wants to prevent me from seeing the New Year?
"Did you receive intelligence on that?"
"Wasn’t that what you said on the phone? You were targeted in an assassination attempt today, and they came straight to your home! Who else but the Demon Clan would want you dead? Choosing this particular time to assassinate you, isn’t that just a declaration of terror? I’d like to see who exactly won’t make it through this year!"
"Xu, are you sure you aren’t just eyeing my five-hundred-square-meter apartment?" Wang Lan said with an exasperated smile.
His imagination is getting a bit carried away.
"What are you talking about? I’m eyeing your thirty-six-floor Xinyu Building, that’s more like it! Five hundred square meters is nothing. My place is at least two hundred square meters, you know," Xu Shiyun replied casually, knowing Wang Lan was joking to relieve stress.
"Since all the brothers have come... that’s good. But this time, it’s really not the Demon Clan causing trouble for me, Xu, brothers. Look what I’ve got!"
Wang Lan took out the two vials and shook them. Most of the men looked puzzled; only Xu Shiyun’s expression changed abruptly.
Demonic Transformation Potion? He got two more bottles? Wait a minute!
Xu Shiyun suddenly jolted, looking at Wang Lan in shock.
If Wang Lan had two bottles of Demonic Transformation Potion, then it made perfect sense why he was attacked.
"You... you haven’t found the whereabouts of a Demon Clan spy again, have you? Didn’t I tell you, if you find a clue, don’t go it alone? Inform our brothers! We won’t steal your credit, but at least we can ensure your safety!"Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs
"No, I really didn’t do anything today. I was just cleaning the house, pasting up ’Fortune’ characters, and things like that. This police officer, Brother Hu Qing, is an undercover operative working near Crow. He fled to my place with two bottles of Demonic Transformation Potion, and only then was he pursued by those expert assassins."
"Today, the police are going to conduct a major crackdown on the underworld organizations in Suzhou City. The ringleader, Crow, has direct connections with the Demonic Transformation Potion. By catching Crow, we can find out the source of the potion."
Now, all the members of the Action Team understood. Their gazes towards Wang Lan became even stranger.
You were just cleaning your house, and someone conveniently delivered two bottles of Demonic Transformation Potion into your hands? We’re also cleaning our homes, so why doesn’t anyone deliver such benefits to us? Did he save the galaxy in his past life?
"What are you brothers waiting for? Don’t just stand there! That kid Lige was sent to assist with the police operation; this might be it. If we’re late, Lige will get all the credit!" Xu Shiyun suddenly shouted.
Wang Lan got into Xu Shiyun’s car. As soon as Xu Shiyun was in, he quickly contacted Wang Qianfeng.
"Director Wang, I have an urgent report. Today, Wang Lan obtained two more bottles of Demonic Transformation Potion. They came from Crow, one of the underworld leaders targeted in the police’s current anti-gang operation."
"We’ve determined that Crow has a direct connection to the Demonic Transformation Potion. The Action Team requests to intervene."
On the other end, Wang Qianfeng was bewildered, pausing for a few seconds before responding.
"You may intervene. I’ll call the Action Department and the Bureau Chief."
"Thank you, Director."
After hanging up, Wang Qianfeng, still somewhat bewildered, took a few seconds to process the information before picking up the phone beside him.
The site for netting Crow was an unfinished building complex on the outskirts of Suzhou City’s Wu District. The government had initially planned this as a key development zone. However, before any official decision was made, real estate developers, having caught wind of the plans, had already rushed to speculate on properties and even schools in the area. But later, the government’s plans changed, and the development was postponed for ten years. This resulted in a large number of abandoned, unfinished buildings. The developers responsible for the projects fled overseas but were eventually captured and brought back. Although the embezzled funds were recovered, no one was willing to take over these derelict structures. Crow’s transaction was set to take place here. Of course, this so-called major transaction was actually a meticulously planned police sting operation, two months in the making.
Now, police sirens wailed as the operation began.
Xu Shiyun instantly shifted gears. As he did, Wang Lan, having experienced Xu Shiyun’s driving once before and knowing how outrageously flamboyant he could be once he got going, lightning-fast grabbed the handrail.
Sure enough, Xu Shiyun’s vehicle instantly carved a Z-shaped lightning trajectory, breaking away from the other cars and hurtling towards the ramp.
"Xu, I think we could make it at a normal speed... We don’t... we don’t need to be in such a rush..."
"It’s better to arrive early; if we’re slow, we won’t even get the scraps. If Crow gets killed, we’ll get nothing at all."
They sped along, arriving outside the police cordon in a mere ten minutes.
The entire construction site was pitch black, but countless police cars, their powerful searchlights blazing, illuminated it from all directions. In addition to the lights on the ground, helicopters circled overhead.
Xu Shiyun and the other four jumped out of the car. A police officer in a high-ranking uniform strode towards them.
"I am Zhao Kai, Capital Commandant of the Suzhou City Police. Which department are you from?"
"The Intelligence Division Action Team from Suzhou City’s Tianjian Bureau. Is there someone named Crow in this operation of yours?"
"Crow is our primary target; he’s in that unfinished building block over there. He and his men are in Building No. 3, and our people are monitoring them from all angles. The police have Building No. 3 completely surrounded; Crow has absolutely no chance of escape."
"He’s carrying important clues; we need to take him alive. Can we go in?"
"Of course, you can go in. Moreover, Lieutenant Li from the Tianjian Bureau is already inside attempting the capture alone. The darkness hinders our main force’s actions, so we initially planned to trap them first and then order their surrender. But Lieutenant Li said that wouldn’t be necessary, that he could handle it alone. Our personnel are positioned around the perimeter, and the floodlights are on them. However, be warned: every one of them is armed."
"Don’t worry, we’re professionals. In our eyes, firearms are no different from fire pokers." Xu Shiyun waved his hand, and Wang Lan, along with his three companions, charged toward Building No. 3, as indicated by Zhao Kai.
Inside Building No. 3, the lights were off, but it wasn’t pitch black. Being an unfinished structure, it had no doors or windows installed. Coupled with the powerful searchlights beaming in from all directions, the entire building glowed like a lit lantern.
Even before they got close to Building No. 3, Wang Lan and the others could hear intermittent gunshots from within.
On the middle floors of Building No. 3, Crow was rapidly retreating under the protection of a dozen of his subordinates.
Although Crow’s face remained ferocious and grim, he had lost his usual composure, that sense of having everything under control. Despite his efforts to appear calm, deep down, he was utterly panicked.
He couldn’t escape.
In this isolated building, with police surrounding the exterior, the moment he stepped outside, countless guns would be aimed at him, instantly riddling him like a beehive. Yet, staying inside was tantamount to waiting for death.
Worse still, the pursuer behind them was a Star Martial Warrior expert.
Damn it! If only I’d kept those two Star Martial Warrior experts by my side for protection! With two Star Cloud Stage experts, I’d at least have a fighting chance.
Relying on these few dozen men and their guns to deal with a Star Cloud Stage pinnacle expert was nothing but a fool’s dream.
Guns still posed a lethal threat to Star Martial Warriors below the Galaxy Stage, but only if they were caught off guard. If a Star Martial Warrior was prepared, forget the Galaxy Stage; even someone at the Starlight Stage might not fear gunfire.
Bullets could indeed kill Star Martial Warriors below the Galaxy Stage, but only if they hit their mark. The speed of a Star Martial Warrior was too fast for ordinary eyes to follow; how could they possibly shoot them?
He had dozens of men and guns, including six automatic rifles. But so what? How could they fight if they couldn’t even see their opponent’s shadow?
Crow carefully crept to the stairwell and stealthily ascended the stairs alone, leaving a dozen of his men to guard the landing.
"Come out! Aren’t you a Star Martial Warrior? Do Star Martial Warriors dealing with us ordinary folk hide and cower? Where’s your Star Martial Warrior pride? If you’ve got the guts, come out and let’s see who dies—"
Crow’s subordinates roared defiantly. Hidden in the shadows, Lige’s lips curled into a cold sneer. "Idiots!"
CRACKLE— Suddenly, an arc of electricity erupted. The instant it appeared, it snaked towards the men’s feet like a nimble serpent.
BOOM—
The ball of lightning exploded, and the electric current spread out like a spiderweb. The dozen or so men at the stairwell instantly had their hair standing on end before they stiffly collapsed.
With no more hidden gunmen posing a threat on this level, Lige finally stepped out from the shadows. He walked past the charred bodies of Crow’s men—whether dead or alive, he didn’t know—and reached the stairwell. Looking up, he saw figures moving on the stairs above.
Lige glanced at the alloy staircase handrail, a disdainful sneer touching his lips. He pressed his palm against the handrail. Instantly, electric arcs crackled around his body.
AHH—
Suddenly, a series of agonizing screams echoed from above. The electric current instantly coursed through the dozen or so men who were gripping the handrail as they fled, charring their bodies black. Amidst wisps of pale smoke, they collapsed.
Lige’s figure flashed, transforming into a streak of lightning as he surged to the upper floor.

chapters.title: Chapter 135: Someone Underground
chapters.content:
Chapter 135: Chapter 135: Someone Underground
In those few minutes, all of Crow’s more than twenty subordinates were taken down.
There were no more stairs to climb; construction had yet to be completed on the upper levels due to the unfinished building. Crow looked at the staircase in despair, then turned and ran toward the balcony on this floor.
The balcony had only finished constructing the load-bearing platform; there was no railing or anything of the sort. At the moment, the balcony was just a platform jutting out of the building, ten stories high. Jumping down meant certain death.
As soon as he stood on the balcony, a strong light shone on him. Perhaps gun barrels were aimed right at him.
Crow looked down in terror as the crisp sound of footsteps approached from behind.
Lige walked closer step by step, his face as cold as ice.
"Don’t come any closer! If you do, I’ll jump from here!"
"For someone like you, dying would be a contribution to society. If you want to jump, go ahead. I won’t stop you," Lige said, advancing step by step toward him.
When he was less than five meters away, the panic on Crow’s face vanished instantly. He viciously raised his head, and Spirit Power Fluctuations accompanied by a huge wind blade fiercely slashed toward Lige.
According to the information obtained and Crow’s previous behavior, there had been no indication that Crow was a Star Martial Warrior, let alone one at the advanced Star Cloud Stage.
Therefore, Crow’s sudden attack caught Lige by surprise. But fortunately, past experience led him to instinctively shoot out a Thunder Gun to counter the wind blade’s slicing.
Wind Attribute is the only attribute that can counter Thunder Attribute. The sharp Thunder Gun fragmented upon contact with the wind blade, splitting apart like wood sliced by a knife.
BOOM—
Suddenly, a cement wall rose in front of Lige. After slicing through the Thunder Gun, the wind blade immediately struck the cement wall.
BOOM—
The cement wall shattered violently. During that instant, Lige transformed into a streak of light and swiftly retreated, creating distance between himself and Crow.
Crow’s face became extraordinarily ferocious, twisted as though it were a sheet of paper clutched in someone’s hand. A tinge of regret flashed in his eyes.
If it weren’t for that wall of earth, the damn guard would probably have died from my sneak attack.
Crow had been steadily chipping away at Lige’s vigilance, using the lives of dozens of his men to make Lige believe he was just an ordinary man.
The plan was set from the very beginning. If I had truly been an ordinary person, there would have been no chance for me to escape the dense cordon of guards outside. If I had revealed myself as a Star Martial Warrior at the beginning, I also wouldn’t have been able to escape with my life. Suzhou City has not only police officers but also the Tianjian Bureau. This young and unreasonably strong guy in front of me is very likely a master from the Tianjian Bureau. He’s here to assist in the arrest, probably as a precaution. I’ve kept my true abilities well concealed. In fact, no one other than myself and that woman knows I’m a Star Cloud Stage Star Martial Warrior. This is my final trump card. I’ve calculated everything clearly. The Tianjian Bureau sending one person to assist is already showing me high regard; there won’t be a second Star Martial expert. Thus, if I can assassinate this Star Martial Warrior with a sneak attack and then use my suddenly emergent strength, I might have a chance to break out of the encirclement.
Crow chose the right moment, and he had almost succeeded.
But why did the unexpected happen at the very moment of imminent success?
Clear footsteps resonated, sounding particularly crisp in the empty, unfinished building.
"What did I just see? Captain Lige was complacent, almost killed by some trash at the early Star Cloud Stage?" Xu Shiyun said with a roguish smirk, teasing him.
"What are you doing here?" Lige didn’t retort or argue back.
Making excuses was not Lige’s style. Yes meant yes, and no meant no. Xu Shiyun wasn’t wrong—Lige had indeed been complacent just now.
I became disdainful facing an ordinary person at a dead end, and I almost died due to that disdain. If it weren’t for Xu Shiyun’s rescue, I would have lain eternally in disgrace.
"I came to save you!" Xu Shiyun wouldn’t miss this rare opportunity to tease Lige.
Crow’s eyes flickered as he watched the four who followed Xu Shiyun arrive.
Clearly, these four are not ordinary guards; they’re most likely all experts from the Tianjian Bureau. Damn it, do they have to be so dramatic? I’m just a regular person, okay? Can’t you all stop thinking so highly of me? Sending five Star Martial experts? And it’s very likely I can’t win against any of them!
"Crow, do you think you have any chance left?" Xu Shiyun took a leisurely step forward, and Star Energy Fluctuation surged wildly from him.
"Get over here obediently, damn you!"
"Be careful, he might undergo Demonization," Wang Lan warned in a low voice.
ROAR— Almost the instant Wang Lan’s voice faded, Crow’s body swelled rapidly. A dark carapace appeared all over his body, bristling with sharp spikes.
As Crow completed his transformation, Wang Lan and the other four charged at him.
Wang Lan was an Earth Attribute Star Martial Warrior and naturally took the lead.
Against other Star Cloud Stage Star Martial Warriors, I would certainly hang back. But when it comes to beating up a Wind Attribute Star Martial Warrior, everyone else step back and let me handle this!
A wind wall suddenly formed around Crow, enveloping him like a tornado, and countless wind blades, like a volley of hidden weapons, shot towards the five of them.
Lige, using his Flash Thunder movement technique, deftly dodged the wind blade assault, while Xu Shiyun conjured a cement wall to counter the barrage of wind blades. Even though the cement wall could block them, it was dangerously unstable.
Under the erosion of the wind blades, the cement wall seemed to rapidly weather, as if instantly experiencing ages of change, and fine sand danced like smoke.
The other two Star Martial experts also used their unique skills to dodge.
After undergoing Demonization, Crow’s strength instantly soared from the early Star Cloud Stage to its peak, and it might have even surpassed that.
Among the five of them, only Wang Lan could rapidly approach amidst the myriad wind blades. Two Flame Swords danced swiftly in front of him, forming a shield of fire. The sharp wind blades dissolved quickly upon contact with the flames.
The higher the temperature of the flames, the faster they dissipated. The heat of his Purple Flame Swords reached nearly ten thousand degrees, turning the wind blades into wisps of smoke upon contact.
Within three seconds, Wang Lan had charged before Crow, stabbing fiercely with his Flame Swords into the tornado. Flames instantly engulfed it. The tornado, as if it were paper set ablaze, vanished almost immediately.
But Crow’s figure had disappeared from within the tornado. A huge round hole, nearly two meters in diameter, had appeared in the ceiling above.
"Chase!"Nᴇw ɴovel chaptᴇrs are published on NovᴇlFirenᴇt
As Xu Shiyun’s words fell, he had already surged through the hole.
Their movement techniques were as fast as lightning. Within two or three seconds, all five had leaped onto the roof. Due to the unfinished construction, the rooftop was like a building with only half its walls completed, as if a toy building block had been split open in the middle.
By this point, the demonized Crow had already reached the edge of the rooftop. With a powerful leap, the unfinished building shook violently beneath its feet.
Crow’s jumping ability was astonishing; it shot dozens of meters into the air in an instant. In the blink of an eye, it seemed to merge with the night sky.
"Does anyone have flying-type Star Martial Skills?" Wang Lan urgently shouted.
"Flash Thunder!" Before Lige’s words were even complete, his figure turned into a bolt of lightning and shot into the sky.
"Chase!" Xu Shiyun instantly pressed his hand against the wall. A slab of concrete soared from the unfinished building, extending towards the opposite structure like a bridge formed between the two buildings in the blink of an eye.
Lige’s figure flashed rapidly across the sky. Crow’s leap might follow a predictable parabolic arc, but Lige’s Flash Thunder had an erratically shifting trajectory. In the air, Crow was no match for Lige.
"Thunderfall!"
A cold shout rang out above Crow’s head, instantly followed by a piercing BOOM that filled the sky.
Crow barely had time to look up before seeing Lige pressing a massive thunder orb down towards its forehead.
Crow spat a powerful gust of wind from its mouth, which rapidly dissipated the thunder orb. Nevertheless, a remnant of the lightning ball still struck fiercely on Crow’s forehead.
CRACKLE—
Crow was smacked down from the sky, crashing into a building where only the foundation had recently been laid and the first story had just begun to rise.
BOOM—
A wall exploded outward as Crow’s large figure burst forth. The direction in which Crow charged was perfect—right towards where Xu Shiyun and the others were converging to provide support.
"Ground Surge!"
Instantly, the ground beneath Crow’s feet churned, transforming into countless earthen tendrils that wound around its legs, dragging them harshly toward the ground.
BOOM— Crow’s body flickered with surging Star Energy Fluctuation, and the tendrils around its feet burst apart instantly.
But Crow wasn’t fighting just one person; it was battling a group.
Crow could easily suppress one opponent with its strength, but now it was fighting five Tianjian Bureau experts. All of them, except for the underwhelming Wang Lan, were Star Cloud Stage experts. And even if Wang Lan was underwhelming, he still held an attribute advantage over Crow and already had the blood of several Star Cloud Stage cultivators on his hands.
A single Crow stood no chance.
Just as Crow freed itself from Xu Shiyun’s Earth Attribute tendrils, Wang Lan’s Cross Decapitation Sword descended from the heavens, pressing fiercely onto Crow’s sturdy back.
"AH—!" For the first time, Crow uttered a human-like scream of agony.
"Wang Lan, we need it alive!" Xu Shiyun hurriedly shouted.
Wang Lan immediately retreated explosively, leaving Crow’s back drenched in blood.
"Thunder Gun!"
BOOM—
Lige instantly followed up with another attack the moment Wang Lan retreated. Xu Shiyun nearly exploded with anger at this scene.
"Lige, you did that on purpose, didn’t you? Didn’t you hear me say we needed it alive?"
"It won’t die!" Lige didn’t retort, instead standing coldly in front of the charred Crow, his eyes as still as a serene autumn pond.
