"I... I don’t know... After I finished making it... the Demon Clan cut off my contact with the workshop. I don’t know where it is. Only the Demon Clan knows."
Wang Qianfeng was not satisfied with this answer. Seeing Wang Qianfeng’s gaze, Ma Bo suddenly panicked again.
"I’m not lying. Although I helped them make the Demonic Transformation Potion, they didn’t trust me. Once the production was complete, they just dropped me."
"I know that creating the Demonic Transformation Potion requires a human genetic code formula. Where did you get that formula from?"
"It was given to me by Song Zifeng..."
"You’re lying! Song Zifeng would never give you the biological genetic code formula. It looks like we still need to engrave. Wu Chao."
"It’s not a lie. It really was Song Zifeng who gave it to me... The experiment accident twelve years ago wasn’t an accident; it was actually a conspiracy planned by the Demon Clan. Their original target was Song Zifeng, but when he refused to cooperate, they engraved Song Zifeng’s memories. They discovered this formula from his memories... I... I..."
"You capitulated because you were afraid of dying?"
"I am not afraid of death!" Ma Bo suddenly lifted his head to look at Wang Qianfeng. "I have never feared death. If I did, I wouldn’t dare to conduct experiments with equipment I knew was faulty. If I were afraid of death, I wouldn’t use myself to test my chemical potions.
"I don’t fear death. My cooperation with the Demon Clan... is simply because I have completely lost hope in humanity as a species.
"I don’t understand why God would create humans. Or rather, God’s original intention in creating humans probably wasn’t this current species. Human thoughts are too filthy, their moral standards too low; humans are born with inherent vices.
"I am a scholar at heart, and I adore my scientific endeavors. They envied me because I was better than them, so they ostracized me.
"They snatched my research grants, the laboratory that should have been mine, my nominations, my honors, and even my research achievements.
"I was angry, and even more sorrowful. Throughout human history, it has been a history of plundering.
"Whether it’s against their own kind or other species, humans are always endlessly plundering. They plunder when they’re hungry and even more unscrupulously when they’re not.
"Perhaps the appearance of the Demon Clan is God’s way of creating something to eliminate this failed species?"
"Just because you can’t get along with your colleagues, you’re blaming the entire human race? Have you ever considered why it’s only you who can’t harmonize with others? Why can everyone else form close friendships and you can’t?"
"Have you ever seen a person become best friends with a monkey? Have you seen someone treat a pig as a friend? After seeing their inherent vices, how could I possibly acknowledge them and become friends with them?
"In this life, science will be my only friend."
"The Demon Clan killed your relatives, yet why do you continue to collaborate with them? Don’t tell me you didn’t know before. When I told you that your son, daughter-in-law, and granddaughter were all dead, your face looked shocked, but your heart rate barely changed, and your emotions weren’t genuinely stirred."
"Relatives? I’m all alone in this world. What relatives do I have?" Ma Bo said with a self-deprecating smile.
"You have a wife, a son, and a granddaughter?"
"Hahaha..." Ma Bo suddenly laughed, a laugh full of irony.
"My son... hahaha... the son I raised for forty years, I only found out that he had no blood relation to me when he turned forty... hahaha...
"You asked me why, even after they killed my son and granddaughter, I would still cooperate with them? Every single second they lived reminded me of what a fool I’ve been. They were my disgrace!"
"So, the deaths of your son, daughter-in-law, and granddaughter were even at your request? Including Professor Zhang Yingqiu’s sudden heart attack seven years ago?"
"Yes! Exactly." Ma Bo seemed to have let everything go, the smile on his face gradually twisting into a maniacal grin.
"Wu Chao, Spirit Engraving."
"I’ve already confessed everything, you... You’re breaking your word!"
"Afraid your confession isn’t complete enough!" Wang Qianfeng coldly delivered this parting shot and rose to his feet.
No sooner had he left the interrogation room than Wang Qianfeng picked up the phone. "What’s the matter?"
"Director Wang, Wang Lan says he’s made a significant discovery and requests to see you."
Again?
This question was quite telling.
In the past, after the Demon Clan had stirred up trouble and left a mess behind, it would only then dawn on the Tianjian Bureau that the Demon Clan had made a move. But in just the span of half a year, Wang Qianfeng felt as if their roles had completely reversed. The Tianjian Bureau, previously the one being bullied, had transformed and started wielding a big stick, bullying the Demon Clan in turn. The change in roles made many people feel a bit disoriented.
Recently, there seemed to be too many Demon Clan spies caught. Lately, there were too many clues about the Demon Clan uncovered. Recently... the Demon Clan had been having a rather miserable time.
Has the performance of this generation of Demon Clan spies deteriorated?
From the end of last year to after the new year, Wang Lan was on fire, as if his personal cosmos had erupted. Previously, it was luck-based to stumble upon clues regarding the Demon Clan. But now, it was as if his cosmos was operating at full throttle, transforming him into a Demon Clan search radar. Despite the Demon Clan hiding so deep, they were still dug out by Wang Lan.
What caused Wang Lan’s cosmos to burst out?
Wang Qianfeng scratched his chin and pondered.
It’s one thing to provoke anyone else, but to provoke Wang Lan’s aunt... Annoy someone else, and Wang Lan might not have been so incensed. But provoke Wang Qi, and Wang Lan practically transformed, his ability to uncover the Demon Clan becoming preternaturally sharp. In the end, the Demon Clan brought this upon themselves!
「Back in the office, both Wang Lan and Xu Shiyun were present.」
"Wang Lan, tell me, what have you found now?"
"Another Demon Clan spy group, or maybe a base, I’m not sure yet. But forty-two kilometers away from here in Changxiang District, there’s someone who’s in contact with an elite Demon Clan unit," Wang Lan reported.
"You... You’ve even got the address locked down?" Wang Qianfeng looked at Wang Lan in shock. He had thought that Wang Lan had merely found a clue, just a clue. But he never imagined Wang Lan would have it all figured out in one go. Not only had he found a clue, but he’d also pinpointed the exact coordinates?
When did finding Demon Clan spies become so easy? Or was the Tianjian Bureau of the past just too incompetent?
"How did you discover it?"
"That tablet belonging to the little girl, Zhang Jixi. Director Wang, do you still remember the scene back then? Zhang Jixi revealed her true form rather than let the tablet fall into my hands. I guessed that there must be important clues inside the tablet.
"In the tablet, I found a private server game which Zhang Jixi often played. And the game’s server is at the coordinates I discovered.
"A tablet game with a private server? And the whole game has only Zhang Jixi as a player? Definitely something fishy there!"
No, it’s not the game that’s fishy; it’s you. That was the only thought in Wang Qianfeng’s mind. Your thought process, how does it even work? How could you think of this? Granted, if you think about it, the logic is sound. But... no normal person would come to this conclusion, right?

chapters.title: Chapter 150: Strike on the Secret Base
chapters.content:
Chapter 150: Chapter 150: Strike on the Secret Base
"Director Wang?"
Wang Lan’s soft call brought Wang Qianfeng back from his daze.
"Oh, I’ll call the Director right away. You wait here for a moment."
Wang Qianfeng returned to his desk and picked up the red phone to dial.
It was supposed to be a brief conversation, but Wang Lan hadn’t expected Wang Qianfeng and Lu Zhao to talk for so long. From their conversation, he vaguely heard the term "Shadow Guard Office."
Wang Lan feigned ignorance, while Xu Shiyun looked up, counting the patterns on the suspended ceiling.
"The Bureau has had a huge workload lately and is short-staffed. You’ll have to wait a bit longer; the Director is arranging for more personnel," Wang Qianfeng said after hanging up the phone.
"Wang Lan, how likely do you think it is that place is a Demon Clan base?"
"Without more information, I can’t make a judgment."
"Could it be the Central Command for the Demon Clan’s spies in Suzhou City?"
Wang Lan’s mouth twitched slightly. You dare to think that way? You really think the Demon Clan would be so foolish? To establish a Central Command for spying? What if they were exposed and all rounded up in one fell swoop?
KNOCK, KNOCK, KNOCK— The sound of knocking interrupted the room. He MingXue pushed the door open and barged in.
"He Lao’er, what are you doing?" Wang Qianfeng was about to open the door when it suddenly swung open, startling him. He scolded with a dark expression.
"Old Wang, has Wang Lan discovered traces of the Demon Clan again?"
"Are you snooping on the Intelligence Agency’s secrets?"
"Scram! Who in the Bureau doesn’t know about the important matter Wang Lan just reported? And who is Wang Lan? Director Zhang of Jin City personally picked him as the mascot. For the past six months, both your Intelligence Agency and the Action Department have been living off the fat of the land, all thanks to Wang Lan’s repeated discoveries of Demon Clan traces.
"In the last few days, how many accolades have you earned? How many big fish have you caught? You should be content by now."
"Oh? Why should I be content with what’s mine?" Wang Qianfeng replied indifferently, picking at a toothpick as he looked at He MingXue.
"Aren’t we brothers anymore?"
"Even blood brothers keep clear accounts."
"What do you want?"
"I really like that pair of sisters under your command..."
"Impossible!" He MingXue exploded on the spot, like an enraged lion.
Wang Lan’s face changed instantly. He quickly composed himself, observing silently and sighing inwardly. The lives of these bigwigs are indeed colorful. If I heard something I shouldn’t have, might I be silenced?
"Remember, you’re the one who said it!" Wang Qianfeng chuckled unconcernedly.
"This is the Director’s intention. I’m here simply to look after our relationship."
"Oh? The Director’s intention? Fine, I’ll go ask the Director right now. I can understand sharing the Intelligence Agency’s credit with the Action Department, but giving it to the Law Enforcement Department? What’s the meaning of that? The Law Enforcement Department handles internal affairs, not external ones."
"Wait a minute!" He MingXue, seething with anger but unable to lash out, forced an ugly smile. "Let’s discuss this. How about a different arrangement?"
"Those two sisters are perfectly in sync; together, they’re as effective as a small squad. Sending them to your Law Enforcement Department would be casting pearls before swine. They deserve better opportunities for development. What can your department offer them? Interrogating prisoners? Lecturing and brainwashing the men?"
"The Tianjian Bureau is going to be restructured soon, and the Law Enforcement Department might become the Shadow Guard Office."
"Who knows when that will happen? You expect them to waste several years waiting for that?"
He MingXue winced, but finally clenched his teeth. "Fine! I’ll hand them over to you. But let me make this clear: if you train them well, they’re yours. If not, send them back to me."
"That’s more like it!" Wang Qianfeng playfully patted He MingXue’s shoulder. "I’m entrusting Wang Lan and Xu Shiyun to you. Don’t let them get hurt; it would be like losing my own two arms."
"Get lost! Am I that kind of person?" He MingXue huffed and turned to leave. "Wang Lan, Xu Shiyun, assemble downstairs."
"Yes, sir!"
TAT-TAT-TAT—
"Reporting!"
"Come in!"
"Reporting, Director Wang, a confidential order from the Director." The person said, opening a file folder and placing the order in front of Wang Qianfeng.
"Old Wang, what’s this confidential order from the Director?"
"Mind your discipline. A confidential order is confidential. Can I show it to you? Aren’t you leaving yet? Don’t let those Demon Clan brats get away."
"Understood." He MingXue flashed out of the room, with Wang Lan and Xu Shiyun quickly following.
When Wang Qianfeng was alone in the office, he suddenly grinned.
The Shadow Guard Office is preparing to launch. This operation is assigned to the Law Enforcement Department as a test. You are to secretly observe and assess the Law Enforcement Department’s operational capabilities, then provide an evaluation.
He Lao’er, get ready for your exam...
Once again, seven or eight cars roared out of the Tianjian Bureau, getting green lights all the way as they sped onto the expressway.
Wang Lan and Xu Shiyun sat in the back, while a pair of twin sisters sat in the front.
Since they weren’t familiar with each other, the atmosphere in the car was somewhat subdued. Although Wang Lan appeared to be looking out the window, he occasionally glanced at the female driver from the corner of his eye, and she, in turn, kept sizing him up through the rearview mirror.
Another female driver who doesn’t pay attention to the road.
Wang Lan tightened his seatbelt and reached out to grip the handrail firmly.
"Let’s get acquainted. I’m Zhang Yeqiu, and this is my younger sister, Zhang Xiaoxue. Our father’s surname is Zhang, and our mother’s maiden name is Ye. We were born on a day with light snow—Xiaoxue. You’re Wang Lan, right? Your name has been coming up frequently at the Bureau lately. You and Lige are known as the ’Suzhou Bureau’s Twin Elites’."
Zhang Yeqiu seemed very talkative. Her voice, crisp and sweet, was like a warm breeze instantly dispelling the somber atmosphere in the car.
Wang Lan asked with a bewildered expression, "What kind of ridiculous title is that? And why am I paired with Lige? If anyone’s paired with him, shouldn’t it be the guy next to me?"
"Xu Shiyun is practically an uncle! How could an uncle be our idol? Besides, he’s not even handsome."
"I’m only thirty-two! How does that make me an uncle? And when it comes to women’s aesthetic sense, there’s serious disagreement. Ten women will have ten different standards of beauty. Mine is a mature handsomeness!"
"Thirty-two isn’t an uncle? Little brother Wang Lan here is only seventeen."
"But... even so, why compare me with Lige? We haven’t been shipped as a CP or anything, have we?"
"It was the girls at the Bureau who decided it! Before, Lige was the one shining solo, with tons of young fans. But Lige is the ’keep your distance’ type, so after you made your mark, a lot of them switched to being your fans."
"Is that so? What an honor," Wang Lan said, his tone dripping with sarcasm.
He hadn’t even realized he had idol potential. Though, whenever he looked in the mirror, he did think he was quite handsome. Objectively speaking, however, Wang Lan merely had a somewhat scholarly air about him; he wasn’t conventionally handsome.
"So, who do you two admire?" Xu Shiyun chimed in.
"Of course, it’s Wang Lan! My family is quite pragmatic; supporting a mascot brings good luck. See? We only got back from our advanced training a month ago, and we already have a mission."The latest_epɪ_sodes are on_the N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
"By the way, how old are you? You don’t look much older than me," Wang Lan asked curiously.
"Hmph! How rude! Asking a lady her age right after meeting her..." Zhang Yeqiu feigned annoyance.
"No, I’m just curious. How did you become Captains at such a young age? Aren’t promotions in the Tianjian Bureau supposed to be difficult?"
"Heh... such an innocent little brother, aren’t you? Blushing so easily? We’ve been with the Tianjian Bureau for five years. Becoming Captains in five years isn’t that fast, you know."
"Five years? Alright, I get it." Wang Lan turned to look out the window.
"Hey, what’s with that look? Are you implying we’re old hags?"
"Not at all!"
"Your expression says otherwise! I’m not even twenty yet, okay?"
"You joined the Tianjian Bureau at fifteen? Didn’t you go to school?"
"School? Of course, we did. Is there a problem with graduating from university at fourteen?"
Wang Lan’s mouth twitched. Anyone who could ask that question was the problematic one.
But Wang Lan wasn’t particularly shocked by this.
If it weren’t for that damned system quest, and if he hadn’t known he would awaken as a Star Martial Warrior, with his abilities, skipping two or three grades would have been no problem for him. Passing the national college entrance exam at twelve and then getting a master’s degree in another year or two wouldn’t have been difficult.
The car was fast, but the driving was steady.
As they chatted and became more familiar with each other, Wang Lan’s group arrived near their destination.
Zhang Yeqiu and Zhang Xiaoxue were both legendary prodigies, perhaps even more terrifyingly talented than Jiang Xinyu. Zhang Yeqiu possessed dual Fire and Earth attributes, while Zhang Xiaoxue, like Jiang Xinyu, had an Ice attribute.
With the sisters’ natural talents, there was no need for them to rush their advancement by taking the Star Martial college entrance exam at thirteen. At that age, they were already at the Star Shine Stage, which was quite remarkable.
Had they progressed normally, reaching the Star Cloud Stage by seventeen wouldn’t have been difficult. Graduating high school at the Star Cloud Stage would have greatly increased their chances of entering one of the four great Star Martial Academies. Yet, they chose a path incomprehensible to ordinary people.
They took the Star Martial college entrance exam at thirteen and were admitted to the Jin City Star Martial Academy. They graduated within a year and then joined the Tianjian Bureau. They rose to the rank of Captain in five years. Although they claimed it was reasonable, it was still fast compared to Xu Shiyun, who had also been a Captain in the Tianjian Bureau for six years. This showed that the sisters’ promotion rate within the Tianjian Bureau was indeed considered rapid.
Once they arrived, the men from the Law Enforcement Department concealed their vehicles and then jumped out, pumped up as if they’d been injected with adrenaline, ready and awaiting orders.
"Scout!" He MingXue ordered in a deep voice.
"Total of twenty individuals. Five are on guard outside; the rest are inside, appearing to do office work. A sign on the second-floor entrance reads, ’Gold Star Network Technology Co., Ltd.’"
"Who would open a company in a place like this? Only twenty people? Infiltrate."
As soon as he finished speaking, the Law Enforcement Department members vanished into the earth one by one, disappearing as silently as Tierra Mice.
"Hey, isn’t anyone going to take me?" Wang Lan exclaimed.
Xu Shiyun patted Wang Lan’s shoulder. "I’m here."
With that, he grabbed Wang Lan’s arm, and WHOOSH, they also disappeared.
The sensation of moving underground using Earth Attribute Star Martial Skills was strange. The solid earth around them seemed to flow like water, only a bit thicker.
Textbooks did describe the characteristics of various elemental Star Martial Skills. The smoothness of an Earth Attribute Star Martial Warrior’s subterranean travel directly depended on their skill level. Highly skilled individuals felt no resistance when burrowing into the earth, moving through it as easily as running on the surface.
However, those with insufficient Cultivation Level felt like they were wading through thick mud, facing significant resistance and slow movement. It was like the one Wang Lan had killed previously; if that person had been faster moving through the earth, Wang Lan’s vertical slicing attack wouldn’t have hit him.
Wang Lan was led by Xu Shiyun, unsure how far they had traveled, when they quietly surfaced. By then, the men from the Law Enforcement Department were already engaged in combat with the enemy.
However, the scene of the battle was somewhat difficult for Wang Lan and Xu Shiyun to process.
It was completely one-sided!
They had expected to catch a big fish, but it turned out to be just a few small fry that had slipped through the net.
The exposed members of the Demon Clan did indeed fight back, but their strength was mediocre. The strongest among them was merely at the Star Cloud Stage, and the others were at the Star Shine Stage. The Law Enforcement Department had dispatched thirty men—more than a dozen at the Star Cloud Stage, plus one at the Galaxy Stage to oversee things. They had cast a wide net, only to catch these few small shrimp.
Watching his subordinates make short work of the Demon Clan, He MingXue didn’t smile. Instead, he glanced with slight resentment at Wang Lan, who was slowly emerging from the ground.

chapters.title: Chapter 151: Forced Out
chapters.content:
Chapter 151: Chapter 151: Forced Out
The previous two times Wang Lan discovered traces of the Demon Clan, he reeled in big fish, making the Law Enforcement Department’s eyes turn red with envy, just like rabbits.
It wasn’t easy for Wang Lan to find traces of the Demon Clan again, so why was it only small fry this time? Nearly all the experts from the Law Enforcement Department had come out, initially expecting a tough fight.
Suzhou City’s Tianjian Bureau had seven departments, with only three related to combat. The heads of each department were of Galaxy Stage strength, but the capabilities of their subordinates varied greatly.
The strongest was undoubtedly the Action Department, the main combat branch of the Tianjian Bureau, boasting four Galaxy Stage experts. The strength of its two squad leaders even surpassed Li Weixin’s by a significant margin.
Below the Action Department was the Intelligence Department. It had fewer people, but all were elites. Wang Qianfeng was the only Galaxy Stage expert, but the Intelligence Department’s function was to gather intelligence, a convergence point for all things strange and extraordinary.
The Law Enforcement Department, despite its formidable name, wasn’t actually that strong. It managed internal discipline, monitored the behavior of internal personnel, and was also responsible for ideological indoctrination and re-education.
The Law Enforcement Department had fewer than one hundred members, and all its most capable personnel were brought out today.
"Report! The battle is over. Twenty Demon Clan spies eliminated. Zero casualties on our side. Awaiting instructions!"
"Control the area. Maintain alert."
"Yes, sir!"
"This doesn’t make sense..." He MingXue still felt somewhat dissatisfied. "Such a concealed base, so hard to find... And there are only these small fries? It’s unreasonable..."
Following He MingXue, Wang Lan entered the Demon Clan’s base. Apart from those on guard, the rest of the Law Enforcement Department were meticulously searching for dangers and clues.
Wang Lan arrived at the server Xiao Ai had pinpointed. Although Xiao Ai had already infiltrated it, Wang Lan had the program uninstall all its tool plugins to reduce the risk of exposure. To crack the server’s password, Wang Lan had to do it himself.
Wang Lan’s typing speed was like lightning. Xu Shiyun could only hear a rapid clatter from the keyboard, unable to even see the fingers move. Symbols typed by Wang Lan instantly flooded the computer screen before him.
When it came to computer technology, Xu Shiyun was clueless. But, clueless as he was, he still liked to make small talk.
"Wang Lan, do you have to use a Star Martial Skill just to type?"
"No way! This is just normal typing speed, okay?"
"Oh, come on! How can normal typing speed be this fast? My hands don’t move this fast even when I’m... attending to my wife," Xu Shiyun said, making his crude remark without any inhibition, completely ignoring whether others were present.
"You old lecher, don’t disturb Wang Lan while he’s cracking the password," Zhang Yeqiu said, shooting him a sideways glance as she looked up.
The potency of Xu Shiyun’s crude remarks lay in their suggestiveness, leaving the rest to the imagination. The problem was, once the imagination kicked in, it was hard to stop. As soon as Zhang Yeqiu finished speaking, her pretty face turned beet red.
"Tsk, it’s your mind that’s dirty. I was talking about finger massage techniques. Look, your sister is perfectly calm, not thinking anything inappropriate at all."
Zhang Xiaoxue’s eyes were fixed on Wang Lan’s screen, staring intently.
Zhang Xiaoxue was an Ice Attribute Star Martial Warrior with a naturally cool temperament, rarely showing strong emotional fluctuations. But at that moment, Zhang Yeqiu was surprised to see a rich range of expressions on her sister’s face.
"Xiaoxue, I almost forgot you’re also proficient with computers. Can Wang Lan handle it? Do you want to give it a try?"
"If Wang Lan can’t handle it, then I definitely can’t. He’s a master, an absolute master," Zhang Xiaoxue said, regaining her composure and sighing in admiration.
"Got it!"
Instantly, a TXT page popped up, filled with computer language code.
One glance would make anyone’s head spin.
"This is the backup information for the game young Zhang Jixi played. These numbers, which look like gibberish, are actually chat messages Zhang Jixi sent through the game. They must be transmitting instructions. Look around, see if there are any books that stand out—something they obviously wouldn’t read."
"Let’s all look together!"
The four of them scattered, quickly rummaging through boxes and cabinets.
"Found one! Here’s a novel titled ’Soldier’s Legend’."
"Bring it here."
Wang Lan quickly used the previously deciphered method, cross-referencing the numbers with the book’s content.
"Before the twelfth, produce fifty bottles of Demonic Transformation Potion."
"Deliver them to the greenbelt beneath the Canyuan Road overpass in the New District."
"..."
The next dozen or so messages were all requests to produce Demonic Transformation Potions. After analyzing these, Wang Lan shot to his feet.
"Director He!"
"Huh?" He MingXue had just walked in when he suddenly heard Wang Lan call out to him loudly.
"Director He, this is a base where the Demon Clan manufactures Demonic Transformation Potions! Everyone, keep looking; there must be more evidence!"
"Really? That’s great!"
They had thought they’d only caught some small fry, but finding a manufacturing base for Demonic Transformation Potions was a completely different matter. The Demonic Transformation Potion was the crowning achievement in this series of accomplishments.
"Assessment complete. Law Enforcement Department operation concluded." Suddenly, a voice rang out. Just as He MingXue’s face lit up with ecstasy, Wang Qianfeng walked in, his face wreathed in a smile as wide as a chrysanthemum.
"Wang, what are you doing here? What’s this about an assessment being over?" He MingXue asked, his expression slightly unnatural.
"See for yourself." Wang Qianfeng held the order paper right in front of He MingXue. He MingXue glanced down at it, and his face immediately turned pitch black.
With the establishment of the Shadow Guard Office, his Law Enforcement Department would be reorganized. The Law Enforcement Department would retain its Law Enforcement Branch, while the Shadow Guard Office would immediately begin recruitment and expansion.
The Shadow Guard Office was primarily responsible for covert operations—tasks not suitable for public exposure, such as assassinations, surveillance, and eliminating internal destabilizing elements.
Most importantly, the identities of Shadow Guard Office personnel were highly secret. Everyone had both a public and a covert identity. The personnel for the Shadow Guard Office would mainly be drawn from various departments within the Tianjian Bureau.
They could come from the Intelligence Department, the Action Department, the Internal Affairs Department, or even the Medical Department. Facing the cunning Demon Clan and preparing for potentially drastic future changes, the Tianjian Bureau was implementing a higher level of strategic preparedness.
Upon seeing this order, a smile spread across He MingXue’s face. Deep down, he was already plotting his next move.
Wang Qianfeng, you poached two of my people! I’m not just getting them back; I’m going to poach your two precious talents as well! Poaching is a game anyone can play!
But just as a hint of triumph appeared on his face, his expression suddenly changed.
What did that old scoundrel Wang Qianfeng just say? Mission complete, assessment over? Does that mean from now on, any discoveries aren’t part of the Law Enforcement Department’s tasks? Is that old scoundrel trying to steal the credit?
A pair of eyes filled with murderous intent coldly stared at Wang Qianfeng.
"He Lao’er, why are you looking at me like that?"
"Wang, let’s have a word on the side."
"No need. The mission is more important. Finding the Demonic Transformation Potion production workshop is urgent."
"No, no, no, those are trivial matters. Let my subordinates handle them... Let’s discuss something important..."
"Is there anything more important than the Demonic Transformation Potion?"
"Yes, yes, yes! Giving you a good thrashing!"
"He MingXue... what are you doing? This is a breach of discipline! Believe it or not, I’ll file a complaint against you!"
"I am the head of the Law Enforcement Department. I accept your complaint. But for now, take this!"
Finding the Demon Clan’s Demonic Transformation Potion production workshop wasn’t difficult for the experts of the Tianjian Bureau. If necessary, they could simply use Earth Attribute Star Martial Skills to flip the entire area upside down.
One hundred meters underground, Zhang Yeqiu was the first to discover a hidden chamber. It took the combined efforts of seven Earth Attribute Star Martial Warriors to excavate this secret chamber from deep underground.
Looking at the three expensive manufacturing devices before him, along with some semi-finished Demonic Transformation Potions, a smile spread across Wang Qianfeng’s face. However, the grin inadvertently tugged at the bruise on the corner of his mouth, causing a twinge of pain.
*"Mission to uncover Demonic Transformation Potion production base complete. Reward: 50,000 experience points, 1,000 skill points."*
As the prompt echoed in his mind, Wang Lan immediately knew something was wrong.
Showing off occasionally feels great, but constantly doing it... that’s just asking for trouble. My last breakthrough was just yesterday! After destroying the elite spy group, I leveled up, and my experience for Star Shine Level 6 increased by about thirty percent, around seventeen or eighteen thousand points. To advance from Star Shine Level 6 to Star Shine Level 7 requires sixty thousand experience points. A direct reward of fifty thousand naturally means I’m leveling up again. The problem isn’t leveling up; it’s leveling up again after just one day! What normal person could handle this kind of provocation?
In an instant, Wang Lan moved. His figure flashed as he tried to escape.
"Wang Lan, what are you doing?" Wang Qianfeng was startled by Wang Lan’s sudden action.
"Director Wang, I... I really need to use the restroom!"
"Cut it out. Holding it in for a bit won’t kill you," Xu Shiyun said, an irrepressible smile on his face as he slung an arm around Wang Lan’s shoulder. "We’ve really hit the jackpot this time. I wonder how big the reward from headquarters will be. Who knows, maybe even my rank will get a boost..."
A ripple of Star Energy Fluctuation spread out.
Xu Shiyun’s voice abruptly stopped.
Staring with wide, ghost-seeing eyes, he watched the Star Energy Fluctuation emanating from Wang Lan.
It was a familiar scene, a truly flamboyant display. But... damn it, it had only been one day!
And naturally, Wang Qianfeng witnessed this entire scene.
Yesterday, Wang Lan broke through while unconscious from overexertion; I saw the whole thing. At the time, I could still rationalize it as potential activation triggered by using a super S-rank Star Martial Skill, the Phoenix Form... Even though that explanation was flimsy even to myself, at least it was an excuse, right? But this... this is just too much! Breaking through every day? Can’t you be a little reasonable?
At this moment, the corner of Wang Qianfeng’s mouth, already bruised, throbbed with pain. It twitched uncontrollably, and he couldn’t stop the frequent spasms.
"Huh? Wang Lan is breaking through?" For Zhang Yeqiu and the others, who were interacting with Wang Lan for the first time, it was a shock. Only Wang Qianfeng and Xu Shiyun knew that Wang Lan had just broken through the previous day.
Even so, Wang Lan breaking through without any warning was already astonishing.
People had heard of killing someone at the slightest disagreement, but never of breaking through at the slightest disagreement.
"Um..." Wang Lan turned his head stiffly, forcing a strained smile at Xu Shiyun, whose excited expression was twisting, on the verge of becoming maniacal.
"Xu, please don’t get too excited..."
"Wang Lan, you’re breaking through again? Every single day? If I don’t give you a good thrashing today, I won’t find peace of mind!" Xu Shiyun declared, raising his palm high, aiming a punch straight for Wang Lan’s forehead.
"Wait, Xu, listen to my explanation!"
"Do you even need to explain?"The most update n0vels are published on ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
"Yes, I do! I’m really innocent. I told you just now, I had to go urgently. You know how it is, when nature calls, you can’t just hold it in. With you stopping me like that, the pressure of my... urgency... just broke through my Star Power shackles. It was all because I was forced to hold it in!"
"Go to hell—!"

chapters.title: Chapter 152: The Dust Settles
chapters.content:
Chapter 152: Chapter 152: The Dust Settles
A late-stage Star Cloud Stage warrior chasing a weak, middle-stage Star Shine Stage rookie across an open field.
Was this a distortion of human nature or a fall from morality?
What infuriated Wang Lan even more was the cold indifference of people’s hearts. So many people were watching from the sidelines, yet not a single one stepped forward to stop Xu Shiyun’s violence.
"Life is about movement. Suddenly exercising my muscles like this feels refreshing," Xu Shiyun commented with a satisfied smile on his face while sitting in the car.
"Screw off! I don’t want to talk to you," Wang Lan disdainfully retorted.
"Being tough is great, though. My hands hurt from hitting you, yet you don’t even have a scratch on you..."
"That reminds me: I’m a Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior. I have a premonition that you’ll eventually end up in my hands."
His voice was deep and chilling, and Xu Shiyun’s face immediately changed color.
In the exhilaration of the fight, he’d almost forgotten that Wang Lan was a Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior, and one of the top-tier ones at that. Forget premonitions, Xu Shiyun was certain he’d eventually fall into Wang Lan’s hands.
A scene flashed through Xu Shiyun’s mind.
Himself, gravely injured on a hospital bed, with Wang Lan approaching in a white coat, striding with ruthless determination.
"Dr. Wang Lan, we have a critically injured patient who urgently needs treatment."
"Oh, isn’t this Brother Xu Shiyun? Don’t worry. Your brother will take good care of you. Now, where’s the saw?"
"Dr. Wang Lan, I’ll go get the anesthetic."
"No need, warriors of the Tianjian Bureau are brave souls. Our creed is to endure without anesthesia..."
The scene shattered there, and Xu Shiyun shivered with a chill.
Wang Lan slightly lowered his head, a cold smirk playing on the corner of his mouth. Seeing that smile, Xu Shiyun knew that if he got injured again, he might be in for a rough time. Looking up, he saw Zhang Xiaoxue, who hadn’t been speaking much, staring at Wang Lan curiously.
"Sister Xiaoxue, is there something wrong with Wang Lan? You’re staring so intently, you’re making him shy," Xu Shiyun hurriedly changed the subject.
"Wang Lan’s Medical Star Martial Technique is different from what we’ve seen. His Self Healing is very fast, and his Star Energy Fluctuation isn’t noticeable. It didn’t even get disrupted when you were hitting him. Does his healing process not get interrupted?"
"Can treatment be interrupted?" Wang Lan asked, looking up.
That question was a bit pointed.
If there were another Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior in the car, they’d probably go crazy. Isn’t it perfectly normal for any Star Martial Skill to be disrupted or countered? Asking such a question is just too much.
"Younger Brother Wang Lan... Almost all Medical Star Martial Techniques can be disrupted. The only exceptions are those that utilize Life Force. Wait a second, Wang Lan, don’t tell me you’ve mastered Life Force?" Zhang Yeqiu suddenly turned around and asked excitedly.
"Sis, can you watch the road while driving?"
"SCREECH—" A harsh braking sound interrupted them.
"Is your Medical Attribute talent related to Life Force?"
"I don’t know. My awakening talent is Self Healing. It was originally a passive skill, capable of repairing my injuries, speeding up wound healing, and tissue regeneration. As I became more proficient and my Star Martial level rose, I could extend this ability to others. However, the energy it uses to heal myself is only a third of what it takes to heal someone else. So basically, my main ability is still Self-Repair."
"Then that must be it. Your true talent is the regeneration of Life Force; Medical Star Martial Techniques are just applications of Life Force. Your ability has many potential paths for development. Using it solely as a Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior seems like a waste," Zhang Xiaoxue said matter-of-factly.
"How so?"
"Your ability has many potential applications. Being a punching bag definitely isn’t the best one. However, your ability allows you to be fearless of injuries, so you could train with more than five times the intensity of an ordinary person. With your healing ability, five times the training intensity should allow you to become a first-rate warrior in a short time."
"Uh..."
Five times the training intensity? I’d love that too, but the system doesn’t allow it.
"Another direction is the development of Star Martial Skills. Developing Star Martial Skills is extremely dangerous, and most people wouldn’t attempt it without absolute confidence. Behind every mature and perfected Star Martial Skill may be the lives of a few, or even dozens, or hundreds of Star Martial Warriors who died developing it. With your unique condition, you can develop Star Martial Skills without fear of danger. If you can develop an A-rank Star Martial Skill, you’ll make history. If you independently develop an S-rank Star Martial Skill, I guarantee you’ll be immortalized."
"Who wants to be immortalized!" Wang Lan was exasperated.
"Of course, being a Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior is the most straightforward path for you, and you’ll probably end up going that way, right?"
"You’re wrong..." Xu Shiyun immediately refuted Zhang Xiaoxue’s speculation. "Wang Lan is destined to become a powerful warrior. If he really wanted to be a comfortable Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior, he wouldn’t have such strong combat abilities."
"But no matter what, I’m envious of the many choices Wang Lan will have in the future. Capable of offense and defense, of scholarly pursuits and martial arts."
"With the way you guys are talking, I feel like I can safely go wild in the future."
"Go ahead and be wild. If you get yourself killed, I will definitely take care of your body. As your brother, I might not have a next life to offer, but for this one, that’s the least I can do."
「Back at the Tianjian Bureau」
Wang Qianfeng and He MingXue reported to Director Lu Zhao. With everything settled, Wang Lan could finally bring his aunt home.
「In the Tianjian Bureau dormitory」
Wang Qi watched the images copied from Dr. Ma Bo’s mind.
"Throughout the vast history of the human race, we have never lacked great scientists. Even if I die today, the door to human biotechnology won’t be closed. Soon, someone will rediscover the treasures I’ve opened up. As long as the human race still draws breath, we shall strive to keep improving."
These were Song Zifeng’s last words. The moment the Soul Bead shattered, Wang Qi was already in tears.
In his final moments, he was still desperately trying to protect her safety. Song Zifeng didn’t know that even if the Demon Clan knew that Wang Qi also possessed that formula, they wouldn’t dare lay a finger on her.
"Auntie!" Wang Lan knocked on the door.
"Hmm! Lan Lan, you’re back? How did it go? I heard you had another operation?"
"The issue is resolved. I’m here to take you home."
"Great!"
Wang Qi had been eager to go home; she hadn’t seen Jiajia for three days and missed her terribly.
「On the eighth day of the new year」
This day was a special one for the whole world.
Just seven days after the release of Life Number One on the first day of the new year, Jiayi Biotech Company announced its Blue Sky Life Potion. It repaired the human genome through gene encoding, fundamentally curing diseases within the body’s own systems.Thɪs NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
A single dose costing only fifty thousand could take effect in a week, curing hundreds of diseases, including cancer.
This news was a true blessing for humanity. The treatment course for Life Number One took three years, but the Blue Sky Life Potion only needed seven days.
With the country’s strong promotion, Jade Country’s entire network was abuzz. Through word of mouth, the Blue Sky Life Potion was hailed like a miracle drug—it was as if one dose could turn back the years and another could grant immortality.
Almost overnight, Wang Qi, who had always been unknown, shot to the top of global trending searches, with an unreachable lead over the second-ranked name.
On every street corner, discussions about the Blue Sky Life Potion abounded. Online and offline, debates about Dr. Wang Qi were everywhere. And at this time, whether deliberately or not, no one remembered Dr. Ma Bo, who had made headlines all over the world on the first day of the new year. Not even comparisons were made between Dr. Ma Bo and Dr. Wang Qi.
What was there to compare?
From its inception, Life Number One was mired in controversy.
Despite its ability to treat cancer, most people couldn’t even fathom the cost of 3.6 million for a three-year treatment. Opinions were polarized then: its supporters praised it exuberantly, while its detractors criticized it vehemently.
Now, with the advent of the Blue Sky Life Potion, it trounced Life Number One with absolute strength.
The treatment cost: only fifty thousand.
The course: merely seven days.
Seven days was practically an instantaneous result.
Moreover, the clear disparity in reception was obvious to any discerning eye. When Life Number One was released, it was just a commercial launch. But the release of the Blue Sky Life Potion—
Imperial Capital TV, Imperial Capital media... One might have thought Jiayi Biotech Company was some secret state research facility.
After the country publicly announced Dr. Ma Bo’s crimes on the fifth day of the new year, Dr. Ma Bo fell from a national hero and great scientist to a traitor of humanity overnight.
Though there were some who questioned Dr. Ma Bo’s crimes online, the evidence presented by the Tianjian Bureau was solid, and no one could find the slightest flaw.
Faced with the evidence and their inherent trust in the government, aside from a few contrarians who jumped out to defend Dr. Ma Bo, the public universally condemned him.
While turmoil stirred outside, Wang Lan was snuggled in bed playing with his phone.
Yesterday, Xu Xiangwen and the gang had dragged him out, and along with Xie Sisi, they had a wild day of fun. Perhaps owing to Xu Xiangwen’s resentment as a single guy, he had secretly spiked Wang Lan’s drink with a cocktail.
That drink... was potent. It tasted light when sipped, more like a flavored beverage. But once it kicked in, it was like an earthquake.
In any case, less than thirty minutes after drinking that cocktail, Wang Lan had no memory of the events that followed. When he woke up, it was three in the afternoon, and he was in his own bed.
With a slight headache, Wang Lan decided to just lie in bed and play with his phone.
Every headline was pushing news about his aunt.
The online praise was quite entertaining to read, and before he knew it, another hour had passed. But as with anything, too much became boring—even a song played on loop all day would be unbearable.
Wang Lan delved into his mind and opened the system.
Player Level: Star Shine Seven, with a balance of one thousand eight hundred skill points left. He originally had over three thousand, but after storing one thousand five hundred into the Phoenix Form, this much remained.
So many skill points, what a pain, he mused.
All of Wang Lan’s skills were at Silver Nine, and they had even been pushed to (99/100).
Once he could break through to the Star Cloud Stage, Wang Lan could upgrade his skills to Gold in minutes. Gold skills, by comparison, would all be S-rank if measured against conventional Star Martial Skills.
Of course, this didn’t refer to S-rank power. Even if the Basic Skills were upgraded to Gold, they could not possibly match the power of an S-rank Star Martial Skill. It merely meant that skills reaching the Gold level had a training difficulty equivalent to S-rank.
Maybe Basic Skills can only be cultivated to S-rank at their limit. After all, upgrading from Gold to Platinum requires ten thousand skill points. Ten thousand points—how long would it take me to accumulate that? At most, I could only upgrade Inch Strength Fist to Platinum. Raising other Basic Skills that high wouldn’t be cost-effective. With those skill points, it would be better to learn an S-rank Star Martial Skill.
"DING-DONG—"
His phone chimed.
Wang Lan lazily picked up his phone, unlocked it, and opened it.
Suddenly, Wang Lan sprang up as if he had been shot from a trampoline. Looking at the notification on his phone, his face lit up with sheer ecstasy.

chapters.title: Chapter 153 Star Martial Skill Crescent Arrow
chapters.content:
Chapter 153: Chapter 153 Star Martial Skill Crescent Arrow
"Respected Mr. Wang Lan, the Star Martial Skill you requested has been found by Star Martial Hall, with a match rate of 99%. Please come to Star Martial Hall to purchase it as soon as you see this notification. If you’re late, someone else might get it first!" The message even ended with a playful little text emoticon. Star Martial Hall’s usual style was quite solemn and old-fashioned, so Wang Lan was surprised their automated message could be so informal.
However, this wasn’t a detail he should be dwelling on.
He got up, dressed, and within just five minutes, was already in the underground garage. He didn’t even take the time to see what the Star Martial Skill was.
What did a 99% match rate mean? It meant that the requirements Wang Lan had submitted were nearly 100% satisfied. He still remembered his demands: long-range, A-grade; just the grade of the Star Martial Skill itself was definitely the kind where if you were quick, you got it, and if not, you missed out. Wang Lan had already figured out Star Martial Hall’s typical antics; even their posted missions were fiercely competed over. An A-grade Star Martial Skill going on the market? Wouldn’t they go crazy competing for it?
He started the engine and engaged the gears.
Time to show off some real skills!
VROOOM—
The giant off-road vehicle roared like a wild beast, charging out of the underground garage towards Star Martial Hall with an air of "death to those who stand in my way."
Luckily, it was only the eighth day of the Lunar New Year, so not many people were returning to Suzhou City yet. Star Martial Warriors, in particular, mostly waited until after the Lantern Festival to come back. The journey was smooth, taking only fifteen minutes to reach Star Martial Hall.
Wang Lan jumped out of the car and headed straight for the Star Martial Skill purchasing area.
"Sir, hello, what kind of Star Martial Skill do you need?" an attendant asked.
"My matched Star Martial Skill has arrived; I’m just buying this one," Wang Lan said, opening the Star Martial Skill store on his device. There, in the A-grade section, the Star Martial Skill that perfectly matched his requirements shimmered with a faint light. The number displayed above the Star Martial Skill was seventy-six. This didn’t mean there were seventy-six copies; rather, seventy-six people had already added it to their shopping carts, just one tap of the ’buy’ button away from owning it. Once pressed, the Star Martial Skill would belong to that single person.
Seeing this, Wang Lan didn’t dare hesitate and quickly added the Star Martial Skill to his cart.
Crescent Arrow, 78.
"Damn it, why can’t I buy it? What’s going on?" Wang Lan exclaimed, frustrated. "Attendant, take a look at this for me! Why isn’t there any response when I click the buy button?"
"Certainly, sir," the attendant replied. "The tablet seems to be lagging, sir. Probably due to heavy traffic recently."
"Heavy traffic, my ass! What kind of traffic is there during the New Year? Hurry and get me another tablet; I want this Star Martial Skill!"
"Crap, mine’s not working either!" another customer shouted.
"Damn, is it really stuck?" someone else muttered.
DING-DONG— "Congratulations on successfully purchasing the A-grade Star Martial Skill, Crescent Arrow."
Suddenly, a notification chimed from the tablet in Wang Lan’s hands. At that instant, the entire Star Martial Skill purchasing hall of Star Martial Hall fell into an unexpected, deathly silence.
"It wasn’t stuck?" Wang Lan looked up, puzzled, and immediately sensed something was wrong. A dozen or so pairs of eyes, blazing with fury as if ready to kill, shot towards him.
The attendant stammered, "Maybe the network just recovered... Congratulations to this gentleman for successfully purchasing an A-grade Star Martial Skill."
"What kind of joke is this!" a man roared. "I made dozens of phone calls to scrape together eight million, and just like that, I can’t buy it? No way! Star Martial Hall must give us an explanation!"
"That’s right! Your network lagged; you should take responsibility!" another chimed in.
"According to you all, should our hall hand out an A-grade Star Martial Skill to every single person here?" Suddenly, a voice cut through the noise, instantly putting Wang Lan on alert.
The man’s voice was soft, like someone muttering to themselves, yet it clearly reached everyone’s ears without the aid of a microphone. Moreover, Wang Lan hadn’t felt even the slightest Star Energy Fluctuation. The person speaking was an expert.
As if confirming Wang Lan’s thoughts, the moment that voice sounded, the group of Star Martial Warriors who had been causing a commotion sat down obediently, like well-behaved children.
The side door opposite opened, and a man in his thirties, wearing a suit and glasses, walked over slowly.
"Good afternoon, Manager."
"Manager!"
"Manager..."
As he walked by, every attendant bowed and greeted the middle-aged man.
"Take him to complete the transaction," the manager said, gesturing towards Wang Lan.
An attendant approached Wang Lan. "This way, sir, please."
Puzzled, Wang Lan stood up. He quickly pieced together the truth of what had just transpired.
Star Martial Hall was doing this deliberately! The so-called lag others were experiencing was definitely due to deliberate interference. If that was the case, then the appearance of this A-grade Star Martial Skill might have even been orchestrated by someone. Otherwise, how could it be such a coincidence? He’d submitted his request only a few days ago; all told, it hadn’t even been ten days, right? Finding a 99% match for a Star Martial Skill in just ten days? If it wasn’t due to his own outrageous luck, then someone must have specifically searched for this Star Martial Skill for him immediately after receiving his request. That was the only way it made sense. If that were the case, it would be utterly absurd if those other people managed to buy the Star Martial Skill.
Realizing this, Wang Lan looked at the man with glasses, a faint smile playing on his lips.
"You’re Wang Lan?" the man suddenly asked as Wang Lan passed by him.
"Yes."
"Do you recognize me?" The man’s gaze was incredibly sharp, like the edge of an arrow.
The instant the man’s gaze met Wang Lan’s, Wang Lan felt as if an arrow had shot him in the face.
"No, I don’t."
"My name is Gong Jian. Gong as in ’Dragon Gong,’ Jian as in ’sword.’ I’m the manager of the Star Martial Skill Trading House here. If you need to buy Star Martial Skills in the future, you can contact me." Saying this, he took out a business card and gently placed it in Wang Lan’s jacket pocket.
"Thank you!" Wang Lan replied. He didn’t know the man’s background, and it was clear Gong Jian wasn’t about to reveal it. So, Wang Lan simply thanked him politely and followed the attendant into the trading area.
To Wang Lan, this scene felt very common—wasn’t a manager giving a customer his business card a normal part of business interactions?
But to the Star Martial Warriors present, it was astonishing. Wang Lan might not know Gong Jian, but how could they not?
Gong Jian had been transferred to the Star Martial Hall in Suzhou City five years ago, serving as the manager of the Star Martial Skill Trading House. He was incredibly strong and ruthless in his methods.
There were two places within Star Martial Hall that definitely required a powerful figure to maintain order: the Soul Bead trading area and the Star Martial Skill trading area. In other places, having someone at the Galaxy Stage to keep order would have been sufficient. Generally, those who needed to purchase Soul Beads or Star Martial Skills through Star Martial Hall were Star Martial Warriors without backing, their strength peaking at the Star Cloud Stage.
But no one had expected Suzhou City to get someone at the Star Sea Stage to maintain order. For such a harmonious city as Suzhou, was it really necessary to bring out such a heavyweight?
It was often said that the stronger one’s power, the better their temper. Many high-ranking individuals at the Star Sea Stage were all smiles and extremely good-natured. But Gong Jian was not like that.
When he first arrived in Suzhou City, a few people, seeing that the manager of the Star Martial Skill Trading House had changed, decided to test Gong Jian’s strength. The outcome was clear, and their end was quite tragic. Five Star Cloud Stage teams all had their Star Palaces crippled.
That move had an immediate impact. From that moment on, there were no more disturbances in the Star Martial Skill Trading House. Not just the Star Martial Skill Trading House, but the entire Star Martial Hall remained peaceful. Even the most hot-tempered individuals would speak in hushed tones once inside Star Martial Hall.
Back then, the five from the Star Cloud Stage had been furious and appealed to the Tianjian Bureau for arbitration. They claimed it was just a prank, merely wanting to test Gong Jian’s strength, yet Gong Jian had crippled their Star Palaces, ruining their lives. Such actions were exceedingly brutal.
However, Gong Jian provided only one reason: Star Martial Hall is a national institution. Causing trouble in Star Martial Hall is tantamount to causing trouble for the nation. Tarnishing the reputation of Star Martial Hall is desecrating the country—how could the country tolerate you? It’s like running up to the gates of Tianhe Building in the Imperial Capital and defacing the portrait of the founding emperor; you’d be shot dead by machine guns on the spot. Having your Star Palace crippled would be getting off lightly in comparison.
Such impeccable logic, truly commanding respect.
What could the Tianjian Bureau say? That they got what they deserved!Follow current novᴇls on NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
Following the attendant into the trading room, Wang Lan’s mind was still pondering who exactly this Gong Jian was. Suddenly, he recalled what He Jinze had once told him: Eld Di’s faction! His mother was the figurehead of Eld Di’s faction. Because of her presence, Eld Di’s faction had coalesced into a very powerful force. The Five Elders’ factions were likely the same. The Five Elders—any one of them could change the landscape of the Jade Country’s Star Martial Warrior world, and this was no exaggeration. It wasn’t that a single person’s power was so immense, but that a faction’s influence was truly that significant. If he hadn’t awakened his Star Martial Warrior talent, Wang Lan would have been like a chick still in its egg—unknown and insignificant to the world. However, once he awakened his Star Martial Warrior talent, it meant Wang Lan had officially emerged. Whether he liked it or not, or whether he left the "novice village," he had already stepped onto this stage. Every move he made would be watched by countless people. Submitting his request this time had immediately resulted in special treatment. And Gong Jian giving him his business card, along with saying he could be contacted directly for future needs, implied only one thing: ’Whatever Star Martial Skill you want, just say the word, and I can get it for you.’ Maybe I should ask Gong Jian later if there are any S-grade or Super S-grade Star Martial Skills available? Getting me ten or eight of them would be nice, wouldn’t it?
"Sir, the Crescent Arrow is priced at eight million. Would you like to pay by card or scan a code?"
A whole month’s rent, gone just like that.
"By card."
"Very well."
As expected, the Star Martial Skill was indeed a Soul Bead; it seemed the technology of imprinting Star Martial Skills onto Soul Beads had matured. The Soul Bead was about the size of a pigeon’s egg, likely a mid-level Soul Bead. A single mid-level Soul Bead was worth hundreds of thousands! No wonder a Star Martial Skill worth eight million came in such exquisite packaging.
Carrying the Star Martial Skill, Wang Lan drove straight home. Upon arriving, he couldn’t wait to enter his room.
This was the second time he was absorbing a Star Martial Skill from a Soul Bead. Flame Sword and Star Cloud Sword Dance had both been directly instilled into his mind through Spiritual Engraving by those two powerhouses.
Picking up the Soul Bead, he absorbed its energy just as he would Star Power. The Star Power within the bead surged into his body instantaneously, while a spiritual message exploded in his mind.
"Acquirable Star Martial Skill detected. Spend one hundred skill points to learn?"
"Learn!"
Instantly, a new skill icon lit up in Wang Lan’s skill list. The icon depicted a bow formed from a crescent moon, with an arrow nocked upon it.
Profound insights instantly washed over his mind. He mastered the basic application of Crescent Arrow as if he had cultivated it for a very long time.
Crescent Arrow, Silver LV1 (0/100)
Crescent Arrow was a ranged Star Martial Skill and also an advanced application of Star Power form manipulation. In his view, this type of form manipulation was far more challenging than the Star Cloud Sword Dance taught by Wang Qianfeng. Wang Qianfeng’s form manipulation, to put it plainly, merely involved evenly distributing Star Power throughout the body and exquisitely coordinating Star Power with bodily movements to execute Star Martial Skills. But the form manipulation of Crescent Arrow was akin to the internal energy cultivation described in the wuxia novels from his previous life; it followed the body’s meridian pathways.
Using the body’s meridians as the tension of a bowstring, Star Power condensed into an arrow between his fingers. A single shot could reach a range of a hundred meters.

chapters.title: Chapter 154 Can Still Be Connected
chapters.content:
Chapter 154: Chapter 154 Can Still Be Connected
Don’t underestimate this 100-meter range. The attack range for elemental Star Martial Warriors is only between 20 to 30 meters, and anything over 50 meters can count as a long-range attack. Hitting a target at 100 meters is already a rare feat of high long-range prowess.
Wang Lan excitedly set up the training field as a 100-meter shooting range. The initial power of a Star Martial Skill determined its growth potential. At least, this standard of judgment was effective for Wang Lan.
Wang Lan arrived at the 100-meter mark, but he frowned.
At this distance, even the circular targets were blurry, let alone the bullseye, much less hitting it.
It feels... I might as well have an automatic rifle in my hands.
He extended one hand, raising his index finger and thumb, with the index finger aimed at the distant target and the thumb forming a right angle with it.
This was the starting posture for Crescent Arrow, and Wang Lan didn’t quite understand why this specific posture was necessary.
Did I *have* to raise my thumb? Could I not fire ten arrows at once with all ten fingers?
The Crescent Arrow Star Martial Skill was activated. Instantly, the specially compressed Star Power coursed through his body’s meridians at high speed. His meridians were like entangled tree roots. As soon as the Star Power flowed through a unique meridian, it accelerated instantly.
Suddenly, Wang Lan’s arm lit up. Amidst the Star Energy Fluctuation, a pair of dull golden wings emerged at his wrist, and a cluster of Star Power began surging back and forth between them.
In that moment, Wang Lan finally understood.
Why it could only be launched from the index finger—maybe the creator of this Star Martial Skill had thought about firing with all ten fingers, but in the end, only the index finger remained.
And why raise the thumb? Only when the thumb was raised would the wings at the wrist unfold. What seemed like superfluous movements were actually essential and could not be skipped; they were crucial.
But really, taking four to five seconds just for the initial steps—is that okay? In four to five seconds, others could finish me off several times over. During that time, couldn’t just about anyone kill me?
Wang Lan looked at the target before him.
WHOOSH—
A silver-white arrow shot out from Wang Lan’s fingertip at breakneck speed, fiercely hurling towards the other side.
Then it zipped past the target, a beautiful near miss, and instantly dispersed like fireworks.
Wang Lan’s face darkened a bit.
This is the A-rank Star Martial Skill I spent eight million on, with an effective range of a hundred meters, right? Did I measure the distance wrong? Am I supposed to practice archery to use this Star Martial Skill?
That doesn’t seem right either. After learning the Star Cloud Sword Dance, a Basic Sword Skill automatically appeared among my Basic Skills. Having mastered Crescent Arrow, shouldn’t I get some basic archery skill?
Instantly, Wang Lan realized the problem.
The key lay in the skill level of Silver 1. Crescent Arrow was an A-rank Star Martial Skill, with the learning difficulty starting at Silver. Being at Silver 1 meant he had barely learned it.
And barely learning it meant that just being able to release it was considered passing, right?
That so-called accuracy, activation speed, as well as the power and range of Crescent Arrow, all needed to be improved later on.
Wang Lan decided not to push the limits and fired an arrow at the PS armor beside him.
BOOM—
A burst of flame erupted, yet the PS armor showed no damage at all. However, the PS armor had a system to record energy quantities, so a number soon popped up on its display—1.
One, representing one point of firepower, roughly equivalent to the power of a single bullet.
The initial power was decent. Being comparable to a bullet, it was certainly much stronger than a regular arrow.
He spent three hundred skill points to push the skill to Silver 4.
Instantly, Wang Lan felt a clearer sense of Crescent Arrow. If the Star Martial Skill had previously given Wang Lan the feeling of toddling, now he felt as though he could run and jump with it.
He raised his hand, and Star Power surged instantly. At his wrist, the pair of golden wings snapped open in a flash. WHOOSH! An arrow was fired in less than a second.
BOOM—
BEEP BEEP BEEP—
The screen displayed an energy equivalent of 3.
This was three times stronger than before, rivaling the power of armor-piercing rounds.
But on the Basic Skills page, there was still no hint of a basic archery skill appearing. Perhaps the arrows fired by Star Martial Skills were fundamentally different from those shot with a regular bow and string. Hence, there was no commonality to learn from.
Wang Lan added points again, directly spending one thousand points to elevate Crescent Arrow to Silver 9.
In an instant, Wang Lan felt a subtle change in the Star Martial Skill. Its operational pathways seemed to have grown more complex.
If the operational pathways of a Star Martial Skill were likened to mechanical parts, then upon reaching Silver 9, both their complexity and precision had increased significantly.
Wang Lan raised his hand again, and Star Power surged in an instant. At the same time, a mass of Star Power suddenly rushed up his arm, shooting straight to his forehead.
If there had been a mirror in front of Wang Lan, he would have seen his right eye covered in a layer of golden light, its pupil seemingly transformed into a slowly rotating gear.
Time seemed to slow down. The previously indistinct bullseye was now magnified and brought closer through the adjustment of his eyes. The previously blurry bullseye now appeared crystal clear.
Damn, is this a scope’s design? A combination of scope and dynamic vision?
FWOOSH—
A silver-white arrow shot out from Wang Lan’s fingertip, breaking the sound barrier and instantly striking the distant bullseye.
BOOM—
With a loud bang, the target burst apart. The scattered fragments were blown away by the shockwave of the explosion, turning into numerous shrapnel littered around. The power of this arrow was comparable to a small hand grenade.
Wang Lan watched the scene in shock. The power of the Silver 9 Crescent Arrow was surprisingly good. And the Star Power consumption wasn’t much more than when it was at Silver 1.
What thrilled Wang Lan more was that this Star Martial Skill actually carried a derivative skill of the Pupil Skill category. With this, Wang Lan not only had long-range attack capabilities but also reconnaissance abilities. Although it might not be as powerful as Xu Xiangwen’s Heavenly Eye, there was at least potential for development.
Just because it’s not strong now doesn’t mean it won’t be strong later. Just pump in the skill points, right? What if a Gold-grade Crescent Arrow could grant abilities like X-ray vision or infrared night vision?
Google seaʀᴄh ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
Wang Lan took several deep breaths to calm his excited heart and immersed his mind in the system.
Crescent Arrow, Silver LV9 (0/100). A long-range shooting Star Martial Skill. Star Power forms a Star Power arrow to kill the target, with an effective range of 150 meters.
An extra fifty meters of range, huh?
In fact, long-range capabilities might not be very useful in actual combat. After all, although Crescent Arrow was powerful, its shooting speed wasn’t faster than firearms. If one were really attacking an enemy from 150 meters away, the chances of hitting them were slim.
Star Martial Skills depended on the context and timing in which they were used. No matter the Star Martial Skill, it only worked effectively when used at the right time. Firearms were still powerful, but in the hands of ordinary people, they couldn’t reach their full potential.
And Star Martial Warriors had Star Martial Skills. In the Different Dimensional Space, firearms couldn’t be used, so gradually, Star Martial Warriors stopped using guns. People like Wang Lan, special agents of the Tianjian Bureau, actually did have gun permits. With an application, they could even get heavy snipers. However, holding a gun not only affected combat but also didn’t guarantee hitting the enemy.
Just then, the system suddenly emitted a buzzing sound.
After that, two Star Martial Skills suddenly lit up on the page. "Discovered combinable Star Martial Skills. Do you want to spend one thousand skill points to combine?"
This prompt made Wang Lan pause, but he quickly understood what the system meant.
Combining Star Martial Skills had another term in this world: Compound Star Martial Skill!
Only when one had a very deep comprehension of two different Star Martial Skills and a certain mastery of controlling Star Power could they attempt to use a Compound Star Martial Skill. Of course, the power of a Compound Star Martial Skill was absolutely a super-enhanced version.
But generally speaking, one shouldn’t even think about a Compound Star Martial Skill while still in the Star Cloud Stage. Only those who had reached the Galaxy Stage in their Cultivation Level and had perfected their Star Martial Skills to a masterful degree could attempt it.
The most classic example of a Compound Star Martial Skill was the Earth Vein Thunder Web used by Wang Qianfeng. The combination of Thunder and Earth Attribute Star Martial Skills could create an attack filled with Thunder Power, paralyzing the enemy with thunder while the earth aspect suffocated them—a fatal move.
And another terrifying feature of performing a Compound Star Martial Skill was losing the attribute counter effect.
For example, Wang Qianfeng’s Earth Vein Thunder Web. Normally, the Thunder Attribute could counter the Earth Attribute. But the activation of Earth Vein Thunder Web itself carried the Thunder Attribute, so an enemy’s Thunder Attribute attacks would no longer be able to counter this move. The weakness of the Thunder Attribute being countered by wind also disappeared, as the Earth Attribute could block wind attacks.
With Compound Star Martial Skills in action, one could only meet force with force.
But... why is it the Flame Sword?
Wang Lan looked puzzled.
Aren’t Compound Star Martial Skills usually based on nature-changing Star Martial Skills? Two different attribute Star Martial Skills are used simultaneously in combination. The Crescent Arrow is a shape-changing type, while Flame Sword is a nature-changing type. What kind of combination is this?
Usually, the correct approach to this kind of problem was, why ask so many questions? Just combine them and see what happens!
Skill points aren’t the issue; the problem is... there are no skill points left!
Dammit, combining Star Martial Skills costs a thousand points, but I only have eight hundred left.
Damn!
All his Star Martial Skill points were pumped up to 99/100 progression. Plus, after using the Phoenix Form twice before and saving one thousand five hundred skill points into the Phoenix Form, Wang Lan had extravagantly reduced his four or five thousand skill points down to just one thousand eight hundred.
Now, after upgrading one A-rank Star Martial Skill to max level, he was left with eight hundred.
He was short two hundred skill points...
Two hundred skill points... undertake two hundred challenges? But whom to challenge? School hasn’t even started yet. To farm points from the likes of Xie Sisi and the others... they’re all my own people; I can’t bring myself to do it.
He flipped through his phone and saw Xu Shiyun’s number.
"Hello, Xu?"
"Wang Lan, I’m in Hainan. What’s up?"
"You went to Hainan? Then never mind..."
"What are you hemming and hawing about? Just spit it out!" Lying on the beach in Hainan and wearing sunglasses, the corner of his eye kept sneaking glances at the joyfully running swimsuit-clad girls on the beach.
Life doesn’t get more pleasant than this.
In this moment, if one were to play a song, ’I’m in the warm southern sun, where it’s summer all year round; you’re in the northern ice and snow, frozen into a dog,’ it would be quite fitting for the scene.
"No worries, I was just thinking of finding someone to spar with to train my actual combat abilities."
"Yo? That dedicated, huh? Not forgetting to improve yourself even during the New Year? Promising! There are plenty of guys in the bureau. The two sisters from the Zhang Family are quite good, and Lige is also decent. They probably wouldn’t refuse to help you train."
"That’s the thing... Xu, I feel like I can’t beat them," Wang Lan said anxiously.
"Huh? Isn’t it normal for you not to beat them? Wait a second... What do you mean by that? You think you can’t beat them, so you come to me? Since when did you get so cocky? You..."
BEEP BEEP BEEP—
Xu Shiyun looked at his phone, so furious he was grinding his teeth.
You little rascal, just wait till I get back...

chapters.title: Chapter 155: I’ve Been Annoyed with You for a Long Time
chapters.content:
Chapter 155: Chapter 155: I’ve Been Annoyed with You for a Long Time
What to do?
In the Tianjian Bureau, the only one willing to let Wang Lan hit them without using Star Martial Skills was Xu Shiyun, I guess. Otherwise, I’d have to buy two hundred Soul Beads. Two hundred Soul Beads would cost eighteen million. Better forget about it. It’s not that I can’t afford it; it’s just completely unnecessary. Forget it, I’ll just save up skill points in battles after school starts.
DING DONG—
A text message popped up on his phone, sent by Xie Sisi.
"Wang Lan, are you home? Can I come over for a visit?"
Huh? Is an opportunity just presenting itself?
Wang Lan’s eyes suddenly lit up.
"Welcome, welcome, a very warm welcome."
It would be awkward for me to take the initiative to invite someone, but since she brought it up, it’s fine to accept. But to hit her over two hundred times... that seems a bit cruel, doesn’t it? Never mind, I’ll get Xu Xiangwen to share the burden.
Immediately, he made a call. "Xu Xiangwen, come over to my house for training and vent your excess bestial energy!"
"You’re the one with excess bestial energy! You just wait, see how I beat you up this time."
Xu Xiangwen and Gong Feiyu came together; they arrived before Xie Sisi.
"Lanzi, did you break through to the Star Cloud Stage this winter break?" Xu Xiangwen asked loudly as they parked their cars in the garage and got out.
"How could it be that easy? I’m only at the mid-stage of the Star Shine Stage now. You two took over a year to break through to the Star Cloud Stage; I’ve only had half a year at most." Wang Lan, seeing them arrive, whipped off his jacket to reveal a tight-fitting t-shirt.
"Then I can rest easy," Xu Xiangwen said with a faint smile, rubbing his wrists.
"Rest easy? About what?"
"Your training room is equipped with PS armor, right? And I remember there’s an electromagnetic protection barrier, isn’t there?"
"Yeah!"
"How about... we don’t practice close combat this time?"
Wang Lan paused, slowly turning his head to look at Xu Xiangwen, who was jauntily slicking back his hair.
"Buddy, you’ve been getting a bit cocky lately... Who gave you that confidence?"
"What confidence? It’s just a minor breakthrough to the Star Cloud Stage and some small progress in my Star Martial Skills..."
"Fine! Since you’re asking for it, I’ll accommodate you. Come on, change your clothes, get up here."
Xu Xiangwen quickly took off his jacket and whooshed up onto the combat platform. Gong Feiyu grabbed a can of cola and lay down on a nearby recliner, a smile on his face.
"Wang Lan, I told you about my Star Martial Skill during the intermediate trials. But at that time, my Star Martial level was only at the Star Shine Stage, so I couldn’t unleash its full power. After breaking through to the Star Cloud Stage, my proficiency with Star Martial Skills has reached a new height. Moreover, my set of Star Martial Skills belongs to the Yang Attribute, which involves a nature transformation. After casting it, my body’s strength will multiply, and I can achieve localized metamorphosis. However, my metamorphosis is purely caused by the Star Martial Skills, not some kind of mutation-type talent. My bloodline is very pure."
"No one is doubting your bloodline. Wait, the Yang Attribute also has nature transformation?"
"Since the Yang Attribute is an attribute, how could it not have a nature transformation? Although the Yin and Yang attributes are not among the seven fundamental attributes, the seven fundamental attributes are derived from them. My Star Martial Skill is called Pure Yang Skill, Star Martial rank: A! Once activated, my speed, strength, reaction, and defense will all multiply by several times. It possesses capabilities for breaching defenses, agile combat, and both long-range and close-range attacks. I haven’t learned the long-range manifestation, ’Mingling,’ yet, but in close combat, three Gong Feiyus wouldn’t be enough for me to handle. This Star Martial Skill actually has deeper potential; it’s still in its nascent stage. Pure Yang Attribute Star Martial Warriors are too rare, which is why this Star Martial Skill hasn’t been completed to this day."
"You dare to train an incomplete Star Martial Skill?"
"The completion of Star Martial Skills requires generations of Star Martial Warriors to perfect them. Especially for those of us with rare attributes, cultivating Star Martial Skills is arduous... However, there’s one advantage we have that you don’t: it’s cheap. After I awakened my Yang Attribute, the Star Martial Hall even proactively contacted me to recommend Star Martial Skills."
"Damn, you get that kind of treatment?"
"Can’t be helped. Yin and Yang attributes are even rarer than your Medical Attribute Star Martial Warriors."
"Alright, are you ready? If you’re ready, I’m going to start." Wang Lan pressed a button on the remote, activating the electromagnetic barrier that had never been turned on before.
Fighting with Star Martial Skills meant a completely different level of destructive power. It was like upgrading from cold weapons to firearms—and not just entry-level firearms; it was like jumping straight to using things like grenades and the Thunder Rocket Launcher.
"Wang Lan, Xie Sisi has arrived."
"Let her come over."
"Wait? Xie Sisi is coming too?" Xu Xiangwen asked curiously.
"Yeah, Xie Sisi wanted to come, so I called you," Wang Lan said casually.
"Hold on! Wang Lan, I’m having a little trouble understanding your logic. Xie Sisi wants to see you, so you invited me over to spar?"
"Ah? Training one person is training; training two is also training. Besides, the New Year holiday is over, right? You guys must have packed on some pounds. It’s a good time to train a bit before school starts, help with digestion."
So you’re really sure Xie Sisi is here to spar with you and not because she’s thinking of sleeping with you? Lanzi, you take playing dumb to a whole new level,
Xu Xiangwen silently thought, giving Wang Lan an appraising look.
Xu Xiangwen was right; Wang Lan was indeed feigning ignorance.
The last time he saved Xie Sisi, the "other" Xie Sisi had clearly told Wang Lan that Xie Sisi liked him. Since Wang Lan knew this, combined with all of Xie Sisi’s actions, he could certainly understand her intentions.
But dating and all that... what a hassle. Mentally, I have no need for romance. Physiologically, I haven’t reached that stage yet either. Considering my ideals and the current situation, the Demon Clan is stirring, and a great war is imminent. At such a critical juncture, shouldn’t I seize every opportunity to become stronger? Who has the mood for dating?
DING DONG—
The elevator opened, and a peerless beauty, as if she had stepped out of a painting, appeared.
