Xie Sisi had an excellent figure, nearly 1.8 meters tall, with legs that seemed to go on for over a meter. A perfect golden ratio physique, paired with a delicate face. Even a little makeup could make passersby walk into lampposts.
Today, Xie Sisi wore a mink coat over a tight, hip-hugging miniskirt, her shapely, straight legs swaying enticingly enough to make one drool. She had also meticulously applied her makeup before leaving home. The moment she stepped out of the elevator, she captured the gazes of the three male creatures present.
"Sisi’s here?" Wang Lan waved enthusiastically.
Xie Sisi looked at the scene before her, a slight surprise on her face. But in an instant, a smile bloomed. "You’re all here? Why didn’t Wang Lan tell me?"
"He didn’t tell us you were coming either," Gong Feiyu said with a faint smile, gesturing for Xie Sisi to sit on a nearby lounge chair. "You look beautiful today."
"Thank you!"
"You’ve come at just the right time. These two are planning to spar using Star Martial Skills. We can learn about practical combat together."
"Oh, good! If Wang Lan had told me you were training, I would have worn sportswear."
"Alright, let’s not dawdle. Let’s begin," Wang Lan said.
"Be careful!" Xu Xiangwen’s smile vanished, his expression becoming incredibly serious.
In an instant, Star Energy Fluctuation surged around him, the immense Star Power visible to the naked eye. His aura erupted like a hurricane, the airflow rushing outwards, giving Wang Lan the sensation of a hot summer wind.
Instantly, Xu Xiangwen moved. He still relied on physical strength, but his speed was almost too fast for Wang Lan’s eyes to follow. In less than a second, he was in front of Wang Lan, throwing a punch at his face.
BOOM—
The ground trembled.
Wang Lan’s figure shattered into an afterimage as he activated Star Cloud Sword Dance.
The two, having distanced themselves again, didn’t move. That brief exchange was for them to size each other up, to get a baseline. Xu Xiangwen was afraid Wang Lan might underestimate him and accidentally get killed, while Wang Lan wanted to gauge Xu Xiangwen’s strength at the Star Cloud Stage.
"Well? Are you confident?" Xu Xiangwen asked, a faint smile playing on his lips.
Wang Lan’s expression was very serious.
To be honest, no confidence!
Before breaking through to the Star Cloud Stage, Wang Lan could easily defeat Xu Xiangwen, with or without Star Martial Skills. However, the gap between the Star Cloud Stage and the Star Shine Stage was far more than just a difference in Star Power.
A Star Cloud Stage Star Martial Warrior surpassed a Star Shine Stage warrior in terms of physical strength, power, and nerve response speed. Coupled with Xu Xiangwen mastering a high-level Star Martial Skill, his strength hadn’t just surpassed Wang Lan’s—it had reached a point where it could potentially crush him.
In other words, if the current Xu Xiangwen were on the Star Martial Tournament stage, he could effortlessly steamroll his way to the finals. Even against Chang Shuangyue, who had once thoroughly suppressed Wang Lan, Xu Xiangwen could now easily win.
This was the brutal dominance of a higher realm.
With Wang Lan’s current Star Power, he had no chance of winning against any Star Cloud Stage opponent unless he used his wits.
That punch also made Wang Lan discard any underestimation. Xu Xiangwen had held back. If he hadn’t, Wang Lan might not have been able to dodge in time.
So, Xu Xiangwen’s question wasn’t arrogant; he was genuinely worried if Wang Lan could handle it. If he couldn’t, Gong Feiyu would have to step in. But Gong Feiyu wasn’t suitable either. As an Earth Attribute Star Martial Warrior, he couldn’t use his Earth Attribute Star Martial Skills on the platform. If he had to draw earth elements from the surroundings, Wang Lan’s office building, worth several hundred million, would be demolished.
"I’m okay, don’t worry. I have a Self-Healing Star Martial Skill, so even if I can’t take it, I can heal. Besides, this is better; it will enhance my practical combat abilities more effectively."Follow current novels on
"Alright then, I won’t hold back next time."
"Begin!"
Nearby, Xie Sisi quietly raised her phone.
"What are you doing?" Gong Feiyu asked curiously as Xie Sisi opened her camera app.
"They’re having a practical combat session using Star Martial Skills. How can I not tell Xinyu? I’ll record it for her to see."
Xu Xiangwen once again transformed into a streak of light, shooting towards Wang Lan with a speed that made Wang Lan’s nerves tighten.
Executing Star Cloud Sword Dance again, Wang Lan narrowly avoided Xu Xiangwen’s fist. But before the afterimage could even dissipate, Xu Xiangwen’s next punch followed closely. Fortunately, Wang Lan’s Star Cloud Sword Dance had reached a profound level, the afterimages he created so realistic they could fool the eye. Because Xu Xiangwen repeatedly attacked mere afterimages, Wang Lan found space to evade.
But as it stood, Wang Lan was simply being chased and beaten by Xu Xiangwen. Forget about counterattacking; if he was too slow, he’d get a fist to the face.
"Lanzi, watch out...!"
Xu Xiangwen let out a strange cry and instantly created two Physical Clones. The problem was, these were tangible clones, and both could use Pure Yang Skill.
"Damn it, that’s just shameless!" Wang Lan’s face paled as he roared.
"This is a real fight, who cares about being shameless? Don’t run! I won’t be satisfied until I’ve hammered you today!"

chapters.title: Chapter 156 Dynamic Vision
chapters.content:
Chapter 156: Chapter 156 Dynamic Vision
Xu Xiangwen had already held back considerably. To put it in perspective, when he was in the intermediate trial grounds, the power of a single punch from him was equivalent to a grenade explosion.
Back then, Xu Xiangwen was only at the Star Shine Stage. That Star Martial Skill application technique must have been an initial application method of the Pure Yang Skill. Now that he had mastered using Star Martial Skills with his entire body, the power of this punch, enough to create a crater, was certainly stronger.
If he had used that move on Wang Lan, Wang Lan would have been mangled, even with Self Healing.
Xu Xiangwen was only using his speed to overwhelm Wang Lan; the slaps he threw weren’t actually that powerful.
But even so, with Xu Xiangwen’s speed advantage, Wang Lan could only endure the onslaught.
He was simply too fast.
Wang Lan could still keep up with the speed of a typical Star Cloud Stage warrior, but Xu Xiangwen’s Star Martial Skill amplified his strength, speed, and reflexes severalfold. Against this velocity, even if Wang Lan were at the Star Cloud Stage himself, he would need restrictive Star Martial Skills to limit Xu Xiangwen’s high-speed movement.
Wang Lan’s evasions with Star Cloud Sword Dance were barely holding up; a counterattack was out of the question. His Flame Sword, despite its cutting power, was useless if it couldn’t connect. A Flame Sword that missed was no different from having no sword at all.
No wonder it’s said that in martial arts, speed reigns supreme; nothing is truly unbreakable if it can’t overcome sheer speed. At this velocity, even a late-stage Star Cloud Stage expert would be pummeled if Xu Xiangwen got close.
Xie Sisi recorded a video and sent it to Jiang Xinyu via her QQ ID.
At that moment, Jiang Xinyu was in the basement Training Room, viciously training Jiang Xinchen.
Jiang Xinchen was obedient and somewhat timid by nature, a fact Jiang Xinyu had lamented more than once.
He managed to inherit his older sister’s good looks and grace, so why hadn’t he picked up any of her ruthlessness?
It was one thing to lack talent, but to also lack ferocity...
But then again, he was a Water Attribute Star Martial Warrior. What could one expect? That was just the temperament that came with the Water Attribute.
"Take a rest," Jiang Xinyu said, looking down from her superior position at Jiang Xinchen, who lay drenched in sweat on the training platform. A hint of pity touched her voice.
"Sis... I’m fine. I can... keep going..."
"Your problem isn’t perseverance, it’s hesitation! Your attacks lack decisiveness. If you can’t defeat an enemy in one strike, your moves are meaningless."
DING-DONG!
Jiang Xinyu casually picked up her phone. It was a video message from Xie Sisi.
She casually clicked it open. Instantly, Jiang Xinyu’s body stiffened. The video showed two figures rapidly exchanging blows inside a transparent electromagnetic shield.
They’ve even activated the electromagnetic shield? That means they’re using Star Martial Skills!
"You continue training here. I need to step out for a bit."
"Huh?"
"No slacking off just because I’m not supervising. I’ll check your progress when I get back."
"Okay!"
Jiang Xinyu hurried back to the villa, took a quick shower, changed into clean combat gear, and rushed to the garage.
Speaking of which, Jiang Xinyu had envied Wang Lan’s family for their electromagnetic shield for more than a day. Star Martial Skills couldn’t be used recklessly. Without specialized equipment or a protective barrier set up by a Star Martial Warrior, one had to bear all consequences themselves.
If public facilities were damaged or people injured, then just you wait. Charges of endangering public safety and social security would be laid against you. To put it bluntly, it meant humanity would eliminate you.
Therefore, electromagnetic barriers had become something Star Martial Warriors desperately needed. With one, they could practice Star Martial Skills at home, even experiment with them boldly and without restraint.
But this device wasn’t something money alone could buy; the technology was still under national protection regulations and not available for civilian use.
Jiang Xinyu had never quite accepted that Wang Lan’s family had one. But that was before.
Two Xu Xiangwens, both fully employing the Pure Yang Skill! They’ve instantly pushed Wang Lan into a desperate situation!
Good heavens, four slaps, back and forth! If it weren’t for Wang Lan’s quick movement technique, using his arms to block several times, his face would have been beaten into a swollen mess by now.
Xu Xiangwen, however, was growing increasingly energized. Though he verbally cautioned Wang Lan to be careful, the excited glint in his eyes thoroughly betrayed his words.
This guy is having the time of his life!
After narrowly dodging two powerful slaps, Wang Lan rolled repeatedly, retreating to a corner of the arena.
Is this the real gap between me and the Star Cloud Stage? I’m completely outmatched in terms of strength,
Wang Lan thought. Xu Xiangwen gave him a few seconds to adjust before a sinister smile spread across his face again.
"Lanzi, Big Brother is coming for you!" Xu Xiangwen taunted.
Calling himself ’Big Brother’ now? Damn it, I can’t let him get away with this cockiness!
But Xu Xiangwen moved like lightning. Almost as soon as the words left his mouth, a slap descended from overhead.
Should I shoot him with an arrow? But what if I kill him...?
In that split second, a realization struck Wang Lan.
Am I being pummeled solely because I can’t keep up with his speed? Not entirely. If that were the case, I wouldn’t be able to block any of his attacks. It’s my eyes that can’t keep up, and that’s slowing down my body’s reactions. That’s the real issue! In the future, I’ll definitely face opponents with incredible speed and movement techniques. Xu Xiangwen might be holding back, but my enemies won’t. Didn’t I just master a new ability? The Crescent Arrow’s auxiliary skill, Hawk Eye! This skill is a high-level application of Star Power, derived from the unique way Star Power moves through the Crescent Arrow’s meridians. It alters retinal imaging through Star Power. And I can use it independently!
In an instant, a surge of Star Power flooded Wang Lan’s right eye, enveloping it in a golden glow. His right pupil transformed, shifting from its normal round shape into that of an intricate gear.
The slap descending towards his head finally appeared to slow down.
Moreover, he could even adjust the degree of this slowdown. At the very least, he could make Xu Xiangwen’s movements appear to be at a normal, manageable speed, as if it took no effort at all.
Wang Lan shifted his body to the side. However, this usually simple action now felt like moving through thick mud; in his enhanced dynamic vision, his own body’s movements seemed snail-paced.
Fortunately, with quick, subtle adjustments, Wang Lan managed to narrowly dodge Xu Xiangwen’s sweeping palm, the attack missing him by mere fingertips.
Wang Lan quickly executed the Star Cloud Sword Dance, transforming into a streak of light that flashed past Xu Xiangwen, reappearing behind him.
After that palm strike missed, Xu Xiangwen suddenly froze.
"What’s wrong?" Xie Sisi, who had been thoroughly enjoying the spectacle, looked up and asked.
"Strange... Wang Lan, your dodge just now... it felt very odd. What did you do?"
"Nothing much. Just that I can track your speed now."
"Hah! Anyone can brag," Xu Xiangwen scoffed.
Track my speed? Let me tell you, when I unleash my full speed, even I can’t track it!
Once more, the two Xu Xiangwens lunged at Wang Lan.
With dynamic vision activated, not only did his opponent’s movements appear slower, but his own movements also felt sluggish in comparison. Wang Lan needed to adjust and adapt to this new perception.
Initially, Wang Lan’s evasions were indeed hair-raisingly close. But after a few minutes of acclimatization, he began to get the hang of it.
Meanwhile, Gong Feiyu and Xie Sisi, watching from the sidelines, wore expressions of utter astonishment.
The image of Wang Lan being relentlessly chased and beaten by Xu Xiangwen was still vivid in their minds. His pathetic predicament had been quite amusing to them. Yet, in just a few short minutes, they were witnessing Wang Lan’s transformation.
From desperately scrambling for safety to his current calm composure—all within about ten minutes—the change, while not glaringly obvious, was unmistakably unfolding before their eyes.
Gong Feiyu, in particular, was shocked beyond words.
Just two days ago, he and Xu Xiangwen had sparred in an open area. At a distance, Xu Xiangwen was no match for Gong Feiyu. But once Xu Xiangwen closed in, his terrifying speed left Gong Feiyu utterly defenseless.
Gong Feiyu’s close-combat abilities weren’t weak; he had previously managed to hold his own against Wang Lan for a good three minutes. And after breaking through to the Star Cloud Stage, his strength had improved significantly.
Even so, if Xu Xiangwen got close, it meant instant defeat for him.
But now, Wang Lan is actually turning the tables in such a short period? This seemingly small change implies a terrifying rate of progress!
Ten-odd minutes... how much can a person improve in that time? Previously, Gong Feiyu would have thought that ten-odd minutes weren’t enough for any significant improvement. Now... damn, what kind of monster is this guy in front of me?
BOOM—
Suddenly, one of the Xu Xiangwens was sent flying backward, spinning a full 360 degrees in mid-air before crashing heavily to the ground.The source of thɪs content is No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
POP!
After a moment of distortion, Xu Xiangwen’s clone vanished into thin air.
This scene left the two onlookers gaping even wider in astonishment.
"Impossible! You..." The remaining Xu Xiangwen stared at Wang Lan, his face etched with shock.
Wang Lan was also momentarily stunned—not because he’d defeated Xu Xiangwen’s clone, but because the system hadn’t registered it as a victory, and he hadn’t received any rewards.
It seems I have to defeat the main body as well for it to count.
With this thought, Wang Lan’s figure flashed, and he instantly charged towards Xu Xiangwen.
"Wait—"
"Wait for what!"
Wang Lan’s fist thundered down, but Xu Xiangwen easily dodged it.
Wang Lan had only enhanced his dynamic vision, not his actual speed. Thus, it wasn’t difficult for Xu Xiangwen, with his superior speed, to evade Wang Lan’s punch.
However, Xu Xiangwen wasn’t like Wang Lan; he couldn’t use Star Martial Skills without a cooldown period.
So, dream on if you think you’re creating another clone!
Wang Lan began to press his attack against Xu Xiangwen. Inside the arena, their movements were still dizzyingly fast, a blur to the eye.
Xie Sisi, watching from outside the barrier, began to discern what was happening.
Xie Sisi herself possessed formidable combat prowess, especially when integrating Star Power into her movements for enhanced speed and attack power. But even her abilities were no match for Xu Xiangwen when his Pure Yang Skill was active.
Xie Sisi realized that Wang Lan hadn’t actually become faster or stronger; rather, he could now anticipate Xu Xiangwen’s moves.
Xu Xiangwen’s actions are all within Wang Lan’s grasp. He can instantly react to Xu Xiangwen’s movements to counter and launch his own attacks. Even though his own speed hasn’t increased, his combat efficiency has effectively doubled!
THUMP, THUMP, THUMP—
Rapid footsteps announced Jiang Xinyu’s hurried arrival. She got there just in time to see the climax of the fight: Wang Lan executed a Thomas flare kick that struck Xu Xiangwen’s waist with pinpoint accuracy, almost as if guided by GPS.
The force of the kick, combined with Xu Xiangwen’s own forward momentum, sent Xu Xiangwen flying backward.
BOOM! A shockwave of energy erupted.
Xu Xiangwen’s face twisted grotesquely as he slammed hard against the protective barrier.
A notification chimed in Wang Lan’s mind: "Defeated an opponent of a higher level. Reward: 1,000 experience points, 10 skill points."
Huh? That counts as defeating a higher-level opponent? Right, Xu Xiangwen is no longer the Star Shine Stage cultivator who could only offer a few skill points. As a Star Cloud Stage expert, he could completely overwhelm me.
"Damn it... Lanzi, what the hell happened to you? Did you, like, evolve or something?" Xu Xiangwen exclaimed, getting right back up as if the powerful kick had done nothing to him.
"You’re not hurt?" Wang Lan asked, surprised.
"With the Pure Yang Skill active, my strength, defense, and everything else are boosted several times over. The force of your kick was... barely adequate," Xu Xiangwen said. "Now, spill it. How did you do that? I felt like... like I’ve been shadowboxing this whole time!"

chapters.title: Chapter 157: Promoted
chapters.content:
Chapter 157: Chapter 157: Promoted
"This is a new Star Martial Skill I’ve learned. Look at my eyes." Wang Lan opened his eyes, revealing a faint layer of golden light within them. This golden light was very subtle, but definitely visible upon close inspection.
"A Pupil Skill-type Star Martial Skill?"
"No, but it grants dynamic vision and farsightedness."
"Impressive!" Xu Xiangwen said, his voice deep.
"Again!"
"Again?"
"This time, I’ll let you create two clones... Huh? Xinyu, you’re here too?" Only then did Wang Lan notice Jiang Xinyu’s arrival.
"You’re sparring and didn’t call me?" Jiang Xinyu said with a smile, her eyes unintentionally sweeping over Xie Sisi. With her intelligence, Jiang Xinyu immediately deduced that Xie Sisi’s attire today definitely wasn’t for sparring.
But she knew better than to point it out. Instead, she immediately looked at Wang Lan. "Keep going."
Once again, Wang Lan struggled to defeat Xu Xiangwen, who had created two clones. Frustrated, Xu Xiangwen threw his hat to the ground, refusing to continue. He was at the Star Cloud Stage but still couldn’t beat Wang Lan!
However, Wang Lan knew Xu Xiangwen had lost because he’d held back on his damage output. If Xu Xiangwen had utilized his full speed and attack power, Wang Lan wouldn’t have stood a chance.
But dynamic vision was an ability tied to Crescent Arrow. Once he used it, Wang Lan’s offensive capabilities were reduced to only his Basic Skills. His only significant damage-dealing attack was the Inch Strength Fist.
This sparring session made Wang Lan fully realize the true gap between himself and the Star Cloud Stage. How long had it been since Xu Xiangwen broke through to the Star Cloud Stage? His strength was definitely on the weaker side for that level.
And if even a weaker Star Cloud Stage cultivator could exert such overwhelming pressure on him, Wang Lan realized he had been far too optimistic about the provincial martial arts competition a few months away. In a real arena, no one would hold back. Not being able to use two Star Martial Skills simultaneously was a fatal restriction for him.
After a break, Xu Xiangwen and Jiang Xinyu sparred again. Inside the electromagnetic barrier, Jiang Xinyu completely unleashed her power. At that moment, Wang Lan truly understood that the gap between him and Jiang Xinyu was still an invisible chasm.
Xu Xiangwen was practically pinned to the ground and thrashed by Jiang Xinyu. His Exploding Fist couldn’t break her Ice Armor; Jiang Xinyu could have just stood still and tired him to death. Combined with her Ice Snow Roar and chilling speed reduction, Xu Xiangwen had no fight left in him.
Today had perhaps been a fulfilling day for Wang Lan, a day of getting pummeled for Xu Xiangwen, and a day of venting for Jiang Xinyu. But for Xie Sisi, it was a day of frustration.
Xie Sisi had originally hoped to spend time alone with Wang Lan. Even if they did nothing but sit on the balcony, drink tea, and bask in the sun, that would have been fine. Instead, she had ended up watching the three of them spar all day.
"School is about to start. Wang Lan, how far is your Star Power from reaching the Star Cloud Stage?" After the sparring ended, as the four of them prepared to leave, Jiang Xinyu asked Wang Lan.
"I’ve only just reached the late phase of the Star Shine Stage. The Star Cloud Stage is still a long way off. It’s unlikely I’ll reach it before graduation."
Unless I get a few more chances to catch spies from the Demon Clan.
Wang Lan didn’t voice this thought, because even he found it unlikely. After the recent operations, the Demon Clan’s spy network in Suzhou City must have suffered a heavy blow.
Even the production lab for the Demonic Transformation Potion had been discovered by the Tianjian Bureau. They likely wouldn’t dare to cause trouble for a while.
"Without reaching the Star Cloud Stage, your chances at the provincial martial arts competition are slim. If advancing seems hopeless, just focus on showcasing your potential. As long as your potential is great, there’s still hope."
"You have so little faith in me?" Wang Lan said playfully. "What if I actually win the championship?"
"Then you’ll have to work hard. Good luck! Sisi, get in the car. Shall we go shopping tonight?"
"Huh? You’ve been sparring all day, aren’t you tired?"
"Sisi, as a woman, you should understand. For women, going shopping can make us feel fully energized again, no matter how tired we are."
"I... I rarely go shopping... so I wouldn’t know. Wang Lan, I’m leaving then?"
"Alright. Be safe on your way."The source of thɪs content is NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
After the three cars had driven away, Wang Lan sat down on a bench, feeling somewhat dejected. Today, Xu Xiangwen had only yielded fifty skill points. *Sigh*... Sparring all day long wasn’t easy.
Maybe it’s really time to buy some Soul Beads? I only need one hundred and fifty more now.
BEEP—BEEP—
His phone rang suddenly. Looking at the caller ID, it was Lige.
"Hello?"
"Are you home?"
"Yes!"
"I’m on my way to your place."
"Huh? What for? Is it a mission... Hello? Hello?"
The caller hung up right after speaking.
What a temper,
Wang Lan thought.
No wonder she has no friends.
He went back to his room and took a shower.
Just as he had changed his clothes and was drying his hair, Xiao Ai informed Wang Lan that Lige had arrived.
He activated the elevator, and Lige walked in holding a stack of clothes.
She handed the clothes to Wang Lan. "Put these on. We’re going back to the bureau."
"A red uniform? Have I been promoted again?" Wang Lan asked instinctively.
"Yes!"
"Why are you the one picking me up?" Only then did Wang Lan notice Lige was also wearing a red uniform. "You got promoted too?"
"Thanks to you. Not only was my disciplinary action lifted, but I also got promoted. And it’s not just the two of us."
"Who else?"
"Xu Shiyun."
"Isn’t he in Hainan?"
"Even if he were at the ends of the earth, he’d have to rush back."
"Oh, please wait a moment; I’ll go change." Wang Lan hugged the clothes and dashed into his room, kicking the door shut joyfully.
From the moment Lige had entered, her face had been stern. It was only when she saw Wang Lan happily kicking the door shut like an eager rabbit that a smile she herself found surprising touched her lips.
Her coldness to others was merely a disguise. She couldn’t stand men approaching, nor could she handle women getting too close. Thus, she resorted to projecting a ’stay away’ aura to repel anyone who tried to approach her.
But in front of Wang Lan, who knew her true identity, she could briefly lower her guard.
Picking up Wang Lan this time wasn’t actually her duty. But... at that moment, she had inexplicably wanted to see him, to share their mutual joy.
She had arrived, still wearing her metaphorical mask. Only when Wang Lan closed his door did her heart feel incredibly relieved, and a radiant, sweet smile blossomed on her face.
Right now, Wang Lan felt like bouncing on his bed and belting out a song.
This was exactly what he needed! The promotion itself wasn’t that important—lieutenant, captain, whatever—it didn’t matter. But skill points were tangible. The system feature that allowed linking Star Martial Skills had been nagging at him, an itch he desperately wanted to scratch.
He had originally thought he’d have to wait until the school term started to accumulate over a hundred skill points. He had even considered being utterly shameless: setting up a fighting ring on the playground and challenging the entire Star Martial Arts Campus.
Bullying first and second-years would do just fine. As long as skill points were coming in, anything was negotiable.
But surprises have a way of showing up when you least expect them.
He quickly changed his clothes and, striking a pose in front of the mirror, gave his hair a suave sweep.
"Wang Lan, how can you be so handsome?" he mused to his reflection.
PFFT—
Outside the door, Lige, who had just taken a sip of black tea, instantly spewed it out.
The door to his room opened, revealing Lige covering her mouth, trying hard to suppress a cough.
"What’s wrong?"
"At home... are you always this narcissistic?"
"No!" Wang Lan shook his head. "I’m merely making a professional and precise statement about an objective fact."
"Let’s go."
"Are we having a celebratory banquet?"
"No, it’s just a rank conferral ceremony for the three of us in the Director’s office."
He got into Lige’s car. The vehicle sped quickly and smoothly along the brightly lit overpass.
The car seemed to be Lige’s personal vehicle. Its interior was simple but high-end, and despite the speed, there wasn’t the slightest bit of turbulence.
It was too quiet. Wang Lan, unaccustomed to the silence, made a slightly awkward attempt at small talk. "Nice car."
"It’s alright."
"Why no music? Driving without music is soulless."
"I don’t like playing music when there’s someone in the back. The sound could mask noises from behind, and if an emergency arose, I wouldn’t be able to react immediately."
"Lige, you’ll have a hard time making friends like that," Wang Lan sighed.
"Hello, system—play some music."
"Huh? Why did you turn it on again?"
"I just realized... I think I can have one friend now."
Leaning against the backrest, Wang Lan suddenly smiled.
The car slowly stopped. Wang Lan pushed the door open, his breath forming a white puff in the cold air illuminated by the lights. He buttoned his collar tighter and smoothed the creases on his uniform.
Although the New Year had passed, the temperature was still minus two degrees Celsius. That was relatively mild; southern cities rarely dropped much further below freezing. However, it was said that temperatures in the coldest northern cities had plunged below minus fifty degrees Celsius today.
As soon as he entered the main building’s lobby, he saw a figure in the hallway, arms crossed, shivering violently. The frequency of his tremors made it look as if he were being electrified.
"Yo, Xu? What’s wrong with you?"
"Wang Lan, quick, pass me some Star Power! I’m freezing to death..."
"Wait, are you just wearing a vest under that military uniform? Xu, it’s minus two degrees Celsius out here, and you dare to dress like that? Man, if there’s anyone I admire, it’s you."
"Don’t even mention it... I was in Hainan eating barbecue just three hours ago. Director Wang called and told me to rush back immediately. Xiaoyao picked me up as soon as I got off the plane. That bastard just dropped me here and didn’t even leave me a coat!"
Seeing Xu Shiyun looking truly miserable, Wang Lan tried to pass a stream of Star Power to him. Unfortunately, Xu Shiyun’s own Star Power instinctively rejected it. Since the Star Power couldn’t be conducted, it couldn’t warm him up.
"Sorry, Xu. I want to help, but I can’t."
Who knew this guy was so brazen? He immediately opened his arms and hugged Wang Lan tightly. Wang Lan himself had a fire-attribute Star Power, and its circulation made him like a personal hot water bottle.
"Xu! What are you doing? Let go! If you don’t let go, I’ll scream!"
"Go ahead and scream. Even if you scream your lungs out, no one will care!" Xu Shiyun laughed heartily, hugging Wang Lan and eliciting a groan from him that almost made Wang Lan resort to a Star Martial Skill.
"Ahem."
From around the corner of the hallway, Lige and Wang Qianfeng approached.
Wang Lan clearly felt Xu Shiyun’s body stiffen. He looked up and saw the strange, disdainful looks in Wang Qianfeng’s and Lige’s eyes, and he wanted the ground to swallow him whole.
"It’s not like that, Director Wang! I was just messing around with Wang Lan... It’s not what you think!"
"Stop fooling around! Don’t make a spectacle of yourselves in front of Director Zhang later."
"Yes, sir!"
TAP-TAP-TAP.
The sound of footsteps approached. A woman in a red uniform strode confidently towards them and saluted Director Wang crisply.
"Director Wang, I’ve been ordered to escort these three to Director Zhang’s office."
"Alright."
"Xu Shiyun, Lige, Wang Lan, please follow me."

chapters.title: Chapter 158: Day Medal
chapters.content:
Chapter 158: Chapter 158: Day Medal
In Lu Zhao’s office, Lu Zhao was not alone; Zhang Shaoyu, the head of the Jin City headquarters and the Director of Jiang Province, was also present.
When Wang Lan and the other two entered the Director’s office, they immediately lined up and stood at attention.
"Suzhou City Tianjian Bureau, Intelligence Action Team Captain, Xu Shiyun, reporting to the Commanding Officer!"
"Suzhou City Tianjian Bureau, Action Department Squadron Leader, Lige, reporting to the Commanding Officer!"
"Suzhou City Tianjian Bureau, Intelligence... Wang Lan, reporting to the Commanding Officer!"
A light chuckle sounded. Upon hearing Wang Lan’s report, the middle-aged man opposite Lu Zhao looked over with a teasing smile. From that smile alone, Wang Lan instantly felt as if he were being eyed by a crafty old fox.
Wang Lan had heard Zhang Shaoyu’s name more than once. He was the Director of the Jin City Tianjian Bureau and also the Director of the entire Jiang Province Tianjian Bureau headquarters. He was not yet fifty years old.
Zhang Shaoyu possessed peak Star Sea strength and was one of Jade Country’s hundred titled Star Martial Warrior masters. His title was "Fierce Fox"—the "fox" not referring to an ordinary fox, but to a nine-tailed demon fox.
If Wang Lan were to search online at that moment, he would find many legends about Zhang Shaoyu. He had risen to fame as a young prodigy before the age of twenty, became more composed after thirty, and broke through to the Star Sea realm. More than a decade had passed since then.
"Is everyone here?" Zhang Shaoyu asked, standing up with a smile.
"Director, everyone is present," Lu Zhao replied.
Zhang Shaoyu reached out and opened the first box. He took out a pair of Senior Captain’s epaulets and slowly approached Xu Shiyun.
"Xu Shiyun, I know you. You were once a soldier in my Southeast Military Region Star Martial Army. You already held the rank of Captain at twenty-six. Later, you participated in overseas missions, enhanced our country’s prestige, and were awarded two second-class individual merits and twelve third-class individual merits. You completed every mission assigned to you by the motherland, defending the nation’s dignity and honor.
South Wing Country even considered trying to win you over with a royal princess. You didn’t consider it?"
"Reporting to the Commanding Officer! I was born a person of Jade Country, and in death, I shall be a spirit of Jade Country! My sincere heart can be judged by the heavens!"
"Well said." Zhang Shaoyu pinned the epaulets onto Xu Shiyun’s shoulders. "If you had stayed in the military, you would have been a field-grade officer by now."
"Reporting to the Commanding Officer, I only wish to fight on the front lines! When I learned that the Demon Clan was stirring and the Tianjian Bureau had already engaged them, I knew the military was no longer the place for me. Therefore, I joined the Tianjian Bureau."
"HA HA HA! That’s what I like to hear! Our Tianjian Bureau is the true vanguard on humanity’s battlefield! The Special Action Star Martial Army? Special Operations Squads? They’re all eating our dust! Excellent! I look forward to your performance." The two saluted each other solemnly.
Zhang Shaoyu took out another set of epaulets and approached Lige. His eyes fixed on hers. "Lige... I haven’t heard your name before. Tell me, when did you join the Tianjian Bureau?"
"Reporting, March 8th, 2017."
"2017... In less than two years, you’ve risen to Senior Captain... Tell me, how did you manage that?"
"Reporting to the Director! In nineteen months, I completed seventeen A-level missions, fifty-four B-level missions, and neutralized one hundred twenty-seven C-level targets. Record of uncompleted missions... one!"
"Why one? Since you have so few uncompleted missions, why isn’t it zero?"
"Reporting! It was because I underestimated the enemy..."
"Director, this is what happened," Lu Zhao quickly explained to Zhang Shaoyu. "At the time, Lige was ordered to surveil a spy group we had discovered. Half a month into the surveillance, the Demon Clan spies were tipped off and quickly retreated. Lige, who was responsible for the surveillance, immediately attempted to apprehend them.
However, she unexpectedly fell into a trap set by the Demon Clan. The spies self-destructed, leaving Lige severely injured and her entire team, apart from herself, killed in action. Actually, that mission wasn’t technically counted as uncompleted, as the Demon Clan member under surveillance didn’t escape. Furthermore, we later succeeded in dismantling the entire Demon Clan spy network."
"In less than two years, you’ve completed so many missions... Did you take on all the tasks from the Suzhou City Bureau? Everyone in the Tianjian Bureau is an iron-willed warrior, but that’s about willpower, not physical endurance. Even if you are a Gold Attribute Star Martial Warrior, you’re not truly made of iron.
You must take care of your body. Don’t wear yourself down with illness at such a young age. The country needs young people—not just for your present contributions, but for your future as well." Saying this, Zhang Shaoyu personally pinned the Senior Captain’s epaulets onto Lige’s shoulders.
The two saluted once again.
Zhang Shaoyu slowly approached Wang Lan. He looked up slightly, his gaze fixed directly on Wang Lan’s eyes.
"Commanding Officer..." Wang Lan began.
"Ordinarily, your Director Lu could have handled today’s award ceremony. Things are quite busy at the Jin City headquarters. But I rushed over to Suzhou City immediately after my meeting this morning. Do you know why?"
"Reporting, I do not."
"No other reason. I just wanted to come and see you!" Zhang Shaoyu took out the third box. From it, he retrieved a pair of Captain’s epaulets and slowly pinned them onto Wang Lan’s shoulders.
A system notification chimed: "Congratulations to the Host for being promoted to Captain. Reward: 1,000 Skill Points."
That sound in my mind... In that instant, I felt a profound sense of relief, like finally being able to urinate after holding it in for ages. The inability to chain my Star Martial Skills had been a constant, maddening itch—like a mosquito sucking blood from my heart that I couldn’t swat or scratch.
"You’re Wang Lan! Do you realize that because of you, many important figures at the Ministry of Defense didn’t have a peaceful New Year?"
"Reporting, this subordinate expresses his deepest apologies."
"Hmm, no need for deep apologies. We welcome more of such actions from you in the future; the more, the better. Do you know, when you first completely uncovered a Demon Clan spy group, the higher-ups immediately praised you on the spot as a ’young hero, a hero among youths’?
Then, on New Year’s Eve, you exposed human traitors; on New Year’s Day, you uncovered spies; and on the second day of the New Year, you busted a Demonic Transformation Potion production workshop. They were pounding their desks and repeatedly exclaiming, ’Incredible!’"
Wang Lan’s face showed no sign of the proud expression typical of a youth in his situation. Instead, he looked calm, his gaze distant.
Witnessing this, Zhang Shaoyu’s estimation of Wang Lan rose even higher.
Such composure at such a young age. No wonder he can repeatedly inflict heavy losses on the Demon Clan.
In reality, Wang Lan was currently admiring his new epaulets in the system interface.
Captain’s epaulets... those three chevrons look really good. On the system page, all the rank insignias are sparkling.
But then, Zhang Shaoyu took another item from the box: a medal.
When Xu Shiyun and Lige saw this medal, their expressions changed instantly.
Is that... the Glory of the Sun Medal?
they thought in unison.
Even Lu Zhao looked utterly shocked.
Zhang Shaoyu brought the Glory of the Sun Medal! Even I hadn’t anticipated this. I figured a First-Class Merit Medal would be the most he’d get. If any special medal were to be awarded, it should have been the Xuan Yue Medal.
Sun-series medals were the highest military honors bestowed by the Ministry of Defense.
Each Sun-series medal represented an extremely high status of honor. They were only awarded to individuals recognized for making outstanding contributions to human civilization, specifically for military achievements.
For instance, only accomplishments like turning the tide during a critical crisis for human civilization, or deciding the fate of the world in a single battle, qualified one for a Sun-series medal. In the more than two hundred years since Jade Country’s imperial era ended, only eighty-eight Sun-series medals had been awarded, with most of those being in the last one hundred years.Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
Of these, sixty had been awarded posthumously. It was exceedingly rare for someone to receive a Sun-series medal while still alive.
"We always hope for capable individuals to emerge from our ranks, and for our soldiers to continuously achieve great merits, safeguarding the continuation of human civilization. But you, Wang Lan, are the only person I’ve ever seen or heard of whose rate of accumulating merits outpaces the speed of our award ceremonies.
No single accomplishment of yours, taken alone, would be enough to warrant this Glory of the Sun Medal. However, considering the sum of your many contributions, the higher-ups at the Ministry of Defense decided to make an exception and award you this Glory of the Sun Medal.
Do you know when the last Sun-series medal was awarded?"
"This subordinate does not know."
"Eight years ago! The recipient of the Azure Day Medal was your mother, Wang Ling. If your mother were to return, she would be incredibly proud of you." Zhang Shaoyu then pinned the medal onto Wang Lan’s chest.
A system notification chimed: "Congratulations, Host! You have obtained a Rare Medal. This item can be sacrificed!"
The sound came at just that moment.
But Wang Lan’s mind was no longer focused on the system’s prompts. He didn’t even spare a thought for why receiving a medal this time hadn’t granted him any skill points.
"’My mom... is coming back?’" Wang Lan lifted his head, looking at Zhang Shaoyu questioningly.
"Er..." Zhang Shaoyu smiled, patted Wang Lan’s shoulder, but said nothing more.
Instead, he turned to Lu Zhao with a faint smile. "Alright, my business here is concluded. I’ll leave the remaining rewards and commendations to you. I have a meeting tonight, so I’ll be heading back to Jin City now."
"Director, I’ll see you out." Lu Zhao then looked at Xu Shiyun, Lige, and Wang Lan. "The three of you are dismissed."
"Yes, Sir!" The trio saluted in unison, then turned, opened the door, and left.
"Wang Lan... the Glory of the Sun Medal, man!" Xu Shiyun exclaimed excitedly to Wang Lan once they were outside.
At that moment, however, Wang Lan’s head was bowed, his expression somber.
Xu Shiyun continued, puzzled, "’Hey... didn’t you just achieve great merit and receive an incredible honor? Why do you look like you’ve been reprimanded?’"
Lige quickly grabbed Xu Shiyun’s arm and said coolly, "’Wang Lan needs some time alone. Don’t disturb him.’"
"’But...’" Xu Shiyun began.
Wang Lan, seemingly deaf to their conversation, continued walking towards the elevator alone.
Once inside, a plaintive mutter echoed in the empty space, "’Why weren’t there any skill points, though?’"
On the system’s medal page, there were only two medals.
One was the Xuan Yue Medal, displayed in red. The other was the Glory of the Sun Medal, positioned ahead of the Xuan Yue Medal, shimmering a brilliant blue. Furthermore, there was a "1/1" indicator beneath the Glory of the Sun Medal’s icon.
What did that system notification say again? At the time, I was too preoccupied with the implications of Zhang Shaoyu’s words about Mom possibly coming back and didn’t listen carefully.
He focused his spiritual power on the medal. Thankfully, a description appeared.
System Description: "Rare Medal. Sacrificial-type item. By sacrificing this medal, one can transform the illusory into reality. Allows the Host to materialize one illusory item from their memories."
"’Materialize an illusory item from my memories? What in the world is that?’" Wang Lan muttered.
When the elevator reached the ground floor, Wang Lan suddenly realized something.
Wait, I came here in Lige’s car... How am I supposed to get back?
He looked around.
Where are Lige and Xu Shiyun?
Fortunately, it wasn’t too late. Wang Lan walked to the edge of Star Sea Park and then called a Didi.
「By the time he walked through his front door, it was nearly ten o’clock.」
Wang Lan eagerly entered the underground Training Room. He now had 1,800 skill points. Naturally, he decided to immediately implement the Star Martial Skill chaining he’d been wanting.
He immersed himself in the system and, with a slight pang of reluctance at spending them, used the skill points to build a bridge between his Crescent Arrow and Flame Sword skills.
The moment the link between the two skills was established, BOOM! A violent storm of information exploded in Wang Lan’s mind.
BUZZ! Wang Lan felt as if his head had been struck hard with a wooden club. He felt top-heavy and muddled, completely disoriented.
After a long while, Wang Lan’s consciousness finally cleared. In that instant of returning clarity, he finally understood the transformation that had occurred within him during that daze.

chapters.title: Chapter 159: Illusory Exchange for Reality
chapters.content:
Chapter 159: Chapter 159: Illusory Exchange for Reality
The most direct change was in his control over two Star Martial Skills. Wang Lan could clearly feel that while using the Crescent Arrow, he could also use the Flame Sword simultaneously. This meant that Star Martial Skills altering form and those altering nature could now be used concurrently.
The problem that had always troubled Wang Lan was his ability to deal with high-speed, highly agile Star Martial Warriors. His dynamic vision helped him see their movements clearly, allowing him to react in time.Thɪs
But while using dynamic vision, he couldn’t use powerful offensive abilities. Now, however, Wang Lan could easily use the Flame Sword while employing dynamic vision.
If he were to fight Xu Xiangwen again, Wang Lan could easily crush him, even if Xu Xiangwen deployed his Exploding Fist. After all, in terms of lethality, the Exploding Fist was no match for the Flame Sword.
But this wasn’t the true value of linking the skills. The true value lay in the perfect combination of the Flame Sword and the Crescent Arrow. He could condense the Fire Arrow in the same manner the Flame Sword was condensed.
A Fire Arrow?
This was a direct transformation of a form-changing long-range shooting Star Martial Skill into a nature-changing long-range attack.
Hurriedly, Wang Lan set up a target at a distance of one hundred meters. After a moment of thought, he added a layer of steel plate behind the target.
After all this preparation, Wang Lan was about to test its power but still felt uneasy, so he moved the target to an area backed by PS armor. Just in case the steel plate wasn’t enough, he didn’t want to blast a hole in his basement.
With thorough preparations complete, Wang Lan walked to a point one hundred meters away from the target.
He looked at the target ahead of him and took a deep breath.
Suddenly, a surge of Star Power swirled, and his eyes were covered in a layer of gold, making the distant target appear as if it were right before him.
Lifting his finger as if it were a handgun, in an instant, a pair of golden wings sprang from his wrist, and upon them burned red flames.
WHIZZ—
With a piercing sound, an arrow, twice as large as before and wreathed in raging flames, shot forth.
BOOM—
The target stood firm, and the steel plate behind it also remained in place. The explosion, however, had struck the PS armor positioned further back.
"BEEP BEEP BEEP—Energy level: 50."
"Damn it!" Wang Lan cursed on the spot.
Before, Wang Lan’s Crescent Arrow, even at silver rank nine, had only reached ten energy points. Ten energy points were roughly equivalent to the damage a Python Sniper Rifle could inflict on a target within five hundred meters.
That was a heavy sniper rifle, the type used against armored vehicles.
If this arrow were to hit a Star Martial Warrior of the Galaxy Stage, it would undoubtedly be fatal, even if it didn’t strike a vital spot. But now, its power had quintupled, practically reaching the level of a Nautical Artillery Machine Gun.
Eagerly, Wang Lan went to check the target. Upon seeing the results, he inhaled sharply once more.
The target stood firm, and so did the steel plate behind it. It wasn’t that the arrow had skirted around the target; instead, the target had been pierced cleanly through with minimal resistance.
There was a thumb-sized penetration hole through the center of the target, a perfect bullseye. On the steel plate behind it, there was a wrist-sized penetration hole. This hole wasn’t formed by the arrow piercing through, but rather scorched into existence by the high-temperature flames enveloping the arrow.
Around the hole, there were clear signs of molten metal.
Such terrifying power from the Fire Arrow?
And this was just with Wang Lan using the red flames. What terrifying level would its power reach if he used the Purple Flame Arrow? The thought alone excited him.
This was a true composite Star Martial Skill, worthy of being something only a warrior at the Galaxy Stage would dare to attempt. No wonder it was said that Galaxy Stage Star Martial Warriors represented the pinnacle of human cultivators; the power of composite Star Martial Skills was amplified several-fold.
His excitement didn’t last long. Wang Lan was not one to stay overly thrilled for extended periods. He quickly regained his composure. After all, there was still a special sacrificial item in his system awaiting his study.
Even now, Wang Lan was still unclear about the meaning of ’fantasy replacing reality.’
His mind immersed in the system, he opened the badge page.
The badge, emitting a blue light, teased Wang Lan like a coquettish woman.
Concentrating his spiritual power on the badge, suddenly, a dialog box popped up.
"Do you want to spend five hundred skill points to make an offering?"
"Damn! It even requires skill points? The system didn’t even give me my badge skill point reward, and now it’s asking for mine?"
Looking at the system, which still had eight hundred skill points remaining, Wang Lan gritted his teeth.
I should have known you were a skinflint system; I should have been prepared. Fine, you win.
He allocated the skill points, and it activated instantly.
Suddenly, the badge in the system erupted with a fireworks-like screen of light, and in an instant, a golden carousel appeared before Wang Lan’s eyes.
This looks familiar.
Before I transmigrated, I saw a carousel like this when I died accidentally... Am I going to die again? Is the system trying to kill me?
The carousel spun rapidly, and many of the scenes inside were from movies, TV shows, and cartoons Wang Lan had seen in his previous life.
At this moment, Wang Lan suddenly understood: fantasy exchanged for reality, transforming the fantasies from his memories into tangible existence. If that was truly the case, what an utterly messed-up power this was!
Is this Havoc in Heaven? Should I summon the Monkey King? If the Monkey King arrived, all members of the Demon Clan would be annihilated like mere monsters. Of course, he might also destroy all the cars and skyscrapers on the streets, mistaking them for monsters too.
The Havoc in Heaven scene passed.
The images flipped rapidly again. Resident Evil? Damn it, go away! If Resident Evil became real, humanity wouldn’t even need the Demon Clan to act; we’d self-destruct.
Alien spaceships down there? Not bad, huh? Technology hundreds of years ahead of Sky Blue Star... But the next scene—damn it, is that an Alien? Crap, what kind of messed-up movies did I used to watch?
The scenes kept flipping rapidly, one after another, so startling that many of them could spell the end of human civilization the moment they appeared.
DING—
"Item matching the host’s needs has been found. Would you like to exchange?"
The image froze on a classic anime from his childhood, Saint Seiya.
"What happens if I don’t exchange?"
"This item exchange will be nullified, and the opportunity shall not be returned," the system, for once, responded to Wang Lan—not verbally, but with a text card.
"Then, how do you know my needs?"
The text card read: "The exchange object will only be beneficial to the host, but its actual utility depends entirely on the host’s luck."
"Alright! Exchange."
DING—
The carousel in front of Wang Lan suddenly burst open, and he vaguely saw a cyan-green box. Before Wang Lan had a chance to look closely, the cyan-green box suddenly transformed into a streak of light. Afterwards, his vision returned to the scene in the underground training room.
"Where’s the stuff? The box?" Wang Lan looked around, shouting loudly, only to find nothing.
Only then did Wang Lan feel something in his palm. A square tag, cyan-green in color, made of an unknown material.
Searching his memory, the image that came to mind was from the GG anime from Japan in his previous life, Saint Seiya, where it seemed the Five Little Powerhouses’ Saint Cloths were no longer the big boxes carried on their backs, but had become handy tags.
Looking at the pattern on the tag—a crudely drawn phoenix—could it be the Phoenix Constellation Saint Cloth? Does it have to be this cliché?
Wang Lan tried to flick the tag gently. It tumbled through the air. DING-DONG—
With a crisp sound, the tag landed on the ground.
In an instant, the tag lit up, and a white magic array instantly unfolded with the tag at its center. From within the array, a loud phoenix cry was heard, and a phoenix reflecting a metallic luster slowly rose from it.
It really is the Phoenix Constellation Saint Cloth!
Wang Lan examined the Saint Cloth. Just then, it burst apart in an instant, its pieces swiftly attaching themselves to Wang Lan’s body.
As Wang Lan recalled it, before he could even process what was happening, the Saint Cloth had already assembled itself on him.
As he donned the Saint Cloth, suddenly, the Star Power around Wang Lan surged wildly. The Star palace above his head slowly opened, and a relentless stream of Star Power flowed from the Saint Cloth into the Star palace, causing the Star Shine inside to emit an even more dazzling and blinding light.
The Saint Cloth was merely an auxiliary item for a Saint Seiya, providing protection and an amplification of their Cosmos. However, a Saint Cloth could not replace a Saint Seiya. Even without a Saint Cloth, a powerful Saint Seiya was still a powerful Saint Seiya.
So, even with the Saint Cloth on, Wang Lan didn’t inherit any Phoenix Wing Sky Soaring skills. But the boost in Star Power was real and substantial.
Furthermore, after donning the Saint Cloth, Wang Lan felt enveloped in a profound sense of security. It was as if, with the Saint Cloth, he could charge headfirst into a mountain of swords or a sea of flames.
Beyond the additional physical strength, the Saint Cloth seemed to bolster Wang Lan’s spirit as well, instilling conviction, tenacity, resolve, passion, courage, and fearlessness...
Damn it, who asked for these things?!
Now, Wang Lan finally understood why the Five Little Powerhouses were so idiotic. Damn it, you guys are just Bronze Saints; where did you get the nerve to challenge the Gold Saints of the Zodiac?
Didn’t you have any clue about your own strength? If the Twelve Gold Saints hadn’t gone incredibly easy on you, your Saint Cloth boxes wouldn’t be for carrying Cloths; they’d be for carrying your ashes!
Now Wang Lan understood; it was the Saint Cloth’s fault! Wearing this Saint Cloth, he felt he could take on ten opponents at once.
Fortunately, this world probably didn’t have Athena’s will. So that kind of blood-pumping excitement didn’t affect Wang Lan’s consciousness. After getting used to it for a while, Wang Lan calmed down again.
The Saint Cloth definitely gave Wang Lan a significant boost. His Star Power had doubled compared to before, and it also seemed to increase his strength and speed to some extent.
This was just a Bronze Saint Cloth. If it were a Silver Saint Cloth or a Gold Saint Cloth, Wang Lan felt he could even go head-to-head with Galaxy Stage masters.
With a thought from Wang Lan, the Saint Cloth on his body suddenly burst apart, reassembling in front of him into the form of a phoenix. But to Wang Lan’s surprise, the Phoenix Saint Cloth didn’t turn back into a tag but instead transformed into a streak of light that shot into Wang Lan’s Star palace.
The Saint Cloth disappeared from view, but Wang Lan could clearly sense its presence. All it took was a thought and opening the Star palace, and the Saint Cloth would automatically appear.
If I wear this to the provincial martial arts competition, wouldn’t that be cheating?
Wang Lan mused, then shook his head with a wry smile.
Forget it. Wearing the Saint Cloth to compete would be even worse than using my Phoenix Form. At least the Phoenix Form is a Star Martial Skill. This Saint Cloth is blatantly an external cheat.

chapters.title: Chapter 160: Are You the Wolf King?
chapters.content:
Chapter 160: Chapter 160: Are You the Wolf King?
The carefree winter vacation flew by in the blink of an eye. While millions of schoolchildren were still immersed in the New Year festivities, the warning bells for the upcoming school term suddenly rang loud and clear.
Looking back, they realized the homework assigned by their teachers was still far from finished.
In the last few days, the students did their utmost to complete their assignments before school started. Alas, the sheer volume of work was overwhelming, and they could only step through the school gates with anxious hearts, full of regret.
"Did you finish your holiday homework?" This became the customary greeting among classmates who hadn’t seen each other for twenty days.
Those students who had dogs at home would exchange knowing smiles after greetings. The old excuse about dogs and homework never got stale; the only question was whether you actually had any unfinished work to use it on.
Compared to the overwhelming workload of regular classes, students at the Star Martial Arts Campus had a much easier time. At least their homework only required them to scribble furiously for a single day.
Companies reopened, schools started, the New Year’s atmosphere dissipated, and the calm of everyday life resumed.
Even the Tianjian Bureau, bustling with activity throughout the New Year, returned to its usual serenity.
For Wang Lan and other students in their final semester of senior high, the coming months would be the most challenging period of their lives.
While regular high school seniors were bombarded with papers and exams daily, those at the Star Martial Arts Campus engaged in daily sparring and practical combat drills. This training was no longer just hand-to-hand sparring; it now involved battles using Star Martial Skills.
Most students had yet to master any Star Martial Skills. Thus, the sparring groups were adjusted: those who had inherited Star Martial Skills formed one group, while those without practiced Basic Combat in another.
In Wang Lan’s class, fewer than twenty students possessed Star Martial Skills, the vast majority of which were D-grade or C-grade. At this point, the disparity between classmates became starkly evident to everyone.
Over the winter break, the number of experts at the Star Cloud Stage in Class One had risen to six. This included three from Star Martial Art families, plus Jiang Xinyu, Xu Xiangwen, and Gong Feiyu. These six students were perfect for three sparring pairs.
Among the other students possessing Star Martial Skills, seven were children from Star Martial families, and six came from wealthy, business-owning families. Almost all Star Martial Warriors from ordinary families could only look on with envy.
To them, classmates once considered to be of similar strength had suddenly become figures so lofty they seemed unreachable, beings they could barely aspire to.
Even a C-grade Star Martial Skill, once deployed, could likely defeat a classmate without such skills easily. However, there were two exceptions to this.
One was Xie Sisi, and the other was Wang Lan.New ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄhapters are published on
These two gave Liu Jie quite a headache. No matter how he divided the groups, it never seemed appropriate. Wang Lan alone could effortlessly defeat all Star Shine Stage classmates. Even the strongest among them, those who had mastered a B-grade Star Martial Skill, would be instantly defeated by Wang Lan.
On the fourth day of school, noticing his system skill points were depleted, Wang Lan brazenly challenged all students below the Star Cloud Stage. The result was rather stimulating; Mr. Liu, caught off guard, felt his blood pressure spike.
In less than ten minutes, relying solely on his dynamic vision, Wang Lan defeated every student below the Star Cloud Stage who had mastered Star Martial Skills. He proved with his strength that Mr. Liu’s grouping method was entirely meaningless.
Unfortunately, only a few students yielded skill point rewards; most did not.
Wang Lan had noticed this towards the end of the previous semester. He eventually deduced that defeating opponents much weaker than himself offered no experience or skill point rewards. By this logic, even if he defeated Mr. Liu now, he probably wouldn’t gain any skill points.
Xie Sisi’s situation was largely similar. At the beginning of the first semester, she was a kitten, a complete novice in practical combat. But by the end of the semester, she had suddenly transformed into a tigress.
Now, at the start of the new term, Xie Sisi often needed only a single move to leave her opponents on the ground, unable to get up.
This deeply troubled Mr. Liu. Xie Sisi had no Star Martial Skills to rely on, putting her at a significant disadvantage against those who did. Although they were all at the Star Shine Stage in terms of raw power, their actual combat capabilities differed significantly when Star Martial Skills were involved.
And what about Wang Lan?
If word got out that a Star Shine Stage student was sparring with Star Cloud Stage students, who knows what kind of rumors would spread.
Shocking news! Suzhou No.1 Middle School’s Star Martial Class combat instructor actually made a Star Shine Stage student spar with Star Cloud Stage students! Is it a personal vendetta or an old feud? A grudge from the previous generation or a conflict of the current one?
Just thinking about such headlines was horrifying.
「On the fifth day of school, at one in the afternoon.」
Mr. Liu faced the neatly assembled students, his brow furrowed with worry and indecision.
"Xie Sisi, Wang Lan, you two step forward. The rest of you, form your usual groups," he directed.
The students shuffled quickly, forming three groups.
Nearly thirty students from ordinary backgrounds looked enviously at the other two groups. The stark difference in strength had caused them several sleepless nights recently.
Usually, everyone got along well. They would often boast and chat, sharing dreams of which Star Martial Academies they hoped to attend after the college entrance exams. Sometimes, they even engaged in a bit of over-the-top mutual praise.
"You’re the expert, I’m the novice. Your liberal arts scores are better than mine, but in combat, we’re evenly matched. You’ll definitely get into a better Star Martial Academy than me," one might say.
"No, no, your combat skills are definitely better than mine. My liberal arts scores are just a small component; they don’t really pull my average down," another would reply.
But in an instant, those past scenes felt like a resounding slap across their faces.
It turns out you were all playing possum, and I was the only real pig!
In the practical combat portion of the college entrance exam, hand-to-hand fighting wasn’t the only thing assessed; Star Martial Skills were also a key evaluation point. And though everyone was at the Star Shine Stage with roughly similar strength, students without Star Martial Skills weren’t necessarily incapable of defeating those who had them. However, the chances of victory... were actually not high. Unless, of course, one was an exception like Xie Sisi.
Xie Sisi didn’t possess any Star Martial Skills, yet every classmate would admit that within the Star Shine Stage, apart from that monster Wang Lan, there wasn’t anyone Xie Sisi couldn’t defeat.
"Alright, after careful consideration, Xie Sisi will join the second sparring group," Mr. Liu announced. "Students in the second group, Student Xie Sisi has not mastered any Star Martial Skills, so I expect you to be careful. Make sure you don’t injure her."
"Understood."
"Teacher, aren’t you being a little too cautious? We’re more afraid of being injured by the class president herself..."
"Exactly! With the class president’s strength, I bet she could rank in the top twenty of the entire grade even without Star Martial Skills."
"Just be careful, that’s all. Student Xie Sisi, what do you think?"
"No problem, Teacher. If they use Star Martial Skills against me, even if I can’t block them, I can still dodge," Xie Sisi replied confidently.
"That’s good."
"As for Student Wang Lan..." Liu Jie scratched his head. "You said you’ve mastered Star Martial Skills? What are they?"
At this question, the entire class fell silent for two seconds.
Indeed. From the very first day of the semester when groups were formed, Wang Lan had stood among the students who possessed Star Martial Skills. Yet, for four consecutive days, no one had seen him use any.
Wang Lan had relied solely on his flamboyant footwork to quickly close in on opponents and then knock them out with a single punch. From start to finish, he hadn’t used a single Star Martial Skill. Only now that Liu Jie had brought it up did the classmates suddenly realize this.
"Teacher, I’ve mastered two A-Level Star Martial Skills," Wang Lan replied dutifully. "One is Star Cloud Sword Dance, and the other is Flame Sword."
"Oh? A-Level Star Martial Skills? To what extent have you mastered them?" Liu Jie asked, his eyes gleaming.
Learning A-Level Star Martial Skills typically required one to be at the Star Cloud Stage. Of course, exceptionally talented individuals might learn them at the Star Shine Stage. However, full mastery was only possible at the Star Cloud Stage.
It was acceptable for Wang Lan to have obtained A-Level Star Martial Skills. Xu Xiangwen, Jiang Xinyu, and Gong Feiyu all had them too. Inheritance wasn’t a prerequisite; as long as one had money, they could acquire good Star Martial Skills. One couldn’t very well complain that the world was unfair—there was plenty of unfairness to go around.
Besides, even if someone could afford to buy A-Level Star Martial Skills, they still had to possess the aptitude to learn them. Having seen a great deal, Liu Jie genuinely admired students like Jiang Xinyu and Wang Lan from the bottom of his heart.
They possessed resources and talent, and yet they worked even harder than those who lacked both. If they didn’t rise to prominence and leave everyone else in the dust, would there be any natural justice?
"To what extent have I mastered them? Well... it’s hard to say. Probably to a rather high degree?"
"Hmm... In that case, do you think it’s alright if I put you in the first group...?"
"Damn!" Suddenly, a cry of shock erupted from someone in the first group.
Liu Jie’s brow furrowed, his expression instantly darkening. Hadn’t he established enough authority in the first semester? How dare someone interrupt him with a shout? And with a "Damn!" no less?
"Shit!"
Before Liu Jie could reprimand anyone, another student from the second group stared at Wang Lan, his eyes wide as if he’d seen a ghost.
"Qin Hai, Ma Chengcheng, you two, step forward! Have you no discipline? Or do you have some objection to what I just said?"
"No, Mr. Liu! Didn’t you hear Wang Lan’s introduction just now? The Star Martial Skills he said he mastered?"
"I heard him. So what?" Liu Jie retorted. "Two A-Level Star Martial Skills? Is that something to be jealous about? Let me ask you, even if two A-Level Star Martial Skills were handed to you, could you learn them? The higher the level of a Star Martial Skill, the greater the difficulty. Do you think high-level Star Martial Skills are some kind of legendary scrolls that anyone can practice and instantly become a master?"
"No, it’s those two Star Martial Skills. One is called Star Cloud Sword Dance, and the other is Flame Sword," Ma Chengcheng quickly interjected.
"Yes, I heard him. What about it?"
"Don’t they sound a bit familiar to you, Teacher?"
"They do sound a bit familiar... Star Cloud Sword Dance... Flame Sword... Shit!"
Liu Jie leaped back several steps, his face a mask of shock as he stared at the still-smiling Wang Lan.
By now, most of the students had also realized the implication of those two Star Martial Skills.
Weren’t these the signature Star Martial Skills of the Wolf King?
Furthermore, both of these Star Martial Skills were quite obscure. Or rather, most A-Level Star Martial Skills were. After the Wolf King became famous overnight from a single battle, many people had scoured information about him, hoping to find clues that might reveal his true identity.
Star Cloud Sword Dance was a Family Secret Skill belonging to a small Star Martial family with the surname Wang. This skill demanded an exceptionally high level of control over Star Power and was generally learned only by those with a natural talent for such control.
Flame Sword wasn’t excessively rare, but unleashing its true power required formidable Basic Combat abilities. And since most fire-attribute Star Martial Warriors preferred long-range attacks, why would a fire mage willingly choose the path of a Close Combat Mage?
Initially, many speculated that the Wolf King belonged to that Wang Family. However, after thorough investigation and elimination, no one from the Wang Family fit the Wolf King’s profile.
The Wang Family had also stated that while Star Cloud Sword Dance was their Family Secret Skill, it wasn’t exclusive to them. Moreover, it had been submitted to the state long ago, so it was perfectly reasonable for someone outside the Wang Family to have learned it.
Liu Jie would have never imagined that the Wolf King, the very subject of the case studies he was preparing for the entire class, was actually one of his own students!

chapters.title: Chapter 161 Reorganization
chapters.content:
Chapter 161: Chapter 161 Reorganization
Ever since the time at the trial ground when Wang Lan had barely used the Flame Sword before Xu Xiangwen and the others recognized him, he knew he couldn’t keep his identity as the Wolf player a secret.
That’s why Wang Lan was so calm about revealing his Star Martial Skill today. After all, one couldn’t just avoid using their Star Martial Skill solely to hide their identity, could they?
Moreover, after half a year of cooling off, the outside world’s attention towards Wang Lan no longer affected him.
After all, Wang Lan’s initial burst of popularity was due to a combination of chance and the effect of a show. If he had chosen to debut at that time and had been managed by an agency, he might still be famous now.
After the competition ended, Wang Lan immediately vanished from the public eye for half a year. Without someone continually stirring up public interest behind him, the Wolf naturally faded from fame before it could even be firmly established.
Half a year later, even if Wang Lan’s true identity were exposed online, the most netizens would say upon seeing it would be, "Oh, so he’s the Wolf King?" As for being pursued by fans and surrounded by crowds... that was out of the question.
But if the Wolf King turned out to be someone close, someone they had spent day and night with, it still caused quite a shock for the students of Class One.
"You’re the Wolf King?" Liu Jie’s eyes widened as he asked again.
"Last year I entered the Suzhou City Star Martial competition anonymously," Wang Lan replied. "Originally, I just wanted to hone my combat skills, but unexpectedly, it turned into a hot topic. Fortunately, I didn’t disgrace you, Teacher—I won the championship."
Yes, you didn’t disgrace me, but why is my face burning?
Liu Jie thought about the times he had used videos of the Wolf in action for class analysis, the questions based on those videos that Wang Lan answered incorrectly, and the severe scoldings that followed... The corner of his mouth twitched involuntarily.
But regardless, having a student who won the Star Martial competition was something he felt he could boast about for a lifetime. If his student was stronger than him, didn’t that mean his teaching was excellent?
At this moment, Liu Jie shamelessly credited Wang Lan’s strength to his own meticulous teaching.
"Well then, Wang Lan, you’ll be in the first group," he said. "Even though you were very impressive in the Star Martial competition, the strongest opponents there were at the Star Shine Stage. Group One has six at the Star Cloud Stage."
"I understand. I’ll be careful," Wang Lan responded.
Liu Jie watched Wang Lan join Group One. For a moment, he didn’t see seven students but seven future heroes who would ride the crest of the waves and support the heavens for humankind.
This year’s class held the most potential Liu Jie had ever taught. Having six students at the Star Cloud Stage in a single class, especially on the eve of their senior year, was inconceivable—typically, even one such student per class was considered impressive.
"Alright, you can now start teaming up for practice fights. Group Three, listen up! Though you may not be strong enough to get into a top-tier school, remember this: as long as you can get into a Star Martial Academy ranked in the top twenty nationwide, your futures are still brilliant.
"What you lack is not talent, but effort. As long as you work hard enough, even without Star Martial Skills, you can still achieve good results. The progress Xie Sisi has made is there for all to see. It only took her half a term to make such significant improvement. What excuse do you have not to work hard?"
His words left the students of Group Three rolling their eyes.
Effort? Is the kind of progress Xie Sisi has made really due to effort? Half a term to go from the bottom of practical combat to unrivaled? If you’re so capable, you try it!
However, Liu Jie was highly respected, so the students of Group Three dared not retort and began to select their opponents. The strategy for students without Star Martial Skills was simple and clear:
So what if I don’t have a Star Martial Skill? If I can’t block it, can’t I just dodge?
As long as I move fast enough, your Star Martial Skills can’t hit me. When your Star Power is drained, we’ll be back to fighting on the same level with hand-to-hand combat.
This was also another important reason why Liu Jie had been relentlessly training the physical abilities of Class One students over the past year.
Meanwhile, Group Two’s students were also getting started. With Wang Lan gone, Xie Sisi had joined them.
Those who had been beaten by Xie Sisi last semester were getting restless.
Back then, Star Martial Skills weren’t allowed in the fights, and that’s why you beat me. This time, we can use them, so I’m definitely going to settle the score!
"Monitor, shall we spar?" a round-faced, chubby kid who was clearly terrible at Basic Combat spoke up eagerly.
"Monitor Xie, let me! Scram, fatty," another student said.
"Monitor... I’ll fight you. Those jerks just want to take advantage of you," said a different student.
"Monitor Xie, I, Song Bo, challenge you!"
Song Bo’s panting could even be heard from the crowd. This put Xie Sisi in a bit of a bind, as she wasn’t the type to reject an invitation; typically, if someone asked, she would agree.
But now, with so many extending invitations, Xie Sisi was troubled. Her gaze swept over each eager pair of eyes as she bit her finger, feigning indecision.
"How about... I accept all of you? You guys... want to take me on together?"
"Shoot—"
"No way—"
"Are you serious?"
Since when had Xie Sisi become so domineering? Wasn’t she always the sweet and soft-spoken girl?
If Wang Lan knew what his classmates were thinking, he would have scoffed.
They clearly haven’t seen Xie Sisi when she’s truly excited—that’s when she’s genuinely wild.
"Let’s go—"
"I’m going in! Witness my Earth Armor—" the chubby kid bellowed, soil swirling around him as he encased himself in a layer of armor and charged towards Xie Sisi.
Xie Sisi’s figure flashed. She nimbly appeared above the chubby kid’s head, which was not yet fully covered by his earth armor, and swept her leg across.
SMACK!
The fatty fell backward like an overturned Brazilian turtle.
Xie Sisi instantly transformed into a Ghost and charged into the group of twelve. With the force of someone ready to "punch the South Mountain Nursing Home and kick the North Sea Kindergarten," she swept through her fellow Star Shine Stage students, all of whom possessed Star Martial Skills.
"What’s going on?" Wang Lan, who was on his side and about to spar with Xu Xiangwen again, was distracted by the commotion behind him. Even Liu Jie dashed from the sidelines towards Group Two’s area. As he approached, Liu Jie came to a sudden halt.Thᴇ link to the origɪn of this information rᴇsts ɪn ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
He stared with terrified eyes at the scene before him. It was a horrific sight: Xie Sisi, alone, her movement technique flowing like water and her fists and kicks bursting like fireworks, weaved through a group of classmates of the same level, all of whom had mastered Star Martial Skills. One person was chasing and beating twelve others!
If Wang Lan were doing this, I could accept it,
Liu Jie thought,
because, in my mind, Wang Lan’s strength is already among the top five in the class. But Xie Sisi? A mid-Star Shine Stage student who doesn’t even know Star Martial Skills, and she can beat twelve of them?
And those twelve all wield Star Martial Skills! Is there any justice in this world? What about your Star Martial Skills? Did you all train for nothing?
But the scene unfolding before him undoubtedly revealed a fact: their Star Martial Skills might really have been practiced in vain.
Apart from the chubby kid’s initial success in releasing his Star Martial Skill, the rest didn’t even get a chance to unleash theirs. Xie Sisi was too fast; the moment they sensed a Star Energy Fluctuation, she would instantly close in and interrupt.
And there were a few who, in their panic, unleashed their Star Martial Skills without even seeing their target, casting their abilities into thin air.
After a moment of astonishment, Liu Jie gradually began to see the pattern. Xie Sisi’s speed and movement technique were too fast, so fast they surpassed what he understood to be possible for the Star Shine Stage.
Moreover, when Xie Sisi attacks and dodges, there’s a faint Star Energy Fluctuation emanating from her. Isn’t this a Star Martial Skill? Could it be a physical-type Star Martial Skill?
"Stop! What are you all doing?" Liu Jie approached, his face dark. "Twelve of you against one! And even then, you let yourselves get beaten so miserably?"
"Teacher, I..."
"No excuses! During the college entrance exams, the proctors won’t listen to your explanations. Rest for a while, then spar individually. Xie Sisi, you come with me."
Liu Jie led Xie Sisi away. Mingyue Wucheng, arms crossed, curiously watched Xie Sisi’s retreating figure and said, "Wang Lan, if I’m not mistaken, Xie Sisi must have mastered a Star Martial Skill, right?"
"Yes, she probably has."
"Then why does she say she doesn’t know any Star Martial Skills? Monitor Xie doesn’t seem like that kind of person."
"She might not even know it herself."
"What do you mean?"
"Xie Sisi has been training very diligently for many years. Every day, she would do weight training with several tens of pounds and would hit cement piles. This self-injurious training method would damage her body; at first, she would be covered in bruises after each session.
"And Xie Sisi also has an extraordinary talent for controlling Star Energy. So, she came up with a method: every time she was about to hit something in a way that might harm her, she would channel Star Energy to the point of impact, forming a protective layer.
"Over the years, Xie Sisi gradually mastered a skill that combines Star Energy and Basic Combat. She just thought this was her training method and didn’t realize that this technique had actually become a Star Martial Skill."
During his time with Xie Sisi, Wang Lan had learned about her training methods. He realized her unique ability had been honed over many years of adaptation and exploration.
But these words sounded alarming to Mingyue Wucheng, who suddenly changed her expression to one of shock and fear.
"She created her own Star Martial Skill?"
"Uh..." Wang Lan looked confused. "Not really? This Star Martial Skill seems very rudimentary; it shouldn’t count as creating a new one, should it?"
