"Rudimentary... Of course, it’s rudimentary because she created it unconsciously. But once she learns advanced theories of Star Energy application and undergoes professional guidance and systematic training, this Star Martial Skill will quickly be refined.
"But that’s not the main point! The point is... Monitor Xie, a Star Shine Stage Star Martial Warrior, successfully created a Star Martial Skill while still a student? What kind of monstrous talent is this?"
"Now that you put it that way, I also think it’s quite amazing," Wang Lan said. "Alright, let’s not waste any more time. Xiangwen, come on! This time, I’ll let you use three clones."
"Damn it!" Xu Xiangwen’s explosive temper flared. "I can’t take this anymore!" He exclaimed, instantly surging with Star Energy and splitting into three identical replicas. Four Xu Xiangwens surrounded Wang Lan, forming a square.
"Lanzi, a four-person combo massage, deluxe package!"
"Wait, mark your original body," Wang Lan said. "I’m afraid I might accidentally kill the real you."
Xu Xiangwen pulled out a red ribbon and tied it tightly around his head.
"Here I come!"
Instantly, all four Xu Xiangwens surged with clear Star Energy Fluctuations, their figures moving like lightning as they bombarded Wang Lan from all sides.
*Dynamic Vision, activate!*
Wang Lan’s eyes snapped open, and in an instant, his right pupil turned a pale gold.

chapters.title: Chapter 162: Compound Star Martial Skill, Quite Simple
chapters.content:
Chapter 162: Chapter 162: Compound Star Martial Skill, Quite Simple
In an instant, Xu Xiangwen’s figure dashed towards Wang Lan, four figures in total moving faster than fleeting light and shadow. Jiang Xinyu and the other four were all highly spirited, intently watching the fierce battle before them.
After Xu Xiangwen activated his three clones, even Jiang Xinyu found it challenging to deal with him. With the four figures’ hearts and minds acting as one, their coordination was impeccable. Jiang Xinyu could only keep Xu Xiangwen at bay by kiting him, preventing him from getting close.
The scions of the three Star Martial Art families, along with Mingyue Wucheng, wore solemn expressions. Although they inherited their families’ legacies, they acknowledged that the potential of Jiang Xinyu’s group was no less than their own.
Wang Lan’s strength had been demonstrated during the Star Martial Contest, but several months had passed since then, and no one knew to what extent Wang Lan had grown.
Under his dynamic vision, the movements of Xu Xiangwen’s four figures were all within Wang Lan’s sight. If Wang Lan were to follow his previous tactics, he could only dodge, as any attempt to strike one would lead to an attack from another.
But now, it was completely different.
In a flash, Wang Lan’s hands produced two Solar Wheels, spinning at high speed like sharp cutting discs, serving as both a defense and a formidable offense.
"BOOM—"
An explosion of air sent the four Xu Xiangwens flying backward. Three retreated on their own, while the fourth was kicked away by Wang Lan.
That moment was so fast. Even the few who were watching the battle without blinking had not seen clearly what had occurred. Only Mingyue Wucheng’s eyes showed a hint of shock.
"Wang Lan... you... you actually utilized the characteristic of Star Martial Skills switching without a time delay to instantly change to the Flame Sword?" Xu Xiangwen asked, a puzzled look on his face.
In that span of time, it was something he definitely couldn’t achieve—completing a switch and counterattacking in less than a second.
If he had reacted even slightly slower, Wang Lan would have landed two blows on him.
"No!" Mingyue Wucheng’s deep voice resounded.
"What’s wrong?" Lin Gao asked in a low voice, frowning, as he too hadn’t seen clearly.
"Wang Lan didn’t switch his Star Martial Skill... he is... using two Star Martial Skills simultaneously."
As disciples of Star Martial Art families, their horizons and knowledge far surpassed what Jiang Xinyu and the others could compare with. Mingyue Wucheng’s words suddenly made Lin Gao and the others’ faces change drastically.
"Composite Star Martial Skill? Are you sure you didn’t see it wrong?"
"I’m not mistaken!"
"How is that possible? A composite Star Martial Skill is something even those at the Star Cloud Stage can’t master. Only at the Galaxy Stage does one have the capability to attempt such high-level combat skills. He’s just at the Star Shine Stage."
"That’s why... I’ve always said that Wang Lan is the most terrifying talent with the deepest potential I have ever seen."
"Even geniuses aren’t *that* much of a genius," Gu Zeyang shook his head in disbelief. "Even if he can’t yet execute a composite Star Martial Skill that merges two Star Martial Skills, the... simultaneous use of two Star Martial Skills, in a sense, is already a composite Star Martial Skill. Mastering a fully integrated composite Star Martial Skill is only a matter of time."
At this moment, Xu Xiangwen launched another attack. This time, he changed his strategy: three feints and one main attack, aiming to take advantage of the instant he believed Wang Lan would switch to the Flame Sword to launch a deadly strike at maximum speed.
Instantly, Wang Lan’s Flame Sword grazed the throat of one Xu Xiangwen. That clone exploded on the spot, while the other two, fearless of death, attacked Wang Lan with mutually destructive moves.
Xu Xiangwen had been watching Wang Lan intently. Wang Lan’s hands had wielded the Flame Swords without extinguishing them for even a second.
This time, I’ve got him!
Xu Xiangwen seized the flaw in Wang Lan’s movement at an incredibly tricky angle and threw a punch at Wang Lan’s back.
And at that moment, a classic scene unfolded.
Wang Lan slightly turned his head, locking eyes with Xu Xiangwen behind him.
That one look gave Xu Xiangwen the sensation that his heartbeat had stopped abruptly.
It wasn’t a love that spanned a thousand years found in a single glance, but rather a peculiar sorrow, one that originated from a very sensitive place.
Because at that moment, Wang Lan made a feint with his leg towards a particularly vulnerable spot. Almost on instinct, Xu Xiangwen’s legs clamped shut fiercely. Seizing this brief opening, Wang Lan instantly struck with an Inch Strength Fist.
BOOM—
Xu Xiangwen’s body flew backward, as if he’d been forcefully shoved from behind with immense power.
"SHIT—"
Xu Xiangwen cursed loudly as he soared through the air.
Meanwhile, Lin Gao and Gu Zeyang, who had been closely observing Wang Lan, exchanged a look and simultaneously raised their middle fingers. "Beast!" they cursed.
They hadn’t seen clearly the first time, but this second time they saw very clearly.
Wang Lan’s eyes were shimmering with distinct Star Energy Fluctuations that one couldn’t sense without specialized training.
This fluctuation was the tell-tale sign of a Star Martial Skill being activated. Perhaps the Star Power required for the skill was minor, or the skill hadn’t actually been released, which was why the fluctuation was exceedingly faint. Sensory-type Star Martial Warriors could discern the hidden locations of enemies through these Star Energy Fluctuations.
Two Star Martial Skills, executed at the same time. They simply couldn’t believe that such a feat would appear on a Star Shine Stage Star Martial Warrior.
"Wang Lan... you..." Xu Xiangwen righted himself and stood up. "How did you manage to use the Flame Sword while your dynamic vision was active?"
Jiang Xinyu and Gong Feiyu’s faces immediately revealed astonishment. They didn’t have the observational power of Mingyue Wucheng and still thought, as Xu Xiangwen had said earlier, that it was a special ability to switch Star Martial Skills without any time interval.
But using two Star Martial Skills at the same time carried a completely different implication.
"This... it’s very complicated to explain," Wang Lan said, relaxing his combat stance and scratching his head with some hesitation.
"To perform a composite Star Martial Skill, one must meet many conditions," Mingyue Wucheng said in a deep voice, approaching slowly. "Mastery of Star Martial Skills must be consummate, control over Star Power through the body must be consummate, and most importantly, the understanding of Star Martial Skills must reach their very essence. Am I right, Wang Lan?"
"This... it’s not that complicated. I don’t know how to explain it in a way you’ll all understand and accept," Wang Lan said, looking conflicted.
"Just say it directly. We’ll ask you if there’s anything we don’t understand," Jiang Xinyu asked eagerly.
When it came to composite Star Martial Skills, if anyone present had the greatest need for them, it was undoubtedly Jiang Xinyu. She was born with three attributes, and with her wind and Water Attributes combined, the number of Star Martial Skills she could potentially perform simultaneously was immense. If she could master this, her strength would absolutely double.
"Didn’t I spar with Xu a few days ago? Although I activated dynamic vision then, I lost my offensive capability. I could dodge Xu’s attacks, but I couldn’t counterattack effectively.
"Just dodging without fighting back, that’s definitely not my style, right? So, I started thinking if there was a way to use the Flame Sword while maintaining dynamic vision.
"I began to study it in-depth, and after four days of research and contemplation, I finally figured it out yesterday..."
"CRACK—"
The jaws of Mingyue Wucheng, Lin Gao, and Gu Zeyang seemed to make a series of crisp, cracking sounds, and their eyes instantly became vacant.
No matter how much you calculate and plan, some things are just impossible to guard against!
Damn it, this guy managed to show off successfully again! Can anyone believe that? ’After four days of research’? Give him four years, and he still wouldn’t figure it out!
"Wang Lan, it’s not right for you to say that," one of them interjected. "Putting other things aside, aren’t we friends? Aren’t Xu Xiangwen and the others your good brothers? It’s not good to keep your insights hidden away, is it?"
"I’m not keeping anything to myself, really. Look, don’t we all have a left hand and a right hand? Isn’t using two Star Martial Skills at the same time just like drawing a circle with your left hand and a square with your right?
"Of course, it’s a bit more difficult than that. It’s more like drawing a circle with your left hand and a square with your right, while simultaneously doing rapid mental arithmetic and writing calligraphy with your feet.
"It’s just multitasking and perfect control of Star Power, that’s all..."
’That’s all?’ Damn it, forget Mingyue Wucheng and the others; even I want to hit you now! Is ’that’s all’ something you can say so nonchalantly?
"What are you all discussing?" a voice asked. Liu Jie and Xie Sisi, who had been gone for quite some time, had returned. Xie Sisi looked very excited and happy.
"Nothing much. We were just discussing the practical possibility of composite Star Martial Skills."ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
Liu Jie scoffed. "Heh."
"You’re all quite ambitious for your age, but are composite Star Martial Skills really something you should be considering right now? Practice well; the provincial martial arts tournament is coming up soon. Do you think it’s enough to be among the best in Suzhou City?
"Suzhou City’s strength is only average in Jiang Province. I’ve heard that in Jin City, your generation alone has sixteen individuals at the Star Cloud Stage. When the time comes, Jin City’s ten-person representative team will consist entirely of Star Cloud Stage warriors."
"But... Wang Lan has already succeeded in using a composite Star Martial Skill!" Xu Xiangwen pointed at Wang Lan with a face full of bitter resentment. "My Star Martial Skill was completely nullified by him; I couldn’t display any of my strength at all!"
Liu Jie let out another chilling laugh. "Heh heh heh..." He then turned and walked over to another sparring group.
"Mr. Liu doesn’t believe me?" Xu Xiangwen asked, looking wounded.
"Who would believe it if they hadn’t seen it with their own eyes?" Mingyue Wucheng said with a wry smile, shaking his head.
"I can’t do it," Jiang Xinyu’s voice suddenly sounded. Everyone turned to look, only to see that in front of her, she had drawn a lopsided square that almost looked like a circle, and a wobbly circle that was somewhat square.
"I can’t even draw different patterns with both hands at the same time, let alone expect to perform two kinds of Star Martial Skills simultaneously. It’s just not possible."
"I’ll try it too, maybe I have the talent," Xu Xiangwen said as he picked up two pebbles and started experimenting on the ground.
"I’ll try it too..."
For a moment, all the elite contestants in the first group stopped sparring and began trying to draw on the ground with both hands. However, everyone failed; only Mingyue Wucheng’s attempt was barely passable. Even so, he was still a long way from mastering a composite Star Martial Skill.
"Lanzi, if you think you’re so good, then show us!" Xu Xiangwen challenged. "You talk a big game, but let’s see you actually try it! I don’t believe you can."
Without a word, Wang Lan took the pebbles, squatted down, and started to draw with both hands, each moving independently as if drawing separate bows. It wasn’t just his hands; it seemed as if each of his eyes was focused on a different task.
It was as if Wang Lan had been split down the middle into two separate people, each side doing its own thing. They looked so independent they could have started fighting each other.
The mouths of Xu Xiangwen and the others gradually fell open.
Because Wang Lan wasn’t just drawing a square with his left hand and a circle with his right; he was sketching portraits with both hands.
His left hand drew Jiang Xinyu, and his right, Xie Sisi.
Two complete portraits were finished in just a few minutes. The movements of his hands never paused, nor did they show the slightest similarity to each other.
Witnessing this scene, Mingyue Wucheng couldn’t help but be awestruck.
This is a master. This is truly a master...
Xie Sisi didn’t feel too surprised;
It seems like I could also draw a square with my left hand and a circle with my right,
she thought. What she cared more about was that Wang Lan drew Jiang Xinyu with his left hand and her with his right hand...
Could it be...
As her thoughts progressed, her small face suddenly turned red.
But to Wang Lan, it was simply that Xie Sisi was beautiful, and it was convenient to draw her alongside Jiang Xinyu.
Should I have drawn Jiang Xinyu with my left hand and Xu Xiangwen with my right? Even Gong Feiyu wouldn’t agree to that,
he mused.

chapters.title: Chapter 163: Xie Sisi’s Birthday
chapters.content:
Chapter 163: Chapter 163: Xie Sisi’s Birthday
"But I have to say, Wang Lan..." Mingyue Wucheng suddenly mused, "haven’t you noticed that the reason you could easily defeat Xu Xiangwen is that his Star Martial Skills were completely countered by yours?"
"Yes, that’s true!" Wang Lan would not argue with that point; Xu Xiangwen was indeed powerful if not for being countered. Especially since any Mage Star Martial Warrior who got within five meters of Xu Xiangwen would generally be overwhelmed by him.
His speed was too fast; one could only see a shadow. In the next instant, who knew from where he would launch an attack?
"Then haven’t you thought that you are also very easy to counter?" This question instantly turned Wang Lan’s face serious.
How could Wang Lan not know that his Star Martial Skills could be countered? Not to mention other factors, facing Water Attribute Star Martial Warriors meant his Flame Sword was basically useless. Not just Water Attribute, Earth Attribute and Thunder Attribute also had a certain restraining power against him.
During the Star Martial Supremacy Tournament, Wang Lan fought against Water, Earth, and even Thunder Attribute warriors. In the end, Wang Lan emerged victorious! But back then, Wang Lan was at the Star Shine Stage, and so were his opponents. The victory hinged on his solid Basic Skills.
None of his opponents possessed powerful Star Martial Skills, and C-grade and D-grade Star Martial Skills had already reached their peak performance at that level of power. With Star Martial Skills of a lesser grade than Wang Lan’s and no overwhelming Star Power level, that was what allowed Wang Lan to pass through the rounds victoriously.
But in the upcoming provincial tournament, Wang Lan’s opponents would be the top graduates from all over Jiang Province. The majority would be at the Star Cloud Stage, and it was possible that these proud talents started with B-grade Star Martial Skills. A-grade or even secret techniques might be as common as cabbages.
Not to mention anything else, just control-type Star Martial Skills alone could completely restrain Wang Lan.
"It looks like you’ve realized this problem too. I can only give you a heads-up; how to solve the issue of being restrained is up to you."
"Wucheng! Xinyu has told me more than once that you are the true number one expert in our class. It’s been half a year, and I still have no idea how strong you really are. Why don’t you let me experience the fear of being restrained?"
"Oh? Fight seriously with me for once?"
"Yes."
"No holding back?"
"Yes!"
"Alright then!" Mingyue Wucheng stretched lazily and twisted his neck.
The others quickly dispersed, leaving a small circle at the center for Wang Lan and Mingyue Wucheng.
"Let me formally introduce myself. My name is Mingyue Wucheng, a direct descendant of the Mingyue Family. Our family’s ancestral Illusion Technique is unparalleled in the world; Illusion Technique has a restraining effect on all Star Martial Warriors. My attributes are Water, Earth, and Fire. Be careful; say when you’re ready to start."
"Start!"
The moment Wang Lan’s words fell, the world before his eyes suddenly changed. On the vast land, a bright moon hung in the sky.
"Illusion Technique!" Instantly, Wang Lan activated his Flame Sword Star Martial Skill.
Before he could even mobilize his Star Power, the world before him shattered, and Mingyue Wucheng appeared in front of him. At this moment, Wang Lan was already encased in a pillar of water.
The water pillar, like a column of poured concrete, engulfed Wang Lan, preventing him from even moving a finger, let alone perform the Star Cloud Sword Dance. As for the Flame Sword, that was even more out of the question. Not even smoke could rise before being extinguished by the water.
Mingyue Wucheng’s hand rested on the water pillar. As long as he didn’t stop using his Star Martial Skill, Wang Lan could only be drowned alive.
Mingyue Wucheng gently lifted his hand, and the water pillar collapsed with a crash.
After freeing himself, Wang Lan gasped for air, his eyes filled with fear. When he was trapped within the water pillar, he had thought of every possible solution, but... none were viable. That sense of despair and helplessness made him very uncomfortable.
"That was the Water Torture Skill; it can’t really be classified as an offensive Star Martial Skill. This Star Martial Skill was initially developed for interrogating prisoners. As long as you could force my palm away from the water pillar, you would be free. If you were an Earth Attribute Star Martial Warrior, you could control your Star Martial Skills to attack me by standing on the ground. You could also use the Earth Movement Skill to escape underground. If you were a Thunder Attribute warrior, you could electrolyze water to extract oxygen, so you wouldn’t be smothered. You could also launch a lightning strike to attack me. If you were a Wind Attribute warrior, you could stir the water pillar and break my control. If you were a Water Attribute warrior, that would be even more perfect, as you could easily pass through the water pillar and escape. The reason I chose this skill against you is that it’s just a basic E-grade Water Attribute Star Martial Skill, but it can still restrain you. Once you are caught, you have no way out."
This was quite an extreme case, perfectly tailored to counter an extreme case like Wang Lan.
No wonder after reaching the Galaxy Stage, a single-attribute Star Martial Warrior’s first priority in training is to develop a second attribute. The likelihood of being countered for single-attribute warriors is just too high. There is far less worry for dual and multi-attribute warriors.
Leaving the school in a somewhat gloomy mood, Wang Lan saw Jiang Xinyu start to speak several times, stopping each time, until finally, Gong Feiyu patted Wang Lan on the shoulder with a nonchalant expression. "Don’t feel too down, Wang Lan. Most Star Martial Warriors are single-attribute. Look at us: only Xinyu has Wind, Water, and Ice attributes; Xu has Yang Attribute; I have Earth Attribute; and Sisi has Water Attribute. Wouldn’t I be in trouble if I met someone with the Thunder Attribute?"
"I’m not thinking about that..." Wang Lan lifted his head, a smile on his face. "By the way, Sisi, what were you doing with Mr. Liu when he took you away? You were gone for half an hour, right?"
"Hmm, Mr. Liu taught me a Star Martial Skill, a C-grade Water Bomb Steel Cannon."
"Is he considering taking you on as an apprentice?" Jiang Xinyu asked in surprise.
"No..." Xie Sisi shook her head. "He said he saw my talent and thought it would be a pity if I didn’t know any Star Martial Skills. He hopes I can learn it before graduation so I can get into a better school."
Liu Jie had no obligation to teach students Star Martial Skills; in high school, the main focus was to lay a solid foundation. This included theoretical courses, essential knowledge Star Martial Warriors must master, combat training, and similar subjects. Star Martial Skills are generally considered advanced skills taught at university. For most students, just getting into a recognizable Star Martial Academy through the college entrance examination was a victory. Clearly, Liu Jie had higher expectations for Xie Sisi, and this Star Martial Skill was quite timely assistance.
"Then you’d better work hard."
"Hmm! Right, want to come and cultivate together tomorrow?"
"That... I might have something to do tomorrow. How about the day after?"
"Understood!"
"Got it!"
"That..." Xie Sisi suddenly hesitated as she called out to the others. "The day after tomorrow... I was wondering if I could treat you guys to a meal? Would that be okay?"
"Why?" Wang Lan asked, puzzled.
"No particular reason. Just to thank you for taking care of me these past days, and also, aren’t you my friends? I’ve learned a new Star Martial Skill, so let’s celebrate!"
"Is that so? Well, okay..." Xu Xiangwen reluctantly agreed. It wasn’t that he didn’t want to, but he was thinking about Xie Sisi’s less-than-ideal circumstances, and since they were all Star Martial Warriors, dining out would be quite expensive.
To the four of them, such an expense was trivial, but to Xie Sisi, it was significant. Probably, several years of her pocket money wouldn’t cover a single meal.
Every time the five of them dined together, it was always the four of them scrambling to pay the bill. This time, since Xie Sisi had issued the invitation, they couldn’t offer to pay even if they wanted to.
"Great! No problem. Sisi, just come to my place then. I’ll book the restaurant, and you can pay," Jiang Xinyu said with a laugh, hugging Xie Sisi.
"Is that a promise? No one stands anyone up!" Xie Sisi said with a joyful laugh.
At the school gate, Wang Lan said goodbye to them and once again dived into the system.
Because of the issue with attribute suppression today, Wang Lan was considering whether he could learn a second attribute. Even though it was said that one must wait until the Galaxy Stage to cultivate a second attribute, he had mastered the Phoenix Form at the outset of the Galaxy Stage and knew the basic compound Star Martial Skills of the Galaxy Stage. So why couldn’t he learn a second attribute? Later, he stared at the Attribute Task page, finding the bare flame symbol unpleasant to look at. At this moment, he suddenly recalled a detail he had overlooked before: the Attribute page hadn’t appeared from the beginning. When the system was initially activated, there was no Attribute section in the interface. It was only after learning the Phoenix Form that the Attribute was revealed. What did his mother’s hologram say again? That he should wait until he reached the Galaxy Stage, and after cultivating the Fire Attribute, then learn this Star Martial Skill specially designed for him? Then the system prompt appeared, allowing forceful loading. Did the Fire Attribute appear then? Could it be... his attribute wasn’t originally Fire? Was it because he cultivated the Phoenix Form that the Fire Attribute then surfaced?
In the realm of common sense, this was unbelievable, and an average Star Martial Warrior wouldn’t make such a wild guess. But was Wang Lan average?
He wasn’t the type to delude himself with such conjectures. He recalled an incident from the beginning of the last semester when Mingyue Wucheng had been teaching him about the variances in attribute properties.
At the time, Wang Lan had found it strange that he had skipped a step yet still successfully changed the attribute’s property. Back then, he had simply thought that one shouldn’t trust books entirely, as this particular step might not apply to everyone. But thinking back now, if there were such a fundamental oversight, how could it have gone undetected and uncorrected for decades? It appeared the textbook wasn’t at fault; he was. If this guess was correct, then he might have struck it big. Could he be the legendary possessor of all attributes? He would go to the Star Martial Hall tomorrow to find out.
「Early the next day」
Wang Lan got up and, when the time was about right, took the subway to the Star Martial Hall.
Arriving at the Star Martial Skill Trading House of the Star Martial Hall, Wang Lan first used a tablet to look up some Star Martial Skills.
Just as he had suspected, the Star Martial Skills at the Star Martial Hall were uniformly C and D-grade. B-grade ones were few, let alone those A-grade or higher. However, there was a wide variety of Star Martial Skills.
DING-DONG—
Suddenly, a message popped up on his phone from Jiang Xinyu.
"Tomorrow is Xie Sisi’s birthday. I checked her ID number."
Seeing this message, Wang Lan instantly understood. No wonder Xie Sisi had suddenly offered to treat them to dinner! It definitely wasn’t just about celebrating learning a new Star Martial Skill... Wait a second, a Star Martial Skill? For Xie Sisi’s birthday, a gift was definitely essential. And Xie Sisi was a proud person, unwilling to accept their kindness. Like last time at the training ground, she had insisted on giving him the 500,000 that he hadn’t really wanted to take. In the end, when pressed, she had said something like, "If you really consider me a friend, don’t pity me." From this, it was clear that Xie Sisi, though gentle, was firm inside and stuck to her principles. This also made it difficult for Wang Lan and the others to help her, as they feared she might misunderstand. But tomorrow was her birthday. Choosing a Star Martial Skill as a birthday gift should be alright, right? The Star Martial Skill didn’t need to be too expensive; she definitely wouldn’t accept it if it was. But it had to be practical...
Wang Lan flipped to the Water Attribute section and quickly scrolled down.
"Water Shadow Substitute, C-grade, creates a water shadow substitute to block attacks? Seems not bad."

chapters.title: Chapter 164: I Might Be That Once in Ten Thousand Years Genius
chapters.content:
Chapter 164: Chapter 164: I Might Be That Once in Ten Thousand Years Genius
This Star Martial Skill is a defensive type. When under attack, the user can shift one meter to the left or right, and a substitute appears in the original position.
Among the basic attributes, there are also Wood Shadow Substitute and Earth Shadow Substitute. However, Fire, Thunder, and Wind cannot form substitutes because they lack substance. Metal is too heavy; it seems the substitute can dodge faster than the user. By the time the substitute appears, the user is already cut down.
This Star Martial Skill is not high-level, its practicality is passable, and the price is just 100,000. Wang Lan estimated it should be within Xie Sisi’s affordability.
After clicking purchase, a waiter soon approached. "Sir, please follow me."
"Swipe the card and start scanning the code?"
"Swipe the card. Oh right, let me ask you, when will you have A-level Star Martial Skills here?"
"Under normal circumstances, we don’t have them," the waiter replied with a smile.
Such a blunt admission, how can you say it so frankly? Under normal circumstances, they don’t have them? Does that mean A-level Star Martial Skills are usually custom-ordered?
"Didn’t you just buy the Crescent Arrow? Why are you asking about A-level Star Martial Skills now?" Gong Jian’s voice rang out.
"Manager Gong, hello!"
"Back to work."
Wang Lan turned back, puzzled, looking at Gong Jian, who also looked at Wang Lan with a curious expression.
"Did Manager Gong come over because he saw me?" Wang Lan ventured.
"I’ve been in Suzhou City for almost three years, and I’ve given out only five business cards in total, so I remember very clearly who I gave each one to."
With this answer, Wang Lan’s eyes narrowed slightly. "Why do you view me differently?"
"Don’t you know?" Gong Jian replied with a faint smile. "Take your Star Martial Skill, and let’s go to my office to talk."
Following Gong Jian, Wang Lan entered Gong Jian’s office inside the Star Martial Skill Trading House.
"Have a seat. What would you like to drink?"
"Anything’s fine."
Gong Jian took out a can of cola, opened it, and placed it in front of Wang Lan. "It seems that if I don’t clarify my identity, we won’t be able to have a proper conversation."
Gong Jian sat down in his office chair and crossed his legs.
"About twenty years ago, a special Star Martial squad was formed. The squad’s codename was Vermilion Bird, and your mother, Wang Ling, was the squad leader. The Vermilion Bird Squad reported directly to the Ministry of Defense, which assigned its missions, and it was active on global battlefields. The entire squad consisted of Star Sea Stage Star Martial Warriors, each a renowned expert.
The Vermilion Bird Squad ranked seventh globally and third in Jade Country. Over twenty years, the squad carried out over one hundred S-level or higher missions. I retired from service due to injury five years ago."
Gong Jian didn’t explicitly state he was a member of the Vermilion Bird Squad, but he unequivocally revealed to Wang Lan that he had once been a soldier under his mother’s command.
"Were Director Wang and Director He also from the Vermilion Bird Squad?"
"PFFT!" Gong Jian scoffed disdainfully. "They are only at the Galaxy Stage, alright?"
That "only" was quite something,
Wang Lan thought, feeling too weary to retort.
"Tell me, why do you want another Star Martial Skill now?"
"I feel that my single attribute is too easily countered, so I want to learn Star Martial Skills of other attributes to see if I can make up for my attribute deficiencies."
"Wait a moment..." Gong Jian suddenly looked at Wang Lan, baffled.
"Aren’t you getting your logic wrong? You’re saying that because your attribute is singular, you’re easily countered, so you want to learn other Star Martial Skills to compensate? But is the singularity of your attribute due to the Star Martial Skills? Isn’t it because of your intrinsic single attribute?"
Gong Jian eyed Wang Lan skeptically.
Is this the legendary top student from Suzhou City? Could he be an idiot?
"I understand, but I feel that I might not be purely of the Fire attribute. I think I should have the ability to learn Star Martial Skills of other attributes," Wang Lan explained.
"HEH..." Gong Jian let out a cold chuckle. "Every year, there are many arrogant idiots who think they’re that one-in-a-million genius.
Knowing they don’t possess a certain attribute, they stubbornly try to learn that type of Star Martial Skill. And the result? They waste money, fail to learn the skill, and lose a precious opportunity to engrave a new one.
The prerequisite for learning a Star Martial Skill is possessing the corresponding attribute. You’re in your final year of high school; you can’t possibly be unaware of this!"
Wang Lan’s brows furrowed. He didn’t want to explain too much to someone he barely knew. "I’m just asking if you have any. Money isn’t an issue."
"It’s not about the money..." Gong Jian started, then halted mid-sentence upon seeing the stubborn look in Wang Lan’s eyes. "What attribute’s Star Martial Skill do you want?"
"Thunder!"
"Thunder? Good! Very well, I’ll acknowledge your confidence for now. I will transmit an E-level Thunder Attribute Star Martial Skill to you." Saying this, he instantly stretched out a finger and touched Wang Lan between the eyebrows.
Wang Lan instinctively wanted to dodge, but before he could even make a move, Gong Jian’s finger had already touched him between the eyebrows.
"Detected a learnable Star Martial Skill, do you wish to learn it?"
"Yes!"
As expected of an E-level Star Martial Skill, it doesn’t even require skill points!
After learning it, a skill icon appeared in the skill list.
Electric Power Output? What a terrible name,
Wang Lan grumbled internally. But his eyes quickly shifted to the system’s character page. When he saw the Thunder attribute newly displayed in the attribute list, his face lit up with ecstasy.
Seeing the smile on Wang Lan’s face, Gong Jian looked surprised.
Could he really learn it?
Gong Jian had thoroughly memorized Wang Lan’s data. The seventy percent Fire attribute from Wang Lan’s attribute test was clearly recorded; there was no mistake.
If Wang Lan couldn’t learn it, why would he be smiling?
And after confirming his own guess, a weight lifted from Wang Lan’s heart.
If I can learn Thunder Attribute skills, then other attributes should be no problem! If I earn enough skill points, I could gather all seven basic attributes and achieve a complete ’Bloodline Assimilation’! How awesome would that be!
Then he examined the newly learned Star Martial Skill: Electric Power Output. Its function was to produce electrical energy to supply power to electrical appliances...
What genius came up with this idea? Is this really a Star Martial Skill? A portable power bank?
"Well? Don’t just stand there grinning. Can you learn it or not? Just tell me. I didn’t actually expect you to master it; I just need to know if you *can* learn it."
"Who’s the creative mastermind behind this portable power bank of a Star Martial Skill?"
"You already know this Star Martial Skill is a portable power bank?"
"What’s so hard about that?" Wang Lan’s eyes swept across Gong Jian’s office computer, moved to the power outlet, and unplugged the monitor. He then held the plug in his palm.
The monitor lit up instantly.
Seeing this, Gong Jian’s brows furrowed deeply.
"You can actually learn Thunder Attribute Star Martial Skills? Did the instrument make an error when you got your Star Martial Badge?"
"I don’t think so. Perhaps my Thunder Attribute was just hidden very deeply," Wang Lan said, choosing his words carefully, not revealing that he might be able to learn skills of all attributes.
"Impossible. The purpose of the attribute detection instrument is to help Star Martial Warriors discover hidden attributes. If it couldn’t detect hidden attributes, the instrument would be pointless!"
"That’s not the point, right?"
"Right, not the point. What did you just say? Which Star Martial Skill did you want again?"
"A Thunder Attribute A-grade Star Martial Skill. You see..."
"I’ll get back to you when I have news."
"Aren’t you a Thunder Attribute Star Martial Warrior? Just give it to me, and I’ll pay for it."
"I am the manager of the Star Martial Skill Trading House, and all transactions follow the house’s procedures."
"That’s rather rigid, isn’t it?"
"It’s not about being rigid. My primary attribute is Wind; Thunder is the second attribute I cultivated at the Galaxy Stage. Therefore, I don’t possess any A-grade Thunder Attribute Star Martial Skills, only two S-grade ones..."
Wang Lan suddenly stepped forward and firmly grasped Gong Jian’s hand. "How much? I want them all."
"You want them? Dream on! S-grade Star Martial Skills are out of reach unless you’re at the Galaxy Stage."
"What level is the Phoenix Form Star Martial Skill?"
"It’s an Above S-grade secret technique."ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
"I’ve learned the Phoenix Form, so S-grade shouldn’t be difficult, right?"
"The Phoenix Form has three manifestations, and you haven’t even mastered the first one. How dare you claim you’ve learned it? It’s been half a year, and according to my intelligence, your Phoenix Form hasn’t shown any improvement at all."
"But I’ve at least grasped the basics, haven’t I?"
When asking for Star Martial Skills, one can’t be too concerned about face,
Wang Lan thought. So, he stared at Gong Jian with wide, pleadingly innocent eyes.
Although acting cute is a bit shameless, what’s dignity in the face of S-grade Star Martial Skills? Not much!
Gong Jian’s brows were tightly knitted as he appeared to mull over something while looking at Wang Lan.
Although Wang Lan was only at the Star Shine Stage and theoretically couldn’t meet the requirements to learn S-grade Star Martial Skills, when had he ever conformed to common sense? From the moment he awakened his Star Martial Warrior talents, he had been hurtling down the path of a true Demon—the kind one couldn’t be pulled back from.
His Soul Resonance failed to activate his Star Martial Warrior talents. Yet, who would have thought that two years later, he’d awaken on his own? Is that something a normal human can do?
After Wang Lan graduated from junior high, many eyes were on him. The news of his failed awakening reached all the upper echelons of Eld Di’s faction within a minute.
Wang Lan carried the hopes of so many in Eld Di’s faction. Yet, he had failed to awaken, seemingly destined for an ordinary life.
But just when everyone had given up, the impossible happened—a barren tree bloomed. While countless people were astonished, the world is never short of miracles, is it?
Perhaps it was this anomaly in his initial development that caused Wang Lan’s subsequent growth to be completely abnormal. His very existence challenged conventional understanding.
The first Star Martial Skill this kid learned was the Above S-grade Forbidden Technique, Phoenix Form? Who would believe it if you told them? But he actually did it.
Others progressed from C-grade to B-grade and so on, but he went straight for the highest-level Star Martial Skill, completely ignoring whether he met the learning requirements.
Then again, this was something the Flame Emperor left for Wang Lan. Considering the Flame Emperor’s incredible abilities, it sort of made sense, didn’t it?
And after that? The kid became even more outrageous. His luck was one thing, but his talent was so demonic it made people question the very meaning of their existence.
Breaking through to the Star Shine Stage within ten days of becoming a Star Martial Warrior? Was he even human?
And now, despite clearly lacking the Thunder Attribute talent, he could somehow learn Thunder Attribute Star Martial Skills? He completely disregarded whether others could even accept such a thing...
Thinking about it this way, maybe he really could do it.
For Gong Jian, there was no heartache in parting with high-level Star Martial Skills. His skills were granted by the state, not developed by him personally.
Who cares who he teaches them to?
Moreover, Wang Lan was destined to be the banner of their faction. Naturally, a banner should fly as high as possible.
If this banner falls, and if Eld Di were to fall later on, then the Flame Emperor’s faction would likely crumble.
Having come to this conclusion, Gong Jian nodded. "Alright. But don’t force it if you can’t learn them."
As he spoke, Gong Jian once again pointed a finger between Wang Lan’s eyebrows.
In an instant, a forceful Spiritual Engraving invaded Wang Lan’s mind.

chapters.title: Chapter 165: Bank Robbery Case
chapters.content:
Chapter 165: Chapter 165: Bank Robbery Case
"Discovering learnable Star Martial Skill... Host does not meet learning requirements... Switching to forced loading mode... Forced loading failed... Missing forced loading conditions..."
As the prompt sounded, a sharp pain pierced his head, as if it were being pricked by needles. Wang Lan’s eyebrows furrowed sharply, and his body subconsciously recoiled, moving away from Gong Jian’s finger, which had been pointed at his brow.
"How is it?" Gong Jian asked anxiously.
"Can’t learn it."
Despite the disheartening reply, an expression of relief subconsciously appeared on Gong Jian’s face, as if a weight had been lifted.
If Wang Lan could really learn an S-grade Star Martial Skill at the Star Shine Stage, that would be too monstrous, too unsettling for anyone to accept.
"If you can’t learn it, then so be it. You want an A-grade Thunder Attribute Star Martial Skill, right? Okay, I’ll report it. I’ll notify you when something suitable becomes available."
"Thank you!"
Though he hadn’t obtained a suitable Star Martial Skill, Wang Lan’s trip wasn’t in vain.
At least the electrical energy output lying dormant in the system proved my guess: I’m not just Fire Attribute; I’m All Attributes!
Anyone else learning they were an All Attributes Star Martial Warrior would be over the moon.
What kind of Attribute Star Martial Skills? Of course, they’d want one of each!
But Wang Lan didn’t let the elation go to his head.
The more attributes I can learn, the better, but upgrading Star Martial Skills requires skill points. Over the New Year, skill points had been plentiful, almost making me believe earning them was easy. However, skill points were actually depleted very quickly. Upgrading one skill to Silver Stage, level nine, costs a thousand points. If I really learned skills for all attributes, that would require at least ten thousand skill points. Are skill points truly that easy to earn? Wasn’t every instance of earning a large number of skill points accompanied by danger? And with every danger, didn’t I need to use my Phoenix form? The Phoenix form causes massive internal consumption, while Star Martial Skills are a voracious drain externally. The skill points I accumulate will never keep up with this rate of consumption. And this is just the Silver Stage. What about when I break through to the Star Cloud Stage and need to upgrade my skills to the Gold level? From Gold level one to Gold level nine, a full ten thousand skill points are needed for each skill. Besides the three Star Martial Skills, there are also five Basic Skills. How many skill points will I need then? Even if I were lucky enough to amass nearly seventy or eighty thousand skill points by then, what about the later Galaxy Stage? And skills at the Platinum level? Will I want those too?
So Wang Lan’s choice of the Thunder Attribute wasn’t a whim; it was a carefully considered decision.
Among the seven fundamental attributes, Thunder boasts top-tier attack power and speed. If not for its vulnerability to the Wind Attribute, it arguably shouldn’t even be classified as a fundamental attribute. Other attributes, aside from those they are weak against, usually have one or two others they struggle to overcome. Thunder, however, can dominate all except Wind.
And Wind, conveniently, is countered by my Fire Attribute. Thus, by combining Heavenly Thunder and Earthly Fire... I could be virtually unstoppable!
Upon leaving the Star Martial Hall, Wang Lan hadn’t driven that day and needed to walk to the bus station.
The morning rush hour had passed, and there were few pedestrians on the street. A sanitation worker in a yellow vest was diligently sweeping the street.
"CRACK—" A crisp sound suddenly shattered the quiet.
The sanitation workers sweeping the street all paused, looking perplexed towards the distance. Wang Lan, who had been walking slowly down the street, also vanished in a flash after a brief moment of surprise.
The moment Wang Lan’s figure vanished, several more faint pops sounded in quick succession.
"That sounded like gunshots, didn’t it?"
"Old Liu, you watch too much TV! Gunshots? You think this is a movie set? It’s probably just a nearby construction site."
"No, I was a soldier. That really could be gunfire... Quick, let’s call the police!"
"Old Liu, don’t make a scene. This is Suzhou City; how could there be guns?"
Wang Lan transformed into a streak of light, rushing towards the source of the gunshots—a nearby Agricultural Bank—at a speed of one hundred meters in five seconds. Once he saw it was the Agricultural Bank, Wang Lan was almost certain it was gunfire.
Bank robberies are usually the stuff of movies; such events rarely happen, perhaps once in decades in real life. Yet, one was unfolding right before his eyes.
As Wang Lan neared the bank, about a hundred meters away, he activated his dynamic vision.
His right eye magnified the distant scene. Through the bank’s thick glass, Wang Lan clearly saw three individuals in black masks and classic bank robber attire.
But their current objective wasn’t robbery; it was murder. Each had a submachine gun slung around their neck and brandished a handgun, firing wildly at the panicked, fleeing people.
The bank doors were locked from the inside. Pedestrians on the street ran in terror, fumbling with their smartphones to call the police.
Such brazen killing, with no attempt at concealment.
This isn’t a bank robbery; it’s an act of terror!
Seeing this, Wang Lan didn’t hesitate. He immediately raised his hand, launching a Fire Arrow.
The three robbers stood exposed in the middle of the bank, recklessly firing at the people inside. Wang Lan instantly fired three arrows. They shot into the bank as if piercing a water curtain, each one precisely striking a robber between the eyes.
The arrows dissipated, but flames remained, instantly engulfing the three robbers, turning them into human torches.
This sudden, horrific change halted the fleeing people in their tracks. It wasn’t that they were foolish or unaware they should flee. Firstly, the doors were locked, leaving them no escape. Secondly, the sudden turn of events was too bizarre, too unbelievable.
Even movies wouldn’t dare film a scene like this.
"Inch Strength—"
BOOM—
With a loud CRASH, Wang Lan, already outside, punched through the tempered glass door.
Glass rained down like powder as Wang Lan flashed into the bank.
"Everyone, don’t panic! I’m an agent from the Tianjian Bureau! I’m here to save you!" Wang Lan shouted, displaying his badge.
"Is the bank manager alive? Were there only three assailants? Is anyone else involved?"
"There... there are..." a female bank employee suddenly shrieked, emerging from the back. "Three more! They took the money and drove off! The car... the car..."
Suddenly, the bank clerk pointed in panic at a black armored car that had just driven onto a nearby overpass.
"That’s the armored car that came to our bank for a cash pickup... That’s it!"
Bank robbers? Using the bank’s own armored car? Are there really criminals like this? They didn’t bring their own vehicle but used the bank’s? Were they not planning to escape, or what? But looking at the three charred corpses, I suddenly felt they might not have come to rob the bank at all, but simply to kill, using the robbery as a cover.
Without hesitation, Wang Lan rushed out of the bank. He glanced up at the bank building’s height, then headed back inside.
"Take me to the rooftop."
"Okay... okay!"
Using the elevator, Wang Lan went straight to the top floor of the bank building. The armored car was still racing along the elevated expressway, which snaked through several large roundabouts. Although two minutes had passed, they hadn’t gotten far.
Wang Lan rushed to the rooftop and instantly leaped towards the roof of the opposite building.
Like a nimble monkey darting through a forest, Wang Lan leaped rapidly between rooftops, closing in on the escaping vehicle as it climbed higher, navigating the spiraling ramps of the interchange.
In five seconds, they’ll exit the interchange and hit the express overpass. The speed limit there is one hundred, but they’ll surely push it to two hundred. In that case, I won’t be able to catch them.
Wang Lan had just landed on a rooftop when he launched himself forward again. Like a meteorite, he plummeted from the sky, landing squarely on the overpass below.
"BEEP BEEP—" Several cars zoomed past, drivers yanking their steering wheels in fright. A person had suddenly appeared on the third-level overpass, a spot tens of meters above the ground.
Forget what this guy is doing up here—how the hell did he even get up here alive?!
Unfazed, Wang Lan coldly stared at the black armored car hurtling towards him. Through its windshield, he clearly saw three masked criminals inside.Tʜe sourcᴇ of thɪs content ɪs NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet
Definitely them!
Wang Lan shifted slightly, raised his hand, his right eye flashing gold. Instantly, a Crescent Arrow shot towards the oncoming vehicle.
SMASH—
The armored car’s glass was bulletproof, but its resistance depended on the type. It might stop regular firearms, but against a Crescent Arrow—with killing power comparable to a sniper rifle—it was utterly useless.
The glass instantly shattered, and the arrow struck one of the men inside, killing him on the spot.
Normally, such an attack would make robbers lose all hope and obediently pull over. But the driver, seemingly unfazed and utterly unflappable, actually accelerated, charging straight at Wang Lan.
WHOOSH—
The second arrow instantly shredded the armored car’s front left tire. The vehicle lost balance and veered sharply, crashing into the side guardrail.
BOOM— The armored car smashed through the guardrail, spinning and tumbling spectacularly through the air.
BOOM—
Another loud CRASH, and the armored car landed upside down in the oncoming lane, skidding for tens of meters.
Distant cars screeched to a halt. A few drivers, not even caring that they were driving into oncoming traffic, immediately U-turned and fled for their lives.
In a flash, Wang Lan was beside the overturned armored car. His Flame Sword ignited, and he sliced open the car door. The three robbers inside were slumped over, all unconscious.
One was obviously dead, pierced through the chest by Wang Lan’s arrow—deader than dead. Wang Lan felt for a pulse in the carotid arteries of the other two, only to find they were also dead.
Wang Lan opened the back of the armored car. Inside were five or six large bags, and unzipping them revealed stacks of cash. However, these weren’t new, consecutively numbered bills, but old, circulated currency.
Wang Lan’s brows furrowed, and he sank into thought.
Were these six really here to rob the bank? Their actions looked like a robbery, but it felt more like they were seeking death. Those three in the bank, recklessly shooting and killing... if I hadn’t intervened, they would have been gunned down by security once they arrived. And these three, driving a special armored car all over the city? Did they think the Jade Country’s road surveillance system was just for show or something? I’d bet that within twenty minutes, the police would have cast a Sky Net, making their escape impossible.
WEE-OOO WEE-OOO—
Wang Lan’s thoughts had barely settled when the piercing wail of police sirens reached his ears.

chapters.title: Chapter 166 Hu Qing’s Romantic Encounters
chapters.content:
Chapter 166: Chapter 166 Hu Qing’s Romantic Encounters
Soon, more than a dozen police cars pulled up on both sides of the overpass, stirring a commotion. Seven or eight officers rushed into the traffic standstill area, each drawing their guns on Wang Lan.
"Don’t move! Raise your hands, hold your head, and squat down!"
"Wang Lan?" a familiar voice called out.
"Put your guns down, he’s one of us!"
It was then that Wang Lan turned around and saw the gaunt Hu Qing, who had actually gained some weight on his face since the New Year.
"Hu Qing, did you become a Commissioner?" Wang Lan greeted with a smile.
"Last time, you earned significant merit and participated in your Tianjian Bureau’s operations. Additionally, the Commissioner has been strongly fostering his own Star Martial Warrior guards. As a result, my police rank and position were promoted. I am now the head of the Major Case Squad. We just received a report of criminals brazenly robbing a bank, so we responded immediately. When we arrived at the bank, we heard a Star Martial Warrior had taken action. Now we’re chasing the three robbers who fled. We quickly divided our forces to intercept them. I never expected it to be you... What are you doing here?"
"I had just come out of the Star Martial Hall when I heard gunshots and came to check it out." The two walked to the side of the overpass, chatting as they went.
Hu Qing was now a senior officer, so naturally, tasks like collecting evidence were handled by his subordinates.
"Sorry, I went a bit too hard," Wang Lan said with a slight apology.
Hu Qing lit a cigarette for himself and slowly exhaled a ring of smoke. "They killed seventeen people inside the bank. Bastards like these don’t need a trial; send them straight to hell."
"Flower Snake Six Mad?" Suddenly, one of the guards let out a shocked exclamation.
"What Flower Snake Six Mad? Zhang, you know them?"
"I do. They’re the Flower Snake Six Mad from the brothel, Hei’s enforcers. I used to be in the Economic Management Division, and we had been monitoring Hei for half a year, so I recognize these guys."
"Underworld faction?" Hu Qing asked in confusion. "Last time the Crow gang was taken down in one fell swoop, why wasn’t this Hei taken care of along with them?"
"It’s not the same. The underworld also has factions, you know? Besides, Hei is not purely underworld; he’s in a grey area. He mainly manages KTVs, bars, and such. Of course, he has some followers underneath him. They don’t extort protection money or bully people around; they just maintain order in their bars and KTVs, or mess with their competitors. The Economic Management Division received numerous complaints suggesting that Hei monopolizes the brothel. Anyone wanting to do business there must get his approval, or trouble is certain. Consequently, the division set their sights on this Hei, waiting to gather enough evidence to take action against him. This Hei is very slippery and typically keeps a low profile. How could his Flower Snake Six Mad get so bold as to carry rifles and rob a bank? And only for five million? Trading six lives for five million?
Wonder how their brains work.
"
At this moment, Wang Lan was also puzzled. Having killed the robbers on the spot and saved dozens of citizens in the bank, he thought there should be a system reward by now, but there had been no prompt.
He accessed the system and saw there was indeed an ongoing task.
It seemed the task wasn’t over yet, and he had to continue following through.
"Call a tow truck to send the armored transport back. All evidence is to be delivered to the Major Case Squad office."
"Hu Qing!"
"Lanzi, look how busy I am; I haven’t even had a moment to properly attend to you. You really saved us this time. Don’t worry, I will report your merits to the Tianjian Bureau."
"That’s not important. Can I follow up on this case?"
"What’s stopping you? You’re with the Tianjian Bureau’s special operations. Let’s join forces, brother, and take down Hei today."
"Alright. They dare to openly carry firearms and even rob a bank in broad daylight. We’ll take care of him tonight!"
"Come on, get in my car. Let’s head back to the Commissioner’s office first."
Following Hu Qing to the Commissioner’s office, Wang Lan made a brief stop in Hu Qing’s office. Inside, there was only one beautiful female officer, just like the pretty guards you see in movies.
Hu Qing asked Wang Lan to sit for a while and then left with his subordinates, leaving Wang Lan idly flipping through the books in front of him. Even though the robbers’ identities had been confirmed, acting on it wasn’t something to be done impulsively. Any operation had to be reported and approved before it could proceed. Intelligence and planning also had to be thorough. So, Wang Lan had to wait at the Commissioner’s office.
As he was boredly flipping through the books on Hu Qing’s desk, he faintly felt a pair of eyes constantly stealing glances at him.
With only two people in the office, I must be irresistibly charming!
Wang Lan conceitedly thought.
"Little brother, would you like a Coke?" The officer suddenly stood up, took a can of Coke from the fridge, and came over to Wang Lan.
"Thank you!" Being younger, Wang Lan thought he should show his polite side in front of the beautiful lady.
"What’s your name?"
"Wang Lan."
"Wang Lan... what’s your relationship with Team Hu?"
"Are you doing a census, miss?"
"No... I’m just curious! What’s your relationship with Team Hu? He seems to treat you very well. No one dares to touch Team Hu’s desk, but he told you to help yourself?"
"Would you believe me if I said I was his brother?"
"I believe you! Why wouldn’t I? Anyway, I have a question for you."
"What is it?"
"Team Hu... is he married?" The lady opposite him had eyes sparkling like Starlight, as adorable as a baby’s.
Uh... okay, forgive my earlier vanity.
Wang Lan curiously sized up the lady before him. She had a sweet appearance, reminiscent of the stars in beverage commercials. As for makeup... though she wore some, it wasn’t overdone.
"Come on, tell me..."
"How can I tell you that? I can’t talk about my brother behind his back."
"What’s there to keep secret? I’m not asking for phone numbers or other private stuff."
"It’s not that I can’t tell you, so why don’t you just ask him yourself?"
"How can I, a girl, ask such a question? It’s embarrassing. I heard colleagues say that Team Hu sometimes picks up a little girl from school after work. They say she’s his daughter. However, we’ve never heard him mention his wife, nor has anyone seen her. Aren’t you curious..."
"Curious?"
"Yes! Curious."
Curious my ass! You were so nervous when you said that, you were practically tearing at the hem of your clothes. Is that curiosity?
But Wang Lan didn’t call her out, instead revealing a wicked smile. He slowly extended a finger and made a gesture.
"EH? I’m a guard, you know? You dare try to extort a guard? Aren’t you afraid I’ll arrest you?"
"What do you mean extort? This is called buying information. You expect to get information without paying?"
"Alright! Since that’s the case, we’re having a proper transaction." The beautiful officer turned, pulled out her purse, opened it, and with a swoosh, pulled out a stack of money. She didn’t even count it before stuffing it into Wang Lan’s hand.
That gesture left Wang Lan dumbfounded. He had thought a hundred would be a token amount, but the beautiful lady had shoved at least two thousand into his hand.
Wang Lan casually drew one hundred from the stack. "Your previous question is worth a hundred. I’m not greedy. My brother isn’t married yet."
"Then who is the young lady he picks up?"
Wang Lan pulled out another bill. "His sister, Hu Feifei."
"Commissioner Hu is already thirty, how come he’s not married yet? Does he have a girlfriend?"
"He used to serve in the army and was discharged last year for special reasons. It’s troublesome to date in the military. Plus, my brother looks like a monkey, so not many girls like him."
"Nonsense, Commissioner Hu isn’t skinny now, is he? And how does he look like a monkey? He’s just spirited!" The young lady puffed her cheeks, cooing indignantly.
How did this girl graduate from the police academy? With that intelligence, she’s sold herself out in three minutes, hasn’t she?
"And for your other question: he currently doesn’t have a girlfriend. If you want to snag him, you should act quickly."
"Who wants to snag him..." The beautiful lady shyly snatched the remaining money from the table.
"By the way, since you’ve let me earn four hundred bucks, I’ll give you an answer for free."
"An answer? I haven’t even asked... What question’s answer?"
"It’s about how to snag Hu Qing the fastest."
"PSH! Who likes him."
"You don’t want it? Then forget it."
"Just tell me! Who stops talking halfway?"
"You don’t want to know, do you?"
"Just tell me!"
"Find a chance to meet Hu Qing’s sister, Hu Feifei. Then, get in good with Hu Feifei first. It’s much easier to make Hu Feifei like you than that blockhead Hu Qing. Once Hu Feifei calls you ’sister-in-law,’ Hu Qing will basically be in the palm of your hand."
"An indirect approach?"
"This is not an indirect approach, but the most direct tactic. It’s called exploiting the vulnerability, a shot to the heart."
"Kid, you seem young but experienced, huh... How many times have you succeeded?"
"No, this is a tactic: finding the enemy’s weakness and striking it. But it’s applicable to love too. First, conquer the person he cares about the most, and you’ve essentially conquered him."
"Hurry, hurry—The Major Case Squad and the Economic Management Division are going at it..."
"Let’s go check it out!"
At this moment, a clamor sounded from outside the door.
Wang Lan hesitated for a moment, then quickly stood up and hurried out with the other officers.
"This is my Economic Management Division’s case! Why should I give it to you? Who do you think you are? Been at the Commissioner’s office for less than a year and already learned to snatch cases? You want files? Get lost!"New ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄhapters are published on ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
"The Flower Snake Six Mad committed an armed bank robbery, causing seventeen deaths. This case now qualifies as a major criminal case and, theoretically, must be handed over to the Major Case Squad."
"What theory? Whoever’s case it is, it stays theirs. That’s the theory! A rookie who hasn’t even been at the Commissioner’s office for a year is teaching me how to handle cases? I’ve been here for fifteen years; I don’t need your lessons!"
Wang Lan squeezed through the crowd to see a middle-aged senior commissioner with a beefy, flushed face, slamming the table and roaring.
"They have guns now. They’re not just some petty thugs or involved in minor illegal businesses."
"They have guns? Don’t I?"
"Inspector Chen, are you willing to let our brothers clash with these violent criminals? Don’t you care about potential casualties among our men? I’m a Star Martial Warrior; I have a better chance of succeeding."
"Star Martial Warrior? So what if you’re a Star Martial Warrior? Think you’re impressive? Think you can do whatever you want? Think you can snatch my cases?"
"What’s all this noise?" A thunderous shout erupted as a senior commissioner dressed in black with snow-white hair walked in from the doorway.
"Chief!"
"Chief!"
"What are you all yelling about? Is this any way to behave?"
"Chief, you be the judge. Hu Qing has barely been at the Commissioner’s office for a few days. Before he could even warm the seat of the Major Case Squad leader, he’s started snatching cases and hogging credit. Is this reasonable? Just because he’s a Star Martial Warrior, he’s all high and mighty? What’s a Star Martial Warrior doing at our Commissioner’s office anyway? If he’s so capable, he should go back to the army or go pioneer some land. Why act all big in the city after being such a coward? He’s a deserter and should behave meekly, so why the strut?"
At these words, Hu Qing’s complexion turned green on the spot.
"Chen Bing, shut your mouth. Hu Qing has already reported this case to me, and I’ve approved it."
"Chief, you’re being too biased! This is disheartening to the other brothers. Just because he’s a Star Martial Warrior, you’re protecting him like this? If Star Martial Warriors are so amazing, fine. I quit. I won’t do this anymore."
"Chen Bing!"
"This Commissioner Chen is quite tyrannical, eh? Hu Qing discusses the matter with you logically, and you’re just being unreasonable. Now that you can’t be unreasonable, you resort to shameless tactics? You get what you deserve based on your abilities. Otherwise, there would be no need to separate units like the Major Case Squad and the Economic Management Division."
"Who are you? Eh? Where did this kid come from? How old are you? Still in school, right? Which school do you attend? How did you get in? What are your parents’ names?"

chapters.title: Chapter 167 Star Martial Warrior Commits a Crime
chapters.content:
Chapter 167: Chapter 167 Star Martial Warrior Commits a Crime
Wang Lan couldn’t say that Chen Bing was a bad person, but he was certainly someone people found annoying. He was the type to arbitrarily vent his anger on others, quick-tempered and inconsiderate of their feelings.
Frankly, Wang Lan had never been yelled at like this in his entire life, not by a single person!
If it were any other senior high school student, Chen Bing’s yelling might have been effective, but with Wang Lan’s temperament, how could he tolerate it?
"You’re right, a Star Martial Warrior isn’t anything special and can’t just snatch your case. But I can!"
As he spoke, he took out his Tianjian Bureau credentials from inside his coat.
"I suspect that the robbers are backed by a Star Martial Warrior, so this case falls under the jurisdiction of the Tianjian Bureau. You ask how I got here? Let me tell you now, I requested the cooperation of the Suzhou City Police Department for the Tianjian Bureau’s operation—specifically, the Criminal Investigation Department, not your Management Section. Are you satisfied with this answer?"
"You!" Chen Bing glared furiously at Wang Lan. "The Tianjian Bureau... The Tianjian Bureau can forget about snatching my case!"
"Director Wang, is Officer Chen speaking on behalf of the Police Department?" Wang Lan asked, a smile playing on his lips as he looked at the grim-faced Director Wang beside him.
"Chen Bing, watch your language! The Tianjian Bureau has the right to request cooperation from local police forces. Hu Qing and the Tianjian Bureau will take over this case; they’ve collaborated more than once."
"Director Wang, if you do this, how can I possibly face my men? How can I explain this to my brothers? If you insist, I’ll resign!"
"Fine! Submit your resignation letter by noon! What are you all still doing here? Dismissed! Liu, gather all the information Hu Qing needs and hand it over to Team Leader Hu."
"Yes, sir!"
The surrounding crowd dispersed, and personnel from the Management Section quickly began searching high and low, organizing the files. Chen Bing, formerly so arrogant and overbearing, now stood stunned, his face a mask of disbelief.
Wang Lan no longer found the man annoying; instead, he felt Chen Bing was both pitiful and pathetic. He hadn’t even realized that, from beginning to end, he had been the only one loudly arguing, without a single subordinate speaking up for him.
Perhaps even within the Management Section, he wasn’t popular.
Hu Qing and his fellow officers from the Criminal Investigation Department took Hei’s information and returned to their unit. The comprehensive data collected by the Management Section over half a year had indeed saved Hu Qing a lot of trouble.
Flower Street and Willow Alley—the brothel district—was, during the imperial and wartime eras, Suzhou City’s notoriously famous... street. This gave rise to the euphemism "seeking flowers and asking about willows," meaning to frequent brothels.
After the war ended, Jade Country vigorously reformed its internal affairs. Although no one dared to openly operate a Phoenix Building anymore, the area remained a well-known spot in Suzhou City for seeking such pleasures.
Flower Street and Willow Alley. The main thoroughfare was called Flower Street; it was five meters wide, and its sides were lined with establishments catering to all needs: clothing, food, lodging, and transport. Of course, unlike ordinary streets, here the KTVs, bars, saunas, and bathhouses were packed tightly together, one after another, from one end of the street to the other.
Willow Alley didn’t refer to a single alley but to the slender lanes branching off from both sides of Flower Street, like the delicate limbs of a willow tree. These alleys were long, narrow, and labyrinthine, a veritable treasure trove inviting exploration.
Many experienced patrons would ignore the conspicuous establishments along Flower Street, preferring to delve into Willow Alley for their own discoveries.
The brothel district featured ancient city architecture, and the labyrinthine complexity of its alleys made it very difficult to apprehend the shady characters who resided there. At the first sign of trouble, they would dart into the alleys, and no one knew where they had vanished.
If not for the detailed information gathered by the Management Section, Hu Qing wouldn’t have been confident about locating Hei, let alone capturing him.
Hei ostensibly ran twenty-seven entertainment venues, but in reality, he controlled the lifeline of all the hidden Phoenix Buildings in the brothel district. This most ancient and profitable of trades had brought Hei countless riches.
Hei had no fixed residence; apart from a few trusted confidants, no one knew where he would spend any given night. Moreover, Hei had numerous mistresses; the more renowned courtesans from the Phoenix Buildings were, by and large, his lovers.
Hei wasn’t particularly possessive. Not only did he not restrict his lovers’ activities, but he even encouraged them to start their own ventures.
If one of Hei’s trusted subordinates hadn’t been a police informant, Hu Qing would never have been able to confirm Hei’s whereabouts.
As dusk settled, Hu Qing positioned his team outside a building at the end of a small alley. No one would have guessed that this dilapidated old structure, which looked for all the world like a condemned building, was Hei’s hideout.
"All units, report status!"
"In position!"
"In position!"
"Good! Commence operation!"
The words had barely left his lips when Hu Qing emerged from a concealed flowerbed with Wang Lan, charging straight for the entrance of the small building.
Hei’s stronghold was on the third floor. The old building’s staircase was wooden. By the time they charged up to the third floor, the rest of their team had just reached the ground-floor entrance.
BANG—
Hu Qing kicked open the door and burst into the room. The air inside was thick with smoke. Four men were playing cards in the living room, and several disheveled women were sprawled on the sofas. On the coffee table before them lay drug paraphernalia.
In stark contrast to the building’s dilapidated exterior, the interior decoration was no less luxurious than that of an upscale apartment, featuring marble and hardwood floors. The walls were pristine white, and colorful lights were set into the dropped ceiling. For a moment, Wang Lan forgot the building’s rundown facade.
Huh? An unexpected bonus?
"Motherfuckers, grab your weapons—!"
"Police! Don’t move!" Hu Qing instantly drew his gun, aiming it at the four men who had leaped up from the card table.
A gun was a far greater deterrent to ordinary people than a Star Martial Warrior. An encounter with a Star Martial Warrior wasn’t necessarily fatal, but a gunshot at this close range definitely was.
"Officer, what’s all this? Is playing cards illegal now...?" one of the men whined.
"What’s that on the table? Think I don’t recognize it? Where’s Hei?" Hu Qing snorted coldly.
"What Hei? Never heard of him."
"Don’t know him? Don’t know what you’re talking about..."
CLICK—
With the faint sound, Wang Lan’s ears twitched. He instantly flashed into the adjacent room. The back window was open, curtains fluttering gently in the breeze.
Just as Wang Lan was about to inspect the window, he suddenly heard a heartbeat.
Heh. Trying to pull a misdirection tactic on me?
Wang Lan scoffed, looking at the tightly closed wardrobe. "Next time you try this, try to keep your heart from racing so much. Come on out. Don’t make me drag you out."
As he spoke, the Flame Sword ignited in Wang Lan’s hand.
Perhaps it was Wang Lan’s status as a Star Martial Warrior that made the person inside the wardrobe abandon any hope of a lucky escape. The wardrobe door slowly creaked open, and a burly, bald man stepped out.
"Sir... I... I..."
"You’re Hei?"
"Yes... Yes!"
Just then, Hu Qing also entered the room, his gun trained on Hei. "What are you doing with your hands? Raise them!"
Instantly, Hei whipped out a handgun from behind his back.
BANG—!
A gunshot cracked, followed by a CLANG as the handgun hit the floor. Hei clutched his arm, his body immediately slumping.
"Trying to pull a gun in front of me?" Hu Qing sneered. "When I was winning rapid-fire championships, you were just a brat who’d never even touched a firearm!"
That single shot completely shattered Hei’s will to resist. His only lingering resentment was how the police had discovered his hideout.
Hardly anyone knew about this place.
Suddenly, Wang Lan’s ears twitched again. This time, there *was* a faint sound from outside the window.
Instantly, Hu Qing raised his hand and fired at the wall beside the window.
It was an old-fashioned wall, its exterior not entirely made of reinforced concrete. The bullet pierced straight through. In that same instant, a figure flashed past the window in front of Wang Lan.
"A Star Martial Warrior!" Wang Lan’s expression changed drastically; he hadn’t expected another Star Martial Warrior to be in Hei’s room.
Without hesitation, Wang Lan leaped out the window.
For a Star Martial Warrior, jumping from the third floor was as easy as a simple hop.
Wang Lan followed, plunging into the night. He could only see a dark shadow flitting past him.
Instantly, the shadow fired a grappling line from its arm, which latched onto the rooftop of an opposite building. Grabbing the line, the figure zipped towards the other rooftop with lightning speed.
Damn it, think you’re Spider-Man?
Without a second thought, Wang Lan loosed a Crescent Arrow with a SWISH, severing the line in mid-air. Its support gone, the figure had no choice but to plummet from the sky once more.
Tumbling through the air, Wang Lan, with his quick reflexes, grabbed a tree branch protruding from the building’s exterior to break his fall. After a few more tumbles, he twisted his body and landed solidly on both feet.
The shadowy figure wasn’t so fortunate. With nothing to slow its descent, it crashed directly into the bushes below, rolling several times before coming to a stop.
Wang Lan instantly closed the distance. The opponent scrambled to his feet, his eyes darting towards a black suitcase nearby.
"I never expected the police department of a mere Suzhou City to have two Star Martial Warriors," the figure said.
"I also didn’t expect to snag a Star Martial Warrior while just trying to catch a minor gang leader," Wang Lan retorted. "I advise you not to resist. I don’t tend to hold back."
"Young, yet you talk so big," the figure sneered, then charged at Wang Lan.
His strength... merely the peak of the Star Shine Stage.
The opponent opened his mouth, blasting a fierce gust of wind at Wang Lan, riddled with countless tiny wind blades. The Flame Sword flared, transforming into a defensive screen of fiery light that instantly melted the incoming wind blades.Google seaʀᴄh N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
Wang Lan pressed his advantage, his Flame Sword a blur of motion, like a stream of light brushing past his opponent.
"AAARGH—!"
The figure shrieked as blood erupted from the joints of his arms and legs. He collapsed to the ground, wailing in agony.
He hadn’t intended to run. He’d been lying in ambush outside the window, waiting for Wang Lan to stick his head out so he could decapitate him with a single wind blade. But who would have thought Wang Lan would be so alert? And then Wang Lan had even discovered Hei hiding in the wardrobe! Left with no choice, he had to make a sound to try and lure Wang Lan out. But who knew Hu Qing would fire a shot just like that, without warning? His plan to lure the snake from its hole had failed, so fleeing was his only option. With his crossbow and grappling line, escape shouldn’t have been too difficult. But how did he end up facing an opponent capable of long-range attacks? Aren’t ranged Star Martial Skills supposed to be incredibly rare? How could he be so unlucky as to encounter one? Intercepted, he had no choice but to fight with his back against the wall. Unfortunately, his wind-attribute abilities were completely suppressed by fire, and he was utterly defeated in a single exchange.
"Over here! Quickly, quickly—!"
Officers from the Criminal Investigation Department rushed over, four or five guns aimed at the Star Martial Warrior wailing on the ground, swiftly subduing him.
The mysterious Star Martial Warrior’s face was a mask of indignation. In my current state, do you lot still think I can put up any resistance?
"Lanzi, how are you? Are you hurt?" Hu Qing asked.
"I’m fine! But this guy’s a Star Martial Warrior. I’m afraid the Tianjian Bureau will really have to take this one. Also, be careful when you open his suitcase. Let’s see what’s inside."
Hu Qing personally and carefully opened the suitcase...
"A Star Martial Warrior, stooping to this kind of work? What an honor," Hu Qing muttered sarcastically. "He’s definitely getting the firing squad for this."

chapters.title: Chapter 168 They’re Just Corpses
chapters.content:
Chapter 168: Chapter 168 They’re Just Corpses
"Assisting the Chief of Police in dismantling a criminal organization: reward five thousand experience points and three hundred skill points." A notification chimed in Wang Lan’s mind, and a smile touched his lips.
Three hundred skill points isn’t bad at all.
"Officer, I really don’t know anything..."
Just as he returned to find Hu Qing, he heard an extremely aggrieved complaint from inside the car.
"Officer, those six bastards robbing the bank had nothing to do with me! I make more than five million a month from my Phoenix Building alone; why would I need to rob a bank? I haven’t seen them since yesterday. Moreover, they’ve grown wings now and hardly listen to me anymore. Ever since Crow died, they’ve all gotten arrogant, wanting to snatch Crow’s territory. It has nothing to do with me."
"Whether it has anything to do with you or not, you can explain it slowly when we get back to the police station. Right now, your problem isn’t just the bank robbery."
"I..." Hei’s face fell, and he silently lowered his head.
"Is Lanzi here? What about that Star Martial Warrior?"
"Take him back to the police station first. Later, call the Tianjian Bureau to pick him up. A Star Martial Warrior involved in drug trafficking... this won’t end well."
"Sigh. He’s a real embarrassment."
"There’s nothing to be embarrassed about. A big forest harbors all kinds of birds. There are always a few bad apples among Star Martial Warriors."
"That..." A plaintive voice rose from the back seat.
"Shut up! Save it for the police station. You don’t get to speak now."
"I just want to say one thing..." Hei’s face was comically aggrieved.
"Officer, if I said... if I said this was my first time, and I hadn’t even succeeded yet, would you believe me?"
"Ask the public if they believe that."
"But I really am... Ah, it was that guy called Stone who approached me. He said the business in Suzhou City is still untapped territory. He’s from Jin City and plans to open up the Suzhou City market. He didn’t ask for any money from me; I just had to sell for him, and we’d split the profits seven-three, his favor.
