Wang Lan needed to attend school most of the time, and only occasionally, when he had spare time, did he handle work for the Tianjian Bureau. But not having the space to operate now did not mean there wouldn’t be any in the future.
He MingXue’s current motto was to poach Wang Qianfeng’s people, leaving Wang Qianfeng with no one to use.
"He Lao’er, Wang Lan has learned a new Star Martial Skill," Wang Qianfeng said indifferently, his arms crossed.
"Learned a new Star Martial Skill? What does that matter?" He MingXue asked with confusion. "Wang Lan now has three Star Martial Skills. Given Wang Lan’s talent, it’s not a big deal as long as it doesn’t exceed four."
"The new skill he learned is called Crescent Arrow."
He MingXue’s face suddenly changed. "Vermilion Bird has set its sights on Wang Lan."
"Hmm."
"It was bound to happen sooner or later. Not to mention Wang Lan’s talent and potential. Just the fact that he had mastered the basics of the Phoenix Form while still in the Starlight Stage meant it was only a matter of time before Vermilion Bird would come knocking."
"But being approached later is better than earlier. An untested gem cannot become a fine jewel, and a gem that undergoes too much too soon can easily be destroyed. The Tianjian Bureau can provide Wang Lan both the intensity and security he needs for his protection. Vermilion Bird has shown up too early."
"Has Vermilion Bird extended an invitation to Wang Lan?"
"No, but by passing on the Crescent Arrow to Wang Lan, it undoubtedly tells everyone that he is the one Vermilion Bird has set its sights on. And how many people are watching Vermilion Bird? Don’t they realize how many enemies they have?"
"But this time, it wasn’t Vermilion Bird who took the initiative to poach him; instead, Wang Lan presented himself at their doorstep. Can you imagine how infuriating that is? He’s still unrepentant, believing that the more Star Martial Skills one has, the better. He arrogantly thinks he can master all of the Star Martial Skills to perfection."
"Who does he think he is? The Xuan Emperor? Capable of mastering a hundred different Star Martial Skills? I just want Xu Shiyun to teach him a good lesson. No matter how many Star Martial Skills one learns, it’s not as effective as specializing in one and refining it to perfection. This way, even if the opponent has a multitude of techniques, one can still remain undefeated."
Wang Qianfeng deliberately raised his voice for the last part. He wanted the sound to reach the two combatants in the arena and those in the shadows who wondered why he had arranged this fight between Wang Lan and Xu Shiyun today.
"It’s not that I’m bullying Wang Lan; I’m doing it for his own good. Wang Lan’s philosophy has already deviated from the right path, intending to improve himself on the crooked path of learning more Star Martial Skills."
Hearing what Wang Qianfeng said, everyone watching in secret nodded in understanding. This was a necessary lesson for Wang Lan. Without a dramatic awakening, he would never return from his misguided path.
Talent is limited, so is stamina. Unable to seek quantitative change, one must strive for qualitative change to reach greater heights in the limited time of life.
Director Wang Qianfeng is deep in planning and far-sighted, truly deserving the title of Wang Lan’s life mentor.
Especially Xu Shiyun, who felt a scorching passion in his chest.
Wang Lan, I’m not bullying you, I’m trying to awaken you. Since that’s the case, I won’t hold back anymore.
Star Power surging, Earth River Chariot!
Suddenly, a dozen or so earth dragons raised their heads from the ground.
"Damn, isn’t that a bit over the top?"
Wang Lan’s heart skipped a beat. Within a five-meter radius around him, these earth dragons, each more than ten meters tall, had sprung up. It gave him the sensation of being plated on a dinner table, ready to be devoured at any moment.
To not act now would be tantamount to sitting and waiting for death.
In an instant, Wang Lan shot away, his left hand shaped like a handgun pointing at Xu Shiyun, who was blocked by an earth wall. In that moment, the earth dragons also moved, striking toward the top of Wang Lan’s head from all directions.
WHOOSH—
A Crescent Arrow shot out. An earth dragon casually flicked its tail, easily blocking Wang Lan’s incoming Crescent Arrow. The arrow exploded upon impact, shattering half of the earth dragon’s tail.
Wang Lan flipped backward in an instant. One foot stepped on the head of an oncoming earth dragon as he slashed down with the Flame Sword in his left hand.
The massive head of the dragon was split by the sharp Flame Sword, disintegrating the earth dragon into rubble. Simultaneously, earth dragons from behind struck towards him. Wang Lan turned and fired an arrow. The Crescent Arrow, like a beam of light, pierced the mouth of the earth dragon.
AAAH—
Suddenly, from the balcony of the dormitory building outside Training Field No. 3, a scream erupted.
The dozen or so female guards standing on the balcony, watching Wang Lan fight, let out high-pitched screams of excitement. Wang Lan’s fluid and consecutive movements were just too cool.
Left hand wielding the Flame Sword, right hand raising an arrow to stab through a dragon’s head. The entire sequence of movements flowed smoothly, exuding an air of easy control and unruffled poise.
The female guards watching from afar couldn’t help but lose control at the sight of such a classic moment.
"Got it recorded, got it recorded... so cool... I’m going to make a video clip! I’m going to post it on the internal network!"
Those watching from a distance failed to realize the brilliance of Wang Lan’s move, but the few spectators at the training field clearly understood.
Was this merely graceful and flowing action? Was it just a sword plus an arrow?
This was the left hand wielding the Flame Sword, the right firing a Crescent Arrow—it was a Combined Star Martial Skill!
Combining Star Martial Skills is a high-end method of utilizing Star Martial Skills that can only be attempted and possibly mastered at the Galaxy Stage. Forget the Star Shine Stage; even those at the Star Cloud Stage shouldn’t even think about it.
But what did Wang Lan do? He used a Combined Star Martial Skill at the Star Shine Stage?
Outrageous! Beastly...
Wang Qianfeng’s face was unapologetic, his mouth twitching continuously.
What was it I said before? Jack of all trades, master of none? Learning more Star Martial Skills will only burden talent and make what could be exceptional, merely ordinary?
Ordinary?
A talent at the Star Shine Stage capable of deploying a Combined Star Martial Skill is called goddamn ordinary!
Several gazes shot towards Wang Qianfeng, who could only feel his face burning.
He had spoken too confidently just now. He had almost forgotten that Wang Lan was far from a normal individual.
"Being able to simultaneously deploy two Star Martial Skills hardly counts as a Combined Star Martial Skill," Wang Qianfeng stammered, trying to save face. "This is just the first step towards a true combination of Star Martial Skills, which is far from fusing them.
"Moreover, Combined Star Martial Skills involve the fusion of two attribute-changing Star Martial Skills. Crescent Arrow is a Form Changing Star Martial Skill, so the conditions for deploying a Combined Star Martial Skill are not met..."
As soon as he finished speaking, Wang Lan used the momentum from the rising earth dragons and successfully broke through to high sky.
Wang Lan understood that it was impossible to defeat Xu Shiyun by taking the straight and narrow path. The longer Xu Shiyun fought, the stronger he became, and the longer Wang Lan dragged it out, the more miserably he would lose. The only chance for Wang Lan to win was to take an unorthodox approach. With absolute firepower, to decide the outcome in one fell swoop.
"Human Cannon, ready!"
Wang Lan paused in midair, his left hand shaped like a handgun pointing at Xu Shiyun.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ NovᴇlFirenᴇt
"Purple Flame Fire Arrow."

chapters.title: Chapter 175 It’s simple, isn’t it?
chapters.content:
Chapter 175: Chapter 175 It’s simple, isn’t it?
The majestic Star Power surged, and a golden light flowed through half of Wang Lan’s body. The golden sunlight, like a curtain cascading down, dyed Wang Lan, making him appear like a half-angel.
From his wrist, a pair of wings engulfed in purple flames unfolded, and a searing arrow of flame took shape at the tip of Wang Lan’s fingers.
This astonishing scene left everyone watching with disbelief written all over their faces.
Whether it was Lige, who had guessed that Wang Lan could turn the tides in a desperate situation, or Zhang Xiaoxue, who thought Wang Lan was bound to lose, at this moment they both felt as if they had seen a ghost.
Lige had speculated that Wang Lan might use some unknown method to turn the situation around, whether it be a Star Martial Skill, a self-harming tactic of exchanging injury for injury, or even using a Star Palace Artifact left by a powerful Star Martial Warrior.
But the one thing he had never imagined was that Wang Lan would use a composite Star Martial Skill. And it was not the basic type of composite, which involves merely using two Star Martial Skills simultaneously, but a perfect fusion of Star Martial Skills.
"Xu, be careful!" Wang Lan warned.
"Damn it!" Xu Shiyun cursed.
Wang Lan’s arrow shot out instantly. Xu Shiyun frantically condensed his strongest defense, layers of granite walls rapidly rising around him.
The Purple Flame Fire Arrow easily pierced through one granite wall after another, reaching Xu Shiyun in an instant.
At that moment, Xu Shiyun was enveloped in a layer of strange stone that gleamed with a black luster. An odd, egg-shaped barrier had formed around him. It was truly baffling why Earth Attribute Star Martial Warriors seemed to enjoy shaping their defenses like eggshells.
BOOM!
A purple flame exploded instantly, and the black-lustered eggshell suddenly ignited, burning fiercely. Where the eggshell had shattered, Xu Shiyun, his eyes as wide as poached eggs, stared at Wang Lan in genuine terror.
It wasn’t that Xu Shiyun wasn’t powerful; it was that Wang Lan was too much of a monster! How could he have mastered a composite Star Martial Skill at the Star Shine Stage? What was he trying to do? Make all Star Martial Warriors at the Star Cloud Stage so ashamed that they’d want to disembowel themselves on the spot as an apology to the world?
The world suddenly became very quiet.
Even in the dormitory buildings outside the training ground, the girls who were watching were left in a daze, replaying the heart-pounding moment that had just passed.
Wang Lan’s body landed on the defensive wall Xu Shiyun had erected, and then he slid down.
By this point, the match should be over, right? Director Wang probably wouldn’t...
Wang Qianfeng could no longer maintain his composure. His mouth hung open as he stared dumbfounded at Wang Lan, his throat even emitting meaningless sputtering sounds.
"Being able to simultaneously deploy two Star Martial Skills hardly counts as a true composite Star Martial Skill. That’s only the first step, far from the true fusion of two Star Martial Skills. Moreover, a composite Star Martial Skill involves the fusion of two different attribute-altering Star Martial Skills. The Crescent Arrow is a Form Changing Star Martial Skill; it fundamentally doesn’t meet the criteria for deploying a composite Star Martial Skill..." He MingXue’s voice, imitating Wang Qianfeng’s, resounded.
Instantly, Wang Qianfeng snapped back to his senses, his face turning as black as thunder.
"He MingXue, there’s no time like the present! I shall seek your ’guidance’ today!" Wang Qianfeng declared.
"Wang, how can you be so shameless? You were the one who wanted to teach Wang Lan a lesson, and when you couldn’t, you got taught one instead. Don’t take your anger out on me!" He MingXue retorted.
"Of course, one can’t just vent anger recklessly. But aren’t you my punching bag? If not you, then who? He MingXue, take this—"
"Punching bag? Wang Qianfeng, you dare! I’m from the Law Enforcement Department—"
"Law Enforcement Department, my ass! This is just a friendly spar between fellow members..." Wang Qianfeng scoffed.
The training ground immediately became the stage for another high-quality, top-tier duel.
Wang Lan gave a wry smile, shook his head, and turned to leave. Just then, Lige, Zhang Yeqiu, Xu Shiyun, and the others appeared before him. They stared at him with unfriendly, fiery gazes, making Wang Lan instinctively want to clutch his collar.
Suddenly, Xu Shiyun stepped forward, instantly closing the distance to Wang Lan. He grabbed Wang Lan’s collar and shook him back and forth. "How did you do it? How did you do it? How can you be such a Demon?"
"I... COUGH, COUGH, COUGH... Let go! Let go!" Wang Lan choked out.
"My lifelong reputation... ruined by you, brat! If I’d known you’d mastered composite Star Martial Skills, why would I have been so unprepared? How could I have let you get the better of me... ARGH!" Xu Shiyun wailed.
"Enough already!" Lige interrupted Xu Shiyun’s furious rant in a low voice. "Limited to using only one Star Martial Skill, your options are too restricted. Even if you knew Wang Lan could use composite Star Martial Skills, you wouldn’t have been able to stop his arrow with just one. The only defensive method I can imagine for you is the Earth Travel Skill. For countermeasures, perhaps Soil Flow Bomb Delivery or gravity control. What else could you have done? Let go of Wang Lan. Let him explain how he managed to perform a composite Star Martial Skill."
"It’s quite simple—" Once released, Wang Lan straightened his ruffled hair and smiled faintly.
"I have a little trick. Once you grasp it, you can perform composite Star Martial Skills. First, divide your mental focus into four parts. Two parts control the left and right sides of your body, respectively, to deploy two different Star Martial Skills.
"A third part of your mind then acts like shuffling a deck of cards, thoroughly overlapping and fusing the Star Power of these two skills. Finally, the fourth part manages the release: you instantly alter the execution methods of both Star Martial Skills. If the alternating frequency is fast enough, it’s quite easy to unleash a fused Star Martial Skill."
"See? Isn’t it very simple?" Wang Lan concluded with a smile.
The expressions of the four people around him shifted continuously as they listened to Wang Lan’s explanation. By the time he finished speaking, their faces had turned ashen.
"Wang Lan, do you have some kind of misunderstanding of the phrase ’very simple’? You call *this* simple?" Zhang Yeqiu asked, clenching her teeth and enunciating each word.
"It’s... not simple?" Wang Lan asked, feigning surprise.
"Sis, don’t dwell on it," Zhang Xiaoxue said to Zhang Yeqiu. "His brain is just wired differently from ours."
"Some people’s talents are simply destined to make others despair," Lige sighed softly, then turned and quietly departed.
"Enough, enough... A Demon’s methods are impossible to learn..." Xu Shiyun waved his hand with a defeated expression and also turned to leave.
"Hey, by the way, have there been any leads on that assassin case?" Wang Lan suddenly asked, catching up to Xu Shiyun. The class had recently been discussing whether Mu Shaoyun could return for the city selections. Since they were at the Tianjian Bureau, Wang Lan seized the opportunity.
"Nothing," Xu Shiyun replied. "The higher-ups only speculate that Wang Mingling might have already quietly infiltrated Suzhou City. However, Wang Mingling didn’t make a move during the assassination of Mu Liancheng. Those four foreigners were probably Wang Mingling’s subordinates. You killed one, and three escaped. But those three seem to have vanished from the face of the earth; we’ve been searching for a week without a single trace."
"Really? What about Mu Shaoyun then? Is he still receiving treatment?" Wang Lan asked.
"Mu Shaoyun? Your classmate?" Xu Shiyun looked at Wang Lan curiously. "Hasn’t he returned to school yet? He was fully recovered and discharged from the hospital the very next day."
"Is that so?" Wang Lan sighed softly. "After such a terrible ordeal, I hope he can pull through."
Wang Lan wasn’t very familiar with Mu Shaoyun. Although they had met a few times, they had barely exchanged words. Wang Lan’s only impression of Mu Shaoyun was that he was a genius on par with Jiang Xinyu. In terms of family background and talent, he was quite similar to Jiang Xinyu, consistently ranking first in overall scores.
After returning from the Tianjian Bureau, Wang Lan found that Jiang Xinyu and the others had already dispersed. He made a phone call and learned that his four friends were eating at the Eastern Heaven Gate. Wang Lan quickly changed his clothes and immediately headed out to join them.
「Another week passed quietly.」
There had still been no news from the Star Martial Hall.
During this week, the five-person group sparred daily in Wang Lan’s home Training Room. With the city selections starting on Monday, it was unrealistic to expect any significant improvement in their strength.
The continuous high-intensity training was primarily to maintain their current condition, ensuring they could face the school selections in peak mental form.
Ever since Wang Lan had submitted the application form, a mission had been active in his system. Undoubtedly, this mission was related to the upcoming provincial martial meeting.
Maximizing the benefits was, of course, Wang Lan’s ultimate goal. Whether or not he could break through to the Star Cloud Stage might also depend on this provincial martial meeting. Therefore, even for the city selections, Wang Lan had to give it his absolute all.
Suzhou City’s only Star Martial High School was Suzhou No.1 Middle School. In Wang Lan’s year, there were five hundred Star Martial Warriors from Suzhou City, spread across ten classes in the senior year of the Star Martial Arts Campus.
However, Wang Lan knew that every year, the city selections for the provincial martial meeting invariably revealed some previously low-profile dark horses. So, even for these initial selections, Wang Lan couldn’t afford to be complacent.
「On the last day before the selections」
The five-person group didn’t spar. Instead, they sat together to study intelligence on their opponents. In their eyes, everyone outside their small circle was a potential adversary.
"Duan Ziqi and Mu Shaoyun are almost certain to be selected; they reached the Star Cloud Stage last semester," Jiang Xinyu began the analysis. "Moreover, they’re all-rounders—exceptional in combat, Star Martial Skills, and tactical thinking. Zhuang Haotian will also likely be selected. I heard he broke through to the Star Cloud Stage during the winter vacation, and his strength is even above mine and Feiyu’s."
"This time, out of the five hundred students from our school who signed up, a total of eighty did," Xu Xiangwen continued, laying out the numbers. "Among those who registered, eight are at the Star Cloud Stage or higher, thirty are at the peak of the Star Shine Stage, and the remainder are all in the late Star Shine Stage. There’s only one at the mid-Star Shine Stage."
As Xu Xiangwen finished speaking, he looked teasingly at Xie Sisi, who was sitting opposite him. "Many students are wondering where Monitor Xie found the courage to sign up..."
"Hahaha! Don’t worry, Sisi. When the time comes, you’ll shock them all with your ’unbeatable below Star Cloud Stage’ prowess!" Jiang Xinyu chimed in with a laugh.
Jiang Xinyu continued, "From the preliminary data we’ve gathered, the overall quality of students in our year is significantly higher than in previous years. In the past, each cohort had at most one or two individuals at the Star Cloud Stage. But this year, we unexpectedly have eight. The critical issue is that it’s not just Suzhou City; other cities are also reporting their best student quality in nearly a decade."
"It’s really damn strange," Xu Xiangwen muttered.Thᴇ link to the origɪn of this information rᴇsts ɪn NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
"Is the Golden Age arriving?" Feiyu wondered aloud.
"Perhaps," Jiang Xinyu mused. "The foundation accumulated over the seventy years since the war ended is now beginning to manifest fully. Our generation of elites isn’t an isolated spike; the upcoming cohorts and even this year’s freshmen are also exceptionally talented."
"Anyway," Jiang Xinyu stated, bringing the focus back to their group, "among the five of us, only I am relatively secure for a top-ten spot. The rest of you four aren’t guaranteed. This is especially true for you, Sisi, Xiangwen, and Feiyu."
"Xinyu, why not Wang Lan?" Xu Xiangwen immediately asked, feeling indignant.
After all, I’m at the Star Cloud Stage!
"It’s different for Wang Lan," Jiang Xinyu explained. "He has mastered composite Star Martial Skills, so his combat power is comparable to someone at the Star Cloud Stage. As long as Wang Lan demonstrates his strength in the initial battles, he’s unlikely to be treated as an easy target in the subsequent challenge rounds.
"However, Xiangwen, there are two, maybe even three or four, competitors whose strength is similar to yours. If I eliminate other Star Cloud Stage contenders in the preliminaries, those eliminated will definitely choose to challenge you guys in the challenge rounds. If you’re defeated in a challenge match, you only get one more chance to challenge someone else back."
"Therefore, you absolutely cannot afford to lose in the initial selection matches. That way, even if you are defeated in a challenge, you’ll still have an opportunity to fight your way back," Jiang Xinyu concluded seriously.
"Understood..." the others murmured, a new sense of pressure settling in.

chapters.title: Chapter 176: Outwardly Strong but Inwardly Weak
chapters.content:
Chapter 176: Chapter 176: Outwardly Strong but Inwardly Weak
Although it’s just a citywide selection, it’s still an important annual event for Suzhou No.1 Middle School.
On Monday, all classes were suspended across the three grades of the Star Martial Arts Campus, from freshman to senior year, and students gathered early in the stands of the sports field.
Every autumn, the campus next door would have their Autumn Sports Festival. Here at the Star Martial Arts Campus, the annual spring Provincial Star Martial Warrior Selection Tournament is just as grandly held as the Autumn Sports Festival.
The opening ceremony, including artistic performances, lacked nothing.
Of course, the artistic performances at the opening were all done by students from the neighboring regular campus. This was also one of the few opportunities for students from the other campus to come to the Star Martial Arts Campus.
Seniors, sixteen or seventeen years old, their minds gradually maturing. Whether it was out of warm hospitality or bursting youthful energy, there would always be a group of Star Martial Arts Campus students showering the girls who came to perform with their enthusiastic attention.
Giving water, offering snacks, exchanging phone numbers and social media contacts—they were all busy and delighted.
As a star figure of both campuses, Wang Lan naturally became the focus of attention. It wasn’t long before some fangirls from next door came to greet her, and soon, old friends came over to give her a long-lost hug.
"Lanzi, do you know, without you that semester, I felt so lonely..." Captain Qiu of the senior first class, with her delicate makeup on, rushed to Wang Lan and mournfully expressed her longing.
Under the scrutinizing gaze of Jiang Xinyu and Xie Sisi, Wang Lan only felt a chill running down her spine.
"Captain Qiu... I didn’t feel you had such deep feelings for me back then? Every time I tried to approach you quietly and talk to you, you generally gave me nothing but a big eye roll and a ’get lost’ in return."
"Back then, I saw you every day and felt nothing... But since you left, I finally understood what you must have gone through all those years. That feeling of ’unrivaled solitude’... It’s really... so awesome! HAHAHA—"
"I..."
Indeed, Captain Qiu was still the same old Captain Qiu. Even with makeup on, and looking gorgeous, nothing could cover up her imposing tomboyish demeanor. The sudden shift in momentum made Xu Xiangwen spit out a rainbow with his mouthful of salty soda.
"How are the brothers in the class doing?" Wang Lan asked with a sunny smile on her face.
"They’re doing great! You wouldn’t believe it, but when they found out you’d awakened your Star Martial Talent and went to the Star Martial Arts Campus, everyone was overjoyed except for Extinction Master, who was heartbroken. Especially Zhang Tie, he recited a poem on the spot, a true masterpiece. You finally developed a conscience and stopped plaguing us. We even had a little farewell party in secret."
"Why didn’t I know about it?"
"How could we tell you? What if you got sentimental and came back?"
"Heartless—" Wang Lan covered her chest, a look of heartache on her face.
"By the way, Captain Qiu, what performance are you doing later?" Xu Xiangwen leaned in to ask.
"Guzheng! I’ll play, and the sophomores will dance. They’re all stunning beauties. Do you want me to introduce a few to you?"
"Yes, please..."
"AHEM—"
After the principal’s enthusiastic speech, the artistic performance of the opening ceremony began. There’s a saying that true masters hide among the common folk, but it should actually be said that true masters are found in schools. Especially at Suzhou No.1 Middle School, where there are numerous hidden dragons and crouching tigers.
Perhaps an unremarkable person might be an heir to some intangible cultural heritage. Someone ordinary might have already reached the level of a professional singer. Street dance, cool and graceful; a piece of guzheng music, touching the soul.
The atmosphere on-site was instantly elevated by several of the currently popular performances.
The Provincial Star Martial Warrior Selection Tournament, the Suzhou team selection, officially began.
Only eighty people signed up. However, they still had to go through four rounds of selection: three preliminary rounds and a fourth challenge round, all spanning two days.
In the middle of the sports field, a huge electronic screen would randomly display the names of the contenders. The first round would consist of forty matches. Since there was only half a day available in the morning, the field was divided into two fighting arenas so battles could proceed simultaneously.
As the official competition commenced, the first matches in both arenas took place under the watchful eyes of the crowd.
Listening to the screams and exclamations from the stands, Wang Lan’s facial expression gradually became more and more bizarre.
Is this the real level of the senior class combatants? There’s no comparison to the Star Martial Art Championship. Even though their Star Power levels might not be lower than those in the Star Martial Art Championship, their battle awareness and experience are worlds apart.
If the fights during the Star Martial Art Championship were criticized for being staged, then the two bouts happening right in front of her were like even faker car crash scenes. Although they were fighting seriously and not faking it, their frequent errors and mishaps made Wang Lan think,
They dare to sign up with such standards? Commendable courage.
Most of the exclamations from the stands were from students of the neighboring school who had come for the artistic performance. For them, just witnessing Star Martial Warriors in action was enough reason to shout,
Wang Lan thought.
"Next match: Xie Sisi versus Song Ting, in arena one."
Xie Sisi stood up and walked toward the field with determined strides.
Song Ting? That name... sounds familiar,
Wang Lan murmured, stroking her chin."Isn’t that one of the Twelve Vajra from the Commoner Genius Association?" Xu Xiangwen said. "Duan Ziqi established the Commoner Genius Association, and in three years, it has gained nearly a hundred members. Twelve core members are called the Twelve Vajra, known by a slogan: ’Clouds in the sky, frost on the ground; invincible in senior year, the Twelve Vajra!’ Their three years of hyped-up reputation will be tested today. After being praised for three years, I wonder how many of them will make it into the ten-person representative team?"
"What’s this about ’clouds in the sky’ and ’frost on the ground’?" Captain Qiu, sitting next to Wang Lan and wrapped in a down jacket, asked curiously.
"’Clouds in the sky’ refers to Mu Shaoyun, and ’frost on the ground,’ of course, refers to our Ice and Snow Queen," Xu Xiangwen sneered.
"Heh... it’s true that a tree without bark is surely dead, and a person without shame is truly invincible." Even though Captain Qiu had heard of Mu Shaoyun’s and Jiang Xinyu’s fame from the neighboring campus, the Twelve Vajra? She’d never heard of them. Moreover, as a friend of Wang Lan and the others, she naturally had to take a clear stance.
"Song Ting! Song Ting! Not a cloud in the sky!"
"Thundering Ten Thousand Catties! Song Ting, attack—"
Across the stands, a wave of fangirl screams erupted like a landslide and tsunami, one after another. It seemed that aside from the first class, the other classes had indeed been thoroughly brainwashed by the Commoner Genius Association.
Song Ting’s figure transformed into thunder and appeared in the arena, a move that once again sparked a round of fangirl-like exclamations. To other experts watching, most just pursed their lips in disdain.
Entering the arena with a Star Martial Skill? Is his Star Power free or something? Wasting so much Star Power just to show off—how childish!
Song Ting casually stretched out a finger, and the cheering from the stands opposite came to an abrupt halt. The pose he thought was so cool only made the teachers shake their heads.
"Xie Sisi, right? In just three months, you’ve risen from 150th place in the grade to the top ten. How did you cheat? But no matter, I will expose your true form in thirty seconds. Teacher, shall we begin?"
Xie Sisi remained calm and motionless.
"Begin!"
The moment the word was uttered, Xie Sisi’s figure shot out like an arrow. Xie Sisi was a close combat specialist. Even though she had learned three Star Martial Skills, her focus was still on close combat, at least at the Star Shine Stage.
Recently, Wang Lan had primarily trained Xie Sisi’s ability to surge forward in close combat. Consequently, Xie Sisi’s advance was extremely fast. It was so fast that even Song Ting on the opposing side and the refereeing teacher were momentarily stunned.
By the time Song Ting reacted, Xie Sisi had already covered half the distance.
In his panic, thunder flickered around Song Ting, and a thunderbolt shot out from his palm.
"Palm Thunder!"
Xie Sisi’s figure flickered, instantly dodging the thunder attack and surging forward another half of the remaining distance.
"Thunder Needle Rain!"
Song Ting’s face finally changed as he expended a huge amount of Star Power to unleash a wide-ranging Star Martial Skill. Countless thunder needles spewed out from his mouth.
"Water Bomb Steel Cannon!"
Star Power formed a transparent circle in front of Xie Sisi, resembling half a magic Array. A water bomb shot out instantaneously from the circle, piercing through the thunder-steel needles fired by Song Ting and clearing a safe path for Sisi to advance.
"How is that possible? You can still run fast while launching a Star Martial Skill?" Song Ting let out an incredulous cry.
This cry of surprise made Wang Lan laugh.
One can’t move while launching a Star Martial Skill? Even if no teacher taught him, he should have watched last year’s Star Martial Art Championship, right? Even during the preliminaries, rapidly evading and advancing while launching Star Martial Skills are basic maneuvers, aren’t they?
Indeed, moving while launching a Star Martial Skill can affect its execution, much like how doing something else while thinking can cause distraction. But launching Star Martial Skills during high-intensity combat is a skill Star Martial Warriors must master. If they can’t even manage this basic feat, the Twelve Vajra are just a joke.
While Song Ting was exclaiming in shock, Xie Sisi had already successfully advanced to within five steps of him. At such a distance, even someone like Xu Xiangwen might be instantly defeated by Xie Sisi, let alone Song Ting.
In an instant, Xie Sisi’s figure seemed to turn into a misty haze, with afterimages flashing before Song Ting. What followed was an onslaught like a violent storm.
The scene was too brutal to describe in detail.
Anyway, she pummeled him for a full twenty seconds, only stopping as if precisely timing it. From start to finish, including the ten seconds of advancing and twenty seconds of beating, it all took thirty seconds—not a second more, not a second less.
Xie Sisi turned and walked back towards the stands, while Song Ting lay on the ground, his face bruised and swollen, continuously twitching. The strong sense of déjà vu caused Song Bo in the stands to shrink his neck slightly, his mouth curled up in a hint of schadenfreude.
Until Xie Sisi disappeared from the competition arena, silence still reigned in the stands.
Song Ting, one of the Twelve Vajra of the Commoner Genius Association...
The Twelve Vajra, supposedly top experts just a line below Mu Shaoyun and Jiang Xinyu. Defeated in thirty seconds by someone who rose suddenly and was widely believed to have cheated?
Is Xie Sisi genuinely skilled? Or are the Twelve Vajra just a bubble?
Even if Xie Sisi is genuinely skilled, didn’t the Commoner Genius Association claim to be invincible among seniors, aside from Jiang Xinyu and the other two top experts?
This scene made countless students who had once praised and believed in the Commoner Genius Association start to doubt the association.
The ones they had admired for three years—were they just hollow geniuses, strong on the outside but weak on the inside?

chapters.title: Chapter 177: One-Hit Kill
chapters.content:
Chapter 177: Chapter 177: One-Hit Kill
The shock from Xie Sisi’s match had not yet faded when it was Jiang Xinyu’s turn to take the stage. There was no suspense about Jiang Xinyu’s strength; from start to finish, it didn’t even take three seconds.
One Frost Slowdown, one Frost Control, followed by a Frost Roar—two C-tier Star Martial Skills and one B-tier—she sent her opponent off with a single combo.
"The Ice-Snow Queen truly lives up to her name, with a combat awareness and rhythm so fast that it catches people off guard," commented a mysterious middle-aged man in the stands.
"Principal Yu, what do you think? How’s the quality of our Suzhou No.1 Middle School this year?"
"Principal Zhang, it’s not just the senior year of Suzhou No.1 Middle School that’s of high quality. The senior year students from all thirteen cities in Jiang Province are several times better than in previous years. Don’t you think you’re being a bit too smug a bit early?"
"Hahaha... Though that may be the case, take another look. This cohort might just produce one or two champion contenders..."
"Oh? It seems Principal Zhang isn’t just confident; you’re getting a little ahead of yourself."
The huge screen once again flipped to reveal the list of matches.
"Senior Year Class 1, Wang Lan VS Senior Year Class 3, Zhuang Haotian"
"Wow?"
"No way..."
"The strongest Star Shine of the senior year actually clashes with Zhuang Haotian of the Star Cloud Stage?"
"Out of the eight Star Cloud Stage students in our senior year, there are seven left, apart from Mu Shaoyun who took a half-month leave. The top ten representatives will definitely include three Star Shine Stage experts. With Wang Lan’s undefeated strength beneath the Star Cloud Stage, it was a given he would make the team. Unexpectedly, he faces Zhuang Haotian in the very first round of preliminaries."
The appearance of this match even made Principal Zhang’s face show surprise.
Aren’t the match arrangements manipulable? Who changed the rules of the competition? For the top ten representatives, which had been nearly decided, such a head-to-head match should not have happened.
Thinking this, Principal Zhang stood up and hurried backstage to see what had happened.
Zhuang Haotian was already entering the stage, and Wang Lan also stood up.
"Wang Lan, do you feel confident?" Jiang Xinyu suddenly asked as she passed by.
"The problem... is not big," Wang Lan smiled.
He really didn’t have a big problem facing ordinary Star Cloud Stage cultivators. Zhuang Haotian, like Xu Xiangwen and Gong Feiyu, had broken through to the Star Cloud Stage this winter vacation. Wang Lan was eighty percent sure he could beat Gong Feiyu and Xu Xiangwen, so naturally, he was confident against Zhuang Haotian.
Stepping into the arena, Zhuang Haotian’s gaze was as sharp as an arrow.
"Wang Lan, you transferred to the Star Martial Arts Campus from the neighboring campus in your senior year. In less than a year, you’ve made quite a splash here. However, I don’t believe it. How can someone who’s been a Star Martial Warrior for less than a year be such a genius?
Those from the Civilian Garbage Society at least spend three years cultivating their image. Are you genuinely talented or just a fluke? Let me see for myself today."
"I don’t want this either; it’s all thanks to my classmates who set off my abilities. From your tone, Zhuang, it seems like you want to step over me?" Wang Lan forced a smile.
His rise had been too rapid; rumors in the Star Martial Arts Campus claimed Wang Lan was a manufactured genius. How much of a genius could someone be who only awoke their Star Martial Art talent at sixteen?
"I don’t mean that. Whether you’re a true genius or a fake one doesn’t matter to me, and stepping on you doesn’t benefit me.
Jiang Xinyu has always been my target, and I don’t want her reputation tarnished by having you as a friend. After all, Jiang Xinyu represents the honor of Suzhou City as the prime representative of our cohort.
I can give you an out; you can claim an upset stomach or not feeling well today. If you need it, I can even play along so you don’t look too bad in defeat."
"Well, thank you for that!"
Zhuang Haotian was always the model student, with a reputation at school that could be described—well—as a gentleman, an orchid among gentlemen. Wang Lan occasionally heard rumors, too, that Zhuang Haotian apparently had a secret crush on Jiang Xinyu. However, Zhuang Haotian never actively appeared before Jiang Xinyu, so naturally, the gossip fell apart on its own. But now, Wang Lan distinctly smelled a sour lemon.
The two appeared to be exchanging private words, but every player’s words were transmitted to the audience’s ears through hidden microphones. It wasn’t a disrespect for privacy, but rather because verbal sparring was also a tactic.
Some took this dialogue seriously, while others revealed knowing smiles and analyzed the tactical intent behind the words exchanged between the two.
Even against Wang Lan, who was of a lower Star Martial level, Zhuang Haotian was not the least bit lax, attempting to agitate Wang Lan with words before the fight began, intending to unsettle his state of mind.
Unfortunately for him, Wang Lan’s mental fortitude was as steady as an old dog’s. Although their verbal sparring consisted of only a few words, Wang Lan skillfully deflected Zhuang Haotian’s provocations.
"I have only one request: please hang in there a little longer," Wang Lan said.
"Wow, Lanzi still has that same dominance as before," Captain Qiu said excitedly, grasping her hands tightly.
"Is that dominance? That’s arrogance, alright! Was he like this at the other campus, always looking for a fight?" asked Xu Xiangwen, enthusiastically moving closer to Captain Qiu.
"Not really... Just once during a monthly exam, the test was exceptionally hard, and the second rank in our class only scored 370. He got 440. That time, a lot of students were crying. And do you know how he comforted us?
’I held back massively for you all, like trying to contain the Pacific, and you’re still this fragile. How am I supposed to show mercy? Can’t you all try a bit harder?’
At that moment, I couldn’t help it; I cried on my desk too."
Xu Xiangwen looked sympathetically at Captain Qiu. "Which time are you talking about? Oh, I remember now, someone in my class cried too..."
Xu Xiangwen suddenly halted his words, his expression turning to one of fright as he lowered his head. Beneath Xu Xiangwen’s seat, the Ice Throne was rapidly spreading into form.
Zhuang Haotian took a deep breath to calm his trembling heart. "Wang Lan, I hope your strength is as sharp as your mouth."
"Begin!" Suddenly, the referee’s whistle sounded in the arena.
Almost instantaneously, both figures flashed, charging towards each other at the same time.
According to intelligence from Xu Xiangwen, Zhuang Haotian was a Thunder Attribute Star Martial Warrior. The characteristic of Thunder Attribute Star Power was concentration, which could erupt with speeds and explosive force far surpassing other attributes. Normally, you’d either need attribute suppression or stage superiority to defeat a Thunder Attribute Star Martial Warrior in a head-to-head fight.
Zhuang Haotian had mastered four kinds of Thunder Attribute Star Martial Skills. Two were the same as Song Ting’s: Thunder Palm and Thunder Rain Dew. Another was Thunder Activity, which used electric stimulation on nerves and cells to greatly enhance physical strength, reflexes, and speed. The last one was unknown to Wang Lan, as Zhuang Haotian had never used it before.
Wang Lan believed that Zhuang Haotian would not start with Thunder Palm or Thunder Rain Dew. Thunder Palm came with attacking restrictions, and Thunder Rain Dew lacked power and consumed too much Star Power. Both skills were not mature, and even if they were freely offered, Wang Lan would not bother learning them. However, Thunder Activity was different. Enhancing bodily reactions and speed was extremely practical. Moreover, the enhancement level completely depended on the degree of electric stimulation. This was the same as Xu Xiangwen’s performance with the Pure Yang Skill. If Wang Lan were Zhuang Haotian, he would definitely choose to instantly kill his opponent with Thunder Activity.
Therefore, it’s a kind of sadness when your opponent sees through all your plans before you even make a move.
At the start, Wang Lan quickly closed in on Zhuang Haotian. Whether or not Zhuang Haotian used Thunder Activity, Wang Lan would force him to use it. Once Zhuang Haotian activated Thunder Activity, Wang Lan wouldn’t give him a chance to switch Star Martial Skills.
Thunder Activity was a great skill: quick movement, quick attacks, essential for survival on the battlefield and for instant kills on rookies. It was also completely countered by Wang Lan’s dynamic vision, and Zhuang Haotian’s fate was clearly arranged by Wang Lan.
Dynamic Vision, activate!
A flash of gold appeared instantly above Wang Lan’s right eye, and Zhuang Haotian’s movements seemed to slow down in an instant.
Zhuang Haotian seemed unaware that his movements had already been effortlessly captured by Wang Lan; even his slightest movements had no place to hide.
Countless eyes were fixed on the clash between Wang Lan and Zhuang Haotian, and many were so wide-eyed they dared not blink, for fear of missing a thrilling moment.
Xu Xiangwen, however, suddenly shook his head with a wry smile. "Zhuang Haotian is about to be instantly killed."
"How is that possible?" Captain Qiu wasn’t a Star Martial Warrior, but she knew about the hierarchy among Star Martial Warriors. Wang Lan was at the Star Shine Stage and Zhuang Haotian was at the Star Cloud Stage—a realm apart. Shouldn’t Wang Lan be the one to get instantly killed?
"Wang Lan’s attribute may not restrain Thunder, but Wang Lan does counter speed, and Zhuang Haotian relies on his Thunder Attribute to increase speed.
If his speed, fighting technique, Star Power, and attacks are all inferior to mine, and I was thrashed by Wang Lan, why would Zhuang Haotian not lose?"
"That... Xu Xiangwen, doesn’t Zhuang Haotian still have another hidden trump card? That powerful Star Martial Skill?" Xie Sisi nervously asked.
"Yes, there is, but he needs an opportunity to use it, right?"
Watching Wang Lan rushing towards him, Zhuang Haotian laughed.
"
Daring to engage in close combat with me while I activate Thunder Activity? You really don’t know the meaning of death...
"
This thought had just popped into his mind. Just as he threw a punch towards Wang Lan’s forehead, Wang Lan lightly raised his left hand, and a bright red Solar Wheel rose.
No need for reminders; the terrifying cutting force emitted by the high-speed rotating Solar Wheel made Zhuang Haotian’s heart jump in alarm.
In a panic, he pulled back his punch. With reflexes beyond those of ordinary people, he quickly changed his move and aimed a kick at Wang Lan’s lower back.
But the instant his foot lifted, Wang Lan had already turned around. With a punch from an eerie angle that avoided the trajectory of the leg whip, it invaded Zhuang Haotian’s chest area.
This punch came when Zhuang Haotian’s strength had not fully transitioned and his footing was unsteady.
Dodging was impossible; blocking, too late.
Even if he executed another defensive Star Martial Skill, the switch between skills would not be fast enough to complete before the fist arrived.
This punch meant certain doom.
Zhuang Haotian bit down hard.
It’s just a punch, isn’t it? Having practiced Star Martial Arts combat for ten years and endured so many punches from old men, such a light punch couldn’t threaten me. Once I survive this, I’ll show you...
UGH—
In an instant, an unimaginable force surged from his stomach into his organs, as if an electric current flowed into every limb.
In a haze, Zhuang Haotian heard something about Inch Strength.
The scene froze.
In everyone’s eyes, the scene seemed to skip a frame. It was as if two people had rapidly converged, and within less than a second, their figures had already frozen.
Wang Lan and Zhuang Haotian’s movements were misaligned and frozen.
Zhuang Haotian’s eyes were almost bulging out of his sockets, the whites bloodshot.
A strong, revolting smell wafted across. Wang Lan’s expression changed drastically, and he instantly retreated three meters. Zhuang Haotian, now unsupported, rigidly collapsed onto the ground.

chapters.title: Chapter 178: Case Emerged
chapters.content:
Chapter 178: Chapter 178: Case Emerged
"Medical staff, quick... medical staff," the referee teacher called out loudly, rushing over to Zhuang Haotian’s side. "What’s that smell? It stinks! Wang Lan, you didn’t do anything to him, did you?"
"No, Teacher. I was very measured in my approach. He might have had an upset stomach, and when I punched him, he accidentally... well, soiled himself."
PUFFT— The referee teacher instantly stood up and took a step back.
"Wang Lan from Senior Three, Class One, wins."
"Successfully completed the first round of the preliminaries for Suzhou City’s representative team. Awarded one thousand experience points and thirty skill points," a prompt sounded in his mind.
Wang Lan bowed to thank the referee teacher and turned to walk towards the stands.
Only then did sporadic exclamations of shock begin to erupt from the stands.
"Holy shit! What did I just see? Zhuang Haotian got one-shotted?"
"I swear, I didn’t even blink! I didn’t even see clearly how Zhuang Haotian fell!"
"Forget not seeing clearly, I still can’t figure out how Zhuang Haotian went down! Isn’t he at the Star Cloud Stage? A Star Cloud Stage cultivator getting one-shotted by a Star Shine Stage cultivator? I now have reason to doubt if Zhuang Haotian is even truly at the Star Cloud Stage!"
"Zhuang Haotian’s Star Cloud Stage status is genuine, but I suspect Wang Lan’s Star Shine Stage is some kind of mutant variant. Is this what a Star Shine Stage can do? A Star Shine Stage one-shotting a Star Cloud Stage?"
"Perhaps Wang Lan has already reached the Star Cloud Stage. Just look at that move earlier. Hey, Cheng, you’re also at the Star Shine Stage, tell us, is that something a Star Shine Stage cultivator can pull off?"
"Screw off! I didn’t even understand what happened. Maybe I’m a fake Star Shine Stage cultivator."
The match had started so unexpectedly and ended so abruptly that even though a new match had begun, the audience was still fervently discussing the previous one.
Wang Lan from Suzhou No.1 Middle School, hailed as the strongest at the Star Shine Stage—what stage was he really at to be able to one-shot someone at the Star Cloud Stage? If it hadn’t happened right before their eyes, who would believe it?
Principal Zhang returned from backstage. Just as he got back to his seat, the match ended. It made Principal Zhang think he had inadvertently been away for several minutes, but when he checked his watch, it had been less than five minutes.
"Principal Yu, why do you look so grave?"
"Principal Zhang, I’m now somewhat convinced that this year’s senior class truly has hidden dragons and crouching tigers. That student, Wang Lan, what’s his family background?"
"What’s wrong?"
"A peerless genius who has mastered composite Star Martial Skills while only at the Star Shine Stage! Such a genius is destined to reach at least the Galaxy Stage in the future. That young prodigy, Zhuang Haotian, didn’t lose unjustly. Reaching the Star Cloud Stage in one’s senior year of high school is indeed a mark of genius. But looking beyond just the national level, even within the entire Jiang Province, there are no fewer than fifty seniors at the Star Cloud Stage. However, finding a genius who can master the application of composite Star Martial Skills while at the Star Shine Stage is rare even nationwide."
"Hahaha... Is that so? It’s truly rare to hear Principal Yu take back his words..." Principal Zhang’s face was wreathed in smiles as he feigned nonchalance, but inwardly, he was utterly bewildered.
What are you talking about? Is it some alien language? A Star Shine Stage student who has mastered the practical application of composite Star Martial Skills? In my school? And I had no idea? Hahaha... He must have seen it wrong... Hehehe...
"By the way, you left earlier because..."
"Originally, our school’s seeded contestants weren’t supposed to meet in the preliminary rounds. I didn’t expect Zhuang Haotian and Wang Lan to actually face each other in the first round. Sigh, it was an oversight on my part. One student had an incident and still hasn’t reported to the school. So, I removed his name. After his name was removed, the original match pairings got misaligned. So... now with Wang Lan and Zhuang Haotian matched up like this, everything that follows is in disarray. I’ve had the backstage staff urgently re-sort the matchups."
This was a tacit understanding among the various schools, a common practice both principals were well aware of, so there was no need for concealment.
The subsequent matches indeed saw one dark horse after another emerge. Students who usually didn’t stand out in school suddenly made a stunning impact in the battle arena. But no matter how stunning their performances, none could surpass Wang Lan’s feat of, as a Star Shine Stage cultivator, instantly defeating a Star Cloud Stage opponent.
In half a day, the first and second rounds of the competition were completed.
Wang Lan’s group of five all successfully advanced to the third round, the contest for the top ten. Xie Sisi, in particular, had exceptionally good luck, avoiding strong opponents in two consecutive rounds.
Conversely, the Commoner Genius Association, on which the school had pinned high hopes and which had been lauded for three years as being composed entirely of elites—with any one of its Twelve Vajra supposedly qualified to represent Suzhou City in the provincial martial arts tournament—suffered a rather pitiful outcome. After two rounds, only three members of the Twelve Vajra, including their leader Duan Ziqi, had made it to the third round. The chances of the remaining two making it into the top ten looked slim.
No matter how much they were hyped up, once put to the test, all that glitters is not gold. And those scions of wealthy families, who had been disparaged by the Commoner Genius Association for three years, finally had their moment of triumphant vindication.
Scions are just rich, right? Their strength is all bought with money. Without money to support you, you’re all cripples, imbeciles!
Heh? But your betters are still your betters.
Didn’t you also fail to make it to the third round?
Sorry, but I successfully took down one of the Twelve Vajra in the first round.
Hard work can indeed help one catch up to the resource-rich scions, but the question is, are you actually working hard? They were all commoners, yet Xie Sisi managed to overcome all obstacles, while the so-called Commoner Genius Association became a laughingstock in comparison to her.
After the first day of the school’s selection tournament concluded, the posts and forums on the campus network were in an uproar. The Commoner Genius Association even earned a new nickname: the Commoner Joke Association.
At five o’clock, school dismissed on time. Wang Lan, shouldering his backpack, walked home along his usual route. His mind was immersed in the system. His character was at Star Shine Stage Eight, with progress around seventy-five percent. He had gained three thousand experience points from participating in two rounds today.
At this rate, reaching the Star Cloud Stage would likely require winning the provincial martial arts tournament. But could he win the championship without breaking through to the Star Cloud Stage? That was a practical problem.
Although his combined use of Crescent Arrow and Flame Sword made him no weaker than a typical Star Cloud Stage Star Martial Warrior, the provincial martial arts tournament saw many atypical Star Cloud Stage cultivators every year.
Previous provincial tournaments hadn’t been public, so there was very little information available. However, Wang Lan had managed to gather some. It could be said that every year, there were contestants who appeared normal but were, in fact, monstrously strong. Some possessed powerful Inborn Talents of the Bloodline, while others had freakishly potent abilities. Against such Star Cloud Stage Star Martial Warriors, Wang Lan didn’t stand a chance.
Two paths now lay before Wang Lan: either learn a widely applicable A-grade lightning-element Star Martial Skill that could successfully chain with another A-grade Star Martial Skill, or break through to the Star Cloud Stage and upgrade his skills to the Gold level.
Half a month has passed; why is there still no news from the Star Martial Hall?
Wang Lan took out his phone and logged into the Star Martial Hall’s online store. In the Star Martial Skill section, only a few B-grade Star Martial Skills were listed; there wasn’t a single A-grade Star Martial Skill in sight.
Wang Lan, who had skill points, could indeed upgrade lower-level Star Martial Skills to higher levels, but their growth potential was too low. Take the E-grade Star Martial Skill he currently mastered, electrical energy output; upgrading it to Bronze still kept it as, frustratingly, electrical energy output—it merely multiplied the amount of electricity produced several times over.
What’s the use of that? Even if upgraded to the Gold level, it would probably only be able to maintain the power supply for a small residential area. A human power generator? Though, to say it’s entirely useless wouldn’t be quite accurate either. At least this Star Martial Skill has one ultimate move: Electrical Energy Self-Destruction. Hmm, instantly gather and expand the voltage within the body, then detonate it. The higher the Cultivation Level, the greater the explosive power. Damn it, I’m not Deidara; art isn’t about self-destruction!
"Assisted in the annihilation of a cross-border Star Martial drug trafficking criminal group. Reward: twenty thousand experience points, eight hundred skill points."
Suddenly, a notification chimed in Wang Lan’s mind, nearly startling him into dropping his phone. This alert left Wang Lan completely baffled.
What the hell did I do?
Upgrading from Star Shine Stage Eight to Star Shine Stage Nine required eighty thousand experience points. He had originally been seventy-odd percent of the way there; this reward had suddenly pushed his progress to over ninety percent.
Seeing this progress bar, Wang Lan was both overjoyed and incredulous.
I assisted? When did I assist?
Hurriedly, Wang Lan logged into the Tianjian Bureau’s official website and navigated to the Intelligence Department’s page.
Sure enough, a new announcement had appeared in the Intelligence Department section; it could be considered good news.
The Tianjian Bureau headquarters in Jin City, acting on information regarding drug traffickers apprehended by the Suzhou City authorities, had followed the clues. After a month and a half of planning, they successfully conducted a raid, dismantling a drug trafficking network that spanned nearly three provinces and seventeen cities. They arrested thirty-two Star Martial Warrior drug traffickers and an additional one hundred and twelve ordinary traffickers.
It seems Ye Feng’s team was just a small part of the entire organization.
This was a major case, one that had sparked nationwide vigilance. This was because the drug trafficking group was led by Star Martial Warriors, something unprecedented. The state’s control over Star Martial Warriors was very strict. Unless a Star Martial Warrior had never been registered in the first place, it was difficult for them to evade surveillance and engage in criminal activities. However, in recent years, there had been multiple reported instances across the country of Star Martial Warriors slipping from state control.
After understanding the full story, Wang Lan contentedly accepted the reward. He wasn’t concerned about what future policies the country might implement regarding the management of Star Martial Warriors. That wasn’t something he needed to consider right now. What he needed to think about was whether his next breakthrough, to Star Shine Stage Nine, was imminent.
He was still short over ninety thousand experience points. The alluring Star Cloud Stage was right before him, beckoning invitingly.
How he longed to conquer it.
「March 15th, clear skies.」
The temperature today was another five degrees Celsius higher than yesterday.
Wang Lan left his house with his schoolbag. Perhaps because it was gradually getting warmer, he saw many stylish city women with extraordinary resistance to cold already shedding their long coats, donning the short skirts commonly seen in summer.
Is it nearing that time of year again for crowded buses and people squatting at bus platforms?
Wang Lan glanced at a bus so crammed its windows seemed almost deformed from the overcrowding, then decisively turned and started walking to school.
Wang Lan lived only one and a half kilometers from the school, his route taking him through the Star Sea Community Park.
There was still an hour before school started, so he had plenty of time. Wang Lan walked at a leisurely pace, occasionally overhearing the cheerful laughter and chatter of other students also walking to school.
Suddenly, Wang Lan stopped in his tracks. At the entrance to the forest park, three police cars were parked, and the periphery of the park had been cordoned off with police tape.
Outside the tape, a dozen or so elderly men, likely out for their early morning exercises, were passionately debating something, spittle flying.
Has there been a crime?
Wang Lan thought, about to continue on his way to school, when he paused again.
"It seems a senior student from Suzhou No.1 Middle School died; they were wearing the school uniform."
"What was a kid from Suzhou No.1 Middle School doing here in the middle of the night instead of being at home?"
"Who knows? The police are already here. We’ll just have to wait for the detectives to solve the case."
A senior from Suzhou No.1 Middle School. Wang Lan knew almost all of them, whether from the regular community or the Star Martial Arts Campus. Even if he couldn’t recall all their names, he would recognize their faces.
Wang Lan turned, his figure flashing past the police tape as he moved towards the interior of the park.

chapters.title: Chapter 179: It Can’t Be Me
chapters.content:
Chapter 179: Chapter 179: It Can’t Be Me
"The victim was seventeen years old, a senior at Suzhou No.1 Middle School. The time of death was between eleven and twelve o’clock last night. The fatal wound was a penetrating chest wound, with the entry and exit wounds being roughly the same size; it doesn’t look like a gunshot wound," a guard quietly said to the plainclothes leader.
"Look around. Are there any other clues?"
"Captain Zhou, we found something. The student might have been a Star Martial Warrior. We discovered scratch marks on the climbing wall. This kid must have been training here last night. He was attacked from behind and then fell into the pool."
"Could it be a student from the Star Martial Arts Campus of Suzhou No.1 Middle School?"
"Yes!" As soon as Captain Zhou’s question landed, Wang Lan’s deep voice rose. When Wang Lan arrived at the scene, he recognized the deceased’s identity the moment he saw the face revealed under the white cloth.
Xu Donghai, a senior in Class Eight, was also one of the Twelve Vajra of the Commoner Genius Association, with a cultivation level at the peak of the Star Shine Stage. Wang Lan had paid attention to Xu Donghai’s two rounds of duels yesterday; his fundamental skills were very solid.
Although he couldn’t possibly be a strong rival for Wang Lan, he was still worthy of Wang Lan saying, "Not bad."
Yesterday, Xu Donghai successfully made it into the third round. It was unexpected that he would die here before the third round, where twenty contestants would be narrowed down to ten, even began.
"Who are you? How did you get in here?" The first thing Captain Zhou thought of when he saw Wang Lan was not to ask about Xu Donghai’s identity but to rebuke Wang Lan for crossing the police cordon to the scene.
"This person is my classmate, Xu Donghai, a senior in Class Eight at the Star Martial Arts Campus of Suzhou No.1 Middle School."
"Am I asking you if you recognize the victim right now? I’m asking who you are. What are you here for?"
"I was on my way to school, passing through..."
"Wang Lan, why are you here?" A voice interrupted Wang Lan. Turning around, he saw Hu Qing approaching quickly with three other people.
"Inspector Hu, why have you come?"
"I heard in the report that the victim’s identity was not simple, being a student from Suzhou No.1 Middle School. The bureau chief sent me to take over the case," Hu Qing said while offering a cigarette to Captain Zhou.
The murder of a high school student would have a significant impact on society and would certainly attract attention from all parties. And now, if it was a Star Martial High School student, the impact would be even greater.
In terms of seniority, Hu Qing couldn’t compare to Captain Zhou, but in terms of rank, Hu Qing was one level higher. The Hei case last time had led to another promotion for Hu Qing. Promotion speeds for regular police officers were much faster than for those in the Tianjian Bureau. Of course, the benefits and compensation also differed.
Hearing that Hu Qing would take over the case, Captain Zhou’s face darkened slightly, but he didn’t have an extreme reaction; instead, he gave Hu Qing a deep look.
"Since it involves a Star Martial Warrior, it’s appropriate for Inspector Hu to take over. But Inspector Hu, you seem quite familiar with this student?"
"Correct. He’s my friend and also a student from the Star Martial Arts Campus of Suzhou No.1 Middle School."
Although Wang Lan had openly shown his Tianjian Bureau ID at the police station last time, Captain Zhou had been on vacation and didn’t know about it. Even after hearing about it later, he treated it as just a story and didn’t know what Wang Lan looked like.
Hu Qing also refrained from spreading Wang Lan’s Tianjian Bureau identity unless necessary, so when introducing him, he didn’t include the title "elite Heavenly Sword Captain from Suzhou City."
"Then Captain Hu may need to recuse himself due to a conflict of interest."
Upon hearing this, Hu Qing’s expression changed instantly. Wang Lan’s face, however, showed no embarrassment or annoyance; rather, he looked at Captain Zhou with curiosity.
"Is this officer suspecting me?"
"You are one of my suspects right now."
"For what reason?"
"The reason is that your appearance here is highly irregular. As a student, you shouldn’t have come. Moreover, as a student, when you saw the body, you didn’t show any sign of panic."
"As a student, even if you are a Star Martial Art student, your demeanor is too composed, too calm, too mature. This isn’t how a sixteen or seventeen-year-old student should behave."
"Unless... you’ve rehearsed all this, or you’ve undergone professional training. Either way, I should suspect you."
"Wang Lan couldn’t possibly be the killer!" Hu Qing exclaimed, hastily shaking his head.
"Inspector Hu, when we police officers handle cases, we must avoid letting emotions influence our judgment. I know you Star Martial Warriors have so-called brotherhood obligations, but the suspicion surrounding this student cannot be overlooked."
"Captain Zhou, the information has been collected and sent to your phone," a bespectacled female guard carrying a notebook hurried over and said in a low voice.
"Inspector Hu, this is Duoduo, a top network security expert from Jade Country and a world-class hacker," Captain Zhou introduced her to Hu Qing.
"Inspector Hu, I’ve long admired your reputation but never had the opportunity to meet." Duoduo smiled warmly and extended her hand.
"Pleased to meet you."
DING DONG—
Wang Lan’s phone chimed with a notification. He casually picked it up; a push message read, "Wang Lan, a bad person tried to hack in just now, but I chased them away. Did I do well?" followed by an emoji of a well-behaved dog.
Unsurprisingly, the one trying to hack in was probably this intelligent-looking beauty right before him.
Captain Zhou quickly scrolled through his phone, and soon, a smile spread across his face.
"It seems my suspicions are becoming more precise..." Captain Zhou held the phone up to Hu Qing. "You’re Wang Lan, right? A senior from Class One at Suzhou No.1 Middle School’s Star Martial Arts Campus. And this is Xu Donghai, a student from Class Eight."
"I believe I already mentioned that," Wang Lan said, somewhat speechless.
Does Captain Zhou only hear what he wants to hear? Or was I not clear enough earlier?
"But you didn’t mention that your school is currently holding city-level selections for the provincial martial arts competition. Both you and this Xu Donghai successfully advanced to the third round, the final ’twenty-into-ten’ contest."
"Xu Donghai might have faced you this morning. To ensure victory and advance, you had every motive to commit murder."
"You live in the Xinyu Building, right? The Xinyu Building is less than a kilometer from Star Sea Park, which is within your usual range of activity. This morning, we came here to investigate because we received a report from someone."
"The person who reported it is very suspicious. They used a public phone to call the police station and used a voice changer. However, voice spectrum analysis suggests this person is between sixteen and eighteen years old."
"I believe the person who reported the crime is a prime suspect. And you arrived at the scene very quickly. Are these not enough reasons to suspect you?" Captain Zhou looked at Wang Lan with sharp eyes, a slight smirk playing on his lips.
"It’s not just those." Duoduo suddenly interjected from the side, opening her notebook and playing a video file.
The video showed the scene where Wang Lan had thwarted the Six Maniacs of the Flower Snake, flipping an armored transport vehicle with a single Crescent Arrow.
"Captain Zhou, Inspector Hu, the fatal penetrating wound on the victim wasn’t caused by a bullet, so I suspected an arrow-like weapon. However, an ordinary arrow wouldn’t typically have the force to inflict such damage."
"But this video gave us another important clue. To be able to penetrate the victim and then leave a twenty-centimeter-deep hole in the rock... your Star Martial Skill fits that profile perfectly..."
As Duoduo finished speaking, not only did Captain Zhou look mockingly at Wang Lan, but Hu Qing also eyed him with suspicion. However, Hu Qing’s gaze wasn’t one of doubt but of inquiry, asking if Wang Lan had an alibi.
Wang Lan stroked his chin and nodded.
It seems the killer knows me... If all the other factors are coincidences, then the wound on Xu Donghai really does resemble one inflicted by a Crescent Arrow.
"However... Captain Zhou, have you noticed Xu Donghai’s socks?"
"Socks?" Captain Zhou hurriedly looked at the victim’s exposed foot. Between Xu Donghai’s sock and shoe, there was a patch of green.
Captain Zhou quickly took a pair of tweezers and extracted the green item—it was a leaf.
"This is a four-leaf clover. Four-leaf clovers symbolize luck, and they aren’t found just anywhere. Although Star Sea Park’s landscaping is well-done, I don’t recall any four-leaf clovers there, at least not in the area where the victim died."
"This suggests that the primary crime scene may not be here. If there are no four-leaf clovers throughout Star Sea Park, then the initial place of death might not even be Star Sea Park."
"Second, it is true that our school’s internal selections are this morning. But the theory that I had a motive for murder because I was worried he would become my competitor is entirely baseless."
"He could never be my competitor. I could beat him with one hand tied behind my back. Defeating him would be a piece of cake! Brother Hu, it seems the Tianjian Bureau needs to get involved in this case."
"Mm, I will contact the Tianjian Bureau," Hu Qing agreed.
Wang Lan nodded and turned to leave.
"Stop right there!" Captain Zhou suddenly barked. "Even if you have reasons to refute my logic, you must cooperate with the police investigation until your suspicion has been completely ruled out. Therefore, you cannot leave."
"Captain Zhou, have you considered that this might be precisely the killer’s objective?" Wang Lan asked, turning his head slightly with a smile.
"What do you mean?"
"If this isn’t the primary crime scene, why would the killer move the body to Star Sea Park, less than a kilometer from my home, and stage the scene here?"
"Many elderly people exercise in Star Sea Park every morning; discovering a body wouldn’t be difficult. But why would the murderer make that call to report it? Isn’t that deliberately exposing information?"
"Isn’t the murderer’s goal to deliberately provide criteria to narrow down the suspects—an age between sixteen and eighteen? Coupled with that fatal wound, so similar to my Crescent Arrow. Isn’t the murderer’s intent to frame me?"
"Moreover, Star Sea Park is on my daily route to school. With your investigation underway while I’m on my way, I would very likely come over out of curiosity, thus falling right into your sights. This way, I would be delayed and miss today’s selections."
"By holding me back for just one day, the killer achieves their goal."
"The killer planned this meticulously, but unfortunately, they overlooked one detail."
"What?"
"I am not just an ordinary high school student," Wang Lan stated slowly, his expression indifferent, uttering a remarkably dramatic phrase.
Catching Wang Lan’s hint, Hu Qing stepped forward with a faint smile to stand before Captain Zhou. "Captain Zhou, my certainty that Wang Lan couldn’t be the murderer isn’t based on personal feelings, but because it’s genuinely impossible for it to be him. Beyond being a senior at the Star Martial Arts Campus, he is also a Captain and an elite special agent of the Suzhou City Tianjian Bureau."
Captain Zhou’s expression changed instantly. He stared at Wang Lan, dumbfounded, and took a deep breath.
"No way! The Tianjian Bureau? And a Captain?"
"I can tell you responsibly, yes, he is."
This was a classic case of being outranked, and Captain Zhou couldn’t help but feel completely overwhelmed by the sheer disparity.

chapters.title: Chapter 180: Only Those Who Have Eaten Know
chapters.content:
Chapter 180: Chapter 180: Only Those Who Have Eaten Know
On the sports field of the Star Martial Arts Campus, the artistic performances on stage were even more spectacular and appealing than yesterday, with the audience in the bleachers periodically letting out bursts of screams. These students were no strangers to live performances, having frequented them regularly.
In a corner of the bleachers, in the preparation area for the third round of the top twenty competitors, Jiang Xinyu slightly furrowed her brows as she put down her phone, her fingers pressing hard against the phone screen.
"Not answering calls, not answering calls... How can he not answer calls at a time like this? Could something have happened?"
"How could it?" Xu Xiangwen immediately shook his head in denial. "Xinyu, stop worrying needlessly. Have you forgotten that Lanzi has the Phoenix Form? Even if he encountered some trouble, he wouldn’t be in danger. Maybe... he was too excited after yesterday’s victory, couldn’t sleep at night, and overslept this morning."
"Did you oversleep?" Jiang Xinyu looked at Xu Xiangwen coldly.
"No, I got up at five o’clock."
"If even you didn’t oversleep, how could Wang Lan possibly oversleep? Since the first grade of elementary school, Wang Lan has always arrived at school half an hour early, never once being late."
Jiang Xinyu’s words caused Xu Xiangwen’s expression to change. Wang Lan’s steady-as-a-rock pattern meant the chances of a mishap were incredibly slim, especially on such an important day. There was no reason for him to be late.
Could something really have happened?
In the preparation area sat the twenty contestants scheduled to compete today. However, apart from Wang Lan, whose absence worried Jiang Xinyu, Xu Donghai’s no-show seemed to garner little attention.
"Ziqi, the call isn’t going through!" Shui Miao whispered into Duan Ziqi’s ear.
"Whose call isn’t going through?"
"Donghai’s. He hasn’t shown up yet, and it’s not that no one is answering his phone; it’s out of the service area..."
"Didn’t he leave the club a week ago? Once he left, he was no longer our brother, so why bother about him?"
"After all, we were brothers for three years. Is our bond just gone like that?" Shui Miao frowned slightly, seemingly dissatisfied with Duan Ziqi’s lack of sentimentality.
"Bond? Once camaraderie is gone, so is the bond. Have you forgotten what he said before leaving the club? That he achieved his current success entirely through his own efforts, and that it had nothing to do with the club?
"The club’s mission is to enable us, through hard work, to catch up with those students from wealthy families who have abundant resources. Working hard is natural; without it, you’re just a salted fish.
"But without the jobs I found for him, could he have made a million or two in a year? Could he have afforded a Soul Bead? Would his hard work have meant anything without the club’s support? Now that graduation is on the horizon, he’s thinking of going solo? Does a thankless wretch like that deserve to be our brother?"
Shui Miao sighed softly and slowly set down his phone.
At that moment, Liu Jie, carrying a list of names, approached with a swaggering gait.
Since yesterday, Liu Jie’s walk had become incredibly cocky. After two rounds, his class boasted seven students in the top twenty of the grade—a staggering statistic. Considering there were ten classes in the senior year, his Class One stood out as the sole luminary.
Although Class One had always been the most outstanding, class assignments usually aimed for balance, with Class One only slightly outperforming the others. Yet, Liu Jie took great personal credit for transforming a slightly leading class into a lone standout.
Thus, when the dust settled on the second round yesterday, Liu Jie’s gait had become noticeably more buoyant, causing the Star Martial Art teachers of other classes to look on with teeth-gritting envy.
"Are all twenty contestants for the third round here?" Liu Jie glanced around casually as he spoke.
In his mind, it was a rhetorical question.
Who would be late for such a crucial third preliminary round? If he’d had such an opportunity twenty or thirty years ago, he would have arrived on time even if it meant staying up all night.
But as his eyes swept over the area, his heart suddenly skipped a beat.
His gaze swept back again.
Two missing? In fact, in that instant, Liu Jie had already identified which two.
"Wang Lan, Donghai! Where are they? Did they go to the restroom?"
"Teacher, I’m here!" a voice rang out. Instantly, Wang Lan’s figure appeared beside Liu Jie like a fleeting shadow. "Sorry, I’m late."
"What’s going on? Why are you only arriving now? The competition is about to start; take your seat. And what about Donghai? Hasn’t he arrived yet? Ziqi, do you have Donghai’s phone number? Call him and ask what he’s up to. There are only five minutes left; if he doesn’t make it before the competition starts, he’ll have to forfeit."
"We just tried calling. Donghai’s phone is out of service. We don’t know what happened to him either."
"Is that so? I’ll go report it upstairs. Anyone who needs to use the restroom, do it quickly. The first match is starting soon, and no one knows who will be facing whom."
Having said that, Liu Jie walked away, whistling, with one hand in his pocket.
Is he really that pragmatic?
one student thought.
When Wang Lan hadn’t arrived, Instructor Liu Jie looked like he was ready to eat someone. But now that Donghai hasn’t shown up, he just casually reports it?
He’s not his kid, so why should he care?
another mused.
"Hey, Duan Ziqi, are you guys in the Commoner Genius Association always this heartless?" a scion of a wealthy family from the back row asked jokingly, crossing his arms.
For three years, the scions of wealthy families had been consistently overshadowed by the Commoner Genius Association. It wasn’t that the wealthy children didn’t compete; it was just that they were outnumbered by the sheer volume of commoner students. With fewer numbers, the wealthy children couldn’t match up.
Using their families’ power was out of the question, primarily because their parents wouldn’t allow it. So, for the past three years, the wealthy young scions had adopted a cold-shoulder approach. You can say what you want; I’ll just treat it as hot air.
In yesterday’s battle, only three of the Twelve Vajra had advanced, one of whom was Duan Ziqi, consistently in the top three of their year. The three-year myth of the Commoner Genius Association had turned into a joke overnight. This gave the elite scions a sense of delightful vindication, as if a great weight had been lifted after five hundred years of suppression.
With such a good opportunity, they naturally took every chance to mock them mercilessly.
Duan Ziqi turned around coldly. A piercingly cold gaze shot from his eyes, and his potent aura surged like a flash flood toward the student who had spoken.
"Pray you don’t draw me in the upcoming battle... Otherwise, I’ll show you what a real joke is."
