Zhang Yu’s form instantly streaked past four afterimages, flashing four times. He had already moved away before the explosions from the lightning afterimages even had a chance to erupt.
You want to wear me down? Then I’ll do the same.
At the Tianjian Bureau, a group of executives sat quietly in the conference room watching the live broadcast after their meeting. Eld Di watched the screen intently alongside Lu Zhao. Suddenly, Lu Zhao turned to Wang Qianfeng with a confused expression.
"Is Wang Lan’s Star Power exceptionally robust? You never mentioned to me that Wang Lan had such an overwhelming advantage with his Star Power."
They were all colleagues in the office, so there was no need for pretense.
"Wang Lan’s Star Power level, when tested, was normal; it wasn’t exceptionally abundant. Could it be... has his body undergone some kind of mutation recently?"
"Mutation?" Eld Di frowned. "Has Wang Lan’s body undergone mutations before?"
"No... not at all..." Wang Qianfeng blurted out, then immediately corrected himself, realizing his mistake.
"It’s just this guy Wang Lan; impossible things always seem to happen with him. For instance, the Phoenix Form, which cannot be learned below the Galaxy Stage, he somehow managed to learn it. Also, despite having no Thunder Attribute talent, he was able to learn Thunder Attribute Star Martial Skills."
"Then, when he was retested after learning Thunder Attribute Star Martial Skills, he suddenly possessed Thunder Attribute talent! We joked, if that’s not a mutation, what is?"
"Heh... so there’s that too. But Wang Lan’s Star Power isn’t robust; it’s just that he has learned the Solar Seal technique," Eld Di chuckled, then sighed softly to himself,
Truly worthy of someone with half-Spirit Realm bloodline.
Zhang Yu once again slashed through the void, breaking through Wang Lan’s remaining two afterimages. By now, Wang Lan had been pushed to the edge of the arena. Blocked by Zhang Yu’s sharp presence in front and limited by the edge of the field behind, Wang Lan had no choice but to go all out.
Just as Zhang Yu’s knife was about to sweep past Wang Lan’s throat, Wang Lan suddenly disappeared.
In that split second, Zhang Yu’s expression changed. He had assumed Wang Lan couldn’t use Phantom Tracer because he hadn’t employed it yet. But the instant Wang Lan activated it, Zhang Yu sensed it.
Ghost Wail pierced the void, thrusting towards Zhang Yu’s waist. In this critical moment, Zhang Yu, unable to think, vanished in a flash.
The instant Zhang Yu disappeared, so did Wang Lan.
This scene puzzled many viewers; expressions of shock and disbelief spread across countless faces. However, Ni Yushu, the coach of the Jin City team, suddenly stood up, his face full of astonishment as he watched the flickering scene before him.
He learned it? He only spent one night? No, this very night he was embroiled in a murder scandal; he practically had no time at all!
How is that possible?
Since when could Phantom Tracer be learned so casually? One night? Are you joking? Could you even fully grasp the cultivation method in one night?
Zhang Yu had one more flash left, while Wang Lan had two. This was Wang Lan’s plan.
When Zhang Yu reappeared, Wang Lan was like a shadow. Faced with Wang Lan’s sword, Zhang Yu had no escape. Clenching his teeth, he blocked with his knife. But the slash Wang Lan brought down was merely an afterimage. Or rather, what Zhang Yu saw was just an illusion.
The next instant, Wang Lan’s Ghost Wail landed on Zhang Yu’s shoulder. Wang Lan himself was just behind him, less than five centimeters away.
"You lost..."

chapters.title: Chapter 234: Breakthrough to the Star Cloud Stage
chapters.content:
Chapter 234: Chapter 234: Breakthrough to the Star Cloud Stage
"How could you... how could you know Phantom Tracer?" Zhang Yu’s expression kept changing before he finally managed to ask with difficulty.
"Is it that hard to understand that I know Phantom Tracer?"
"Phantom Tracer is a secret technique of the Jin City Star Martial Academy, and you’re a student from Suzhou City... Yesterday, Xu Ruo was severely injured, and even the two masters from the Medical Attribute couldn’t heal her. But last night, she suddenly recovered. Could it be... could it be that she made a deal with you?"
Wang Lan’s brow furrowed slightly.
I have to admit, their deal was aboveboard, and Ni Yushu actively sought the exchange. How could it possibly be pinned on me?
Seeing the look of utter frustration on Zhang Yu’s face, a slight smile tugged at the corners of Wang Lan’s lips.
"What era is this that we still keep unshareable secrets? The very existence of academies is to teach Star Martial Skills. If there really are secrets that cannot be passed on, then we might as well not have Star Martial Academies at all. The country has repeatedly emphasized promoting the circulation of Star Martial Skills. Star Martial Skills have no ownership. Talking about undisclosed secrets of the Jin City Star Martial Academy, aren’t you afraid of being laughed at?"
"And even if I did make a deal last night, could I really demonstrate proficiency second only to yours today? Have you ever considered how much time it took you to practice to your current level?"
Wang Lan’s words immediately dispelled Zhang Yu’s suspicions. It wasn’t that he had much faith in Wang Lan’s character; an A-grade Star Martial Skill isn’t that easy to master. He vividly remembered all the hardship he had endured to learn Phantom Tracer.
But...
"While that may be true, Star Martial Academies keep certain Star Martial Skills under wraps to maintain their core competitive edge. Otherwise, the Dragon Emperor Form from the Modu City Star Martial Academy would have become commonplace long ago. You’re right. I lost, and I am fully convinced by my loss.
I dedicated almost all my time to mastering Phantom Tracer for the past three years. This Star Martial Skill has indeed not disappointed me; I have sparred countless times over these three years and seldom tasted defeat.
It is precisely because I know how difficult it is to master Phantom Tracer that I am convinced by you. You have practiced so many Star Martial Skills to an advanced level and still managed to master Phantom Tracer to this extent.
In terms of talent and effort, I may not compare to you. So, I admit defeat."
"BEEP—"
"Wang Lan is the winner—"
"Congratulations, Host, for completing the fourth round of the provincial martial competition and being the first to enter the top eight. Reward: eight thousand experience points, eight hundred skill points—"
A voice like heavenly music resounded in his mind, and suddenly, a warm current flowed through his body. Just as Wang Lan was about to turn around, his body abruptly paused. Panicked, he sank his mind into his Spiritual Sea of Consciousness.
It had been a long time since he had checked the system. He knew only that he wasn’t far from the Star Cloud Stage, but because he had been so busy these past few days, Wang Lan hadn’t paid much attention to the specifics.
When the system interface appeared before his eyes, the experience value for Star Shine 9 had already maxed out. Instantly, it was as if a wheel of fireworks rose on the system display.
Both of them, though leaving the ring, instinctively paused. Wang Lan sensed he was about to break through, while Zhang Yu sensed Wang Lan seemed to be breaking through.
"Do you two students still have any doubts?" The refereeing teacher strode over, but just as he neared, the Spirit Power Fluctuations from Wang Lan surged like waves, sweeping over him layer by layer.
Zhang Yu whipped his head around, his expression as horrified as if he had seen a ghost.
"CRAP—" Xu Xiangwen abruptly stood up.
This scene was all too familiar. This wasn’t the first time Wang Lan had pulled such a stunt. Even without sensing the Star Energy Fluctuation, Xu Xiangwen had already guessed what Wang Lan was up to.
"Wang Lan, he is..." Jiang Xinyu hesitated slightly. Although she had a guess in her heart, her expression was one of disbelief. "He broke through? Impossible! Didn’t he just finish a fight?"
"That damn Lanzi! Breaking through after a battle isn’t his first time. Remember the Star Martial Conquest? It was the same thing... Wait, Lanzi is already at the peak of Star Shine, right?"
"You mean... he’s about to break through to the Star Cloud Stage?"
More and more people in the stands realized what Wang Lan was doing. Such an absurd event was actually happening?
Shouldn’t this only be a plotline in TV dramas?
The teachers in charge of observation stood up in unison. Then, under the visible Spirit Power Fluctuations surrounding Wang Lan, many students realized he was breaking through.
"What... what a joke! Breaking through after a battle? How can he ensure that his Star Palace is filled with overflowing Star Power? Don’t tell me his Star Power actually increases the more he uses it!"
"I now have reason to suspect this guy secretly popped Soul Beads during the competition."
"Are you stupid? Setting aside whether Zhang Yu would have noticed him popping Soul Beads, even if he wasn’t discovered, did you see the intensity of the battle just now? Did he even have a chance to pop Soul Beads?"
"Then explain to me, what is going on here? This definitely defies common sense! The ancestors must be rolling in their graves!"
Compared to the live audience who couldn’t accept Wang Lan breaking through after the battle, the online acceptance was much higher. This wasn’t the first time, after all; there was nothing surprising about it.
"Same familiar scene, same familiar recipe."
"What do you think the reason for his breakthrough this time is? Excitement from winning?"
"Isn’t that it? It was like that last time. He broke through in his excitement, and it ended with dozens of contestants backstage ganging up on him."
"Could Wang Lan be cheating? Secretly popping pills?"
"To the sourpuss upstairs: Our Wolf King has a history of breaking through like this."
"Not the first time. Get used to it..."
BOOM—
Suddenly, the Spiritual Power surrounding Wang Lan transformed into bright red flames that swept out in all directions. The heatwave turned into a hurricane, causing a surge of wind throughout the entire gymnasium.
In an instant, the system interface update was complete, and new data displayed before Wang Lan’s eyes:
Character: Wang Lan
Level: Star Cloud Stage LV1
To the left of the character, the red and blue bars instantly lengthened and widened.
The changes in the data were just numbers, but the changes Wang Lan personally felt were the most real. His strength, neural reflexes, and physical toughness had all been massively enhanced. The most noticeable change was in his Star Power, which had expanded explosively. What had been mere warm currents of Star Power now felt as though it had solidified into substance.
The density of his Star Power had increased by at least five times. If he were to engage in another battle of the same intensity, Wang Lan wouldn’t even need to use his stored, sealed Star Power; he could face Zhang Yu head-on.
After the breakthrough was complete, Wang Lan’s aura returned to normal.
He walked toward the stands with an arrogant swagger, his every move followed by countless gazes locked on him until he settled quietly back into his seat.
"You broke through?"
"Mm," Wang Lan replied, his voice flat.
"Star Cloud Stage?"
"Yeah."
SLAP—
Xu Xiangwen slapped Wang Lan on the back of the head. Wang Lan looked up and saw Xu Xiangwen’s eyes, red as a rabbit’s, with veins faintly twitching at his temples.
"Lanzi, this is a breakthrough! Why do you look so dissatisfied? You look like you’re at a funeral!"
"A breakthrough is just a breakthrough. It’s not the first time, nothing to fuss over."
Xu Xiangwen couldn’t stand this response. He shot up, teeth bared, but Gong Feiyu immediately restrained him, advising, "This is just Lanzi’s usual act to show off. Don’t fall for it. Stay cool."
Clenching his teeth, Xu Xiangwen found Wang Lan’s smirk unbearable.
I really want to stomp a footprint right on his face!
The next match officially began, and everyone’s attention shifted to it. Meanwhile, Wang Lan immersed his mind in his Spiritual Sea of Consciousness.
I’m so busy now. Busy with what? So many Star Martial Skills are waiting to be upgraded to Gold-level!
All of his Star Martial Skills, except for Phantom Tracer at Silver 7, were at Silver 9.
With such high levels, it would be a waste not to upgrade them all to Gold.
Having just earned eight hundred skill points, the now-wealthy Wang Lan naturally went,
Tap, tap, tap.
Star Cloud Sword Dance, add one point.
In an instant, the silver-white skill icon turned gold as if by alchemy. At that moment, a tumultuous pain, like a raging river, pierced Wang Lan’s mind.
The Gold-level Star Cloud Sword Dance brought a sparkle to Wang Lan’s eyes.
Previously, I could only create a dozen afterimages. Now that it’s Gold-level, the number has instantly increased to a flurry, like that side-stepping technique. Even though I haven’t executed it yet, I guarantee it’s enough to scare someone to death!
If Star Cloud Sword Dance has become so mighty, what about Flame Sword?
Upon activating Flame Sword, Wang Lan’s perception changed. The thrill of that moment nearly caused his aura to flare out of control.
"Just now... did I suddenly feel a sense of... danger?" Xu Xiangwen, sitting next to Wang Lan, asked hesitantly, glancing surreptitiously at him.
"That’s definitely your imagination," Wang Lan said, lifting his head and offering a harmless smile.
Flame Sword, Gold-level. It’s no longer just an enhancement of the flame’s temperature, but an improvement in flame control. Previously, though Flame Sword had many variations, like vertical and horizontal slashes, it couldn’t be detached from my hands.
Just like a normal Wind Release: Rasengan.
But once upgraded to Gold-level, Flame Sword can be thrown! That’s formidable. Flame Sword has no fixed shape and can morph into any form of sharp blade. Could I possibly shape it into flame shuriken?
This idea crossed his mind, and Wang Lan was so excited he wished he could go onto the field and try it immediately.
Now that Star Cloud Sword Dance and Flame Sword are Gold-level, Thunder Snake and Crescent Arrow naturally can’t be left behind. However, Crescent Arrow wasn’t at Silver 9.99, so upgrading these two to Gold cost me two hundred skill points.
Then, I also upgraded Basic Combat, Basic Body Skill, Basic Sword Skill, Basic Swordsmanship, and the most important Inch Strength Fist, all to Gold-level.
After this massive skill upgrade, Wang Lan didn’t know how much stronger he had become.
But I’m sure of one thing: I could beat ten of my former selves now!
Anyway, bragging isn’t illegal.
"Wang Lan, still daydreaming? It’s noon. Let’s go eat."
"Oh..."
After Wang Lan upgraded Phantom Tracer to Gold-level, he was left with one hundred skill points.
But in the future, skills won’t be so easy to upgrade. When a skill reaches Gold-level, each subsequent level will require one thousand skill points, making it ten thousand points to get a single skill from Gold to Platinum. Even focusing on my main Star Martial Skills won’t be enough. It’s time to give up on the Basic Skills.

chapters.title: Chapter 235 The Crow’s Mouth is the Most Effective
chapters.content:
Chapter 235: Chapter 235 The Crow’s Mouth is the Most Effective
After finishing the meal, Wang Lan upgraded Phantom Tracer to Gold level. In that moment, Wang Lan truly felt like she’d traded a peashooter for a cannon.
It was now Jiang Xinyu’s turn to take the stage. Xu Ruo and Jiang Xinyu seemed like fated opposites, almost mirror images of each other. Jiang Xinyu’s Ice Attribute was perfectly countered by Xu Ruo’s Flame Attribute. Coincidentally, their fighting styles and combat philosophies were also strikingly similar.
From beginning to end, Jiang Xinyu struggled to break free from the disadvantage of elemental suppression. Xu Ruo, naturally, would not let Jiang Xinyu succeed. They exchanged stratagems, both overt and covert, but ultimately, Jiang Xinyu could not defy destiny, and her Ice Attribute finally succumbed to the Flame Attribute.
Ice and Flame Attributes naturally counter each other, with the latter dominating the former in the early stages. However, this situation can change in the later stages. If an Ice Attribute Star Martial Warrior could comprehend Aurora, the tide would turn.
Aurora is the ultimate esoteric art of the Ice Attribute Star Martial Warriors, known as Rapid Freezing Light or sometimes Absolute Zero. An Ice Attribute Star Martial Warrior who has grasped Aurora is a nightmare on the battlefield, unmatched even by a Flame Attribute Star Martial Warrior who has mastered the Fusion Esoteric Art.
But now, Jiang Xinyu was still far from comprehending Aurora.
The fight was thoroughly exhilarating. Its flawless displays of brilliance and tactical deployment, from breadth to depth, left no room for criticism. Almost all the evaluating teachers nodded continuously in approval. Eventually, they both received an ’excellent’ rating.
This evaluation wasn’t from a semester-end report but a ranking among the one hundred thirty contestants in the Provincial Tournament. Even among the elite of the province, they were both exceptionally outstanding.
Jiang Xinyu returned to her seat, her expression calm.
"I’m sorry," Wang Lan said with deep remorse to Jiang Xinyu.
"You don’t need to apologize. Defeating Xu Ruo while she was injured would have been a disgrace to me. Knowing me as you do, do you think I would accept that? I’m happy to have had the chance to fight Xu Ruo with all my might."
"But... the Four Great Star Martial Academies."
"If the Four Great Academies are recruiting this year, the top three will definitely get in. But that doesn’t mean there’s no chance for those ranked lower. Besides, although I lost outside the top eight, I’m determined to take ninth place."
After hearing Jiang Xinyu’s words, Wang Lan finally felt at ease. She extended her hand and placed it on Jiang Xinyu’s injured shoulder to start healing her. After the Top Eight Championship Battle ended, if time allowed, the ninth to sixteenth place rankings would also be determined.
This duel would also be fiercely contested, as two top-ten positions were at stake.
After Jiang Xinyu’s defeat, the leaders from Suzhou No. 1 Middle School showed not a hint of regret on their faces. It wasn’t that they were indifferent to Jiang Xinyu; rather, they were already content with how far the Suzhou City team had come.
Even if all of Suzhou City’s participants were eliminated in the fourth round, they would have found it acceptable. Moreover, Wang Lan had already secured a spot in the top eight.
Reaching the top eight in the Provincial Tournament was a feat Suzhou City hadn’t achieved in a long time. In the past few tournaments, their best results were eleventh or twelfth. Those four major cities were simply too dominant, securing at least two spots in the top ten, sometimes three, almost monopolizing the top ranks. The fact that Wang Lan had managed to wrestle a top-eight spot from Zhang Yu made the Head of Academics swell with pride!
After Jiang Xinyu’s match concluded, it was showtime for the representatives of the Four Great Cities. It was a clash of titans, with each battle showcasing a quality no less than Wang Lan’s match.
Soon, the last competitor from Suzhou City, Mu Shaoyun, stepped onto the stage to face off against the team captain from Chang City.
Everyone thought it would be a battle between equals, but the outcome was unexpected. The team captain from Chang City had almost no chance to fight back against Mu Shaoyun. He was defeated even before he could demonstrate his real strength.
Having two advance to the top eight filled the Suzhou City officials with joy, kindling ambitions they hadn’t even dared to entertain before.
With two in the top eight, wasn’t aiming for one in the top four reasonable? And if one made the top four, wasn’t vying for champion or runner-up also possible? That seemed only fair...
After the fourth round of competition concluded, the battles for the ninth to sixteenth rankings followed immediately. All competitors in this ranking contest had already fought once today, and many carried injuries.
Even after treatment from healing-specialized Star Martial Warriors, their injuries hadn’t fully healed so quickly. It was easy to imagine the significant advantage Jiang Xinyu had, being completely healed by Wang Lan.
Almost effortlessly, she cut through her opponents like a hot knife through butter and clinched the coveted ninth position.
Making the top ten greatly increased their chances of being scouted by the Four Great Star Martial Academies.
The day’s competitions thus came to an end, and Wang Lan and the others gathered again in the penthouse suite to analyze the strengths of the top eight. Nearly all top-eight contestants had had their utmost limits revealed throughout these four rounds of combat.
However, one person remained an enigma.
"At this point, anyone could be an opponent. I don’t know much about Mu Shaoyun. You guys have interacted with him more, so what do you think?" Wang Lan asked, sprawled on the sofa.
"It doesn’t make sense! Mu Shaoyun is impressive, sure, but he shouldn’t be *this* dominant!" Xu Xiangwen was the first to exclaim in amazement.
"Like Xinyu, Mu Shaoyun awoke his Star Martial Warrior Inborn Talent at the age of eight. His Inborn Talent was a strange Devouring-type. It seems he can devour a person’s stamina. When he first awakened his talent, he hospitalized seven of his classmates.
The results of the medical examination showed they were all suffering from extreme exhaustion due to overexertion, and testimonies from the other students indicated that Mu Shaoyun only touched them. As a result, Mu Shaoyun was suspended from school for two months before returning. Since then, he never again displayed such power."
"What’s terrifying is that even up to now, Mu Shaoyun still hasn’t revealed that ability. If that incident hadn’t been officially recorded, we might have assumed Mu Shaoyun no longer possessed that Inborn Talent of the Bloodline.
This type of Inborn Talent of the Bloodline isn’t in the database, and as Mu Shaoyun isn’t from a Star Martial family, it’s unknown if he has even developed this Inborn Talent of the Bloodline. Leaving that aside, Mu Shaoyun’s strength remains unfathomable."
"To date, he has displayed Earth Attribute, Wind Attribute, Flame Attribute, and Water Attribute Star Martial Skills. This means he has at least four types of attribute talents."
"His close-quarters combat skills are practically perfect. However, I’ve sparred with him before, and his combat prowess was on par with mine," Jiang Xinyu said quietly.
"During this period of practicing combat through real battles, my combat prowess has at least doubled compared to before. I originally thought that I had far surpassed Mu Shaoyun. However, the combat ability he’s displaying now feels utterly unfathomable to me.
Either he has always been hiding his strength, or he’s had some fortuitous encounter that allowed him to progress much faster than me. Wang Lan, which do you think it is?"
"I’m thinking, how could someone possibly be such a genius? His talent is actually comparable to mine?"
This shameless remark instantly quieted the room.
"Regardless, Mu Shaoyun will be Lanzi’s most formidable rival. The only thing to hope for now is that the draw doesn’t pit you two against each other," Xu Xiangwen said.
"Wang Lan, I’ve been thinking, if Mu Shaoyun had always been this strong, why would he hide his true power during his three years at school?" Jiang Xinyu asked Wang Lan thoughtfully.
"This... might have something to do with his background," Wang Lan said uncertainly, stroking her chin. "His background isn’t particularly positive. Honestly, if it weren’t for the investigation proving Mu Shaoyun was innocent, he wouldn’t have been allowed to appear at the Provincial Tournament."
As everyone was discussing, the television began broadcasting the draw for the quarterfinal matches.
Of the remaining eight contestants, Jin City held three spots, Tong City two, Chang City one, and Suzhou City two. The first drawn match was an internal clash between two contestants from Jin City.
Jin City’s team captain, Xiao Zi, was pitted against Jin City’s Xu Ruo.
"How brutal!" Xu Xiangwen couldn’t help but sigh the moment the matchup appeared. Although internal battles were inevitable at this stage, Xu Ruo, who had just scraped a hard-won victory against Jiang Xinyu, hadn’t even had time to celebrate before having to face her own team captain.
Xiao Zi, the team captain from Jin City, possessed five Star Martial Attributes, and his Star Power was extraordinary. His Star Power wasn’t just exceptionally strong; it was on a whole different order of magnitude, almost inhumanly vast.
When he first awakened his Star Martial talent, the Star Power he unleashed nearly collapsed the classroom. After testing, its density reached the peak Star Shine Stage. When breaking through to the Star Shine Stage, his Star Power’s density already far surpassed the Star Cloud Stage.
If not for the fact that qualitative advancements in Star Martial levels can’t be offset by sheer quantity, Xiao Zi’s Star Power might be approaching the Star Sea Stage. This seemingly bottomless well of Star Power once led Xiao Zi to make a famous declaration:
"Don’t ask how much Star Power I have; I’ve never experienced the feeling of it running out. I, too, want to know my Star Power limit. But even when I faint from exhaustion, my Star Power still shows no sign of depletion."
What a monster. I have no intention of challenging his Star Power limits. Let Hu Feifei deal with that later.
Soon, the next group’s drawing began, and Mu Shaoyun’s portrait was the first to appear. The next second, the screen froze. Wang Lan was stunned. Then her eyes fixed on Xu Xiangwen, who was looking utterly bewildered beside her.
"This... this... it’s not my fault, right?"
"Oh, so it’s my fault now?" Wang Lan retorted irritably. "It’s that jinx mouth of yours!"
And when the second group’s match-up was drawn, it wasn’t just Wang Lan who had something to say; the internet absolutely exploded.
"Is this the top eight showdown? Might as well call it the Civil War Tournament! The first match: two from Jin City. The second match: two from Suzhou City. What’s next, the third match with two from Tong City?"
"’Do they have to be this brutal? I strongly suggest they split the groups! I want to see Xu Ru thrash the Suzhou City team!’"
"’Exactly! If they split them, our great Jin City will sweep the top three!’"
"’Who gave you the guts to make such shameless claims, risking your tongue? Xu Ruo thrash the Wolf King? You clearly don’t know how ferocious my Wolf Bro is!’"
"’Since his debut, Wolf Bro has been undefeated, unmatched!’"
"’That’s right! My Wolf Bro is at the Star Cloud Stage now! Back when he was at the Star Shine Stage, he thrashed a whole bunch of Star Cloud Stage cultivators. Now that he’s at the Star Cloud Stage, won’t he demolish anyone at the Galaxy Stage?’"
"’Hey, hey, snap out of it! That’s going way overboard!’"

chapters.title: Chapter 236: The Formidable Mu Shaoyun
chapters.content:
Chapter 236: Chapter 236: The Formidable Mu Shaoyun
Feel free to give any feedback; if they listen to even one word, consider it my loss. That was probably the organizers’ mindset. No matter how many netizens flooded the official website’s comment section, the organizers neither responded nor explained, simply pretending they hadn’t seen anything.
The difference between officialdom and commercial organizers was starkly evident here. The Provincial Martial Arts Tournament is an activity in the training process of Star Martial Warriors like us, not a commercial competition for public viewing. They don’t care about viewership ratings; watch it or not, it’s up to you.
After a night of commotion, those who needed to calm down eventually did. The remaining two groups did not put on the spectacle of a fight to the death.
The next morning, Wang Lan and his group arrived back at their stands and settled down. Seeing Mu Shaoyun again, they both could sense that the other’s aura had changed. Wang Lan’s change was due to a desire to perform strongly after his major upgrade. As for Mu Shaoyun, perhaps he felt threatened by Wang Lan.
Under the eager anticipation of the audience, the battle between Xiao Zi and Xu Ruo began. Xu Ruo’s Flame Attribute broad-range Star Martial Skill swept across the arena, giving everyone a taste of the desert’s scorching heat and the ruthless power of fire.
Even though Xu Ruo’s Star Martial Skill was overwhelmingly powerful, she met the man who completely countered her. Xiao Zi’s fighting style was like that of a refined gentleman, each move an exhibition of art.
While others treasured their Star Power as invaluable, rationing a single unit as if it were two, Xiao Zi generously unleashed his Star Power in torrents. Ever seen Water Surge?
Many students probably had; this Water Attribute B-grade Star Martial Skill was something many aspired to. The water flow not only attacked opponents but also added a layer of water wall defense for oneself, integrating offense and defense.
But in Xiao Zi’s hands, Water Surge felt like a galaxy pouring down, the ocean itself inverting. The relentless waves of the onslaught were so fierce they made people see the waves (làng) as wolves (láng)!
Xiao Zi stood at the crest of the waves, his palms moving lightly, and the seawater charged like a battalion of ten thousand horses.
Facing such overwhelming force, Xu Ruo could only raise her hands and surrender. Even if she had many powerful Flame Attribute Star Martial Skills left to use, like Scorching Steam, Intense Heat Ray, or Boiling Water Strangulation, what was the use? Useless!
Did she really need to push Xiao Zi to the point of using the Thundering Tsunami to hold her underwater before she would be satisfied? When Xiao Zi finally ceased his Star Martial Skill, the Earth Attribute Star Martial Warriors hurriedly diverted the massive amount of water into the artificial lake.
Just diverting the water and repairing the arena would take at least half an hour.
"Fighting Xiao Zi is a real headache," someone remarked.
"You better think about how you’re going to fight Mu Shaoyun," Jiang Xinyu said worriedly in a low voice. "You’re up soon. Are you confident?"
"Confidence is something I’ve never had in any fight. But didn’t I make it to the top eight? Even though Mu Shaoyun hasn’t yet met an opponent who can force out his full strength, I want to give it a try."
It didn’t feel like much rest had passed before the second match was announced. Wang Lan and Mu Shaoyun leisurely stood up and walked towards the arena. For the audience of Suzhou City, this match was both heart-wrenching and highly anticipated.
If one had to describe the mood of the Suzhou City audience at this moment, it would be like trying to eat three bowls of food while sobbing.
There were two competitors. One was their beloved Wolf King, who had never disappointed them. The other was Mu Shaoyun; his performance had been as steady as an old hand throughout, and he still exuded an unfathomable aura.
Either of them was a strong contender for the championship.
If the contestants of this Provincial Martial Arts Tournament were to be graded, Wang Lan, Mu Shaoyun, and Xiao Zi, all of whom had broken through to the Star Cloud Stage, would be in the top tier—and there were only three of them!
Their clash was definitely a visual feast. But this showdown had come too early.
"You really surprised me," Mu Shaoyun said, speaking first as they stood on the battle platform. "We’re not in the same class, so I don’t know much about you, other than that Duan Ziqi suffered a big loss at your hands."
"To awaken your Star Martial Warrior talent at the end of your second year and reach this level in just one year. Truly impressive!"
"You’ve surprised me too," Wang Lan replied. "To reach this stage in the Provincial Martial Arts Tournament, almost all the contestants have shown their trump cards, but you haven’t revealed even the tip of the iceberg. If you’re so strong, why do you hide your strength at school?"
"I’m not hiding. My performance at school is merely to meet the school’s requirements. As long as I can secure first place, anything more is a waste. Enough talk, let’s begin."
As soon as he finished speaking, Mu Shaoyun disappeared in an instant. The speed of his Earth Travel Skill was so fast that even if Wang Lan stared without blinking, he still didn’t see how Mu Shaoyun vanished.
To be able to burrow underground at that speed, his movement through the soil surely won’t be slow,
Wang Lan thought. In a flash of intuition, he slapped his palm onto the ground.
"Electric Net—"
CRACKLE—
A spiderweb of lightning instantly spread out from Wang Lan as its center. Amid the electric arcs, countless clods of earth tumbled and leapt.
BOOM— Just three meters behind Wang Lan, a figure burst out from the ground. In less than three breaths, Mu Shaoyun had closed in on Wang Lan.
SWOOSH—
Wang Lan suddenly flicked his hand, and a flame rose from his fingertips. The flame detached from his palm and turned into a crescent-shaped Flame Sword, slashing towards the emerging figure.
RIP—
Like the sound of scissors tearing through ragged cloth, the figure was bisected at the waist in mid-air. Blood sprayed like a downpour.
"Ah—"
This scene shocked countless people to their feet.
The invincible Mu Shaoyun, defeated in just one exchange? And not just defeated, but... dead?
Wang Lan was also startled, but in the next instant, a strong gust of wind came from behind him. Without time to hesitate, he quickly drew Ghost Wail and countered with a slash.
CLANG—
As the first clash rang out, the flash of blades instantly filled their vision. Wang Lan’s short sword and Mu Shaoyun’s battle saber erupted in a dazzling light.
"What... What’s going on? Wasn’t that figure Mu Shaoyun?"
"Obviously not, but damn, it looked so alike," said a fat man, lowering his binoculars with a long sigh. "It turned out to be an earth clone. But heck, it was made so skillfully, identical to the real person! And that blood made from mud, did it have to be so lifelike?"
"If it weren’t lifelike, how could it deceive anyone?" a red-dressed, alluring woman in front of the fat man said coldly. "Even though you’re all high school seniors, your awareness is far inferior to Mu Shaoyun’s. On a real battlefield, if it’s not real, you’ll die."
This beautiful teacher, from an unknown Star Martial Academy, made her point. When she spoke, the students behind her fell silent. Although the students qualified for the Provincial Martial Arts Tournament were the pride of the heavens, each more arrogant than the last, they still knew who deserved their respect.
At this moment, a growing commotion spread through the stands.
Wang Lan and Mu Shaoyun were currently engaged in close combat, one wielding a short sword and the other a battle saber, slashing at each other. It was merely Basic Combat, yet bafflingly, it produced light and shadow effects similar to Star Martial Skills.
From a distance, the center of the combat looked like a glowing orb, enveloping both fighters. Those of higher cultivation realms could discern that this was the reflection and refraction of their blades’ light in the sun, but those of lower realms could only watch in ignorant awe.
It wasn’t just the spectators who were in ignorant awe; Wang Lan, in the midst of battle, felt it too.
He knew his own capabilities; he had already upgraded his Basic Sword Skill to the Gold level.
Gold-level swordsmanship represented reaching the realm of formlessness. His sword techniques and momentum were no longer bound by rigid forms; each move harmonized with the natural forces of the universe. With swordsmanship of this caliber, forget Star Cloud Stage, even in the Galaxy Stage, few would possess such profound Basic Combat power!
Yet, Mu Shaoyun’s every move flows like clouds and water, completely unaffected by my sharp assaults,
Wang Lan mused.
Has Mu Shaoyun also cheated? Does he have a ’golden finger’ too? Otherwise, how could his Basic Combat abilities be this strong?
SCHINK—
Wang Lan’s sword sliced through Mu Shaoyun’s saber light. His left index finger shot out, and a beam of golden fire erupted from his fingertip like a laser. This sudden attack didn’t make Mu Shaoyun panic or even change his expression; instead, he abruptly spat a jet of water from his mouth.
Wang Lan instantly reversed his grip on Ghost Wail, holding it horizontally in front of him. The jet of water smashed against Ghost Wail’s blade, and Mu Shaoyun, in turn, was violently propelled backward by the recoil.
The two disengaged from their deadlock, each standing at opposite ends of the arena.
Electric arcs flickered around Wang Lan. In a blink, they wrapped around his entire body, and the cry of myriad birds echoed from his Thunderbolt Sword.
Mu Shaoyun’s expression changed, and he instantly shot back again.
Wang Lan coldly lifted his head. With a BOOM, the ground beneath his feet suddenly cracked open. In that same instant, Wang Lan’s figure vanished.
RUMBLE—
Earthen walls suddenly rose from the ground, one after another, as if set up by invisible hands like a line of dominoes.
In Wang Lan’s vision, time around him seemed to slow down countlessfold. Wrapped in electric light, his speed surpassed all limits. Yet, even at such velocity, the earthen walls rose at a speed that was not the least bit inferior to his own.
But lightning countered earth; the defensive power of the earthen walls could not withstand a lightning attack.
He thrust his sword at the earthen wall before him. The wall was instantly eroded by electric arcs and disintegrated into dust in a flash.
To the onlookers, however, the series of earthen walls that rose seemed to shatter without warning, as if destroyed by an invisible armor-piercing projectile.
When the final earthen wall was blasted apart, Wang Lan’s gaze fixed solely on Mu Shaoyun. At that moment, however, ripples began to spread around Mu Shaoyun, quickly extending from his body down to his feet. The instant Wang Lan stepped into this rippling zone, his expression changed dramatically.
Intense gravity pressed down, making Wang Lan instantly feel as if he bore a weight of ten thousand catties.
In that same instant, he understood Mu Shaoyun’s strategy.
With Thunder Activity, my speed increased severalfold. For Mu Shaoyun to have a chance of winning, his only option was to reduce my speed, and the only way to do that was by increasing gravity.
But do you think this alone can stop me?
The electric arcs around Wang Lan flared violently. His body, which had just slowed, suddenly accelerated, and he charged toward Mu Shaoyun, thrusting his sword at Mu Shaoyun’s chest.
BOOM—
An earthen wall rose from beneath at the critical moment, blocking Wang Lan’s path. The sword pierced the wall, and it exploded violently. In that moment, Wang Lan’s eyes revealed his astonishment.
"Compound Star Martial Skill... You’ve really mastered the use of Compound Star Martial Skills as well."

chapters.title: Chapter 237: Turning the Tables in a Desperate Situation
chapters.content:
Chapter 237: Chapter 237: Turning the Tables in a Desperate Situation
"The difficulty of combining Star Martial Skills lies merely in multitasking Star Power manipulation and comprehending the principles of the Star Martial Skills. The so-called notion that those below the Galaxy Stage cannot master them is just an excuse used by those of mediocre talent to gloss over their inadequacies. Some people are simply born capable of skipping this process, aren’t they?"
Since he had already displayed a compound Star Martial Skill, Mu Shaoyun stopped pretending.
In an instant, his body crouched sharply, his palm pressed against the ground. The earth beneath his feet suddenly surged like the ocean’s surface.
The ground under Wang Lan’s feet instantly turned into a quagmire. The surrounding quagmire suddenly came to life, extending countless tendrils to stab at Wang Lan.
Electric arcs flashed around Wang Lan, and the pulling force beneath his feet dissipated under the onslaught of electricity. Wang Lan’s Thunder Sword swept out, severing the quagmire tendrils around him.
But the tendrils seemed endless. If this continued, Wang Lan would eventually be worn down by the prolonged battle. Suddenly, Wang Lan’s figure blurred, and a dense, seemingly infinite mass of afterimages appeared around him.
All the spectators who witnessed this scene couldn’t help but gape in utter astonishment.
"Holy shit—"
It wasn’t that Wang Lan’s clones were particularly strong or difficult to comprehend; rather, their bizarrely relentless nature rendered the audience speechless. Layers upon layers of afterimages, each seemingly capable of attack. With a flicker, a large swath of quagmire tendrils around Wang Lan was cleared away.
Instantly, Wang Lan leaped up and pointed at Mu Shaoyun in the distance.
"Messenger Bird—"
From Wang Lan’s fingertips, thunderous arrows shot out in rapid succession. In the void, the arrows transformed into Thunder Snakes, which then suddenly burst apart. Ten Thunder Snakes became a hundred small, flapping, thunderous birds.
They assaulted Mu Shaoyun from all directions like an encompassing net.
Mu Shaoyun, who was about to manipulate the quagmire for another attack, was forced to halt his actions. He raised a wall of mud before him to defend against Wang Lan’s strike.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
Electric arcs exploded, and the mud wall was bombarded, sending mud splattering everywhere. Mu Shaoyun’s eyes instantly turned cold.
Wang Lan’s strength far exceeds my expectations. He only just broke through from the peak of the Star Shine Stage to the early Star Cloud Stage. So why does it feel like he’s as difficult to handle as someone breaking through from the pinnacle of Star Cloud to the Galaxy Stage? His skills are powerful, and his Star Power seems as inexhaustible as a bottomless pit.
The wave of bombardment finally dissipated. Mu Shaoyun cracked open an observation slit in the dark crystal barrier before him. With just one glance, his eyes widened completely.
An arrow, formed by Wang Lan from combined fire and thunder attributes, had taken the shape of a diving phoenix and was heading straight for him. The moment Mu Shaoyun saw it, the phoenix had already reached his face, engulfing his entire field of vision.
BOOM!—
The seemingly indestructible dark crystal barrier shattered instantly. Flames engulfed Mu Shaoyun’s world.
The power of this arrow is already at the Galaxy Stage level! If this isn’t enough to win, am I even human?
I understand now,
Wang Lan thought.
I can’t afford to get entangled with Mu Shaoyun. His combat intellect is too high; a prolonged engagement will likely lead me into one of his traps. My advantage is firepower. I have to decide this with overwhelming offensive power!
HUMMM—
The expected explosion didn’t occur. Within the sea of fire, a distortion suddenly appeared, followed by a void that opened up amid the flames, like a space torn apart by a black hole.
The void grew larger and larger, swallowing all the flames. From its center, a figure slowly emerged.
Mu Shaoyun, after enduring such a terrifying strike from Wang Lan, walked out completely unharmed.
Suddenly, Mu Shaoyun’s body turned a glazed amber color, resembling a human-shaped container filled with iridescent light. Brilliant flames erupted around this figure, with electric arcs dancing amidst them.
Wang Lan immediately retreated to a safe distance. In an instant, a phoenix formed from a thunder-and-fire arrow burst forth from Mu Shaoyun’s body, appearing right before Wang Lan in a flash.
How is this possible!
Wang Lan’s expression changed drastically. His figure flickered, and he narrowly avoided the attack.
BOOM!—
The arena’s protective barrier rippled violently from the impact, shimmering and wobbling precariously as if on the verge of collapse.
This scene stunned everyone. After unleashing the Thunder and Fire Phoenix, Mu Shaoyun returned to his original state, standing silently in place.
"Student Mu Shaoyun, please explain how you accomplished that," a voice suddenly boomed from the venue’s loudspeakers.
The abilities Mu Shaoyun displayed were incomprehensible. To rule out cheating and uphold the principles of fairness and justice, the provincial martial arts tournament organizers had the right to request contestants to explain their abilities.
"Respected leaders, teachers," Mu Shaoyun began, "the ability I just used is my Inborn Talent of the Bloodline: Black Emperor Form! Teachers can review the records from when I first awakened as a Star Martial Warrior. I once accidentally caused seven classmates to collapse from exhaustion and fall unconscious. My Black Emperor Form can devour all Star Martial Skills and Star Power, then release them to attack my opponent. Moreover, it can absorb others’ vitality to replenish my own energy consumption and alleviate fatigue. Because I’ve never fully mastered this ability, I’ve never displayed it publicly. It’s perfectly normal that the leaders and teachers are unaware of it."
"Are you saying this is your Inborn Talent of the Bloodline, not some kind of external item?"
"It is my Inborn Talent of the Bloodline."
"Very well. There are no further issues. The competition continues."
Once the leader finished speaking, Mu Shaoyun looked at Wang Lan with a mocking expression. "Is there really any need to continue? Your attacks are ineffective against me."
Wang Lan frowned.
I recall the Thunder and Fire Phoenix attack Mu Shaoyun returned earlier—it didn’t seem instantaneous, did it?
He immediately raised his hand, and a Crescent Arrow shot out from his fingertips.
Mu Shaoyun, a smile on his face, stood unmoving as the arrow approached. When it reached his face, it vanished as if it had entered a Different Dimensional Space.
But just as the arrow was about to disappear, electric arcs flashed around Wang Lan, and he instantly fired off six Thunder Snakes. The snakes weaved through the air, reaching Mu Shaoyun’s face the moment he absorbed the Crescent Arrow.
BOOM!—
Suddenly, a Crescent Arrow shot out from Mu Shaoyun’s fingertips just as the Thunder Snakes converged. The single arrow caused an explosion that sent electric arcs and flames soaring into the sky.
This scene shattered Wang Lan’s hopes. In the stands, Xiao Zi sighed in dejection.
"It seems the championship is out of my reach..."
"Don’t lose heart, Xiao Zi! You have twenty times their Star Power!" someone comforted her.
"What’s the use of having more Star Power against Mu Shaoyun?" Xiao Zi lamented. "It’s like loading more bullets, only for them to end up in the enemy’s gun. How can such a perverse Inborn Talent of the Bloodline exist in this world..."
"So, you’re saying... Wang Lan is definitely going to lose?"
"He’s doomed. Any Star Martial Skill is countered. He’d have to use an Inborn Talent of the Bloodline or pure physical combat. But pure physical combat won’t work either; Mu Shaoyun’s physical fighting strength isn’t inferior to Wang Lan’s, and his talent lets him absorb vitality. As one’s strength wanes, the other’s waxes. Wang Lan can only be worn down to defeat."
The speed Mu Shaoyun exhibited in his Black Emperor Form is beyond my imagination,
Wang Lan thought.
He can absorb any attack instantly and release it back.
After a moment of reflection, Wang Lan’s figure shot forward. Boosted by Thunder Activity, he moved like a bolt of lightning. A smug smile touched Mu Shaoyun’s lips.
He spread his arms, and an invisible ripple emanated outwards. The moment Wang Lan stepped into this field, his movements abruptly slowed. Decelerated, Wang Lan quickly raised his arm, shooting a Crescent Arrow from his fingertip.
"It’s useless! As long as it’s a Star Martial Skill, it’s ineffective against me," Mu Shaoyun declared calmly, as the Crescent Arrow vanished upon reaching his face.
Suddenly, Wang Lan’s body flashed with lightning, and amidst the arcs, flames danced violently. An arrow imbued with both attributes shot from his fingertip, transforming into a purple projectile that sped towards Mu Shaoyun.
Mu Shaoyun has already absorbed one Crescent Arrow and will release it in the next second,
Wang Lan calculated.
But can an ordinary Crescent Arrow withstand my strongest attack? Obviously not. An ordinary Crescent Arrow will be obliterated by my arrow, and the remaining power will still hit Mu Shaoyun.
This was the latest tactic Wang Lan had devised. When he unleashed it, the eyes of all the teachers who were still pondering how to counter Mu Shaoyun’s ridiculously overpowered ability lit up.
Wang Lan’s tactical acumen is even more advanced than that of all the teachers present!
they thought.
Many believed,
Mu Shaoyun’s Inborn Talent of the Bloodline—it’s been broken!
But in the next instant, all the teachers were stunned. Mu Shaoyun hadn’t released the Crescent Arrow. Instead, he had absorbed Wang Lan’s second attack as well.
His talent isn’t just absorbing one attack and releasing one; he can keep absorbing?
At that moment, Wang Lan sensed imminent danger. Just as he made an evasive maneuver, Mu Shaoyun’s body once again turned into its glazed amber state. Two attacks, one after the other, shot towards Wang Lan.
BOOM! BOOM!
A series of afterimages flickered around Wang Lan, only to be engulfed in the explosions.
Seizing the moment Mu Shaoyun was unleashing the returned attacks, Wang Lan had closed the distance to within three meters of him. Faced with Wang Lan’s close proximity, Mu Shaoyun revealed a sinister smile.
"Thinking of close-quarters combat? You still hold no advantage over me," he said, drawing his combat blade, preparing to engage Wang Lan face-to-face once again.
But Wang Lan suddenly halted. He drew one fist to his waist, and blue flames erupted around him.
"Surging Waves—"
With a single punch, a beam of blue light erupted from Wang Lan’s fist. It separated from his hand and transformed into a ferocious blue wolf’s head.
Mu Shaoyun hadn’t expected Wang Lan to still provoke him with a Star Martial Skill at such a moment. His estimation of Wang Lan plummeted.
I thought he wouldn’t be so foolish, but he’s lost his composure at this crucial juncture. It seems I overestimated him. He knows Star Martial Skills are ineffective against me, yet he still uses one.
Mu Shaoyun sneered, ready to face Wang Lan’s attack head-on. With a BANG, the wolf’s head slammed harshly into his chest. At that instant, Mu Shaoyun’s expression changed.
The Star Martial Skill, which should have been absorbed by his Black Emperor Form, wasn’t. Instead, a powerful force slammed into his chest, rampaging through his body like an electric current.
ARGH!—
A mouthful of blood sprayed out as Mu Shaoyun’s body was flung high into the air.
Wang Lan wouldn’t miss this golden opportunity. He instantly rushed towards Mu Shaoyun’s airborne form, unleashing punch after punch. With each impact, shockwaves erupted from Mu Shaoyun’s body. He went spinning backward through the air, flying all the way out of the arena.

chapters.title: Chapter 238 That’s Not a Star Martial Skill, It’s an Ancient Martial Technique
chapters.content:
Chapter 238: Chapter 238 That’s Not a Star Martial Skill, It’s an Ancient Martial Technique
"Wow—"
Above the stands, almost everyone stood up. The scene before their eyes was a reversal that was too unexpected. Mu Shaoyun, previously in his Invincible Form, had left everyone with the impression of being unbeatable.
But in just one second, to be so suddenly defeated? Hadn’t it been agreed that Star Martial Skills were ineffective against Mu Shaoyun? Why had they suddenly become effective?
Could it be that Mu Shaoyun’s Star Power was exhausted? It didn’t seem like it.
Mu Shaoyun, who had been thrown out of the ring, quickly got up. When he saw the yellow boundary of the field half a meter in front of him, his face instantly turned pitch black, and his ferocious eyes stared at Wang Lan unwillingly.
"The last move you used was not a Star Martial Skill! What is it?"
Wang Lan was breathing heavily, large beads of sweat continuously sliding down his cheeks. The desperate gamble had indeed paid off in the end. Wang Lan’s last move was indeed not a Star Martial Skill, but merely Inch Strength Fist upgraded to Gold level.
Inch Strength Fist, having reached the Gold level, could create a powerful shockwave by striking the air. Under Inch Strength Triple Force, the concentrated punch power formed a columnar air bullet.
The appearance of the blue wolf head shape was nothing but an outer shell simulated by Wang Lan’s use of Flame Sword—an empty shell with no core.
The Black Emperor form could devour Star Power and all Star Martial Skills, but it could not devour pure air. If Mu Shaoyun had understood the deceptive nature of this move beforehand, it would have been easy for him to dodge.
And if this were a life-or-death battle, Wang Lan’s move would have been meaningless. However, this was a provincial martial arts competition with rules. Using the rules, Wang Lan successfully pushed Mu Shaoyun out of the ring.
"Cheating—"
"Staged fight!"
Suddenly, an uproar arose from the stands, with countless voices of doubt coming one after another.
This scene was too strange, too incomprehensible, so for many, the last act seemed like a farce. Mu Shaoyun was not supposed to lose; Wang Lan was not supposed to win.
Adding to this, both competitors were from the Suzhou City team, which fueled suspicions of a fixed fight.
Wang Lan’s last Star Martial Skill clearly wasn’t strong, so why couldn’t Mu Shaoyun absorb it? This was illogical, and the masses needed an explanation. Moreover, who among all present were mere bystanders?
The noise swelled in waves, and the referee paused abruptly as he was about to announce the result. The organizers huddled together, discussing what to do.
"Hello Wang Lan, I am a recruiting officer from Huadong Star Martial Academy. Could you explain the reason behind your last-moment comeback? I can’t see anything special in the Star Martial Skills you displayed." A middle-aged teacher suddenly stood up from the stands, his voice spreading like a gentle breeze throughout the entire arena.
"There’s nothing much to explain." Suddenly, a voice rose from a corner of the venue. Instantly, everyone turned their heads; it was a skinny old man with sunglasses and silver-white hair.
The old man was slightly hunched, his sunglasses obscuring his expression.
But all the teachers who saw the old man stood up excitedly.
"Eld Di?"
"Eld Di!"
"So Eld Di has already arrived... Wasn’t it said that Eld Di would only come on the day of the finals?"
"If you cannot see the subtlety in it, it only proves your level is not high enough. Go back and study the relevant knowledge. I think you haven’t participated in actual combat for a long time.
This move Wang Lan used was not any Star Martial Skill, but an ancient martial art. If I am not mistaken, it should be Inch Strength Fist. Inch Strength Fist, although executed from a very short distance, starts by bending the body from the legs, waist, and arms into the Strong Bow State. Tense muscles are like a fully drawn strong bow.
Even an ordinary person, with years of training, could punch through walls and break tree trunks.
Almost all of you have placed your focus on Star Martial Skills and neglected ancient martial arts, considering them inferior for ordinary people’s cultivation and not comparable to Star Martial Skills.
Indeed, ancient martial arts are hard to cultivate. They require cumulative effort to be effective, and their power is not as strong as that of Star Martial Skills. However, ancient martial arts have an advantage that all Star Martial Skills cannot match: ancient martial arts do not require Star Power to be activated, or if they do, it’s merely as a boost without consuming Star Power.
Ordinary people practicing ancient martial arts can never reach the heights of Star Martial Skills, but it’s not because ancient martial arts are inferior; rather, it’s due to the physical limitations of ordinary people.
Star Martial Warriors possess physiological qualities far beyond ordinary people, and there is no upper limit to these qualities. Star Martial Warriors practicing ancient martial arts can still display power not inferior to Star Martial Skills.
Wang Lan’s punch just now proves that. He unleashed Inch Strength Fist with the power of Split Air Fist, compressing the air and forming an air bullet that hit Mu Shaoyun.
Although Mu Shaoyun has the ability to absorb all Star Martial Skills, he could not absorb the impact of the air bullet. Being pushed out of the ring was not any kind of match-rigging."
With Eld Di’s explanation, all the students understood and, showing expressions of realization, sat down.
Many lower-level Star Martial Warriors who heard this explanation through the live television broadcast felt the flames in their hearts suddenly soar.
They were Star Martial Warriors of the lowest rank, some having even resigned themselves to their low status, lacking resources, wealth, or family background.
To them, everything a Star Martial Warrior needed had to be fought for with their lives on the line. Soul Beads, Star Martial Skills—all were so precious.
Eld Di’s words were like a lighthouse in an ocean, illuminating their world. Star Martial Skills were expensive and scarce, beyond their reach. But ancient martial arts skills weren’t costly.
Because ancient martial arts were considered weaker, many schools even offered to teach their skills for free.
In the hands of ordinary people, these are a waste of heavenly treasures! Damn it, only in our hands as Star Martial Warriors can they be fully utilized!
At this moment, numerous Star Martial Warriors desperate for Star Martial Skills had eyes that shone red with passion, utterly forgetting the key points Eld Di had made during his commentary.
Ancient martial arts skills weren’t something that could be mastered overnight; they required consistent, long-term cultivation to grow stronger. To replace Star Martial Skills with ancient ones, one either had to be a cheat like Wang Lan or be born for it—possessing an extraordinary constitution, a martial talent one in ten thousand.
Upon hearing the explanation, many people sat down, but the teacher from Huadong Star Martial Academy was still unwilling to give up.
"Eld Di, although your explanation makes sense, the move Wang Lan just performed had very obvious characteristics of a Star Martial Skill, even displaying Star Energy Fluctuation."
Hearing that the teacher was still not enlightened, Eld Di sighed and shook his head. "This teacher, can’t you even recognize a Star Power simulation? Wang Lan used the Flame Sword to simulate the appearance of the Flame Wolf Head, which is why the Star Energy Fluctuation was observed.
Wang Lan used form transformation to simulate a Star Martial Skill to deceive his opponent, but the real core was that punch—the Split Air Fist."
With that explanation, the teacher’s face instantly changed color. Although he now understood the reason, it seemed that, in Eld Di’s eyes, he had equated himself with foolishness.
"BEEP—"
"Mu Shaoyun versus Wang Lan—Wang Lan wins!" After Eld Di’s perfect explanation, the referee felt no pressure and directly declared the outcome of the match.
As the referee’s announcement settled, the system notification in his mind also rang out,
"Congratulations to the host for entering the top four of the provincial tournament and advancing to the semifinals. Rewarded with 10,000 experience points and 1,000 skill points."
Advancing to the top four directly rewarded 1,000 skill points. The total skill points from becoming the Champion of the Star Martial Clash didn’t even add up to 1,000.
"The limitation of the competition arena is an illogical setting," Mu Shaoyun snorted, dissatisfied, seeing that the dust had settled and there was no turning back.
Wang Lan smiled softly. "By that logic, the limitation against killing is also illogical."
Wang Lan didn’t enter into an endless debate with Mu Shaoyun.
If their roles were reversed, he would have been just as dissatisfied. Mu Shaoyun’s strength had been overwhelming, almost rendering Wang Lan immobile. Moreover, at that time, Wang Lan’s Star Power was nearly depleted; there should have been no chance for a comeback. But a momentary lapse allowed Wang Lan to pull a fast one and knock him out of the ring. He’d eat his hat if Mu Shaoyun felt okay with that. To have victory snatched away when it had seemed so assured—that frustration could even make someone hang themselves in sheer vexation.
As Wang Lan secured his victory, another person in the arena heaved a long sigh of relief: Xiao Zi.
"It seems the championship is still up for grabs," Xiao Zi commented to Ni Yushu, who was beside her.
"Indeed, you’d stand no chance against Mu Shaoyun. His Inborn Talent of the Bloodline is at an insurmountable level for you now. However, you mustn’t take anything for granted; this Wang Lan absolutely defies conventional judgment."
"Indeed. If it wasn’t for Wang Lan’s use of ancient martial skills at the last moment, who would have known he had such a move hidden? He’s like a bag of myriad treasures; you never know what he might pull out next.
Even a situation where Mu Shaoyun was sure to win was turned on its head. It seems I need to be even more cautious and serious."
"Your tactics remain unchanged: crush with absolute power, and never give Wang Lan any exploitable opening. Remember not to get entangled; your advantage lies in your Star Power."
"Mm!"
Two more high-quality duels followed, each more spectacular than the previous round of sixteen matches. But perhaps due to the dazzling performance by Wang Lan and Mu Shaoyun beforehand, the subsequent matches seemed rather lackluster in comparison.
The afternoon battles raged fiercely, and the internet was already abuzz.
"Your daddy is still your daddy, and the Wolf King is still the Wolf King. Even in such a situation, he managed a comeback from the brink. Is there any opponent he cannot defeat?"
"Indeed. Although it seemed like a fluke, looking back at the Wolf King’s combat record, in which battle did he not emerge victorious through trials and tribulations? Once is luck, twice is luck, but is it always just luck?"
"Beneath the Wolf King’s feet lie five seeded players, each with the potential to be champion. Whoever says the Wolf King relies on luck clearly doesn’t see his strength."
"Don’t know if you’ve all noticed, but it seems like the Wolf King has a new trick up his sleeve for every match. In the first match, the Wolf King’s public info was that he was Fire attribute. So some idiot remarked, ’My Star Power crushes yours, my attribute counters yours, how could I lose?’
But lo and behold, the Wolf King pulled out a Thunder Attribute Star Martial Skill and scored an instant kill. Then in the second match, the opponent’s Star Palace Artifact was seemingly invincible, but who knew the Wolf King would also bring out a Star Palace Artifact for a perfect, decisive kill.
In the third match, an opponent immune to pain encountered a support who could heal himself; the Wolf King stubbornly traded blow for blow, exhausting a berserker until he was completely spent. Our great Wolf King is truly mighty and domineering!"

chapters.title: Chapter 239: Another Collision
chapters.content:
Chapter 239: Chapter 239: Another Collision
Suzhou City had fought its way to this point, and everyone at Suzhou No.1 Middle School Star Martial Academy was extremely elated. Amid the celebrations, Wang Lan, the only one who had made it to the semifinals, became all the more precious.
The guidance director, who was a bit drunk, patted Wang Lan’s shoulders with great affection. Despite the festive celebrations, Mu Shaoyun, who had secured fifth place for the school, was absent.
Theoretically, after the competition ends, players who no longer have matches can leave the hotel and go home. But so far, only Mu Shaoyun had left early.
That night was silent. Yet, in that silence, the sports hall underwent a silent transformation. Experts from the Tianjian Bureau quietly entered the sports hall to set up defenses.
"TAP TAP TAP—" The door was knocked, interrupting Wang Lan and his two companions as they were having a midnight snack. Xu Xiangwen walked to the door, puzzled.
"Who is it?"
"Room check," a clear and icy female voice sounded from outside the door. It bore a hint of Jiang Xinyu’s voice but was definitely not hers.
Xu Xiangwen instantly became excited, peering through the peephole to see two twins dressed in security uniforms, both strikingly beautiful.
"Uh..." The fire in Xu Xiangwen’s chest was instantly extinguished as he opened the door and stood at attention, "Captain Zhang, good evening."
It was Zhang Yeqiu and Zhang Xiaoxue who had come.
Upon entering the room, Zhang Yeqiu surveyed the three. "Just the three of you here?"
"Yeah. What’s going on? The Tianjian Bureau is doing room checks now?"
"We’ve cleared out all the security and staff, so their duties naturally fall to us now. Also, starting today, be a bit nicer to the cleaning ladies coming to clean the rooms. They’re our colleagues."
"Got it. By the way, how’s the progress on that case? Did you find anything?"
"Nothing! We can be certain that it was Wang Mingling himself who took action. Besides him, no one could have killed Xuan Lin in such a short span of time. And surely he has been hidden away by some force. It is like looking for a needle in a haystack in the vast area of Suzhou City."
"So the bureau plans to draw the snake out of the hole? I was wondering why Eld Di was released today."
"Captain Wang Lan, please watch your words. What do you mean ’released’? That’s called ’inviting’!"
"That’s not right, shouldn’t it be called ’offering’?" Xu Xiangwen quipped.
"OK! You’re right. So, we’re ’offering’ Eld Di?"
"Now, the entire venue is staffed by people from the Tianjian Bureau, with the exception of the team leaders, competitors, and leaders from Suzhou City. Current speculation suggests that Wang Mingling might have infiltrated the venue and possessed someone. It’s just unknown whether he has been ’invited’ out by us yet."
"If it were so easy to ’invite’ him out, he wouldn’t have been troubling the United Nations for so many years."
"Regardless, the Tianjian Bureau has made all the necessary preparations and will guard Eld Di every step of the way. As long as we keep an eye on Eld Di, Wang Mingling, no matter where he hides, will show himself."
"Alright then! Be extra careful."
After sending away Zhang Yeqiu and her sister, they moved on to the next room belonging to Jiang Xinyu and Xie Sisi.
"What... were you talking about?" Gong Feiyu asked hesitantly after closing the door again.
"Someone wants to disrupt the Provincial Martial Arts Tournament. It’s that simple – the Tianjian Bureau is providing protection throughout the event."
"Oh!"
Time quickly moved on to 8 a.m., the moment of another thrilling lottery draw. No, rather, the draw for the semifinal matchups.
Tomorrow would be the last day of the Provincial Martial Arts Tournament, with the semifinals in the morning and the finals in the afternoon. At the same time, the battles for third and fourth place would take place. It seemed like there would only be four competitors, but the schedule was packed tight.
Soon, the much-anticipated semifinal matchups were announced, and to everyone’s surprise, Wang Lan was the first to compete. His heart instantly leaped to his throat.
In the next second, the image on the left appeared: a handsome and sunny smile, as stunning as Wang Lan’s.
"Damn, Xiao Zi!"
"What the hell? They’re wrapping up the finals in the semifinals? With only four people left, couldn’t the organizers be a bit more perceptive? It’s clear who the top two are, yet they have to clash in the semifinals?"
Xu Xiangwen, along with countless viewers watching on TV, shared the same complaint. Even if they were not Star Martial Warriors, it was evident that at this stage of the competition, the top-ranked contestants were known.
Wang Lan, Xiao Zi, Mu Shaoyun—although not ranked in any particular order, the top three were definitely among them. But what was the outcome? Amidst the tigers’ clash, the defeated Mu Shaoyun could only scoop up fifth place.
And now, Wang Lan was about to battle Xiao Zi, with only one of them doomed to fall to third place. The runner-up position had been nabbed by someone clearly weaker than them—didn’t that just seem irritating?
But even if this question were posed aloud, no one would answer. Each year’s Provincial Martial Arts Tournament was just like this. Luck was also a part of strength. Every year, there would be those fortunate enough to slip through to the higher ranks. If objections to such matchups were raised, what then should be said about those who advanced by a bye?
In the Provincial Martial Arts Tournaments, though there might be one or two lucky enough to scrape through, there would absolutely not be any strong talent with good performance slipping through the net. Why did the major Star Martial Academies specifically send observers to the scene if not to avoid students with great strength and excellent performance from unluckily facing tougher opponents?
Take Jiang Xinyu, for example. After achieving her final rank, many Star Martial Academies had already phoned her. Although most of them were thinking that if Jiang Xinyu had a lapse of judgment and agreed, wouldn’t that be picking up a huge bargain? But there were also top-tier academies like Jin City Star Warrior Academy, Huadong Star Martial Arts Academy, and Shenlong Military Star Martial Arts Academy that had extended olive branches to Jiang Xinyu.
For the moment, Jiang Xinyu had not given a definitive response. She was waiting for the admissions from the top four Star Martial Academies.
The top four Star Martial Academies would issue direct admission notices to students fulfilling their entrance requirements seven days after the end of the Provincial Martial Arts Tournament. With Jiang Xinyu ranking in the top ten of the province and her exemplary performance on the field, the chances of her being accepted into the top four were high.
Anyway, Jiang Xinyu had already calculated that whichever of the top four was willing to take her, she would go there. If she failed to catch the eye of the top four, then she would attend Jin City Star Warrior Academy. In terms of the scale of the school and training students, Jin City Star Warrior Academy came the closest to the top four.
As the second most developed province in Jade Country and the one with the most generous investment in education, Jin City Star Warrior Academy virtually had whatever it asked for. In recent years, they even vowed to make the top four into the top five.
That’s a bit off-topic, but when this match schedule was announced, it meant that Zhang Hao and Qiu Tianci, who were originally stopped in the semifinals, still had a chance to reach for the runner-up. There was obviously no need to draw for the remaining two matchups, as they were directly arranged.
Perhaps feeling that Wang Lan’s battle against Xiao Zi should be saved for the climax, the order of appearance was swapped, placing their confrontation as the second match. This, of course, Zhang Hao and Qiu Tianci had no complaints about.
With the match schedule drawn, the TV channel nonchalantly switched its broadcast to a television drama series starting in the eight o’clock prime time slot. This projected an air of utter detachment, as if to say, "Argue all you want; if you can shake my resolve even one bit, I’ll admit defeat."
The night passed in silence. For some, it was an excruciating ordeal, but for others, it was a mere blink of an eye.
Early the next day, after breakfast, the group arrived at the competition venue. At nine o’clock in the morning, amid stirring music, the first match of the Provincial Martial Arts Tournament semifinals was about to begin.
If Zhang Hao and Qiu Tianci’s strengths were placed in any previous tournament, they would be hot contenders for the championship, even holding an eighty percent chance of winning it. But they were unlucky this time, finding themselves in a tournament of deities clashing.
As they took to the field, the applause was sparse and sporadic.
Both men approached the arena with expressionless faces, solemnly staring at one another. Watching them, a glint flickered in Wang Lan’s eyes.
Weird... It’s only been one day since I saw them, but why does their momentum seem different?
"Different? How so?" Jiang Xinyu asked perplexedly, lifting her head.
Can’t quite put my finger on it, but it feels... even though this match should be more relaxed, why does it feel as though a death squad is marching to battle?
Perhaps realizing his explanation was problematic, Wang Lan made an analogy, "It’s like facing an exam for which the answers have been memorized, yet it’s laden with the heaviness of a make-or-break retest."
"Lanzi, just say it’s supposed to be a happy occasion but it’s being conducted like a funeral!"
"With their strength, neither had hope for the runner-up, but at least one would move on, so there’s no way they would exhibit such a dismal aura."
"Sorry, I didn’t notice it."
"TWEET—"
The referee’s whistle sounded, and immediately both men’s bodies moved. From Wang Lan’s perspective, their fighting styles were standard. Their strength was not beneath Jiang Xinyu’s, but Wang Lan felt Jiang Xinyu had a better chance of winning in an actual fight.
Within the first three seconds of the match starting, both had unleashed their Star Martial Skills twice against each other.
Since both sides had comparable strength, neither gained an edge in this exchange of skills. This scene had all the observing teachers furrowing their brows.
Having witnessed the high-quality bouts of Wang Lan and others, to then see the clash between these two was almost unbearable. But logically, these two should not be wrong in their by-the-book performance, which seemed no worse—and potentially even better—than that of most first-year students of their own academies.
Yet for some reason, it was simply intolerable.
Many teachers couldn’t help but think: if it were Wang Lan and Xiao Zi, would they have exchanged blows at the very start? What tactics would they employ? How would they strategize before acting?
But such growth accompanies real combat experience, and they are after all still students. Even at the Star Cloud Stage, how much real combat experience can a student possess? A methodical approach to combat is reasonable. If they were that polished, even surpassing their teachers, then what’s the point of having teachers? Why even bother with college?
Even with such self-explanations and self-reassurances, many teachers remained with tightly knit brows that refused to relax.
The gap... Like a chasm, so stark and pronounced, it was blatantly apparent.
Zhang Hao and Qiu Tianci had very close attributes, and since neither was a single-attribute Star Martial Warrior, there was no scenario of Star Martial Attributes overpowering one another. Therefore, a continuous barrage of Star Martial Skills ensued as they relentlessly attacked back and forth.
Tactical errors were committed multiple times by both men. Either one, if facing Wang Lan or Xiao Zi, would be finished within five minutes.
In the past, Wang Lan and those at the Star Cloud Stage had a difference in level, but the Wang Lan who had broken through to the Star Cloud Stage had already leaped out of its bounds. Within the Star Cloud Stage, except for crafty veterans like Xu Shiyun, the rest, Wang Lan could call rubbish.
Finally, the seemingly intense—but in the eyes of discerning teachers, mistake-ridden—battle of attrition ended as both appeared to have nearly depleted their Star Power. Zhang Hao was the first to draw his saber and charge at Qiu Tianci.

chapters.title: Chapter 240 Mutual Destruction
chapters.content:
Chapter 240: Chapter 240 Mutual Destruction
If there’s anything redeemable about the clash of Star Martial Skills, the hand-to-hand combat between these two was seriously lacking. While they might have been considered outstanding among the senior class, they fell far short of the overall level at the provincial martial arts competition.
Perhaps it was because both Zhang Hao and Qiu Tianci were Mages.
Suddenly, Wang Lan, who had been quietly watching the match, leaped to his feet, a look of horror on his face. Almost simultaneously, Xie Sisi and the other experts widened their eyes, feeling a chill crawl over their scalps.
Zhang Hao thrust his knife into Qiu Tianci’s chest, hitting the heart, while Qiu Tianci slit Zhang Hao’s throat. An exchange of life for life, executed without the slightest hesitation. Their seemingly foolish fight was underpinned by a deadly resolve to kill the opponent.
This moment was frozen in time, as if it had become eternal.
"TRRRR—" The referee blew the whistle frantically, sprinting towards the arena. But by that time, it was already too late.
The mutual destruction happened too quickly; it didn’t seem like a situation where they had no strength left to pull back. It could be said that any other competitor, had they still possessed the strength, would not have allowed the situation to reach this point.
All the spectators in the stands stood up in shock, while the countless viewers watching the live broadcast were simply dumbfounded.
It had long been said that the world of Star Martial Warriors is cruel, and that their battles are a matter of life and death. Many hadn’t believed it before, always thinking it was an exaggeration to glorify Star Martial Warriors.
With such a beautiful country and a stable and prosperous society, where were these life-and-death battles? Where was the call to serve one’s country with no regrets in life or death? Even online, there were always some idiotic comments. There were claims that the Pioneer Space did not exist, that it was a fiction created by the state to romanticize Star Martial Warriors. If it existed, where was it? Why couldn’t it be found?
The Pioneer Space is a Different Dimensional Space. Of course, ordinary people can’t see it or enter it. This beautiful country, this prosperous era—they were all shouldered by the Star Martial Warriors.
And the brutality of this moment left many keyboard warriors speechless. Actual lives had been lost, right before the public’s eyes.
Stretcher bearers quickly carried the two away. With vital spots hit and without Wang Lan’s Self Healing ability, even gods couldn’t save them. Just moments before, when Qiu Tianci unhesitatingly took Zhang Hao’s lethal blow, Wang Lan had thought he too possessed some Self Healing trump card.
The outcome... could it truly be this?
"Star Martial Warriors are warriors. The provincial martial arts competition is not just a sports event. In the world of Star Martial Warriors, there’s no such thing as safety first.
The competition is a drill; the battle is real combat. Even if casualties occur, that is within the bounds of acceptance. Injuries and deaths are inevitable at the annual provincial martial arts competition..."
Before the keyboard warriors could even react, the organizers of the provincial martial arts competition quickly issued a statement on the necessity of real combat and the rationale behind casualties. Just as drills allow for casualties, so too do Star Martial contests.
