If cultivated correctly, he will undoubtedly become one of the new generation of Five Emperors. We must make every effort to recruit this student."
"Mr. Zhang, you’re right. But historically, provincial champions have always been prime acquisitions for the Four Great Star Martial Academies. How can we possibly recruit him?"
"Principal, I’ve studied recent batches of students and found them to be increasingly confident and proud. As they gain access to more information, their choices are becoming more rational.
While the Four Great Star Martial Academies still lead by a considerable margin, their inherent arrogance is often a turn-off for prospective students. Nowadays, many students prefer to be a big fish in a small pond rather than a small fish in a big one.
I believe Wang Lan will feel the same way. It’s true he’ll be favored by the Four Great Star Martial Academies, but those academies are teeming with experts and geniuses. Even if Wang Lan is recruited, he might not receive the best resources. We are different. If we promise to dedicate all our resources to his development, we still have a fighting chance.
Furthermore, our Zezhou Star Martial Academy isn’t significantly inferior to the Four Great ones. Our relationship with Wang Lan would be mutually beneficial. If we pour all our resources into cultivating him, and he becomes a new Emperor, our academy could ascend to become the fifth major. It’s a win-win situation."
"You make a good point, but don’t forget, in Jiang Province, there’s also Jin City Star Martial Academy, which is on par with us."
"Then it all comes down to who is more determined."
The principal rested his chin in his hand, pondering for a long time before quietly nodding. "Contact Wang Lan discreetly. You can offer whatever terms you deem necessary. As long as our academy can provide it, I will approve it."
"Understood!"
「Elsewhere」
An almost identical conversation was taking place at an administrative meeting in Jin City Star Martial Academy. For Jin City Star Martial Academy, they leveraged their home-province advantage. And Jin City Star Martial Academy, also aspiring to become the fifth major academy, saw Wang Lan as their golden opportunity.

chapters.title: Chapter 247 Various Parties Stir
chapters.content:
Chapter 247: Chapter 247 Various Parties Stir
While the major Star Martial Academies were furiously crunching numbers, the top four Star Martial Academies were also specifically studying Wang Lan in a meeting room.
In the meeting room of Imperial Capital Star Martial Academy, a recently returned observation teacher from Jiang Province brought first-hand information on Wang Lan. Compared to the guessing game of netizens who knew little beyond shouting "666", the Star Martial Academy’s observation teachers had more objective and detailed data analysis.
"Principal, our trip to Jiang Province was very fruitful. Eight candidates have met our direct admission criteria. However, among them is Jiang Province’s number one, Wang Lan, whom I think we must secure at all costs. We can consider improving the enrollment package."
"Oh? Mr. Wu, our school hasn’t broken precedent to improve enrollment packages for almost twenty years. Is that Wang Lan worth breaking a twenty-year tradition for?" a middle-aged teacher from the guidance office asked in a deep voice.
"Director Zhao, what if that Wang Lan is the next Five Emperors?"
"PFFT!" Upon hearing this, many people in the meeting room laughed. Over the years, they had heard too many labeled as the next Five Emperors. Although each was truly extraordinary, everyone ultimately fell short of the Five Emperors. Hearing the same comment repeatedly had turned it into a joke.
"Wang Lan, born in the year 5002, awakened his Star Martial Warrior talent at the end of June 5018..." Mr. Wu read from the information in his hands.
"Wait a minute!" Director Zhao suddenly sat up straight. "Mr. Wu, are you sure you’re not mistaken? Did he awaken in 5018? It hasn’t even been a full year since his awakening?"
"Yes!"
"He became the champion of Jiang Province within a year of awakening?" As he said this, his expression became serious. To become the champion of Jiang Province within a year meant either Jiang Province was very weak this year, or he was extremely talented.
"Indeed, and he’s also been called the strongest high school student in the history of Jiang Province."
"Mr. Wu, please continue to tell us what’s special about this Wang Lan," the principal said gently, interrupting the digression.
"Yes! Wang Lan independently awakened his Star Martial Warrior talent at sixteen and entered the Star Shine Stage ten days later. In less than a year, he publicly advanced to the Star Cloud Stage during a provincial competition.
His stats were: Basic Combat, A+; combat talent, A+; combat wisdom, A+. His Star Martial Skills included: Flame Sword, advanced level; Star Cloud Sword Dance, advanced level; Crescent Arrow, advanced level; Thunder Snake, advanced level; and Phantom Tracer, advanced level!
His Inborn Talent of the Bloodline is healing of the Medical Attribute, with S-grade practicality and beyond S-grade potential.
Furthermore, immediately after the competition, a terrorist attack occurred at the site of the provincial competition. The international fugitive Wang Mingling attacked the venue, and Wang Lan single-handedly confronted him, employing a beyond S-grade Star Martial Skill, Phoenix Form. The combat power he displayed was at the peak of the Galaxy Stage."
"What?"
At these words, the meeting room fell silent; even the principal of Imperial Capital Star Martial Academy was dumbstruck.
"You’re talking about the Phoenix Form? To what extent has he cultivated it?"
"The first stage of the Phoenix Form is already completed up to the second step, with flames ignited all around his body, just one step away from complete body flame transformation."
"This Wang Lan already learned the Phoenix Form at the Star Cloud Stage? Is he Eld Di’s disciple? When did Eld Di accept a new disciple?"
"No, as far as I know, he’s the son of the Flame Emperor, and his Phoenix Form comes from the Flame Emperor. Moreover, he didn’t learn it at the Star Cloud Stage, because he only advanced to the Star Cloud Stage a few days ago. By that time, he had already mastered the Phoenix Form."
"Mastering the Phoenix Form at the Star Shine Stage... That’s the next Flame Emperor."
"Correct. His growth to the Star Cloud Stage in just one year shows his tremendous potential. He’s worth breaking our twenty-year tradition for and merits enhanced enrollment benefits."
"However, he’s the son of the Flame Emperor; he’s probably already Modu Star Martial Academy’s to take, right?"
"The Flame Emperor was once a student of our Imperial Capital Star Martial Academy. How could he be considered meat in Modu Star Martial Academy’s pot?"
"Can you really reason that way? Back then, Eld Di was our dean, and the Imperial Capital Star Martial Academy of those days has become today’s Modu Star Martial Academy. Now, with Eld Di as the principal of Modu Star Martial Academy, Wang Lan is definitely heading there for Eld Di."
"That’s not necessarily the case. Imperial Capital Star Martial Academy is still his mother’s alma mater. Plus, we’re ranked number one nationwide. In terms of resources and strength, we’re still above Modu.
Besides, what can Modu Star Martial Academy offer Wang Lan? He’s already learned the Phoenix Form, and he cannot learn the Dragon Emperor Form. Modu Star Martial Academy offers him no real benefits. As long as we clearly lay out the pros and cons for him, he should make a wise choice."
"Indeed. All of Modu Star Martial Academy’s secret techniques are based on the Dragon Emperor Form. Having learned the Phoenix Form, Wang Lan will have missed out on those powerful techniques. No one can compare to us in researching the Phoenix Form. Notify the admissions office to call Wang Lan immediately."
"No, Director Zhao, you go personally," the principal suddenly decided. "You negotiate with Wang Lan yourself. Whatever conditions he asks for, as long as we can meet them, agree. The sooner, the better."
"Eh? Isn’t it our procedure that we should only contact students five days after the provincial competition has ended?"
"Who cares about procedure at this time?" Mr. Wu was exasperated. "Of course, we should act swiftly. If Modu Star Martial Academy signs him first, then it will be too late for everything."
「At the same time」
In the meeting room of Xiangjiang Star Martial Academy, the decision was almost the same. "I must personally go to Suzhou City and ensure that Wang Lan is recruited into our academy. Our Xiangjiang Star Martial Academy has never produced one of the Five Emperors, and this failure has always provoked criticism, making it impossible for me to hold my head high among the other top three Star Martial Academies. Wang Lan has the potential of the Five Emperors; we cannot let him slip away."
"Yes!" The director of the guidance office promptly stood at attention and saluted, the military style of the academy as uncompromising as ever.
The situation was similar at Jinghua Star Martial Arts Academy; they even acted faster than Imperial Capital Star Martial Academy. As Director Zhao was stepping out with his luggage, representatives from Jinghua Star Martial Arts Academy were already in the boarding lounge, preparing to board a plane.
Of the four major Star Martial Academies, Jinghua Star Martial Arts Academy and Imperial Capital Star Martial Academy were both located in the capital. This led them to vie vehemently to be recognized as the number one Star Martial Academy in Jade Country. Despite both being among the four major Star Martial Academies, they relished devaluing each other.
"PAH! You think you’re worthy of being Jade Country’s number one? You’re nothing! I’m the true number one."
"Get lost! You’re just my branch campus. How dare you compete with me for first place? In terms of history, I’m three hundred years ahead of you."
This competitive jest had been ongoing for nearly fifty years. The people of Jade Country watched for amusement, treating it as something of a joke. Everyone knew that even though the academies differed in ranking, their strength was more or less equal.
Imperial Capital Star Martial Academy led the world with its profound research in advanced Star Martial Skills, possessing the most secret techniques and forbidden techniques globally. On the other hand, Jinghua Star Martial Arts Academy was world-renowned for its research into the application of Star Martial Skills. More than half of the existing Form Changing Star Martial Skills were created by Jinghua Star Martial Arts Academy or its students. Xiangjiang Star Martial Academy followed a group formation strategy, a characteristic related to its military roots. Almost all powerful Star Martial Groups were graduates of Xiangjiang. In particular, their Star Power Bridging Formation Map was unmatched worldwide.
Modu Star Martial Academy, with the shortest but most legendary history, didn’t have any particularly prominent features. If any, it would be its laissez-faire approach to education. With minimal restrictions on students, as long as they accumulated enough Academic Credits and passed exams, no one cared if they attended classes or not. There were no restrictions on which Star Martial Skills to learn; students could exchange points for them. In terms of freedom, it could be compared to the colleges in White Eagle Country.
A terrorist attack occurring at the provincial competition was no trivial matter. Even though Eld Di resolved it with absolute force, the lack of damage was not a reason to underestimate its seriousness. Who was providing cover for Wang Mingling? Who was supplying the Demon Clan with Space Stones to open a Different Dimensional Space? How did they infiltrate Suzhou City without a trace? And why were the checkpoints throughout Jade Country seemingly useless? All these questions needed in-depth investigation and accountability.
So, the Tianjian Bureau was very busy.
With the provincial competition over, the Star Martial Arts Campus began the tense sprint towards the college entrance exams. Wang Lan, along with other students who had participated and performed excellently in the provincial competition, returned to the classroom after resting for two days.
No matter how sensational an event, it would cool down with the passage of time. At least for Senior Three, Class One, this was the case.
During a class break, Mingyue Wucheng stared at Wang Lan for a long time with an envious look, like someone who had just eaten a lemon. That gaze made Wang Lan’s tailbone feel somewhat chilly.
"Wucheng, stop looking at me like that. It’s creeping me out!"
"Wang Lan, do you know what you remind me of? A Soul Bead. A supreme Soul Bead containing an S-grade Star Martial Skill. So smooth, so beautiful..."
"Stop! I get your point, but can you please not stare at me like that? Remember, I was the one who encouraged you to sign up. You chose not to."
"Who the hell knew the provincial champion would get an S-grade Star Martial Skill? Before, the best was A-grade... Ah... I regret it so much. Once, an S-grade Star Martial Skill was right before me, and I didn’t cherish it..."
"Wucheng, are you short of S-grade Star Martial Skills? You’re acting as if you’ve been dumped," Xu Xiangwen said, patting Mingyue Wucheng’s shoulder.
"Short? It’s an S-grade Star Martial Skill! Even if I can’t use it, couldn’t I just keep it? My family only has four or five S-grade Star Martial Skills."
"Well used, that ’only’!" Lin Gao chimed in from the side, looking up at Mingyue Wucheng with disdain. "Having one is good enough. A decent Star Martial family might have at most two. Your family has at least six, and you still think it’s not enough?"
"By the way, the principal and others were waiting at the entrance early this morning. Are they welcoming an important guest?"
"It’s all so secretive. What’s happening?"
"Perhaps their arrival was so sudden that the principal wasn’t aware either," Wang Lan quickly interjected, trying to change the topic.
"And how would you know that? Or are you saying you know who’s coming?"
"I’m not a clairvoyant who can predict things. But if the principal knew we were having visitors today, wouldn’t he have had us do a major clean-up yesterday?"
As Wang Lan and the others were speculating, a black business van pulled up at the entrance of the Star Martial Arts Campus. Principal Zhang hurriedly went to meet them, his face wreathed in smiles.
"Welcome, welcome! We are honored to have the leaders from Jinghua Star Martial Arts Academy visit our campus for inspection and guidance..."
"You are Principal Zhang from Suzhou No.1 Middle School’s Star Martial Arts Campus."
"Yes, yes, that’s me."
"Principal Zhang, you’ve done an excellent job, cultivating so many outstanding students," said Pang Long, Director of the Guidance Office at Jinghua Star Martial Arts Academy, as he enthusiastically shook Principal Zhang’s hand.
"Director Pang, you’re too kind. Please, this way. Liu, quick, take Director Pang for a tour of our school."
"Hmm?" Pang Long paused and looked at Principal Zhang, who remained standing in place. "Principal Zhang, are you expecting more visitors?"
"Yes, yes, Director Zhao from Imperial Capital Star Martial Academy also called to say he will arrive shortly."
Upon hearing this reply, Pang Long’s face darkened, and he muttered, "They sure arrived fast!"

chapters.title: Chapter 248 Difficult Choice
chapters.content:
Chapter 248: Chapter 248 Difficult Choice
At the Conference Center Hotel, a graceful woman in red draped a coat over her shoulders and gently pulled back the curtains.
"DING-DONG. Ms. Sun, your morning tea has arrived."
"Alright, come on in."
The hotel attendant wheeled a food trolley into the suite, her gaze inadvertently sweeping over Ms. Sun.
Even as a fellow woman, she couldn’t help but feel a sense of admiration. Could this woman be some celebrity?
The attendant placed the delicate breakfast items on the table, then wheeled the trolley out. No sooner had the attendant left than there was a knock at the door.
"Who is it?"
"Teacher Sun, hurry up! We’ll be late if we don’t leave now."
"Did you find their itinerary?" Ms. Sun asked as she opened the door to let the young woman in.
"I found it. I hacked into Capital City Airlines. Director Pang from Jinghua Star Martial Arts Academy took a flight yesterday afternoon. Director Zhao from the Imperial Capital Star Martial Academy was on a flight last night. They both arrived in Suzhou City this morning. Major General Yu from Xiangjiang Star Martial Academy, however, only arrived in Suzhou City an hour ago. But he didn’t even look for a place to stay and went straight to Suzhou No.1 Middle School."
"They seem to be in quite a hurry..."
"Isn’t that obvious? None of us are blind. Think about Wang Lan’s performance and assessment! Let’s hurry, or they’ll snatch him away. These days, proximity isn’t necessarily an advantage."
"No rush. Let’s have our morning tea first."
"You’re still eating? Wang Lan is the one Eld Di personally took a liking to..." The young woman was anxious, but Sun Li wasn’t in a hurry at all. She sat at the breakfast table, enjoying the unique morning tea of Suzhou City.
Sun Li had a motto: in this life, only her country and food were not to be forsaken. In her eyes, the importance of food was on par with that of the country. She was the type to give her life for a good meal.
Knowing her teacher’s personality, the young woman could only watch with a wry smile, despite her urgency.
"Sit down and eat with me. Don’t rush. Recruiting is a technical skill; it requires strategy. Mere inducements are useless. Besides, with all three of them there, Wang Lan won’t be able to decide quickly. Let them argue first. We need to eat our fill to have the energy to contend with them..." Sun Li playfully stuck out her tongue, making the young woman shiver.
"Teacher... what are you planning... to do to compete? You’re not actually going to fight them, are you?"
"What are you thinking? They are all veteran teachers, our seniors. How could we possibly fight our seniors?"
"You still care about things like that? Don’t tell me... you’re thinking of poisoning them?"
"Is that how you see me?" Sun Li shot the young woman a glare. "Put that down. You can’t eat it now."
"Huh?" The young woman glanced at the pastry she was holding; it looked quite appetizing.
"I’ve already poisoned it. Try it if you don’t believe me."
"So stingy!" The young woman put the pastry down and started blowing bubbles into her glass of juice with a straw.
「」
"Reporting in!"
"Come in!"
Wang Lan pushed open the meeting room door. Instantly, several pairs of eyes shot towards him. Their intense gazes made Wang Lan want to turn and flee.
"Wang Lan, let me introduce you. This is Director Zhao from the Imperial Capital Star Martial Academy, this is Director Pang from Jinghua Star Martial Arts Academy, and this is Major General Yu from Xiangjiang Military Star Martial Academy."
"Good day, Teachers, Major General!"
"Have a seat," Director Zhao said, pointing to a nearby chair.
Wang Lan approached the chair and sat down, somewhat reservedly. Although Wang Lan was experienced, such experience was context-dependent. These were all legendary figures; it would be a lie to say he wasn’t nervous at all.
After sitting down and taking a deep breath, Wang Lan calmed himself.
"You’ve probably guessed why I’m here. Your performance at the provincial martial arts competition was outstanding. Therefore, on behalf of the Imperial Capital Star Martial Academy, I formally invite you to enroll in our academy this September. What do you say, Wang Lan?"
"I..."
"Wang Lan, Jinghua Star Martial Arts Academy also hopes you will enroll with us. Are you aware that Jinghua Star Martial Arts Academy possesses the world’s most diverse range of Star Martial Skills and the finest teaching faculty? The comprehensive strength of students from Jinghua Star Martial Arts Academy is widely acclaimed. Choosing Jinghua Star Martial Arts Academy would be a wise decision for you."
Alright, Director Pang’s words have put me in a bind. Agreeing to one would offend the other two. Couldn’t they invite me privately instead of putting me on the spot like this?
A troubled expression immediately appeared on Wang Lan’s face.
"Wang Lan, as far as I know, you hold a military rank?" Major General Yu suddenly spoke.
Wang Lan quickly stood up. "Yes! Reporting to the Major General, I am a special operative from Suzhou City’s Tianjian Bureau, holding the rank of Captain."
"Since you’re a soldier, what are you hesitating about?"
"Major General Yu, you’re misleading him. Military academies and the military aren’t directly linked. Military academies operate independently of the military, and the Tianjian Bureau is an even more separate system from yours. He is a special operative of the Tianjian Bureau. Holding a military rank doesn’t dictate which academy he must attend. What? If he chooses Xiangjiang Academy, will he get into the Ministry of Defense after graduation, or something?"
"If he performs exceptionally well, it’s not impossible."
"But that might not be what Wang Lan needs. Wang Lan, you should come to Imperial Capital Star Martial Arts Academy. Your mother, Wang Ling, graduated from there. The Imperial Capital Star Martial Arts Academy is ranked first in Jade Country and has conducted the most in-depth research on the Phoenix Form. There are many derivative skills of the Phoenix Form, and they could all be yours if you come. We can also promise to waive your tuition fees for five years. Additionally, we guarantee you an S-level Star Martial Skill, three A-level Star Martial Skills, and training to reach the elite level of the Galaxy Stage before your senior year. We haven’t made an exception like this in twenty years."
Director Zhao laid out these conditions all at once, causing the expressions of the two people beside him to change immediately. These were the best terms they, too, could offer.
"Xiangjiang Academy can offer the same terms. Wang Lan, although you’re in the Tianjian Bureau system, both the Tianjian Bureau and Xiangjiang Academy report directly to the Ministry of Defense. We have a complete military academy system with significant connections and networks within the military. If you continue to work within the military system, these connections and networks are invaluable. They will bring unimaginable convenience to your future work and promotions."
"Wang Lan, Jinghua Star Martial Arts Academy can also offer the same terms. Moreover, I think you might have heard a saying: Imperial Capital Star Martial Arts Academy focuses on research and further studies, while Jinghua Star Martial Arts Academy is where you learn to fight. Your talent should be displayed on the battlefield, not wasted in some sealed laboratory, tearing your hair out over a research project."
"Old Pang, you’re mistaken there. Hasn’t our Imperial Capital Star Martial Arts Academy produced many powerful warriors? The Southern Flame Emperor is from our academy."
"We also have the Northern Nether Emperor! Besides, was the Southern Flame Emperor really trained by Imperial Capital Star Martial Arts Academy? Wasn’t he trained by Eld Di? And now Eld Di is..." Director Pang’s words abruptly ceased.
"Oh? Did I just hear someone mention Eld Di? Why did you stop?" The conference room door was gently pushed open, and a woman as beautiful as a fairy walked in. "My apologies, esteemed seniors, I’m late," she said. "Wang Lan, let me introduce myself. I am Sun Li, a recruitment teacher from Modu City Star Martial Arts Academy."
Seeing the hand Sun Li extended, Wang Lan touched it lightly. "Hello, Teacher."
"Modu City Star Martial Arts Academy is here too. Good, now everyone has arrived. Wang Lan, what is your choice?" Director Zhao stared sharply at Wang Lan. Suddenly, Wang Lan felt immense pressure emanating from the four individuals before him.
"Well, Wang Lan, I arrived late and haven’t had a chance to properly introduce our academy. But that’s alright; I imagine you’re already very familiar with Modu City Star Martial Arts Academy. Eld Di thinks highly of you. Before I left, he specifically instructed me to give you as much freedom of choice as possible. On behalf of the academy, I promise you an S-level Star Martial Skill. You’ll be grouped with elite team members, receive lessons from elite teachers, and we will prioritize a student slot for you. We guarantee to help you reach the peak of the Galaxy Stage before graduation. These terms should adequately represent our sincerity, shouldn’t they?"
"Teacher Sun, I am truly flattered by your esteemed academy’s interest. But right now... with all these excellent offers, it’s really difficult for me to make an immediate choice. Perhaps..." Wang Lan blinked frantically, trying to send a hint.
"Alright, I’ll give you ten minutes to consider. If the pressure is too much, you can leave the room to think it over. Return in ten minutes with your answer." Ignoring Wang Lan’s hints, Sun Li casually flicked her head and looked at the other three. "And you? Anything else to add?"
"We’ve said all that needs to be said. The choice is up to Wang Lan now."
"Agreed!"
"Let’s leave it at that."
The four great Star Martial Academies were, after all, institutions at the apex. Even if they desperately wanted Wang Lan, they still had to maintain a dignified facade. They couldn’t act like merchants, clinging to someone and refusing to let go. They had laid out their offers and stated their respective advantages; the choice naturally fell to Wang Lan. Furthermore, they were all confident in their own academies. Each believed their institution offered unique advantages that Wang Lan needed and that others could not replicate.
They exchanged glances, then quietly looked away from each other.
As for Modu City Star Martial Arts Academy, the other three were least concerned. Previously, they had worried that Modu City Star Martial Arts Academy held too great an advantage, prompting them to rush over and try to secure Wang Lan first. But now, it appeared Modu City Star Martial Arts Academy wasn’t giving Wang Lan enough importance, having sent only a recruitment teacher.
Perhaps Eld Di did strongly desire to recruit Wang Lan. But after the recent assassination attempt on him, his entire faction was preoccupied with finding who was secretly paving the way for the Demon Clan and providing cover for Paradise Bird’s entry. They were likely too busy to be concerned with this.
This was just as well. With their biggest competitor seemingly sidelined, the other three Star Martial Academies felt more confident.
Stepping out of the conference room, Wang Lan heaved a long sigh.
This is truly a deadly dilemma. No matter which one I choose, I’m bound to offend the other three. Rejecting an ordinary Star Martial Academy’s invitation is one thing, but rejecting invitations from the top three Star Martial Academies... I can guarantee I’ll be headline news tomorrow. Reporters are ubiquitous, and unscrupulous media outlets will stop at nothing for a sensational headline. If I leave a bad impression on these teachers and they speak ill of me when they return, I’ll likely gain many unknown enemies, won’t I? But a choice had to be made; he had to pick one.
"DING-DONG—" His phone chimed with a text message; it was from Jiang Xinyu.
Strange, shouldn’t Jiang Xinyu be in class right now? Why would she send me a message... especially when she knows I’m busy...
Lost in thought, he unlocked his phone. Upon seeing the message’s content, a peculiar expression immediately crossed Wang Lan’s face.

chapters.title: Chapter 249: Because It’s Close to Home
chapters.content:
Chapter 249: Chapter 249: Because It’s Close to Home
"The Modu Star Martial Academy just contacted me and invited me to enroll as well," Jiang Xinyu’s message read.
"Also?" Wang Lan quickly sent a question mark.
"Yes, haven’t you already agreed to attend the Modu Star Martial Academy with Eld Di? That way we can be together and won’t have to separate," she replied.
"Did Mrs. Sun tell you that?" he asked.
"Yeah, wasn’t it?" Jiang Xinyu’s message came back quickly.
Seeing this, Wang Lan suddenly showed a strange smile. No wonder the Modu Star Martial Academy was the last to arrive; they were playing such a cunning trick, undermining the others.
"Right, yeah! I forgot to tell you earlier," Wang Lan hurriedly replied.
The enrollment conditions offered by the four major Star Martial Academies were roughly the same, and Wang Lan would have been very satisfied with any of them. However, each academy had its own advantages, making the decision quite difficult. But now that Jiang Xinyu had chosen the Modu Star Martial Academy, Wang Lan no longer needed to struggle over which one to choose.
He put away his phone and took a deep breath.
Turning around, he pushed open the door and entered the conference room.
"Have you decided, Wang Lan?" one of the teachers asked as he entered.
Everyone in the conference room stopped their discussions or put down what they were doing and looked up at him.
"Esteemed teachers, I have made my decision. I have decided to enroll in the Modu Star Martial Academy," he declared.
As Wang Lan finished speaking, a mysterious smile appeared on Sun Li’s face, while the expressions of the other three representatives didn’t change much, showing only a hint of regret.
The four major Star Martial Academies were comparable in strength, and the conditions they offered were also similar. It was only natural for Wang Lan to pick any one of them, and choosing one naturally meant forgoing the other three.
But even though Wang Lan had given his answer, the representatives from the other three academies weren’t ready to give up just yet.
Director Zhao leaned back in his chair, arms folded, watching Wang Lan. "Wang Lan, can you tell me why you chose the Modu Star Martial Academy? Or rather, why didn’t you choose one of our three institutions?"
Wang Lan shot Sun Li a desperate look, but she merely returned a helpless gesture. His face fell, and a wry smile appeared. "Do I have to answer?"
"You must answer," Director Pang stated firmly, staring at Wang Lan.
"Because... Modu City is closer to home," Wang Lan said, a shy, innocent smile on his face. "I’ve grown up here and never left Suzhou City. The Imperial Capital and Xiangjiang are so far away... I’m a bit reluctant to be away from family and friends.
"Modu City is so close. If I want to go home, I can return on a Saturday or Sunday. It only takes two hours," he explained.
All three of them were taken aback. No one had expected Wang Lan’s reason to be so simple. They had imagined he would offer countless reasons for choosing Modu City, but they had never considered proximity to home!
Director Zhao sighed deeply. "Alright, since you’ve made your choice, we won’t pressure you. Wang Lan, I hear you have a good relationship with Jiang Xinyu. Do you have her phone number?"
"I do," Wang Lan replied, the corners of his mouth twitching slightly as he maintained a serious expression.
"Give her a call and ask her to come over."
"What, Director Zhao, have you taken an interest in Jiang Xinyu? She only ranked ninth," Director Pang asked indifferently.
"But her performance was also very impressive, and she has met the admission standards of the Imperial Capital Star Martial Academy. If I can’t recruit Wang Lan, surely you wouldn’t want me to have come all this way for nothing?" Director Zhao replied.
"Director Zhao, I’m afraid you really have made this trip for nothing," Sun Li said with a triumphant smile. "Before I came here, Jiang Xinyu had already agreed to attend the Modu Star Martial Academy."
"Hmm? You went to see Jiang Xinyu first?" Major General Yu looked at Sun Li with a puzzled expression, a speculative glint in his eyes as he seemingly hit upon a guess.
"Yes, it was on the way, so recruiting Jiang Xinyu hardly caused any delay," Sun Li replied.
"Sigh! Your Modu City moves fast, snatching away both promising talents from Suzhou No. 1 Middle School. Well, this was a wasted trip," Director Zhao said, standing up and walking out of the conference room.
"Then I, too, will take my leave," Major General Yu declared, standing and departing with a robust and imposing gait.
Soon, only Wang Lan and Sun Li remained in the conference room. Sun Li waved at Wang Lan. "Come here and fill out the application form."
Wang Lan did as instructed, quickly filling out the form with the pen Sun Li handed him, occasionally catching a whiff of a delicate fragrance from her.
"Now that we’re alone, Wang Lan, I’d like to hear your real reason for choosing the Modu Star Martial Academy," she said.
"Doesn’t Mrs. Sun already know? Why state the obvious?" he replied.
"So my strategy worked? Don’t worry, my promises to you will stand, and your little girlfriend will also receive much better treatment than the average student," she assured him.
Once Wang Lan finished filling out the form, a notification suddenly sounded in his mind: "BEEP. Congratulations to the Host for being directly admitted to the Modu Star Martial Academy, completing the task ’Enter one of the Four Great Star Martial Academies.’ Reward: 20,000 Experience Points, 1,000 Skill Points."
"Teacher, although these conditions are very favorable to me, I’m puzzled. Won’t this special treatment bring disadvantages? Like, people being jealous?"
"There’s usually no such issue, because this is standard practice at Star Martial Academies. Their guiding principles have never been fairness, justice, and transparency, nor are they about those slogans on banners you see at elementary school entrances that often display phrases like:
"’Everything for the children, for the sake of all children.’
"Star Martial Academies operate on the principle of survival of the fittest," Sun Li continued, her voice firm. "As long as you perform well enough, you’ll stand out and receive special consideration.
"The privileges offered to you aren’t unique; you’ve just been promised them in advance. In fact, the more outstanding students need these less. Even without preferential resource allocation, they’ll quickly distinguish themselves after enrollment, and the academy’s resources will naturally favor such excellent students.
"The sole purpose of Star Martial Academies is to cultivate outstanding students, and to train even more of them.
"Jealous? What’s there to be jealous about? If you’re capable, strive to be better than others. Excel, and you’ll have everything. If you’re mediocre, naturally, you’ll end up with nothing."
Hearing Sun Li’s explanation, Wang Lan felt reassured.
"Is it similar to the survival principles of the Sect Gates in those Star Martial Art novels?"
"Quite similar. You can consider Star Martial Academies worldwide as Sect Gates, with the four major academies being the largest and strongest among them. The only difference is that all these Sect Gates are under state management, and they aren’t allowed to fight amongst themselves or plunder resources."
"I heard that after we enroll in a Star Martial Academy, our actual combat training will no longer take place in Trial Fields? We’ll enter Pioneer Spaces, or go abroad to offer support?" Wang Lan asked with concern.
"Correct! Star Martial Warriors cannot improve their strength without Soul Beads, and Soul Beads are only found within the Exotic Beasts of Different Dimensional Spaces. Trial Fields are for junior Star Martial Warriors to improve in a relatively safe environment. Anyone admitted to Modu Star Martial Academy is at least at the Star Cloud Stage of cultivation. Why would they still go to such comfortable places as Trial Fields?
"Your actual combat will take place in Pioneer Spaces, or you might receive invitations for international support missions, sending you to volatile regions. Of course, going abroad is much more dangerous than operating in our own Pioneer Spaces. But the rewards are also greater: you don’t have to surrender a portion of the Soul Beads to the host country—you can pocket all of them and also receive a hefty mercenary fee.
"From the day you officially enroll in Modu Star Martial Academy, though you are students, you will already be protectors of the nation and the world. At that moment, you become true warriors. And because of your inherent excellence, you will be even more distinguished than Pioneers or members of the Star Martial Army.
"For ordinary people, getting into college means liberation. College life is countless times more relaxed than the preceding twelve years of schooling. For Star Martial Warriors, however, it’s the opposite; college marks the true beginning of an arduous journey.
"Wang Lan, you and Jiang Xinyu are both exceptionally talented; few in Suzhou City can compare to you. But you should have also seen how many in Jiang Province are your equals or even superior? Over thirty such individuals participated in the provincial martial arts competition alone, not to mention those who didn’t.
"Modu Star Martial Academy recruits nationwide. Here, in Suzhou City, you and Jiang Xinyu might be considered peerless prodigies. But after you enroll, you’ll discover just how many geniuses there are. Never think you’re *the* genius. Once you enter the academy, you’ll find it’s full of them."
"Yes!" Wang Lan promptly nodded in understanding.
"Anything else you want to ask?"
"How do we learn Star Martial Skills? I mean, after enrollment, where do we gain access to learning them? Are they taught collectively by teachers?"
"Teachers provide hands-on instruction for subject-specific knowledge, practical combat experience, and during combat internships. For other things, like learning and developing Star Martial Skills, teachers can only offer guidance.
"After all, Star Martial Skills are transmitted directly into the mind through inscriptions. This includes not just the cultivation methods but also the experiential insights of the Star Martial Skill. Since everything is directly infused into your mind, there’s naturally no need for others to elaborate further.
"As for the source of Star Martial Skills, the academy has a Star Martial Skills Hall—you can just go and purchase them there."
"That easy?" Wang Lan’s eyes instantly lit up.
For him, anything that could be bought with money was generally easy to obtain.
"Don’t get too excited. The currency for purchasing Star Martial Skills isn’t money, but points. These points, also known as Academic Credit, are earned through your performance at the academy. Examples include participating in community service activities, maintaining perfect attendance in classes, passing exams, and assisting with school administration through the student council, among other things. You’ll learn the specifics of how to earn Academic Credit after you enroll. In any case, the primary task for freshmen is to study theoretical knowledge and accumulate Academic Credit. You’ll have a full year to understand all this. If you have no other questions, I’ll be going. Your admission notice will be mailed to you in a few days."
"Safe travels, Teacher. Goodbye, Teacher."
"Oh, by the way," Sun Li suddenly paused as she reached the door and turned back to ask, "although your combat strength is impressive, you’re still considered a Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior, right?"
"Am I... considered one?"
Wang Lan wasn’t sure how to answer. He wanted to say that although he could fight well, he was still in the Medical Attribute. But it wasn’t up to him; it depended on whether others would agree. People had seen Medical Attribute Star Martial Warriors who could take a beating, but never one who could fight like *him*. *Am I considered one? No, you’re not worthy!*
"Yes!" Sun Li said, beckoning to Wang Lan with a finger. "I’m a Medical Attribute teacher too, you know. Remember to sign up for my class."
"Oh..."
As Sun Li left, Wang Lan breathed a sigh of relief.
But he had completely forgotten her invitation almost as soon as she’d made it.
Medical Attribute? Did he even need to enroll in classes? Even Star Sea Stage Medical Attribute Star Martial Warriors probably didn’t have his healing abilities, did they?
After leaving the conference room and returning to his classroom, all eyes were fixed on Wang Lan.
This was the guy who had already been admitted to one of the four major Star Martial Academies. While others were desperately cramming for the college entrance exams less than twenty days away, he could legitimately sleep through classes, attending school merely for show.
It was downright infuriating to watch.
"Ahem—Wang Lan, go back to your seat. Don’t disturb the other students’ studies," the teacher in charge of the class said softly.
That sounded as if I used to cause trouble in class or something.

chapters.title: Chapter 250: A Rare Moment of Leisure
chapters.content:
Chapter 250: Chapter 250: A Rare Moment of Leisure
Several days later, the acceptance letter from Modu City Star Martial Academy was in hand. Jiang Xinyu received hers on the same day. Meanwhile, the rest of the classmates were working hard for the college entrance exam.
Apart from Wang Lan and Jiang Xinyu, Zhuang Haotian and Gong Feiyu were allotted spots by Zezhou Star Martial Academy. Xu Xiangwen originally wanted to join Gong Feiyu. Unfortunately, Zezhou Star Martial Academy did not extend an invitation to him, so he had no choice but to diligently prepare for the exams.
Regarding this, Xu Xiangwen had something to say.
He and Gong Feiyu were eliminated in the same round, so why did Zezhou Star Martial Academy look down on him? Even Zhuang Haotian got a recommendation despite being knocked out in the first round, yet he didn’t.
In response, as a good brother, Wang Lan naturally had to console him properly.
"Xiangwen, don’t feel discouraged. Isn’t it just a reserved spot? With your strength, getting into a top Star Martial Academy is as easy as turning your hand over. Besides, so what if Zezhou Star Martial Academy doesn’t appreciate you? Their lack of interest only proves that they aren’t blind. Look, Jin City Star Warrior Academy didn’t contact you either."
The first part sounded sincere. However, the latter part provoked Xu Xiangwen, who was standing at the edge of the rooftop, to turn and pounce on Wang Lan.
"Ah, I-I-I— I’m gonna fight it out with you!"
"Relax, Xiangwen, even if you end up in some no-name university, we brothers won’t look down on you, and we’ll still carry you in the future," Gong Feiyu added insult to injury at just the right moment, scattering a handful of salt on the wound.
"You shouldn’t say such things... Xiangwen is already pitiful. Why pour salt on his wounds?" Xie Sisi said softly, feeling somewhat sympathetic.
That remark would have been better left unsaid. As soon as she spoke, Xu Xiangwen retreated into his shell.
That kind of comfort was worse than saying nothing at all.
"It’s fine, I’m tough as nails; I’ve got the mental fortitude. So what if Zezhou doesn’t appreciate me? I don’t give a damn. With my strength, I could pass their exam. I’ll exceed their passing score by twenty points and still won’t attend their crappy school. I’ve decided, I’m going for Jin City Star Warrior Academy."
"Jin City? Not coming with me?" Gong Feiyu was slightly taken aback. His ruthless teasing wasn’t meant to kick Xu Xiangwen when he was down. With Xu Xiangwen’s strength, getting into any top Star Martial Academy was practically a sure thing.
Moreover, there were eight other top-tier second-level Star Martial Academies nationally that weren’t inferior to Zezhou Star Martial Academy. Xu Xiangwen would undoubtedly be accepted by one of them. Not receiving a recommendation wasn’t necessarily because they looked down on him, but possibly because there were limited slots.
For someone with real strength, direct admission isn’t important—they could easily choose where to go even with the college entrance exam. Of course, that excludes the top four Star Martial Academies.
"Psh, why would I bother with them when they’re so blind? Don’t I have any dignity? Besides, Jin City Star Warrior Academy has always been my goal. If a top-tier Star Martial Academy had offered me a spot, I might’ve gone, but without one, Jin City is my first choice."
"Sigh— How many Star Martial Academies’ recommendations have you refused these days?" Gong Feiyu shook his head and sighed lightly. "Luzhou Star Martial, Wuling Star Martial, these are no worse than Zezhou Star Martial, you know."
"I’m not interested in any that rank beyond the top ten!" Xu Xiangwen declared confidently, waving his hand dismissively.
"Old Xu is mighty."
"Speaking of which, Sisi, which one are you aiming for?"
"Hmm..." Xie Sisi looked down shyly, a bit embarrassed. "Jin City, I guess."
"Eh?" Xu Xiangwen looked at Xie Sisi in surprise. Even Jiang Xinyu turned to look at her curiously.
"I know it’s difficult to get into Jin City, and I’m slightly lacking in strength. But... my theoretical grades are decent, plus I have experience participating in the provincial tournament, and I possess an above-average talent for Star Power control. If I perform a little better, I think I can give it a try."
"That’s true; if it weren’t for Sisi’s late development, her potential wouldn’t be inferior to Xinyu’s or mine."
"Lanzi, what makes you say Sisi developed late? That figure... tsk tsk tsk!" Xu Xiangwen’s suggestive comments always hit the mark so precisely.
"Lanzi, from your tone, it seems like you think our talents are no good?" Gong Feiyu asked with a menacing grin.
"Are you trying to deny it?" Wang Lan bluntly rolled his eyes.
In the group of five, if they were to rank innate talents, Wang Lan was practically a cheat, followed by Jiang Xinyu, then Xie Sisi in third place. Xu Xiangwen was fourth due to his Inborn Talent of the Bloodline and great potential, while Gong Feiyu’s talent was actually quite average. Of course, this ’average’ was in comparison to someone with a specialty like Wang Lan. Gong Feiyu was of the Earth attribute and didn’t possess any special Innate Abilities. His fighting style was stable, effective in defense. In Suzhou City, he was considered a top-notch seed, but nationally, there were many better than him.
This was also why Xu Xiangwen said Zezhou Star Martial Academy was blind. In terms of raw power, Xu Xiangwen wasn’t necessarily better than Gong Feiyu, but when it came to potential, he was far superior. Xu Xiangwen was bound to be one of the prominent figures in the future.
「In the upcoming days」
Wang Lan’s life was simply going to and from school. The pace was slow and the mood, pleasant. Frankly, ever since he awakened that damn system in elementary school, Wang Lan had never been this relaxed.
To activate the system, he had been working hard every day to improve himself; his nerves were always taut. After successfully activating the system, he struggled to keep up with Jiang Xinyu and the others. He went through so much peril to earn skill points and to level up.
Now, finally having been accepted by Modu City Star Martial Academy, one stage of his accomplishment was complete. Though the road ahead was still fraught with thorns, and the threat of the Demon Clan loomed like the sword of Damocles overhead, Wang Lan could truly take a break at this moment. He could rest for at least one summer vacation.
Days without the need to toil passed quickly.
The calendar turned from May to June. June 5th was the day of the college entrance exam for the Star Martial Arts Campus, also the province-wide joint exam. However, Wang Lan wouldn’t be partaking in such a grand event.
Xu Xiangwen took the college entrance exam while Wang Lan and others who didn’t need to take it went straight on vacation. Once he left school, he completely relaxed.
He didn’t feel the pressure of studying while in school. However, seeing his classmates sprinting, Wang Lan also attended classes and practiced questions with them. After the vacation started, Wang Lan turned into a complete slacker. Drinking tea with Jiang Xinyu and playing games with Gong Feiyu, five or six days passed without notice.
Suddenly finding himself completely idle, Wang Lan started to feel unaccustomed. He sensed that his entire being was becoming sluggish. Once he noticed a decline in his physical condition, he became alarmed; even during summer vacation, this was no good.
But the training ground was being renovated, and the practice area at home was too small. Moreover, it felt particularly awkward to hold back during fights after having gone all out during the provincial martial arts competition.
When Wang Lan shared this trouble with Xu Shiyun, Xu Shiyun instantly replied, "Are you just looking for trouble because you’re bored? Is it that hard to stay in shape? Come to the Bureau, train every day, and I guarantee you will be in top form every single day."
"
Maybe I was just born with a masochistic streak,
" Wang Lan muttered to himself after driving to the Tianjian Bureau and getting out of his car.
When busy, he complained about how exhausting life was and wished to lie down without a care, perhaps for a lifetime. But after actually lying down for a few days, he felt as if he had lost his soul. He couldn’t help running back to the Tianjian Bureau to request more training.
Apart from the internal training ground at the Tianjian Bureau, there was also a massive training ground in a Folding Space. Wang Lan had heard of it but never visited before. It had been a year since he joined the Tianjian Bureau. However, he was either busy studying or busy catching spies, so the time he actually spent at the Tianjian Bureau was indeed very short.
Among the Red Captains, Wang Lan was perhaps the only one who hadn’t been to the Folding Space training ground.
Folding Space technology was truly next-level, almost unbelievable tech. It was said to be made from Space Stones, which only come from Different Dimensional Spaces. However, Space Stones are also a nationally banned item. Anyway, the state’s control over Space Stones is even stricter than over drugs.
Approaching a huge iron door similar to the ones at the training ground, Xu Shiyun pressed his palm on the door sensor, and the door slowly opened. Blinding white light shone through, completely swallowing their figures.
Entering the Folding Space Training Room, they saw an endless gray land along with an endless pale sky. Far off in the distance, people were chasing and fighting in the vast space.
"This place, is it similar to a Different Dimensional Space?" Wang Lan asked as he looked around.
"It’s not just similar, it is one!" Xu Shiyun casually threw his cigarette butt into the space, and it instantly went out.
"See that? The way things burn here is different. Every time I bring a cig in, I have to relight it," Xu Shiyun said as he pulled out another cigarette. "Here, give me a light."
Wang Lan produced a flame from his fingertip to light the boss’s cigarette. "Since it’s a Different Dimensional Space, how come there are no Exotic Beasts?"
"Killed them all. We used Space Stones to carve out a Different Dimensional Space. Then, we slaughtered all the Exotic Beasts and reinforced the spatial nodes. What’s left is a good space for storing supplies or for training."
As he spoke, Xu Shiyun pointed to the distant figures flickering in the space. "Those are brothers from the Bureau. Don’t be shy, just go and practice with them. Plus, learning Star Martial Skills here is also a good idea. It seems Lige has been in seclusion here for the last half month."
"Doesn’t he need to do missions?"
"He’s learning a new Star Martial Skill, so he’s in seclusion for training."
"Speaking of which, I also learned a new Star Martial Skill recently. I haven’t found the right place to test it out, but it seems like I can do so here."
"You can drop the ’seems.’ This place’s biggest advantage is you can unleash Star Martial Skills freely." As they spoke, the two walked to a relatively open spot.
"Oh, Captain Wang is here? What a rare guest."
"Seems like the first time I’ve seen Captain Wang come here."
A few nearby brothers stopped their sparring and called out to Wang Lan. They recognized him, but Wang Lan didn’t recognize them, so he could only nod in response.
"Captain Wang, you’re super famous now, called the strongest high school student in Jiang Province’s history. Also, what was that Star Martial Skill you displayed the other day? It was so powerful."
"If you shouldn’t ask, then don’t. Why so nosy? Need motivation to train, or should I help you?" Xu Shiyun immediately shouted.
"No need, no need, just taking a short break," the two quickly scattered, apologizing and moving away from Xu Shiyun.
"Wang Lan, what’s the new Star Martial Skill you learned? Was it the prize for winning the provincial martial arts competition?"
"Yes, it’s a fire-type Star Martial Skill, Earth Surge Fire Sea."
"Which one?" Xu Shiyun suddenly exclaimed beside him.
"Earth Surge Fire Sea. You seem very surprised?"
"That’s an S-level Star Martial Skill!"
"Yes, a reward of an S-level Star Martial Skill. Is that surprising?"
Seeing Wang Lan’s nonchalant attitude, Xu Shiyun seriously wanted to slap him.
"I don’t even have an S-level Star Martial Skill. Also, even Director Wang and the others have at most one S-level Star Martial Skill to their names. And you, a high school student... you already have an S-level Star Martial Skill!"
"I’ve already graduated," Wang Lan responded coolly, his Star Power suddenly surging around him.
"Wait! What are you doing? Start slow. Don’t just go wasting Star Power trying to cast it outright."
"Start slow? Why do it slowly?"
"Don’t you need to follow steps when learning a Star Martial Skill?"
"Do you?"
You’re putting on an act, pretending! Who learns Star Martial Skills without steps? Heck, even going to the toilet to take a dump has the step of pulling down your pants, right?
But just as this thought crossed his mind, the scene before him was so shocking that he was left speechless.

chapters.title: Chapter 251 The Beast
chapters.content:
Chapter 251: Chapter 251 The Beast
Wang Lan’s hands pressed against the ground, and suddenly the earth in front of him turned crimson, as if transforming into surging magma. Without warning, bright red flames burst forth from the ground like an erupting volcano, fiercely scorching everything within thirty meters.
Less than a month had passed since the provincial Star Martial Art competition ended. An S-level Star Martial Skill, learned in such a short time?
It was only when the cigarette burned down to his fingers that Xu Shiyun suddenly realized and hurriedly threw the butt away. Unbeknownst to him, a large group of warriors from the Tianjian Bureau had gathered around Wang Lan.
They seemed fine, simply watching curiously as Wang Lan manipulated the Star Martial Skill, changing the position and shape of the flames.
Not until he felt his Star Power waning did Wang Lan finally stop.
"The furthest I can control it is thirty-five meters; any further and the Star Power won’t cover it. Although it’s an S-level Star Martial Skill, its power is somewhat disappointing. The enemy won’t just stand there; they could escape thirty-five meters in an instant. Could this S-level Star Martial Skill be a fake?"
"Scram!" Xu Shiyun lifted his foot as if to kick.
"Even if it is an S-level Star Martial Skill, you’ve only just mastered it, alright? To unleash its true power, you need to at least reach the Galaxy Stage. A range of thirty-five meters is already impressive, but you also have to consider the flame temperature. I’m standing behind you and I can feel the intense heatwave. This flame’s temperature could instantly kill someone. Moreover, this technique has tremendous potential. You should look to the Fire Emperor for reference. Earth Surge Fire Sea is the Fire Emperor’s signature move. It covers a hundred-meter range with purple flames that instantly devour everything. You know, the Fire Emperor once single-handedly flattened an entire Different Dimensional Space, right?"
Wang Lan had just mastered Earth Surge Fire Sea, and he was still at Gold One. Most of his other Star Martial Skills were also at Gold One; only skills like Crescent Arrow and Flame Sword had been upgraded to Gold Two.
Ever since his skills reached the Gold level, skill points were becoming increasingly insufficient. Doing small tasks was utterly useless. Thankfully, once university started, there would be annual real-world internships, which might make earning skill points easier.
There’s an old saying: "In the mountains, there’s no calendar." This was also true for Wang Lan, who was in the Folding Space. Had Xu Shiyun not informed him, Wang Lan would have been unaware that he had been in the Folding Space for over ten days.
In the Different Dimensional Space, without the distinction of day and night, any sense of time was completely disordered. Wang Lan only knew to rest when he was tired. Once his energy was replenished, he would spar with his teammates. At the Tianjian Bureau, especially in the Folding Space training ground, most were at the Star Cloud Stage, every one of them a battle-hardened veteran.
This suited the current Wang Lan perfectly. Over the past ten days, Wang Lan progressed from occasionally being caught up in the rhythm of his Tianjian Bureau comrades to having virtually no openings. To beat Wang Lan now, one would have to rely on sheer strength to overpower him. This improvement was visibly apparent.
Though his brothers didn’t speak of it, deep down they were all genuinely impressed by Wang Lan.
"Brothers, I’m going to step out for a couple of days to rest up, then I’ll be back. Don’t miss me too much."
"Go ahead, and it’d be better if you don’t come back."
"Exactly. There’s not much more we can teach you. What’s left is improving your own strength; you’re not lacking in combat experience anymore," several Red Elites said dismissively, shooing him away with disdain.
Upon leaving the Folding Space and turning on his recently retrieved phone, a barrage of buzzing notifications erupted.
Although he had informed the others that he would be training at the Tianjian Bureau, he hadn’t expected to be completely out of touch for ten straight days.
Xu Xiangwen had sent the most messages, each one reeking of his eagerness to show off.
"Lanzi, I scored four hundred and thirty points, hahaha... That’s thirty points more than the admission score for Zezhou Star Martial Academy! But I won’t list their school as a preference. I’m going to show them. The face I lost, I will personally reclaim."
"Still alive? If you are, give a sign."
"When are you getting out of jail? When you do, your bro’s treating you to drinks."
It was almost a message a day. Between the lines, one could detect a single thought: ’Hurry up and come out, I’m dying to show off.’
"I’m out! How’s everyone?"
DING DONG! Almost three seconds after the message was sent, Xu Xiangwen replied.
"Lanzi, you’re finally back from the dead! I thought you were a goner. Tonight at six, Eastern Heaven Gate, Longmen Inn."
"OK!"
"Lanzi, I scored four hundred and thirty points! One hundred and seventy in theory, two hundred and sixty in combat. In the combat exam, I ranked first in Suzhou City and fourth in Jiang Province. Awesome, right?"
Four hundred and thirty? Is that a lot?
Wang Lan felt it necessary to curb his friend’s burgeoning arrogance. He was already so arrogant. Who knew what he’d be like at the gathering later?
"First in Suzhou City? That’s not bad. I guess those who did better than you must have been recommended for admission, right?"
After sending two messages in a row, there was no reply from the other side. But Gong Feiyu chimed in at just the right moment with a jab.
"Lanzi, don’t be harsh. It’s rare for the ’mountain’ to be without a ’tiger.’ Let him play king for a while, even if he’s just deceiving himself."
"Just wait, I’ll roast you all tonight."
Deep into the night, Wang Lan’s steps were slightly unsteady as he ambled towards Xinyu Building, the brilliant lights at his back.
During dinner, everyone had been in high spirits. Overwhelmed by the mood, Wang Lan, who normally didn’t drink, broke his routine and had two bottles of beer.
In Xu Xiangwen’s opinion, could beer even count as alcohol? It was more like a beverage at most. But for Wang Lan, the difference between two bottles of beer and two bottles of baijiu wasn’t significant. After one bottle, Wang Lan’s face turned red, and after two, his head felt like it had grown a whole size bigger.
Although he was a bit dizzy, he was still conscious. After declining Jiang Xinyu’s offer to see him home, Wang Lan went back by himself.
Just as he arrived at the building’s entrance, a warm breeze blew by, and Wang Lan instantly became alert.
He stopped in his tracks, his back tensing. "Who’s there?"
"Wang Lan, it’s me..." Xie Sisi’s voice rang out as she emerged from around a nearby corner. Seeing Xie Sisi, Wang Lan immediately relaxed, a smile spreading across his face at her meticulously dolled-up appearance.
"Sisi, what are you doing here? I invited you to the get-together earlier, why didn’t you come?"
The sound of high heels on the tiled floor grew closer, and Wang Lan’s expression suddenly became serious. "Is that you? How did you get out? What happened?"
Although the person in front of him was still Xie Sisi, from the look in her eyes, Wang Lan instantly recognized that this was Xie Sisi’s second personality—a hidden one that only emerged when Xie Sisi was in danger.
"There’s no danger, she’s fine!" Xie Sisi came up to Wang Lan, naturally hooking her arm around his, and said gently, "Walk with me."
"Sure!"
The two walked slowly under the streetlights along the internal path.
"She scored 410, ten points above the admission cutoff for Jin City Star Warrior Academy."
"Mm, I heard from Xiangwen. Congratulations. By the way, you *are* her, why do you refer to her as ’she’?"
"I am different from her," Xie Sisi said calmly, "she’s very happy. After awakening her Star Martial talent, she has never been this joyful. A few days ago, her parents threw a celebratory feast for her, and all her relatives and friends attended. Thank you. If it weren’t for you and Xinyu, she definitely wouldn’t have gotten into such a good school. Now that she’s admitted to Jin City Star Warrior Academy, she won’t need my protection anymore. In the future, she’ll become a strong and brave warrior, right?"
"Of course. She’s already a strong and brave warrior."
"I have to go," Xie Sisi suddenly stopped and said with a hint of sadness.
"Go?" Wang Lan was taken aback, looking at Xie Sisi. "You mean..."
"I’ve said before that the day Sisi no longer needs my protection, I’ll disappear. My existence is due to her inner fear and weakness. But now, she’s no longer afraid or weak, so it’s time for me to vanish."
The disappearance of this personality was undoubtedly good for Xie Sisi. A normal person shouldn’t have dual personalities. However, Wang Lan felt a strange sense of melancholy welling up from deep within.
Her existence was a mistake, but at the same time, she was so innocent. She had been protecting Xie Sisi from the shadows for many years, and now, no longer needed, she was to vanish like smoke.
From a scientific perspective, an independent personality is, in essence, a separate person. Even though she shared a body with Xie Sisi, she had a life as unique as Xie Sisi’s. For this Xie Sisi, disappearing was akin to dying.
"Don’t feel sorry for me. It was destined from the moment I came into existence. If I were never to disappear, it would mean she had never overcome her psychological shadows. Today, see me off. I’ll buy you a drink," she said, pointing and smiling at the flickering lights of a bar across the street.
A sliver of sunlight came streaming through the gap in the curtains, striking Wang Lan’s eyelids directly. He fluttered his eyelids slightly and let out a soft groan.
Slowly opening his eyes, he gently held his forehead.
This feeling was like being in the grips of a severe cold.
Sick?
Obviously not. Star Martial Warriors rarely get sick, especially not from something like a cold.
Last night, after drinking with Xu Xiangwen and the others, he had left the party and headed home, then encountered... Xie Sisi’s second personality. And then, they had gone to a bar... then a toast to the past, a toast to tomorrow, a toast to dreams, a toast to death.
And in the end, he remembered nothing.
Raising his head to survey his surroundings, there was no doubt he was in his own home. Clothes were scattered on the floor, looking almost as if they had been torn off.
Suddenly, Wang Lan’s gaze cleared, and he sat up abruptly.
With a stiff neck, he slowly turned his head. A bare, pale form was curled up in the bedding, sleeping soundly.
Could I have behaved like a beast?
The words struck his mind like a thunderbolt.
Probably!
After drinking himself into a stupor last night, he had likely lost all sense of reason. What occurred afterward seemed to just fall into place.
Only... to experience my first time like this, without any recollection? Even if it wasn’t my first time in two lifetimes, still...
Wang Lan carefully lifted the blanket, worried he might wake Xie Sisi.
If this were a TV drama, upon waking up and discovering what they had done, there would be an earth-shattering scream, followed by her pointing at him in profound grief.
In that brief moment, Wang Lan had already mentally drafted an apology and a pledge.
Just as he was about to get out of bed, suddenly, a pair of soft, jade-like arms tightly embraced him.
"Wang Lan... I’m sorry. I really didn’t mean to scheme against you... Last night I... I drank too much as well... Wang Lan, I didn’t intentionally try to come between you two..."
Xie Sisi was already awake. But why wasn’t her reaction following the script?

chapters.title: Chapter 252 Reporting
chapters.content:
Chapter 252: Chapter 252 Reporting
Wang Lan’s silence made Xie Sisi even more panicked. "Wang Lan, believe me. Although I like you, I am not the kind of woman who would scheme. It was really an accident yesterday. Please don’t think of me as that kind of despicable woman, okay...?"
"Sisi, with what you’re saying, it sounds as if I’m the one who lost out," Wang Lan said with a wry smile, patting Xie Sisi’s hand. "Actually, that wasn’t you... How should I put it? You’ve always had another personality."
Xie Sisi was unaware of the existence of another her. Perhaps that was the other Xie Sisi’s tragedy. She was like Xie Sisi’s Guardian Angel, silently protecting her. Yet, the one she protected never knew of her guardian’s existence.
It was like the many ordinary people who are always protected by Star Martial Warriors but lavishly praise the peaceful times. How many truly understand that the so-called peaceful times are merely the result of someone else shouldering the burdens?
"My other personality?" Although Xie Sisi had stopped crying, her grip on Wang Lan’s arm tightened. "Why don’t I know about it?"
"Do you remember that time you were drugged? How could you possibly have escaped under those circumstances, let alone when you’d been shot? It was your second personality, always protecting you. Ever since the incident with that pervert when you were a child, you’ve always had a second personality.
"Last night, she came to say goodbye to me. She appeared because you yearned for protection. And now, you’ve become stronger, more resilient, so you no longer need her protection. That’s why she disappeared.
"Yesterday, she came to bid me farewell. From now on, you’ll just be you. I just didn’t expect she would do that yesterday."
"I..." Xie Sisi’s face was filled with shock, but she knew Wang Lan would never lie to her. Furthermore, her memory of last night was somewhat fuzzy. It felt like she was the one doing it, yet it was also like a dream.
"Do you regret it?" Wang Lan asked softly, looking at Xie Sisi’s perfect body. "Even though I can’t make you any promises."
"Not at all! I don’t regret it one bit! We’re Star Martial Warriors; who can promise anything to anyone? Who knows, we might die in battle any day. Wang Lan, I don’t regret it, not now, not ever..." Xie Sisi pressed her face against Wang Lan’s back, gently nuzzling him.
"You don’t feel wronged? This is quite unfair to you."
"Outstanding men possessing more outstanding women—that’s the fairest rule in the Law of nature. Being able to be your woman, how is that unfair to me? From the first day you came to our class, this outcome was already destined."
Wang Lan let out a soft sigh. "Are you hungry? Do you want to get up and eat something?"
"Not hungry. I just want to hold you a little longer."
"Just holding..." Wang Lan turned over and pushed Xie Sisi down. "Who initiated things yesterday? Maybe we should reenact it..."
「The summer vacation passed quietly.」
On August 25th, students from various places could start returning to school. Freshmen, needing to enroll, had to set off even earlier than other students.
Parting always comes with a hint of sadness. From Suzhou City, there were direct high-speed trains to both Modu City and Jin City. Modu City was closer, with the high-speed train journey taking only forty minutes.
Wang Lan and his three companions arrived at the station with their luggage. Each carried only a carry-on suitcase, intending to buy living supplies after reaching their destination.
"Xiangwen, after arriving in Jin City, Sisi is in your care," Jiang Xinyu said, holding Xie Sisi’s hand, a rare expression of sadness on her face.
"Of course! But Jin City is only about two hundred kilometers from Suzhou City, isn’t it? Is there a need to act as if it’s a final goodbye? Any day you feel like returning, you can. Look, Lanzi seems much more composed about it."
Jiang Xinyu looked at Wang Lan beside her. He was holding tickets and searching for the check-in gate, looking eager to board the train immediately.
"Xinyu, our check-in gate is over there, and they’re about to start boarding. Let’s go," Wang Lan said, striding over.
"Hey, Lanzi, aren’t you going to say goodbye before we part?" Xu Xiangwen’s eyes reddened slightly. "The next time we see each other, it will be the New Year."
"Oh, then goodbye!" Wang Lan waved absentmindedly. "Never mind, let’s hug instead."
He shared a gentle embrace with Xu Xiangwen and Xie Sisi. "Take care of yourselves, keep in touch often."
"Mm!"
Xu Xiangwen and Xie Sisi’s departure times were actually similar to Wang Lan’s, only about fifteen minutes apart. As Wang Lan’s train was preparing to depart, Xu Xiangwen’s group also began boarding.
"Feeling sentimental at a time like this? Isn’t your reaction a bit slow?" Jiang Xinyu teased.
"I’m not sentimental. It’s just that I’m about to leave Greater Su City, so I’m feeling a bit reflective. I’ve only left here three times in my entire life, and the last time was two years ago."
"I have to leave several times a year. I don’t get that feeling, but this is my first time taking a high-speed train."
「Meanwhile, on the train heading for Jin City」
Xie Sisi sat down and turned her head slightly to look out the window, while Xu Xiangwen had already picked up his phone and was engrossed in a fierce game of TM.
As a train pulled out of the station, Xie Sisi suddenly snapped back to reality. Remembering something, she opened her bag and took out a beautiful jewelry box. Seeing the azure mid-grade Soul Bead inside, Xie Sisi’s face showed surprise. Instantly, her nose tingled, and tears welled up in her eyes.
The forty-five-minute journey hardly felt tiring. They hadn’t even finished watching two episodes of a TV series before the train arrived at the station.
Stepping off the train with their luggage, they were greeted outside the station by buses from various universities, designated to pick up new students. Among them, the most prominent was the bus for the Modu City Star Martial Academy.
After all, everything about the Star Martial Academy could pique public curiosity, especially the Modu City Star Martial Academy. Although a Star Martial Warrior walking down the street wouldn’t be treated like a giant panda, a student from the Modu City Star Martial Academy wearing their uniform would certainly attract numerous admiring glances.
Even those who weren’t new students at the Modu City Star Martial Academy would gather outside the school bus to take selfies and show off. Paired with some background music and posted on a short video platform, they’d instantly rake in countless likes.
"Is the big shot a new student at the Modu City Star Martial Academy?"
"My respects to the big shot, let me get you a drink."
"I’m already a fan! Big shot, could you post more videos about life at the Modu City Star Martial Academy, please?"
Students of the Modu City Star Martial Academy generally wouldn’t linger outside the bus. When Wang Lan approached, carrying his luggage, senior students enthusiastically took it, helped store it away, and then guided them to their seats to wait.
All along the way, a multitude of gazes fixated on Wang Lan’s face. Regardless of gender, their eyes blazed with fervor.
These five or six steps felt as long as walking five or six hundred meters. Wang Lan was puzzled. Jiang Xinyu, next to him, was the true beauty, so why were they all staring at *him*? Could it be that his charm had completely overshadowed Jiang Xinyu’s?
"Xinyu, do you feel that something’s... off?" Wang Lan whispered to Jiang Xinyu after sitting down.
"Hmm?" Jiang Xinyu looked up at Wang Lan, puzzled.
The atmosphere inside the bus was somewhat oppressive. Though half-full, it felt as empty as a vacant bus. Many people, intentionally or unintentionally, glanced at Wang Lan. Even those busy with something kept their attention on him.
"From the moment I boarded this bus, I’ve been the target of countless intense stares. Those looks carry some kind of strong signal. I suspect we might have already been marked."
"What are you thinking?" Jiang Xinyu shot Wang Lan a look, baffled by his bizarre train of thought.
Is his mind always this peculiar?
"Think about it. We don’t know any of them, so why are they looking at me like that? It can’t be just because of my handsome face, right? Anyone eligible to attend the Modu City Star Martial Academy can’t be that superficial."
"COUGH! COUGH! COUGH!"
Suddenly, a handsome guy in the row ahead started coughing violently. It took him a while to recover. "Everyone who can get into the Modu City Star Martial Academy is a genius, but you, Wang Lan, are a real piece of work! The fact that you almost made me choke to death is enough for me to want to be your friend. I’ve heard so much about you. I’m Tong Wei, from Ji’an City in Lu Province."
"Is Wang Lan always this entertaining?" A sweet-looking girl greeted Wang Lan. "Hi, I’m Deng Duoduo from Jin City. Xu Ruo and the others came back and couldn’t stop talking about you, so when we saw you in person, we couldn’t help but stare a bit."
"Huh, a fellow provincial! What a pleasure. How come I didn’t see you at the provincial martial arts meet?" Wang Lan asked.
"Please, half the people on this bus are from the same province as you," a lazy voice chimed in. "Today is the first day of new student registration. Anyone who arrived by 10:30 this morning must live fairly close to Modu City. Bai Ze from Tai’an City. Wang Lan, I’ve long admired your name."
"Whoa, you all know me? Why don’t I recognize a single one of you?" Wang Lan exclaimed.
"The strongest high school student in the history of Jiang Province. It would be hard for us *not* to know you," a petite girl with dimples smiled. "You don’t recognize us because we didn’t attend the provincial martial arts meet."
"Impressive! All of you are such big shots, deeming yourselves above attending the provincial martial arts meet and getting in directly. My respects, my respects!" Wang Lan said.
"I could hear your voice from a mile away!" Suddenly, a familiar voice rang out as Mingyue Wucheng, wearing a backpack, boarded the bus. "You two certainly ran fast! My bus was just fifteen minutes after yours. I saw you at the station and wanted to say hi, but you all took off like the wind."
"Wucheng? What are you doing here? Didn’t you skip the college entrance exams?" Wang Lan asked.
"Ah! Yes, I did. So what? Didn’t you skip them as well?" Mingyue Wucheng replied.
"But you didn’t attend the provincial martial arts meet either, right? How did the Modu City Star Martial Academy accept you?" Wang Lan was completely baffled.
Wang Lan knew Mingyue Wucheng came from a Star Martial family. He had assumed that since Mingyue Wucheng skipped both the provincial martial arts meet and the college entrance exams, his family would arrange for him to pursue cultivation or work after high school instead of attending college.
"I was recommended back in eighth grade. Why would I need to take the college entrance exams?" Mingyue Wucheng stated, as if it were the most obvious thing in the world, making Wang Lan want to throttle him.
"So you’re saying... after eighth grade, you were just coasting?" Wang Lan turned to Deng Duoduo, who had spoken first. "You too?"
"No!" Deng Duoduo lowered her head in embarrassment. But before Wang Lan could breathe a sigh of relief, she added, "I’m not as impressive as Mingyue Wucheng. I was recommended a year later than him, just before finishing ninth grade."
"Amazing, amazing! And I only got recommended after my first year of high school. The gap is just... glaring!" Wang Lan said with feigned awe.
Thanks to Wang Lan’s humorous interruption, the previously tense atmosphere on the bus suddenly lightened. These were all individuals who had once made waves, each a personality in their own right. After a round of introductions, they quickly became familiar with each other.
"Let’s start a group chat! Anyone not in yet?"
"Coming! Damn, what’s the group ID? YU335? What does that mean?"
"It’s our bus’s license plate! We all met on this bus, so isn’t this group ID pretty meaningful?"
The guys warmed up quickly, their conversation igniting easily. The girls, being more reserved, formed small circles and chatted quietly amongst themselves while waiting for more new students to arrive.

chapters.title: Chapter 253 You Must Have Been Picked Up
chapters.content:
Chapter 253: Chapter 253 You Must Have Been Picked Up
The enrollment process at the school went very smoothly. No upperclassmen jumped out to show off, and no rich second-generation students, spotting Jiang Xinyu’s unparalleled beauty, came over to get a face-smashing from Wang Lan. After filling out forms and registering their student information, they received their room keys and could head to their dorms.
After escorting Jiang Xinyu to the entrance of the girls’ dormitory area, Wang Lan, carrying his luggage, found the assigned dormitory using his admission slip.
Upon entering the dormitory, he saw two people already lying around inside.
The dormitory was an apartment-style unit with a living room, a bathroom, and two bedrooms, each containing two beds. Wang Lan glanced at the two open bedroom doors; both rooms seemed to have been claimed.
"Hello, everyone. My name is Wang Lan, and I’m from Jiang Province. Which bed is mine?" Wang Lan asked softly as he entered.
"Damn! You’re finally here?" a student engrossed in a mobile game suddenly exclaimed, putting down his phone.
"Wang Lan’s here? Perfect, I have a score to settle with you," said another student, jumping up from a bed in the inner room and hastily making his way to the living room.
