His roommates’ reactions left Wang Lan slightly taken aback. Looking at their eager gazes, he hesitantly asked, "Do we know each other?"
"No, but I’ve heard so much about you," the student lying on the sofa laughed.
"Wang Lan, I used to be *that* kid—obedient, sensible, diligent in my cultivation, praised by friends and family. Until a year ago, my life was carefree and utterly enjoyable. I had everything I wanted; things always went my way.
But ever since the summer vacation of my senior year in high school, my dad started beating me up for no reason, always because of you!"
Wang Lan was even more confused. "Is he really your dad? And why because of me?"
"Because my dad raised his standards for excellence. In my family, there was always a benchmark. As long as I met it, everything was peaceful, and I was free to do as I pleased once my tasks were done. But then, my dad raised the benchmark to your level, and I got beaten daily. If he didn’t have time to beat me, he’d have his brothers do it. Tell me, don’t we have a score to settle?"
"His brothers beat you too? Are you sure you weren’t found in a dumpster?"
"HAHAHA..." The other student suddenly burst out laughing. "Wang Lan, don’t listen to his nonsense. A beating? That was combat training. Right, his dad’s a soldier. During the summer of our senior year, we had planned to travel to the West Continent, but instead, his dad dragged him to a military camp to train with the Star Martial Army for the entire summer.
We were only released right before school started. We thought the hardship would only last two months. But afterward, whenever he wasn’t in class, his dad pulled him into the military camp to train. He’s worked harder than an ox this past year."
"But what does that have to do with me?"
"It’s because when his dad was training him, he’d constantly say, ’Is that all the skill you have? Is that your limit? You’re far behind Wang Lan. You’re both sixteen, and he’s streets ahead of you.’ If you were in his shoes, wouldn’t you be annoyed?
What made him even angrier was that he considered himself exceptionally talented and harder working than most, respecting no one in his generation except Princess Yu Ruoyun. How could he tolerate such humiliation? He thought his dad was deliberately trying to pressure him by bringing you up. But then, everyone in the Martial Arts Corps said he couldn’t compare to you. It pissed him off so much; look, his face is still dark from it."
"Nonsense, I just got a good tan, okay?"
"The Martial Arts Corps? Might I ask who you are...?" Wang Lan asked, clasping his hands in a fist-and-palm salute.
"Easy. My father is He Jinze, Commander of the Martial Arts Corps. I’m He Jing. Wait, don’t change the subject. I’ve been waiting for you. Perfect. Come on, let’s go to the training grounds and spar. I want to see just how I ’can’t compare.’ Otherwise, after all the suffering I’ve endured this past year, I just can’t accept it."
Wang Lan turned his head to look at the other student. "Does this count as trouble finding me even when I’m just minding my own business?"
"Haha, he’s just kidding. Don’t take him seriously. My name is Ming Guodong. My father is the director of the Action Department of the Modu City Tianjian Bureau."
Wang Lan’s eyes narrowed slightly.
Another high-ranking official, possibly a Senior Colonel?
Modu City was directly administered by the central government. During the imperial era of the Jade Country, Modu City and the Imperial Capital were known as the two capitals. After the shift to a republic, Modu City retained its prominent status.
Although both were directors of Action Departments, the director in Modu City would be ranked one or two levels higher than the one in Suzhou City, at least a Colonel or Senior Colonel.
"You’re both big shots. From now on, I’ll be relying on you two to look out for me."
"Why are you playing humble? As if we don’t know who you are," He Jing said impatiently. "Speaking of second generations, you’re the real deal, okay? The son of the Southern Flame Emperor. Everyone who needs to know, knows by now.
Speaking of which, our fathers and your mother were classmates; they’re of the same generation’s circle, and we are of the second generation’s circle. In our circle, you’re the boss now."
"Me?" Wang Lan was curious. "How come I didn’t know?"
"Well, you know now, don’t you? Everyone knows there are the Five Elders and Five Emperors in the Star Martial Warrior world; it can basically be divided into five factions. The Five Elders are the spiritual leaders, and the Five Emperors are the commanders. You, you’re the Crown Prince. Us? At best, we’re like secondary generals."
Wang Lan’s expression shifted subtly.
Had he been thrust into the spotlight?
At the end of the provincial martial arts tournament, when Eld Di had him fight Wang Mingling alone, Wang Lan had suspected something.
Indeed, Eld Di had pushed him into the limelight.
"What era are we living in? Who still talks about this stuff?" Wang Lan said nonchalantly, dragging his luggage into a room. "Ming Guodong, am I rooming with you?"
"No problem. I’ll help you unpack."
"No need, I didn’t bring much. I’ll go out and buy whatever I need later. By the way, the school doesn’t restrict us from going out, right?"
"Not before the semester starts. After it begins, it seems only Sundays are free. Normally, unless you have special permission, the entire campus is covered with surveillance and sensor devices. It’s called a school, but it’s more like a military fortress."
"Want to go out together later? I guess you guys just arrived too, right?"
"Aren’t we supposed to go to the training grounds for a fight later?" He Jing still hadn’t forgotten.
"Forget it, He Jing. Even a stubborn mule knows when to stop banging its head against a wall. Didn’t you watch this year’s Jiang Province provincial martial arts tournament?"
"Wasn’t I thrown into the intermediate trial grounds by my old man back then? To help maintain... Damn him! He just treated me as free labor, the kind that’s completely neglected.
Guodong, you have no idea. If I weren’t such a genius, I would have ended up as Exotic Beast dung several times."
"Perfect then. I have a video on my phone. As the saying goes, ’Know yourself and know your enemy, and you will never be defeated.’ You need to understand Wang Lan’s strength to come up with the right tactics."
"Psh, this young master fears nothing!" But in the blink of an eye, He Jing’s expression changed. "A video of Wang Lan’s battle? The kind where he’s going all out?"
"Absolutely all out. The kind where he couldn’t hold back even if he wanted to."
"Alright then, give it to me quickly. I’ll study it and then challenge Wang Lan," He Jing said, walking into his room.
"Where are you going?"
"To use the projector. It’ll be clearer that way."
Wang Lan had just finished making his bed when his phone chimed. It was a message from Jiang Xinyu: "Settled into the dorm. Two roommates, three people per room. Dorm number 305."
"Why are you sending me this? It’s not like I can just pop over for a visit."
"Have you finished unpacking?"
"Yeah. Want to go out and buy some daily necessities together later?"
"Okay! See you at the school gate in an hour."
Wang Lan never quite understood why they had to meet an hour later when everything was supposedly ready.
What did girls need so much time for?
In his memory, "in a while" had never meant more than ten minutes.
Not even twenty minutes had passed when a sudden roar erupted from the adjacent room.
"Monster! What a freaking monster!" As the words faded, He Jing stormed out of the room, plopped down on the sofa, and stared at Wang Lan. "How did you manage to achieve full mutation at your age?"
"Still want to challenge our Flame Emperor’s Crown Prince, He Jing?"
"Challenge my ass! One punch turns half the field to dust. My small frame would probably crumble just from the aftershock, right? Wang Lan, your strength is likely not beneath Princess Yu Ruoyun’s."
"I’ve heard you guys mention Princess Yu Ruoyun several times now. Who is she?"
"Of course, she’s Her Highness Princess Yu Ruoyun of the Jade Country. She’s from the royal family’s direct lineage, a pinnacle Galaxy Stage master. And the thing is, she’s only a sophomore, just eighteen this year."
"An eighteen-year-old at the peak of the Galaxy Stage?" Wang Lan exclaimed in surprise.
"Yeah, that’s why she was called the top genius of the new generation. But that was in the past. Many ’demons’ have emerged in recent years. Just like you—’the strongest high school student in history’ is also a pretty resounding title."
"Empty titles, all of them," Wang Lan said modestly, smiling.
"Oh, please. You’re clearly thrilled," He Jing retorted sharply. "Your grin’s as wide as a ladle. By the way, to celebrate our first day here, how about we go out for a big meal tonight? My treat!"
"Sounds good. But what about the other roommate?"
"He probably won’t arrive for another couple of days. I know Modu City well. I’ll take you guys out later; I guarantee you’ll be satisfied," Ming Guodong said.
"Can I bring a friend? I have a friend who came to Modu City with me."
"It’s that Jiang Xinyu, right?" He Jing said, a hint of sourness in his voice. "He’s abnormally strong and talented, and yet he still has time to find a girlfriend. We spend practically all our free time cultivating, and you can still manage a love life. This, I suppose, is what it means to be a winner in life."
"Sure! By the way, is your girlfriend settled in too? Why not invite her dorm mates? It’d be a good chance for us to meet some girls," Ming Guodong chimed in.
"I’ll ask her for you later." Saying this, Wang Lan walked to the door and changed his shoes. "I’m going out to buy some things. Do you guys want to come?"
"No need, we brought everything."
Exiting the dormitory building, he headed straight for the school gate. The male and female dormitories were as far apart as the North and South Poles, so meeting at the school gate was the most time-efficient plan.
Come to think of it, perhaps the school had intentionally arranged for both roommates to be easy to get along with.
Coupled with the connection their parents shared, the three of them naturally found common ground.
So, he’d just been pushed out to carry the banner? While not particularly eager, he wasn’t averse to it either.
His experiences from his past life had long taught Wang Lan that one cannot escape their standing in life. No matter where you positioned yourself, you were always part of some circle. Most people existed within the circle of their family; Wang Lan’s circle just happened to be larger, drawing more attention.
Previously, Ming Guodong had mentioned he was familiar with Modu City, but Wang Lan was also quite familiar with it. Although he seldom visited Modu City, he owned a commercial plaza in its business district. The entire plaza belonged to Wang Lan, and the rent he collected each year was an astronomical sum. This commercial center was conveniently located not far from Modu City’s Star Martial Academy and had everything from fitness and entertainment facilities to a wide array of restaurants. However, the supermarkets in the commercial plaza operated on a membership basis, and ordinary people didn’t typically choose to buy their daily necessities there.

chapters.title: Chapter 254: Royal Princess
chapters.content:
Chapter 254: Chapter 254: Royal Princess
At 5:30 PM, Wang Lan and Jiang Xinyu, following the information sent by Ming Guodong, found an authentic Jiangnan cuisine restaurant called Jiangnan Kitchen. He and He Jing had gone ahead to reserve a table and order food; Wang Lan and Jiang Xinyu would join them once Jiang Xinyu arrived.
"Xinyu, these are my two roommates: He Jing, son of Commander He of the Martial Arts Corps, and this is Ming Guodong. Everyone, this is Jiang Xinyu," Wang Lan introduced as he entered the private dining room.
"The Ice-Snow Queen of Suzhou City! I’ve long admired your reputation," Ming Guodong said with a smile, quickly standing up.
"Jiang Xinyu, my dad told me about you. Back then, you led Wang Lan’s team to discover a Demon Clan base they had searched three years for without success, and you personally killed a Demon Clan spy. Impressive!" He Jing exclaimed, standing up and offering a compliment.
"Hey, that’s not what you said to me before. How can your tune change so completely for someone else?" Wang Lan teased He Jing.
"Can you even compare to Jiang Xinyu? Besides, Jiang Xinyu brought her roommates today. Speaking of which, where are yours?" He Jing retorted.
"Both of my roommates are second-year upperclasswomen; they just got back and might take a little while to arrive," Jiang Xinyu replied.
"Second-year upperclasswomen, huh?" He Jing’s interest visibly deflated. "Sounds like a bit of a letdown..."
As the dishes began to arrive one by one, the four of them chatted animatedly, and the atmosphere was quite congenial. Soon, Jiang Xinyu’s phone rang. She stood up and announced, "My roommates are here."
He Jing hurriedly pulled open the door to the private room. Not far from the entrance, two young women exuding a youthful aura were gracefully approaching. One was tall, dressed in a white shirt and high-waisted jeans. The other, about half a head shorter than her companion, wore a blue sleeveless dress and carried a handbag slung over her arm.
Their looks weren’t exceptionally stunning, but their presence was extraordinary. With bright eyes scanning the room numbers on either side, upon seeing He Jing open the door, they immediately recognized the private room and strode towards it.
However, He Jing, who had opened the door, abruptly ducked his head back inside, staring intently at Jiang Xinyu. "You share a dorm with the Second Princess?"
"The Second Princess? Who’s that?" Jiang Xinyu clearly had no idea who the Second Princess was.
"Yu Ruoyun!" Wang Lan whispered the Second Princess’s name.
"Yes, the one who shares my room is named Yu Ruoyun, but I had no idea she was some ’Second Princess.’ He Jing, what’s with your reaction?" Jiang Xinyu asked, puzzled.
"Nothing! It’s nothing at all!" He Jing said, a wide, somewhat forced smile plastered on his face as he stood by the door. Ming Guodong had also risen to his feet.
"Greetings, Second Princess!"
"Second Princess."
Just as Wang Lan was wondering if he too should stand and address her as "Second Princess," Yu Ruoyun spoke.
"Please, don’t call me Second Princess. There are no princes or princesses anymore. We’ve been a republic for two hundred years; where would a princess come from? If we’re close, you can call me Ruoyun. More formally, just Student Yu Ruoyun is fine," she said, then nonchalantly approached Wang Lan’s side, pulled out a chair, and sat down. "Hello, Wang Lan. My great-grandfather has been singing your praises ever since he returned from Suzhou City. I’ve wanted to meet you for a while. My name is Yu Ruoyun, a second-year Mage."
"Your great-grandfather? You mean Eld Di?" Wang Lan asked, hazarding a guess.
"Yes," Yu Ruoyun confirmed. "My mother is Eld Di’s granddaughter."
Now *that* was a pedigree!
Wang Lan thought.
But what is she getting at? Is this a test, or something else? If I weren’t around, Yu Ruoyun would undoubtedly be the flag-bearer for the new generation.
A direct descendant of Eld Di, and a royal princess by status—her talent and strength must be impeccable, right? But what does it matter to me? I’m just a student; focusing on my studies is enough.
"Are you the Jiang Province champion who caused such a stir at the provincial tournament?" the girl opposite Wang Lan, Lan Qi, asked with a surprised look. "No wonder Ruoyun agreed to come to dinner today. She usually never agrees to these kinds of social engagements. Hello, my name is Lan Qi. It’s a pleasure to meet you all."
At these words, Wang Lan, He Jing, and Ming Guodong couldn’t help but frown slightly.
Is this woman clueless, or is she doing this on purpose? What does she mean, Yu Ruoyun ’never agrees to these kinds of social engagements’? Is this some kind of obligation? Do we need a favor from her or something? The problem is, she’s trying to elevate someone’s status, but it’s not even her own! Is she some kind of anti-fan?
"Student Yu Ruoyun," Wang Lan inquired, "does our Star Martial Academy also have different departments? I assumed it was like high school, without such divisions."
"How could it be the same?" Yu Ruoyun replied. "Everyone’s talent is different, and so is their role on the battlefield. The school is broadly divided into four departments: the Close Combat Department, the Mage Department, the Auxiliary Department, and the Scout Department. However, students aren’t strictly confined to these. In addition to the compulsory courses for each department, students can also choose various electives."
"Our school offers eighty elective courses, each representing a specific skill or specialization. Wang Lan, once the semester officially starts, you can select a few practical courses. I personally recommend Advanced Star Power, Human Genetics, and Rule Analysis."
"Uh..."
He had never even heard of these subjects before. He could grasp Star Power, but what on earth was Advanced Star Power?
Yu Ruoyun continued, "Wang Lan, Advanced Star Power involves tracing the essence of Star Power, studying how Star Martial Skills are executed using Star Power, and understanding the principles behind their activation. Learning this will benefit your future comprehension of Star Power and can help you develop your own Star Martial Skills."
Lan Qi interjected, "However, I personally feel that unless you’re a super genius like Ruoyun, studying it isn’t very useful. There are so many existing Star Martial Skills that one can’t even learn them all. Human Genetics is much the same. The mysteries of the human body, especially those of Star Martial Warriors, are vast; to this day, we’ve only uncovered the tip of the iceberg. As for Rule Analysis... that’s even more profound."
Lan Qi went on for quite a while but didn’t say anything of real substance.
However, Wang Lan sensed it wasn’t that she was unwilling to say more, but that she simply didn’t know.
Yu Ruoyun then clarified, "These three subjects are indeed the most arcane among the elective courses. Genetics, for instance, goes without saying; countless top scientists worldwide spend their entire lives researching it. My point is, even though we’re Star Martial Warriors, we can’t be mere brutes who only know how to fight, can we?"
"Human genes are a treasure trove, especially the segment sealed by the gods, which is said to hold infinite power."
"That gene segment... could it be... the one we Star Martial Warriors awaken?" He Jing asked curiously. "But haven’t we already awakened it?"
"The awakening of a Star Martial Warrior only proves that the gene segment has been activated, not fully developed," Yu Ruoyun explained. "It’s like a person: being able to eat, drink, and sleep only proves they are alive. What that person can actually *do* and *achieve* is what constitutes development."
"Legend has it that this segment of genes holds the power of the gods. Whoever can fully develop this segment will gain god-like power. Of course, this is just speculation. Whether it’s merely a utopian dream or not, who can say?"
"As for Rule Analysis, it’s essentially the rules of all things, the rules of the universe. After all, in our Star Palace, once we move past the Galaxy, we begin to birth a universe itself. The nurturing of the Star Cloud, the embryonic form of the Galaxy, and the accumulation within the Star Sea are all preparations for breaking through to the realms beyond the Star Sea Stage."
"At that level, one must evolve the Laws of the universe within their Star Palace. The realm of the Five Emperors signifies that a Law has already evolved within their Star Palace, and they can wield the power of that Law. In the face of such power, even those at the Star Sea Stage can be turned to ash and annihilated with a mere snap of the fingers. No number of people can bridge such a gap."
"Sounds like we’re hearing some incredibly profound stuff..." Ming Guodong said, looking hesitantly at He Jing. "Did you understand any of that?"
"This is probably a topic only geniuses can discuss," He Jing muttered.
"It’s alright if you don’t understand now," Yu Ruoyun said. "Once you reach the later stages of the Galaxy Stage or break through the Star Sea Stage, you’ll begin to sense it. If you start preparing early, you won’t have to relearn everything later. But enough about that, let’s eat! I’m starving."
Everyone at the table stood up. "Alright then, to our new acquaintance today, cheers!"
「 」
After dinner concluded and everyone went their separate ways, Wang Lan quickly showered and lay down on his bed. Having completed the enrollment procedures, it was time to get back into his training regimen after a break of over two months.
Wang Lan was currently in the early Star Cloud Stage, and all his Star Martial Skills were at the Gold level. To upgrade Gold-level Star Martial Skills to their peak required 10,000 skill points. However, the skill points for abilities like Earth Surge Fire Sea and Song of Life were progressive, costing five times more than standard skills. Even Phantom Tracer required 15,000 skill points.
Thinking about the total need for hundreds of thousands of skill points made Wang Lan despair. And that wasn’t all; upgrading from the Star Cloud Stage to the Galaxy Stage apparently required over 5,000,000 experience points. Dammit, the road ahead felt impossibly difficult.
Before doing the math, he had felt quite content. But now, looking at these numbers, his future seemed like an abyss.
"Sigh—"
"You’ve just enrolled, and you’re already sighing like that?" Ming Guodong, who was leaning against his headboard playing a game, looked up and asked.
"I really envy you guys, being able to level up so smoothly," Wang Lan sighed with feeling. Although the system, his "cheat," saved him time in learning Star Martial Skills and allowed for rapid advancement in the early stages, the system was both his boon and his bane.
In the later stages, leveling up felt like feeding a gluttonous beast. Others could break through their bottlenecks using Soul Beads and their own comprehension, but Wang Lan couldn’t. He could only rely on experience points and skill points.
"You envy us?" Ming Guodong put down his phone, looking at Wang Lan in shock. "Could you at least try to have some shame? You think I don’t know? Being able to break through after a battle has left you completely exhausted, with nearly all your Star Power depleted—in all of history, you’re the only one I know who could do such a thing! And you envy our ’normal’ upgrading? Aren’t you afraid of getting beaten up if word of this gets out?"
"I..." Wang Lan found himself speechless in the face of this accusation.
"By the way, when will we get a chance to hunt Exotic Beasts? I’m in desperate need of Soul Beads," Wang Lan asked.
"You say that as if we aren’t short on Soul Beads," Ming Guodong retorted. "But don’t even think about it before your sophomore year. Freshman year is mainly for theoretical studies. And don’t take it lightly; the theories we learned in high school are just rudimentary basics. The truly profound and practical theories are all taught in college. Failing to master these theories will affect your future progress. We only know that cultivating Star Martial Skills and absorbing Soul Beads makes us stronger."
"But after reaching the Galaxy Stage, relying solely on those methods is useless. There are countless excellent Star Martial Skills, but you simply can’t learn them without a solid theoretical grounding. You can’t just depend on Soul Beads for breakthroughs either; comprehension is also crucial. Don’t aim too high and end up damaging your foundation. The basics are extremely important."
"Huh?" Wang Lan looked at Ming Guodong curiously. "You’ve had this kind of understanding for a long time? That doesn’t sound very youthful of you."
"This is the difference between having a solid foundation and not," Ming Guodong explained. "How would ordinary people know these things? They just absorb, learn, and focus solely on increasing their strength, wishing they could get stronger every single day. But that path only gets narrower. To be frank, your progress so far has been too rapid; it could lead to hidden problems down the line."
"Think about it: you awakened just over a year ago and are already at the Star Cloud Stage. I’m telling you, the Star Cloud Stage is all about accumulation. Eighty percent of people never break through to the Galaxy Stage in their entire lifetimes because their foundations aren’t solid enough. By the time they try to compensate, it’s already too late. When classes officially start, the teachers will explain this too, even if I don’t."

chapters.title: Chapter 255: Supernatural Dreams
chapters.content:
Chapter 255: Chapter 255: Supernatural Dreams
"I’m just asking when I can hunt Exotic Beasts, and you give me a lecture? Are you sure there’s no chance for a freshman?"
"Generally speaking, the chances are indeed slim. However, Modu City Star Martial Academy opens the Nine-layer Pagoda once a year. The Nine-layer Pagoda is like a trial space, but the Exotic Beasts inside are much stronger. It’s usually meant for senior students to make their final sprint."
"When does it open?"
"Around November, I guess."
November, that’s a little over two months away, not too long. After all, Mrs. Sun Li had promised him many benefits. Although the Nine-layer Pagoda was intended for seniors making their final sprint, wasn’t the school supposed to focus on nurturing him specifically? They ought to bend the rules a bit for him, right?
In a daze, Wang Lan’s eyelids grew heavy.
DRIP... DROP... DRIP... DROP...
Clear dripping sounds echoed in his ears. It sounded like water droplets slowly carving through stone in a silent cave, falling from a stalactite.
He was clearly sleeping in the school dormitory, so where was this dripping sound coming from? Was a faucet not turned off tightly? That wasn’t right either; it wasn’t the old-fashioned type of tap that could drip.
His consciousness gradually cleared, and Wang Lan slowly opened his eyes.
But in the next instant, his pupils dilated sharply because the dripping sounds were not from actual water droplets, but from drops of blood.
Before him, in the open space of the room, stood a woman enveloped in a hazy white light, a sword pierced her chest. Blood dyed her snow-white dress red and dripped from her fingertips.
"Junior... avenge me... avenge me..."
Suddenly, a breeze blew, and the woman in front of him vanished like smoke. Wang Lan, who should have sat up, instead suddenly opened his eyes to find himself lying comfortably in bed.
"PHEW—" Wang Lan sat up abruptly, quickly scanning the dark space before his eyes, but there was no girl wrapped in white light, nor the dazzling blood.
Dreaming?
"Oh my god! Wang Lan, I just felt a bit cold, so I turned the air conditioner up by two degrees. Did you have to react so dramatically? It was like you just rose from the dead!" exclaimed Ming Guodong from beside him.
"Huh?" Wang Lan turned his head to look at Ming Guodong. "Just now... I had a dream."
"Pfft! Dreaming? I dream every day. Out of 365 days a year, I dream I’m one of the Five Emperors for about 200 of them. Let’s sleep, let’s sleep! Didn’t expect it to be colder here at night than other places."
"That dream felt so real. I haven’t dreamt in a long time, let alone had a nightmare!" Wang Lan figured that misery loves company; why should he let his roommate sleep soundly after he himself had been startled?
"Just now, a really beautiful older girl was standing right there, radiating a light like moonlight, wearing a snow-white dress..." Wang Lan’s low, eerie voice sounded as he pointed to the spot where the woman had appeared in his dream.
Ming Guodong’s breathing became noticeably heavier, and he gulped.
"Then what?"
"A sword was thrust into her chest, with blood staining her front. The blood dripped down her fingers, pooling into a lake of blood on the ground... She slowly came to your bedside, stood right next to you, and whispered..."
"Whispering...what?"
"Junior, avenge me..."
"AAH—" Ming Guodong suddenly screamed and switched on the light with a snap. The room instantly brightened.
Wang Lan was also stunned by this. You’re a Star Cloud Stage Star Martial Warrior, and that’s all the courage you have?
At this moment, Ming Guodong looked at Wang Lan with a face full of horror. "Are you serious? Don’t scare me, man! Did you see a photo or something? You..."
"What photo?"
"What’s with you two? Up so late, are you having a little bromance? What was all that noise earlier?" He Jing knocked on the door from outside.
"He Jing, hurry up, bring that photo you found today over here."
"For what?"
"Just bring it."
Soon, He Jing returned to Wang Lan’s room, casually tossing a photo next to Ming Guodong.
"Why the rush? Were you so desperate you couldn’t wait to get your kicks from the photo? Don’t you dare defile my goddess! I was planning on asking around tomorrow to find out which year’s senior she is."
Ming Guodong took the photo and handed it to Wang Lan. "Take a look. Is this the girl you were talking about?"
Wang Lan took the photo, and with just one glance, his expression changed dramatically.
Ever since waking up, Wang Lan had thought it was just a very vivid dream. But the moment he saw the photo, his heart suddenly tightened.
Could there truly be ghosts in this world?
The woman in the photo was the same one Wang Lan had just seen; even her clothes were exactly the same.
But how could that be possible?
Wang Lan could accept the existence of gods in this world because he had crossed over into it. With the Demon Clan in existence, the presence of gods was completely logical. But that said, the presence of gods didn’t necessarily mean that ghosts must exist too.
Gods are but unexplained science. Demons, merely creatures beyond human understanding.
Even the existence of Star Martial Warriors had been scientifically identified as linked to a segment of the X gene in human evolution; some people possessed this gene, while others didn’t. Moreover, this gene was scattered throughout the entire human population and wasn’t mandatorily hereditary.
Thus, even if this world seemed unscientific, Wang Lan only believed in things that had been proven to exist. Those that had never been witnessed by anyone or verified were mostly denied or ignored by most people. Ghosts fell into that category.
The human soul had been proven to exist, but ghosts hadn’t. Because the soul and body were symbiotic, the phenomenon of the soul remaining after the body’s death didn’t exist, let alone the soul detaching to become another life form. This symbiotic relationship theoretically eliminated the possibility of ghosts. Once someone died, their soul would dissipate. Without a soul, how could there be ghosts?
But... what did I just see?
"Wang Lan, stop spacing out... Tell me, did you or did you not just see her?"
As Wang Lan’s face turned pale, Ming Guodong already had an answer in his heart, his voice shaking unconsciously.
"What are you talking about? Wang Lan saw that senior girl? Where, where?" He Jing asked excitedly, like a dog in heat, only just short of sticking his tongue out.
"Right in this room," Ming Guodong’s trembling voice arose, causing He Jing to pause slightly.
"Wang Lan said that the senior girl, with a sword sticking out of her and covered in blood, told me to avenge her... We’re done for... We might be haunted."
"Hold on!" He Jing quickly cut Ming Guodong off. "Revenge? How could such a cute senior girl die so young? We can just ask the upperclassmen about her tomorrow."
"By the way, where did you get this photo?" Wang Lan asked curiously.
"We came early today and found it under the bed while cleaning."
"Isn’t this a men’s dorm? How could there be a photo of a woman here?"
"Who knows? We’ll ask tomorrow. But the problem is, what are we going to do tonight? I’m too scared to sleep," Ming Guodong said before suddenly turning and looking at He Jing with a mournful expression.
"What’s with that look? My gender is male, and my preference is female. Definitely no bromance," He Jing declared firmly.
"Let’s squeeze into your room."
"Are you... serious?" He Jing still didn’t quite believe what Wang Lan and Ming Guodong were saying, asking hesitantly.
"At this point, do you think I would joke about something like this?"
"I..." Wang Lan’s eyes suddenly lit up; he realized an ongoing mission had appeared on the system interface.
He knew that since receiving the admission notice from Modu City Star Martial Academy, the mission column had been empty. Now, with an ongoing mission added, could it be the female ghost? No way! Is this going to be an unfinished human-ghost romance?
"I think I’ll just sleep here. After all, she didn’t come for me," Wang Lan said after some thought.
Since the female ghost wants me to avenge her, she probably won’t harm me. Besides, this so-called female ghost is likely different from the kind I imagine—not one that can attack people.
Ming Guodong ended up sleeping in the next room over, and Wang Lan fell asleep shortly after lying down.
「Early the next morning」
He was awakened by Ming Guodong’s knocking.
"Wang Lan, you still alive?"
"Get lost!" Wang Lan responded with a strong voice.
School hadn’t officially started yet, but the cafeteria was already in full operation. The three of them went to the cafeteria for breakfast together. After returning to the dorm, Wang Lan picked up his laptop to search for information on the girl.
However, it was strange that he couldn’t find any data about the girl on the school network.
Could she be a senior from a long time ago?
Wang Lan took a USB drive out of his luggage bag and plugged it into the computer.
The progress bar quickly filled. "Xiao Ai 007 has been successfully awakened. Hello, Wang Lan," a synthesized voice announced from the laptop.
"Xiao Ai, infiltrate the school’s system network for me and pull up the information of the person in this photo," Wang Lan commanded.
The laptop camera turned on, swiftly scanning the photo. "Alright, Wang Lan. Please do not shut down the computer or disconnect from the network," Xiao Ai replied.
Letting Xiao Ai do the searching, Wang Lan took his reading card from the bed and headed to the library.
Although Modu City Star Martial Academy was a school for Star Martial Warriors, focusing on teaching fighting techniques and the practical theory of Star Martial Skills, it was also a first-class academic institution in the country. It had all the courses a regular university would have, and possibly even some that they didn’t.
Therefore, not all teachers at Modu City Star Martial Academy were Star Martial Warriors; many were ordinary people holding titles like doctor or professor. Naturally, the Modu City Star Martial Academy library was also a vast ocean of knowledge.
Although Wang Lan had always been considered a genius by others, he knew he wasn’t truly one. He just worked harder than others and knew how to make better use of his time.
Last night during dinner, although he found Yu Ruoyun’s words somewhat confusing, he didn’t dismiss them like He Jing and the others did. Arriving at the library, Wang Lan followed the category signs to find the section on advanced Star Power.
An entire shelf was filled with books detailing the theoretical analysis and practical records of advanced Star Power. Since a unifying theory to serve as the discipline’s backbone had yet to be established, many of the books’ titles and viewpoints conflicted.
Perhaps in the future, some genius will have a flash of insight, developing a groundbreaking theory to integrate all these diverse books into a systematic body of knowledge.
Wang Lan randomly pulled out a book titled "Phenomena and Questions of Advanced Star Power" and took a seat to start reading. He soon became engrossed in the explanation of what constituted advanced Star Power.

chapters.title: Chapter 256 Tianjian Bureau’s Call for help
chapters.content:
Chapter 256: Chapter 256 Tianjian Bureau’s Call for help
This absorption in his reading made Wang Lan forget the time. When he finally looked up again, the sky had already darkened.
High-level Star Power isn’t about the advanced utilization of Star Power. Regardless of how Star Power is applied, such uses are considered low-level. High-level Star Power is about tracing the origin of Star Power to fundamentally understand how it is generated.
In high school textbooks, Star Power is described as being generated by the human body itself, with all the cells in a person’s body containing Star Power. Through special methods, Star Power is extracted from these cells. However, cells that lose Star Power age more quickly and can even die.
But this leads to a paradox: if Star Power is energy extracted from human cells, then the amount of Star Power each Star Martial Warrior possesses should fluctuate within a certain average. It would be absolutely impossible for the current situation to exist, where some individuals have vast amounts of Star Power while others are severely lacking.
Of course, some might mention Soul Beads, as those with strong Star Power have absorbed a large number of them. Breaking the shackles of the Star Palace’s limit also requires the absorption of Soul Beads.
But the Soul Bead is merely the key to unlocking this limit; the amount of Star Power absorbed to achieve this is incomparable to the amount gained *after* breaking through to a higher Star Power level.
It’s like pouring water into a cup. Even if the cup bursts and the water enters a larger cup, the amount of water remains the same. It’s not possible for the water to instantly fill the larger container just because the original cup burst and spilled into it.
Therefore, the true source of Star Power is definitely not human cells. What high school textbooks describe is merely the initial source of Star Power for Star Martial Warriors, not the actual origin of Star Power.
So, if Star Power does not come from the body, where does it come from? Some believe it comes from the universe, as it has been proven that the universe is filled with a massive amount of Star Power.
But this enormous amount of Star Power cannot be used by Star Martial Warriors, nor can it be collected. The Star Power in the universe is like an exquisite woman in a painting: she is right before your eyes, you can see her but never possess her. You can fantasize about her, but she will never become pregnant or bear children.
Therefore, a hypothesis exists: the X gene of Star Martial Warriors must possess the function to absorb and convert the universal Star Power, but we just haven’t found it yet. If this hypothesis holds true, it would perfectly explain why Star Martial Warriors have Star Power and ordinary people do not. It would also explain the source of Star Power, and even why some people have more and some have less.
It’s a matter of conversion efficiency, then.
But a hypothesis is just a hypothesis, especially one as vague as this. Despite the many unresolved mysteries, the realm of higher Star Power still lured Wang Lan like the Sea Demon’s song. He wanted to know the truth more than anyone.
What was the actual physical manifestation of the skill points in his body? What on earth were ’experience points’?
Wang Lan didn’t attempt to scientifically explain the existence of the system, but he at least needed to know if the power he now possessed belonged to him or to the system. If the system was just a form of expression, that would be fine. But if the system was the essence, then Wang Lan might truly panic.
Closing the book, he returned it to the shelf. Wang Lan stood up and left the library. Since school hadn’t started yet, there were very few people around. It wasn’t until he reached the outer areas of the library that he saw a few scattered students.
Back in the dormitory, Xiao Ai’s work was finished. Looking at the file rack on the table, Wang Lan opened it but paused.
"Is there only a student status form?"
"Inside the school’s system, there’s only one student status form."
"’Ma Chuchu, female, from Long City, Sichuan Province, enrolled in the year 5016,’" Wang Lan read, continuing with the student’s related information. "’The final record is filed as: Deceased. Student status canceled.’ And shockingly, the cause of death listed was ’suicide.’"
After reviewing the information, Wang Lan fell silent.
For Modu Star Martial Academy to cover up this matter so thoroughly... things definitely weren’t as simple as they seemed.
As Wang Lan was speculating, He Jing and Ming Guodong returned to the dormitory. Those two still had some conscience; they had actually remembered to bring food back for Wang Lan.
"Wang Lan, guess what I found out?"
"What?"
"Damn it, we’re really living in a haunted house!" Ming Guodong sighed with despair. "It turns out that the senior student who lived here before was named Ma Chuchu, from the class of 2016. In her sophomore year, it seems she started dating a freshman from a Star Martial family."
"But, as fate would have it, his family forbade the relationship and forced them to break up. The guy from the Star Martial family broke up with Senior Ma. Heartbroken, she committed suicide in the dorm using a weapon her boyfriend had given her."
"It caused a huge sensation at the time; nearly all the juniors and seniors knew about it. Afterward, that dormitory became reputed to be haunted. Since then, no one has stayed in that room. And that room is the very one we’re living in now! Damn it!"
"Wait, isn’t this a boys’ dormitory?"
"It used to be a girls’ dormitory. But after ghost rumors spread in 2018 – apparently, boys have stronger yang energy or something – they swapped dormitories with the girls. This room, in particular, has been vacant ever since. No wonder! I found stockings and women’s underwear when cleaning and thought the previous guy who lived here was some kind of pervert. ARGH!"
"So what do we do now?"
"What else can we do? We’ll ask to change rooms. If they don’t let us, we’ll... we’ll rent a place outside. Even though rent in Modu City is expensive, we can still afford something for around ten thousand yuan."
"Hold on, you’re talking about renting a dorm room for ten thousand yuan? You’re planning to rent a whole apartment suite, right?"
"Yeah, what else would I rent if not an apartment suite? A single room?"
"Wang Lan, why don’t you give the internal affairs office a call?" He Jing leaned in and whispered.
"Why me?"
"You’re our leader, who else would it be?"
"Wait a minute! When did I become your leader? Are you guys abandoning all principles just to push me into this?"
"From the moment you entered this dormitory, you were!"
"From the time we were assigned to this dorm, you became the dorm chief!"
Seeing the two so unwaveringly form a strategic alliance, it was clear they had already discussed this before returning. Although Wang Lan wasn’t particularly afraid of ghosts—especially after becoming a Star Martial Warrior, his courage had expanded boundlessly—he also didn’t want to be halfway through a good night’s sleep only to suddenly find a blood-soaked woman standing by his bed.
Wang Lan wasn’t afraid; he was concerned about disrupting his sleep.
After brief consideration, Wang Lan finally nodded. "Alright then."
The phone call went smoothly, so smoothly that Wang Lan almost couldn’t believe it was real. Almost immediately after Wang Lan stated his request, the person on the other end agreed and said they would come over to change the dormitory nameplate and keys.
This efficiency was as if they were just waiting for Wang Lan to ask for a dormitory change.
They had only moved in the day before and didn’t have much luggage, so it took just one trip for the three of them to move everything. The new dormitory was on the sixth floor, meaning they had to climb stairs every day. But for Star Martial Warriors, this wasn’t an issue at all; the amount of exercise wouldn’t even cause their breathing to change.
"Finally, I can get a good night’s sleep. Wang Lan, let me tell you, I didn’t sleep a wink last night."
"I was fine. I didn’t see anything... unsettling after that."
BEEP! BEEP! BEEP!
Suddenly, Wang Lan’s phone rang. The moment he saw the screen, his expression changed drastically; a red dot pulsed incessantly on the map.
"Huh? Wang Lan, that phone model of yours looks really fami...liar!"
Ming Guodong looked at the open window and the empty bed, the last word unspoken.
"What’s going on?" He Jing was just coming over to visit. The door had just opened when a figure flashed past and disappeared in an instant.
"I thought Wang Lan was just starting to take off, but now I realize he’s already flown much farther than us," Ming Guodong said, slowly closing the window as he looked at it.
"What are you talking about? Also, what’s going on with Wang Lan?"
"He’s on a mission."
"Mission? What mission?"
"How would I know? I’m not from the Tianjian Bureau."
"Wait, you mean... aside from being our roommate and a student at Modu Star Martial Academy, Wang Lan is also..."
"I didn’t know at first, but that knockoff phone he just pulled out? I happen to recognize it. That must be it!"
After Wang Lan dashed out of the dormitory, he transformed into a streak of light and sped away. With his speed fully unleashed, the school, which usually felt vast, now didn’t seem so large.
"Stop!"
Just as he was about to reach the school gate, a voice boomed into Wang Lan’s ears like thunder, the sound causing a momentary paralysis in his body.
An old man wearing a sanitation worker’s hat and an orange vest was leaning on a broom, looking at Wang Lan.
"What are you doing? Going out so late?"
Wang Lan didn’t have time to consider just how many hidden masters there might be at Modu Star Martial Academy—perhaps even a random auntie cleaning the toilets could be an extraordinary expert. He pulled out a red ID booklet from his pocket.
"Go on, go on!" The old man didn’t even bother to take it to check, waving his hand impatiently. "Be careful. If there’s trouble, ask the school for help. Although classes haven’t started yet, there are still a few old-timers around."
Wang Lan nodded in acknowledgment and, with a flash, disappeared again.
The distress signal was less than three kilometers from Wang Lan, but it was three kilometers away in the direction opposite the prosperous area. At Wang Lan’s full speed, it would take him at most ten minutes to get there.
Like a ghost of the night, Wang Lan reached the interior of a park with a few flashes. Once there, the reverberations of the battle were as distinct in the darkness as a beacon.
Wang Lan hurried over, only to see two dark figures engaging in fierce combat in the night. One of them, wearing a black baseball cap, clutched his chest with one hand while desperately using his weapon to block the attacks from the opposing Star Martial Warrior.
The opposing Star Martial Warrior moved like a ghost, their movements completely unpredictable. If not for the man in the baseball cap relying on his exquisite Earth Attribute Star Martial Skill to alter the terrain and execute complex, coordinated defenses, he would have already been killed by the opponent.
The comrade calling for help must be one of them, but since neither was wearing a uniform, Wang Lan couldn’t be sure.
In an instant, Wang Lan appeared in the sky and, pointing towards the two combatants, fired a Crescent Arrow.
WHOOSH!
The sudden attack caused both to pause their movements abruptly, and they separated in an instant.
The man in the baseball cap suddenly coughed violently, clutching his chest and swaying, on the verge of collapse.
The opposing shadow hesitated for a moment, then flashed and vanished into the night.
"Are you a comrade from the Bureau?" the man in the baseball cap called out warily.
"Are you from the Tianjian Bureau?" Rustling footsteps sounded as Wang Lan emerged from the darkness.
"Modu City Intelligence Section field agent Cai Jianjun. You look unfamiliar, kid; I haven’t seen you at the Bureau before."
"Suzhou City Tianjian Bureau Intelligence Section special agent Wang Lan, currently studying at Modu Star Martial Academy," Wang Lan said, pulling out his ID as he walked over slowly. The other man was slightly taken aback; he had never encountered such an introduction method before but quickly produced his own ID as well.
After verifying each other’s IDs, their wariness relaxed.
"You’re hurt? Here, let me treat you."

chapters.title: Chapter 257 Pure Energy Loading
chapters.content:
Chapter 257: Chapter 257 Pure Energy Loading
A hazy, pure moonlight-like glow suddenly enveloped Wang Lan. Then, the light morphed into a beam, connecting to the wounded Tianjian Bureau agent like a lifeline.
Almost instantly, the agent felt a change in his body. He stared at Wang Lan with a shocked expression, "You... you’re a Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior?"
"Quick, over here!"
SWOOSH, SWOOSH, SWOOSH— Several figures flashed and landed beside Wang Lan and Cai Jianjun.
"Old Cai, are you okay?"
"Director Ming, quickly, get to Dock Seventeen! Someone is smuggling a large number of Space Stones."
"How are you?" Cai Jianjun asked.
"I’m fine. This brother’s medical skill is very strong; my injuries are no longer serious."
Ming Baiye turned his head to look at Wang Lan as the light around Wang Lan dissipated. Seeing Ming Baiye’s colonel rank, Wang Lan immediately stood at attention and saluted, "Wang Lan, Senior Special Agent of the Suzhou City Tianjian Bureau Intelligence Department, reporting to the commanding officer!"
"Oh? So you’re that mascot from Suzhou City, huh? I’ve heard of you," Ming Baiye said. "There’s no time to delay. We’re heading to Dock Seventeen immediately. Young man, you come with us."
"Yes, sir!"
The group sped towards their destination. Since they had arrived in a hurry, few had vehicles, so most were running on foot. But one shouldn’t underestimate the legs of a Star Martial Warrior; at full speed, they were no slower than a car.
In less than ten minutes, they arrived at the silent Dock Seventeen.
Dock Seventeen was still under construction. Construction began in 2016 and was expected to be completed in 2026. Temporary warehouses were available for rent outside the dock. Dock Seventeen was enormous. Without Cai Jianjun’s guidance, finding the Space Stone smugglers would have been quite difficult.
Dozens of Tianjian Bureau agents cautiously approached the target warehouse. The black warehouse subtly distorted in the moonlit night, its silence pierced only by the noise from a distant construction site.
Cai Jianjun explained, "I had just investigated this place when they discovered me. Then, I was chased by four squads of experts. I killed three along the way but was also seriously injured. If Brother Wang Lan hadn’t arrived and scared them off, I might have been done for. But I’ve been exposed. They might be alert by now and could have already moved the goods."
"No!" Ming Baiye suddenly halted and shouted, "The distortion of the warehouse ahead is a bit too severe."
The moment Ming Baiye spoke, Wang Lan also realized it. The warehouse, shrouded in the moonlit mist, seemed unnaturally twisted, like chopsticks refracted on the water’s surface.
Just as Ming Baiye finished speaking, the space before them suddenly rippled. The warehouse contorted as though violently twisted by someone into a bizarre shape.
"Damn it!" Ming Baiye cursed. "Those bastards! They’ve activated the Space Stone and opened a Different Dimensional Space!"
HUM, HUM, HUM—
ROAR—
A savage beast with a head like a Winged Dragon protruded from the shimmering ripples and let out a piercing roar at Wang Lan and the others.
BOOM—
Ming Baiye extended a finger, and a bolt of lightning instantly exploded the beast’s head. "Roar at your mother! Go! Close this Different Dimensional Space!"
Wang Lan had never seen a Different Dimensional Space opened so abruptly. When Ming Baiye gave the order, he charged towards the Different Dimensional Space along with dozens of others.
It felt like passing through a curtain of water or jumping into water itself. One moment they were in the outside world, and the next, they had entered the Different Dimensional Space.
Inside was a mountainous spatial world. The sky was gray-white, without a sun, yet it was illuminated. In the distance, dense swarms of Exotic Beasts were converging towards the entrance.
"Good, they’re all Star Shine Stage Exotic Beasts," Ming Baiye said, sighing with relief when he saw these beasts with leopard-like bodies and Winged Dragon-like heads. "Engage in team combat! Close the Different Dimensional Space as quickly as possible!"
"Yes, sir!"
The Modu City Tianjian Bureau agents were all battle-hardened warriors. They needed only the command for team combat to coordinate flawlessly. But Wang Lan, a newcomer, suddenly found himself awkwardly alone.
"Wang Lan, I’ve heard about your medical abilities. You take care of support and healing," Ming Baiye said, immediately noticing Wang Lan’s predicament.
"Yes, sir!"
The battle began. Instantly, the Modu City Tianjian Bureau agents unleashed their powerful offensive capabilities. In five areas, terrifying area-of-effect Star Martial Skills wreaked havoc, engulfing thousands of densely packed Exotic Beasts in a moment.
Such magnificent scenes of combat, rarely seen in one-on-one battles, roused Wang Lan’s fighting spirit.
After thirty seconds of continuous damage output, the distant Exotic Beasts halted their charge, roaring as they gathered just beyond the range of the Tianjian Bureau’s Star Martial Skills. As the dust from the Tianjian Bureau’s Star Martial Skills began to settle, the Exotic Beasts suddenly opened their mouths. Countless, densely packed wind blades rained down on the Tianjian Bureau agents like a storm of bullets.
Individual wind blades wouldn’t have been very powerful, nor would the spectacle be as striking. But thousands of wind blades descending like a deluge was terrifying to witness firsthand.
"Extreme Wall of Water!" Ming Baiye roared. Instantly, five Star Martial Warriors lined up with him and summoned a water wall before them, blocking the dense onslaught of wind blades.
ROAR—
With another roar, some of the Exotic Beasts in front charged at them again, while those behind provided cover with wind blade attacks. This classic human-devised tactic was being executed instinctively by the beasts.
"Kill—!" Facing the Exotic Beasts, the Tianjian Bureau agents fearlessly charged forward.
"Everyone, spread out—!" Wang Lan roared. After finding a solid position, he instantly squatted and slapped the ground with one palm. "Earth Surge Fire Sea!"
BOOM—
Even on the ground that had just been doused with water, intense flames burst forth in an instant. This time, Wang Lan held nothing back, unleashing his ultimate move. The surging fire was not like a wildfire spreading across a prairie but like a roiling sea of flames. Before their eyes, a ten-meter-high wave of fire rolled forward.
The rapidly charging Exotic Beasts crashed headlong into the sea of fire, their flesh visibly disintegrating into charred remains within the flames.
"Nice—!"
The Tianjian Bureau agents cried out in unison. With this single move, Wang Lan had directly annihilated hundreds of the charging Exotic Beasts. The results were so substantial that even Ming Baiye wore an incredulous expression.
"Who would’ve thought Brother Wang Lan wasn’t just a Medical Attribute Star Martial Warrior?" Cai Jianjun exclaimed, his face a mask of astonishment. "Damn it, when did medical types start hitting harder than us?"
"Impressive! An S-class Star Martial Skill, just like that?" another agent remarked. "With this kind of skill, we have nothing to worry about. Brother Wang Lan, you lead the way! Let’s head straight to the space node!"
In a Different Dimensional Space, mana was probably the one thing they wouldn’t run out of. An S-class Star Martial Skill had emptied Wang Lan’s mana bar, but killing several hundred Exotic Beasts yielded enough Soul Beads to refill his mana seven or eight times over.
With everyone’s help, Wang Lan quickly collected the Soul Beads. As his mana bar refilled, he also gained several hundred skill points.
How delightful!
The Exotic Beasts in this space were all wind-attributed, which Wang Lan perfectly countered. Coupled with his own considerable strength, Wang Lan, frankly, felt no danger in this Different Dimensional Space.
With Wang Lan clearing the path, Ming Baiye slaying the more powerful individual Exotic Beasts, and dozens of people forming a spearhead formation to charge forward, it took less than an hour for the group to reach the space node.
It was Wang Lan’s first time seeing a space node. It looked like a cluster of crystal vines emitting a blue glow. Starlight-like dust occasionally drifted down from the vines.
"Director Ming, is this the space node? What exactly is it?" Wang Lan asked.
"I don’t know what it actually is either. All we need to know is that it’s a space node," Ming Baiye replied. "Many scientists are researching what space nodes really are, but we just need to know that shattering the space node will cause the Different Dimensional Space to collapse."
As he spoke, his Star Power flared, and he struck the space node with a thunderous punch.
CRACK—
With a crisp sound, the blue gemstone at the center of the space node instantly fractured like shattered glass.
"Why not use a Star Martial Skill?" Wang Lan asked.
"Space nodes are very peculiar. No Star Martial Skill can destroy them, yet they are inherently fragile. A force of over five tons is enough to shatter it."
Saying this, Ming Baiye threw another punch.
BOOM—
With this punch, the entire space seemed to tremble violently. The space node before them suddenly spiderwebbed with cracks. Fragments broke off, only to dissipate in mid-air.
A hazy white light spilled out from the space node, instantly sweeping over Wang Lan’s body.
"System Alert: Compulsory loadable energy detected. Load now?"
Huh?
Wang Lan’s heart skipped a beat.
What was that compulsory load last time? Phoenix Form, right?
"Yes!"
"System: Scanning compulsory load container. Loadable energy: Phoenix Form. Expend skill points to load?"
What a pointless question!
Instantly, the skill points on his system interface began to decrease rapidly, as if being devoured, at a rate of ten per second. Wang Lan couldn’t have stopped it even if he’d wanted to.
"System: Load complete—"
In less than three seconds, over forty skill points were gone.
But... wasn’t that a bit too fast?
As the loading finished, the space node before them completely vanished. Then, the entire space began to distort, gradually becoming hazy.
"Retreat, quickly! The space is about to collapse!" Ming Baiye shouted. The Tianjian Bureau agents instantly rushed towards the exit.
At the exit, they met up with the agents who had been guarding the entrance to the Different Dimensional Space. The group streamed out of the Different Dimensional Space in single file. Looking back at the warehouse, they saw it gradually wink out like a twisting flame as it distorted.
In this battle, they had killed nearly five thousand Exotic Beasts. Wang Lan had received 20,000 experience points and 700 skill points. These experience points were only a tenth of the 200,000 needed to level up. However, the rewards were proportional to the effort. The Star Power he had consumed was replenished by the Soul Beads, and the fight hadn’t taken much time.
"Allow me to formally introduce myself again," Ming Baiye said. "I am Ming Baiye, Director of the Action Department of the Modu City Tianjian Bureau. Wang Lan, you’re affiliated with the Suzhou City Tianjian Bureau, right? Now that you’re here in Modu City and will be studying here for four years, why not affiliate with the Modu City Tianjian Bureau?"
"So... am I switching sides?" Wang Lan asked.
"Not exactly. It’s just a temporary affiliation. Your official post will remain with the Suzhou City Bureau."
I don’t even have an official post in Suzhou City yet,
Wang Lan grumbled inwardly. Then, showing a polite expression to Ming Baiye, he said, "Director Ming, perhaps you shouldn’t call me ’young brother’ anymore. Ming Guodong and I are roommates."
"Oh? What a coincidence!" Ming Baiye exclaimed. "Then just call me Mr. Ming, or Uncle Ye if you like. Come on, let’s head back to the Bureau."

chapters.title: Chapter 258: Official Start of the New Semester
chapters.content:
Chapter 258: Chapter 258: Official Start of the New Semester
"Mr. Ming, why do Different Dimensional Spaces open up?" Wang Lan asked curiously on the way back.
"Although you are already a qualified warrior, you’ve only just started college and are still a newbie, so what you know is similar to what most newbies know.
"First of all, one question: why do Different Dimensional Spaces exist? Initially, humans always believed that Different Dimensional Spaces were the work of the Demon Clan. Since ancient times, the Demon Clan and Exotic Beasts, like natural allies, have been continuously invading our world, causing one disaster after another.
"With the resurgence of technology two hundred years ago and its vibrant development up to the present, many things we once steadfastly believed in have come into question. This includes Different Dimensional Spaces.
"Different Dimensional Spaces actually have nothing to do with the Demon Clan. Exotic Beasts are the original inhabitants of Different Dimensional Spaces. These spaces are very complex; the most mainstream view is that they are Subspace—spaces without complete Laws or operational rules.
"The mystery of their existence is like the mystery of humankind’s own existence, or why there is life on Sky Blue Star. It’s one of the ten great unsolved mysteries of antiquity. Different Dimensional Spaces are inevitable and exist randomly.
"It’s like where there is light, there are shadows. You might like the light and not the shadows, but you can never throw your shadow away.
"Other smaller countries suffer greatly from the unregulated openings of Different Dimensional Spaces. Every time one opens, the Exotic Beasts inside charge out, causing substantial damage to cities and people. Meanwhile, powerful countries are relatively stable, with much lower frequencies of Different Dimensional Space openings. Do you know why?"
Wang Lan shook his head.
"Because of the existence of Pioneer Spaces." Ming Baiye looked out the window, towards the east. "Pioneer Space is essentially a Different Dimensional Space, only much larger. At the very beginning, Pioneer Space was a very, very small space, which the Pioneering Legion expanded step by step into a huge space.
"Why pioneer? Many people don’t understand. Pioneers work so hard, always at risk of dying in battle. Are they doing it for Soul Beads? To become stronger?
"Neither. It’s to protect our country. If the army is our country’s sharp sword, then the Pioneers are our country’s shield. Pioneer Space is like a wall locking down our territory.
"Different Dimensional Spaces open randomly; no one knows when or where one will appear. And Different Dimensional Spaces have an attraction to each other. It’s like soap bubbles: if one space opens, then another Different Dimensional Space opening nearby will be absorbed by the first one. Do you understand this concept?"
"I get it. It’s like universal gravitation."
"Another Law of Different Dimensional Spaces is that smaller spaces are dependent on larger spaces. As long as a Pioneer Space is large enough, any other spaces that would have opened randomly in its vicinity will instead open within that Pioneer Space. Because our country has five large Pioneer Spaces, there are almost no records of unregulated openings of Different Dimensional Spaces here.
"However, there is one exception: Different Dimensional Spaces forcibly opened using Space Stones. Space Stones act like magnets that firmly attract Different Dimensional Spaces. Spaces that would have been drawn towards a Pioneer Space are thus forcibly kept in place."
"So, that’s the reason for the space that opened up just now?"
"So, this is why the state strictly forbids smuggling Space Stones," Ming Baiye said coldly. "Space Stones are good things; used well, they benefit the state and the people. But they are also double-edged swords that can bring catastrophic disasters upon us. Therefore, many Star Martial families smear this state law, saying things like, ’Only officials are allowed to commit arson, while commoners can’t even light lamps.’ But it’s all just to satisfy their own interests."
"Interests? Can they be sold for money?"
"Money? What does that mean to the Star Martial Families? Didn’t you just see? Exotic Beasts! Soul Beads! These Exotic Beasts and Soul Beads are all unrecorded and tax-free."
"Are you saying that today’s Different Dimensional Space opening is..."
"Very likely."
"But what if the Exotic Beasts in the Different Dimensional Space they opened are extremely ferocious?"
"If they can handle it, they’ll deal with it. If not, they’ll just walk away. As long as they clean up their tracks, who’s to know it was them? Even if someone suspects it, without evidence, what can be done to them? In the end, doesn’t the Tianjian Bureau have to clean up the mess? If the Tianjian Bureau can’t handle it, isn’t there still the military, and experts dispatched by the state?"
Shameless!
"So, people like that, we deal with them as we find them, regardless of their status or position. Once they touch this red line, there will be no leniency."
As they talked, the group returned to the Tianjian Bureau.
"Wang Lan, thank you for tonight. I’ll arrange an affiliation procedure for you; you’ll be attached to my Action Department. Any problems with that?"
"No, no problem!"
"Later, you’ll need to make a written statement for our records."
"Alright... By the way, Mr. Ming, do you know about the female student who committed suicide at Modu City’s Star Martial Academy two years ago?"
"That... I need to check the internal records. Why? Are you interested in this? Do you have some connection to that female student?"
"No, there isn’t a connection. It’s just... Mr. Ming, with your wide knowledge and experience, do ghosts exist in this world?"
"Ghosts?" Ming Baiye looked at Wang Lan and suddenly laughed. "There are certainly no ghosts. Don’t worry about that."
"But..." Wang Lan immediately told Ming Baiye about the events of the previous night. Ming Baiye, who had initially dismissed it as a joke, gradually grew serious.
"What you’re describing isn’t a ghost, but an apparition of spiritual power remnants. After all, as Star Martial Warriors, we are different from ordinary people. If it were purely spiritual power, it couldn’t remain after death. But for a Star Martial Warrior, it’s possible. It’s similar to an Illusion Technique!
"For instance, if a Star Martial Warrior casts an Illusion Technique on another, making them believe they’ve turned into a dog, the one under the illusion will genuinely think they are a dog and mimic all of a dog’s behaviors. Even if the Caster is killed, the Illusion Technique won’t automatically dispel.
"Another Star Martial Warrior would need to disrupt the victim’s Star Power to help them break free from the Illusion Technique’s effects. And what you saw could very well be a room where an Illusion Technique was placed, set to trigger when certain conditions are met."
"So you’re saying, I was under an Illusion Technique last night? Was the Illusion Technique cast by that senior student back then, or by someone else?"
"Normally, even an Illusion Technique wouldn’t last that long. Moreover, the girl in the Illusion Technique asked you to avenge her. But if it was the Caster themself, why wouldn’t they directly tell you who to seek revenge against? Who to target?
"The only possibility I can think of is that the Caster also didn’t know the truth. He believed the girl died unjustly but was unclear about who was responsible for her death. So... he cast the Illusion Technique on you."
"I see, that makes sense. As long as there are no ghosts... hahaha..."
"Wang Lan, look at this. This is the file from the incident two years ago; it was ruled a suicide. Her boyfriend was from the main lineage of the Duanmu Family and, moreover, the son of the clan leader. Ma Chuchu, on the other hand, was just an ordinary girl from ChuanProvince. Although her talent was outstanding, her social status was vastly different. The couple was ultimately forced to separate. Ma Chuchu, heartbroken, then used the weapon her boyfriend had given her to take her own life."
"Are we certain it was suicide?"
"The Tianjian Bureau’s official finding was suicide. If you want to reopen the case, you can investigate, but you’ll need compelling evidence."
Wang Lan laughed. "School is about to start. I don’t have time for that."
Right then, a sudden commotion was heard from outside, and a captain in bloodstained red attire entered the office, hesitating slightly as he glanced at Wang Lan.
"Juan, take Wang Lan to give his statement, then arrange for him to rest. He can’t go back to the school dormitory."
"Okay!"
"Director, we were too late. After receiving your instructions, we immediately followed the leads. However, by the time we reached the trading company, someone had already beaten us to it, killing everyone there and destroying all the ledgers and computers."
"Killed everyone? How many?"
"This trading company was established by a Pioneer Team. Its seventeen core members were all murdered. These core members rarely gathered together. Yet today, all were present and wiped out in one fell swoop. I suspect the perpetrator was someone in a position of command over them."
"That’s obvious. But a lost lead isn’t a reason to give up the investigation. Keep looking!"
"Yes!"
Wang Lan slept in the Tianjian Bureau’s dorm for one night and returned to his dorm the next morning. Neither He Jing nor Ming Guodong asked where Wang Lan had been, acting as if he had never left.
「Before he knew it, the official start of school on September 1st had arrived.」
The school, which had been almost empty just days before, was suddenly teeming with people.
The atmosphere of the university campus was completely different from that of high school. If high school students looked like unripe peaches, still showing their greenness, then university students were like fully ripened fruit, exuding an alluring temptation.
Girls who were still bare-faced and wore ponytails were undoubtedly new students, freshly arrived at the academy. The upperclassmen, in contrast, all projected an air of maturity. They even managed to wear the standard school uniforms with a distinct, sophisticated flair.
As a combat-proficient Star Martial Warrior, which idiot assigned me to the Auxiliary Department?
Wang Lan fumed internally.
Even if not the Mage Department, I should have been assigned to the Close Combat Department, right?
Although Wang Lan was utterly reluctant, He Jing and Ming Guodong were so envious they practically wished they could take his place.
The Auxiliary Department was notoriously female-dominated. At the Star Martial Academy, the Mage Department had the most balanced gender ratio. The Close Combat Department was full of burly guys, and while the Investigation Department had more males, it wasn’t excessively so. But the Auxiliary Department? Eighty percent female Star Martial Warriors.
Each one of them was sweet and delicate. Wang Lan, walking through the Auxiliary Department’s building, felt like a lone blade of grass in a vast garden of flowers—glaringly out of place.
Being surrounded by beauties might sound wonderful, but actually being immersed in it wasn’t so great. Especially with all the stories about girls pranking their male classmates—like forcing them into drag... There were tons of posts about it online, enough to make Wang Lan’s hair stand on end and break out in a cold sweat.
The first order of business wasn’t military training; that was for ordinary universities. It was entirely unnecessary for the Star Martial Academy. The actual first order of business was choosing electives.
Mandatory courses included Tactics, Battlefield Survival, In-depth Study of the Demon Clan and Different Dimensional Worlds, Advanced Combat, and Spiritual Engraving. All students also had to choose at least four electives. With a total of nine courses, the workload was by no means less than that of high school.

chapters.title: Chapter 260: Dare Not Skip My Class
chapters.content:
Chapter 260: Chapter 260: Dare Not Skip My Class
Lan Qi’s eyes drooped inadvertently as he looked at the pair, who seemed like a match made in heaven, a flash of jealousy flickering in the depths of his gaze.
Why are they so outstanding, so happy? Both of them are so wealthy, gifted with talent, and have backgrounds that are the envy of everyone. Even world-renowned scientists are their relatives?
But in an instant, Lan Qi realized. How could I harbor such thoughts? How could I be so easily jealous of others? But... it’s truly infuriating, why don’t I have such a good family background?
Jealousy is the original sin, an inherent aspect of human nature. Seeing the good in others can evoke feelings of envy, which turn into jealousy when such envy is for things one cannot have.
After finishing their meal, the trio walked around the mall before returning to the university.
Wang Lan and his friends had dined well and were enjoying themselves physically and mentally, but far away in the university’s Medical Star Martial Research department, the beautiful teacher Sun Li was not in a good mood.
This year, there were six hundred freshmen. Compared to previous years, the number of students electing to take battlefield medical courses had increased, with over seventy individuals. Just after class, Sun Li eagerly went to the office to review the student profiles, picking out the new students she favored.
However, as she went through the profiles, Sun Li’s expression grew darker and more unsightly. After flipping through the last one, only a cold smile remained on her face.
"Really taking my words as a passing breeze? I recruited you, and you dare not choose my course?"
Just after entering the school, Wang Lan and Jiang Xinyu parted ways. Walking on the school’s main avenue, full of dreamy colors, a warm breeze played with his elegant hair. It was especially comfortable and pleasant.
Such an afternoon should be for a nap.
It was just that there was only half an hour left before class, so there would be no time for a nap.
Suddenly, Wang Lan stopped in his tracks; he suddenly felt a heart-stopping premonition.
What’s going on? Could it be Duanmu Yi making his move?
"Wang Lan... Wang Lan, are you Wang Lan?" A senior-looking girl came running from a distance and arrived in front of Wang Lan, sizing him up.
"Yes, you are...?"
"Hello, I’m from the fourth-year Auxiliary Department. Here’s the thing, Director Sun from the medical department wants you to visit right now."
"Director Sun? Who is that? What does she want with me?"
"Sun... Director Sun, you should have met her, right? The one who recruited you into the school..."
"Oh! I remember now." An image of a female teacher in a sexy, tight dress with a head of gorgeous wavy hair suddenly flashed through Wang Lan’s mind.
"Do you know what she wants?"
"Not sure, but you better hurry. Director Sun has a bit of a temper, and if you’re late, you might suffer for it."
Following the senior girl, Wang Lan arrived at the medical department. All the students there wore white lab coats, just like doctors in a hospital. The seniors passing by Wang Lan were engrossed in academic discussions, heads bowed. Even if they saw Wang Lan, they treated him as if he were invisible.
Then he was led to the third floor, which consisted of numerous labs. Inside, students were either observing test tubes and reagents or recording data displayed on instruments. The intense atmosphere of scientific research made Wang Lan almost believe he had stumbled into some pharmaceutical research institute.
"Director Sun, Wang Lan has been brought here."
"Come in!" an icy voice came from inside.
The senior girl gave Wang Lan a look that said, ’Good luck,’ and then pushed him inside.
The entire office was very large, with three walls of shelves stacked densely with an impressive array of inscrutable bottles and containers.
Sun Li propped up her sharp chin, looking slightly flirtatiously at a somewhat bewildered Wang Lan. She extended her seductive tongue and licked the corner of her mouth. "Wang Lan, we meet again... I remember telling you that I hoped you would enroll in the battlefield medical course... you’ve gone back on your word, huh."
"Hello, Mrs. Sun... I don’t recall agreeing?"
"You didn’t refuse, so I thought you had agreed." Sun Li slowly stood up and came over to Wang Lan, scrutinizing his eyes.
"You’ve awakened your Medical Star Martial Innate Ability but did not sign up for the battlefield medical discipline... give me a reason."
"I think my Medical Star Martial Technique is already suitable for the battlefield. My Star Martial Skill can quickly heal wounds, even achieving organ regeneration and limb reattachment. To put it arrogantly, as long as one doesn’t die on the spot, my Star Martial Skill can fully heal them." Wang Lan stood straight, his eyes not straying as he spoke. This teacher gave him a very dangerous feeling. Initially, Wang Lan had wanted to express his thoughts in a more tactful manner, but under Mrs. Sun’s direct gaze, he subconsciously voiced his most sincere thoughts.
"Is that so..." Sun Li gently adjusted Wang Lan’s collar. "What about now?"
As Sun Li’s words landed, Wang Lan’s complexion suddenly changed. The Song of Life instantly activated automatically, and a hazy glow rose around Wang Lan. In the blink of an eye, a green impurity of light appeared within the white light surrounding his body.
About ten seconds later, the surrounding white glow returned to its milky white color. Wang Lan’s body also recovered.
"Mrs. Sun, what are you implying? Poisoning a student, is that something a teacher like you should do?"
"Indeed! Your Inborn Talent of the Bloodline is truly remarkable. It only takes you ten seconds to detoxify."
"Thank you for the compliment."
"But do you know that many people poisoned with this toxin would die within thirty seconds? If you had thirty poisoned warriors in front of you, how would you ensure your battlefield medicine?"
Wang Lan’s face changed slightly.
"Your talent is indeed very effective in healing physical injuries, but what about other afflictions? When I use the term ’affliction,’ I’m not referring to a single concept; it covers two things: disease and poison. Do you think Medical Star Martial Warriors are only for treating teammates’ injuries?
"Those who only treat mere bruises and sprains are called quacks, not Medical Star Martial Warriors. Besides physical trauma, there is another type of damage that is more powerful and widespread—Star Martial Toxins.
"And Star Martial Toxins are never a singular killing force. Once they appear, they always sweep over a large area. Is your Innate Ability still sufficient?"
"This... such cases are quite rare, aren’t they?"
"In the world, there are currently 170,000 recorded species of Exotic Beasts, among which 20,000 species are Poisonous Beasts.
