But all these precious treasures had been lost, resulting in Star Martial Warriors having only two ways to obtain Star Power: absorbing Soul Beads or absorbing the Star Power within their cells. Soul Beads required money and significant resources, while absorbing Star Power from cells depleted one’s life force.
This was also why Star Martial families firmly occupied the top of the pyramid, and why countless Star Martial Warriors depended on them. Star Martial Warriors without family backing who wished to obtain Soul Beads or Star Martial Skills to improve themselves could only attach themselves to Star Martial families, serving at their beck and call.
However, if Star Martial Warriors no longer needed to depend on Soul Beads to advance their Star Power levels, the Star Martial families would lose their appeal to lower-ranking warriors. The power of these families would quickly diminish, eventually leading to their collapse.
And that was not even the most lethal issue.
While Star Martial families possessed profound resources, they also relied on them to cultivate generations of outstanding disciples. Even someone lacking talent could be molded into a genius through an abundance of Soul Beads and Star Martial Skills. Outstanding younger generations could bring immeasurable influence to their families.
But if this imbalance were broken, geniuses from commoner families would close the gap with the descendants of Star Martial families. It would no longer be an era dominated by Star Martial families, but a time when talented individuals from humble backgrounds could rise to prominence.
For the nation, this was a tremendously positive development, with talent emerging in abundance and offering nothing but benefits. But for the Star Martial families, this represented an unprecedented catastrophe—they were almost pushed to the edge of a cliff, liable to be shoved over at any moment.
In an instant, a terrifying thought crossed Yu Huailong’s mind:
Kill them both! If I just kill them, the ancient cultivation technique won’t be spread... Even if I’m blasted to pieces, it would be worth it!
But this thought could only flicker through his mind. Even with his peak Star Sea Realm strength, aside from Wang Lan and Yu Ruoyun, who among those present wasn’t at the Star Sea Realm? Ninety percent of them were Titled Strongmen, for goodness’ sake!
Make a move? Lift a finger, and I’d probably be incinerated on the spot,
he thought.
Then, Wang Lan took out a large handful of Soul Beads from his backpack. "When I was bored in the Nine-layer Pagoda, I engraved a few hundred copies of this Immortal Cloud Mysterious Green Record. They’re all here. Grab a handful if you want one."
This move by Wang Lan almost made Yu Huailong, who had just been contemplating murder, spit out a mouthful of old blood.
You... just how bored were you? Engraving a few hundred copies? With everyone present getting a copy, the spread of this technique couldn’t be suppressed! Were you... that afraid this technique wouldn’t become widespread?
"Oh? Interesting. Give me one, let me take a look," Zuo Ming said, accepting a Soul Bead.
Instantly, the Soul Bead in his fingertips shattered, and a surge of Star Power enveloped Zuo Ming. A series of sharp CRACKLING sounds erupted—the noise of twelve meridian checkpoints being breached. This rapid succession of pops, like firecrackers, made Wang Lan’s mouth twitch.
This guy isn’t just formidable; he’s ruthless!
Wang Lan possessed a system cheat, allowing him to instantly clear blocked meridians by adding points. In contrast, Yu Ruoyun had spent several hours to clear just three, each breakthrough as arduous as overcoming severe constipation. But Zuo Ming, in a flash, experienced an unstoppable torrent, blasting through all the checkpoints of the twelve meridians in mere seconds.
According to Yu Ruoyun, breaking through each checkpoint induced an unbearable soreness and swelling, an agony few could endure. A single point was excruciating, yet Zuo Ming had instantly cleared over a hundred such points. The compounded pain must have been immense, yet he hadn’t even furrowed his brow.
He merely frowned slightly before opening his eyes. "It’s truly possible to absorb the Heavenly Earth Star Power," he declared. "Though the absorption speed is very slow, not as pronounced as the immediate boost from Soul Beads. However, little drops make a mighty ocean, and rivers merge into the sea. Seven days of cultivation would yield gains comparable to a low-grade Soul Bead.
"Personally verified—it’s truly effective! The rise of Jade Country is in sight! Hahaha! Wang Lan, your contribution is unparalleled in history!"
Hearing Zuo Ming’s words, all the influential figures present eagerly reached for a Soul Bead, each one absorbing it. Even Yu Huailong couldn’t resist extending his hand.
Wang Lan wasn’t sure of the proportion of relentless individuals to ordinary people outside, but he was certain that the dozens of people here were all cut from that relentless cloth. Almost every person who absorbed a Soul Bead did so in one go, their bodies emitting CRACKING sounds as if not their own.
Doesn’t that hurt?
Wang Lan wondered.
"It really works!"
"The problem that has plagued us for millennia, the ancient cultivation techniques lost for thousands of years, have reemerged!"
"The ancient cultivation civilization has reappeared! Hahaha! Demon Clan, let’s see you act so brazenly now! In thirty years, how will you withstand our human army, its strength vastly increased? Hahaha!"
The dignitaries in the meeting room lost their composure, ecstatic. This simple cultivation technique could completely replace Soul Beads! No longer fettered by the restrictions on acquiring Star Power, many talented Star Martial Warriors would not be held back for a decade.
Ten years—how many decades does a person have in their lifetime? Those who experienced Soul Resonance Awakening might only be delayed by three years, but what about those who awakened on their own? The future achievements of those geniuses who awakened at age eight, nine, or ten would be vastly different.
Consider Duan Ziqi. If this cultivation technique had existed back then, would he have become the Demon Clan’s Poison Sting? His talent was so exceptional that even the Demon Clan considered him the perfect candidate for the Poison Sting—a testament to his profound natural gifts. The likes of Mu Shaoyun couldn’t even compare to Duan Ziqi. Mu Shaoyun, like Jiang Xinyu, came from wealth and never lacked Soul Beads. Moreover, the strength Mu Shaoyun displayed at the provincial martial arts tournament was on par with Wang Mingling’s.
After about half an hour, the excitement in the room gradually subsided. The gazes fixed on Wang Lan were filled with profound admiration. If they hadn’t all been grown men, some might have been tempted to grab Wang Lan and give him a hearty kiss.
"Today has truly been one joyous event after another," Eld Di said, his voice bringing the room to order. "Alright, everyone here holds important positions and is incredibly busy. Let’s conclude things swiftly.
"Let’s return to the main agenda. Wang Lan, although you miraculously survived, it’s clear you were lured into a trap. You’ve always been meticulous in your thinking. Do you have any suspects?"
Upon hearing this, Wang Lan’s expression changed drastically. "Principal," he urged, "quickly send someone to bring Mrs. Sun Li here. It must be an expert!"
"What? You suspect Mrs. Sun Li?"
"She is highly suspicious."
"I’ll go personally." Nangong Meng stood, his expression grim, and promptly left the room.
Once Nangong Meng had departed, Eld Di looked at Wang Lan and asked, "Tell us, what is your reasoning?"
"If one examines the progression of events, everything appears logical. However, if you work backward, it becomes evident that this was all orchestrated. The trap was set in The Death Valley, a remote location also known as the Life Forbidden Zone. Furthermore, before the culprits activated the Space Stone, one of them said, ’Princess Yu, we’ve been waiting for you for a long time.’
"From this, it’s clear the trap was specifically laid for Yu Ruoyun. This raises a couple of questions. First, whoever set the trap must have already possessed the antidote—which I suspect was actually a vaccine.
"Second, they needed to lure us into The Death Valley. Only by going there could we discover the pickaxe they left behind, leading us to suspect someone was illicitly mining Space Stones, and thus walk right into their trap.
"To enter The Death Valley, we had to overcome the Ghost Eye Toxin present there. While I’ve grasped the principles for formulating a vaccine, I don’t know how to actually produce it.
"Therefore, our only option was to create an antidote for the Ghost Eye Toxin, essentially fighting poison with poison. However, this entire plan hinged on one prerequisite: the Star Martial Toxin Synthesizer. Without that device, I couldn’t have produced an antidote, much less entered The Death Valley with Yu Ruoyun.
"Yet, just before I entered the Nine-layer Pagoda, Mrs. Sun Li gave me her personal, portable Star Martial Toxin Synthesizer.
"At the time, I simply thought my teacher was concerned for me, giving it to me for unforeseen circumstances. Now, it seems it was a necessary component to lead me into The Death Valley."
Hearing Wang Lan’s analysis, Eld Di nodded silently and glanced at his watch.
Less than ten minutes later, Nangong Meng returned, alone.
"Eld Di, Dean Sun has committed suicide by poison."
"What?!"
"In her office at the Medical Department. When I arrived, she had already been dead for some time. The poison she ingested appears to be Ghost Eye Toxin. She was clutching a sample vial of the poison in her hand."
Upon hearing this, Wang Lan shot to his feet and vanished from the conference room in a flash.
When Wang Lan reached the Medical Department, its entrance was crowded with students. Though they were engaged in heated discussion, no one had entered to disturb the scene.
"Little Junior Brother, you’re here! Mrs. Sun... why would she... so suddenly..."
"Little Junior Brother, the Vice-Principal instructed us not to go inside and disturb the scene."
Wang Lan approached the door but was intercepted by two senior members of the student council.
"I am a special agent from the Tianjian Bureau’s Action Department. I am authorized to inspect the scene."
Wang Lan presented his credentials. Though still skeptical after examining them, the student council members eventually allowed him to pass following his explanation.
The office was just as he remembered: rows of bookshelves and various impressive-looking samples. Mrs. Sun Li was slumped over the desk, as if asleep. In her hand, she clutched a labeled sample vial.
Wang Lan reached out and touched the nape of Mrs. Sun Li’s neck. Her skin was cool; she had indeed been dead for some time. Taking the vial from her hand, Wang Lan poured out a drop of the liquid and analyzed it. It was, as suspected, Ghost Eye Toxin.
Gently lifting Mrs. Sun Li’s upper body, Wang Lan noticed the corner of an envelope tucked into her collar. He slowly extracted it. On the envelope, in handwritten script, were the words: "For Wang Lan’s eyes only."
"Wang Lan, your teacher cannot bid you farewell in person, so I must resort to this crude method to leave my last words.
"I must offer you my sincerest apologies. You are the student who has made me, your teacher, proudest in my entire life. Having had the chance to teach you, I can die without regrets.
"Your teacher tried. I even had a fierce argument with the Principal, but I still couldn’t prevent you from entering the Nine-layer Pagoda.
"I know you’re incredibly clever. If you made it out alive, you’ve likely figured out that I was the one who arranged things in the Nine-layer Pagoda, haven’t you? I am truly sorry; it should have been me who went. But... well, who asked you to agree to team up with Yu Ruoyun?
"I know what you want me to tell you; you must be wondering about my reasons. But... never mind. This world is a complicated place, and it’s better if the reasons remain unsaid.
"Let it all end here, with me. Don’t investigate further. If this is uncovered, Jade Country will be plunged into turmoil.
"I have so much I could say, but it boils down to three words: I am sorry. My time is nearly up. I have one last request: please take care of Tong Tong for me."
The letter’s content was disjointed, evidently written in great haste, the handwriting messy and rushed. By the time Wang Lan finished reading it, the group of influential figures had also arrived outside the door.

chapters.title: Chapter 313: Wherever she dissatisfies you, I’ll have her change it.
chapters.content:
Chapter 313: Chapter 313: Wherever she dissatisfies you, I’ll have her change it.
Mrs. Sun Li was definitely not the only mastermind behind the scenes; Wang Lan had figured this out during his time in the Nine-layer Pagoda. Sun Li alone could not have orchestrated such a skillful arrangement.
But her death had definitively severed any possibility of Wang Lan continuing his investigation. Even if he had suspects, he wouldn’t be able to find a shred of evidence.
Wang Lan thought he would hate Mrs. Sun Li for her deception and betrayal.
However, at this moment, even though his emotions were incredibly complex and heavy, there wasn’t the slightest hint of hatred in his heart.
She had set up a murderous scheme to kill both Wang Lan and Yu Ruoyun. Yet, it was also she who had imparted all her life’s learning. Leaving aside her theoretical knowledge of Star Martial Toxins and her wealth of experimental data, Universal Decomposition alone was enough for Wang Lan to sincerely regard Sun Li as his teacher.
One must not negate the kindness one has received from others because of a single act of malice. Similarly, the murderous scheme Sun Li devised couldn’t erase the respect Wang Lan held for her.
Perhaps she was just someone caught in the currents of life, unable to act of her own accord.
If Sun Li hadn’t felt any reluctance or unwillingness to harm him, she could have left during that time. With the forces behind her, she surely could have kept herself well hidden.
Yet, she chose to use her own death to put an ellipsis on the matter.
Those who are detestable also have their pitiable sides.
"Mrs. Sun Li committed suicide, but there must be someone behind her," Wang Lan said calmly to the crowd entering the office.
"Besides Sun Li, do you have any other suspects?"
"There’s a possibility that the person behind Xiao Qing knows something. Otherwise, they wouldn’t have been able to infiltrate the Nine-layer Pagoda and attempt to assassinate Bai Ji. This needs a thorough investigation."
"This matter will be investigated by the Tianjian Bureau," Yi Zuguo said gravely. "Eld Di, with the current situation largely resolved, I plan to head to the Imperial Capital this afternoon to report to the paramount leader."
"Good!"
"Now that Princess Yu Ruoyun is unharmed, we will take our leave as well. Eld Di, we hope the academy will pay more attention to the safety of the students, especially the Princess. Although this was a false alarm, there’s no guarantee there won’t be a next time."
"Rest assured, King Ning, such an incident will not happen again," Nangong Meng replied, his expression grim.
"It had better not."
Wang Lan was specially permitted to take three days off. Upon receiving permission to leave, he immediately phoned Jiang Xinyu. The two met again.
This incident had fully broken the ice between Wang Lan and Jiang Xinyu. In full view of everyone, Jiang Xinyu threw herself into Wang Lan’s arms, cementing their relationship.
Jiang Xinyu was not the kind of girl who needed to be coddled. She knew how to regulate her own emotions, so by the time they met again, her spirits had already cleared like clouds parting to reveal the moon.
To put it romantically: if you are well, then it is a sunny day.
"All done?"
"Everything is almost wrapped up. Although the experience was bizarre, it was ultimately a narrow escape with many benefits. Actually... since we’re Star Martial Warriors, there’s no need to make such a big fuss about these types of incidents. We may encounter many more in the future. It was only because it was your first time that you were so unsettled. After a few more experiences like this, you might get used to it."
Before he could finish speaking, Wang Lan gasped in pain. Jiang Xinyu pinched the soft flesh at his waist and twisted.
"Are you planning for there to be several more times? Even though Star Martial Warriors constantly dance with danger, it’s not usually to the extent of practically announcing your own death, is it? Taking risks below forty percent is considered an adventure; anything above fifty percent is a suicide mission. Have you ever heard of a Star Martial Warrior seeking death for no reason?"
"That was an accident."
"Accidents can happen at any time."
"Xinyu, actually... I feel the danger exists primarily because we’re not strong enough. If we were stronger, we could disregard any danger. Oh, while I was in there, I obtained an ancient qi cultivation method. I’ll teach it to you."
"Hm?"
"It’s a cultivation method for refining Star Power from the heavens and earth, and it will be widely spread in a few days. The country will fully support this initiative. I’ll pass it on to you now, so your strength can continue to improve steadily even without Soul Beads."
As he spoke, Wang Lan formed a sword-finger gesture and touched the center of Jiang Xinyu’s brow. Spiritual power was channeled, and the skill inheritance was completed in less than a minute.
"Really?" Jiang Xinyu asked, her eyes sparkling with delighted surprise.
"Personally tested, tried and true."
"Wang Lan—" While Wang Lan and Jiang Xinyu were strolling around the school, Yu Ruoyun’s voice called out from behind them.
"Classmate Yu Ruoyun."
Hearing Wang Lan’s response, Yu Ruoyun’s expression faltered for a moment but quickly returned to normal.
During their time in the Nine-layer Pagoda, the four of them had grown very close, and Wang Lan had always called her Ruoyun. But once outside, he reverted to calling her ’Classmate Yu Ruoyun.’
"Wang Lan, may I have a moment of your time? My uncle would like to meet with you."
"Sure," Jiang Xinyu responded for Wang Lan before he could. "Let’s have dinner together tonight, Ruoyun?"
"Okay!"
On the surface, Jiang Xinyu and Yu Ruoyun seemed to have a better relationship—after all, they were roommates.
Following Yu Ruoyun, they reached an area behind the academy’s sports field where there was an artificial lake. The lake was large, encircled by a lush green lawn and a pebble-strewn path, with several quaint pavilions dotted around its edge.
The Qing Emperor was over fifty, yet he appeared to be in his early forties. He was tall and slender, with a refined, scholarly demeanor.
The Qing Emperor stood with his hands behind his back, gazing absently at the shimmering lake, a seemingly unresolvable sorrow in his eyes.
"Uncle, Wang Lan is here."
"Greetings, Lord Qing Emperor."
"Just call me Uncle," the Qing Emperor said affably. "Walk with me."
"Alright!"
"In the blink of an eye, you’ve grown so much," the Qing Emperor said, looking at Wang Lan with sudden emotion. "If your mother knew how accomplished you’ve become, she would be overjoyed."
"Uncle, what mission was my mother really on? Or was the mission a fabrication? Has she actually..." Wang Lan hesitated.
He had always been afraid to consider that possibility.
But this time, having narrowly escaped death in the Nine-layer Pagoda, with still no word from his mother, Wang Lan felt a deep unease.
"Don’t overthink it; your mother is still alive," the Qing Emperor said with a faint smile, his tone firm.
Words from the Qing Emperor were to be trusted. He would either withhold information from Wang Lan or, if he chose to speak, would not deign to lie.
"Where is she? When will her mission end?"
"I cannot tell you where she is; it’s a long-term mission. But your mother has already established a firm foothold. As for when she might return... I don’t know either."
"Is that so?"
"Thank you for this time. If it weren’t for you, Ruoyun probably wouldn’t have escaped this disaster."
"There’s no need for thanks; we supported each other. She saved my life too. It wasn’t a matter of who helped whom. Without her, I wouldn’t have survived either."
"I am merely thanking you on my own behalf. With Ruoyun safe, the Jade Country is secure." Saying this, he took a jade pendant from his robes and handed it to Wang Lan. "This jade pendant is my token. In the future, should you encounter any trouble or difficulty, you can bring it to find me. If you cannot find me, you can seek out anyone from the Yu Family."
One does not refuse a gift from an elder. Wang Lan accepted the jade pendant respectfully.
"Right, let me teach you another Star Martial Skill. You’re fire-attributed, aren’t you?"
"Actually, I’m all-attributed," Wang Lan replied softly.
"No matter. Meteor Fire Rain is a skill your mother excelled at. I shall pass it on to you." As he finished speaking, the Qing Emperor’s two fingers were already pressed against Wang Lan’s forehead.
A stream of spiritual power surged into Wang Lan’s mind. Instantly, a vast amount of information flooded in.
"Detectable learnable Star Martial Skill. Spend one thousand skill points to learn?"
"Yes!"
With his confirmation, one thousand skill points were deducted, and a brand-new Star Martial Skill appeared on Wang Lan’s skill panel.
"Detectable linkable Star Martial Skills. Spend twenty thousand skill points to link them?"
"Yes!"
After the ordeal in the Nine-layer Pagoda, Wang Lan’s depleted skill points had been substantially replenished. While not an immense amount, he still had a surplus of fifty thousand skill points.
"Among the younger generation, you are a clear leader. The qi cultivation method you’ve brought back this time will elevate the strength of Jade Country’s Star Martial Warriors to a new level. We are old; we may not live to see the day the Demon Clan invades. The future of the Jade Country rests on your generation."
"Thank you for your high esteem, Uncle. I fear my knowledge and abilities are too shallow for such a weighty responsibility."
"There’s no need for modesty in such matters. If you cannot bear this responsibility, who can? Besides, even if you truly feel you cannot, you must still bear it. The preservation of human civilization to this day has not been easy."
"Yes, I understand."
"What do you think of Ruoyun?" the Qing Emperor suddenly asked.
"Classmate Yu Ruoyun’s talents and strength far exceed my own. I hold her in high admiration."
"That’s not what I mean. Do you think you and Ruoyun could date?"
Wang Lan was immediately taken aback by the question.
You’re Yu Ruoyun’s elder. It’s hard to believe that a person of your stature, the esteemed Qing Emperor, would stoop to such crude matchmaking!
Wang Lan remained silent.
"What’s the matter? Not satisfied with Ruoyun? If there’s anything you’re not satisfied with, I’ll have her change it."
Hmm.
Whatever you find satisfactory about me, I’ll change it. How about that?
But Wang Lan didn’t dare say this aloud.
"Uncle, I have a girlfriend..."
"I know. It’s not like you only have one girlfriend. Adding another wouldn’t be a big deal, would it?"
What the hell—
At that moment, the Qing Emperor’s image in Wang Lan’s heart began to crumble.
Are these really words an uncle should say?
"Did you think your affair with that female student at Jin City Star Warrior Academy could escape my notice?"
"Cough, cough, cough... Uncle, can we perhaps not talk about this?"
"Sigh, your skin isn’t thick enough. That won’t do. Do you have any idea what a man as outstanding as you represents to those female Star Martial Warriors?"
"A brother!" Wang Lan blurted out without thinking.
"Heh... To think that old gag is still popular with your generation. To female Star Martial Warriors, you’re like a top-grade Soul Bead. You’re as fatally attractive to them as a large diamond is to an ordinary woman.
"But Star Martial Warriors tend to be more direct in their ways. They dare to love, dare to hate, and dare to act on their feelings. If necessary, they might even take you by force. You’re so shy and naive; you’ll easily be taken advantage of.
"For Star Martial Warriors, having two or three girlfriends is no big deal. A man should be more open-minded."
"Uncle, your words are deeply shaking my values. May I ask why you’re saying this?"
"I hope you can date Ruoyun, then marry her, and have children."
"..."
"Ruoyun’s status is very special. She is the last of the direct Yu Family bloodline. She is to inherit the position of Matriarch of the Yu Family’s main branch, and her children will inherit it from her.
"Because of this, many people are scheming against her. This recent incident is a prime example. It’s not just her; her future children will also be targeted.
"I hope you can protect her, and you are the only one who can. Of course, this is merely my suggestion, not coercion."
"Well... my girlfriend and I are childhood sweethearts, and we’re very devoted to each other..."
"And the one in Jin City?"
"Hahaha... Alright, I’m just teasing you."
"Um, Uncle, if there’s nothing else, I’ll take my leave now."
"Mm!"
Wang Lan bowed and excused himself, then turned and bolted like a wisp of smoke.

chapters.title: Chapter 314: No More Worries About Experience Points
chapters.content:
Chapter 314: Chapter 314: No More Worries About Experience Points
"Uncle, what did you say to him? Why did you scare him like that?" Yu Ruoyun quietly asked Yu Qing.
"I scared him?"
"Didn’t you? Otherwise, why would he have run off in such a hurry?"
"Have you comprehended the Dragon and Phoenix Auspicious?" Yu Qing suddenly asked.
"Yes!" Yu Ruoyun felt somewhat uneasy.
But... my explanation should be fine, right? I absorbed Wang Lan’s Phoenix Form Star Power, gaining the opportunity to cultivate the complete Dragon Emperor Form.
"Ruoyun, in my life, I’ve been through hundreds of fierce battles, but only three times did I come close to death. The first was when I was young; ambushed by over a hundred people, I fought for three days and nights and nearly died from exhaustion.
The second time was twenty years ago. I heard Wang Ling had mastered the Phoenix Form and came running, hoping I could complete my Dragon Emperor Form. Wang Ling chased me for two hundred kilometers and almost beat me to death.
I hoped Wang Lan would date you, but this damned brat got what he wanted and then tried to squirm out of his responsibility! If I hadn’t spent the last ten years cultivating my temperament, I would have slapped him to death just now."
"Uncle!" Yu Ruoyun’s face flushed, but her tone was calm and cold. "He didn’t know about that, and you shouldn’t mention it again."
"Hmm? You didn’t get him drunk, did you?"
"We were on the seventh floor then. Even if I had wanted to, I wouldn’t have had any wine. He fainted from exhaustion. Let’s drop it. I’m destined to be loveless; you shouldn’t have scared him."
"I won’t interfere in your affairs, but I’ll be staying in Modu City for a short while. You will train with me."
"Alright."
Only after running a good distance did Wang Lan secretly let out a sigh of relief.
Was that necessary? Just because I refused, you wanted to get violent?
Wang Lan ran, not because he couldn’t handle the Qing Emperor’s proposal, but because of the momentary murderous intent the Qing Emperor had displayed the second time he declined. It felt as though a knife was at his throat, and he was being asked with a smile, "Touched, aren’t you? Think it over, then speak."
Even a hint of it was terrifying. That was the Qing Emperor, one of the Jade Country’s strongest Star Martial Warriors. Wang Lan didn’t dare risk his life to test the Qing Emperor’s restraint. Besides, what kind of restraint could be expected from someone who would suggest having several girlfriends?
That evening, Wang Lan had dinner with Jiang Xinyu and Yu Ruoyun. At the table, the two women chatted happily, and Yu Ruoyun even suggested that Jiang Xinyu train with her for the next month under the personal guidance of the Qing Emperor.
For Jiang Xinyu, this opportunity was like a beggar suddenly inheriting millions. With less than a month until her team departed for overseas, any improvement was welcome.
Wang Lan returned to his dormitory, pushed open the door, and his face instantly darkened.
The room had been meticulously arranged, but it looked like a memorial hall. A tablet computer was on the desk, an incense burner placed before it, and, damn it, three cigarettes were stuck in the burner.
This is too much!
As Wang Lan was boiling with anger, pondering how to deal with those two bastards, he suddenly heard a faint noise outside the door.
"Keep it down! Wang Lan isn’t back yet; let’s quickly clear this stuff out. He’s going to explode if he sees it."
"Who the hell told you to skip class and go play? Because of you, we only got the message when it was already dark!"
"Like you didn’t skip class! What are you dilly-dallying for? Open the door, will you?"
"Quiet! What if Wang Lan is already back in the dorm?"
"Impossible. He was just having dinner with his girlfriend, Princess Yu. After dinner, they’d at least go for a walk or sing karaoke or something..."
The dormitory door was slowly nudged open a crack, and a head carefully poked in.
"Seems like he’s not here."
"Hurry, go and clean up!" The two rushed into Wang Lan’s room, pushed the door open, and saw a sinister shadow standing in deep contemplation before the computer desk.
"Uh? Wrong room, sorry for disturbing." He Jing turned around decisively and started to run.
"Stop!" an angry shout rang out, and Wang Lan was standing at the door. "You two are really my good brothers, huh? You even prepared a memorial hall for me. I guess I won’t be needing it, but it’s a waste to leave it like this. What do you guys think?"
"Lanzi, it’s okay, it didn’t cost much. It’s fine if it’s wasted."
"I’ll clean it up for you right away."
"The great leader taught us to eliminate waste. This is just right for the two of you. Prepare for a beating—"
It had been seventy days since the start of school. He Jing, who had insisted on playing games every night for seventy days, finally had his streak broken.
He lay on the sofa, periodically emitting pig-like grunts.
"Wang Lan, you were a bit harsh..."
"Harsh? Not really. At least I didn’t beat you to death. You should be grateful."
"Wang Lan, what really happened? Why did the school list you as deceased? We couldn’t find out anything. Even when I asked my dad, he wouldn’t tell me."
"Your dad, Director Ming, is my direct superior. If he won’t tell you, what makes you think I will? Forget it; it’s all confidential. Stop prying."
"Fine."
"I’ve been exhausted for ten days. No games tonight, you two. Let me get a good night’s sleep."
"Do you think I can still play games? My whole body aches! Hey—Wang Lan, this wasn’t your real goal, was it? You’re too sinister!"
"Want another massage?"
"No thanks! Guodong’s skin is thick enough; feel free to rough him up. I can’t take any more."
After closing the door, Wang Lan sat cross-legged on the bed quietly. Too many things had happened in the past ten-plus days, and there was so much that needed to be sorted out.
He sank his consciousness into his Spiritual Sea of Consciousness and opened the system interface. He currently had twenty thousand skill points remaining. Previously, he had over fifty thousand, but after learning an S-rank Star Martial Skill, Meteor Fire Rain, and then linking it with Earth Surge Fire Sea, his fifty thousand skill points had dwindled to twenty thousand.
Meteor Fire Rain wasn’t purely a Fire-attribute Star Martial Skill; it was a hybrid of Fire and Earth attributes. The Earth attribute formed the meteor, and flames then encased it, allowing it to smash ferociously into the ground. A basketball-sized meteor, accelerated by its fall from high altitude, could create a three-meter kill radius.
It was an area-of-effect Star Martial Skill, highly effective on large battlefields. Wang Lan had seen Yu Ruoyun use it more than once, and its power was formidable. After linking it with Earth Surge Fire Sea, the original S-rank Star Martial Skill was upgraded to S+.
Now, Earth Surge Fire Sea no longer summoned mere flames, but magma. Although Wang Lan estimated that the Star Power needed to execute this move was terrifying, potentially exhausting his Star Power in a single use, it would become his trump card once he broke through to the Galaxy Stage.
Thinking of breaking through to the Galaxy Stage, Wang Lan suddenly remembered the only Bronze-level skill among all his Star Martial Skills, one he had just successfully learned: the Immortal Cloud Mysterious Green Record’s Qi Cultivation Chapter.
Wang Lan had tested it: the Bronze-level Immortal Cloud Mysterious Green Record granted one experience point per minute of cultivation. At this rate, relying on it to break through to the Galaxy Stage seemed like it would take an eternity.
Without hesitation, he added one hundred skill points to upgrade the Immortal Cloud Mysterious Green Record to Silver-level. As Wang Lan meditated, the speed at which he absorbed and converted natural Star Power noticeably increased.
On the system interface, a gain of five experience points per minute, while still slow, was much faster than one point per minute. Since he had plenty of skill points, Wang Lan invested another thousand into the Immortal Cloud Mysterious Green Record.
Upgrading to the Gold-level Immortal Cloud Mysterious Green Record increased the experience gain to twenty points per minute. Wang Lan felt this was noticeably faster.
He could clearly feel the world’s natural energy rushing into his body through his mouth and nose, where it was then absorbed and transformed.
Twenty points a minute meant 1,200 points in an hour. In twenty-four hours, that would be 28,800 experience points. He was currently at Star Cloud 7. If advancing to Star Cloud 8 required 800,000 experience points, it would only take him a little over thirty days.
Leveling up in just over a month meant breaking through to the Galaxy Stage before his sophomore year wouldn’t be difficult. And although leveling up in the Galaxy Stage started at two million experience points per level, couldn’t the Immortal Cloud Mysterious Green Record be upgraded further then? If it reached fifty points per minute, breaking through to the Star Sea Realm by his senior year internship wasn’t impossible.
Wang Lan had tested it: as long as he didn’t use any Star Martial Skills, the automatic operation of the Immortal Cloud Mysterious Green Record wouldn’t be interrupted. There was hardly any chance to use Star Martial Skills at school. Plus, there were so many Star Martial Toxins in the Medical Department’s storage waiting for him to clear.
His advancement to the Star Sea Realm would likely be much faster than he initially expected.
After a good night’s sleep, the next day began, and he was full of energy.
Upon waking in the morning, the first thing he saw was a text message from Jiang Xinyu. She informed him that the Qing Emperor had agreed to guide her cultivation, and she would be turning off her phone to focus entirely on training for the next twenty days.
Wang Lan would wholeheartedly support such great news without a second thought.
Refocusing his mind, Wang Lan dove back into his work—not studying, but actual work.
As for studying, after one month of diligent effort, Wang Lan had received eight Academic Credits from his professors for the current semester’s subjects. This might seem trivial compared to the eight hundred Academic Credits Wang Lan had been awarded for clearing the Nine-layer Pagoda, but the maximum for any single course was only ten points, with ten signifying a flawless full score.
Wang Lan had devoted so much time to developing the Star Martial Toxin Vaccine and Soul Bead grenades, so managing to secure an excellent eight points was no easy feat.
Mrs. Sun Li’s suicide had been a tough and heavy blow to the Medical Department, nearly leading to its collapse. Later, the Ministry of Education directly appointed a retired dean from the National Defense Army to the Modu City Star Martial Academy, finally stabilizing the Medical Department.
This new dean wasn’t specialized in Star Martial Toxins, but his research in Medical Star Martial Techniques was unparalleled. Compared to the former Mrs. Sun Li, Vice President Han’s prestige and status were far superior.
Thanks to Vice President Han’s arrival, the Medical Department quickly returned to normal. Many students even requested transfers to major in Medical Star Martial Arts.
But Wang Lan wasn’t very interested in these matters; what intrigued him more were the over thirty thousand kinds of Star Martial Toxin Vaccines in storage.
Once back in work mode, Wang Lan settled into an extremely regular routine: editing Star Martial Toxin Vaccines in the morning and developing Soul Bead grenades in the afternoon.
Dean Nangong was relieved to see Wang Lan finally getting serious and volunteering to make Soul Bead grenades.
The Star Martial Toxins weren’t urgent; Soul Bead grenades were the pressing matter.
Wang Lan nodded repeatedly.
Yes, you’re right about everything, Dean. Jiang Xinyu is going abroad next month, and if I don’t hurry, I won’t be able to ’shear enough wool’ from her.
Unconsciously, more than ten days slipped by quietly.
And just as quietly, Wang Lan successfully broke through to Star Cloud 8, truly stepping into the late stage of the Star Cloud realm.
RING RING RING—
The ringing of the phone in his pocket interrupted Wang Lan’s thoughts. He took out his phone; it was a call from Ming Baiye.
"Mr. Ming! What? Okay, I’ll be right there."
Ming Baiye had instructed Wang Lan to report to the Tianjian Bureau immediately, and in formal attire. Without delay, Wang Lan got up, rode his electric scooter back to his five-hundred-square-meter home in Phoenix Plaza, changed into his military uniform, pinned on his rank insignia, and then hurried to the Tianjian Bureau.

chapters.title: Chapter 315
chapters.content:
Chapter 315: 315
"Hello, Mr. Wang Lan! We meet again." General Yi Zuguo, whom he had met last time, was in Cheng Jianlong’s office. As Wang Lan pushed the door open, Yi Zuguo greeted him with a smile.
"Greetings, General." Wang Lan stood at attention and saluted.
"Wang Lan, you have contributed six super S-class Star Martial Skills and recovered the ancient Qi cultivation methods for Jade Country. Previously, you also developed the method for producing the Star Martial Toxin vaccine and Soul Bead grenades.
After deliberation by the Military Commission, it has been decided to promote Mr. Wang Lan to the rank of Major, award the Azure Day Medal, present a reward of ten million Jade Coins, confer the title of Fellow of the Jade Country Academy of Sciences, and bestow the Jade Country Outstanding Contribution Medal..."
Yi Zuguo was a straightforward person. Without a second word, he stood up and rattled off the long list of awards all at once.
Witnessing these awards, even General Cheng Jianlong looked as if he’d seen a ghost.
Except for the promotion to Major, which he could somewhat understand, none of the other rewards made sense to him.
The Azure Day Medal? What was that? It was the hardest medal to earn within the military system and the highest honor. Only those who performed world-saving feats, averting utter disaster, could receive it.
In the seventy years of peace after the war, only three people had been awarded the Azure Day Medal, and only the Flame Emperor was still alive. Now, with the Flame Emperor having been missing for eight years, Wang Lan was the only living recipient of the Azure Day Medal.
And a Fellow of the Academy of Sciences? Some world-renowned scientists hadn’t received this title. Even some Jade Country scientists who had won the highest scientific accolades, like the Nobel Prize, weren’t Fellows.
Beyond that, the Jade Country Outstanding Contribution Medal, the World Peace Prize? Was this a joke? These accolades had even crossed international borders.
Even the lightest award, promotion to Major—an eighteen-year-old Major, who the hell has ever seen that?
Just how significant were his achievements, and how much favor had he won from superiors to garner such a stack of honors?
Cheng Jianlong was so envious it made his teeth ache with bitterness. However, what Wang Lan truly cared about weren’t these awards themselves.
"Congratulations, Host, on your promotion to Major. Reward: 5,000 skill points."
"Congratulations, Host, on acquiring a special Sacrificial Offering item."
"Congratulations, Host, on earning the title of Scholar. Reward: 30,000 skill points."
"Congratulations, Host, on winning the World Peace Prize. Reward: 500,000 experience points."
A series of system notifications nearly overwhelmed Wang Lan. He clutched four or five boxes filled with rewards, his eyes glazed over.
"Wang Lan, snap out of it! Don’t be so happy you go dumb," Cheng Jianlong suddenly said sternly.
"Oh, huh?"
"Hahaha... Jianlong, he’s still young, and young people should have the vigor of youth. If he were as serious and lacking in youthful spirit as you described, I’d wonder if he were some ancient creature hundreds of years old," Yi Zuguo said, laughing.
"You’re joking, General. By the way, General, have you found out who is behind Mrs. Sun Li?"
"You still call her ’Mrs.’? She almost killed you."
"After all, she taught me all she knew, and what she taught me was substantial. Without her, there would be no Star Martial Toxin vaccine. Hatred is hatred, and gratitude is gratitude. My mother taught me from a young age to clearly distinguish between the two."
"Hmm? That’s not Wang Ling’s style. As for the person behind Sun Li, I can only say I have a guess. But I can’t tell you who it is; I fear you’ll do something foolish in your youthful zeal. Against someone so powerful and of such extraordinary status, no one can act rashly without irrefutable evidence."
"I understand," Wang Lan said in a low voice.
"That’s good. You’re still in school, and I shouldn’t interrupt your studies. However, I have a plane to catch soon, so I had to interrupt your class time. Now that it’s done, you can go back."
"Wang Lan, should I arrange for someone to see you out?"
"No need, Chief. I rode my bike here."
Wang Lan did not return to school; it wasn’t practical to take these items back to the dormitory. Not that he couldn’t, but it would attract too much jealousy. Any one of these award certificates was historic. Flaunting them in the dormitory? Wasn’t that just asking to be struck by lightning?
Moreover, the other items were manageable, but he couldn’t explain the Sacrificial Offering item. If he summoned something strange and He Jing and the others saw it, even with an IQ of 140, Wang Lan wouldn’t be able to talk his way out of it.
Back in his dormitory, Wang Lan first put away the pile of certificates. Then, he closed the windows and drew the curtains.
The Sacrificial Offering item didn’t require him to sacrifice his actual medals, but rather the medals within the system. The real medals would still remain.
He accessed the system and opened the medals page. Unbeknownst to him, Wang Lan’s medals page already displayed seven or eight medals, but only the Azure Day Medal shimmered with a multicolored light.
This medal was even more prestigious than the Glory of the Sun Medal he had received before; he wondered what marvels it might conjure.
He focused his spiritual power on the medal and chose "Sacrifice."
Instantly, his vision became blurry, and soon, the familiar carousel of images appeared.
The last time he saw this scene was over six months ago, yet it felt like just yesterday.
Demons, Angels, viruses, Transformers, dragons, deities, and various anime characters flashed before his eyes.
Because I knew the items from the exchange would be entirely beneficial, posing no hidden dangers, I wasn’t as terrified as last time. Even seeing a wave of zombies, I merely wondered if I could exchange for a virus antibody.
The carousel of images slowed, gradually showing signs of stopping.
Hey, this Bumblebee car isn’t bad. I indeed lack a vehicle, and Bumblebee can drive, fight, and even be a pet. Not bad, not bad...
But it seemed the carousel of images hadn’t heard Wang Lan’s thoughts; it suddenly skipped over the Bumblebee sports car and stopped on a katana.
A weapon? Do I bloody lack weapons? Such a high-grade medal, and you offer me a blade? Even if it’s the Sky Cloud Sword, that’s not acceptable!
But the image finally froze.
BOOM—
A vast stream of information rushed into Wang Lan’s mind. In an instant, countless bizarre blades flashed through his thoughts. Eventually, an ordinary-looking katana paused in his mind’s eye.
This sword had no guard and looked like a long rod. The hilt and scabbard shared the same color and pattern. The sword was 1.3 meters long, with a 30-centimeter hilt.
To Wang Lan, it felt like a dark orchid, possessing a gentleman’s aura.
And the moment he saw the sword clearly, his eyes lit up. The sword’s name was Sword of Light, and it, along with its brethren, had a collective name: Zanpakuto.
This was a Zanpakuto, but not one from the world of Death Gods. After all, this was Wang Lan’s own Zanpakuto. Depending on an individual’s soul, a Zanpakuto manifests with a unique form, abilities, and true name.
Only by calling its true name can a Zanpakuto achieve its initial release—Shikai—a process requiring patient communication and mutual understanding with the Zanpakuto. However, Wang Lan didn’t need this, as this Zanpakuto’s true name was indeed Sword of Light.
Wang Lan’s eyes suddenly opened wide. As he reached out, a long rod materialized in his empty hand. The grip felt extremely comfortable—its length, weight, and feel were as if custom-made for him.
Wang Lan slowly drew the Zanpakuto. As the blade extended an inch, an inch of the sheath vanished, disappearing completely as the blade was fully drawn.
The body of the blade shimmered like autumn water, its edge sharp as starlight.
With a light flick of a finger, the blade emitted a crisp, dragon-like ring.
The craftsmanship of this blade must have reached the pinnacle of cold weapons. Even the Dragon Spring Sword Pavilion couldn’t promise to forge a treasured blade of the same quality. Yet, this is but a disguise for the Zanpakuto. Even the disguise is a masterpiece; the Zanpakuto’s reputation is well-deserved.
Because this blade was straight and only two fingers wide, it could be used as both a saber and a sword, making it versatile for either saber or sword techniques.
Wang Lan held the sword with both hands, his expression solemn, concentrating his spiritual power on the blade.
"Release—Sword of Light!"
Almost as soon as Wang Lan’s voice fell, the blade in his hand suddenly shattered, the fragments turning into a sky full of starlight. The starlight converged, a dazzling white light erupted, and a sword formed entirely of light appeared in Wang Lan’s grasp.
The sword in his hand was both blade and light. It possessed all the functions of a sword; additionally, the light could extend, change shape, and unleash blades and showers of light.
The Sword of Light was a blade capable of piercing through darkness.
However, its Shikai form, the Sword of Light, consumed Star Power, for the wielder is the ultimate source of all power.
When the Shikai was canceled, the glow faded, and the Sword of Light returned to its former katana appearance. The moment Wang Lan thought of sheathing it, the scabbard instantly reappeared around the blade.
Like the Phoenix Constellation Saint Cloth, this sword could reside within the Star Palace. Of course, the Star Palace wasn’t its true destination; Zanpakuto normally dwell within the soul.
But then again, how do you explain suddenly pulling out such an odd sword without opening the Star Palace? It wouldn’t be easy to explain. At least the Saint Cloth emerges from an opened Star Palace, but what about a Zanpakuto?
This trip to the Tianjian Bureau yielded 35,000 skill points. Adding to the 50,000 skill points he had previously received for developing the Star Martial Toxin Vaccine, he now had enough for a major skill upgrade.
Previously, after reaching the Gold Tier, I felt there wasn’t much point in upgrading normal skills. In fact, even some Star Martial Skill upgrades seemed meaningless. Now the situation is different; my combat style has also started to evolve. In the past, my power was too weak, so I had to be cautious with my Star Martial Skills. But now, I prefer to be more aggressive. Take Star Cloud Sword Dance, for example; it’s now at Gold Tier, Level Three. The main difference between the Gold and Silver Tiers was merely more afterimages and the addition of Sky Step techniques. But I already have Phantom Tracer at Gold Tier, allowing for six instantaneous shifts in any direction with no blind spots. This traceless spatial movement is far superior to mere afterimages. Furthermore, Sky Step has been replaced by the flight from Weight Exchange. Now with the Zanpakuto, even Sword Qi is obsolete. I feel Star Cloud Sword Dance upgrades should stop here. Flame Sword is different, though. I need to improve it at least until I learn the Infinite Fire Skill. Who knows? Applying the five unique flames to Flame Sword after learning Infinite Fire Skill might yield unexpected benefits. I do use Crescent Arrow frequently, though. But I have a hunch Crescent Arrow will soon be replaced by Flame Sword. Flame Sword is already showing long-range capabilities. Beyond Platinum Tier, its range might rival Crescent Arrow’s. As for Thunder Snake, I feel there’s still a lot of room for improvement. I vaguely sense it’s connected to another domain: Elementalization. For skills like Sentient Beings, my current plan is to learn the basics first. I can always boost them later when needed.
As his strength increased and approached the state of Return to the Original, it all boiled down to the same three fundamental elements:
Star Power level, speed, and power!
In gaming terms: Evasion, Defense, and Damage Output.

chapters.title: Chapter 316: The New Mission
chapters.content:
Chapter 316: Chapter 316: The New Mission
"Hey, Mr. Ming. Is that so? Alright... okay... I’ll come over right away."
It was another weekend. Wang Lan was planning to go to the medical department to continue grinding Star Martial Toxins for experience and skill points when he received a call from Ming Baiye right after stepping out of his dorm.
The Tianjian Bureau had encountered another tricky case and hoped Wang Lan could assist.
Wang Lan rode his electric motorcycle to the Tianjian Bureau, where Director Ming had just finished a case briefing and greeted Wang Lan with a slightly embarrassed, apologetic smile.
"Wang Lan, your primary duty is to study. Honestly, I wouldn’t have called you if we weren’t really short-handed."
"It’s no problem; I was resting anyway. I saw the men rushing around when I arrived. Has it been very busy recently?"
"Weren’t you there that day? The mastermind framing you, the origin of so many Space Stones, and so on... Each line of investigation requires a lot of manpower and resources. Although the Tianjian Bureau of Modu City has high standards, Modu City is only so big, so it’s impossible to allocate as many personnel as an entire province could. Especially for this type of work, it’s all about the numbers."
Ming Baiye was venting his frustrations to Wang Lan, who could only respond with a dry laugh.
"Mr. Ming, what case has got you so tangled up?"
"There have been several incidents recently where individuals with mysterious identities were murdered."
"People with mysterious identities?" Wang Lan looked at Ming Baiye in surprise.
Such a term shouldn’t be coming from Ming Baiye’s mouth.
As long as someone is from Jade Country, they definitely have an identity. For the Tianjian Bureau, Jade Country’s professional special agent intelligence department, to fail to ascertain their identities—is that appropriate?
Ming Baiye raised his hand to turn on the projector on the wall and turned off the lights. A series of photos appeared on the projection.
"This is from the night of November 7th, at the entrance of Red Dust Bar. Two men were assassinated by a mysterious person as they left the bar. The Tianjian Bureau intervened immediately, but strangely, the two men killed had no identity records. Even after their fingerprints, facial features, and DNA were entered into the Cloud Sea System, nothing matched any existing identities. These two men seemed to have appeared out of thin air, with no birth records, schooling records, or employment records..."
"A blank slate of a person? But aren’t there cameras at the entrance of the bar? Didn’t the cameras capture the murderer’s appearance?"
"They did, but it’s useless!"
The screen changed to a photo of the captured murderer. The instant Wang Lan saw the photo, he felt a bit uneasy.
Damn, Deadpool!
"What? You know him?" Ming Baiye asked in confusion.
"No, his outfit resembles a character from an anime I’ve seen: dressed in a red tight suit, with two swords on his back. But obviously, it’s not him. Dressed like that, he really doesn’t have to worry about being caught on camera."
"After that incident, another person was murdered in an alley. This time, there were no witnesses or cameras, and the victim, similarly, had no identity records. Up until today, December 10th, thirteen people have been killed, and all the victims lacked identity records. This might be why the killer targets them."
"Could they be from a secretive organization? And someone is hunting down its members? No, that’s not right. If they were from some secret organization, they would still need legitimate identities for cover. No identity records mean that someone was hiding them from birth. Or maybe... someone is capable of altering the Cloud Sea System."
"That’s what I need your help to look into. I’m assigning you four capable team members," he said, picking up the phone. "Send the members of the independent S-Group to my office."
Soon after, four young men and women knocked on Ming Baiye’s office door—two men and two women, a perfect balance.
All four were in military uniform, looking very sharp. Wang Lan thought the Tianjian Bureau’s military uniforms were the most stylish he had seen among various versions, unlike the uniforms of the regular military, which were merely tops and trousers with a belt in between. The men’s uniforms featured long trench coat-style jackets; summer attire had short sleeves, autumn attire had long sleeves, and the winter version included a lining. The women’s uniforms consisted of a short jacket with shorts or a skirt, while the winter uniform was a long coat. So, even if someone had average looks, donning this military uniform would automatically enhance their appearance by thirty percent, not to mention that all four in front of him were genuinely attractive. The two men were one masculine and one handsome; the two women, though different in appearance and temperament, both deserved to be called beauties.
In contrast, Wang Lan’s casual attire seemed somewhat plain before the four.
"Let me introduce you. This is Mr. Wang Lan, a major attached to the Action Department. This is Yang Yang, the temporary leader of the independent S-Group; this is Liu Yifeng; the tall woman is Zhang Xiao, and the long-haired woman is Bai Xu. Bai Xu is a perception-type Star Martial Warrior with exceptional perception abilities. Zhang Xiao’s Innate Ability is air manipulation. Liu Yifeng is a Wind Attribute Star Martial Warrior, mastering two A-rank Star Martial Skills. Yang Yang is a Gold Attribute Star Martial Warrior with top-notch close-combat abilities. They have just finished their drill as an independent squad and haven’t been put to use yet. Wang Lan, what do you think of them as your temporary team members?"
"Their composition is very balanced, and their complementarity is high. It’s just that I’m only a major," Wang Lan said with a wry smile.
Before him stood one lieutenant colonel and three majors. In terms of seniority and military rank, Wang Lan was the junior.
"What’s the problem? The Tianjian Bureau only considers ability, not rank or seniority. Besides, with all the contributions you’ve made, you could have been promoted to general already if it weren’t for how recently you joined the Tianjian Bureau."
"Listen up, you four. From now on, Wang Lan is your temporary captain. Don’t let his young age fool you; at least five high-level Demon Clan spy groups have fallen to him. And he has personally killed six or seven high-level Demon Clan spies. Starting now, you four must fully obey Wang Lan’s orders and assist him in investigating these mysterious murders."
"Yes!"
"Alright, you can go now." The four saluted and left the office.
Stepping outside the office, their gazes kept exchanging. Having trained together for over half a year, they were very familiar with each other, yet they could see skepticism in one another’s eyes. All four had been chosen from thirty trained elites; wasn’t each one of them extraordinarily talented with a boundless future? The independent groups were special operations squads of the Modu City Tianjian Bureau. Although each squad had only four members, they carried out the highest-level missions. In the entire Modu City Tianjian Bureau, there were only seven such independent groups, and their designation was ’S,’ signifying the Bureau’s expectation for them to be super squads.
And the first leader of this super squad appeared to be a teenager, barely seventeen or eighteen? Even if this young man was already a major... it just didn’t seem reliable.
"I say, Old Yang, the case we’re supposed to investigate seems to require technical skills, not much to do with strength, right?" Liu Yifeng asked in a hushed voice, leaning against a stone pillar outside the office building.
"If you’ve got something to say, spit it out. Don’t beat around the bush."
"Being a major at such a young age definitely signifies a genius. He must be at least at the peak of Star Cloud rank, or in the early stages of Galaxy rank. But still, he’s young and lacks experience."
"Didn’t Director Ming say that four or five Demon Clan spy groups have fallen into Captain Wang’s hands?" Bai Xu asked in her soft voice.
"Do you actually believe that? This type of genius, with a family background and resources we can only envy. Tagging along to pick up some effortless merits that are then attributed to him—I’ve seen that kind of thing plenty of times," Zhang Xiao said, arms crossed and somewhat disdainfully.
"You’d better keep those words to yourselves. Think about it: majors under the age of twenty—how many can you find in the entire military, no, in the entire Ministry of Defense system? Someone like him, even with a good family background and privileged status, must have real skills. In the Tianjian Bureau, the hierarchy and system are different. No matter how high your military rank is elsewhere, it’s reset here, and you have to climb up again. That means Captain Wang’s major rank was earned within the Bureau. I haven’t heard of him before, so he might have been parachuted in. Regardless, while we may outrank him, he’s the team leader by position. Even if it’s temporary, I don’t want to hear any dissent while he’s in charge, not even behind-the-scenes chatter. We’re soldiers. Our duty is to obey, obey, and obey again. Understood?"
"What if his orders are clearly wrong?"
"We can file a complaint; we can lodge a complaint with Director Ming afterward, but his orders must be followed unconditionally. This is basic common sense. Do I need to teach you this?"
Obviously, Yang Yang held absolute authority in the four-person squad. So when he spoke, Liu Yifeng and Zhang Xiao fell silent.
"Huh? What are you guys doing here?"
"Captain."
"Good day, Captain."
"Reporting, Captain! From this moment on, we are your team members. We cannot disband without your orders."
"Is that so? Alright then, you guys go back and change into civilian clothes. We’ll meet at the entrance in twenty minutes. Oh, do you all have cars?"
"Each independent operations team is equipped with two vehicles to facilitate our missions."
"I see. Then take me to the vehicles first. I came on a donkey, so it’s not convenient for me to move around without a car."
In the open-air parking lot, a domineering off-road vehicle and a low-key business van were parked in S-designated spots. The vehicles were brand new; Wang Lan noticed the odometer hadn’t even reached two hundred kilometers.
Wang Lan patted the off-road vehicle, quite satisfied.
This, dammit, is what a man should drive.
"You guys go change into civilian clothes; I’ll wait for you here."
Sitting in the car, Wang Lan browsed his phone, looking at the detailed information about the case he had just taken on. Two mission progress prompts appeared in his mind. One was the revenge mission for Ma Chuchu. It was the first task he accepted after coming to the Modu City Star Martial Academy, and it remained uncompleted. The other was the newly accepted mission: to solve the mystery of these murders and find the killer.
The Tianjian Bureau’s original approach was to investigate the victims’ identities, hoping to uncover the reasons for their deaths and the killer’s motives. But due to recent frequent emergencies in Modu City, the investigation had been sporadic. Almost twenty days had passed with no progress, yet the killer’s murderous hand hadn’t stopped. More than a dozen people had died just like that.
Soon, the four returned to Wang Lan’s side. Out of their military uniforms, they no longer had such a serious demeanor, possessing a more youthful and lively vibe instead.
That’s more like it,
he thought.
It’s not like they’re attending an important event or meeting someone crucial. Why dress so seriously and stiffly? They were all in their early twenties to around thirty, yet they made themselves look as if they were in their forties.
"Captain!"
"Get in the car!"
"Captain, let me drive. I have an A-level military license."
"Huh? Is that a lack of trust in my driving skills? Well, Comrade Old Yang, bias and arrogance are unbecoming. As for my driving skills... not to boast, but your distrust is entirely justified."
PFFT! Bai Xu suddenly choked and started coughing violently.
"Just trying to lighten the mood. No need for such a dramatic reaction, right?"
But apart from Bai Xu, the other three were expressionless, their faces devoid of emotion.
"Captain, where should we start the investigation?"
"Phoenix Plaza."
"Phoenix Plaza? I don’t remember there being any crime scenes there."
"It’s almost twelve o’clock. Aren’t you hungry? Let’s eat first and then investigate."

chapters.title: Chapter 317 important clues
chapters.content:
Chapter 317: 317 important clues
It’s essential to foster good relationships with fellow team members during our first meeting. Even if it’s just a temporary alliance, we’ll still be part of the same system eventually.
For Wang Lan, he could conduct the investigation alone if necessary, but that’s just the way society works.
Wang Lan chose a barbecue restaurant that prided itself on its authentic style. It didn’t add any unnecessary seasonings, allowing customers to taste the pure flavor of the meat.
The restaurant had been open for less than half a year, but its reputation was already quite good.
The four of them ordered portions fit for ten. Casual conversations flowed as they dined, allowing the five of them to formally start getting acquainted.
The four quickly changed their initial impression of Wang Lan. They thought that since Wang Lan was promoted to major at such a young age, he must be from a distinguished background, and those with such backgrounds often shared a common flaw: arrogance.
Even if they seemed approachable on the surface, they might occasionally reveal an air of arrogance through their expressions and words. However, none of these traits were seen in Wang Lan. To the two men, he seemed good-natured and easy to get along with, speaking in a tone that was never aggressive.
To the two women, he seemed warm, as girls are usually more sensitive in this regard.
After the meal, Wang Lan started checking out each crime scene. Yang Yang had already dealt with some aspects of this case before but not in great depth. With reference to the available information, he barely managed to reconstruct the scenes.
"The bar manager also said that those two were first-timers and seemed quite restrained. They just sat at the bar and watched quietly without hitting on the girls," Yang Yang recounted.
"How can he be so sure they were first-timers?" Wang Lan asked.
"This bar is a quieter establishment, favored by an executive clientele. The whole bar environment is rather peaceful; people come here to relax. Those who are out for wilder entertainment usually head to those noisy bars with dance floors and long-legged beauties. So, most of the bar-goers are regulars. The manager may not know everyone personally but recognizes their faces. Those two were very restrained, and the manager is quite sure they hardly ever, or have never been to such a place before."
"The victim’s identity is unknown, the killer’s identity is unknown, and the motive for the murder is unclear. There’s simply no way to start with this case."
"Let’s move on to the next place."
An afternoon was spent visiting five locations, all of which resembled the first, with no information to be found. No ID cards, no mobile phones, no clues that could be used to trace their identities.
"No wonder the colleagues from the Intelligence Department are so troubled; it’s like trying to find a way into a hedgehog rolled into a ball," Yang Yang mused.
"Bai Xu, what did you say?" Wang Lan suddenly looked up from his thoughts and asked.
"Nowhere to start?"
"No, the other thing, what was it like?"
"A hedgehog rolling into a ball?"
"Rolling into a ball..." Wang Lan quickly took out his phone to pull up the map. "If we change our perspective, this is the Qinghai District. All the crime scenes are densely concentrated within the East Forest Town area. Doesn’t it strike you as odd? Why do these people without identities appear? We have sophisticated support equipment and can make use of all resources in Modu City to investigate their identities, yet we’ve found nothing. How does the killer accurately locate them? It’s easy for people without identities to hide. Leaving is also too simple for them. All they have to do is hide somewhere, and the killer would not be able to track them down, unless the killer was watching them nonstop. But there’s only one killer; it’s impossible to keep an eye on many people at once."
"Maybe there’s more than one murderer?"
"If there were more than one, there would be no need to kill one by one. To closely watch them, at least twice the number of people would be needed, and the killer could easily take down several at the same time."
"Could it be someone secretly stalking, with only one person actually committing the murders?"
"Xiao Ai?"
"I’m here!"
Is this thing even aware it’s hiding its intelligence? This formulaic reply was just like that of the most common AI.
"Compile all the surveillance footage from the crime scenes. Check for anyone who might have been watching the victims or followed them there before the incidents."
"Got it."
"Team leader, is this... your cyber sprite?"
"Yeah, I was really into robotics in high school, so I wrote some intelligent code to handle some monotonous tasks for me."
"Pretty good. It’s no worse than those artificial intelligences on the market," Liu Yifeng commented objectively.
Heh, Xiao Ai is deliberately downplaying itself. If it went all out, it would outmatch everyone except Ice Snow. Just analyzing the data collected by the Tianjian Bureau? Impossible, Xiao Ai must have hacked into every surveillance system in the area to carry out its analysis.
While Xiao Ai was checking all the surveillance footage, Wang Lan had already started marking out on the map the areas where the victims were found. The markings formed a crescent-shaped trajectory on the map.
"Team leader, do you think there’s a pattern to this trajectory?" Bai Xu asked, looking at the marked routes on the map.
"Right now, I’m just taking a shot in the dark. Though they say that solving cases shouldn’t rely on luck, in the absence of any clues, we’re left with no choice but to chance it."
"BEEP. BEEP. BEEP. Wang Lan, the big data search is complete. No individuals fitting your described parameters have been found. Would you like to update the search criteria?"
The last sentence is pure nonsense. With Xiao Ai’s level of intelligence, it’s impossible for it not to know what Wang Lan is looking for. It has definitely searched through all possible options. If there’s nothing, then there truly is nothing.
RING RING—
Suddenly, Wang Lan’s cell phone rang.
"Hello, Director Ming? What? I’ll be right there."
Wang Lan hung up the phone, his face instantly darkening. "East gate of Dongming Hospital, another murder case has occurred. Two people were killed in the street by a red-clothed masked killer. We must go immediately."
The SUV roared, transforming into a ferocious beast as it charged through the streets. When they arrived at the scene, police guards had already secured the area. Beyond the cordon, there was a crowd of onlookers.
Wang Lan and his colleagues showed their credentials and were allowed to enter.
"Captain Lu, people from the Tianjian Bureau have arrived," a police officer said in a low voice as he approached a detective.
Detective Lu quickly stood up and walked towards Wang Lan and his four companions. "You got here quickly. This case is similar to the previous ones. There are plenty of witnesses, but the killer was masked and killed in broad daylight. We don’t know where he came from. So, even with witnesses and security cameras, he doesn’t hold back. These two people just happened to walk to the entrance of the hospital when suddenly a person in a red tight-fitting suit appeared, drew two deadly weapons from behind, and killed one of them. The other seemed to be about to use a Star Martial Skill but was beheaded by the killer before he could use it."
"Captain Lu, still no identification?" Wang Lan asked in a low voice.
"None. We’ve checked the facial recognition system, and there’s no match for this person. Our facial recognition system is linked to the Cloud Sea Central Hub and can analyze one million faces per second. No cell phone, no ID card, no money, nothing that could prove their identities."
Wang Lan surveyed the scene; it was brutal and bloody. The one who was first killed had been cut in half at the waist, their lower and upper body separated by at least two meters, with intestines and internal organs spilled all over the place. The second one was decapitated, blood sprayed like an ink painting.
"Have you conducted a reverse investigation?"
"We could only track a one-kilometer route; before that, they seemed to intentionally avoid surveillance cameras, so we couldn’t continue the investigation."
"Are these guys nuts? Knowing that someone is hunting them, they still bloody well run around outside?" Yang Yang spat out angrily. "Even if they’re thick-skulled, they should at least leave us some clues!"
Against victims and perpetrators whose identities were both a mystery, Wang Lan was also at a loss.
The entire population of Jade Country didn’t include these people. Where to find their identities, their social connections, the killer’s next target?
RING RING— Detective Lu’s phone suddenly rang.
"Hello? What? Where? Okay!"
"Major Wang, three kilometers east, someone has reported the killer chasing down five Star Martial Warriors."
"Let’s go!" Wang Lan said, and with a WHOOSH, he shot into the sky. Seeing Wang Lan fly into the sky and disappear in the blink of an eye, Yifeng also quickly leaped up into the sky.
Both had flying-type Star Martial Skills. Three kilometers wasn’t particularly far or close, but to leap three kilometers through the sky took at least three to five minutes. From a high vantage point, they quickly spotted the disturbance. Below, in a narrow alley, a crowd of onlookers blocked the entrance.
Wang Lan could never understand why these people were so keen on watching the excitement. Moreover, they never considered whether this kind of excitement should be watched or whether it was dangerous. You dare watch a Star Martial Warrior battle? If they dare to fight in a major city, they certainly wouldn’t care about mistakenly killing a few civilians, right?
Wang Lan landed. "Everyone go back home! No one is allowed to come near!"
By the time of the alert, it was likely already over.
When Wang Lan arrived, all that was left was a dreadful scene and nothing else.
In the alley lay six bodies, all freshly killed. The blood staining the walls was still warm.
Wang Lan walked past the bloodstains and carefully examined the corpses. They were all killed by swords, which showed that the killer was a master at using them.
From the security camera footage Detective Lu had seen, it was evident that the killer was not only adept with sword skill but also had an extremely fast movement technique and a sort of invisibility Innate Ability. This was because the first person to be cut in half at the waist hadn’t realized it until it was too late.
Of the five people in front of him, apart from the one furthest away who did not react before death, the rest had postures indicating attempts to run or twist their bodies. Yet, even though they knew the grim reaper was upon them, they were helplessly slaughtered.
"Yifeng, go and ask if there are any eyewitnesses. Find out what happened," Wang Lan directed.
"Yes!"
There were six bodies: one bisected at the waist, two beheaded, one pierced through the heart, one through the throat, and one cleaved in half right through the head. Despite the disgusting mess, Wang Lan endured his queasiness and observed carefully.
The cuts were clean, especially the one that split a head open. Either the killer was an expert in wind attributes, or their sword was extremely sharp.
Among the six, the clothing style of five was exactly the same as those previously killed, but one young man’s attire did not seem like that of someone living in seclusion.
Wang Lan tried to search his personal belongings.
Suddenly, a look of surprise appeared on his face as he found a cell phone in the young man’s chest pocket.
Having a phone meant potential access to his identity.

chapters.title: Chapter 318: Sure Enough, Guessed Right
chapters.content:
Chapter 318: Chapter 318: Sure Enough, Guessed Right
"Captain!"
"Captain!" Yang Yang and the other two also rushed over.
"You’re just in time. Check whose phone this is immediately."
"Captain, I’m back," Liu Yifeng returned, drenched in sweat. "I asked ten eyewitnesses. They all came out after hearing the loud noise. By the time they looked, they saw someone in a red skintight suit and a mask, wielding two knives and slashing at those six people. The two knives were extremely sharp, and the slashing was incredibly fast. They described it as taking less than five seconds for all six people to die. Then the masked person disappeared into the wall."
Disappeared into the wall? Earth Movement Skill?
"Captain, we’ve found his identity. His name is Duanmu Jing, a collateral member of the Duanmu Family who graduated last year."
The Duanmu Family? Could the murderer’s target be the Duanmu Family?
No useful clues were left at the scene; the only useful clue was likely Duanmu Jing’s cell phone.
As darkness gradually fell, Wang Lan and his four-person team concluded their on-site investigation and headed to the police station. Utilizing the police department’s resources for cases was standard procedure for the Tianjian Bureau.
Reorganizing the clues confirmed that the murderer killed with a clear purpose. Each time they struck, they killed the same type of person: individuals with no identity, no history, all aged between twenty-five and thirty-five.
It was hard to imagine how someone could hide their identity from birth until now.
This might happen in remote villages, where some people live their entire lives without household registration or an ID card. But in large cities, it’s nearly impossible to get by without an ID.
What part of daily life doesn’t require an ID card?
This time, their only lead was a cell phone, which provided the phone number of one of the deceased. After they compiled the clues, there was a knock on the door of their temporary office.
"Major Wang, representatives from the Duanmu Family are here."
"Okay, please ask them to wait!"
Wang Lan organized the documents before him and walked out of the room with the four others. At this, the four of them felt their cheeks flush. Since taking the case, they felt they had merely been tagging along. They had neither constructive suggestions nor significant discoveries. When Wang Lan asked for their input, they were at a loss. After all, the victims’ identities were unknown, as was the murderer’s. People like the victims, who had no identity at all, were an even greater mystery. The only victim with a known identity, Duanmu Jing, might not even be connected to the others. Currently, there was no evidence to prove Duanmu Jing had any connection with the other victims.
In the interrogation room sat an elderly couple. Both were nearly sixty but remarkably well-preserved. However, at this moment, their expressions were somber, their complexions pale.
"What’s your relation to Duanmu Jing?"
"He’s my son," the old lady quickly replied. "Officer... my son, he... has he really been killed by that murderer? He was perfectly fine just yesterday..."
"Do you know why he was in an alley in Beijiao Ancient Village?"
"I don’t know. He just said he was going out to see friends today and had been gone for less than half a day... I didn’t expect..." she said, covering her face and sobbing.
"Officer, has my son really been murdered? Why would he be murdered?" the middle-aged man asked, his expression dark.
"You’re Duanmu Jing’s father?"
"Yes!"
"Name?"
"Duanmu Qi."
"Age?"
"Sixty."
"Occupation?"
"I’m a late-stage Star Cloud Star Martial Warrior, currently a sub-detachment leader in the Duanmu Pioneer Team. I was on leave last month, so I came home to rest."
"Do you recognize these people?" Wang Lan placed the restored photos in front of Duanmu Qi. He took them and examined each one carefully.
After a long while, he shook his head. "I don’t recognize them. Who are they? The ones who murdered my son?"
"No, these are the people who were killed by the same murderer as your son. None of them have any identity information. They aren’t missing persons, nor are they using fake identities. They’ve had no identity since birth—mysterious individuals with no records whatsoever. We suspect they belong to the same organization, and Duanmu Jing was mingling with them..."
"Impossible!" Duanmu Qi said firmly. "If my son was involved with any organization, it would definitely be the Duanmu Family. Although our line is a collateral branch of the Duanmu Family, we want for nothing. He would never betray the family for some dubious organization. Moreover, my son is not like me. He’s a top graduate from Jin City Star Martial Academy and has already reached mid-Galaxy Stage strength. The family values him highly.
